A decrease in glutamate removal, whether caused by drugs or a reduction in glial coverage near the synapses, impacted the release of transmitters by altering the activity of presynaptic metabotropic glutamate receptors. Consequently, the wrapping of neurons by astrocytes plays a role in controlling the effectiveness of synapses in the central nervous system.

title: Duration of androgen suppression in the treatment of prostate cancer.
text:
In this study, we aimed to compare the effectiveness of radiotherapy combined with short-term androgen suppression versus long-term androgen suppression in the treatment of locally advanced prostate cancer. Previous research has shown that the combination of radiotherapy and long-term androgen suppression (> or = 2 years) improves overall survival in these patients.

To conduct the study, we randomly assigned patients who had received external-beam radiotherapy and 6 months of androgen suppression into two groups. One group received no further treatment (short-term suppression), while the other group received an additional 2.5 years of treatment with a luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone agonist (long-term suppression). We set a noninferiority outcome, where short-term suppression would be considered as effective as long-term suppression if the hazard ratio for overall survival was more than 1.35, with a one-sided alpha level of 0.05. However, an interim analysis showed futility, and the results are presented with an adjusted one-sided alpha level of 0.0429.

A total of 1113 men were registered for the study, with 970 randomly assigned to either the short-term suppression group (483 patients) or the long-term suppression group (487 patients). After a median follow-up of 6.4 years, 132 patients in the short-term group and 98 in the long-term group had died. Among these deaths, 47 in the short-term group and 29 in the long-term group were due to prostate cancer. The 5-year overall mortality rates were 19.0% for short-term suppression and 15.2% for long-term suppression. The observed hazard ratio was 1.42 (upper 95.71% confidence limit, 1.79; P=0.65 for noninferiority). Both groups experienced adverse events such as fatigue, diminished sexual function, and hot flushes.

In conclusion, our findings indicate that the combination of radiotherapy and 6 months of androgen suppression is less effective in terms of survival compared to radiotherapy combined with 3 years of androgen suppression for the treatment of locally advanced prostate cancer. (ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00003026.)

title: A Functional Neuroimaging Study of Sound Localization: Visual Cortex Activity Predicts Performance in Early-Blind Individuals
text: Blind individuals often exhibit improved nonvisual perceptual abilities, but the exact neural basis for this enhancement is not fully understood. A previous study found that some early-blind individuals are better at localizing sounds using monaural cues compared to sighted individuals. To investigate the neural mechanisms behind these behavioral differences, we conducted functional imaging studies using positron emission tomography and a speaker array that allowed for pseudo-free-field presentations in the scanner. During binaural sound localization, the sighted control group showed decreased blood flow in the occipital lobe, which was not observed in early-blind individuals. However, during monaural sound localization (with one ear plugged), early-blind individuals who excelled at sound localization displayed activation in two areas of the occipital cortex. This activation was not seen in blind individuals who did not have superior monaural sound localization abilities, nor in sighted individuals. The level of activation in one of these areas was strongly correlated with sound localization accuracy across the entire group of blind individuals. These findings suggest that blind individuals who outperform sighted individuals in sound localization recruit occipital areas to process auditory information under monaural conditions. Therefore, we conclude that the occipital cortex plays a crucial role in the enhanced ability to utilize monaural cues. Our results not only provide insights into compensatory mechanisms between sensory modalities, but also shed light on individual differences in these mechanisms and the inhibitory patterns that differ between sighted individuals and those who have been blind since early life.

title: High-Infiltration of Tumor-Associated Macrophages Predicts Unfavorable Clinical Outcome for Node-Negative Breast Cancer
text: The tumor microenvironment consists of tumor cells, fibroblasts, endothelial cells, and infiltrating immune cells. These components can either hinder or facilitate tumor growth and progression. The aim of this retrospective study was to examine the density of tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) in breast cancer and determine its correlation with clinicopathological parameters. We collected paraffin-embedded specimens and clinicopathological data, including up to 5 years of follow-up information, from 172 breast cancer patients. Immunohistochemical staining for CD68, a marker for macrophages, was conducted and assessed in a blinded manner. Our findings revealed a significant prevalence of TAMs in breast cancer patients with high histopathological grades. Patients with a high density of TAMs experienced significantly lower rates of disease-free survival and 5-year overall survival compared to those with a low density of TAMs. Moreover, a high infiltration of TAMs indicated a poorer survival rate for patients with node-negative breast cancer. In conclusion, the number of TAMs in the tumor stroma serves as an independent predictor of survival time for breast cancer patients. A high infiltration of TAMs is a significant unfavorable prognostic factor for patients with invasive breast cancer and can potentially serve as a useful prognostic marker for this disease.

title: Murine Dishevelled 3 Functions in Redundant Pathways with Dishevelled 1 and 2 in Normal Cardiac Outflow Tract, Cochlea, and Neural Tube Development
text:
Dvl proteins play a crucial role in signaling pathways that control cell proliferation, cell polarity, and tissue development. Specifically, they are involved in the beta-catenin/Wnt pathway, which regulates cell proliferation and patterning, and the planar cell polarity (PCP) pathway, which coordinates cell polarity within a group of cells and directs tissue narrowing and elongation. In mammals, there are three Dvl genes, and the functions of Dvl1 and Dvl2 have been previously studied. In this study, we investigate the role of Dvl3 in development and find evidence of functional redundancy among the three Dvl genes in mice.

Mice lacking Dvl3 die shortly after birth and exhibit abnormalities in the cardiac outflow tract, including double outlet right ventricle and persistent truncus arteriosus. These mutants also show misorientation of stereocilia in the organ of Corti, a structure in the ear, and this phenotype is worsened when combined with the loss of a single allele of the PCP component Vangl2/Ltap. Although neurulation, the process of neural tube formation, appears normal in both Dvl3 mutants and LtapLp/+ mutants, mice with a combination of Dvl3(+/-) and LtapLp/+ mutations display incomplete neural tube closure.

Importantly, we find that many of the functions of Dvl3 are also carried out by Dvl1 and Dvl2. When Dvl3 mutants are combined with the deficiency of another Dvl gene, more severe phenotypes are observed. Additionally, increasing the dosage of Dvl genes through genetic manipulation shows that Dvls can compensate for each other to ensure normal development. Interestingly, the overall activity of the canonical Wnt signaling pathway, which is regulated by Dvl proteins, does not seem to be significantly affected in the double Dvl mutants. This suggests that low levels of Dvl proteins are sufficient for functional canonical Wnt signals.

In summary, our study demonstrates that Dvl3 is necessary for the development of the cardiac outflow tract and plays a crucial role in the PCP pathway during neurulation and cochlea development. Furthermore, we establish that the three Dvl genes have overlapping functions in various developmental processes.

title: Dynamics of adherens junctions in epithelial establishment, maintenance, and remodeling
text:
The E-cadherin-catenin complex, known as the epithelial cadherin, binds to various components of the cytoskeleton as well as regulatory and signaling molecules. This binding results in the formation of a mature adherens junction (AJ), which serves to physically connect adjacent epithelial cells. Additionally, the AJ couples intercellular adhesive contacts to the cytoskeleton and plays a role in defining the apical-basal axis of each cell. These collective activities are crucial in coordinating the shape, polarity, and function of all cells within an epithelium.

The formation and integrity of the AJ are regulated by several molecules, including Rho family GTPases and Par polarity proteins. However, it is only recently, with the advancement of live-cell imaging, that the active turnover of E-cadherin at junctions has been fully recognized. This turnover process contributes to the formation of junctions and is essential for maintaining the integrity of epithelial tissues during both homeostasis and remodeling.

title: Long-term outcome of patients with asystole induced by head-up tilt test.
text:
The aim of this study was to analyze the long-term outcome of the largest group of patients who experienced asystole during a head-up tilt test. From 1990 onwards, a total of 1322 patients with unexplained syncope underwent tilt-table testing. Out of these patients, 330 (24.9%) had an abnormal response, either syncope or pre-syncope. Among those with an abnormal response, 58 (17.5%) experienced a period of asystole lasting at least 3000 milliseconds during the test. The duration of asystole ranged from 3 to 90 seconds, with a median of 10 seconds. Two different protocols of tilting were used, with 1124 patients tilted at a 60-degree angle and 198 patients tilted at an 80-degree angle using isoproterenol. The tilting protocol influenced the time to the syncopal episode, with a median time of 13 minutes for the 60-degree angle group and 2 minutes for the 80-degree angle group. However, the duration of asystole was not affected by the tilting protocol. 

During the study period, the treatment for asystole went through three stages. Initially, patients were treated with pacemakers. Later, drug therapy with metoprolol and/or etilefrine was recommended. From 1995 onwards, no specific treatment was given for asystole. In a separate study, patients with and without asystole were compared in terms of syncopal recurrences. The follow-up period was 40.7 months for patients with asystole and 51.6 months for patients without asystole. During this time, 20.6% of patients with asystole had syncopal recurrences, while 28.8% of patients without asystole experienced syncopal episodes. The Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no significant difference in the mean time free of recurrence between patients with and without asystole. The number of previous syncopes was found to be a significant factor in predicting recurrences, but therapy did not have a significant impact. There were no deaths related to cardiac issues during the study. 

In conclusion, asystole during a head-up tilt test does not necessarily indicate a serious outcome, and the recurrence of syncope is low. The use of pacemakers or drug therapy does not significantly affect the outcome, which is more closely related to the number of previous syncopal episodes. Gender, age, asystole occurrence, asystole duration, and timing of asystole during the tilt test do not have a significant impact on the outcome. The angle of tilting during the test may influence the time to and incidence of asystole.

title: ZINC 15 – Ligand Discovery for Everyone
text: We have developed a range of tools to bridge the gap between chemoinformatics and biology, making it easier for investigators without computer expertise to access information about the biological activity and availability of small molecules. These tools have been incorporated into ZINC, a platform that offers ligand annotation, purchasability, target, and biology association features. The latest version of ZINC includes a vast collection of over 120 million purchasable "drug-like" compounds, encompassing all organic molecules available for sale. Approximately a quarter of these compounds can be delivered immediately. ZINC not only connects purchasable compounds but also links them to valuable substances like metabolites, drugs, natural products, and annotated compounds from scientific literature. Users can access compounds based on the genes they are annotated with, as well as the major and minor target classes associated with those genes. The platform also provides user-friendly analysis tools that cater to nonspecialists while still offering advanced capabilities for experts. ZINC maintains its original focus on 3D structures, ensuring that all molecules are provided in biologically relevant formats ready for docking. Best of all, ZINC is freely accessible at http://zinc15.docking.org.

title: Condensin-mediated remodeling of the mitotic chromatin landscape in fission yeast
text: The DNA molecules in the eukaryotic genome are much longer than the cells that hold them. They become most compact during mitosis when the chromosomes condense. Condensin, a member of the structural maintenance of chromosomes (SMC) family, assists in this process. However, the exact spatial organization of mitotic chromosomes and how condensin shapes the structure of chromatin is not fully understood. To address this, we utilized chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) to investigate mitotic chromosome condensation in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe. Our findings revealed that the small chromatin domains observed during interphase are replaced by fewer, but larger domains in mitosis. Condensin achieves this by establishing longer-range interactions within the DNA of a single chromosome, resulting in the compaction and individualization of chromosomes. Additionally, condensin restricts local chromatin contacts, which has significant implications for the function of chromatin during mitosis. These results emphasize the crucial role of condensin in altering the chromatin landscape as cells prepare their genomes for cell division.

title: Efficacy of the 6-month thrice-weekly regimen in the treatment of new sputum smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis under clinical trial conditions.
text:
In the context of the Revised National Tuberculosis Control Programme in India, patients diagnosed with new smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis are typically treated with a regimen of antitubercular drugs taken three times a week for a period of six months. In this study, we conducted a retrospective analysis to evaluate the effectiveness and tolerability of this treatment in HIV-negative patients with newly diagnosed smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis.

The data used for this analysis was obtained from two clinical trials conducted between 2001 and 2006 at the National Institute for Research in Tuberculosis in Chennai, India. We specifically focused on patients who were assigned to the control regimen of antitubercular drugs (2H(3)R(3)Z(3)E(3)/4H(3)R(3), where H isoniazid, R rifampicin, Z pyrazinamide, and E ethambutol).

Out of the 268 patients who received this regimen, data on efficacy was available for 249 patients. At the end of the treatment period, 238 out of 249 patients (96%) showed a favorable response. Treatment failure was observed in the remaining 11 patients, with 7 initially having drug-susceptible organisms and 4 having initial drug resistance. Among the 238 patients who responded favorably to treatment, 14 (6%) experienced a recurrence of tuberculosis within the following 24 months.

In the intention-to-treat analysis, 245 out of 262 patients (94%) showed a favorable response at the end of treatment. Among the 28 patients with initial drug resistance, 24 (86%) had a favorable outcome. Only 4 out of these 24 patients experienced a recurrence of tuberculosis during the two-year follow-up period. None of the 7 patients in whom treatment failed or the 10 patients who experienced a recurrence of tuberculosis developed drug resistance among the 221 patients initially infected with drug-susceptible organisms. Additionally, 5 out of the 7 patients in whom treatment failed continued to excrete drug-susceptible bacilli after six months.

Adverse drug reactions were observed in 38 out of 262 patients (14%). However, only 3 patients (1.1%) required a modification in their treatment.

In conclusion, this six-month regimen of antitubercular drugs taken three times a week, when administered under close supervision, has shown a high rate of favorable treatment outcomes in HIV-negative patients with newly diagnosed smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis. Furthermore, adverse drug reactions were minimal in these patients.

title: Curcumin attenuates inflammatory response in IL-1beta-induced human synovial fibroblasts and collagen-induced arthritis in mouse model.
text: The aim of this study was to investigate the potential benefits of curcumin, a compound found in turmeric, in treating collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) and IL-1beta-induced activation in fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLSs). To do this, DBA/1 mice were immunized with bovine type II collagen (CII) and then treated with curcumin every other day for two weeks. The incidence of arthritis and paw thickness were used to assess the severity of the disease. In addition, the proliferation of splenic T cells and the levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-alpha and IL-1beta were measured. The levels of serum IgG1 and IgG2a isotypes were also analyzed. Furthermore, the expression levels of prostaglandin E(2) (PGE(2)), cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), and matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) in human FLSs were examined. The results showed that curcumin treatment reduced the severity of arthritis, suppressed the proliferation of splenic T cells, decreased the levels of TNF-alpha and IL-1beta in the ankle joint, and lowered the levels of IgG2a in the serum. Moreover, curcumin inhibited PGE(2) production, COX-2 expression, and MMP secretion in FLSs by altering nuclear factor (NF)-kappaB transcription activity. These findings suggest that curcumin has anti-inflammatory properties and can regulate immune responses, making it a potential therapeutic option for inflammatory conditions.

title: Loss of IGF-IEa or IGF-IEb impairs myogenic differentiation.
text:
In recent years, there has been increasing interest in understanding the effects of alternative splicing of the Igf1 gene on protein products. However, the significance and functional relevance of these findings are still not well-defined. To investigate the functions of different IGF-I splice variants, we conducted a study on cultured mouse myoblasts to examine the impact of losing IGF-IEa and IGF-IEb on cell proliferation and differentiation.

Through RNA interference, we were able to reduce the levels of total IGF-I, IGF-IEa, or IGF-IEb individually, without affecting cell viability in growth medium. However, we observed that cells lacking total IGF-I or IGF-IEa alone had significantly slower proliferation rates compared to control cells or cells lacking IGF-IEb when cultured in serum-free media. Under differentiation conditions (48 hours in 2% horse serum), the simultaneous loss of both splice variants or the specific loss of either variant resulted in a substantial decrease (70-80%, P < 0.01) in myosin heavy chain (MyHC) immunoreactivity, as confirmed by Western immunoblotting.

This decrease in protein levels was accompanied by a reduction in MyHC isoform mRNAs. Specifically, reductions in total IGF-I or IGF-IEa mRNA led to a significant decrease (approximately 50-75%, P < 0.05) in MyHC mRNAs. Loss of IGF-IEb also caused a significant reduction in MyHC isoform mRNA, except for Myh7, albeit to a lesser extent (around 20-40%, P < 0.05). Interestingly, the provision of mature IGF-I, but not synthetic E peptides, restored Myh3 expression to normal levels in cells lacking IGF-IEa or IGF-IEb.

Based on these findings, it can be inferred that IGF-I splice variants may play a role in regulating myoblast differentiation through the actions of mature IGF-I rather than the E peptides.

title: Antimicrobial peptide pleurocidin synergizes with antibiotics through hydroxyl radical formation and membrane damage, and exerts antibiofilm activity.
text:
BACKGROUND: Pleurocidin is a 25-mer antimicrobial peptide (AMP) that has been found to have bactericidal properties. However, little is known about its synergistic activity and mechanisms when combined with conventional antibiotics, as well as its ability to combat biofilms.

METHODS: We used a checkerboard assay to evaluate the interaction between pleurocidin and antibiotics. To understand the mechanisms behind their synergism, we measured hydroxyl radical formation using 3'-(p-hydroxyphenyl) fluorescein, assessed the NAD(+)/NADH ratio through NAD(+) cycling assay, observed changes in bacterial viability with the hydroxyl radical scavenger thiourea, and investigated cytoplasmic membrane damage using propidium iodide. Additionally, we examined the antibiofilm effect of pleurocidin using the tissue culture plate method.

RESULTS: All combinations of pleurocidin and antibiotics showed synergistic interaction against bacterial strains, except for Enterococcus faecium when treated with a combination of pleurocidin and ampicillin. We found that pleurocidin, both alone and in combination with antibiotics, induced the formation of hydroxyl radicals. This oxidative stress was caused by a temporary depletion of NADH, and the addition of thiourea prevented bacterial death, particularly in the case of the combined treatment of pleurocidin and ampicillin. The combination of pleurocidin and erythromycin also increased the permeability of the bacterial cytoplasmic membrane. Furthermore, pleurocidin demonstrated a strong inhibitory effect on preformed bacterial biofilms.

CONCLUSION: Pleurocidin synergizes with antibiotics through the formation of hydroxyl radicals and a membrane-active mechanism, and it also exhibits antibiofilm activity.

GENERAL SIGNIFICANCE: The synergistic effect between pleurocidin and antibiotics suggests that this AMP could be a potential therapeutic agent and adjuvant for antimicrobial chemotherapy.

title: Outcome of pregnancy in women with moderate or severe renal insufficiency.
text:
BACKGROUND: Pregnant women who have mild preexisting renal disease experience relatively few complications during pregnancy. However, the risks of maternal and obstetrical complications in women with moderate or severe renal insufficiency are still uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a study to determine the frequency and types of maternal and obstetrical complications, as well as the outcomes of pregnancy, in 67 women with primary renal disease (82 pregnancies). All of the women had initial serum creatinine concentrations of at least 1.4 mg per deciliter (124 mumol per liter) and pregnancies that continued beyond the first trimester.

RESULTS: The mean serum creatinine concentration increased from 1.9 +/- 0.8 mg per deciliter (168 +/- 71 mumol per liter) in early pregnancy to 2.5 +/- 1.3 mg per deciliter (221 +/- 115 mumol per liter) in the third trimester. The frequency of hypertension rose from 28 percent at baseline to 48 percent in the third trimester, and the frequency of high-grade proteinuria (urinary protein excretion, > 3000 mg per liter) increased from 23 percent to 41 percent. Among the 70 pregnancies (57 women) for which data were available during pregnancy and immediately postpartum, 43 percent experienced pregnancy-related loss of maternal renal function. In 10 percent of these pregnancies, there was a rapid acceleration of maternal renal insufficiency. Obstetrical complications included a high rate of preterm delivery (59 percent) and growth retardation (37 percent). The infant survival rate was 93 percent.

CONCLUSIONS: Pregnant women with moderate or severe renal insufficiency have increased rates of complications related to worsening renal function, hypertension, and obstetrical issues. However, fetal survival rates remain high.

title: High-mobility group box-1 protein induces osteogenic phenotype changes in aortic valve interstitial cells.
text: The aim of this study was to investigate the involvement of the HMGB1-TLR4 axis in calcific aortic valve (AV) disease and its effect on the pro-osteogenic phenotype change of valvular interstitial cells (VICs). Immunohistochemical staining and immunoblotting were used to evaluate the expression of HMGB1 and TLR4 in human calcific AVs. In vitro experiments were conducted using cultured VICs. The VICs were stimulated with HMGB1 with or without TLR4 siRNA, JNK MAPK and NF-κB inhibitors. The results showed increased accumulation of HMGB1 and TLR4 in calcific valves. HMGB1 induced high levels of pro-inflammatory cytokine production and promoted osteoblastic differentiation and calcification of VICs. It also induced phosphorylation of JNK MAPK and NF-κB, but these effects were suppressed by TLR4 siRNA. Blocking JNK MAPK and NF-κB phosphorylation inhibited HMGB1-induced production of pro-osteogenic factors and mineralization of VICs. In conclusion, the HMGB1 protein may promote osteoblastic differentiation and calcification of VICs through the TLR4-JNK-NF-κB signaling pathway.

title: RiboSys, a high-resolution, quantitative approach to measure the in vivo kinetics of pre-mRNA splicing and 3'-end processing in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
text: We present techniques for accurately measuring RNA processing in budding yeast at a high level of detail. To study gene expression, we created yeast strains with tetON (for induction) and tetOFF (for repression, derepression, and RNA degradation) systems. These strains contained reporter genes integrated into the genome, controlled by a tetO7 promoter. We modified reverse transcription and quantitative real-time PCR (RT-qPCR) methods to determine the abundance of mRNA as the average number of copies per cell in a population. To validate this approach, we used fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) to measure transcript numbers in individual cells, confirming the accuracy of the RT-qPCR method despite variations in transcript levels within the cell population. Additionally, we used RT-qPCR to differentiate between the different steps in splicing of the reporter transcripts, and developed techniques to map and quantify 3'-end cleavage and polyadenylation. This system allows for the quantitative monitoring of pre-mRNA production, splicing, 3'-end maturation, and degradation with precise kinetic detail, making it suitable for mathematical modeling. Using this approach, we demonstrate that reporter transcripts are spliced before undergoing 3'-end cleavage and polyadenylation, indicating cotranscriptional processing.

title: Generation of mice with a conditional allele for the p75(NTR) neurotrophin receptor gene.
text:
The p75(NTR) neurotrophin receptor has been linked to various biological and pathological processes. Although progress has been made in understanding its physiological function, there are still many details and aspects that need to be determined. This is partly due to the limitations of the current knockout mouse models, which have deletions in either Exons 3 or 4 and exhibit features that make definitive conclusions difficult.

In this study, we present the creation of mice carrying a conditional p75(NTR) allele (p75(NTR-FX)) by flanking Exons 4-6, which encode the transmembrane and cytoplasmic domains, with loxP sites. To validate this new conditional allele, we generated both neural crest-specific p75(NTR)/Wnt1-Cre mutants and conventional p75(NTR) null mutants. Both mutant mice showed abnormal hind limb reflexes, suggesting that the loss of p75(NTR) in neural crest-derived cells leads to a peripheral neuropathy similar to that observed in conventional p75(NTR) mutants.

This novel conditional p75(NTR) allele provides exciting opportunities to investigate the role of p75(NTR) in specific tissues and cells.

title: A Triple-Stain Flow Cytometric Method to Assess Plasma- and Acrosome-Membrane Integrity of Cryopreserved Bovine Sperm Immediately after Thawing in Presence of Egg-Yolk Particles1
text: This study aimed to develop a new triple-stain combination for the simultaneous evaluation of postthaw viability and acrosome integrity of bovine sperm using flow cytometry. The combination of SYBR-14 and propidium iodide (PI) allowed for the discrimination of sperm cells from egg yolk and debris particles, eliminating the need for washing steps. Additionally, phycoerythrin-conjugated peanut agglutinin (PE-PNA) was used to differentiate acrosome-damaged/reacted sperm cells from acrosome-intact cells. Repeatability was assessed using two processed ejaculates from 10 bulls, with three straws per batch analyzed in duplicate measurements. Method-agreement analysis compared the new combination to fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC)-conjugated PNA staining. The new combination showed a repeatability index of 2.6% and provided a more accurate estimate of intact head membrane and acrosome compared to FITC-PNA staining. Overall, the new triple-stain combination is highly repeatable and suitable for routine use in assessing sperm viability and acrosome integrity.

title: Universal voluntary HIV testing with immediate antiretroviral therapy as a strategy for elimination of HIV transmission: a mathematical model.
text:
CONTEXT At the end of 2007, approximately 3 million individuals worldwide were receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART) for HIV, but there were still an estimated 6.7 million people in need of treatment. Additionally, 2.7 million new HIV infections occurred in 2007. While prevention efforts can help reduce HIV incidence, completely eliminating the disease is unlikely. In this study, we explored the potential impact of a theoretical strategy involving universal voluntary HIV testing and immediate treatment with ART, aiming to drive the HIV epidemic towards elimination.

METHODS To assess the effects of this strategy, we utilized mathematical models. These models examined the case reproduction number (stochastic model) and long-term dynamics of the HIV epidemic (deterministic transmission model) when all individuals aged 15 years and older in a test-case community were tested for HIV annually and immediately started on ART upon diagnosis. We used data from South Africa as a representative example of a generalized epidemic, assuming that all HIV transmission occurred through heterosexual contact.

RESULTS Our findings suggest that implementing this strategy could significantly expedite the transition from the current endemic phase, where most HIV-positive adults do not receive ART, to an elimination phase where the majority are on treatment within five years. By 2016, or within ten years of full implementation, this approach could reduce HIV incidence and mortality to less than one case per 1000 people per year. Furthermore, it could decrease the prevalence of HIV to less than 1% within 50 years. We projected that by 2032, the annual cost of both the present strategy and the theoretical strategy would be $1.7 billion. However, beyond this point, the cost of the present strategy would continue to rise while the cost of the theoretical strategy would decrease.

CONCLUSION Universal voluntary HIV testing and immediate ART, in conjunction with existing prevention methods, could have a significant impact on severe generalized HIV/AIDS epidemics. Further mathematical modeling, research, and extensive consultation are necessary to explore the potential of this approach.

title: Common variants in DGKK are strongly associated with risk of hypospadias
text: Hypospadias is a common birth defect affecting the male external genitalia. To investigate its genetic basis, we conducted a study using DNA samples from 436 individuals with hypospadias (cases) and 494 individuals without the condition (controls) of European descent. We identified two specific genetic variations (rs1934179 and rs7063116) in the DGKK gene, which encodes diacylglycerol kinase κ, that were strongly associated with hypospadias. This association was confirmed in additional samples from the Netherlands and Sweden. Furthermore, our expression studies revealed that DGKK expression in the preputial tissue was lower in individuals carrying the risk allele of rs1934179. Based on these findings, we propose that DGKK is a major risk gene for hypospadias.

title: Neutrophils Suppress Intraluminal NK Cell-Mediated Tumor Cell Clearance and Enhance Extravasation of Disseminated Carcinoma Cells.
text: The roles of immune cells in promoting the spread of carcinoma cells from primary tumors are not well understood beyond the initial stages of metastasis. In this study, we uncover new functions of neutrophils in aiding the survival and movement of tumor cells during metastatic dissemination. We find that neutrophils, specifically those expressing CD11b and Ly6G, enhance the formation of metastases through two distinct mechanisms. Firstly, neutrophils inhibit the function of natural killer cells, resulting in a longer survival time for tumor cells within blood vessels. Additionally, neutrophils facilitate the movement of tumor cells out of blood vessels through the secretion of IL1β and matrix metalloproteinases. These findings highlight the important role of neutrophils in promoting the survival and movement of tumor cells during metastasis, and their interaction with both host cells and disseminating carcinoma cells. This study provides valuable insights into the systemic contributions of neutrophils to cancer metastasis by elucidating their involvement in intermediate steps of the invasion-metastasis cascade. We demonstrate that neutrophils suppress the activity of natural killer cells and increase the extravasation of tumor cells.

title: High Km soluble 5'-nucleotidase from human placenta. Properties and allosteric regulation by IMP and ATP.
text: An 8000-fold purification of a human placental soluble "high Km" 5'-nucleotidase was achieved using AMP-Sepharose affinity chromatography, resulting in a specific activity of 25.6 mumol/min/mg. The enzyme has a subunit molecular mass of 53 kDa and a native molecular mass of 210 kDa, indicating a tetrameric structure. It exhibits the highest activity with IMP and GMP, as well as their deoxy derivatives. IMP is hydrolyzed 15 times faster than AMP. The enzyme is highly dependent on magnesium ions and is regulated by them. Purine nucleoside 5'-triphosphates, particularly dATP, ATP, and GTP, strongly activate the enzyme. Additionally, 2,3-Diphosphoglycerate activates the enzyme as effectively as ATP. The presence of three millimolar ATP decreases the Km for IMP from 0.33 to 0.09 mM and increases the Vmax by 12-fold. The activation of ATP is influenced by the concentration of IMP. At 20 microM IMP, the ATP-dependent activation curve is sigmoidal, while at 2 mM IMP, it becomes hyperbolic. The A0.5 values for ATP are 2.26 and 0.70 mM, and the relative maximal velocities are 32.9 and 126.0 nmol/min, respectively. The addition of inorganic phosphate changes the substrate velocity relationship for IMP from hyperbolic to sigmoidal. Under physiological conditions (3 mM ATP, 1-4 mM Pi, 150 mM KCl, pH 7.4), the enzyme is 25-35 times more active towards 100 microM IMP compared to 100 microM AMP. These findings indicate that: (a) the soluble human placental high Km 5'-nucleotidase coexists with the low Km enzyme in the human placenta; (b) the enzyme prefers the hydrolysis of IMP and is significantly regulated by IMP, ATP, and Pi levels; and (c) the kinetic properties of ATP and IMP are mutually influenced, suggesting a complex interaction between their associated binding sites.

title: Histones are incorporated in trans during reassembly of the yeast PHO5 promoter.
text: In yeast, when the PHO5 promoter chromatin is activated, it undergoes remodeling accompanied by temporary hyperacetylation and subsequent removal of histones from the promoter in a trans manner. During the process of repressing the promoter again, nucleosomes need to be reassembled on it. We have investigated the origin of the histones used to rebuild the inactive promoter chromatin. By using a strain with two different versions of histone H3, each with distinct tags and regulations, we were able to distinguish between histones derived from the chromatin fraction and those originating from the soluble histone pool. Our findings demonstrate that the incorporated histones come from an external source. The closure of the promoter happens rapidly, and the histone chaperones Asf1 and Hir1, as well as the SWI/SNF nucleosome remodeling complex, play crucial roles in the swift reassembly of nucleosomes at the PHO5 promoter.

title: National study of physician awareness and adherence to cardiovascular disease prevention guidelines.
text:
BACKGROUND: Limited data exist on how well physicians adhere to cardiovascular disease (CVD) prevention guidelines based on their specialty or patient characteristics, particularly gender.

METHODS AND RESULTS: A study was conducted online, involving 500 randomly selected physicians (300 primary care physicians, 100 obstetricians/gynecologists, and 100 cardiologists). A standardized questionnaire was used to assess their awareness of, adoption of, and barriers to national CVD prevention guidelines based on their specialty. An experimental case study design was used to test physician accuracy and factors influencing the assignment of CVD risk levels and application of guidelines for high-, intermediate-, and low-risk patients. Primary care physicians were more likely to assign intermediate-risk women, as determined by the Framingham risk score, to a lower-risk category compared to men with identical risk profiles (P<0.0001). Similar trends were observed among obstetricians/gynecologists and cardiologists. The assignment of risk level significantly influenced recommendations for lifestyle changes and preventive pharmacotherapy. After adjusting for risk assignment, the impact of patient gender on preventive care was not significant, except for less aspirin being recommended (P<0.01) and more weight management being advised (P<0.04) for intermediate-risk women. Physicians did not rate themselves as highly effective in helping patients prevent CVD. Less than 20% of physicians were aware that more women than men die from CVD each year.

CONCLUSIONS: The perception of risk was the main factor influencing CVD preventive recommendations. Gender disparities in recommendations for preventive therapy were largely due to the lower perceived risk for women, despite similar calculated risk compared to men. Educational interventions for physicians are necessary to improve the quality of CVD preventive care and reduce morbidity and mortality from CVD in both men and women.

title: TECHNICAL ADVANCE Floral dip: a simplified method for Agrobacterium-mediated
text: The Agrobacterium vacuum infiltration method has revolutionized the transformation of Arabidopsis thaliana, eliminating the need for plant tissue culture or regeneration. In this study, we evaluated and developed a significantly modified transformation method. We replaced the labor-intensive vacuum infiltration process with a simple dipping technique, where developing floral tissues were dipped into a solution containing Agrobacterium tumefaciens, 5% sucrose, and 500 microliters per liter of surfactant Silwet L-77. The presence of sucrose and surfactant proved crucial for the success of the floral dip method. We found that the highest transformation rate was achieved when plants were inoculated with numerous immature floral buds and few siliques. We discovered that plant tissue culture media, the hormone benzylamino purine, and pH adjustment were unnecessary, and Agrobacterium could be applied to plants at various cell densities. By repeatedly applying Agrobacterium, we were able to improve transformation rates and overall yield of transformants by approximately twofold. Additionally, covering plants for 1 day after inoculation to retain humidity resulted in a twofold increase in transformation rates. This modified method was successful in transforming multiple ecotypes. Overall, this modified method will greatly facilitate high-throughput transformation of Arabidopsis for various research purposes, including T-DNA gene tagging, positional cloning, and targeted gene replacement.

title: Pathway connectivity and signaling coordination in the yeast stress-activated signaling network
text: The response of stressed cells involves various physiological levels, but our understanding of the complete stress-activated regulatory network and the principles of signal integration is still incomplete. To address this, we developed an experimental and computational approach that combines protein interaction data, gene fitness contributions, mutant transcriptome profiles, and phospho-proteome changes in cells under salt stress. By doing so, we were able to infer the salt-responsive signaling network in yeast. This inferred subnetwork provided several new predictions, including the identification of new regulators, the discovery of previously unknown crosstalk between known pathways, and the identification of previously unrecognized 'hubs' of signal integration. One of our key findings was that the Cdc14 phosphatase plays a central role in the network, and that modification of RNA polymerase II coordinates the induction of stress-defense genes with the reduction of growth-related transcripts. Additionally, we found that the human network, which shares similarities with the yeast network, is enriched for cancer-causing genes, highlighting the importance of our subnetwork predictions in understanding stress biology.

title: Premigratory and migratory neural crest cells are multipotent in vivo.
text: The neural crest (NC) is a group of cells in the embryo that can develop into various types of cells, such as peripheral neurons, myelinating Schwann cells, and melanocytes. However, there has been a debate about whether each individual NC cell has the ability to develop into multiple cell types or if the NC is made up of different types of cells that can only develop into specific lineages. To settle this debate, we conducted experiments using the R26R-Confetti mouse model to track the fate of single NC cells at different stages of development. By analyzing the cells and using markers to identify their differentiation, we found that most individual NC cells are indeed capable of developing into multiple cell types, with only a small number of cells contributing to a single lineage. Interestingly, even as the NC cells migrate, they still maintain their ability to develop into different cell types. Therefore, our findings provide conclusive evidence that both premigratory and migrating NC cells in mice are multipotent.

title: Implementing the ESHRE 'poor responder' criteria in research studies: methodological implications.
text: The Bologna criteria, which are used to define poor ovarian response (POR) in IVF, offer a valuable framework for further research in the field of assisted conception. However, it can be challenging to design studies based on the POR criteria set by the European Society for Human Reproduction and Embryology, as this new definition encompasses various subpopulations with different baseline characteristics and unknown clinical prognosis. If women from each subpopulation are not evenly distributed among intervention groups, potential bias in the results may arise when conducting randomized controlled trials (RCTs). In smaller or moderate-sized RCTs, a single-sequence randomization method may not guarantee balanced allocation between groups. To address this issue, stratified randomization methods can be employed as an alternative approach. Depending on the chosen methodology, it may be more appropriate to report patient characteristics and outcomes within each intervention group based on the relevant subpopulations.

title: Generation of gene-edited rats by delivery of CRISPR/Cas9 protein and donor DNA into intact zygotes using electroporation
text: We have successfully optimized an electroporation method for intact rat zygotes, which offers a more efficient and time-saving alternative to the traditional microinjection technique used for generating gene-edited animals using the CRISPRs/Cas9 system. This method requires high technical skills and is known to be inefficient. By utilizing sgRNAs and Cas9 protein, along with ssODNs (~100 nt), we achieved a high frequency of knockouts, ranging from 15 to 50% of the analyzed animals. Notably, when using ssODNs as a donor template, we were able to achieve precise knock-in mutations in 25-100% of the analyzed animals, which is comparable to the results obtained through microinjection. Despite the visualization of dsDNA within the zygotes, the electroporation of long ssDNA or dsDNA donors, previously successful in microinjection, did not result in the generation of genome-edited animals. Therefore, the simultaneous electroporation of a large number of intact rat zygotes represents a rapid, simple, and efficient method for generating a variety of genome-edited rats.

title: Uridylation of miRNAs by HEN1 SUPPRESSOR1 in Arabidopsis
text: The HEN1 enzyme plays a crucial role in protecting plant microRNAs (miRNAs), small interfering RNAs (siRNAs), and animal piwi-interacting RNAs (piRNAs) from degradation and 3' terminal uridylation. However, the enzymes responsible for uridylating unmethylated miRNAs, siRNAs, or piRNAs in hen1 are currently unknown. In this study, a genetic screen identified a mutation called hen1 suppressor1-2 (heso1-2), which partially suppresses the morphological effects of the hypomorphic hen1-2 allele and the null hen1-1 allele in Arabidopsis. The HESO1 gene was found to encode a terminal nucleotidyl transferase that adds untemplated uridine to the 3' end of RNA, a process that is completely inhibited by 2'-O-methylation. The heso1-2 mutation affects the profile of u-tailed miRNAs and siRNAs, leading to an increase in truncated and/or normal-sized molecules in hen1. This often results in an overall increase in the total amount of miRNAs and siRNAs in hen1. Conversely, overexpressing HESO1 in hen1-2 leads to more severe morphological defects and reduced miRNA accumulation. These findings demonstrate that HESO1 is responsible for uridylating unmethylated miRNAs and siRNAs in hen1. Additionally, the study suggests that uridylation may destabilize unmethylated miRNAs through an unknown mechanism and compete with 3'-to-5' exoribonuclease activities in hen1. These findings may have implications for understanding piRNA uridylation in hen1 in animals.

title: Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis to Prevent HIV Infection: Current Status, Future Opportunities and Challenges
text: In order to combat the global HIV epidemic, it is crucial to implement effective interventions that can reduce transmission rates. Studies have shown that daily oral antiretroviral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), using a combination tablet containing tenofovir disoproxil fumarate and emtricitabine, can significantly decrease the incidence of HIV among various at-risk populations. The success of PrEP is closely linked to adherence levels. Official guidelines recommend offering PrEP to those at the highest risk of acquiring HIV, and real-world projects have demonstrated that high levels of uptake and adherence are achievable outside of controlled studies. However, there are still obstacles to overcome in implementing PrEP. These challenges include low awareness and utilization of PrEP among at-risk individuals, uncertainty about adherence in real-life situations, a lack of training among healthcare providers in providing PrEP, limited data on potential long-term side effects of tenofovir-emtricitabine, high costs of PrEP medications, and the stigma associated with PrEP use and the behaviors that warrant it. Innovative approaches in pharmacologic chemoprophylaxis could help address some of these challenges. Less frequent oral dosing regimens and long-acting injectable medications could reduce the burden of taking pills and improve adherence. Additionally, local delivery of PrEP medications to genital areas through gels, rings, and films may limit systemic drug exposure and potential toxicities. As the range of chemoprophylactic agents and delivery systems expands to meet the diverse sexual health needs and preferences of individuals who could benefit from PrEP, it is hoped that antiretroviral chemoprophylaxis will become an acceptable, feasible, and highly effective addition to existing HIV prevention strategies.

title: Prepregnancy BMI and the risk of gestational diabetes: a systematic review of the literature with meta-analysis.
text: The aim of this study is to evaluate and quantify the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) based on the mother's body mass index (BMI) before pregnancy. The study design involves a systematic review of observational studies published within the past 30 years. We conducted a search of four electronic databases for publications between 1977 and 2007. BMI was chosen as the sole measure of obesity, and all diagnostic criteria for GDM were considered. Studies that used selective screening for GDM were excluded, and there were no language restrictions. We assessed the methodological quality of the primary studies. A total of 1745 citations were reviewed, and we included 70 studies (including two unpublished studies) involving 671,945 women (59 cohorts and 11 case-controls). Most of the studies were of high or medium quality. In comparison to women with a normal BMI, the unadjusted pooled odds ratio (OR) for underweight women developing GDM was 0.75 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.69 to 0.82). The OR for overweight, moderately obese, and morbidly obese women were 1.97 (95% CI 1.77 to 2.19), 3.01 (95% CI 2.34 to 3.87), and 5.55 (95% CI 4.27 to 7.21), respectively. For every 1 kg/m² increase in BMI, the prevalence of GDM increased by 0.92% (95% CI 0.73 to 1.10). The risk of GDM is positively correlated with prepregnancy BMI. This information is crucial for counseling women who are planning a pregnancy.

title: Multiple risk behaviour: increasing socio-economic gap over time?
text: In this study, we examined the relationship between education and lifestyle, specifically a cluster of unhealthy behaviors. Our goal was to assess how socio-economic changes impact multiple risk behaviors over time. We analyzed cross-sectional data from the Belgian Health Interview Surveys conducted in 1997, 2001, and 2004. The study included individuals aged 15 years and older who provided information on their health behaviors and education (n = 7431, n = 8142, and n = 7459, respectively). We created a lifestyle index based on four unhealthy behaviors: smoking, risky alcohol use, sedentary behavior, and poor diet. The index was divided into low (0-2) and high (3-4) categories. To measure socio-economic inequalities in multiple risk behavior, we calculated summary measures such as Odds Ratio (OR) and Relative Index of Inequality (RII) using logistic regression, stratified by sex. Our findings showed that 7.5% of the adult population engaged in three to four unhealthy behaviors, with lower educated men being the most at risk. Additionally, the OR among men significantly increased from 1.6 in 2001 to 3.4 in 2004 (P = 0.029), indicating a growing disparity. The increase in OR among women was less pronounced. However, the RII did not show any gradient for either men or women. In conclusion, multiple risk behavior is more prevalent among lower educated individuals, and there is an increasing polarization in socio-economic inequalities among men from 2001 to 2004. Therefore, health promotion programs should target the lower socio-economic classes and address multiple risk behaviors simultaneously.

title: Variations and Trends in Health Burden of Visual Impairment Due to Cataract: A Global Analysis.
text:
Objective: This study aims to assess the worldwide trends in the health burden of cataract-related vision loss, measured in disability-adjusted life years (DALY), and its relationship with national levels of socioeconomic development.

Methods: Data on global, regional, and national DALY numbers, crude rates, and age-standardized rates of cataract-related vision loss by age and sex were obtained from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2015 database. Socioeconomic variables such as the human development index (HDI) and per capita gross domestic product (GDP) were derived from international open databases. Regression analysis was conducted to examine the correlations between age-standardized DALY rates and socioeconomic factors.

Results: The global DALY numbers for cataract-related vision loss increased by 89.42% from 1990 to 2015, rising from 2048.18 (95% CI: 1457.60-2761.80) thousands to 3879.74 (95% CI: 2766.07-5232.43) thousands (P < 0.001). After adjusting for age and country, females had higher DALY numbers (315.83, 95% CI: 237.17-394.4) and crude rates (38.29, 95% CI: 35.35-41.23) (all P < 0.001). The age-standardized DALY rate was higher in countries with lower HDI, with rates of 91.03 (95% CI: 73.04-108.75) for low HDI, 81.67 (95% CI: 53.24-108.82) for medium HDI, 55.89 (95% CI: 36.87-69.63) for high HDI, and 17.10 (95% CI: 13.91-26.84) for very high HDI countries (P < 0.01). In 2015, the national age-standardized DALY rates were negatively associated with both HDI (R2 = 0.489, P < 0.001) and per capita GDP (R2 = 0.331, P < 0.001). Stepwise multiple regression analysis revealed that HDI remained significantly correlated with national age-standardized DALY rates in 2015 after adjusting for other confounding factors (P < 0.001).

Conclusion: Despite efforts from the World Health Organization and VISION 2020 initiatives, the global health burden of cataract-related vision loss has increased between 1990 and 2015. This burden is higher in countries with lower levels of socioeconomic development, as measured by HDI.

title: Multiplex genome engineering using CRISPR/Cas systems.
text: To understand the function of specific genetic variants and elements, it is crucial to have advanced genome editing technologies. The CRISPR/Cas system, derived from prokaryotes, has proven to be effective in guiding RNA to cleave DNA at specific sites. In our study, we modified two different CRISPR/Cas systems and successfully demonstrated that Cas9 nucleases can be guided by short RNAs to precisely cleave DNA at specific locations in human and mouse cells. Additionally, we found that Cas9 can be transformed into a nicking enzyme, which aids in repairing DNA with minimal mutagenic effects. Furthermore, we discovered that multiple guide sequences can be incorporated into a single CRISPR array, allowing for simultaneous editing of multiple sites in the mammalian genome. This highlights the versatility and ease of use of RNA-guided nuclease technology.

title: Transformation of intact yeast cells treated with alkali cations.
text: Yeast cells that were treated with alkali cations and remained intact were able to absorb plasmid DNA. The alkali cations Li+, Cs+, Rb+, K+, and Na+ were all effective in inducing competence. The transformation process of Saccharomyces cerevisiae D13-1A with plasmid YRp7 was thoroughly examined using CsCl. It was found that the optimal incubation time was 1 hour, and the ideal cell concentration was 5 x 10(7) cells per ml. The optimal concentration of Cs+ was determined to be 1.0 M. The efficiency of transformation increased as the concentration of plasmid DNA increased. The presence of polyethylene glycol was absolutely necessary for the process. The uptake of plasmid DNA was enhanced by a heat pulse, as well as various polyamines or basic proteins. In addition to circular DNA, Cs+-treated yeast cells were also able to absorb linear plasmid DNA, although the efficiency of uptake was significantly reduced. The transformation efficiency achieved with Cs+ or Li+ was comparable to that of traditional protoplast methods for a plasmid containing ars1, but not for plasmids containing a 2 microns origin replication.

title: Health-Related Quality of Life as Measured with EQ-5D among Populations with and without Specific Chronic Conditions: A Population-Based Survey in Shaanxi Province, China
text:
The purpose of this study was to analyze the health-related quality of life (HRQoL) using the EQ-5D measurement tool, and to explore the impact of chronic conditions and other risk factors on HRQoL in a sample from Shaanxi Province, China. 

A multi-stage stratified cluster sampling method was used to select participants for the study. The EQ-5D was used to assess HRQoL. The likelihood of individuals with specific chronic diseases reporting problems in the EQ-5D dimensions was calculated and compared to two reference groups. Multivariable linear regression models were employed to identify factors associated with EQ VAS scores. 

The most commonly reported problems were pain/discomfort (8.8%) and anxiety/depression (7.6%). Almost half of the respondents who reported problems in any of the five dimensions were chronic patients. Higher EQ VAS scores were associated with being male, having a higher level of education, being employed, being younger, living in an urban area, having access to free medical services, and engaging in higher levels of physical activity. With the exception of anemia, all selected chronic diseases were associated with lower EQ VAS scores. The three main risk factors were cerebrovascular disease, cancer, and mental disease. Age, number of chronic conditions, and frequency of physical activity showed a gradient effect on HRQoL. 

These findings contribute to our understanding of the health status of the population in this region, beyond what can be determined from mortality and morbidity data. It is important for medical, policy, social, and individual attention to be focused on managing chronic diseases and improving HRQoL. Longitudinal studies should be conducted to monitor changes in HRQoL and evaluate the effectiveness of interventions for chronic diseases.

title: Memory and Modularity in Cell-Fate Decision Making
text: Cells that are genetically identical and share the same environment can exhibit different characteristics. It is often unclear whether this variation is due to chance, external signals, or the individual cells' attempts to control their own characteristics. To understand this, we observed thousands of cells over hundreds of generations in a controlled environment. Specifically, we studied the decision-making process between a solitary, moving state and a connected, stationary state in Bacillus subtilis. Our findings reveal that the moving state has no memory and does not have autonomous control over the duration of this state. On the other hand, the time spent in the connected state is tightly regulated, ensuring coordination among related cells in the multicellular state. We also discovered that the regulatory circuit involving three proteins that govern this decision is modular, with the initiation and maintenance of the connected state being separate functions. Additionally, we found that stimulating the same pathway that initiates the connected state leads to the formation of biofilms. This suggests that autonomous timing allows cells to make a trial commitment to multicellularity, which can be extended by external signals.

title: Lpd depletion reveals that SRF specifies radial versus tangential migration of pyramidal neurons
text: During the process of corticogenesis, the majority of cortical neurons, known as pyramidal neurons, originate from the ventricular zone. They undergo a transformation from a multipolar stage to a bipolar stage and attach themselves to radial glia. Subsequently, these neurons migrate to their appropriate positions within the cortex. As they migrate radially, pyramidal neurons remain connected to their glial substrate while passing through the subventricular and intermediate zones. These regions are abundant in tangentially migrating interneurons and axon fiber tracts. Our study focused on investigating the role of lamellipodin (Lpd), which is similar to a crucial regulator of neuronal migration and polarization in Caenorhabditis elegans, in the process of corticogenesis. Depletion of Lpd resulted in bipolar pyramidal neurons adopting a tangential migration mode instead of the usual radial-glial mode, without affecting their ultimate fate. Mechanistically, Lpd depletion led to a decrease in the activity of SRF, a transcription factor that is regulated by changes in the ratio of polymerized to unpolymerized actin. Consequently, the absence of Lpd revealed the involvement of SRF in guiding pyramidal neurons to choose a radial migration pathway along glia, rather than a tangential migration mode.

title: Identification of p18 INK4c as a tumor suppressor gene in glioblastoma multiforme.
text: The pathogenesis of many common human tumor types is driven by genomic alterations that cause abnormal activation of cyclin/cyclin-dependent kinase (cdk) complexes. In the case of glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), these alterations are most frequently caused by the complete deletion of p16(INK4a), and less commonly by amplifications of specific genes that encode cyclins or cdks. In this study, we present the deletion of the p18(INK4c) cdk inhibitor as a new genetic alteration that drives the development of GBM. Deletions of p18(INK4c) often occurred in tumors that also had complete deletions of p16(INK4a). Immunohistochemistry analysis showed that p18(INK4c) expression was completely absent in 43% of primary GBM tumors. When p18(INK4c) expression was reintroduced at normal levels in GBM cells lacking p18(INK4c), it resulted in a senescence-like G(1) cell cycle arrest. These findings establish p18(INK4c) as a tumor suppressor gene in GBM, providing further insight into the mechanisms that lead to abnormal activation of cyclin/cdk complexes in this devastating malignancy.

title: Two-stage control of an oxidative stress regulon: the Escherichia coli SoxR protein triggers redox-inducible expression of the soxS regulatory gene.
text:
Escherichia coli responds to oxidative stress caused by superoxide-generating agents like paraquat by activating the synthesis of approximately 80 polypeptides. The expression of a specific group of these proteins is controlled at the transcriptional level by the soxRS locus, also known as the soxRS regulon. A two-stage control system was proposed for soxRS, where an intracellular redox signal would trigger the SoxR protein to act as a transcriptional activator for the soxS gene. The increased levels of SoxS protein would then activate the transcription of various genes within the soxRS regulon (B. Demple and C.F. Amábile Cuevas, Cell 67:837-839, 1990).

To monitor soxS transcription, we have created operon fusions of the E. coli lac genes with the soxS promoter. The expression from the soxS promoter is highly inducible by paraquat, but this induction strictly depends on the presence of a functional soxR gene. Other superoxide-generating agents also trigger soxR(+)-dependent soxS expression, and the inductions by paraquat and phenazine methosulfate require the presence of oxygen. However, various other oxidative stress agents like H2O2, gamma rays, and heat shock do not induce soxS expression. Interestingly, aerobic growth of bacteria lacking superoxide dismutase leads to soxR-dependent soxS expression. These findings suggest the existence of a specific redox signal for soxS induction.

The involvement of SoxR protein in the activation of the soxS gene is supported by band-shift and DNase I footprinting experiments. These experiments demonstrate that the SoxR protein in cell extracts specifically binds to the soxS promoter. The manner in which SoxR binds to DNA appears to be similar to its homolog MerR, as the SoxR footprint spans the -10 to -35 region of the soxS promoter.

title: Air pollution and cardiovascular disease: a statement for healthcare professionals from the Expert Panel on Population and Prevention Science of the American Heart Association.
text: Air pollution is a complex and varied mixture of gases, liquids, and particles. Numerous studies have shown that exposure to current levels of ambient particulate matter increases the risk of cardiovascular events in both the short and long term. Various mechanisms have been proposed to explain this relationship, including increased blood clotting, irregular heart rhythms, narrowed arteries, inflammation throughout the body, and the long-term development of artery-clogging plaque. The purpose of this statement is to provide healthcare professionals and regulatory agencies with a comprehensive overview of the research on air pollution and cardiovascular disease. It also discusses the implications of these findings for public health and regulatory policies. Practical recommendations for healthcare providers and their patients are provided, and suggestions for future research are offered to address remaining scientific questions.

title: Non-invasive ventilation in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease patients: helmet versus facial mask
text: The helmet is a new device that has the potential to improve the success rate of non-invasive ventilation by enhancing tolerance. We conducted a study to compare the physiological effects of the helmet and the conventional facial mask in delivering non-invasive ventilation to hypercapnic patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. This was a prospective, controlled, randomized study with a cross-over design. We evaluated gas exchange, inspiratory effort, patient-ventilator synchrony, and patient tolerance in 10 patients after 30 minutes of non-invasive ventilation using either the helmet or facial mask. Both trials were preceded by periods of spontaneous unassisted breathing. We measured arterial blood gases, inspiratory effort, duration of diaphragm contraction and ventilator assistance, effort-to-support delays (at the beginning and end of inspiration), number of ineffective efforts, and patient comfort. Non-invasive ventilation improved gas exchange (p<0.05) and inspiratory effort (p<0.01) with both interfaces. However, the helmet was less effective than the mask in reducing inspiratory effort (p<0.05) and worsened patient-ventilator synchrony, as indicated by longer delays to trigger on (p<0.05) and cycle off (p<0.05) the mechanical assistance, as well as the number of ineffective efforts (p<0.005). Patient comfort was similar with both interfaces. Both the helmet and facial mask were well tolerated and effective in improving gas exchange and reducing inspiratory effort. However, the helmet was less efficient in reducing inspiratory effort and negatively impacted patient-ventilator interaction.

title: Case Management and Client Access to Health and Social Services in Outpatient Substance Abuse Treatment
text: The main objective of case management is to coordinate services across different treatment settings and integrate substance abuse services with other community services such as housing, mental health, medical, and social services. However, case management is a complex concept that includes various important aspects, such as the extent of coverage, the level of control over the referral process, and the location of case management activities (on-site, off-site, or both). This research aims to explore the connection between specific dimensions of case management and the utilization of health and additional social services in outpatient substance abuse treatment. Overall, the findings indicate that a more proactive approach to case management during the referral process, as well as providing case management both on-site and off-site, aligns with our expectations of increased use of health and ancillary social services by substance abuse clients. However, these effects are primarily observed in relation to general healthcare and mental health services. Case management seems to have minimal impact on the utilization of social services or aftercare plans.

title: Evidence that the Ipl1-Sli15 (Aurora Kinase-INCENP) Complex Promotes Chromosome Bi-orientation by Altering Kinetochore-Spindle Pole Connections
text: The mechanism by which sister kinetochores attach to microtubules from opposite spindle poles during mitosis (known as bi-orientation) is not well understood. In yeast, the Aurora B-INCENP protein kinase complex (Ipl1-Sli15), which is similar to its human counterpart, may play a crucial role in this process. It is believed that this complex is necessary to prevent the attachment of sister kinetochores to microtubules from the same spindle pole. To investigate the function of IPL1, we conducted experiments using cells that were unable to replicate their chromosomes but still duplicated their spindle pole bodies (SPBs). In cells with the IPL1 gene present, kinetochores detached from old SPBs and reattached to both old and new SPBs with equal frequency. However, in cells lacking the IPL1 gene, kinetochores remained attached to old SPBs. This suggests that Ipl1-Sli15 may facilitate bi-orientation by promoting the turnover of connections between kinetochores and SPBs until tension is created in the surrounding chromatin, causing sister kinetochores to be pulled towards opposite spindle poles.

title: CRITICAL REVIEW Cutaneous Vasculitis Update: Diagnostic Criteria,
text: Vasculitis is the inflammation of the vessel wall, which can lead to the destruction of the wall itself, resulting in hemorrhage, aneurysm formation, and tissue infarction. It can also cause intimal-medial hyperplasia, leading to stenosis and tissue ischemia. The skin is particularly susceptible to vasculitis due to its large vascular bed, exposure to cold temperatures, and frequent stasis. There are various types of vasculitic syndromes that can affect the skin, ranging from localized and self-limiting to generalized and life-threatening with multi-organ involvement. To accurately diagnose cutaneous vasculitis and rule out other conditions that mimic its symptoms, a biopsy confirmation is necessary. The biopsy should identify acute signs of vasculitis such as fibrinoid necrosis, chronic signs like endarteritis obliterans, or past signs such as the presence of an acellular scar from healed arteritis. Additionally, the presence of extravascular findings like patterned fibrosis or collagenolytic granulomas should be noted. While some cases of vasculitis can be attributed to a specific cause, many cases have no identifiable cause, and a single cause can result in different expressions of the disease. Therefore, the classification of cutaneous vasculitis is best determined by examining the size of the affected vessels and the principal inflammatory response. These histologic patterns roughly correspond to the underlying mechanisms of the disease. By combining this information with direct immunofluorescent examination, anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA) status, and findings from a systemic disease work-up, a specific diagnosis can be made, leading to more effective treatment. In this review, we will discuss the diagnostic criteria, classification, epidemiology, etiology, pathogenesis, and evaluation of patients with cutaneous vasculitis.

title: E2F-dependent histone acetylation and recruitment of the Tip60 acetyltransferase complex to chromatin in late G1.
text: E2F proteins have the ability to activate or suppress transcription. When cells are stimulated, repressive E2F4-p130-histone deacetylase complexes separate from target promoters, while activating E2F species (E2F1, -2, and -3) associate with them. Histones H3 and H4 become hyperacetylated at the same time, but it is not clear whether this is a requirement or a result of E2F binding. Our study demonstrates that activating E2F species are necessary for the hyperacetylation of target chromatin in human cells. When a dominant-negative (DN) E2F1 mutant was overexpressed in serum-stimulated T98G cells, all E2F binding, H4 acetylation, and partially H3 acetylation were blocked. DN E2F1 also prevented target gene activation and entry into the S-phase. On the other hand, when E2F1 was activated, H3 and H4 acetylation increased rapidly, indicating a direct involvement of E2F in these processes. Previous research has shown that E2F1 binds to histone acetyltransferases (HATs) p300/CBP and PCAF/GCN5. In our experiments, ectopically expressed E2F1 also bound to the unrelated HAT Tip60 and recruited five subunits of the Tip60 complex (Tip60, TRRAP, p400, Tip48, and Tip49) to target promoters in vivo. Furthermore, E2F-dependent recruitment of Tip60 to chromatin occurred in late G(1) phase after serum stimulation. We propose that the activities of multiple HAT complexes contribute to E2F-dependent acetylation, transcription, and entry into the S-phase.

title: Chemical approaches to stem cell biology and therapeutics.
text: The utilization of small molecules to control the behavior and characteristics of stem cells presents promising prospects for fully harnessing the therapeutic capabilities of these cells. By employing a rational design and screening process, researchers have successfully identified valuable compounds that can investigate the fundamental processes of stem cell self-renewal, differentiation, and reprogramming. This has not only facilitated the advancement of cell-based therapies and therapeutic drugs aimed at targeting the body's own stem and progenitor cells for repair and regeneration but has also contributed to significant scientific and therapeutic advancements. In this article, we will explore recent progress in the field, as well as new perspectives and future challenges associated with employing chemical approaches in stem cell biology and regenerative medicine.

title: Genome-wide maps of chromatin state in pluripotent and lineage-committed cells
text: We present the use of single-molecule-based sequencing technology to analyze histone modifications in mammalian cells on a large scale. By sequencing over four billion bases of DNA obtained from chromatin immunoprecipitation, we created genome-wide maps of chromatin states in mouse embryonic stem cells, neural progenitor cells, and embryonic fibroblasts. Our findings demonstrate that trimethylation of lysine 4 and lysine 27 can effectively distinguish between genes that are actively expressed, poised for expression, or repressed, providing insights into cell state and lineage potential. Additionally, trimethylation of lysine 36 is associated with both coding and non-coding transcripts, aiding in gene annotation. We also observed trimethylation of lysine 9 and lysine 20 at satellite, telomeric, and active long-terminal repeats, with the potential to spread into nearby unique sequences. Furthermore, we discovered that imprinting control regions are marked by trimethylation of lysine 4 and lysine 9. Lastly, we demonstrate that chromatin state can be analyzed in an allele-specific manner using single nucleotide polymorphisms. This study establishes a framework for comprehensive chromatin profiling to characterize various mammalian cell populations.

title: Oncofetal long noncoding RNA PVT1 promotes proliferation and stem cell-like property of hepatocellular carcinoma cells by stabilizing NOP2.
text: Many genes that code for proteins associated with cancer and fetal development are highly active in the livers of mice and humans during fetal stages, but become inactive in adult livers. These protein products have been used as markers for the recurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and as targets for HCC treatment. In this study, we investigated the expression patterns of long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) in fetal and adult mouse livers. We identified several lncRNAs that are active in fetal livers, including lncRNA-mPvt1, which promotes cell growth, cell division, and the expression of stem cell-like properties in mouse cells. Interestingly, we found that a similar lncRNA called lncRNA-hPVT1 is up-regulated in HCC tissues in humans, and patients with higher levels of lncRNA-hPVT1 have a worse prognosis. We confirmed the pro-cancer effects of lncRNA-hPVT1 on cell growth, cell division, and stem cell-like properties in HCC cells through experiments conducted in the lab and in living organisms. Additionally, we discovered that lncRNA-hPVT1 interacts with a protein called NOP2, which is involved in RNA binding. We found that lncRNA-hPVT1 increases the stability of NOP2 proteins, and that its function relies on the presence of NOP2. In conclusion, our study reveals that many lncRNAs are activated during early liver development and suggests that fetal liver can be used to identify new diagnostic markers for HCC. LncRNA-hPVT1 promotes cell growth, cell division, and the acquisition of stem cell-like properties in HCC cells by stabilizing NOP2 protein. Targeting the lncRNA-hPVT1/NOP2 pathway may have therapeutic benefits for HCC treatment.

title: Candida albicans, a distinctive fungal model for cellular aging study
text: Unicellular eukaryotic organisms are widely used as model systems to study aging in eukaryotes. Candida albicans, a polymorphic fungus, is an additional unicellular aging model alongside Saccharomyces cerevisiae (budding yeast) and Schizosaccharomyces pombe (fission yeast). Candida cells exist in two forms: yeast (blastospore) and hyphal (filamentous), both of which have similar replicative lifespans. By taking advantage of their morphological changes, we can obtain cells of different ages. Older Candida cells tend to accumulate glycogen and proteins that have been damaged by oxidation. The deletion of the SIR2 gene reduces lifespan, while inserting an extra copy of SIR2 extends lifespan. This suggests that, similar to S. cerevisiae, Sir2 plays a role in regulating cellular aging in C. albicans. Interestingly, deleting Sir2 does not lead to the accumulation of extra-chromosomal rDNA molecules, but it does affect the retention of oxidized proteins in mother cells. This suggests that the presence of extra-chromosomal rDNA molecules may not be linked to cellular aging in C. albicans. This unique aging model, which allows for the efficient isolation of old cells on a large scale, can facilitate biochemical characterizations and genomics/proteomics studies of cellular aging. It can also help validate aging pathways observed in other organisms, including S. cerevisiae.

title: ANKTM1, a TRP-like Channel Expressed in Nociceptive Neurons, Is Activated by Cold Temperatures
text: Specialized neurons in the peripheral nervous system are responsible for detecting temperature in mammals. Heat is sensed by four TRPV-class channels, while cold is sensed by one TRPM-class channel. These channels cover a wide range of temperatures that most mammals can sense, but there is a significant gap in the ability to sense extremely cold temperatures.
