AMPK and ACC phosphorylation also increased with exercise regardless of genotype. PDHa activity was higher in control mice at 10 and 60 minutes of exercise compared to rest, but it remained unchanged in IL-6 MKO mice. Additionally, PDHa activity was higher in IL-6 MKO mice compared to control mice at rest and 60 minutes of exercise. The differences in PDHa activity between genotypes could not be explained by PDH phosphorylation or acetylation. These findings suggest that IL-6 in skeletal muscle contributes to the regulation of PDH at rest and during prolonged exercise. It also indicates that muscle IL-6 normally reduces carbohydrate utilization during prolonged exercise by affecting PDH.

title: Clinical and pathologic characteristics of patients with BRCA-positive and BRCA-negative breast cancer.
text:
The aim of this study was to compare the tumor pathologic features and clinical characteristics of patients with and without BRCA mutations in breast cancer. A total of 491 women who underwent genetic testing for BRCA mutations between 1997 and 2006 were included in the analysis. The medical records of these patients were retrospectively reviewed to gather information on ethnicity, age and clinical stage at diagnosis, age at parity, number of full-term pregnancies, use of oral contraceptives and hormone replacement therapy, and BRCA mutation status. Tumor pathology was also examined to determine histologic type, tumor grade, and estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER-2/neu status. 

Out of the 491 patients, 391 were found to be BRCA negative, while 86 were BRCA positive. The majority of BRCA1-positive patients (57.1%) were diagnosed with triple-negative breast cancer, compared to 23.3% of BRCA2-positive patients and 13.8% of BRCA-negative patients. Additionally, BRCA1 mutation carriers had higher nuclear grade tumors compared to the other two groups. Among the triple-negative cancer patients, BRCA2 mutation carriers were older at the time of diagnosis compared to BRCA1 mutation carriers and noncarriers. 

In conclusion, our findings suggest that breast tumors associated with BRCA1 mutations can be categorized into two distinct groups: triple-negative and non-triple-negative. Further research should investigate whether patients with BRCA1 mutations and triple-negative breast cancer respond differently to treatment compared to BRCA-negative patients with similar tumor pathology.

title: Interferons: Success in anti-viral immunotherapy.
text: The interferons (IFNs) are glycoproteins that have strong antiviral properties and are among the first defense mechanisms against invading pathogens. These proteins are divided into three groups, Type I, II, and III IFNs, based on the structure of their receptors on the surface of cells. Because of their ability to regulate immune responses, they have become attractive options for treating chronic virus infections. Type I IFNs, when used in combination with other drugs, are considered the standard treatment for suppressing Hepatitis C (HCV) and Hepatitis B (HBV) infections. Type III IFN has also shown promising results in phase III clinical trials as a treatment for HCV infection. However, while IFNs are effective, caution is necessary when using them as a treatment. IFNs are potent cytokines that can affect various types of cells, leading to unpleasant symptoms in patients, and in some cases, systemic effects. Therefore, constant monitoring is essential for patients undergoing IFN treatment to achieve the treatment goals of suppressing virus infection and maintaining a good quality of life.

title: Genetic analysis of human obesity in an Italian sample.
text: A study was conducted to analyze the genetic factors associated with obesity. The study focused on nuclear families from Aosta, Northern Italy. The families included parents and siblings of elementary school children who were identified as obese during an initial screening. A comparison was made with a group of non-obese children and their nuclear families. The study included 67 obese families and 112 non-obese families. Various tests were conducted to assess the genetic contribution to obesity, specifically to determine if there was a dominant major gene involved. The findings indicate that genetic factors are indeed present. Multiple analyses suggest the presence of a dominant major gene with a mild impact.

title: The non-coding RNA landscape of human hematopoiesis and leukemia
text: The understanding of non-coding RNAs and their role in gene expression and cell fate decisions is still incomplete, especially in normal and malignant human hematopoiesis. In this study, we present a comprehensive resource that defines the non-coding RNA landscape of the human hematopoietic system. By analyzing the expression patterns of non-coding RNAs in different blood cell populations, we identify unique fingerprint non-coding RNAs, such as LINC00173 in granulocytes, and link them to critical regulatory circuits involved in blood homeostasis. We also incorporate samples from acute myeloid leukemia patients into our analysis and discover prognostically relevant non-coding RNA stem cell signatures that are shared between leukemia blasts and healthy hematopoietic stem cells. These findings emphasize the importance of the non-coding transcriptome in the development and maintenance of the human blood hierarchy. While micro-RNAs are known to regulate hematopoiesis and leukemogenesis, the role of long non-coding RNAs is still unclear. Our study provides insights into the expression landscape of non-coding RNAs in the human hematopoietic system and highlights their involvement in the formation and maintenance of the human blood hierarchy.

title: Incidence and risk of central nervous system metastases as site of first recurrence in patients with HER2-positive breast cancer treated with adjuvant trastuzumab.
text:
We conducted a comprehensive meta-analysis to determine the risk of central nervous system (CNS) metastases as the first site of recurrence in patients with HER2-positive breast cancer who received adjuvant trastuzumab. Our study included eligible randomized trials of adjuvant trastuzumab administered for 1 year to patients with HER2-positive breast cancer who experienced CNS metastases as their first site of disease recurrence. Statistical analyses were performed to calculate the incidence, relative risk (RR), and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using fixed-effects inverse variance and random-effects models.

A total of 9020 patients were included in our analysis. The incidence of CNS metastases as the first site of disease recurrence in HER2-positive patients receiving adjuvant trastuzumab was 2.56% (95% CI 2.07% to 3.01%), compared to 1.94% (95% CI 1.54% to 2.38%) in HER2-positive patients who did not receive adjuvant trastuzumab. The RR of CNS metastases as the first site of relapse in trastuzumab-treated patients was 1.35 (95% CI 1.02-1.78, P = 0.038) compared to control arms without trastuzumab therapy. The ratio of CNS metastases to the total number of recurrence events was 16.94% (95% CI 10.85% to 24.07%) and 8.33% (95% CI 6.49% to 10.86%) for the trastuzumab-treated and control groups, respectively. We did not find any statistically significant differences based on the trastuzumab schedule or median follow-up time. Additionally, we observed no evidence of publication bias.

In conclusion, our findings suggest that adjuvant trastuzumab is associated with a significant increased risk of CNS metastases as the site of first recurrence in HER2-positive breast cancer patients.

title: Neutrophils in the activation and regulation of innate and adaptive immunity
text: Neutrophils have traditionally been seen as the ultimate cells responsible for resolving acute inflammation, primarily by eliminating pathogens outside of cells. However, recent evidence has expanded our understanding of their capabilities. Neutrophils have been found to possess a diverse range of effector molecules, including cytokines, extracellular traps, and effector molecules associated with the innate immune system's humoral arm. Furthermore, neutrophils play a role in activating, regulating, and carrying out effector functions for both innate and adaptive immune cells. As a result, neutrophils play a critical role in the development of various diseases, such as infections caused by pathogens residing within cells, autoimmune disorders, chronic inflammation, and cancer.

title: Functions of DNA methylation: islands, start sites, gene bodies and beyond
text: The epigenetic mark known as DNA methylation is often referred to as a 'silencing' mechanism, a concept that was initially proposed in the 1970s. However, with advancements in genome-scale mapping of methylation, we are now able to assess DNA methylation in various genomic settings. These include transcriptional start sites with or without CpG islands, gene bodies, regulatory elements, and repeat sequences. As a result, we are beginning to comprehend that the role of DNA methylation can differ depending on the context, and the relationship between DNA methylation and transcription is more intricate than previously understood. Enhancing our understanding of the functions of DNA methylation is crucial for interpreting alterations in this mark that are observed in diseases like cancer.

title: Metaplasia and transdifferentiation: from pure biology to the clinic
text: The principles of developmental biology explain a well-established set of phenomena involving the transformation of one tissue type into another. While these occurrences may be uncommon in nature, we can now envision the potential to intentionally reprogram cells from one tissue type to another by manipulating the expression of transcription factors. This innovative approach holds the promise of creating novel therapies for numerous human diseases.

title: Pioglitazone Use and Risk of Bladder Cancer and Other Common Cancers in Persons With Diabetes.
text: The importance of studies suggests that the use of pioglitazone may increase the risk of cancers. The objective of this research was to examine whether the use of pioglitazone for diabetes is associated with the risk of bladder cancer and 10 additional types of cancer. The study involved cohort and nested case-control analyses among individuals with diabetes. The bladder cancer cohort consisted of 193,099 individuals aged 40 years or older from 1997-2002 until December 2012. A total of 464 case patients and 464 matched controls were surveyed about additional factors that could affect the results. The cohort analysis of the 10 additional cancers included 236,507 individuals aged 40 years or older from 1997-2005 and followed until June 2012. These cohorts were from Kaiser Permanente Northern California. The exposures examined were ever use, duration, cumulative dose, and time since initiation of pioglitazone as time-dependent variables. The main outcomes and measures were incident cancer, including bladder, prostate, female breast, lung/bronchus, endometrial, colon, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, pancreas, kidney/renal pelvis, rectum, and melanoma. Among the 193,099 individuals in the bladder cancer cohort, 34,181 (18%) received pioglitazone, with a median duration of 2.8 years and a range of 0.2-13.2 years. A total of 1261 individuals had incident bladder cancer. The crude incidences of bladder cancer in pioglitazone users and nonusers were 89.8 and 75.9 per 100,000 person-years, respectively. The study found that the use of pioglitazone was not associated with an increased risk of bladder cancer. The results were similar in the case-control analyses. In adjusted analyses, there was no association with 8 of the 10 additional cancers. However, the use of pioglitazone was associated with an increased risk of prostate cancer and pancreatic cancer. The crude incidences of prostate and pancreatic cancer in pioglitazone users were higher compared to nonusers. No clear patterns of risk were observed for any cancer in relation to time since initiation, duration, or dose. In conclusion, the use of pioglitazone was not statistically significantly associated with an increased risk of bladder cancer, although the possibility of an increased risk could not be completely ruled out. The increased risks of prostate and pancreatic cancer associated with the use of pioglitazone require further investigation to determine whether they are causal or due to other factors.

title: Embryonic stem cell lines from human blastocysts: somatic differentiation in vitro
text: We will explain how pluripotent embryonic stem (ES) cells are derived from human blastocysts. Over an extended period, two diploid ES cell lines have been cultivated in a laboratory setting while maintaining the expression of markers that are characteristic of pluripotent primate cells. In human ES cells, the transcription factor Oct-4 is expressed, which is crucial for the development of pluripotential cells in mice. When these cell lines are transplanted into SCID mice, they give rise to teratomas that contain derivatives of all three embryonic germ layers. Additionally, both cell lines can differentiate into extraembryonic and somatic cell lineages in a laboratory setting. By differentiating ES cell cultures, it is possible to isolate neural progenitor cells that can be induced to form mature neurons. Embryonic stem cells serve as a valuable model for studying early human embryology, an investigative tool for discovering new growth factors and medicines, and a potential source of cells for transplantation therapy.

title: Multipoint Kras oncogene mutations potentially indicate mucinous carcinoma on the entire spectrum of mucinous ovarian neoplasms
text: The presence of Kras mutation is a common occurrence in various types of human tumors. Our objective was to examine the Kras mutational status across different stages of ovarian mucinous neoplasms, ranging from normal ovaries to the development of benign, borderline, and malignant tumors. We analyzed a total of 41 cases of malignant tumors, 10 cases of borderline tumors, 7 cases of benign tumors, and 7 cases of normal ovarian tissue. The prevalence of Kras mutations in normal ovaries was found to be 0.00% (n=0/7), while the prevalence in benign, borderline, and malignant mucinous neoplasms was 57.14% (n=4/7), 90.00% (n=9/10), and 75.61% (n=31/41), respectively. Among the cases of mucinous carcinoma, we detected multiple Kras mutations in 6 cases, including 5 cases with double mutations (G13D/V14I, G12V/G13S, G12D/G13S) and one case with a triple mutation (A11V/G13N/V14I). Additionally, we identified 3 novel Kras mutations (A11V, V14I) in mucinous carcinomas and one novel mutation (A11T) in a mucinous borderline tumor, which have not been previously described in the COSMIC database. In conclusion, Kras mutation appears to be a crucial event in the progression from ovarian mucinous adenoma to borderline tumor and ultimately to carcinoma. The presence of multiple Kras mutations is strongly associated with the development of unequivocal malignancy in ovarian mucinous neoplasms.

title: Identification and distinct regulation of yeast TATA box-containing genes.
text: Despite being one of the earliest identified eukaryotic transcriptional regulatory elements, the exact sequence and significance of a native TATA box remain unknown. To investigate this, we examined several Saccharomyces genomes using TATA box criteria and found a consensus sequence of TATA(A/T)A(A/T)(A/G). It is interesting to note that around 20% of yeast genes contain a TATA box. What is even more remarkable is that genes with a TATA box are associated with stress responses, tightly regulated, and preferentially utilize SAGA instead of TFIID compared to promoters without a TATA box. This suggests that transcriptional regulation in yeast is mechanistically bipolar, possibly reflecting the need to balance inducible stress-related responses with constitutive housekeeping functions.

title: IL6 derived from cancer-associated fibroblasts promotes chemoresistance via CXCR7 in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
text: In many types of cancer, drug resistance is influenced by various factors and cellular components in the tumor microenvironment. In this study, we focused on understanding the factors and molecular mechanisms that contribute to chemoresistance in patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Our findings revealed that interleukin 6 (IL6), primarily produced by cancer-associated fibroblasts, plays a crucial role in chemoresistance by increasing the expression of C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 7 (CXCR7) through the signal transducer and activator of transcription 3/nuclear factor-κB pathway. By suppressing CXCR7, we observed a reduction in IL6-induced proliferation and chemoresistance. Furthermore, silencing CXCR7 led to a decrease in gene expression associated with stemness, chemoresistance, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, as well as a decrease in the proliferation ability of ESCC cells in three-dimensional culture systems and angiogenesis assays. In clinical samples, ESCC patients with high levels of CXCR7 and IL6 had significantly worse overall survival and progression-free survival when treated with cisplatin after surgery. These findings suggest that targeting the IL6-CXCR7 axis could be a promising approach for treating ESCC.

title: Myelodysplastic syndromes: revisiting the role of the bone marrow microenvironment in disease pathogenesis
text: Myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) are a diverse group of diseases characterized by ineffective blood cell production and a tendency to develop into leukemia. The causes of MDS are complex and likely involve interactions between abnormal blood cells and their surrounding environment. The specific role of niche cells in the progression of the disease is not well understood, but recent advancements in studying the hematopoietic stem cell niche in animal models have provided valuable insights. The available data suggest that the microenvironment can actively contribute to the development of MDS and related disorders, highlighting the importance of investigating therapeutic approaches that target the interactions between mesenchymal and hematopoietic cells in these conditions.

title: SMC complexes differentially compact mitotic chromosomes according to genomic context
text: The organization of chromosomes is greatly influenced by the protein complexes known as structural maintenance of chromosomes (SMC). In our study, we utilize Hi-C and polymer modeling techniques to investigate how two highly conserved SMC complexes, cohesin and condensin, organize chromosomes in the budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Cohesin's primary function is to align sister chromatids, while condensin generally compacts chromosomes during mitosis. However, our findings reveal distinct roles for these complexes in budding yeast mitosis. Firstly, cohesin is responsible for compacting the arms of mitotic chromosomes, independent of sister chromatid cohesion. Through polymer simulations, we demonstrate that this role can be fully explained by the looping of chromatin within the chromosome. Secondly, condensin is not essential for compaction along chromosome arms. Instead, it specifically targets the regions near the rDNA and facilitates the resolution of peri-centromeric regions. Our results suggest that the conserved mechanism of SMC complexes involves the formation of chromatin loops, and different SMC-dependent looping activities are selectively employed to appropriately compact chromosomes.

title: Patterns of chlamydia testing in different settings and implications for wider STI diagnosis and care: a probability sample survey of the British population
text:
BACKGROUND
After chlamydia testing became widely available in non-specialist and community settings in the UK, many people are receiving chlamydia tests without being offered comprehensive testing for other sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and HIV. In order to understand the need for other STI diagnostic services, we examined the sexual behavior of individuals who were tested in different settings.

METHODS
We conducted a survey of the British population between 2010 and 2012, known as the third National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles. We analyzed data on chlamydia testing in the past year, including the location of the most recent test, as well as diagnoses of STIs in the past five years. The survey included individuals aged 16-44 years who reported having at least one sexual partner in the past year (4992 women, 3406 men).

RESULTS
Of the women, 26.8% (95% CI 25.4% to 28.2%) and of the men, 16.7% (15.5% to 18.1%) reported having a chlamydia test in the past year. Among those who were tested, 28.4% of women and 41.2% of men were tested in genitourinary medicine (GUM) clinics, 41.1% of women and 20.7% of men were tested in general practice (GP), and the rest were tested in other non-GUM settings. Women who were tested outside of GUM clinics were more likely to be older, in a relationship, and living in rural areas. Individuals who were tested outside of GUM clinics reported fewer risky behaviors. However, 11.0% (8.6% to 14.1%) of women and 6.8% (3.9% to 11.6%) of men who were tested in GP, and 13.2% (10.2% to 16.8%) of women and 9.6% (6.5% to 13.8%) of men who were tested in other non-GUM settings reported engaging in "unsafe sex," defined as having two or more partners and not using a condom with any partner in the past year. Individuals who were treated for chlamydia outside of GUM clinics in the past five years were less likely to have had an HIV test during that time period (women: 54.5% (42.7% to 65.7%) vs 74.1% (65.9% to 80.9%) in GUM clinics; men: 23.9% (12.7% to 40.5%) vs 65.8% (56.2% to 74.3%)).

CONCLUSIONS
The majority of chlamydia testing is taking place in non-GUM settings among populations with fewer risky behaviors. However, there is a need to provide comprehensive STI care to the significant minority who are at higher risk.

title: Treatment of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease: role of AMPK.
text: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a global epidemic that poses a significant risk for insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), and hepatic cellular carcinoma (HCC). Despite its prevalence, the only accepted treatments for NAFLD are lifestyle interventions involving exercise and weight loss. However, in recent years, several experimental compounds have shown promise in improving NAFLD in animal models, with many of these therapeutics increasing the activity of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), a cellular energy sensor. Given that AMPK activity is diminished by inflammation, obesity, and diabetes, boosting its activity has been considered a viable strategy for enhancing NAFLD. In this review, we propose three primary mechanisms through which AMPK activation can improve NAFLD and explore the mechanisms by which AMPK is activated. Additionally, we highlight 27 studies that have utilized AMPK activators to reduce NAFLD and discuss future considerations for investigating the relationship between AMPK and NAFLD.

title: Microenvironment-dependent growth of pre-neoplastic and malignant plasma cells in humanized mice
text: There is a need for in vivo models to study the interaction between human preneoplastic cells and non-malignant cells in the bone marrow microenvironment. To address this, we genetically modified mice to allow the growth of primary human preneoplastic and malignant plasma cells alongside non-malignant cells. The growth primarily occurred in the bone marrow, similar to patients with myeloma. The xenografts accurately represented the genomic complexity of the original tumors and revealed additional genetic changes. Interestingly, xenografts from patients with preneoplastic gammopathy showed progressive growth, suggesting that factors outside of the tumor cells may contribute to the stability of these lesions. These findings demonstrate a novel approach to studying human plasma cell neoplasia and highlight the usefulness of humanized models in understanding the diverse functionality of human tumors.

title: Effect of activated charcoal hemoperfusion on renal function in patients with paraquat poisoning.
text: In this retrospective study, 19 patients diagnosed with paraquat (PQ) poisoning were analyzed to investigate the impact of activated charcoal hemoperfusion on renal function and PQ elimination. The findings revealed that out of the 19 patients, 7 unfortunately passed away while 12 survived. All 7 patients who died experienced non-oliguric renal failure. Among the 12 patients who survived, 10 had normal renal function while 2 developed non-oliguric renal failure. The study also found a direct correlation between plasma and urine paraquat concentration before and during activated charcoal hemoperfusion. The equation parameters and correlation coefficient upon admission were as follows: Y=0.5820+1.7348X (R2=0.678; F=35.768; P<0.0001). During activated charcoal hemoperfusion, the equation parameters and correlation coefficient were as follows: Y=0.6827+1.2649X (R2=0.626; F=50.308; P<0.0001). Therefore, it can be concluded that in patients with normal renal function, the elimination of PQ by the kidneys is solely influenced by the plasma PQ concentration. Activated charcoal hemoperfusion has limited effectiveness in preventing acute kidney injury in patients with severe PQ poisoning.

title: Diabetes-induced effects on cardiomyocytes in chick embryonic heart micromass and mouse embryonic D3 differentiated stem cells.
text: Diabetes mellitus during pregnancy poses significant medical challenges due to the increased risks of morbidity and mortality for both the fetus and the pregnant woman. The causes of diabetic embryopathy are complex, with various factors potentially contributing to the development of congenital malformations. To explore the potential harmful effects of high blood sugar and ketone levels on the heart, this study investigated two in vitro models: primary chick embryonic cardiomyocytes and stem cell derived cardiomyocytes. Adverse effects were observed in both systems, including changes in beating activity, cell function, protein content, production of reactive oxygen species (ROS), DNA damage, and stem cell migration. The use of diabetic formulas resulted in increased DNA damage and decreased cell migration in mouse embryonic stem cells. These findings shed light on the negative effects of gestational diabetes mellitus and emphasize the importance of monitoring blood sugar levels well in advance of conception for expectant mothers and healthcare professionals. Additionally, the study supports the use of antioxidants during pregnancy to prevent DNA damage caused by ROS production, which could lead to heart defects and other developmental abnormalities.

title: Motion magnification
text: Introducing motion magnification, a technique that functions as a microscope for visual motion. It has the ability to enhance subtle movements in a video, enabling the visualization of deformations that would otherwise go unnoticed. To achieve motion magnification, we must accurately measure visual motions and group the pixels that require modification. Following an initial image registration process, motion is measured through a robust analysis of feature point trajectories, and pixels are segmented based on similarities in position, color, and motion. A unique measure of motion similarity effectively groups even the tiniest movements by examining correlation over time, often indicating a physical cause. An outlier mask is used to identify observations that cannot be explained by our layered motion model, and these pixels are simply reproduced in the output from the original registered observations. Users have the ability to magnify the motion of any selected layer by a specified amount, and texture synthesis is employed to fill in unseen "holes" that are revealed by the amplified motions. The resulting motion-magnified images can expose or highlight small movements in the original sequence, as demonstrated through examples such as deformations in load-bearing structures, subtle motions or adjustments made by individuals, and the bending of "rigid" structures under hand pressure.

title: Human TRPML1 channel structures in open and closed conformations
text: We present two electron cryo-microscopy structures of full-length human TRPML1, a calcium-releasing cation channel responsible for lysosomal calcium signaling and homeostasis. Mutations in TRPML1 result in mucolipidosis type IV, a severe lysosomal storage disorder. Our findings include a 3.72-Å apo structure of TRPML1 in the closed state at pH 7.0, and a 3.49-Å agonist-bound structure in the open state at pH 6.0. Within the channel, specific aromatic and hydrophobic residues in pore helix 1, helices S5 and S6, and helix S6 of an adjacent subunit create a hydrophobic cavity that accommodates the agonist. This suggests a distinct agonist-binding site compared to TRPV1, a TRP channel from a different subfamily. The opening of TRPML1 involves noticeable expansions of its lower gate, accompanied by a slight structural shift of pore helix 1. Our research uncovers the regulatory mechanism of TRPML channels, enhances our comprehension of TRP channel activation, and provides insights into the molecular foundation of mucolipidosis type IV pathogenesis.

title: Integrative Genomics Viewer (IGV): high-performance genomics data visualization and exploration
text: Genomic data analysis relies heavily on data visualization, but the increasing size and diversity of data sets generated by modern sequencing and array-based profiling methods pose significant challenges for visualization tools. The Integrative Genomics Viewer (IGV) is a powerful viewer designed to efficiently handle large and varied data sets, while offering a seamless and user-friendly experience across all levels of genome resolution. One of IGV's key features is its ability to integrate different types of genomic studies, supporting both array-based and next-generation sequencing data, as well as the integration of clinical and phenotypic information. While IGV is commonly used to explore publicly available genomic data, its main focus is to assist researchers in visualizing and analyzing their own data sets or those of their colleagues. To facilitate this, IGV allows for flexible loading of local and remote data sets and is optimized to provide high-performance visualization and exploration on standard desktop systems. IGV is freely accessible for download from http://www.broadinstitute.org/igv, under a GNU LGPL open-source license.

title: Can genome engineering be used to target cancer-associated enhancers?
text: The misregulation of gene expression is implicated in the development of numerous diseases, particularly the transformation of normal cells into cancerous ones. Regulatory elements located far from the genes, known as enhancers, play a crucial role in determining the specific patterns of gene expression in both healthy and diseased tissues. This suggests that targeting enhancers could be a promising approach for therapeutic intervention. By focusing on modulating gene regulation through cell-specific enhancers, it is hoped that the normal epigenetic patterns in affected tissues can be restored with fewer side effects compared to treatments that use less specific inhibitors like epigenetic drugs. Recent advancements in genomic nucleases and site-specific epigenetic regulators, which can be directed to specific regions of the genome using artificial DNA-binding proteins or RNA-DNA interactions, offer the potential for precise manipulation of enhancers. However, this field is still in its early stages, and further improvements to enhance specificity and efficiency are necessary.

title: Long‐Term Follow‐up of CD19 CAR Therapy in Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
text: A study was conducted at the Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSKCC) to assess the effectiveness and safety of CD19‐specific chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells in treating relapsed B‐cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) in adults. The trial involved 53 patients who received an infusion of autologous T cells expressing the 19‐28z CAR. The results showed that 83% of the patients achieved complete remission. However, severe cytokine release syndrome occurred in 26% of the patients, leading to one death. The median event‐free survival was 6.1 months, and the median overall survival was 12.9 months. Patients with a low disease burden before treatment had longer remission duration and survival, with a median event‐free survival of 10.6 months and a median overall survival of 20.1 months. On the other hand, patients with a higher disease burden had a higher incidence of cytokine release syndrome and neurotoxic events, as well as shorter long‐term survival. Overall, the study concluded that CAR T-cell therapy showed promising results in treating relapsed B‐cell ALL, particularly in patients with a low disease burden. The study was funded by the Commonwealth Foundation for Cancer Research and others.

title: Periosteum contains skeletal stem cells with high bone regenerative potential controlled by Periostin
text: The activation of skeletal stem cells (SSCs) is crucial for bone regeneration, but these cells are not well understood. In this study, we demonstrate that periosteum, a tissue covering the outer surface of bones, contains SSCs that have a higher potential for bone regeneration compared to bone marrow stromal cells/skeletal stem cells (BMSCs) in mice. Despite both periosteal cells (PCs) and BMSCs originating from the same embryonic mesenchymal lineage, PCs exhibit superior clonogenicity, growth, and differentiation capacity compared to BMSCs after birth. During the healing process of bone injuries, PCs efficiently contribute to the formation of cartilage and bone, and they can integrate into the tissue for a long time after transplantation. Molecular analysis reveals that genes encoding Periostin and other extracellular matrix molecules are associated with the enhanced response of PCs to injury. Deletion of the Periostin gene impairs the functions of PCs and the consolidation of fractures. Furthermore, periosteum lacking Periostin is unable to replenish the pool of PCs after injury, indicating the presence of SSCs within periosteum and the necessity of Periostin for maintaining this pool. Overall, our findings emphasize the importance of studying periosteum and PCs to gain a better understanding of bone characteristics.

title: Metabolism strikes back: metabolic flux regulates cell signaling.
text: The reliance of mammalian cells on growth factor signaling for nutrient uptake has long puzzled scientists, particularly when it comes to coordinating the uptake of glucose and glutamine. However, a recent study published in Genes & Development by Wellen and his team sheds light on this mystery. Their research reveals that the flow of glucose through the hexosamine biosynthesis pathway plays a crucial role in regulating the glycosylation of growth factor receptors, which in turn enables the consumption of glutamine. This intricate mechanism ensures that cells refrain from engaging in anabolic metabolism when nutrients are scarce, and it underscores the significance of substrate availability for protein modifications in modulating cell signaling.

title: Association of Pembrolizumab With Tumor Response and Survival Among Patients With Advanced Melanoma.
text: The importance of the programmed death 1 (PD-1) pathway in limiting immune responses to melanoma has led to the development of pembrolizumab, a humanized anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody. The objective of this study was to assess the association between pembrolizumab and tumor response and overall survival in patients with advanced melanoma. The study was conducted as open-label, multicohort, phase 1b clinical trials from December 2011 to September 2013, with a median follow-up duration of 21 months. The study took place in academic medical centers in Australia, Canada, France, and the United States. Eligible patients were 18 years and older with advanced or metastatic melanoma. Data from 655 enrolled patients were analyzed, including 135 from a nonrandomized cohort and 520 from randomized cohorts. Pembrolizumab was administered at different dosages and intervals until disease progression, intolerable toxicity, or investigator decision. The primary outcome measured was the confirmed objective response rate, while secondary outcomes included toxicity, duration of response, progression-free survival, and overall survival. The results showed that among the 655 patients, 33% had an objective response, with a higher rate of 45% in treatment-naive patients. The majority of responses were ongoing at the time of data cutoff, with 44% lasting for at least 1 year and 79% lasting for at least 6 months. The 12-month progression-free survival rate was 35% in the total population and 52% in treatment-naive patients. The median overall survival was 23 months in the total population and 31 months in treatment-naive patients. Adverse events of grade 3 or 4 were experienced by 14% of patients, and 4% discontinued treatment due to these events. Serious adverse events related to treatment were reported in 9% of patients, but there were no drug-related deaths. In conclusion, pembrolizumab showed promising results in patients with advanced melanoma, with an objective response rate of 33%, a 12-month progression-free survival rate of 35%, and a median overall survival of 23 months. However, grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 14% of patients. The trial was registered under clinicaltrials.gov Identifier: NCT01295827.

title: Inflammatory signaling in human Tuberculosis granulomas is spatially organized
text: The formation and function of granulomas, which are characteristic of tuberculosis (TB), are not well understood. In order to gain insight into the role of granulomas in TB, we conducted an unbiased analysis of the proteomes of granulomas from individuals with tuberculosis. Through the use of laser-capture microdissection, mass spectrometry, and confocal microscopy, we created detailed molecular maps of human granulomas. Our findings revealed that the centers of granulomas exhibit a pro-inflammatory environment, characterized by the presence of antimicrobial peptides, reactive oxygen species, and pro-inflammatory eicosanoids. In contrast, the tissue surrounding the caseum, a necrotic material found in granulomas, displays a comparatively anti-inflammatory signature. These observations were consistent across six human subjects and in rabbits. While the balance between systemic pro- and anti-inflammatory signals is crucial for the outcome of TB, we discovered that these signals are physically separated within each granuloma. Based on our analysis of protein and lipid profiles in human and rabbit lesions, we propose that the pathological response to TB is influenced by the precise anatomical localization of these inflammatory pathways during granuloma development.

title: Suppression of interferon-mediated anti-HBV response by single CpG methylation in the 5′-UTR of TRIM22
text: The aim of this study was to investigate the effectiveness of interferons (IFNs) in treating HBV infection compared to other viral infections. We conducted a proteome-wide screening to identify the cellular targets of HBV in response to IFNs. Through LC-MS/MS analysis, we discovered proteins that were either downregulated or upregulated by IFN treatment in HBV X protein (HBx)-stable and control cells. Among the downregulated genes, we found TRIM22, which is known for its antiretroviral properties. Further investigation revealed that HBx suppresses the transcription of TRIM22 by methylating a single CpG site in its 5′-UTR. This methylation reduces the binding affinity of IFN regulatory factor-1, thereby inhibiting the IFN-stimulated induction of TRIM22. To validate our findings, we conducted experiments using a mouse model, primary human hepatocytes, and human liver tissues. Our results provide insights into how HBV evades the host innate immune system.

title: Developmental Analysis of Bone Marrow Neutrophils Reveals Populations Specialized in Expansion, Trafficking, and Effector Functions
text: In this study, the researchers aimed to better understand the differentiation pathways of neutrophils, which are specialized innate cells that have a short lifespan and require constant replenishment from bone marrow precursors. They used mass cytometry and cell-cycle-based analysis to identify three subsets of neutrophils in the bone marrow: a proliferative precursor that differentiates into immature and mature neutrophils. Through transcriptomic profiling and functional analysis, they found that the proliferative precursor relies on a specific transcription factor for its generation and transitions to a migratory and effector function as it matures. These precursor cells expand under stress conditions, such as microbial infection and tumors, and immature neutrophils are recruited to the peripheral tissues in tumor-bearing mice. Overall, this study provides insights into the specialized populations of neutrophils in the bone marrow and their role in maintaining homeostasis and responding to stress.

title: TAK1-mediated autophagy and fatty acid oxidation prevent hepatosteatosis and tumorigenesis.
text:
We investigated the role of the MAP kinase kinase kinase TGFβ-activated kinase 1 (TAK1) in regulating autophagy, lipid metabolism, and tumorigenesis in the liver. TAK1 is activated by TLRs, IL-1, TNF, and TGFβ, and it in turn activates IKK-NF-κB and JNK, which play important roles in cell survival, growth, tumorigenesis, and metabolism. TAK1 signaling also upregulates AMPK activity and autophagy.

In our study, we found that mice with hepatocyte-specific deletion of Tak1 and subjected to fasting developed severe hepatosteatosis, characterized by increased mTORC1 activity and suppression of autophagy compared to their wild-type counterparts. Furthermore, TAK1-deficient hepatocytes showed suppressed AMPK activity and autophagy in response to starvation or metformin treatment. However, when we ectopically activated AMPK in these cells, autophagy was restored.

We also observed that the expression of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor α (PPARα) target genes and β-oxidation, which are involved in hepatic lipid degradation, were suppressed in hepatocytes lacking TAK1. As a result, a high-fat diet challenge exacerbated steatohepatitis in mice with hepatocyte-specific deletion of Tak1. Interestingly, when we inhibited mTORC1, autophagy and PPARα target gene expression were restored in TAK1-deficient livers, suggesting that TAK1 acts upstream of mTORC1.

Furthermore, mTORC1 inhibition not only restored autophagy and PPARα activity but also suppressed spontaneous liver fibrosis and hepatocarcinogenesis in animals with hepatocyte-specific deletion of Tak1. These findings indicate that TAK1 plays a crucial role in regulating hepatic lipid metabolism and tumorigenesis through the AMPK/mTORC1 axis, affecting both autophagy and PPARα activity.

title: Formins at the Junction.
text: The physical and functional connection between the actin cytoskeleton and adhesion junctions occurs at the interface between epithelial cells. The Arp2/3 complex, which regulates actin turnover, is known to play a role in this process. However, the role of formins, the largest group of actin regulators, is not as well understood. Formins are responsible for shaping the actin cytoskeleton and have various functions within cells. In this review, we discuss recent advancements in understanding how formins regulate actin dynamics at cell-cell contacts. Additionally, we highlight the importance of formins in facilitating polarized protein traffic, which is crucial for epithelialization.

title: CRISPR adaptation biases explain preference for acquisition of foreign DNA
text: The CRISPR-Cas system is a bacterial defense mechanism that protects against invading phages or plasmids. During the process of CRISPR adaptation, small pieces of DNA called "spacers" are obtained from foreign elements and incorporated into the CRISPR array. However, it has remained unclear why spacers are selectively acquired from foreign DNA while the bacterial chromosome is avoided. Our study reveals that spacer acquisition is dependent on DNA replication and that breaks in DNA occurring at stalled replication forks promote spacer acquisition. The acquisition of spacers from the bacterial chromosome is limited to specific regions called Chi sites, which are octamers of DNA sequence highly concentrated on the bacterial chromosome. This suggests that Chi sites restrict spacer acquisition from the bacterial chromosome. Additionally, we demonstrate that the avoidance of acquiring spacers from the bacterial chromosome is facilitated by the RecBCD complex, which repairs double-stranded DNA breaks. Our findings indicate that in Escherichia coli, the acquisition of new spacers primarily relies on RecBCD-mediated processing of double-stranded DNA breaks that occur mainly at replication forks. The preference for acquiring spacers from foreign DNA is achieved through the higher density of Chi sites on the bacterial chromosome, combined with the greater number of replication forks on foreign DNA. This model explains the strong inclination to acquire spacers from both high copy plasmids and phages.

title: High-resolution mapping of open chromatin in the rice genome.
text:
The control of gene expression is a complex process involving the interaction of transcription factors with promoters and other regulatory DNA elements. One notable characteristic of genomic regions associated with regulatory proteins is their sensitivity to DNase I digestion. In our study, we created detailed maps of DNase I hypersensitive (DH) sites throughout the genome of rice (Oryza sativa), using both seedling and callus tissues. Surprisingly, only about 25% of the DH sites in both tissues were found in putative promoters, indicating that the majority of gene regulatory elements in rice are located elsewhere.

Interestingly, we observed a 58% increase in DH sites in the callus compared to the seedling. Furthermore, when comparing DH sites that were present in both tissues, we found that 31% exhibited significantly different levels of DNase I sensitivity. Genes that showed differential expression between the seedling and callus were often associated with DH sites in both tissues.

We also discovered that the DNA sequences within the DH sites were hypomethylated, which aligns with what is known about active gene regulatory elements. Notably, tissue-specific DH sites located in promoters displayed higher levels of DNA methylation compared to the average methylation level of all DH sites in promoters.

Additionally, we observed a distinct increase in H3K27me3, a histone modification associated with gene repression, at intergenic DH sites. These findings suggest that epigenetic modifications play a role in the dynamic changes of DH site numbers and DNase I sensitivity during development.

title: Prospective study of body fat distribution and the risk of endometrial cancer.
text:
The background of this study reveals that previous research has shown a positive relationship between overall obesity and the risk of endometrial cancer (EC). However, there is limited data on the association between body fat distribution and EC risk. 

The methods of the study involved following 51,948 women from the Nurses' Health Study who reported their waist circumference (WC) and hip circumference in 1986. The researchers calculated the waist-to-hip ratio (WHR). 

Over a 24-year follow-up period, 449 cases of invasive EC were diagnosed. In a multivariate analysis that did not account for body mass index (BMI), the relative risks (RRs) for EC were 2.44 for WC and 1.69 for WHR. However, after adjusting for BMI, these associations were greatly weakened and no longer statistically significant. The RRs were 1.08 for WC and 1.15 for WHR, respectively. 

In conclusion, this prospective cohort study found no independent association between body fat distribution and the risk of EC after accounting for BMI.

title: Breast cancer clusters in the northeast United States: a geographic analysis.
text:
The authors of this study aimed to investigate the distribution of high breast cancer mortality rates in the northeastern part of the United States, particularly in Long Island, New York. They wanted to determine if these high mortality rates were randomly spread across the region or if there were statistically significant clusters of deaths. To do this, they collected demographic data and age-specific breast cancer mortality rates for women from all 244 counties in 11 northeastern states and the District of Columbia between 1988 and 1992.

The researchers utilized a spatial scan statistic, a recently developed method that identifies clusters of cases without predefining their size or location. This statistic also tests for the statistical significance of these clusters while accounting for the multiple testing involved in such an analysis. The initial analysis adjusted for age, but additional analyses were conducted to assess the impact of confounding variables such as race, urbanicity, and parity.

The results revealed a statistically significant and geographically extensive cluster of breast cancer deaths in the New York City-Philadelphia metropolitan area (p = 0.0001). This cluster had a 7.4% higher mortality rate compared to the rest of the Northeast. Even when considering confounding variables like race, urbanicity, and parity, this cluster remained significant. Furthermore, within this area, four smaller subclusters were also found to be significant: Philadelphia with suburbs (p = 0.0001), Long Island (p = 0.0001), central New Jersey (p = 0.0001), and northeastern New Jersey (p = 0.0001).

The elevated breast cancer mortality on Long Island should not be viewed as an isolated local phenomenon but rather as part of a broader issue affecting significant portions of the New York City-Philadelphia metropolitan area. Several known and hypothesized risk factors, such as age at first birth, age at menarche, age at menopause, breastfeeding, genetic mutations, and environmental factors, may contribute to the observed cluster. However, these factors were not accounted for in the analysis.

title: CD200R/CD200 Inhibits Osteoclastogenesis: New Mechanism of Osteoclast Control by Mesenchymal Stem Cells in Human
text: The balance between bone-forming osteoblasts and bone-degrading osteoclasts is responsible for maintaining bone homeostasis. Osteoblasts originate from mesenchymal cells, while osteoclasts belong to the myeloid lineage. Communication between osteoclasts and osteoblasts occurs through the secretion of soluble factors, interaction with the bone, and direct contact between cells, which regulate their activities. CD200, a member of the immunoglobulin superfamilly, is expressed on various cell types, including mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). The CD200 receptor (CD200R) is expressed on myeloid cells like monocytes/macrophages. We hypothesize that CD200 may be involved in the control of osteoclastogenesis and could play a role in the communication between MSCs and osteoclasts in humans. In this study, we have shown that soluble CD200 inhibits the differentiation and maturation of osteoclast precursors into bone-resorbing cells in vitro. Soluble CD200 does not alter the phenotype of monocytes but inhibits the signaling pathway of receptor activator of nuclear factor kappa-B ligand (RANKL) and the expression of osteoclast markers such as osteoclast-associated receptor (OSCAR) and nuclear factor of activated T cells cytoplasmic 1 (NFATc1). Furthermore, MSCs inhibit the formation of osteoclasts through cell-cell contact, which is associated with the expression of CD200 on the surface of MSCs. Our results clearly demonstrate that MSCs, through the expression of CD200, play a crucial role in regulating bone resorption and bone physiology. Targeting the CD200-CD200R interaction could be a potential strategy for controlling bone diseases.

title: Tumor-specific Th17-polarized cells eradicate large established melanoma.
text: The potential roles of different subsets of CD4+ T cells in anti-tumor immunity have not been fully explored. To investigate the impact of CD4+ T cell polarization on tumor rejection, we created a new mouse model that mimics human disease. In this model, CD4+ T cells recognize a unique epitope in tyrosinase-related protein 1 (TRP-1), which is expressed by normal melanocytes and B16 murine melanoma. In vitro experiments showed that these cells can be polarized into Th0, Th1, and Th17 subtypes, as indicated by their cytokine, chemokine, and adhesion molecule profiles, as well as surface markers. This suggests that they may have different effector functions in vivo. Contrary to the prevailing belief that Th1 cells are most important in tumor rejection, our findings demonstrate that Th17-polarized cells are more effective in destroying advanced B16 melanoma. Their therapeutic effect relies on the production of interferon-gamma (IFN-gamma), while the depletion of interleukin (IL)-17A and IL-23 has minimal impact. These results highlight the importance of appropriately polarizing effector CD4+ T cells in vitro for successful tumor eradication. This principle should be taken into account when designing clinical trials involving adoptive transfer-based immunotherapy for human malignancies.

title: Defining community acquired pneumonia severity on presentation to hospital: an international derivation and validation study.
text:
In order to assess the severity of community acquired pneumonia (CAP), the modified British Thoracic Society (mBTS) rule is used to identify patients with severe pneumonia. However, this rule does not identify patients who may be suitable for home management. To address this, a multicentre study was conducted to develop a practical severity assessment model for adults hospitalized with CAP, which would help categorize them into different management groups.

Data from three prospective studies of CAP conducted in the UK, New Zealand, and the Netherlands were combined for this study. The model was developed using a derivation cohort, which consisted of 80% of the data. Prognostic variables were identified using multiple logistic regression, with 30-day mortality as the outcome measure. The final model was then tested against a validation cohort.

A total of 1068 patients were included in the study, with a mean age of 64 years and 51.5% of them being male. The 30-day mortality rate was 9%. The analysis revealed that age of 65 years or older (OR 3.5, 95% CI 1.6 to 8.0) and albumin levels below 30 g/dl (OR 4.7, 95% CI 2.5 to 8.7) were independently associated with mortality, in addition to the mBTS rule (OR 5.2, 95% CI 2.7 to 10).

Based on the information available at the initial hospital assessment, a six-point score was developed. Each point was assigned for the presence of Confusion, Urea levels above 7 mmol/l, Respiratory rate of 30/min or higher, low systolic (<90 mm Hg) or diastolic (</=60 mm Hg) Blood pressure, and age of 65 years or older (CURB-65 score). This score allowed patients to be stratified into different management groups based on their increasing risk of mortality: score 0 (0.7% mortality), score 1 (3.2% mortality), score 2 (3% mortality), score 3 (17% mortality), score 4 (41.5% mortality), and score 5 (57% mortality). The validation cohort confirmed a similar pattern.

In conclusion, a simple six-point score based on confusion, urea levels, respiratory rate, blood pressure, and age can be used to categorize patients with CAP into different management groups.

title: Mitochondrial iron chelation ameliorates cigarette-smoke induced bronchitis and emphysema in mice
text: Cigarette smoking and genetic factors are both associated with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Our previous research has identified a gene called iron-responsive element-binding protein 2 (IRP2) as a key contributor to COPD susceptibility. We have observed increased levels of IRP2 protein in the lungs of individuals with COPD. In this study, we found that mice lacking the Irp2 gene were protected from COPD induced by cigarette smoke. Through various techniques such as RNA immunoprecipitation followed by sequencing (RIP-seq), RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), and gene expression and functional enrichment clustering analysis, we discovered that Irp2 regulates mitochondrial function in the lungs of mice. Irp2 promotes the accumulation of iron in mitochondria and increases the levels of cytochrome c oxidase (COX), leading to mitochondrial dysfunction and the development of COPD. Mice with a deficiency in frataxin, a protein involved in iron metabolism, exhibited impaired airway mucociliary clearance (MCC) and higher levels of lung inflammation even without exposure to cigarette smoke. On the other hand, mice lacking the ability to synthesize cytochrome c oxidase, which results in reduced COX levels, were protected from cigarette smoke-induced lung inflammation and MCC impairment. Treatment with a mitochondrial iron chelator or a low-iron diet provided protection against COPD induced by cigarette smoke. Mitochondrial iron chelation also improved MCC impairment, lung inflammation, and lung injury in mice with established COPD, suggesting that targeting the mitochondrial-iron axis could be a potential therapeutic approach for COPD.

title: Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts Neutralize the Anti-tumor Effect of CSF1 Receptor Blockade by Inducing PMN-MDSC Infiltration of Tumors.
text: Tumor progression is influenced by tumor-associated macrophages (TAM) in various ways. Although targeting TAM using CSF1R inhibitors seems promising as a therapeutic approach, its effectiveness against tumors has been limited. In this study, we have identified the underlying mechanism that hampers the impact of CSF1R targeted therapy. Our findings reveal that carcinoma-associated fibroblasts (CAF) play a significant role in recruiting granulocytes to tumors by releasing chemokines. Interestingly, the presence of CSF1, produced by tumor cells, leads to the downregulation of granulocyte-specific chemokine expression in CAF through HDAC2-mediated processes. Consequently, the migration of these cells towards tumors is restricted. However, treatment with CSF1R inhibitors disrupts this communication between tumor cells and CAF, resulting in a substantial increase in granulocyte recruitment to tumors. Furthermore, when combined with a CXCR2 antagonist, the CSF1R inhibitor effectively prevents granulocyte infiltration into tumors, leading to potent anti-tumor effects.

title: Phenotypic deficits in the HIV-1 envelope are associated with the maturation of a V2-directed broadly neutralizing antibody lineage
text: The development of broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) to HIV-1 is a complex process that involves the virus escaping from the immune system and the antibodies adapting to counteract it. Scientists are trying to replicate this process in HIV-1 vaccine design. In order to do this, they need to understand the properties of the virus that trigger the production of bnAbs. In this study, we examined the evolution of a specific bnAb lineage called VRC26 in a patient with HIV-1 subtype C. We looked at how the virus changed over time, both before and during the early stages of bnAb production. We found that there were significant changes in the virus's properties, particularly in its envelope protein (Env), which is responsible for eliciting bnAb responses. These changes coincided with the virus becoming resistant to VRC26. We also observed that the resistant viruses were less infectious, had altered entry kinetics, and were less sensitive to neutralization after attaching to CD4 cells. Interestingly, VRC26 was still able to neutralize the virus when it was transmitted between cells, suggesting that this route of transmission is not a major pathway for viral escape. The early escape variants of the virus had reduced fitness and were still sensitive to cell-cell transmission, which limited their ability to replicate and escape quickly. This suggests that VRC26 only allowed partial viral escape for an extended period of time, potentially increasing the window for bnAb development. Our findings demonstrate the flexibility of the HIV-1 Env in evading bnAb pressure and emphasize the importance of considering phenotypic traits when designing immunogens. By selecting and designing Env variants with different phenotypic patterns and bnAb sensitivity, we may be able to maximize the effectiveness of vaccination in inducing bnAb responses.

title: High somatic mutation and neoantigen burden are correlated with decreased progression-free survival in multiple myeloma
text: The presence of specific mutations in tumors can lead to the development of immunogenic neoantigens, which have been linked to the effectiveness of immune checkpoint inhibitors in cancers with high mutation rates. However, initial findings from studies using single-agent checkpoint inhibitors in multiple myeloma (MM) have been disappointing. Therefore, our objective was to investigate the connection between mutations, neoantigens, and the response to treatments in MM patients. We analyzed interim data from the MMRF CoMMpass study (NCT01454297), which included 664 MM patients, to determine the somatic mutation burden, neoantigen load, and response to therapy. In this group, the average number of somatic mutations and missense mutations per patient were 405.84 (standard deviation = 608.55) and 63.90 (standard deviation = 95.88), respectively. We observed a positive linear relationship between the number of mutations and the burden of neoantigens (R2 = 0.862). On average, patients were predicted to have 23.52 neoantigens (standard deviation = 52.14), with an average of 9.40 expressed neoantigens (standard deviation = 26.97). Survival analysis showed that patients with a higher than average somatic missense mutation load (N = 163) and predicted expressed neoantigen load (N = 214) had significantly shorter progression-free survival (PFS) compared to those with lower loads (0.493 vs 0.726 2-year PFS, P = 0.0023 and 0.555 vs 0.729 2-year PFS, P = 0.0028, respectively). This trend persisted when patients were stratified by disease stage and cytogenetic abnormalities. Therefore, a high mutation and neoantigen load are important risk factors that negatively impact the survival of MM patients under current treatment standards.

title: Postmarket Safety Events Among Novel Therapeutics Approved by the US Food and Drug Administration Between 2001 and 2010
text:
The occurrence of postmarket safety events for new pharmaceuticals and biologics is crucial as it involves identifying safety risks after these therapeutics have been initially approved by regulatory authorities. These safety events have the potential to impact how these novel therapeutics are used in clinical practice and influence decision making for both patients and clinicians. 

The objectives of this study were to determine the frequency of postmarket safety events among novel therapeutics approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and to investigate whether any specific characteristics of these therapeutics, known at the time of FDA approval, were associated with an increased risk of such events. 

This cohort study examined all novel therapeutics approved by the FDA between January 1, 2001, and December 31, 2010, with follow-up conducted until February 28, 2017. The study analyzed various characteristics of these therapeutics, including drug class, therapeutic area, priority review, accelerated approval, orphan status, near-regulatory deadline approval, and regulatory review time. 

The main outcomes measured were a composite of three factors: withdrawals due to safety concerns, incremental boxed warnings issued by the FDA during the postmarket period, and safety communications issued by the FDA. 

The results showed that between 2001 and 2010, the FDA approved a total of 222 novel therapeutics, consisting of 183 pharmaceuticals and 39 biologics. During a median follow-up period of 11.7 years, there were 123 new postmarket safety events, affecting 71 (32.0%) of the novel therapeutics. The median time from approval to the first postmarket safety event was 4.2 years, and at the 10-year mark, the proportion of novel therapeutics affected by a postmarket safety event was 30.8%. 

In the multivariable analysis, it was found that postmarket safety events were significantly more frequent among biologics, therapeutics indicated for psychiatric disease, those receiving accelerated approval, and those with near-regulatory deadline approval. Conversely, events were less frequent among therapeutics with regulatory review times less than 200 days. 

In conclusion, this study highlights that 32% of the novel therapeutics approved by the FDA between 2001 and 2010 experienced postmarket safety events. Biologics, psychiatric therapeutics, accelerated and near-regulatory deadline approval were associated with higher rates of events, emphasizing the importance of continuous monitoring of the safety of novel therapeutics throughout their life cycle.

title: Who is where at risk for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease? A spatial epidemiological analysis of health insurance claims for COPD in Northeastern Germany
text:
BACKGROUND
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is highly prevalent in Germany and is expected to increase in the coming years. While individual risk factors are well understood, there is limited knowledge about the spatial heterogeneity and population-based risk factors of COPD. Understanding broader population-based processes could help in planning healthcare provision and prevention strategies. This study aims to analyze the smallest possible spatial-scale variations in COPD prevalence across northeastern Germany and identify location-specific population-based risk factors using health insurance claims from AOK Nordost.

METHODS
To visualize the spatial distribution of COPD prevalence at the municipal and urban district level, we used the conditional autoregressive Besag-York-Mollié (BYM) model. Geographically weighted regression modeling (GWR) was used to analyze location-specific ecological risk factors for COPD.

RESULTS
In 2012, the sex- and age-adjusted prevalence of COPD was 6.5% and varied significantly across northeastern Germany. Population-based risk factors included the proportions of insured individuals aged 65 and older, insured individuals with a migration background, household size, and area deprivation. The GWR model revealed considerable variation in the population at risk for COPD across northeastern Germany.

CONCLUSION
Area deprivation directly and indirectly influences the prevalence of COPD. Individuals aging in socially disadvantaged areas have a higher likelihood of developing COPD, even if they are not directly affected by individual-level deprivation. This highlights the importance of considering the impact of area deprivation on health when planning healthcare services. Additionally, our results show that in certain parts of the study area, insured individuals with a migration background and those living in multi-person households are at a higher risk of COPD.

title: Large intergenic non-coding RNA-RoR modulates reprogramming of human induced pluripotent stem cells
text: The process of reprogramming lineage-committed cells into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) involves a significant restructuring of the epigenome, leading to changes in gene expression. In this study, we examine the transcriptional reorganization of large intergenic non-coding RNAs (lincRNAs) during the generation of human iPSCs and identify several lincRNAs that are associated with pluripotency. Specifically, we identify ten lincRNAs that are upregulated in iPSCs compared to embryonic stem cells, suggesting that their activation may play a role in the emergence of iPSCs. Our findings also indicate that these lincRNAs are directly regulated by key pluripotency transcription factors. Through loss-of-function and gain-of-function experiments, we demonstrate that one particular lincRNA (lincRNA-RoR) influences the reprogramming process, providing the first evidence of the crucial role of lincRNAs in the derivation of pluripotent stem cells.

title: Extracellular vesicle isolation and characterization: toward clinical application.
text: There are two main types of extracellular vesicles (EVs) known as exosomes and shed microvesicles (sMVs). These EVs differ in their size distribution, as well as the proteins and RNA they contain. EVs are important for cell-cell communication, both locally and throughout the body. In this article, we explore the different subtypes of EVs, methods for isolating them from cell-culture media and body fluids, and techniques for quantifying them. We also examine specific proteins found in exosomes and sMVs that could be used as markers to distinguish between EV subtypes. Additionally, we discuss the various ways EVs can be utilized in clinical diagnosis.

title: Up-regulated NRIP2 in colorectal cancer initiating cells modulates the Wnt pathway by targeting RORβ
text:
Colorectal cancer is a prevalent form of cancer worldwide, with colorectal cancer initiating cells (CCICs) playing a crucial role in its malignant behavior. The Wnt pathways, responsible for the self-renewal of CCICs, are activated abnormally, but the exact mechanism behind this remains unclear. 

To shed light on this, we conducted retroviral library screening and discovered Nuclear Receptor-Interacting Protein 2 (NRIP2) as a new interactor of the Wnt pathway in enriched colorectal cancer colosphere cells. We further examined the expression levels of NRIP2 and retinoic acid-related orphan receptor β (RORβ) using various techniques such as FISH, qRT-PCR, IHC, and Western blot. We created colorectal cancer cells with overexpressed and silenced NRIP2 to study its role in the Wnt pathway. Additionally, we investigated the binding between NRIP2 and RORβ and explored the impact of RORβ on CCICs both in vitro and in vivo. Through genechip-scanning, we speculated that downstream target HBP1 is involved. To confirm this, we conducted Western blot, ChIP, and luciferase reporter assays to examine the interaction between NRIP2, RORβ, and HBP1. 

Our results showed that NRIP2 was significantly up-regulated in CCICs from cell lines and primary colorectal cancer tissues. Increased NRIP2 expression enhanced Wnt activity, while silencing NRIP2 attenuated it. The transcription factor RORβ played a crucial role as a target through which NRIP2 regulated Wnt pathway activity. RORβ acted as a transcriptional enhancer of inhibitor HBP1 in the Wnt pathway. NRIP2 prevented RORβ from binding to downstream HBP1 promoter regions, leading to reduced transcription of HBP1. Consequently, this weakened the HBP1-dependent inhibition of TCF4-mediated transcription. 

In conclusion, NRIP2 is a novel interactor of the Wnt pathway in colorectal cancer initiating cells. The interactions between NRIP2, RORβ, and HBP1 provide a new mechanism for CCIC self-renewal through Wnt activity.

title: Speed Limits for Nonvesicular Intracellular Sterol Transport.
text: The movement of sterols between the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and plasma membrane (PM) happens through nonvesicular mechanisms that involve sterol transport proteins (STPs). In this study, we explore the concept that transport is more efficient at membrane contact sites where the ER and PM are closely connected. Our findings suggest that the main limiting factor for sterol transfer in cells is the detachment of sterols from the membrane, rather than the diffusion facilitated by STPs. Therefore, there doesn't seem to be a significant advantage in having STP-mediated sterol transfer occur at contact sites in terms of kinetics. Instead, these contact sites may serve to compartmentalize lipid synthesis or transport machinery, offering opportunities for regulation.

title: Misunderstandings in prescribing decisions in general practice: qualitative study.
text: AIMS To identify and describe misunderstandings between doctors and patients regarding prescribing decisions in general practice. METHOD Qualitative study. LOCATION 20 general practices in the West Midlands and south east England. PARTICIPANTS 20 general practitioners and 35 patients seeking consultation. MAIN OUTCOMES Misunderstandings between doctors and patients that may have negative effects on medication adherence. RESULTS 14 categories of misunderstandings were discovered, including lack of patient information known to the doctor, lack of doctor information known to the patient, conflicting information, disagreement about side effect attribution, breakdown in communication regarding doctor's decisions, and relationship issues. All misunderstandings were linked to patients' limited participation in the consultation, such as not expressing expectations or preferences, or not voicing responses to doctors' decisions and actions. These misunderstandings resulted in potential or actual negative outcomes, such as non-compliance with treatment. Many misunderstandings were based on inaccurate assumptions and guesses. Doctors appeared to be unaware of the importance of patients' ideas about medications for successful prescribing. CONCLUSIONS Patients' active participation in consultations and the negative consequences of limited participation are significant. The authors are developing an educational intervention based on these findings.

title: Phase-plate cryo-EM structure of a biased agonist-bound human GLP-1 receptor–Gs complex
text: The G protein-coupled receptor known as class B glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is a key target for treating type 2 diabetes and obesity. Both natural and synthetic GLP-1 peptides display biased agonism, meaning they have different functional selectivity, which could lead to improved therapeutic outcomes. In this study, we present the structure of the human GLP-1 receptor bound to the G protein-biased peptide exendin-P5 and a Gαs heterotrimer. The resolution of our structure was 3.3 Å. We observed differences in the organization of extracellular loop 3 and nearby transmembrane segments compared to a previous structure of the GLP-1 receptor bound to GLP-1. On the intracellular side, there was a six-degree difference in the angle of engagement between the Gαs–α5 helix in our structure and the previous one, which was also seen throughout the G protein heterotrimer. Furthermore, the structures differed in how the Gαs protein underwent conformational changes. Our findings shed light on the molecular mechanisms underlying biased agonism.

title: Therapeutic equivalence of alendronate 70 mg once-weekly and alendronate 10 mg daily in the treatment of osteoporosis. Alendronate Once-Weekly Study Group.
text:
Convenience in dosing is crucial for effectively managing any chronic disease, especially when it comes to long-term management of osteoporosis. Taking medication less frequently can improve adherence and maximize the effectiveness of treatment. Animal studies support the idea that taking alendronate 70 mg once a week (which is equivalent to 7 times the daily oral dose) can be just as effective as taking alendronate 10 mg daily due to its long-lasting effects on bone. Additionally, studies in dogs suggest that once-weekly dosing may reduce the risk of esophageal irritation, which is commonly seen with daily oral bisphosphonates. This dosing schedule would provide patients with more convenience and likely improve adherence. 

To compare the efficacy and safety of different dosing regimens, we conducted a one-year, double-blind, multicenter study on postmenopausal women with osteoporosis. The participants were divided into three groups: one received oral alendronate 70 mg once a week (N=519), another received alendronate 35 mg twice a week (N=369), and the third group received alendronate 10 mg daily (N=370). The primary measure of effectiveness was the increase in bone mineral density (BMD) in the lumbar spine, using strict predefined criteria for equivalence. Secondary measures included changes in BMD at the hip and total body, as well as markers of bone turnover. 

Both of the new dosing regimens met the criteria for equivalence compared to daily therapy. At 12 months, the mean increase in lumbar spine BMD was 5.1% (95% CI 4.8, 5.4) in the once-weekly group, 5.2% (4.9, 5.6) in the twice-weekly group, and 5.4% (5.0, 5.8) in the daily treatment group. Increases in BMD at other sites were similar across all three dosing regimens. All three treatment groups effectively reduced markers of bone resorption and formation. The tolerability of the regimens was comparable, with a similar incidence of upper gastrointestinal (GI) adverse events. However, there were fewer serious upper GI adverse events and a trend towards fewer esophageal events in the once-weekly dosing group compared to the daily dosing group. The occurrence of clinical fractures was similar among all groups. 

In conclusion, the once-weekly dosing regimen of alendronate 70 mg provides a more convenient and therapeutically equivalent option to daily dosing. It has the potential to improve adherence and long-term persistence with therapy, while also potentially reducing the risk of upper GI adverse events.

title: Association of Toll-Like Receptor 4 on Human Monocyte Subsets and Vulnerability Characteristics of Coronary Plaque as Assessed by 64-Slice Multidetector Computed Tomography.
text: The expression of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR-4) on circulating monocytes and its relationship with coronary plaque vulnerability has not been previously studied in patients with stable angina pectoris (SAP). In this study, we used 64-slice multidetector computed tomography (MDCT) to investigate this relationship in 65 patients with SAP. We measured three monocyte subsets (CD14++CD16-, CD14++CD16+, and CD14+CD16+) and the expression of TLR-4 using flow cytometry. The vulnerability of intracoronary plaques was determined based on positive remodeling (remodeling index >1.05) and/or low CT attenuation (<35 HU). We found that CD14++CD16+ monocytes expressed TLR-4 more frequently than CD14++CD16- and CD14+CD16+ monocytes (P<0.001). The relative proportion of TLR-4 expression on CD14++CD16+ monocytes was significantly higher in patients with vulnerable plaque compared to those without (10.4 [4.1-14.5] % vs. 4.5 [2.8-7.8] %, P=0.012). Furthermore, the relative proportion of TLR-4 expression on CD14++CD16+ monocytes was positively correlated with the remodeling index (r=0.28, P=0.025) and negatively correlated with CT attenuation value (r=-0.31, P=0.013). In conclusion, the upregulation of TLR-4 on CD14++CD16+ monocytes may be associated with coronary plaque vulnerability in patients with SAP.

title: Expandable Cardiovascular Progenitor Cells Reprogrammed from Fibroblasts.
text: Cardiac regeneration using stem cell-based approaches is becoming an increasingly viable option for treating heart failure. However, one major obstacle is the generation of a sufficient number of functional cells for transplantation.
