In this study, we successfully isolated a cell population from mouse fibroblasts that had a high capacity for proliferation and limited potential for cardiovascular differentiation during the process of cardiac transdifferentiation. These cells, known as induced expandable cardiovascular progenitor cells (ieCPCs), were able to proliferate extensively for over 18 passages under specific chemical conditions. Starting with just 10(5) fibroblasts, we were able to robustly produce 10(16) ieCPCs. These ieCPCs expressed genes characteristic of cardiac cells and were able to differentiate into functional cardiomyocytes, endothelial cells, and smooth muscle cells in vitro, even after long-term expansion. When transplanted into mouse hearts after a heart attack, the ieCPCs spontaneously differentiated into cardiomyocytes, endothelial cells, and smooth muscle cells, leading to improved cardiac function for up to 12 weeks post-transplantation. Therefore, ieCPCs represent a powerful tool for studying cardiovascular development and offer potential strategies for regenerative medicine in the heart.

title: Thyroid hormone inhibits lung fibrosis in mice by improving epithelial mitochondrial function
text: The role of thyroid hormone (TH) in lung fibrosis is not yet understood, but it is known to be crucial for maintaining cellular balance during stress responses. In this study, we discovered that the activity and expression of iodothyronine deiodinase 2 (DIO2), an enzyme that activates TH, were higher in the lungs of patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis compared to healthy individuals. These levels were also correlated with the severity of the disease. Additionally, when we tested Dio2-knockout mice, we observed that they had increased lung fibrosis when exposed to bleomycin. However, when we administered TH through aerosol delivery, we found that it improved survival rates and resolved fibrosis in two different mouse models of pulmonary fibrosis. We also discovered that Sobetirome, a TH mimetic, reduced bleomycin-induced lung fibrosis. Furthermore, TH promoted the growth of new mitochondria, improved their energy production, and reduced mitochondria-related cell death in alveolar epithelial cells both in vivo and in vitro after bleomycin-induced injury. However, TH did not have the same effect in mice lacking the Ppargc1a or Pink1 genes, suggesting that these pathways are necessary for TH's antifibrotic properties. In conclusion, our findings suggest that TH has potential as a therapy for pulmonary fibrosis by protecting alveolar epithelial cells and restoring mitochondrial function.

title: Tenomodulin promotes human adipocyte differentiation and beneficial visceral adipose tissue expansion.
text:
Maintaining insulin sensitivity is crucial for proper regulation of energy storage in adipose tissue, but the molecules involved in this process are not fully understood. In this study, we found that the type II transmembrane protein tenomodulin (TNMD) is upregulated in adipose tissue of insulin-resistant individuals compared to insulin-sensitive individuals with similar body mass index (BMI). We also discovered that TNMD expression increases during the differentiation of human preadipocytes, and blocking TNMD prevents adipogenesis. 

To further investigate the role of TNMD, we conducted experiments using transgenic mice that overexpress Tnmd and fed them a high-fat diet. These mice showed increased mass in the epididymal white adipose tissue (eWAT), and preadipocytes derived from these mice displayed enhanced proliferation, indicating elevated adipogenesis. Additionally, lipogenic genes were upregulated in the eWAT of Tnmd transgenic mice, and Ucp1 expression in brown fat was also increased. Interestingly, these mice had reduced triglyceride accumulation in the liver. 

Despite the expansion of eWAT, the Tnmd transgenic mice exhibited improved systemic insulin sensitivity. Furthermore, they showed decreased collagen deposition and inflammation in the eWAT, as well as increased insulin stimulation of Akt phosphorylation. Based on these findings, we propose that TNMD acts as a protective factor in visceral adipose tissue, alleviating insulin resistance in obesity.

title: Evidence for a limit to human lifespan
text: Advancements in technology have significantly increased human life expectancy since the 19th century. Studies on population data have revealed a continuous decrease in mortality rates among the elderly and a rise in the maximum age at death, potentially leading to a gradual extension of human longevity. Additionally, research has shown that lifespan in various animal species can be expanded through genetic or pharmaceutical interventions, suggesting that strict genetic limitations may not govern longevity. However, our analysis of global demographic data indicates that improvements in survival rates decline after reaching 100 years old, and the age at death of the world's oldest individual has not increased since the 1990s. These findings strongly indicate that the maximum lifespan of humans is fixed and subject to natural constraints.

title: Effect of Oral Semaglutide Compared With Placebo and Subcutaneous Semaglutide on Glycemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomized Clinical Trial
text:
The importance of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists as effective therapies for type 2 diabetes cannot be overstated. Currently, all available GLP-1 receptor agonists require injection. The objective of this study was to compare the effects of oral semaglutide with placebo (primary) and open-label subcutaneous semaglutide (secondary) on glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes.

This was a phase 2, randomized, parallel-group, dosage-finding trial conducted over 26 weeks with a 5-week follow-up period. The trial took place at 100 sites in 14 countries, including hospital clinics, general practices, and clinical research centers. A total of 632 participants with type 2 diabetes and insufficient glycemic control using diet and exercise alone or a stable dose of metformin were randomized. Randomization was stratified by metformin use.

The interventions included once-daily oral semaglutide at various doses (2.5 mg, 5 mg, 10 mg, 20 mg, 40-mg 4-week dose escalation, 40-mg 8-week dose escalation, 40-mg 2-week dose escalation) or oral placebo (double-blind), as well as once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide at 1.0 mg. The primary endpoint was the change in hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) from baseline to week 26. Secondary endpoints included changes in body weight and adverse events.

Baseline characteristics were similar across treatment groups. Of the 632 randomized patients, 583 (92%) completed the trial. The mean change in HbA1c level from baseline to week 26 decreased with oral semaglutide (dosage-dependent range, −0.7% to −1.9%) and subcutaneous semaglutide (−1.9%), while placebo showed a decrease of −0.3%. The reductions in HbA1c with oral semaglutide were significant compared to placebo. Reductions in body weight were also greater with oral semaglutide and subcutaneous semaglutide compared to placebo, with significant reductions observed for oral semaglutide dosages of 10 mg or more. Adverse events were reported by a majority of patients in all treatment groups, with gastrointestinal events being the most common.

In conclusion, oral semaglutide demonstrated better glycemic control than placebo over 26 weeks in patients with type 2 diabetes. These findings support the need for phase 3 studies to assess longer-term and clinical outcomes, as well as safety. The trial was registered under clinicaltrials.gov Identifier: NCT01923181.

title: Fast and accurate short read alignment with Burrows–Wheeler transform
text:
The advancement of DNA sequencing technologies has led to the generation of a large number of short reads, necessitating the development of rapid and precise read alignment programs. Initially, hash table-based methods like MAQ were created, offering accuracy, extensive features, and sufficient speed for aligning short reads from a single individual. However, MAQ lacks support for gapped alignment in single-end reads, making it unsuitable for aligning longer reads with frequent indels. Additionally, MAQ's speed becomes a concern when aligning reads from hundreds of individuals during resequencing.

To address these limitations, we have introduced the Burrows-Wheeler Alignment tool (BWA). BWA utilizes backward search with Burrows-Wheeler Transform (BWT) to efficiently align short sequencing reads against large reference sequences, such as the human genome, while allowing for mismatches and gaps. BWA is compatible with both base space reads (e.g., from Illumina sequencing machines) and color space reads from AB SOLiD machines. Evaluations using simulated and real data indicate that BWA is approximately 10-20 times faster than MAQ, while maintaining similar accuracy. Furthermore, BWA provides alignment outputs in the new standard SAM (Sequence Alignment/Map) format. Users can perform variant calling and other downstream analyses using the open source SAMtools software package.

For more information and access to BWA, please visit http://maq.sourceforge.net.

title: The financial cost of doctors emigrating from sub-Saharan Africa: human capital analysis
text:
The objective of this study was to estimate the financial loss of domestically educated doctors migrating from sub-Saharan African countries to Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the United States. The study used a human capital cost analysis approach and publicly accessible data. The research focused on nine sub-Saharan African countries with a high HIV prevalence or a large number of people with HIV/AIDS, and with at least one medical school. The main outcome measures were the cost of educating a doctor, the number of doctors currently working in the destination countries, and the savings to the destination countries from receiving trained doctors. 

The results showed that the government subsidised cost of a doctor's education in the source countries ranged from $21,000 to $58,700. The estimated loss of returns from investment for all doctors currently working in the destination countries was $2.17bn, with costs varying for each country. Zimbabwe and South Africa had the largest losses in terms of the ratio of lost investment to gross domestic product. The United Kingdom and United States benefited the most from recruiting trained doctors. 

In conclusion, the emigration of doctors from sub-Saharan African countries heavily impacted the investment made in their education. Destination countries should consider investing in measurable training for source countries and strengthening their health systems.

title: Chromatin modifying enzymes as modulators of reprogramming
text: The process of generating induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) through somatic cell reprogramming involves making changes to the epigenetic landscape of cells. While we know that certain proteins are involved in regulating the chromatin marks associated with different epigenetic states before and after reprogramming, the exact role of specific chromatin-modifying enzymes in this process is still unknown. To investigate the influence of these enzymes on reprogramming, we used short hairpin RNAs (shRNAs) to target genes involved in DNA and histone methylation pathways. Through this approach, we identified both positive and negative regulators of iPSC generation. Inhibiting the core components of the polycomb repressive complex 1 and 2, including the enzyme EZH2, which adds a methyl group to histone 3 at a specific site (lysine 27), reduced the efficiency of reprogramming. On the other hand, suppressing the enzymes SUV39H1, YY1, and DOT1L enhanced reprogramming. Specifically, inhibiting DOT1L, which adds a methyl group to histone 3 at a different site (lysine 79), either through shRNA or a small molecule, accelerated reprogramming, increased the number of iPSC colonies, and acted as a substitute for the transcription factors KLF4 and c-Myc. Inhibiting DOT1L early in the reprogramming process led to a significant increase in two important factors, NANOG and LIN28, which play crucial roles in enhancing reprogramming. By analyzing the distribution of the H3K79me2 mark throughout the genome, we found that genes specific to fibroblasts and associated with the transition from an epithelial to mesenchymal state lose this mark during the initial stages of reprogramming. Inhibiting DOT1L facilitates the removal of this mark from genes that are destined to be repressed in the pluripotent state. These findings suggest that specific chromatin-modifying enzymes can either hinder or facilitate reprogramming, and demonstrate how manipulating these enzymes can lead to a more efficient generation of iPSCs without the need for additional transcription factors.

title: Natural variation in the parameters of innate immune cells is preferentially driven by genetic factors
text: The measurement and characterization of immune cells in the bloodstream are important indicators of human health and disease. In order to understand how environmental and genetic factors contribute to the variation in innate and adaptive immune cells in normal conditions, we conducted a study using standardized flow cytometry and DNA genotyping of 1,000 healthy individuals of Western European descent. Our findings revealed that smoking, along with age, sex, and latent cytomegalovirus infection, were the primary non-genetic factors influencing the variation in human immune cell parameters. Through genome-wide association studies, we identified 15 genetic loci that were enriched with variants associated with diseases. Additionally, we discovered that genetic variation played a stronger role in controlling the parameters of innate immune cells compared to adaptive immune cells, which were more influenced by environmental exposure. This research provides a valuable resource for generating new hypotheses in immunology and emphasizes the importance of innate immunity in susceptibility to common autoimmune diseases. By analyzing data from the Milieu Intérieur Consortium, Albert and colleagues have comprehensively described the impact of lifestyle, environment, and genetics on human innate and adaptive immunity.

title: The transcriptional program, functional heterogeneity, and clinical targeting of mast cells
text: Mast cells are a unique type of immune cells found in tissues. They have a wide range of receptors that can be activated by various external signals, such as antigen-immunoglobulin E (IgE) complexes, bacteria, viruses, cytokines, hormones, peptides, and drugs. Although mast cells make up a small population in tissues, their ability to quickly release stored and newly produced mediators is crucial in maintaining health and combating diseases. This article aims to explore the biology of mast cells and present new perspectives on their role in human diseases beyond IgE-mediated allergic responses and antiparasitic functions. We also discuss recent advancements in mast cell research, including the regulation of their functions, differentiation, survival, and the development of novel mouse models. Lastly, we emphasize the current and future possibilities for therapeutic interventions targeting mast cell functions in inflammatory diseases.

title: LIN28B enhanced tumorigenesis in an autochthonous KRASG12V-driven lung carcinoma mouse model
text: LIN28B is a protein that binds to RNA and primarily regulates let-7 microRNAs, which play important roles in inflammation, wound healing, embryonic stem cells, and cancer. LIN28B expression is linked to the initiation, progression, resistance, and poor outcomes of various solid cancers, including lung cancer. However, the specific role of LIN28B in non-small cell lung adenocarcinomas is still not well understood. To address this, we conducted a study using a mouse model in which LIN28B was overexpressed alongside the KRASG12V mutation, a common driver of lung cancer. Our findings revealed that LIN28B overexpression significantly increased the number of tumor cells expressing CD44 and CD326 markers, upregulated VEGF-A and miR-21, and promoted tumor angiogenesis and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). These effects were accompanied by enhanced AKT phosphorylation and the movement of c-MYC into the nucleus. Furthermore, LIN28B accelerated tumor initiation, enhanced proliferation, and ultimately led to a shorter overall survival. Additionally, we analyzed lung adenocarcinomas from the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and found that LIN28B was expressed in 24% of cases with KRAS mutations, further highlighting the relevance of our model.

title: Cost-effectiveness comparison between topical silver sulfadiazine and enclosed silver dressing for partial-thickness burn treatment.
text: The standard treatment for partial-thickness burns involves using silver products like silver sulfadiazine (SSD) cream and enclosed dressings such as silver-impregnated foam (Mepilex Ag) and silver-laden sheets (Aquacel Ag). However, the current state of healthcare is constrained by limited resources and focuses on evidence-based outcomes and cost-effective treatments. This study conducted a decision analysis to compare the cost and utility of enclosed silver dressings with SSD in partial-thickness burn patients with a total body surface area (TBSA) less than 20%. A thorough review of the literature was conducted to identify relevant health states in these patients, including successful healing, infection, and noninfected delayed healing requiring surgery or conservative management. The probabilities of these health states were combined with Medicare CPT reimbursement codes (cost) and patient-derived utilities to create a decision model. Utilities were obtained through patient interviews using a visual analog scale. The expected cost and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) were calculated using the roll-back method. The incremental cost-utility ratio for enclosed silver dressings compared to SSD was $40,167.99/QALY. One-way sensitivity analysis of complication rates confirmed the robustness of the model. To be cost-effective, the complication rate for SSD must be 22% or higher, assuming a maximum willingness to pay of $50,000/QALY. Two-way sensitivity analysis, by varying complication rates for both SSD and enclosed silver dressings, demonstrated the cost-effectiveness of using enclosed silver dressings at the majority of complication rates for both treatment options. In conclusion, enclosed silver dressings are a cost-effective treatment for partial-thickness burns.

title: Randomized clinical study of Hydrofiber dressing with silver or silver sulfadiazine in the management of partial-thickness burns.
text:
In this study, two different protocols of care were compared for the management of partial-thickness burns. One protocol used AQUACEL Ag Hydrofiber dressing with silver, while the other used silver sulfadiazine. The study included 42 participants in each group and lasted for up to 21 days.

The results showed that the use of AQUACEL Ag dressing was associated with several advantages. Patients experienced less pain and anxiety during dressing changes, as well as less burning and stinging while wearing the dressing. They also required fewer dressing changes, less nursing time, and fewer procedural medications. On the other hand, the use of silver sulfadiazine provided greater flexibility and ease of movement.

Both treatment groups had comparable rates of adverse events, including infection. However, the AQUACEL Ag dressing protocol tended to have lower total treatment costs (Dollars 1040 vs. Dollars 1180) and a higher rate of re-epithelialization (73.8% vs. 60.0%). This resulted in a cost-effectiveness per burn healed of Dollars 1,409.06 for AQUACEL Ag dressing and Dollars 1,967.95 for silver sulfadiazine.

Overall, the study concluded that a protocol of care using AQUACEL Ag dressing provided both clinical and economic benefits compared to silver sulfadiazine for patients with partial-thickness burns.

title: Hepatitis C virus and blood transfusion: past and present risks.
text: Since the early 1980s, the risk of transmitting HCV through blood and blood products has significantly decreased. This is due to various measures such as selecting non-paid donors, implementing donor selection protocols to prevent HIV transmission, conducting initial surrogate testing in certain regions, and introducing anti-HCV testing. The use of ALT surrogate testing has become outdated with the introduction of anti-HCV testing. Currently, the residual risk of HCV transmission from donations during the anti-HCV window period is approximately 1 in 100,000 transfusions of cellular products. There have been no reported cases of HCV transmission through plasma products treated with modern inactivation methods like solvent-detergent treatment. The implementation of hemovigilance programs will provide more data on the safety of blood transfusions. Many European countries are expected to adopt HCV nucleic amplification technology (NAT) as a quality control measure for manufacturing pools of plasma products or as a screening method for blood donors using minipools in the near future. With advancements in technology, NAT testing of individual blood donations may become available within the next two years. HCV NAT testing will further reduce the residual risk, and its cost-effectiveness will be relatively low compared to other public health measures.

title: p62/SQSTM1 by Binding to Vitamin D Receptor Inhibits Hepatic Stellate Cell Activity, Fibrosis, and Liver Cancer.
text: Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) have important roles in liver fibrosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Activation of the Vitamin D receptor (VDR) in HSCs inhibits liver inflammation and fibrosis. Our research has shown that p62/SQSTM1, a protein that is increased in liver parenchymal cells but decreased in HCC-associated HSCs, negatively regulates HSC activation. When p62 is removed from the entire body or specifically from HSCs, it enhances HSCs and increases inflammation, fibrosis, and HCC progression. p62 directly interacts with VDR and RXR, promoting their combination, which is crucial for recruiting target genes of VDR:RXR. The absence of p62 in HSCs impairs the ability of VDR agonists to suppress fibrosis and inflammation. This demonstrates that p62 acts as a negative regulator of liver inflammation and fibrosis by facilitating VDR signaling in HSCs, which are involved in HCC development.

title: Developing criteria for evaluation of geroprotectors as a key stage toward translation to the clinic
text: In the next few decades, there will be a significant change in the aging population, which will have significant social and economic implications worldwide. One way to counteract this increase is to accelerate the development of geroprotectors, substances that slow down aging, repair age-related damage, and extend a healthy lifespan, or healthspan. Although more than 200 geroprotectors have been identified in model organisms and some are being used in humans for specific diseases, it is still unclear whether they have an impact on aging in humans. The translation of these substances to clinical use is hindered by various challenges, including the lack of a common set of criteria to define, select, and classify them. This is due to the complexity of the aging process and the diverse mechanisms of action of geroprotectors. To address these issues, it is crucial to establish a scientific consensus on the definition of 'geroprotector', the criteria for selecting them, a comprehensive classification system, and an analytical model. In this article, we examine current approaches to selection and propose our own criteria. By standardizing the selection of geroprotectors, the discovery and analysis of new candidates can be streamlined, saving time and costs associated with translating them to clinical use.

title: β-Catenin Signaling and Roles in Liver Homeostasis, Injury, and Tumorigenesis.
text: β-catenin, which is encoded by CTNNB1, plays a crucial role as a component of the cell surface cadherin protein complex. It acts as an intracellular signal transducer in the WNT signaling pathway and has been linked to the development of hepatocellular carcinoma and other liver diseases. In addition to WNT, β-catenin can also interact with various signaling pathways. It interacts with transcription factors like T-cell factor, forkhead box protein O, and hypoxia-inducible factor 1α to regulate the expression of target genes. This article focuses on the involvement of β-catenin in the metabolic zonation of the adult liver. Furthermore, β-catenin controls the expression of genes responsible for glucose, nutrient, and xenobiotic metabolism. Dysregulation of β-catenin activity may contribute to the pathogenesis of nonalcoholic steatohepatitis. Moreover, alterations in β-catenin signaling can activate hepatic stellate cells, which are crucial for fibrosis. Mutations in CTNNB1 leading to constitutive activation of β-catenin are frequently observed in hepatic tumors such as hepatocellular adenomas, hepatocellular cancers, and hepatoblastomas. Therefore, β-catenin could serve as a potential therapeutic target. This article explores how changes in β-catenin activity contribute to liver disease and discusses their potential applications in diagnosis, prognosis, and the development of therapeutics.

title: The global burden of dengue: an analysis from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2013.
text:
BACKGROUND
Dengue is a widespread arbovirus infection, but its impact is not well understood. In the Global Burden of Disease Study 2013, we aimed to estimate the mortality, incidence, and overall burden of dengue.

METHODS
Using the Cause of Death Ensemble Modelling tool, we analyzed mortality data from vital registration, verbal autopsy, and surveillance sources. We also examined officially reported cases to estimate incidence, adjusting for under-reporting based on expansion factors. Our analysis included 1780 country-years of mortality data from 130 countries, 1636 country-years of dengue case reports from 76 countries, and expansion factor estimates for 14 countries.

FINDINGS
Between 1990 and 2013, we estimated an average of 9221 dengue deaths per year. The number of deaths increased from a low of 8277 in 1992 to a peak of 11,302 in 2010. In 2013 alone, dengue was responsible for 576,900 years of life lost due to premature mortality. The incidence of dengue also rose significantly during this period, with the number of cases more than doubling every decade. In 2013, there were an estimated 58.4 million apparent cases of dengue. When considering disability from moderate and severe acute dengue, as well as post-dengue chronic fatigue, dengue accounted for 566,000 years lived with disability in 2013. Overall, dengue caused 1.14 million disability-adjusted life-years in 2013, taking into account both fatal and non-fatal outcomes.

INTERPRETATION
Our findings support the commonly cited range of 50 million to 100 million symptomatic cases of dengue per year. While our mortality estimates are lower than other studies, it is important to consider the possibility that dengue mortality may actually be higher. 

FUNDING
This study was funded by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.

title: Formin-mediated actin polymerization at cell–cell junctions stabilizes E-cadherin and maintains monolayer integrity during wound repair
text: The integrity of epithelial tissue in various situations, including homeostasis, development, and tissue repair, relies on the adhesion between cells mediated by cadherins. The stability of E-cadherin, a specific type of cadherin, is dependent on F-actin. However, the mechanisms that regulate actin polymerization at the junctions between cells are not well understood. In this study, we aimed to investigate the role of formin-mediated actin polymerization at these cell-cell junctions. Our findings reveal that two factors, mDia1 and Fmnl3, play a significant role in enhancing actin polymerization and stabilizing E-cadherin at epithelial junctions. Fmnl3 is found to be localized at adherens junctions downstream of Src and Cdc42. Depletion of Fmnl3 leads to a decrease in F-actin and E-cadherin at junctions, resulting in weakened cell-cell adhesion. Notably, Fmnl3 expression is up-regulated and its localization at junctions increases during collective cell migration. When Fmnl3 or mDia1 is depleted in migrating cell monolayers, the leader cells become dissociated, and wound repair is impaired. In conclusion, our study demonstrates that formin activity at epithelial cell-cell junctions is crucial for adhesion and the maintenance of epithelial cohesion during dynamic processes, such as wound repair.

title: A mechanically active heterotypic E-cadherin/N-cadherin adhesion enables fibroblasts to drive cancer cell invasion
text: Our research demonstrates that Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) play a crucial role in promoting the invasion and metastasis of tumors. We have discovered that CAFs exert a physical force on cancer cells, facilitating their collective invasion. This force transmission occurs through a heterophilic adhesion mechanism involving N-cadherin on the CAF membrane and E-cadherin on the cancer cell membrane. Importantly, this adhesion is not only a passive interaction but also mechanically active. When subjected to force, it triggers the recruitment of β-catenin and reinforces adhesion through the interaction of α-catenin and vinculin. Disruption of the E-cadherin/N-cadherin adhesion prevents CAFs from guiding collective cell migration and inhibits cancer cell invasion. Additionally, N-cadherin is responsible for repolarizing CAFs away from cancer cells. Simultaneously, nectins and afadin are recruited to the interface between cancer cells and CAFs, and the repolarization of CAFs is dependent on afadin. We have also observed heterotypic junctions between CAFs and cancer cells in patient-derived samples. Overall, our findings highlight the importance of a mechanically active heterophilic adhesion between CAFs and cancer cells in facilitating cooperative tumor invasion.

title: Long non-coding RNA HOTTIP promotes BCL-2 expression and induces chemoresistance in small cell lung cancer by sponging miR-216a
text: Despite advancements in the treatment of small cell lung cancer (SCLC), the issue of multidrug chemoresistance and poor prognosis still persists. In order to address this, we conducted a comprehensive assessment of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) on their impact on SCLC chemoresistance using microarray data, as well as in vitro and in vivo experiments. Our findings reveal that HOTTIP, a frequently amplified lncRNA in SCLC, is closely associated with SCLC cell chemosensitivity, proliferation, and the unfavorable prognosis of SCLC patients. Furthermore, our mechanistic investigations demonstrate that HOTTIP acts as an oncogene in the progression of SCLC by binding to miR-216a and inhibiting its tumor-suppressive function in this context. Additionally, HOTTIP enhances the expression of the anti-apoptotic factor BCL-2, which is another crucial target gene of miR-216a, thereby collectively promoting chemoresistance in SCLC through the regulation of BCL-2. In summary, our study establishes the role of HOTTIP in the progression and chemoresistance of SCLC, suggesting its potential as a novel diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for the clinical management of SCLC.

title: GSDS 2.0: an upgraded gene feature visualization server
text: The Gene Structure Display Server (GSDS) is a valuable tool for biologists, allowing them to visualize genes' structure and annotated features, aiding in the investigation of their function and evolution. Since its initial release in 2007, GSDS has been widely utilized by over 60,000 users. In this report, we present the upgraded version, GSDS 2.0, which features a newly designed interface, expanded support for various types of annotation features and formats, and an integrated visual editor for modifying the generated figure. Additionally, users can now incorporate a user-specified phylogenetic tree to facilitate further evolutionary analysis. The complete source code is also available for download. The GSDS web server and source code can be accessed freely at http://gsds.cbi.pku.edu.cn. For any inquiries, please contact gaog@mail.cbi.pku.edu.cn or gsds@mail.cbi.pku.edu.cn. Supplementary data can be found at Bioinformatics online.

title: SLP-65 regulates immunoglobulin light chain gene recombination through the PI(3)K-PKB-Foxo pathway
text: Although we understand the important role of the adaptor protein SLP-65 in the differentiation of pre-B cells, we still have limited knowledge about how it functions at a molecular level. In this study, we have discovered a connection between SLP-65-dependent signaling and the phosphoinositide-3-OH kinase (PI(3)K)–protein kinase B (PKB)–Foxo pathway. Our findings demonstrate that the transcription factor Foxo3a, belonging to the forkhead box family, plays a role in promoting light chain rearrangement in pre-B cells. Our data also suggests that PKB inhibits light chain recombination by phosphorylating Foxo proteins. However, when we restore SLP-65 function, it counteracts PKB activation and enhances the activity of Foxo3a and Foxo1 in pre-B cells. These results shed light on the molecular function of SLP-65 and highlight the crucial role of Foxo proteins in regulating light chain recombination, receptor editing, and B cell selection.

title: A case-mix classification system for explaining healthcare costs using administrative data in Italy.
text: In Italy, the National Health Service (NHS) offers healthcare coverage to all citizens, including primary and hospital care. Outpatient and drug services require a copayment. Local Health Trusts (LHTs) receive funding based on a capitation system that considers age, gender, and area of residence. To better understand healthcare costs, we utilized the Johns Hopkins Adjusted Clinical Groups System (ACG® System) with administrative data from the Veneto Region in northeastern Italy. All residents in the region were included in the study. We analyzed various sources of information, such as hospital discharges, emergency room visits, chronic disease registry, ambulatory visits, medications, home care database, and drug prescriptions for the year 2015. By using simple linear regressions, we compared an age-gender model to models that incorporated more comprehensive risk measures to predict healthcare costs. The results showed that the simple age-gender model only accounted for 8% of the variance in total costs for 2015. However, when diagnoses-related variables were added, there was a 23% increase in explained variance, and pharmacy-based variables provided an additional 17% increase. The comprehensive model had an adjusted R-squared value that was six times higher than the simple age-gender model. In conclusion, the ACG System significantly improves the prediction of healthcare costs compared to simple age-gender adjustments. The increase in healthcare costs is primarily driven by the accumulation of chronic conditions and resulting multimorbidity, rather than aging alone.

title: EpCAM-regulated intramembrane proteolysis induces a cancer stem cell-like gene signature in hepatitis B virus-infected hepatocytes.
text:
BACKGROUND & OBJECTIVES: The replication of the hepatitis B virus (HBV) in hepatocytes leads to the loss of a chromatin modifying protein complex called polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2), which in turn causes the re-expression of certain genes that are normally suppressed by PRC2. One of these genes is epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM), which is normally expressed in hepatic progenitor cells but becomes re-expressed in hepatic cancer stem cells (hCSCs). In this study, we aimed to investigate the functional significance of EpCAM re-expression in HBV-induced hepatocarcinogenesis.

METHODS: Using various molecular techniques, we examined the role of EpCAM-regulated intramembrane proteolysis (RIP) in HBV replicating cells in vitro, as well as in liver tumors from HBV X/c-myc mice and patients with chronic HBV infection.

RESULTS: We found that EpCAM undergoes RIP in HBV replicating cells, leading to the activation of canonical Wnt signaling. Transfection of a plasmid expressing green fluorescent protein (GFP) that responds to Wnt signaling revealed a population of GFP-positive cells in HBV replicating cells. These GFP-positive/Wnt-positive cells exhibited resistance to cisplatin and sorafenib, similar to hCSCs, and showed increased expression of pluripotency genes NANOG, OCT4, SOX2, as well as hCSC markers BAMBI, CD44, and CD133. We referred to this gene expression pattern as the EpCAM RIP and Wnt-induced hCSC-like gene signature. Interestingly, this gene signature was also found to be overexpressed in liver tumors of X/c-myc bitransgenic mice. Clinically, we identified a group of HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinomas that exhibited elevated expression of the hCSC-like gene signature and were associated with reduced overall survival after surgical resection.

CONCLUSIONS: The hCSC-like gene signature shows promise as a prognostic tool for classifying subtypes of HBV-induced hepatocellular carcinomas. Inhibition of EpCAM RIP and Wnt signaling pathways could be explored as a therapeutic strategy for this subtype of HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinomas.

LAY SUMMARY: This study provides evidence for a molecular mechanism by which chronic infection with the hepatitis B virus leads to the development of liver cancer with a poor prognosis. Based on this mechanism, our results suggest potential therapeutic interventions.

title: Parathyroid Hormone Directs Bone Marrow Mesenchymal Cell Fate.
text: The mechanism of action for intermittent PTH administration, which helps build bone mass and prevent fractures, remains unclear. To investigate further, we deleted the PTH/PTHrP receptor (PTH1R) in mesenchymal stem cells using Prx1Cre. This resulted in low bone formation, increased bone resorption, and high levels of bone marrow adipose tissue (BMAT). We discovered that the BMAT originated from Prx1 and expressed typical adipogenic markers, as well as high levels of receptor activator of nuclear factor kappa B ligand (Rankl). RANKL levels were also elevated in the bone marrow supernatant and serum, but not in other adipose depots. Through cell sorting, we found that Pref1+RANKL+ marrow progenitors were twice as abundant in the mutant mice compared to the control group. Interestingly, intermittent PTH administration significantly reduced BMAT in control mice, and a similar effect was observed in male osteoporotic patients. These findings suggest that marrow adipocytes possess both osteogenic and adipogenic characteristics, respond uniquely to PTH, and secrete RANKL. Overall, these studies provide valuable insights into the therapeutic action of PTH by influencing the fate of mesenchymal cells.

title: Metformin attenuates blood-brain barrier disruption in mice following middle cerebral artery occlusion
text:
The effect of metformin, a commonly used hypoglycemic drug, on ischemic stroke is not well understood. In this study, we aimed to investigate the impact of metformin on ischemic stroke in mice and explore the underlying mechanisms. Ninety-eight adult male CD-1 mice were subjected to transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) for 90 minutes. Metformin was administered at a dose of 200 mg/kg for up to 14 days. We evaluated neurobehavioral outcomes, brain infarct volume, inflammatory factors, blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, and AMPK signaling pathways following tMCAO. Additionally, we performed oxygen glucose deprivation on bEND.3 cells to understand the mechanisms of metformin in inhibiting inflammatory signaling pathways. 

Our results showed that metformin treatment reduced infarct volume compared to the control group after tMCAO. Neurobehavioral outcomes were significantly improved in metformin-treated mice. Metformin administration also led to a decrease in MPO+ cells, Gr1+ cells, MPO activity, and BBB permeability. Furthermore, metformin activated AMPK phosphorylation, inhibited NF-κB activation, and down-regulated cytokine (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α) and ICAM-1 expression after tMCAO. In bEND.3 cells, metformin activated the AMPK signaling pathway and alleviated oxygen-glucose deprivation-induced ICAM-1 expression. This effect was eliminated when a selective AMPK inhibitor, Compound C, was used. 

In conclusion, metformin down-regulated ICAM-1 in an AMPK-dependent manner, which effectively prevented ischemia-induced brain injury by reducing neutrophil infiltration. These findings suggest that metformin holds promise as a therapeutic agent in stroke therapy.

title: Epstein-Barr Virus nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA1) confers resistance to apoptosis in EBV-positive B-lymphoma cells through up-regulation of survivin.
text: The resistance to programmed cell death, known as apoptosis, plays a crucial role in driving the development of tumors. EBV, a common human gamma-herpesvirus, tends to establish latent infections in B-lymphocytes that are already infected by the virus. In most cases of EBV-positive cancers, a protein called EBNA1 is expressed and plays a vital role in replicating the viral DNA within the host cells. In this study, we examine how EBNA1 affects the up-regulation of survivin, a protein that inhibits apoptosis, in B-lymphoma cells infected with EBV. Our findings provide evidence that EBNA1 forms a complex with Sp1 or Sp1-like proteins, which bind to a specific region on the survivin gene. This complex enhances its activity and leads to an increase in survivin levels. When we reduced the levels of survivin and EBNA1, we observed an increase in apoptosis in the infected cells. This supports the idea that EBNA1 plays a role in suppressing apoptosis in EBV-infected cells and suggests that the virus-encoded protein can contribute to the development of cancer by up-regulating survivin, an apoptosis inhibitor, in B-lymphoma cells associated with EBV.

title: Microfluidic platform to evaluate migration of cells from patients with DYT1 dystonia.
text:
BACKGROUND
Microfluidic platforms have emerged as a cost-effective and time-efficient tool for studying biological and pathological events, such as cell migration, through real-time imaging. Cell migration plays a crucial role in development, wound healing, and maintaining homeostasis in both healthy and disease states.

NEW METHOD
In this study, we utilized microfluidic chambers to precisely measure and compare the migration properties of fibroblasts carrying a mutation in the TOR1A gene, which is associated with the hereditary neurologic disease DYT1 dystonia, with control cells.

RESULTS
Our findings revealed that fibroblasts from DYT1 patients exhibited abnormalities in key aspects of cell migration, including reduced velocity and persistence of movement.

COMPARISON WITH EXISTING METHOD
By employing the microfluidic method, we were able to demonstrate reduced polarization of the nucleus, abnormal orientation of nuclei and Golgi within the moving DYT1 patient cells, and vectorial movement of individual cells, when compared to control cells.

CONCLUSION
In conclusion, our study presents various assays that can be used to assess different parameters of cell migration in DYT1 patient cells as a result of the TOR1A gene mutation. Additionally, the microfluidic platform offers a valuable means to evaluate real-time vectorial movement with single cell resolution in a three-dimensional environment.

title: Sugar-sweetened beverages and weight gain in children and adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
text:
BACKGROUND: The relationship between sugar-sweetened beverages (SSBs) and body weight is still a topic of debate.

OBJECTIVE: We conducted a comprehensive review and analysis to summarize the available evidence in both children and adults.

DESIGN: We searched through various databases for prospective cohort studies and randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that examined the relationship between SSBs and weight. We then conducted separate meta-analyses for children and adults, as well as for cohort studies and RCTs, using different statistical models.

RESULTS: Our meta-analyses included 32 original articles: 20 in children (15 cohort studies, involving 25,745 participants, and 5 trials, involving 2,772 participants) and 12 in adults (7 cohort studies, involving 174,252 participants, and 5 trials, involving 292 participants). In cohort studies, each additional daily serving of SSBs was associated with a 0.06 (95% CI: 0.02, 0.10) and 0.05 (95% CI: 0.03, 0.07) increase in BMI in children, and a weight gain of 0.22 kg (95% CI: 0.09, 0.34 kg) and 0.12 kg (95% CI: 0.10, 0.14 kg) in adults over a period of 1 year, according to random- and fixed-effects models, respectively. RCTs in children showed a reduction in BMI gain when SSBs were reduced [random and fixed effects: -0.17 (95% CI: -0.39, 0.05) and -0.12 (95% CI: -0.22, -0.2)], while RCTs in adults showed an increase in body weight when SSBs were added (random and fixed effects: 0.85 kg; 95% CI: 0.50, 1.20 kg). Sensitivity analyses of RCTs in children revealed more significant benefits in preventing weight gain in trials that substituted SSBs (compared to school-based educational programs) and among overweight children (compared to normal-weight children).

CONCLUSION: Our systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies and RCTs provide evidence that the consumption of SSBs promotes weight gain in both children and adults.

title: The tumorigenic potential of pluripotent stem cells: What can we do to minimize it?
text: Human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) possess the ability to revolutionize the treatment and comprehension of human diseases. However, it is crucial to acknowledge that these cells have an inherent tendency to develop tumors in individuals with compromised immune systems when introduced in their pluripotent state. Although current therapeutic approaches involve transplanting only differentiated hPSC derivatives, there remains a concern that a small fraction of undifferentiated cells may be present in the transplanted cell populations. Furthermore, these cells have been observed to undergo genetic alterations that, in certain cases, are linked to specific types of human cancers. In this article, we aim to distinguish between unwarranted panic and factual information, while objectively assessing the actual tumorigenic potential of these cells. Additionally, we explore a recent study that investigates the impact of culture conditions on the genetic stability of hPSCs. Lastly, we propose a set of practical guidelines to minimize the tumorigenic risk associated with hPSC-derived cells. © 2016 The Authors. Inside the Cell published by Wiley Periodicals, Inc.

title: Epidemiology of sepsis and septic shock in critical care units: comparison between sepsis-2 and sepsis-3 populations using a national critical care database
text:
The new definitions for sepsis and septic shock have the potential to change how we understand and study the epidemiology of these conditions. To investigate this, we analyzed a comprehensive database of intensive care unit (ICU) admissions in England over a five-year period. Our main focus was on acute hospital mortality as the primary outcome.

We compared the incidence, outcomes, trends, and predictive validity of sepsis and septic shock populations using both the old (Sepsis-2) and new (Sepsis-3) definitions. Out of a total of 197,724 cases of Sepsis-2 severe sepsis and 197,142 cases of Sepsis-3 sepsis, we identified 153,257 cases of Sepsis-2 septic shock and 39,262 cases of Sepsis-3 septic shock.

In 2015, the estimated incidence of Sepsis-3 sepsis and Sepsis-3 septic shock per 100,000 person-years was 101.8 and 19.3, respectively. We found that Sepsis-2 severe sepsis and Sepsis-3 sepsis had similar incidence rates and mortality rates, and both showed significant improvements in mortality over time after adjusting for risk factors. However, Sepsis-3 septic shock had a higher Acute Physiology And Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II) score, higher mortality rate, and no significant improvement in mortality over time compared to Sepsis-2 septic shock.

ICU admissions identified as either Sepsis-3 sepsis or septic shock, as well as Sepsis-2 severe sepsis or septic shock, had a significantly higher risk-adjusted odds of death compared to non-sepsis admissions. The predictive validity was found to be highest for Sepsis-3 septic shock.

In conclusion, our analysis of the ICU database revealed that the new Sepsis-3 definition identifies a similar sepsis population with a high degree of overlap with the Sepsis-2 definition. However, the Sepsis-3 definition identifies a smaller septic shock population with improved predictive validity.

title: Thymic expression of the golli-myelin basic protein gene in the SJL/J mouse
text: The aim of this study was to investigate the expression of the golli-MBP gene in the mouse thymus and to analyze the transcripts of this gene in the organ. It is believed that the T cell antigen-specific repertoire is influenced by the presence of self molecules in the thymus. Previous research has shown that the golli-MBP gene, which is similar to the myelin basic protein (MBP) gene, is expressed in immune cells. To determine if the golli-MBP gene is expressed in the thymus, cDNA from the thymus and other tissues was amplified using specific primers for MBP and golli-MBP. The amplified products were then analyzed using Southern blotting with oligonucleotide probes specific to different exons. The amplified products were further examined by subcloning and DNA sequencing to characterize the inserts. The results revealed that the thymic transcripts contained exons 1, 2, 3, 5A, 5B, 5C, 6, 7, 8, and 11 of the golli-MBP gene.

title: Urine microRNAs as biomarkers for bladder cancer: a diagnostic meta-analysis
text:
BACKGROUND: The diagnostic value of microRNA (miRNA) detection in bladder cancer (BCa) patients is a topic of debate. We conducted a meta-analysis to assess the current evidence on the use of miRNA assays for diagnosing BCa.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science for studies published before March 31, 2015. We calculated pooled sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative likelihood ratios, diagnostic odds ratio, and area under the curve (AUC) to evaluate overall test performance. Subgroup analyses were conducted to explore heterogeneity between studies. Deeks' funnel plot asymmetry test was used to assess publication bias. We used RevMan 5.2 and Stata 11.0 software for the meta-analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 23 studies from nine articles were included in the meta-analysis, involving 719 patients and 494 controls. The pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.75 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.68-0.80) and 0.75 (95% CI, 0.70-0.80), respectively. The pooled positive likelihood ratio was 3.03 (95% CI, 2.50-3.67), negative likelihood ratio was 0.33 (95% CI, 0.27-0.42), and diagnostic odds ratio was 9.07 (95% CI, 6.35-12.95). The pooled AUC was 0.81 (95% CI, 0.78-0.85). Subgroup analyses indicated that multiple miRNA assays and urine supernatant assays had high accuracy in diagnosing BCa.

CONCLUSION: MiRNA assays have the potential to be a noninvasive diagnostic tool for detecting BCa. However, further validation through large prospective studies is necessary for their clinical application in BCa diagnosis.

title: Elevated Plasma Transforming Growth Factor &bgr;1 Levels Predict the Development of Hypertension in Normotensives: The 14-Year Follow-Up Study
text:
BACKGROUND: Transforming growth factor β1 (TGF-β1) is a cytokine with multiple functions. There is increasing evidence suggesting that TGF-β1 plays a role in the development of hypertension and target organ damage in individuals with hypertension. While previous studies have shown that TGF-β1 induces vascular hypertrophy and remodeling in various vascular diseases, there is a lack of longitudinal data on hypertension in epidemiological studies. The aim of this study was to investigate whether elevated levels of TGF-β1 can predict the development of hypertension.

METHODS: Between 2002 and 2004, a total of 528 individuals underwent health examinations in Uku town, southwestern Japan. Blood pressure (BP), body mass index, and blood tests were conducted. Data on fasting plasma TGF-β1 levels were collected from all 528 individuals. Among them, 149 individuals who were normotensive (BP <140/90 mm Hg without antihypertensive medications) at baseline were followed-up for a period of 14 years.

RESULTS: Using a receiver-operating characteristic curve, a cutoff value of 8.9 ng/ml for plasma TGF-β1 levels was calculated. Out of the 149 normotensive individuals at baseline, 59 subjects developed hypertension during the follow-up period. After adjusting for confounding factors, there was a significant association between plasma TGF-β1 levels and the development of hypertension. Logistic regression analysis was performed to further examine this association. The baseline plasma TGF-β1 levels were divided into two groups using the cutoff value. The highest group of TGF-β1 levels showed a significantly higher odds ratio [3.582 (95% confidence interval, 1.025-12.525)] for the development of hypertension compared to the lowest group, even after adjusting for confounders.

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the first evidence of a causal relationship between elevated plasma TGF-β1 levels and the development of hypertension in normotensive individuals within a community-dwelling Japanese population.

title: MYC Disrupts the Circadian Clock and Metabolism in Cancer Cells.
text: The MYC oncogene produces a transcription factor called MYC, which binds to specific sites in the genome known as E-boxes (5'-CACGTG-3'). These E-boxes are the same binding sites used by the CLOCK-BMAL1 master circadian transcription factor. Based on this, we hypothesized that abnormal expression of MYC disrupts the circadian clock in cancer cells by affecting E-box-driven components of the circadian network. Our findings show that deregulated expression of MYC or N-MYC directly interferes with the molecular clock in laboratory settings. This interference occurs through the induction of REV-ERBα, which reduces the expression and oscillation of BMAL1. However, we found that knocking down REV-ERB can rescue this disruption. In neuroblastomas driven by N-MYC, high expression of REV-ERBα predicts a poor clinical outcome, as these tumors have reduced levels of BMAL1. Interestingly, reintroducing BMAL1 into neuroblastoma cell lines suppresses their ability to form colonies. Additionally, abnormal expression of MYC significantly affects the oscillation of glucose metabolism and disrupts glutaminolysis. These results reveal an unexpected connection between oncogenic transformation and disturbances in circadian and metabolic rhythms. We believe that these dysrhythmias may provide an advantage for cancer cells.

title: Integrated maps in quail (Coturnix japonica) confirm the high degree of synteny conservation with chicken (Gallus gallus) despite 35 million years of divergence
text: The comparison of the quail genome with that of the chicken allows us to detect chromosome rearrangements that have occurred over 35 million years of evolution. This information helps us predict the position of genes in quail based on the chicken sequence, which improves our understanding of the quail genome structure and enhances its utility in biological studies. Previous research has provided a genetic map for quail using microsatellite and AFLP markers, as well as comparative cytogenetic data with chicken for macrochromosomes. In this study, we have expanded and integrated these maps to create a comprehensive linkage map for quail. The map consists of 14 autosomal linkage groups and a Z chromosome-specific linkage group, aligned with the quail AFLP map. The size of the linkage groups varies, with a total map distance of 904.3 cM and an average spacing of 9.7 cM between loci. However, there are still some regions of the quail genome that have not been assigned markers. By aligning the quail linkage groups with the chicken genome sequence assembly, we have confirmed the high conservation of gene order between the two species for macrochromosomes. Additionally, our study suggests that there is valuable information in the chicken genome that can be used for genome analyses in quail, particularly for microchromosomes. Integrating the microsatellite and AFLP quail genetic maps improves the quality of the information and will facilitate the identification of Quantitative Trait Loci (QTL).

title: Cadherin activity is required for activity-induced spine remodeling
text: The activity of neurons causes changes in the structure of the membranes before and after synapses, which are held together by cell adhesion molecules. One of these molecules, N-cadherin, is redistributed and undergoes changes in shape due to neural activity, and it is necessary for synaptic plasticity. In this study, we demonstrate that depolarization leads to an increase in the width of the spine head, and that the activity of cadherin is crucial for this rearrangement of synapses. Using green fluorescent protein to visualize dendritic spines in hippocampal neurons, we observed that activation of the AMPA receptor caused the expansion of the spines, resulting in a larger synaptic apposition zone. The N-cadherin-venus fusion protein spread out along the expanding spine head. When dominant-negative forms of N-cadherin were overexpressed, the expansion of the spines was prevented. Additionally, inhibiting actin polymerization with cytochalasin D stopped the expansion of the spines. These findings suggest that the adhesion machinery based on cadherin, along with the actin-cytoskeleton, plays a crucial role in remodeling the synaptic apposition zone.

title: Aliskiren combined with losartan in type 2 diabetes and nephropathy.
text:
In developed countries, diabetic nephropathy is the primary cause of end-stage renal disease. We conducted a study to assess the renoprotective benefits of dual blockade of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system by adding aliskiren, an oral direct renin inhibitor, to the recommended dose of losartan (100 mg daily) and optimal antihypertensive therapy in patients with hypertension and type 2 diabetes with nephropathy.

For this multinational, randomized, double-blind study, we enrolled 599 patients. After a 3-month open-label run-in period with 100 mg of losartan daily, patients were randomly assigned to receive either aliskiren (150 mg daily for 3 months, followed by an increase to 300 mg daily for another 3 months) or placebo, in addition to losartan. The primary outcome measured at 6 months was a reduction in the albumin-to-creatinine ratio in an early-morning urine sample.

The baseline characteristics of both groups were similar. Treatment with 300 mg of aliskiren daily resulted in a 20% reduction in the mean urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio compared to placebo (95% confidence interval, 9 to 30; P<0.001). Additionally, 24.7% of patients receiving aliskiren experienced a reduction of 50% or more in the ratio, compared to 12.5% in the placebo group (P<0.001). There was a slight difference in blood pressure between the groups at the end of the study, with the aliskiren group showing a 2 mm Hg lower systolic pressure (P=0.07) and a 1 mm Hg lower diastolic pressure (P=0.08). The incidence of adverse events and serious adverse events was similar in both groups.

In conclusion, aliskiren may have renoprotective effects independent of its blood-pressure-lowering effect in patients with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and nephropathy who are already receiving recommended renoprotective treatment. (ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00097955 [ClinicalTrials.gov].)

title: Overweight in Celiac Disease: Prevalence, Clinical Characteristics, and Effect of a Gluten-Free Diet
text:
BACKGROUND: The fact that only a small number of celiac patients experience typical symptoms due to malabsorption is widely known. However, there have been limited studies focusing on the distribution of body mass index (BMI) in celiac populations and its correlation with clinical characteristics, as well as its response to treatment. 

METHODS: We examined BMI measurements, along with other clinical and pathological characteristics, from a database of 371 celiac patients who were diagnosed over a 10-year period and treated by a single gastroenterologist. To evaluate the effectiveness of gluten exclusion, we compared the BMI at the time of diagnosis with the BMI after 2 years of treatment in patients who showed serological evidence of dietary compliance. 

RESULTS: The average BMI was 24.6 kg/m2 (ranging from 16.3 to 43.5). Out of all the patients, 17 (5%) were underweight (BMI <18.5), 211 (57%) had a normal weight, and 143 (39%) were overweight (BMI ≥25), including 48 (13% of all patients) who fell into the obese category (BMI ≥30.0). We found a significant correlation between low BMI and female gender, a history of diarrhea, decreased hemoglobin levels, reduced bone mineral density (BMD), osteoporosis, and higher grades (subtotal/total) of villous atrophy. Among patients who adhered to a gluten-free diet, 81% experienced weight gain after 2 years, including 82% of those who were initially overweight. 

CONCLUSIONS: At the time of diagnosis, only a small percentage of celiac patients are underweight, while a significant minority are overweight. These overweight patients are less likely to exhibit typical symptoms such as diarrhea and reduced hemoglobin levels. The failure or delay in diagnosing celiac disease may be attributed to a lack of awareness regarding this particular subgroup. The weight gain observed in already overweight patients after adopting a gluten-free diet can lead to additional health issues, suggesting that modifications should be made to the conventional approach of prescribing a gluten-free diet.

title: Structural Studies of a Four-MBT Repeat Protein MBTD1
text: The Polycomb group (PcG) proteins are a family of proteins that play a crucial role in development. They form large protein complexes that are involved in controlling the expression of genes related to development. One of these PcG proteins is called MBTD1, which contains four MBT repeats. In this study, we determined the crystal structure of MBTD1 and found that it is similar to another protein called L3MBTL2, which also has four MBT repeats and binds to methylated lysine histones. Our experiments confirmed that MBTD1 specifically binds to histone peptides that are mono- or di-methylated at lysine residues, similar to L3MBTL1 and L3MBTL2. Previous studies have shown that MBT-peptide complexes do not have a strong preference for specific histone peptide sequences, but instead recognize the methylated lysine in a "cavity insertion recognition mode." However, our mutagenesis data suggest that histone peptides cannot bind to MBT repeats in any orientation. The four MBT repeats in MBTD1 have an asymmetric rhomboid structure, and like other MBT repeat proteins, MBTD1 binds to mono- or dimethylated lysine histones using one of its four MBT repeats and a semi-aromatic cage.

title: Glutamine supports pancreatic cancer growth through a Kras-regulated metabolic pathway
text: Cancer cells have unique metabolic dependencies that set them apart from normal cells. One of these dependencies is an increased reliance on the amino acid glutamine to fuel their growth. The specific types of tumors that depend on glutamine and the mechanisms by which glutamine supports cancer metabolism are still being actively studied. In this study, we have discovered a non-traditional pathway of glutamine utilization in human pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cells, which is crucial for tumor growth. While most cells use an enzyme called glutamate dehydrogenase (GLUD1) to convert glutamine-derived glutamate into a molecule called α-ketoglutarate in the mitochondria, which then fuels the tricarboxylic acid cycle, PDAC cells rely on a different pathway. In this pathway, glutamine-derived aspartate is transported into the cytoplasm, where it is converted into oxaloacetate by an enzyme called aspartate transaminase (GOT1). This oxaloacetate is then converted into malate and finally pyruvate, which potentially increases the NADPH/NADP(+) ratio and helps maintain the cellular redox state. Importantly, PDAC cells heavily depend on this series of reactions. When glutamine is deprived or any enzyme in this pathway is genetically inhibited, PDAC cells experience an increase in reactive oxygen species and a decrease in reduced glutathione. Additionally, when any component enzyme in this pathway is knocked down, PDAC growth is significantly suppressed both in laboratory settings and in living organisms. Furthermore, we have found that the reprogramming of glutamine metabolism in PDAC is driven by an oncogene called KRAS, which is a common genetic alteration in this type of cancer. KRAS regulates the expression of key metabolic enzymes in this pathway, leading to the essentiality of this pathway in PDAC cells while being dispensable in normal cells. These findings suggest that targeting this pathway could be a promising therapeutic strategy for treating PDAC, which is known to be resistant to current treatments.

title: CD4+ T cell help guides formation of CD103+ lung-resident memory CD8+ T cells during influenza viral infection.
text: Tissue-resident memory T (Trm) cells play a crucial role in protecting mucosal sites from infection. Our study reveals that CD4(+) T cells are essential for the formation of functional lung-resident CD8(+) T cells during influenza virus infection. In the absence of CD4(+) T cells, CD8(+) T cells showed reduced expression of CD103 (Itgae), were not properly located near airway epithelia, and had a diminished ability to recruit CD8(+) T cells to the lung airways when faced with a different subtype of the virus. Interferon-γ produced by CD4(+) T cells was necessary for the generation of lung-resident CD103(+) CD8(+) Trm cells. Additionally, the transcription factor T-bet was found to be increased in "unhelped" lung Trm cells, but reducing T-bet levels restored CD103 expression in the absence of CD4(+) T cell assistance. Therefore, signals from CD4(+) T cells are crucial in regulating T-bet expression and facilitating the development of CD103(+) CD8(+) Trm cells in the lung airways following respiratory infection.

title: Inhibition of Apoptosis Overcomes Stage-Related Compatibility Barriers to Chimera Formation in Mouse Embryos.
text:
Advanced cell types in development, such as EpiSCs, are unable to contribute to chimeras when injected into blastocysts at the pre-implantation stage. This is likely due to the injected cells undergoing apoptosis. However, we have discovered that by temporarily promoting cell survival through the expression of the anti-apoptotic gene BCL2, EpiSCs and Sox17+ endoderm progenitors can successfully integrate into blastocysts and contribute to the development of chimeric embryos.

When BCL2-expressing EpiSCs were injected into blastocysts, they were able to contribute to all bodily tissues in the resulting chimeric animals. Similarly, Sox17+ endoderm progenitors specifically contributed to endodermal tissues in a region-specific manner. Furthermore, the expression of BCL2 allowed rat EpiSCs to contribute to mouse embryonic chimeras, resulting in the formation of interspecies chimeras that could survive into adulthood.

Our findings present a solution to the compatibility issues that typically hinder chimera formation. By utilizing this approach, we can expand the use of embryonic chimeras, including region-specific chimeras, for both basic developmental biology research and regenerative medicine.

title: Computational and Statistical Analyses of Amino Acid Usage and Physico-Chemical Properties of the Twelve Late Embryogenesis Abundant Protein Classes
text:
Late Embryogenesis Abundant Proteins (LEAPs) are widely distributed proteins that are believed to play significant roles in the ability of organisms to tolerate desiccation. However, our understanding of the relationship between their structure and function is limited due to the lack of available 3-D structures for LEAPs. To address this gap, we previously created LEAPdb, a database specifically dedicated to LEAPs from plants and other organisms. Through this database, we were able to classify 710 LEAPs into 12 distinct classes with unique properties.

Using the resources provided by LEAPdb, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of the physico-chemical properties and amino acid usage of LEAPs. This analysis revealed distinct characteristics for each class, allowing for a thorough characterization of the 12 LEAP classes. Additionally, we found that while most LEAPs are predicted to be intrinsically disordered proteins, LEAP class 7 (PF03168) and possibly LEAP class 11 (PF04927) are likely to be natively folded proteins.

This study provides a detailed description of the structural properties of the LEAP protein family, which paves the way for further analysis of their structure and function. Furthermore, the unique physico-chemical properties associated with each LEAP class will enable the development of software capable of predicting proteins as LEAPs.

title: Direct Reprogramming of Hepatic Myofibroblasts into Hepatocytes In Vivo Attenuates Liver Fibrosis.
text: The direct conversion of fibroblasts into induced hepatocytes (iHeps) has shown promise as a regenerative medicine strategy, but has only been demonstrated in laboratory settings. In this study, we present the successful formation of iHeps in vivo using transcription factor induction and genetic fate tracing in mouse models of chronic liver disease. By introducing the transcription factors FOXA3, GATA4, HNF1A, and HNF4A through a lentiviral vector, we were able to transform mouse myofibroblasts into cells with hepatocyte characteristics. Additionally, when these same transcription factors were expressed in fibrotic mouse livers using a p75 neurotrophin receptor peptide (p75NTRp)-tagged adenovirus, we observed the generation of hepatocyte-like cells and a reduction in liver fibrosis. This innovative approach of directly reprogramming pro-fibrogenic myofibroblasts into hepatocyte-like cells holds great potential for the treatment of chronic liver disease.

title: Epithelial to Mesenchymal Transition by TGFβ-1 Induction Increases Stemness Characteristics in Primary Non Small Cell Lung Cancer Cell Line
text:
The Cancer Stem Cells (CSCs) hypothesis suggests that only a small portion of cells within a tumor have the ability to initiate and sustain tumor growth. The Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition (EMT) is a developmental program that is often activated during the invasion and spread of cancer. This study aims to explore the relationship between EMT and CSCs using the LC31 lung cancer primary cell line. 

To investigate EMT, the A549 and LC31 cell lines were treated with 2 ng/ml TGFβ-1 for 30 and 80 days, respectively. Morphological changes were assessed using light microscopy, immunofluorescence, and cytometry to examine markers such as cytokeratins, e-cadherin, CD326 (epithelial markers), and CD90 and vimentin (mesenchymal markers). Additionally, RT-PCR was performed to analyze the expression of Slug, Twist, and β-catenin genes. Stemness tests, including pneumosphere growth and the expression of stem markers Oct4, Nanog, Sox2, c-kit, and CD133, were conducted on the TGFβ-1 treated and untreated LC31 cell lines. Western Blot and tumorigenicity assays using NOD/SCID mice were also performed to assess CD133 expression and tumor-forming ability, respectively. 

The results showed that the TGFβ-1 treated LC31 cell line and the control A549 cell line both exhibited a loss of epithelial morphology and acquired a fibroblast-like appearance. Immunofluorescence and cytometry analysis revealed an up-regulation of vimentin and CD90, as well as a down-regulation of cytokeratin, e-cadherin, and CD326 in the TGFβ-1 treated LC31 and A549 cell lines. The up-regulation of Slug, Twist, and β-catenin mRNA transcripts in the TGFβ-1 treated LC31 cell line confirmed the occurrence of EMT. Furthermore, this cell line demonstrated an over-expression of Oct4, Nanog, Sox2, and CD133, which are all stem cell markers. Additionally, the TGFβ-1 treated LC31 cell line exhibited an increased capacity to form pneumospheres and the ability to form tumors in NOD/SCID mice. 

In conclusion, the induction of EMT through TGFβ-1 exposure in the primary lung cancer cell line resulted in the acquisition of a mesenchymal profile and the expression of stem cell markers.

title: Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b Associate with Enhancers to Regulate Human Epidermal Stem Cell Homeostasis.
text: The localization and function of endogenous Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b in adult stem cells throughout the genome are currently unknown. However, our study demonstrates that in human epidermal stem cells, these two proteins bind to the most active enhancers in a histone H3K36me3-dependent manner. Additionally, they are essential for the production of enhancer RNAs associated with these enhancers. Both Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b show a preference for super-enhancers that are linked to genes involved in defining the ectodermal lineage or establishing the stem cell and differentiated states. However, they differ in their mechanisms of enhancer regulation. Dnmt3a works in conjunction with p63 to maintain high levels of DNA hydroxymethylation at the center of enhancers, relying on Tet2 for this process. On the other hand, Dnmt3b promotes DNA methylation along the body of the enhancer. Depletion of either protein leads to the inactivation of their target enhancers and has a profound impact on the function of epidermal stem cells. Overall, our findings uncover new roles for Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b at enhancers, which could contribute to their involvement in disease and tumorigenesis.

title: CDK inhibitors in cancer therapy: what is next?
text: For over 15 years, there has been a strong focus on finding drugs that can inhibit cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs). The development of first-generation inhibitors, such as Flavopiridol and CY-202, has reached the late stages of clinical trials. However, their effectiveness has been only modest thus far. As a result, several second-generation inhibitors are currently being tested in clinical trials. To determine the clinical benefits of CDK inhibitors in cancer therapy, future approaches should take into account the lessons learned from these early compounds and the recent genetic analysis of CDKs in preclinical models. In this discussion, we will explore key concepts that should be considered when validating the clinical usefulness of CDK inhibitors.

title: Lipid Desaturation Is a Metabolic Marker and Therapeutic Target of Ovarian Cancer Stem Cells.
text: The lack of tools for analyzing individual cells has hindered the understanding of metabolic activity in cancer stem cells. However, through the use of hyperspectral-stimulated Raman scattering imaging and mass spectrometry analysis, we have discovered that ovarian cancer stem cells (CSCs) have significantly higher levels of unsaturated lipids compared to non-CSCs. We also found that CSC-enriched spheroids have higher lipid unsaturation levels than monolayer cultures of ovarian cancer cell lines or primary cells. By inhibiting lipid desaturases, we were able to effectively eliminate CSCs, suppress sphere formation in vitro, and block tumor initiation capacity in vivo. Our research also revealed that the expression levels of lipid desaturases are directly regulated by nuclear factor κB (NF-κB), and inhibiting desaturases blocks NF-κB signaling. Overall, our findings suggest that increased lipid unsaturation can serve as a metabolic marker for ovarian CSCs and a potential target for CSC-specific therapy.

title: Mesenchymal Inflammation Drives Genotoxic Stress in Hematopoietic Stem Cells and Predicts Disease Evolution in Human Pre-leukemia.
text: The molecular mechanisms and relevance to human disease of mesenchymal niche cells driving tissue failure and malignant transformation in the hematopoietic system are not well understood. In this study, we investigated the effects of perturbing mesenchymal cells in a mouse model of the pre-leukemic disorder Shwachman-Diamond syndrome (SDS). We found that this perturbation led to mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and activation of DNA damage responses in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells. Through RNA sequencing of purified mesenchymal cells in the SDS mouse model and various human pre-leukemic syndromes, we identified p53-S100A8/9-TLR inflammatory signaling as a common mechanism driving genotoxic stress. Activation of this signaling axis in the mesenchymal niche was found to predict leukemic evolution and progression-free survival in myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS), the main leukemia predisposition syndrome. Overall, our results highlight the role of mesenchymal niche-induced genotoxic stress in heterotypic stem and progenitor cells through inflammatory signaling as a targetable factor influencing disease outcome in human pre-leukemia.

title: Novel Functional Sets of Lipid-Derived Mediators with Antiinflammatory Actions Generated from Omega-3 Fatty Acids via Cyclooxygenase 2–Nonsteroidal Antiinflammatory Drugs and Transcellular Processing
text: Aspirin therapy works by inhibiting the production of prostaglandins, but it does not directly affect lipoxygenases. Instead, it acetylates cyclooxygenase 2 (COX-2), leading to the production of bioactive lipoxins (LXs) that are epimeric at carbon 15 (referred to as 15-epi-LX or aspirin-triggered LX [ATL]). In this study, we discovered that when mice were treated with ω-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids and aspirin (ASA), their inflammatory exudates produced a new set of bioactive lipid signals. Human endothelial cells with increased COX-2 levels, when treated with ASA, converted C20:5 ω-3 into 18R-hydroxyeicosapentaenoic acid (HEPE) and 15R-HEPE. Polymorphonuclear leukocytes then used these compounds to generate different types of novel trihydroxy-containing mediators, including 5-series 15R-LX5 and 5,12,18R-triHEPE. These newly discovered compounds were found to be powerful inhibitors of human polymorphonuclear leukocyte transendothelial migration and infiltration in vivo (with ATL analogue being the most potent, followed by 5,12,18R-triHEPE and 18R-HEPE). Acetaminophen and indomethacin also allowed for the generation of 18R-HEPE and 15R-HEPE through recombinant COX-2, as well as the oxygenation of other fatty acids that affect hematologic cells. These findings reveal new pathways for the production of bioactive lipid mediators through COX-2-dependent oxygenations and cell-cell interactions, which have an impact on microinflammation. The discovery of these compounds and their related compounds provides a new mechanism for the therapeutic benefits of ω-3 dietary supplementation, which could be significant in the treatment of inflammation, neoplasia, and vascular diseases.
