The degradation of lamin B1 occurs through transport from the nucleus to the cytoplasm, ultimately leading to its breakdown in the lysosome. When autophagy or the interaction between LC3 and lamin B1 is inhibited, the loss of lamin B1 induced by activated RAS is prevented, and the senescence caused by oncogenes is reduced in primary human cells. These findings suggest that autophagy serves as a protective mechanism against tumorigenesis by degrading nuclear components.

title: Pro-resolving lipid mediators are leads for resolution physiology
text: Recent advancements in our comprehension of the processes involved in resolving acute inflammation have revealed a novel category of lipid mediators known as specialized pro-resolving mediators. This group includes the lipoxin, resolvin, protectin, and maresin families. Synthetic versions of these mediators have demonstrated potent bioactivities when administered in vivo. Animal experiments have shown that these mediators elicit anti-inflammatory and innovative pro-resolving mechanisms, while also improving microbial clearance. Although their identification primarily stems from their role in inflammation resolution, specialized pro-resolving mediators are structurally conserved and also play a crucial role in host defense, pain management, organ protection, and tissue remodeling. This comprehensive review delves into the mechanisms of specialized pro-resolving mediators and the pathways of omega-3 essential fatty acids, shedding light on their physiological functions.

title: ZMYND11 links histone H3.3K36me3 to transcription elongation and tumour suppression
text:
The regulation of chromatin relies heavily on proteins known as 'reader' proteins, which are responsible for recognizing modified histones. One such modification, H3K36 trimethylation (H3K36me3), is added to nucleosomes in transcribed regions after RNA polymerase II elongation. In yeast, this modification recruits epigenetic regulators that reset the chromatin to a repressive state, preventing unwanted transcription. However, the role of H3K36me3 in transcription regulation in mammals is not well understood, especially considering the incorporation of the histone variant H3.3 during transcription. 

In this study, we demonstrate that the potential tumor suppressor protein ZMYND11 specifically recognizes H3K36me3 on H3.3 (H3.3K36me3) and regulates RNA polymerase II elongation. Structural analysis reveals that ZMYND11's PWWP domain binds to the trimethyl-lysine, while the recognition of H3.3 is facilitated by the tandem bromo-PWWP domains encapsulating the H3.3-specific 'Ser 31' residue. Chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by sequencing confirms that ZMYND11 co-localizes with H3K36me3 and H3.3 in gene bodies throughout the genome, and its presence requires the prior deposition of H3.3K36me3. 

Despite its association with highly expressed genes, ZMYND11 functions as an unconventional transcription co-repressor by modulating RNA polymerase II during the elongation stage. ZMYND11 is crucial for repressing a transcriptional program that is vital for tumor cell growth. Low expression levels of ZMYND11 in breast cancer patients are associated with a worse prognosis. Consistently, overexpression of ZMYND11 inhibits cancer cell growth in vitro and tumor formation in mice. This study establishes ZMYND11 as an H3.3-specific reader of H3K36me3, linking histone-variant-mediated transcription elongation control to tumor suppression.

title: Autocrine BDNF–TrkB signalling within a single dendritic spine
text: The role of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and its receptor TrkB in neuronal plasticity, specifically structural long-term potentiation (sLTP), which is linked to learning in animals, is not fully understood. This study aims to investigate whether BDNF release and TrkB activation occur during sLTP, and if so, when and where. To do this, the researchers used a fluorescence resonance energy transfer-based sensor for TrkB and two-photon fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy to monitor TrkB activity in individual dendritic spines of CA1 pyramidal neurons in cultured murine hippocampal slices. The results show that in response to sLTP induction, there is a rapid and sustained activation of TrkB in the stimulated spine, which depends on NMDAR and CaMKII signaling, as well as BDNF synthesized postsynaptically. The presence of postsynaptic BDNF was confirmed using electron microscopy to locate endogenous BDNF in the dendrites and spines of hippocampal CA1 pyramidal neurons. Additionally, the study demonstrates the rapid release of BDNF from single dendritic spines in response to glutamate uncaging, using BDNF fused to superecliptic pHluorin. The researchers also show that this postsynaptic BDNF-TrkB signaling pathway is necessary for both structural and functional LTP. Overall, these findings reveal a spine-autonomous, autocrine signaling mechanism involving NMDAR-CaMKII-dependent BDNF release from stimulated dendritic spines and subsequent TrkB activation on the same spines, which is crucial for structural and functional plasticity.

title: Whole genomes redefine the mutational landscape of pancreatic cancer
text: Pancreatic cancer remains a highly lethal form of cancer and a significant burden on public health. In our study, we conducted whole-genome sequencing and analysis of copy number variation in 100 cases of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). We found that chromosomal rearrangements leading to gene disruption were common, affecting genes known to play a crucial role in pancreatic cancer (TP53, SMAD4, CDKN2A, ARID1A, and ROBO2), as well as identifying new potential drivers of pancreatic carcinogenesis (KDM6A and PREX2). By examining patterns of structural variation, we were able to classify PDACs into four subtypes with potential clinical significance: stable, locally rearranged, scattered, and unstable. A significant number of cases showed focal amplifications, many of which contained targetable oncogenes (ERBB2, MET, FGFR1, CDK6, PIK3R3, and PIK3CA), although these were present at low frequencies in individual patients. We also observed that genomic instability was associated with inactivation of DNA maintenance genes (BRCA1, BRCA2, or PALB2) and a mutational signature indicating deficiency in DNA damage repair. Notably, among the eight patients who received platinum therapy, four out of five individuals with these markers of defective DNA maintenance showed a positive response.

title: Human oocytes reprogram adult somatic nuclei of a type 1 diabetic to diploid pluripotent stem cells
text: The transfer of nuclei from somatic cells into oocytes has the potential to generate pluripotent stem cells that are consistently equivalent to embryonic stem cells. This holds promise for autologous cell replacement therapy. While methods to induce pluripotent stem cells from somatic cells using transcription factors are commonly used in basic research, there have been numerous reported differences between induced pluripotent stem cells and embryonic stem cells, which could impact their clinical application. To explore the therapeutic potential of diploid embryonic stem cell lines derived from adult cells of diseased human subjects, we conducted a systematic investigation into the factors affecting the efficiency of blastocyst development and stem cell derivation. Our findings demonstrate that improvements to the oocyte activation protocol, including the use of kinase and translation inhibitors, as well as cell culture in the presence of histone deacetylase inhibitors, enhance development to the blastocyst stage. The efficiency of development varied among oocyte donors and was inversely related to the duration of hormonal stimulation required for oocyte maturation. However, the daily dose of gonadotropin or the total number of metaphase II oocytes retrieved did not impact developmental outcome. To prevent premature oocyte activation caused by an increase in intracellular calcium concentration induced by concentrated Sendai virus for cell fusion, we utilized diluted Sendai virus in calcium-free medium. By employing this modified nuclear transfer protocol, we successfully derived diploid pluripotent stem cell lines from somatic cells of both a newborn and, for the first time, an adult female with type 1 diabetes.

title: A three-dimensional human neural cell culture model of Alzheimer’s disease
text: Alzheimer's disease is the most prevalent type of dementia and is characterized by two main features: amyloid-β plaques and neurofibrillary tangles. The amyloid hypothesis suggests that the excessive buildup of amyloid-β peptide leads to the formation of neurofibrillary tangles made up of aggregated hyperphosphorylated tau. However, so far, no disease model has successfully linked these two pathological events using human neuronal cells. Mouse models with familial Alzheimer's disease (FAD) mutations show synaptic and memory deficits caused by amyloid-β, but they do not fully replicate other key aspects of Alzheimer's disease, such as distinct neurofibrillary tangle pathology. Human neurons derived from Alzheimer's disease patients have shown increased levels of toxic amyloid-β and phosphorylated tau, but they do not exhibit amyloid-β plaques or neurofibrillary tangles. In this study, we demonstrate that FAD mutations in β-amyloid precursor protein and presenilin 1 can induce significant extracellular deposition of amyloid-β, including amyloid-β plaques, in a three-dimensional (3D) culture system derived from human neural stem cells. Importantly, the 3D-differentiated neuronal cells expressing FAD mutations also exhibit high levels of detergent-resistant, silver-positive aggregates of phosphorylated tau in both the cell body and neurites, as well as filamentous tau, as observed through immunoelectron microscopy. Inhibiting the generation of amyloid-β using β- or γ-secretase inhibitors not only reduces amyloid-β pathology but also attenuates tauopathy. Additionally, we discovered that glycogen synthase kinase 3 (GSK3) regulates amyloid-β-induced tau phosphorylation. Our successful replication of amyloid-β and tau pathology in a single 3D human neural cell culture system provides a unique approach for studying Alzheimer's disease and may aid in the development of more accurate human neural cell models for other neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Mesenchymal-endothelial-transition contributes to cardiac neovascularization
text: Endothelial cells play a role in the development of a specific type of cardiac fibroblasts through a process called endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition. However, it is unclear whether cardiac fibroblasts can transform into endothelial cells and directly contribute to the formation of new blood vessels after a cardiac injury. In this study, we used genetic fate mapping techniques to show that cardiac fibroblasts quickly acquire characteristics similar to endothelial cells following an acute ischemic cardiac injury. These fibroblast-derived endothelial cells exhibit both structural and functional features of native endothelial cells. We also discovered that the transcription factor p53 regulates this transformation of cardiac fibroblasts. When p53 is absent in cardiac fibroblasts, the formation of fibroblast-derived endothelial cells is significantly reduced, leading to a decrease in vascular density and worsening of cardiac function after an infarction. On the other hand, activating the p53 pathway in cardiac fibroblasts enhances the transition from mesenchymal to endothelial cells, resulting in increased vascularity and improved cardiac function. These findings highlight the importance of mesenchymal-to-endothelial transition in the formation of new blood vessels in the injured heart and suggest that targeting this process could be a potential therapeutic strategy for enhancing cardiac repair.

title: Estimation of optimal serum concentrations of 25-hydroxyvitamin D for multiple health outcomes.
text: New evidence indicates that higher vitamin D intakes than currently recommended may have positive effects on health. However, the ideal levels of 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] in the blood have not been determined. This review examines studies that have explored the thresholds for 25(OH)D concentrations in relation to bone mineral density (BMD), lower-extremity function, dental health, and the risk of falls, fractures, and colorectal cancer. The findings suggest that the most beneficial 25(OH)D concentrations start at 75 nmol/L (30 ng/mL), with the optimal range being between 90 and 100 nmol/L (36-40 ng/mL). However, the currently recommended vitamin D intakes of 200 and 600 IU per day for younger and older adults, respectively, are unlikely to achieve these concentrations in most individuals. Therefore, it is suggested that an increase in the recommended intake of vitamin D is necessary for younger adults to maintain bone health and for older adults to improve various health outcomes. To ensure that at least 50% of the population reaches a 25(OH)D concentration of 75 nmol/L, it is recommended that all adults consume more than 1000 IU (25 microg) of vitamin D (cholecalciferol) per day. The potential implications of higher doses for the entire adult population should be investigated in future studies.

title: Cohesin-dependent globules and heterochromatin shape 3D genome architecture in S. pombe
text: The three-dimensional structures of eukaryotic genomes, such as self-associating topological domains, are not well understood in terms of how they are governed by local chromatin interactions and the role of cohesin in this process. To address this, we conducted a genome-wide chromatin conformation capture (Hi-C) analysis of the Schizosaccharomyces pombe genome, which shares fundamental features with other eukaryotes despite its small size. Our analysis of both wild-type and mutant strains revealed important aspects of chromosome architecture and genome organization. We observed that small regions of chromatin on chromosome arms interact locally to form "globules." Interestingly, this globule formation requires a different function of cohesin than its role in sister chromatid cohesion. Cohesin is found at the boundaries of these globules, and its loss disrupts both local globule structures and the overall organization of chromosomes. On the other hand, heterochromatin, which loads cohesin at specific sites like pericentromeric and subtelomeric domains, is not necessary for globule formation but still influences genome organization. We discovered that heterochromatin compacts chromatin fibers at centromeres and promotes significant interactions between different chromosome arms in centromere-proximal regions. These interactions provide important structural constraints for proper genome organization. When heterochromatin is lost, these constraints are relaxed, leading to an increase in both intra- and inter-chromosomal interactions. Overall, our findings reveal fundamental principles of genome folding that drive the higher-order organization of chromosomes, which is crucial for coordinating nuclear functions.

title: A temporal shift in the circuits mediating retrieval of fear memory
text: Fear memories play a vital role in helping animals avoid danger and increase their chances of survival. While it is known that fear memories can be recalled long after they are learned, little is understood about how the circuits involved in retrieval change over time. In this study, we focused on the dorsal midline thalamus of rats and discovered that it is necessary for the retrieval of auditory conditioned fear at later time points (24 hours, 7 days, 28 days) but not earlier time points (0.5 hours, 6 hours) after learning. We also found that the paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus (PVT), a specific region within the dorsal midline thalamus, exhibited increased c-Fos expression only at later time points, suggesting that the PVT gradually becomes involved in fear retrieval. Additionally, the responses of PVT neurons to the conditioned tone increased over time following training. The prefrontal cortex's prelimbic (PL) region, which is known to be essential for fear retrieval, sends dense connections to the PVT. Activation of PL neurons projecting to the PVT was observed during retrieval at later time points, and when these connections were silenced using optogenetics, retrieval was impaired at later but not earlier time points. On the other hand, silencing PL inputs to the basolateral amygdala impaired retrieval at earlier but not later time points, indicating a time-dependent shift in the circuits involved in retrieval. Furthermore, we found that retrieval at later time points also activated PVT neurons projecting to the central nucleus of the amygdala, and silencing these projections induced a persistent reduction in fear only at later time points. These findings suggest that the PVT plays a crucial role as a thalamic hub in the cortico-amygdalar networks involved in the retrieval and maintenance of long-term fear memories.

title: Derivation of novel human ground state naive pluripotent stem cells
text:
We isolate mouse embryonic stem (ES) cells from the inner cell mass of blastocysts. These cells can be preserved in vitro in a naive inner-cell-mass-like state by providing external stimulation with leukaemia inhibitory factor (LIF) and inhibiting ERK1/ERK2 and GSK3β signalling using small molecules (referred to as 2i/LIF conditions). Naive pluripotency is characterized by the activation of Oct4 transcription through its distal enhancer, maintenance of an X chromosome state before inactivation, and a reduction in DNA methylation and H3K27me3 repressive chromatin marks on developmental regulatory gene promoters. When 2i/LIF is withdrawn, naive mouse ES cells can transition towards a primed pluripotent state similar to the post-implantation epiblast.

While human ES cells share some molecular features with naive mouse ES cells, they also exhibit epigenetic properties similar to primed murine epiblast stem cells (EpiSCs). These properties include the use of the proximal enhancer element to maintain OCT4 expression, X chromosome inactivation in most female human ES cells, increased DNA methylation, and the deposition of H3K27me3 and bivalent domains on lineage regulatory genes. The establishment of human ground state naive pluripotency in vitro, with molecular and functional features equivalent to those observed in mouse ES cells, is yet to be defined.

In this study, we establish specific conditions that enable the derivation of genetically unmodified human naive pluripotent stem cells from primed human ES cells, somatic cells through induced pluripotent stem (iPS) cell reprogramming, or blastocysts. These newly derived naive pluripotent cells exhibit molecular characteristics and functional properties highly similar to mouse naive ES cells, distinguishing them from conventional primed human pluripotent cells. Notably, these cells are capable of generating cross-species chimeric mouse embryos that undergo organogenesis when human naive iPS cells are microinjected into mouse morulas. Our findings open up new possibilities for regenerative medicine, patient-specific iPS cell disease modeling, and the study of early human development both in vitro and in vivo.

title: Predicting immunogenic tumour mutations by combining mass spectrometry and exome sequencing
text: Human tumors often contain a large number of somatic mutations. If these mutations are presented on major histocompatibility complex class I molecules (MHCI), peptides containing these mutations could potentially trigger an immune response as they would be recognized as foreign by the adaptive immune system. Recent research has shown that mutant peptides can act as T-cell epitopes. However, the discovery of these mutant epitopes has been challenging and time-consuming, as it required screening patient tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes to identify peptides that can recognize antigen libraries constructed from tumor exome sequencing. To simplify this process, we aimed to characterize the general properties of immunogenic mutant peptides. We developed an approach that combines whole-exome and transcriptome sequencing analysis with mass spectrometry to identify neo-epitopes in two commonly used mouse tumor models. Out of the more than 1,300 amino acid changes identified, approximately 13% were predicted to bind MHCI, and only a small fraction of these predictions were confirmed by mass spectrometry. We then modeled the peptides bound to MHCI to understand their structure. Mutations that were exposed to the solvent and accessible to T-cell antigen receptors were predicted to be immunogenic. Vaccination of mice confirmed the validity of this approach, as each predicted immunogenic peptide elicited therapeutically active T-cell responses. The predictions also allowed us to generate peptide-MHCI dextramers, which could be used to monitor the timing and distribution of the anti-tumor T-cell response before and after vaccination. These findings suggest that a suitable prediction algorithm could be used for monitoring T-cell responses and developing personalized vaccines for cancer patients.

title: In vivo genome editing using Staphylococcus aureus Cas9
text: The Cas9 enzyme, guided by RNA, has become a versatile tool for editing genomes. However, the commonly used Cas9 from Streptococcus pyogenes (SpCas9) is too large to be effectively used with the adeno-associated virus (AAV) delivery vehicle, which is highly versatile for basic research and therapeutic applications. In this study, we examine six smaller Cas9 variants and find that Cas9 from Staphylococcus aureus (SaCas9) can edit the genome just as efficiently as SpCas9, but is over 1 kilobase shorter. We package SaCas9 and its single guide RNA into a single AAV vector and target the cholesterol regulatory gene Pcsk9 in the liver of mice. Within a week of injection, we observe over 40% gene modification, leading to significant reductions in serum Pcsk9 and total cholesterol levels. We also evaluate the targeting specificity of SaCas9 and SpCas9 using BLESS, and demonstrate that SaCas9-mediated genome editing in vivo has the potential to be both efficient and specific.

title: Effects of exercise intensity on cardiovascular fitness, total body composition, and visceral adiposity of obese adolescents.
text:
BACKGROUND: Limited knowledge exists regarding the impact of exercise intensity on cardiovascular fitness and body composition in obese adolescents.

OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to examine the effects of physical training intensity on cardiovascular fitness, percentage of body fat (%BF), and visceral adipose tissue (VAT) in obese adolescents.

DESIGN: Eighty obese adolescents aged 13-16 were divided into three groups: 1) biweekly lifestyle education (LSE), 2) LSE + moderate-intensity physical training, or 3) LSE + high-intensity physical training. The intervention lasted for 8 months, with physical training offered 5 days a week and a target energy expenditure of 1047 kJ (250 kcal) per session. Cardiovascular fitness was assessed using a multistage treadmill test, %BF was measured using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, and VAT was evaluated using magnetic resonance imaging.

RESULTS: The high-intensity physical training group demonstrated a significantly greater increase in cardiovascular fitness compared to the LSE alone group (P = 0.009), while no other between-group comparisons were significant. When combining both physical training groups, participants who attended training sessions at least twice a week showed favorable improvements in cardiovascular fitness (P < 0.001), %BF (P = 0.001), and VAT (P = 0.029) compared to the LSE alone group. There was no clear evidence that high-intensity physical training was more effective than moderate-intensity physical training in enhancing body composition.

CONCLUSIONS: Physical training, particularly high-intensity training, significantly improved cardiovascular fitness in obese adolescents. Additionally, physical training reduced both visceral and total-body adiposity, but the intensity of training did not appear to have a significant impact on body composition.

title: Low methionine ingestion by rats extends life span.
text: We have discovered that reducing the concentration of the essential amino acid L-methionine in the diet can significantly increase the lifespan of male Fischer 344 rats. By lowering the methionine content from 0.86% to 0.17%, we observed a 30% longer lifespan. Interestingly, this reduction in methionine completely halted growth, despite the fact that the rats consumed more food based on their body weight. When we examined energy consumption during early life, we found that the 0.17% methionine-fed rats consumed a normal amount of energy for their size, although their consumption per individual was lower than the larger 0.86% methionine-fed rats. Surprisingly, increasing the energy intake of the 0.17% methionine-fed rats did not promote growth, while restricting the food intake of the 0.86% methionine-fed rats to match that of the 0.17% methionine-fed rats did not significantly reduce growth. This suggests that food restriction was not the main factor contributing to the extended lifespan in these experiments. The well-established pathways of methionine metabolism and utilization provide an opportunity to uncover the precise mechanism(s) responsible for this specific dietary restriction-related increase in lifespan.

title: Epicatechin and a cocoa polyphenolic extract modulate gene expression in human Caco-2 cells.
text:
We conducted a functional genomic analysis to investigate the impact of epicatechin and polyphenolic cocoa extract on the Caco-2 human colon adenocarcinoma cell line. We utilized the Human Hematology/Immunology cDNA arrays by Clontech, which consisted of 406 genes in duplicate. The genes that exhibited differential expression were categorized based on their level of expression, determined by the ratio of the values obtained after each treatment compared to control cells. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05, with upregulated genes having a ratio greater than 1.5 and downregulated genes having a ratio less than 0.6.

Epicatechin treatment resulted in the downregulation of 21 genes and the upregulation of 24 genes. On the other hand, incubation with the cocoa polyphenolic extract led to the underexpression of 24 genes and the overexpression of 28 genes. We validated the changes in expression of ferritin heavy polypeptide 1 (FTH1), mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase 1 (MAPKK1), signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1), and topoisomerase 1 following epicatechin treatment. Similarly, we confirmed the changes in myeloid leukemia factor 2 (MLF2), CCAAT/enhancer binding protein gamma (C/EBPG), MAPKK1, ATP-binding cassette, subfamily c member 1 (MRP1), STAT1, topoisomerase 1, and x-ray repair complementing defective repair 1 (XRCC1) expression after incubation with the cocoa polyphenolic extract using RT-PCR.

Furthermore, we verified the changes in messenger RNA levels for MAPKK1, STAT1, MRP1, and topoisomerase 1 at the protein level through Western blotting, following incubation with either epicatechin or cocoa extract. The alterations in the expression of STAT1, MAPKK1, MRP1, and FTH1 genes, which are involved in the cellular response to oxidative stress, align with the antioxidant properties of cocoa flavonoids. Additionally, the changes in the expression of C/EBPG, topoisomerase 1, MLF2, and XRCC1 suggest novel mechanisms of action of flavonoids at the molecular level.

title: An atlas of active enhancers across human cell types and tissues
text: Understanding the regulation of gene expression in multicellular eukaryotes relies on the control of enhancers, which ensure the correct activation of genes in specific cell types and at specific times. To gain insight into their properties and regulatory activity, we utilized the FANTOM5 panel of samples, which encompasses a wide range of human tissues and cell types, to create a comprehensive atlas of active enhancers that are transcribed in vivo. Our findings reveal that enhancers exhibit similarities to CpG-poor messenger RNA promoters, but produce short, unspliced RNAs that are sensitive to exosome degradation and are transcribed bidirectionally. The production of these RNAs is closely linked to enhancer activity. This atlas enables us to compare regulatory programs across different cells in unprecedented detail, identify disease-associated regulatory single nucleotide polymorphisms, and classify enhancers as either cell-type-specific or ubiquitous. Additionally, we investigate the concept of enhancer redundancy, which explains the strength of gene expression rather than the specific patterns of expression. The online FANTOM5 enhancer atlas serves as a valuable resource for studying cell-type-specific enhancers and gene regulation.

title: Precision microbiome reconstitution restores bile acid mediated resistance to Clostridium difficile
text:
The gastrointestinal tracts of mammals are home to numerous microbial species that play a role in maintaining good health, including protecting against intestinal pathogens. However, the use of antibiotics can disrupt these microbial communities, making individuals more susceptible to infections. One such infection is caused by Clostridium difficile, a bacterium that commonly leads to antibiotic-induced diarrhea and can be particularly dangerous for hospitalized patients. Despite its significance, we still don't fully understand which intestinal bacteria provide resistance against C. difficile infection and how they do so. 

To address this knowledge gap, we conducted experiments on mice, treating them with different antibiotics to observe changes in their microbiota and their susceptibility to C. difficile infection. By combining mathematical modeling with analysis of the microbiota of hospitalized patients, we were able to identify bacteria that are associated with resistance to C. difficile infection, and we found that these bacteria are common to both mice and humans. Specifically, we discovered that a bacterium called Clostridium scindens, which is involved in the metabolism of bile acids in the intestines, is associated with resistance to C. difficile infection. Furthermore, when we administered this bacterium to mice, it enhanced their resistance to infection in a manner that depended on secondary bile acids. 

Using a comprehensive approach that involved mouse models, clinical studies, metagenomic analyses, and mathematical modeling, we were able to identify a potential probiotic candidate that can address a clinically relevant deficiency in the microbiome. These findings have important implications for the development of targeted antimicrobials, as well as for the diagnosis and treatment of individuals at risk of C. difficile infection based on their microbiome.

title: Transcription initiation complex structures elucidate DNA opening
text: We have discovered that the process of transcribing eukaryotic protein-coding genes begins with the assembly of the RNA polymerase (Pol) II initiation complex and the opening of the promoter DNA. Through cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), we have obtained high-resolution structures of yeast initiation complexes, revealing both closed and open DNA conformations at resolutions of 8.8 Å and 3.6 Å, respectively. The DNA is securely positioned and held in place over the Pol II cleft through a network of interactions involving the TATA-box-binding protein TBP and transcription factors TFIIA, TFIIB, TFIIE, and TFIIF. The opening of the DNA occurs near the tip of the Pol II clamp and the TFIIE 'extended winged helix' domain, and interestingly, it can happen even in the absence of TFIIH. We propose that the loading of the DNA template strand into the active center is facilitated by the movement of obstructing protein elements, triggered by the allosteric binding of the TFIIE 'E-ribbon' domain. These findings support a unified model for transcription initiation, highlighting the crucial event of trapping open promoter DNA through extensive protein-protein and protein-DNA interactions.

title: Multiple mechanisms disrupt the let-7 microRNA family in neuroblastoma
text: The prognosis for neuroblastoma is poor when there is genetic amplification of MYCN. MYCN is targeted by let-7, a family of microRNAs that suppress tumors and are involved in various cancers. In neuroblastoma, LIN28B, which inhibits the production of let-7, is overexpressed and has been found to regulate MYCN. However, our research shows that LIN28B is not necessary in neuroblastoma cell lines with MYCN amplification, even though let-7 is no longer suppressed. We also discovered that the levels of MYCN messenger RNA are extremely high in amplified disease, enough to counteract let-7, which explains why LIN28B is not needed. We observed that let-7 is commonly lost in neuroblastoma, and this loss is inversely related to MYCN amplification and independently associated with poor outcomes. This provides an explanation for the chromosomal loss patterns seen in neuroblastoma. We propose that disruption of let-7 by LIN28B, MYCN sponging, or genetic loss is a common mechanism in the development of neuroblastoma, with significant implications for cancer pathogenesis.

title: Radiation and Dual Checkpoint Blockade Activates Non-Redundant Immune Mechanisms in Cancer
text: Combining immune checkpoint inhibitors with other therapies is necessary to achieve optimal results, despite the impressive clinical responses they produce. This raises important questions about the mechanisms of non-redundancy and resistance. In our study, we observed significant tumor regressions in a specific group of patients with metastatic melanoma who were treated with an anti-CTLA4 antibody and radiation. We were able to replicate this effect in mouse models as well. While the combined treatment improved responses in both irradiated and unirradiated tumors, resistance was still common. Our unbiased analyses of mice revealed that this resistance was caused by an increase in PD-L1 expression on melanoma cells, which led to T-cell exhaustion. Therefore, achieving the best response in melanoma and other types of cancer requires a combination of radiation, anti-CTLA4, and anti-PD-L1/PD-1. Anti-CTLA4 primarily inhibits T-regulatory cells, which increases the ratio of CD8 T-cells to T-regulatory cells. Radiation, on the other hand, enhances the diversity of the T-cell receptor repertoire within the tumor. Together, anti-CTLA4 promotes the expansion of T-cells, while radiation shapes the T-cell receptor repertoire of these expanded peripheral clones. Adding PD-L1 blockade reverses T-cell exhaustion, improves the CD8 T-cell to T-regulatory cell ratio, and encourages the expansion of oligoclonal T-cells. Similarly, in our clinical trial, we found that patients with melanoma who had high levels of PD-L1 did not respond to radiation plus anti-CTLA4, experienced persistent T-cell exhaustion, and rapidly progressed. This suggests that PD-L1 expression on melanoma cells allows tumors to evade anti-CTLA4 therapy. However, the combination of radiation, anti-CTLA4, and anti-PD-L1 promotes a response and enhances immunity through distinct mechanisms.

title: G-protein-independent coupling of MC4R to Kir7.1 in hypothalamic neurons
text: The controlled release of anorexigenic α-melanocyte stimulating hormone (α-MSH) and orexigenic Agouti-related protein (AgRP) from specific neurons in the hypothalamic arcuate region plays a crucial role in regulating energy balance. Both peptides have a strong affinity for the melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R). Previous research has shown that α-MSH acts as an agonist, activating the receptor through the Gαs signaling pathway. On the other hand, AgRP competes with α-MSH for binding and blocks the receptor's activity, which is mediated by the ligand-mimetic amino-terminal domain. In this study, we demonstrate that in mice, the firing activity of neurons in the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus (PVN) can be regulated by α-MSH and AgRP independently of Gαs signaling. Instead, the coupling of MC4R to the closure of inwardly rectifying potassium channel, Kir7.1, is responsible for this regulation. Additionally, AgRP acts as a biased agonist, hyperpolarizing neurons by binding to MC4R and opening Kir7.1, regardless of its inhibition of α-MSH binding. Consequently, Kir7.1 signaling appears to be crucial for the melanocortin-mediated regulation of energy balance within the PVN. The coupling of MC4R to Kir7.1 may explain certain unique aspects of energy balance control through melanocortin signaling, such as the gene dosage effect of MC4R and the prolonged effects of AgRP on food intake.

title: Role of ghrelin in the relationship between hyperphagia and accelerated gastric emptying in diabetic mice.
text: The aim of this study was to investigate the role of ghrelin in mice with streptozotocin-induced diabetes. Ghrelin is a peptide that stimulates appetite and promotes gastric movement. The study compared mice with ghrelin receptor knockout (GHS-R(-/-)) and wild-type (GHS-R(+/+)) mice with diabetes. Gastric emptying was measured using a breath test, and the expression of neuropeptide Y (NPY), agouti-related peptide (AgRP), and proopiomelanocortin was quantified. Neural contractions were also measured in fundic smooth muscle strips. The results showed that diabetes increased plasma ghrelin levels in both genotypes. Hyperphagia was more pronounced in GHS-R(+/+) mice compared to GHS-R(-/-) mice. The expression of NPY and AgRP was lower in diabetic GHS-R(-/-) mice compared to GHS-R(+/+) mice, while the decrease in proopiomelanocortin expression was similar in both genotypes. Gastric emptying was accelerated in both genotypes, and this was not affected by ghrelin signaling. In fundic smooth muscle strips, neuronal relaxations were reduced and contractions were increased in both genotypes. This increase was related to changes in muscarinic and tachykinergic receptors. In conclusion, diabetic hyperphagia is regulated by central mechanisms involving the ghrelin-signaling pathway. The acceleration of gastric emptying is not the cause of hyperphagia and likely involves local changes in contractility in the fundus.

title: Human serum 25-hydroxycholecalciferol response to extended oral dosing with cholecalciferol.
text:
BACKGROUND: The exact amount of cholecalciferol needed to achieve or maintain a specific serum 25-hydroxycholecalciferol concentration is unknown, especially within ranges similar to the natural supply of the vitamin.

OBJECTIVES: The objectives were to determine the relationship between cholecalciferol intake and resulting serum 25-hydroxycholecalciferol concentration, and to estimate the proportion of daily winter cholecalciferol requirement met by reserves in body tissue.

DESIGN: Cholecalciferol was administered daily in controlled oral doses labeled at 0, 25, 125, and 250 micro g cholecalciferol for approximately 20 weeks during winter to 67 men living in Omaha (41.2 degrees N latitude). Serum 25-hydroxycholecalciferol concentration was measured at intervals throughout the treatment period.

RESULTS: Starting from an average baseline value of 70.3 nmol/L, serum 25-hydroxycholecalciferol concentrations changed proportionally to the dose during winter, with an approximate increase of 0.70 nmol/L for each additional 1 micro g cholecalciferol intake. The calculated oral intake required to maintain the starting serum 25-hydroxycholecalciferol concentration (in autumn) was 12.5 micro g (500 IU)/day, while the total amount needed from all sources (supplement, food, tissue stores) was estimated at approximately 96 micro g (3800 IU)/day. Tissue stores provided approximately 78-82 micro g/day.

CONCLUSIONS: Healthy men appear to require 3000-5000 IU cholecalciferol/day, with the majority of their winter cholecalciferol needs met by cutaneously synthesized vitamin D from sun exposure during the preceding summer months. Current recommended vitamin D intake is insufficient to maintain serum 25-hydroxycholecalciferol concentration without significant cutaneous production of vitamin D.

title: Intratumor heterogeneity and branched evolution revealed by multiregion sequencing.
text:
BACKGROUND: The presence of intratumor heterogeneity can hinder personalized medicine strategies and tumor evolution. In this study, we examined intratumor heterogeneity in primary renal carcinomas and associated metastatic sites using various methods.

METHODS: We performed exome sequencing, chromosome aberration analysis, and ploidy profiling on multiple spatially separated samples. We also conducted immunohistochemical analysis, mutation functional analysis, and messenger RNA expression profiling to characterize the consequences of intratumor heterogeneity.

RESULTS: Our phylogenetic reconstruction revealed branched evolutionary tumor growth, with a significant portion of somatic mutations not detectable across all tumor regions. We observed intratumor heterogeneity for a mutation in the mTOR kinase, which correlated with phosphorylation in vivo and constitutive activation of mTOR kinase activity in vitro. Multiple tumor-suppressor genes showed mutational intratumor heterogeneity, suggesting convergent phenotypic evolution. Additionally, different regions of the same tumor exhibited gene-expression signatures of good and poor prognosis. Allelic composition and ploidy profiling analysis revealed extensive intratumor heterogeneity.

CONCLUSIONS: Intratumor heterogeneity can lead to an underestimation of the tumor genomics landscape and pose challenges to personalized medicine and biomarker development. It can also contribute to tumor adaptation and therapeutic failure.

title: Succession of microbial consortia in the developing infant gut microbiome.
text: Insufficient documentation of the factors affecting the microbiome has led to the characterization of the colonization process of the infant gut microbiome as chaotic. To address this, we conducted a 2.5-year case study to examine the assembly of the human infant gut microbiome and its relationship to life events. Throughout the study, we collected sixty fecal samples from a healthy infant and recorded their diet and health status in a diary. Our analysis of over 300,000 16S rRNA genes revealed that the phylogenetic diversity of the microbiome increased gradually over time, with changes in community composition following a smooth temporal gradient. However, major taxonomic groups exhibited abrupt shifts in abundance corresponding to changes in diet or health. The assembly of the microbiome was nonrandom, characterized by discrete steps of bacterial succession punctuated by life events. Additionally, our analysis of approximately 500,000 DNA metagenomic reads from twelve fecal samples showed that the earliest microbiome was enriched in genes facilitating lactate utilization, and functional genes involved in plant polysaccharide metabolism were present before the introduction of solid food, preparing the infant gut for an adult diet. However, the ingestion of table foods resulted in sustained increases in the abundance of Bacteroidetes, elevated levels of fecal short-chain fatty acids, enrichment of genes associated with carbohydrate utilization, vitamin biosynthesis, and xenobiotic degradation, and a more stable community composition, all of which are characteristic of the adult microbiome. This study demonstrates that seemingly chaotic shifts in the microbiome are associated with life events, but further experiments are needed to assess how different infants respond to similar life events.

title: gamma-tocopherol, the major form of vitamin E in the US diet, deserves more attention.
text: Gamma-tocopherol, the primary form of vitamin E found in plant seeds and the US diet, has received less attention compared to alpha-tocopherol, which is the main form in tissues and supplements. However, recent studies suggest that gamma-tocopherol may play a crucial role in human health and possesses unique characteristics that set it apart from alpha-tocopherol. It appears that gamma-tocopherol is more effective at trapping lipophilic electrophiles than alpha-tocopherol. Additionally, gamma-tocopherol is well absorbed and accumulates significantly in certain human tissues. However, it is mostly metabolized into gamma-CEHC and excreted in urine. Interestingly, gamma-CEHC, unlike its counterpart derived from alpha-tocopherol, has natriuretic activity that may have physiological importance. Both gamma-tocopherol and gamma-CEHC exhibit anti-inflammatory properties by inhibiting cyclooxygenase activity, unlike alpha-tocopherol. Some studies in humans and animals suggest that higher plasma levels of gamma-tocopherol are associated with a lower risk of cardiovascular disease and prostate cancer. These unique characteristics of gamma-tocopherol and its metabolite suggest that it may contribute significantly to human health in ways that were previously unrecognized. This possibility should be further investigated, especially considering that high doses of alpha-tocopherol deplete plasma and tissue gamma-tocopherol, whereas supplementation with gamma-tocopherol increases both. In this review, we examine the current knowledge on the bioavailability, metabolism, chemistry, and non-antioxidant activities of gamma-tocopherol, as well as epidemiological data on its relationship with cardiovascular disease and cancer.

title: Disclosure of APOE genotype for risk of Alzheimer's disease.
text:
In this study, we investigated the impact of disclosing the apolipoprotein E (APOE) genotype, which provides information on the risk of Alzheimer's disease, to asymptomatic adults with a parent who has Alzheimer's disease. We randomly assigned 162 participants to either receive their APOE genotyping results or not. We then measured symptoms of anxiety, depression, and test-related distress at multiple time points after disclosure or nondisclosure.

The results showed no significant differences between the two groups in terms of changes in anxiety, depression, or test-related distress. This was true at 6 weeks, 6 months, and 1 year after disclosure or nondisclosure. We also compared the nondisclosure group to a subgroup of participants who carried the APOE epsilon4 allele, which is associated with increased risk. Again, there were no significant differences between these groups. However, we did find that the subgroup without the epsilon4 allele had significantly lower levels of test-related distress compared to the subgroup with the epsilon4 allele.

Participants who experienced clinically meaningful changes in psychological outcomes were evenly distributed among the nondisclosure group and the epsilon4-positive and epsilon4-negative subgroups. Baseline scores for anxiety and depression were strongly associated with post-disclosure scores, indicating that individuals with higher levels of emotional distress before genetic testing were more likely to experience emotional difficulties after disclosure.

In conclusion, disclosing APOE genotyping results to adult children of Alzheimer's patients did not pose significant short-term psychological risks. In fact, test-related distress was reduced among those who learned they were APOE epsilon4-negative. However, individuals with high levels of emotional distress prior to genetic testing were more susceptible to emotional difficulties after disclosure.

title: Blood pressure and incidence of twelve cardiovascular diseases: lifetime risks, healthy life-years lost, and age-specific associations in 1·25 million people
text:
BACKGROUND: The comparison of blood pressure associations with different manifestations of incident cardiovascular disease in a contemporary population has not been done. This study aims to analyze the associations of blood pressure with 12 different presentations of cardiovascular disease.

METHODS: Electronic health records from 1997 to 2010 were used in the CALIBER program to create a cohort of 1.25 million patients, aged 30 or older, who were initially free from cardiovascular disease. A fifth of the cohort received blood pressure-lowering treatments. The study examined the age-specific associations of clinically measured blood pressure with 12 acute and chronic cardiovascular diseases. Lifetime risks and cardiovascular disease-free life-years lost were estimated, adjusted for other risk factors, at ages 30, 60, and 80.

FINDINGS: Over a median follow-up of 5.2 years, 83,098 initial cardiovascular disease presentations were recorded. The lowest risk for cardiovascular disease was found in individuals with systolic blood pressure of 90-114 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure of 60-74 mm Hg, with no evidence of increased risk at lower blood pressures. The effect of high blood pressure varied depending on the cardiovascular disease endpoint. Associations with high systolic blood pressure were strongest for intracerebral hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage, and stable angina, and weakest for abdominal aortic aneurysm. Raised systolic blood pressure had a greater effect on angina, myocardial infarction, and peripheral arterial disease, while raised diastolic blood pressure had a greater effect on abdominal aortic aneurysm. Pulse pressure associations were inverse for abdominal aortic aneurysm and strongest for peripheral arterial disease. Individuals with hypertension had a higher lifetime risk of overall cardiovascular disease and developed it earlier compared to those with normal blood pressure. Stable and unstable angina accounted for the majority of years of life lost associated with hypertension.

INTERPRETATION: The assumptions that blood pressure has strong associations with all cardiovascular diseases across a wide age range, and that diastolic and systolic associations are concordant, are not supported by this study. The burden of hypertension remains substantial despite modern treatments, highlighting the need for new blood pressure-lowering strategies. These findings will inform the design of randomized trials to assess these strategies.

FUNDING: Medical Research Council, National Institute for Health Research, and Wellcome Trust.

title: Can Online Consumers Contribute to Drug Knowledge? A Mixed-Methods Comparison of Consumer-Generated and Professionally Controlled Psychotropic Medication Information on the Internet
text:
Ongoing efforts to filter online health searches often exclude consumer-generated content, despite the lack of evidence showing that it is inferior to professionally controlled content. The antidepressant escitalopram and the antipsychotic quetiapine have been top-selling drugs in their respective classes for the past 5 years. These drugs have various off-label uses, ranging from treating insomnia and migraines to severe developmental disorders. 

The objective of this study was to describe the most commonly reported effects of escitalopram and quetiapine in online consumer reviews, compare them with effects described in professionally controlled health websites, and assess the usability of online consumer medication reviews. A random sample of 960 consumer reviews was selected from four health websites: two consumer-generated (www.askapatient.com and www.crazymeds.us) and two professionally controlled (www.webmd.com and www.revolutionhealth.com). Professional medication descriptions included standard information from the latter two websites. The textual data were coded for medication effects, and intercoder agreement was assessed. Chi-square tests were used to analyze associations between consumer-reported effects and website origin.

The results showed that consumers taking escitalopram or quetiapine most frequently reported symptom improvement or worsening, changes in sleep, and changes in weight and appetite. More consumers posting reviews on consumer-generated websites reported symptom worsening on quetiapine, while more consumers posting on professionally controlled websites reported symptom improvement. Professional descriptions more frequently listed physical adverse effects and warnings about suicidal ideation, while consumer reviews emphasized effects that disrupted daily routines and provided richer descriptions in context. The most recent consumer reviews on each drug from each website were comparable to the full sample of reviews in terms of commonly reported effects.

In conclusion, consumer reviews and professional medication descriptions generally reported similar effects of these psychotropic medications but differed in their descriptions and frequency of reporting. Professional medication descriptions offer a concise yet comprehensive listing of drug effects, while consumer reviews provide greater context and situational examples. The dispersion of consumer reviews across websites limits their integration, but a brief browsing strategy on the two target medications can still retrieve representative consumer content. Filtering online health searches to return only trusted websites may inappropriately limit access to a valuable source of health information.

title: Effect of supplemental zinc on the growth and serum zinc concentrations of prepubertal children: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
text:
BACKGROUND Numerous studies have been conducted to evaluate the impact of zinc supplementation on the growth of children. However, the results of these studies have been inconsistent, and the factors responsible for these varying outcomes remain unknown. 

OBJECTIVE To address this issue, meta-analyses of randomized controlled intervention trials were conducted to assess the effects of zinc supplementation on the physical growth and serum zinc concentrations of prepubertal children. 

DESIGN A total of 33 relevant studies with appropriate data were identified through searches on MEDLINE (National Library of Medicine, Bethesda, MD) and other methods. Weighted mean effect sizes, expressed in standard deviation units, were calculated for changes in height, weight, weight-for-height, and serum zinc concentration using random-effects models. Additionally, meta-regression techniques were employed to explore factors associated with effect sizes. 

RESULTS The findings revealed that zinc supplementation had a highly significant and positive impact on height and weight increments, with effect sizes of 0.350 (95% CI: 0.189, 0.511) and 0.309 (0.178, 0.439) respectively. However, there was no significant effect of zinc on weight-for-height indexes, with a weighted mean effect size of -0.018 (-0.132, 0.097). Notably, zinc supplementation led to a substantial increase in serum zinc concentrations among the children, with an effect size of 0.820 (0.499, 1.14). Furthermore, it was observed that growth responses were more pronounced in children with low initial weight-for-age z scores and those aged over 6 months with low initial height-for-age z scores. 

CONCLUSIONS Based on these findings, interventions aimed at improving zinc nutrition in children should be considered in populations at risk of zinc deficiency, particularly in areas with high rates of underweight or stunting. Additionally, the population mean serum zinc concentration can serve as a useful indicator of the successful delivery and absorption of zinc supplements in children.

title: Mechanisms of Age-Related Macular Degeneration
text: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a progressive condition that affects a large percentage of elderly individuals worldwide and can lead to blindness. Unfortunately, up to 90% of patients with AMD have a form of the disease that is currently untreatable. AMD is classified into two forms, wet and dry, based on the presence or absence of blood vessels that have invaded the retina. Significant progress has been made in understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying wet AMD, leading to the development of several effective FDA-approved therapies. However, there are currently no approved treatments for dry AMD. In this review, we explore the key pathways involved in each form of the disease. One common factor in AMD pathogenesis is the malfunctioning of the immune system in the eye, which is typically considered immune-privileged. Interestingly, recent research has revealed shared molecular disease pathways between AMD and other neurodegenerative disorders. Finally, we discuss the potential for therapeutic interventions targeting specific steps in the development of AMD.

title: The N-end rule pathway regulates pathogen responses in plants.
text: Plants rely on a complex immune system to effectively combat pathogens. This system is carefully regulated to ensure the timely activation, appropriate duration, and sufficient strength of defense mechanisms. The coordination of this immune response in plants is dependent on the ubiquitin/proteasome system, which controls protein stability in eukaryotes. In our study, we have discovered that a specific subset of this system, known as the N-end rule pathway, is responsible for regulating defense against a wide range of bacterial and fungal pathogens in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana. We have found that this pathway positively influences the production of plant-defense metabolites, such as glucosinolates, as well as the synthesis and response to the phytohormone jasmonic acid, which is crucial for plant immunity. Additionally, our findings suggest that the arginylation branch of the N-end rule pathway controls the timing and strength of the defense program against the model pathogen Pseudomonas syringae AvrRpm1.

title: H3K9 demethylase KDM4E is an epigenetic regulator for bovine embryonic development and a defective factor for nuclear reprogramming.
text: Abnormal changes in the epigenetic programming often lead to developmental abnormalities in embryos created through somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT) during the activation of the embryonic genome (EGA). In bovine eight-cell SCNT embryos, there is a widespread increase in the methylation of histone H3 lysine 9 tri- and di-methylation (H3K9me3/2), but the underlying cause for this phenomenon is still unknown. In this study, we present evidence suggesting that two genes responsible for demethylating H3K9, lysine-specific demethylase 4D (KDM4D) and 4E (KDM4E), are associated with active demethylation of H3K9me3/2 in embryos created through in vitro fertilization (IVF), but their expression is deficient in cloned embryos during EGA. Additionally, KDM4E plays a more significant role in the development of IVF and SCNT embryos, and overexpression of KDM4E can restore the overall gene expression, enhance the formation of blastocysts, and improve the efficiency of cloning SCNT embryos. These findings suggest that KDM4E acts as a critical regulator of EGA and is an internal factor responsible for the persistent barriers to reprogramming H3K9me3/2 in SCNT. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the interaction between RNA and KDM4E is crucial for the demethylation of H3K9 during EGA. These discoveries contribute to our understanding of incomplete nuclear reprogramming and have significant implications for the production of transgenic cattle.

title: Risk of gestational hypertension in relation to folic acid supplementation during pregnancy.
text: The aim of this study was to examine the relationship between folic acid supplementation and gestational hypertension. The participants were women from the United States and Canada who had given birth to nonmalformed infants between 1993 and 2000. The women were interviewed within 6 months after delivery to gather information on sociodemographic and medical factors, as well as the occurrence of hypertension during pregnancy and their use of multivitamins. Cox regression models were used to estimate the relative risks, taking into account various factors such as weight, parity, twin pregnancy, diabetes, smoking, education, and family income. Out of the 2,100 women included in the study, 204 (9.7%) reported experiencing gestational hypertension after the 20th week of gestation. After adjusting for these factors, the relative risk of developing gestational hypertension within a month of taking folic acid supplementation was found to be 0.55 (95% confidence interval: 0.39, 0.79) compared to those who did not use folic acid during that same month. This suggests that folic acid-containing multivitamins may potentially lower the risk of gestational hypertension.

title: Aire regulates negative selection of organ-specific T cells
text: Autoimmune polyendocrinopathy syndrome type 1 (APS-1) is a hereditary disorder caused by mutations in a newly discovered gene called AIRE. This condition is characterized by various autoimmune diseases that specifically target different organs. The exact mechanisms of tolerance impairment resulting from AIRE mutations are still unknown. However, through studying transgenic mice with an Aire mutation, we have found that the absence of Aire leads to a significant inability to eliminate organ-specific autoreactive CD4+ T cells in the thymus. These findings suggest that APS-1 is caused by the failure of a specialized mechanism responsible for eliminating forbidden T cell clones, highlighting the crucial role of this tolerance mechanism.

title: Extracellular Acidic pH Activates the Sterol Regulatory Element-Binding Protein 2 to Promote Tumor Progression.
text: The tumor microenvironment is influenced by various conditions, including hypoxia and nutrient deprivation, which play crucial roles in the advancement of cancer. However, the impact of acidic extracellular pH on cancer progression has not been extensively studied compared to hypoxia. In this study, we demonstrate that an extracellular acidic pH of 6.8 triggers the activation of sterol regulatory element-binding protein 2 (SREBP2). This activation is achieved by promoting the translocation of SREBP2 to the nucleus and its binding to the promoters of target genes, resulting in intracellular acidification. Interestingly, inhibiting SREBP2, but not SREBP1, suppresses the upregulation of genes related to cholesterol biosynthesis under low pH conditions. Additionally, acyl-CoA synthetase short-chain family member 2 (ACSS2), a direct target of SREBP2, confers a growth advantage to cancer cells in an acidic pH environment. Furthermore, the acidic pH-responsive genes regulated by SREBP2 are associated with reduced overall survival in cancer patients. These findings highlight the significance of SREBP2 as a key transcriptional regulator of metabolic genes and the progression of cancer cells, particularly in response to extracellular acidification.

title: Mutation of the Human Circadian Clock Gene CRY1 in Familial Delayed Sleep Phase Disorder
text: The natural daily patterns of human activity are regulated by an internal circadian clock that promotes approximately 24-hour rhythms in various behavioral and physiological processes. However, this system can be disrupted in individuals with delayed sleep phase disorder (DSPD), a common type of insomnia where sleep episodes occur at later times that do not align with societal norms. In our study, we have identified a hereditary form of DSPD that is linked to a dominant coding variation in the core circadian clock gene CRY1. This variation leads to the creation of a transcriptional inhibitor that has a stronger affinity for circadian activator proteins Clock and Bmal1. As a result, the expression of important transcriptional targets is reduced and the period of circadian molecular rhythms is prolonged. This discovery provides a mechanistic explanation for the symptoms of DSPD. The frequency of this allele is estimated to be up to 0.6%, and further investigation of unrelated families with this genetic variation confirms that carriers experience late and/or fragmented sleep patterns. This suggests that a significant portion of the human population is affected by this genetic variant, which influences sleep behavior.

title: Lateral Hypothalamic Signaling Mechanisms Underlying Feeding Stimulation: Differential Contributions of Src Family Tyrosine Kinases to Feeding Triggered Either by NMDA Injection or by Food Deprivation
text: Feeding in rats can be experimentally induced using various methods. Two of these methods include food deprivation and the injection of l-glutamate (Glu) or its receptor agonist NMDA into the lateral hypothalamic area (LHA). In both cases, the NMDA receptor (NMDA-R) in the LHA plays a crucial role in transmitting signals encoded by Glu to stimulate feeding. However, the specific intracellular mechanisms involved in this signal transmission are not yet understood. Since protein-tyrosine kinases (PTKs) are known to be involved in NMDA-R signaling, we investigated their role in the mechanisms underlying both types of feeding stimulation through food intake and biochemical measurements in the LHA. Our findings showed that injecting PTK inhibitors into the LHA significantly reduced feeding induced by NMDA injection (up to 69%), but only had a mild effect on deprivation-induced feeding (24%). This suggests that PTKs may be less important for the signals underlying deprivation-induced feeding. On the other hand, food deprivation led to significant increases in the activity of Src PTKs and the expression of Pyk2, an Src-activating PTK. Taken together, these behavioral and biochemical results demonstrate that while it is easier to suppress NMDA-induced feeding with PTK inhibitors, food deprivation readily activates PTKs in vivo. This suggests that PTK recruitment may be greater for neurotransmitter receptors other than NMDA-R, which are activated during deprivation-induced feeding. These findings highlight the importance of considering multiple feeding stimulation paradigms to fully understand the role of signaling molecules in the pathways underlying feeding behavior in vivo.

title: Relationship between advanced glycation end‐product accumulation and low skeletal muscle mass in Japanese men and women
text: The aim of this study was to examine the relationship between the accumulation of advanced glycation end-products and skeletal muscle mass in middle-aged and older Japanese men and women. A total of 132 participants were enrolled in this cross-sectional study. Skin autofluorescence was used to measure advanced glycation end-products, while dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry was used to measure appendicular skeletal muscle mass. The skeletal muscle index was calculated by dividing appendicular skeletal muscle mass by height squared. Participants were divided into two groups based on their skeletal muscle index (low and normal) using the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia's criteria. Multivariate logistic regression analysis and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve were used to identify significant factors associated with low skeletal muscle index. The study included 70 men (mean age 57 ± 10 years) and 62 women (mean age 60 ± 11 years), with 31 participants in the low skeletal muscle index group and 101 participants in the normal skeletal muscle index group. Skin autofluorescence was significantly higher in the low skeletal muscle index group compared to the normal skeletal muscle index group. Skin autofluorescence was found to be a significant independent factor associated with low skeletal muscle index based on multivariate logistic regression analysis. The cut-off for skin autofluorescence was determined to be 2.45 arbitrary units, with a sensitivity of 0.75 and specificity of 0.91. In conclusion, skin autofluorescence was found to be an independent factor associated with low skeletal muscle index in middle-aged and older Japanese men and women.

title: Large-Scale Profiling Reveals the Influence of Genetic Variation on Gene Expression in Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells.
text:
In this study, we utilized whole-genome sequencing and gene expression profiling of 215 human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) lines from various donors. Our aim was to identify genetic variants that are associated with RNA expression for 5,746 genes. Through our analysis, we successfully predicted causal variants for these expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) that disrupt transcription factor binding. To validate our findings, we conducted experimental tests on a subset of these variants.

Furthermore, we discovered copy-number variant (CNV) eQTLs, some of which were found to impact gene expression by altering the copy number of intergenic regulatory regions. Additionally, we observed effects on gene expression caused by rare genic CNVs and regulatory single-nucleotide variants. Interestingly, we also found that the reactivation of gene expression on the X chromosome is dependent on the gene's chromosomal position.

Our study underscores the significance of iPSCs in genetic association analyses and provides a valuable resource for investigating the genetic regulation of gene expression in pluripotent cells.

title: Ethanol extract of Allium fistulosum inhibits development of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease
text:
In this study, we aimed to investigate the potential of Allium fistulosum extract (EAF) as a natural treatment for non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), a common liver disease associated with metabolic syndrome. We conducted experiments using an in vitro model of NAFLD induced by oleic acid (OA) and an in vivo model of NAFLD induced by a high-fat high-sucrose Western diet (WD) in obese mice.

For the in vitro experiments, we divided HepG2 cells into three groups: a normal diet group (ND), a WD group, and a WD group supplemented with 1% EAF. We found that EAF reduced lipid accumulation in the cells without causing any cytotoxicity. It also inhibited the activation of genes involved in lipid synthesis. 

Next, we conducted in vivo experiments using mice fed either a normal diet or a WD, with or without EAF supplementation. The WD-fed mice showed increases in body weight, liver weight, epididymal fat weight, and fat accumulation in hepatocytes. However, these effects were significantly reduced in the mice supplemented with EAF.

Based on our findings, we conclude that Allium fistulosum extract has a protective effect against the development of NAFLD. EAF specifically exhibits anti-lipogenic activity in the liver. Therefore, EAF shows promise as a potential candidate for the development of new therapeutic drugs or drug combinations for the prevention and treatment of NAFLD.

title: Cardiovascular risk factors in childhood and carotid artery intima-media thickness in adulthood: the Cardiovascular Risk in Young Finns Study.
text: The aim of this study was to examine the connection between cardiovascular risk factors measured during childhood and adolescence and the thickness of the common carotid artery, which is an indicator of early-stage atherosclerosis, in adulthood. The study was conducted as a population-based, prospective cohort study at five centers in Finland. The participants were 2229 white adults aged 24 to 39 years who were examined during their childhood and adolescence between 1980 and 2002. The main outcome measures were the association between cardiovascular risk factors (such as cholesterol levels, blood pressure, body mass index, and smoking) measured during childhood and adulthood, and the thickness of the common carotid artery measured in adulthood. The results showed that there was a significant association between the thickness of the common carotid artery in adulthood and LDL cholesterol levels, blood pressure, body mass index, and smoking during childhood. The same association was found with blood pressure, body mass index, and smoking in adulthood. The number of risk factors measured during adolescence, including high levels of LDL cholesterol, blood pressure, body mass index, and smoking, were directly related to the thickness of the common carotid artery in young adults. This relationship remained significant even after adjusting for other risk factors. The number of risk factors measured during early childhood showed a weak association with the thickness of the common carotid artery in men but not in women. In conclusion, the risk factors assessed during adolescence can predict the thickness of the common carotid artery in adulthood, independently of other risk factors. This suggests that exposure to cardiovascular risk factors early in life can lead to changes in the arteries that contribute to the development of atherosclerosis.

title: MicroRNA-29 induces cellular senescence in aging muscle through multiple signaling pathways
text: The exact mechanisms responsible for the development of muscle atrophy in aging are not yet fully understood. However, through the use of microRNA array and individual qPCR analyses, we have discovered a significant increase in miR-29 levels in the muscles of aged rodents compared to young ones. As aging progresses, the levels of p85α, IGF-1, and B-myb in the muscles decrease, while the expression of certain cell arrest proteins (p53, p16, and pRB) increases. When miR-29 was introduced into muscle progenitor cells (MPC), their ability to proliferate was impaired, and the expression of SA-βgal increased, indicating the onset of senescence. This impaired proliferation of MPCs was a result of the interaction between miR-29 and the 3'-UTR of p85α, IGF-1, and B-myb, which suppressed the translation of these proteins responsible for myoblast proliferation. In vivo experiments involving the electroporation of miR-29 into the muscles of young mice replicated the effects seen in aging-induced muscle, suppressing proliferation and increasing the levels of cell arrest proteins. We also discovered that Wnt-3a may be a potential trigger for the expression of miR-29, as exogenous Wnt-3a stimulated a 2.7-fold increase in miR-29 expression in primary cultures of MPCs. Therefore, the senescence of muscles induced by aging is a result of the activation of miR-29 by Wnt-3a, leading to the suppressed expression of several signaling proteins (p85α, IGF-1, and B-myb) that work together to impair the proliferation of MPCs, ultimately contributing to muscle atrophy. The increase in miR-29 may serve as a potential mechanism for the development of sarcopenia in aging.

title: Rictor, a Novel Binding Partner of mTOR, Defines a Rapamycin-Insensitive and Raptor-Independent Pathway that Regulates the Cytoskeleton
text: The mTOR pathway in mammals is responsible for regulating growth by integrating signals from nutrients and growth factors. mTOR is a large protein kinase that is targeted by rapamycin, an immunosuppressant with potential anticancer properties and the ability to block vessel restenosis. It forms a complex with raptor and GbetaL proteins, which is the target of rapamycin. However, our research shows that mTOR is also part of a separate complex that includes a novel protein called rictor (rapamycin-insensitive companion of mTOR). Rictor shares similarities with other proteins such as pianissimo from D. discoidieum, STE20p from S. pombe, and AVO3p from S. cerevisiae. Interestingly, AVO3p is part of a rapamycin-insensitive TOR complex that does not have the yeast equivalent of raptor and signals to the actin cytoskeleton through PKC1. In line with this discovery, the rictor-containing mTOR complex includes GbetaL but not raptor, and it does not regulate the mTOR effector S6K1 nor is it bound by FKBP12-rapamycin. Our findings indicate that the rictor-mTOR complex plays a role in modulating the phosphorylation of Protein Kinase C alpha (PKCalpha) and the actin cytoskeleton, suggesting that this aspect of TOR signaling is conserved between yeast and mammals.

title: Activation of the estrogen receptor through phosphorylation by mitogen-activated protein kinase.
text: The phosphorylation of serine residue 118 on the human estrogen receptor (ER) is necessary for the ER activation function 1 (AF-1) to function at its full capacity. This specific serine residue, known as Ser118, can be phosphorylated by mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) in laboratory settings and in cells treated with epidermal growth factor (EGF) and insulin-like growth factor (IGF) in living organisms. When MAPK kinase (MAPKK) or the guanine nucleotide binding protein Ras, both of which activate MAPK, are overexpressed, they enhance the transcriptional activity of wild-type ER in response to estrogen and antiestrogen (tamoxifen). However, this enhancement is not observed in a mutant ER where Ser118 is replaced with alanine. Therefore, the phosphorylation of Ser118 through the Ras-MAPK cascade in the growth factor signaling pathways regulates the activity of the amino-terminal AF-1 of the ER.

title: Regulation of the antimicrobial response by NLR proteins.
text: Nucleotide-binding, oligomerization domain (NOD)-like receptor (NLR) proteins are a group of receptors in the innate immune system that are crucial for detecting microbes and initiating immune responses against them. Dysregulation of multiple NLR proteins has been associated with increased susceptibility to infections and autoinflammatory diseases in both mice and humans. Despite our growing knowledge of NLR function and interactions, there are still many unanswered questions regarding how they sense microbes, transmit signals, and function in living organisms. This review focuses on important members of the NLR family, discussing how they are activated by different microbes, their roles in immune responses, and their interactions with other innate sensor proteins. Additionally, the review explores how microbial detection by NLR receptors activates the adaptive immune system, which works together with the innate immune system to fight against microbial threats.

title: Acetylcysteine for prevention of acute deterioration of renal function following elective coronary angiography and intervention: a randomized controlled trial.
text:
The purpose of this study was to investigate whether oral acetylcysteine can prevent acute deterioration in renal function in patients with moderate renal insufficiency who undergo elective coronary angiography. The study was conducted at the Grantham Hospital at the University of Hong Kong from May 2000 to December 2001. Two hundred Chinese patients with stable moderate renal insufficiency were included in the study. They were randomly assigned to receive either oral acetylcysteine or a placebo on the day before and the day of angiography. All patients received a low-osmolality contrast agent. The main outcome measures were the occurrence of a more than 25% increase in serum creatinine level within 48 hours after contrast administration, as well as changes in creatinine clearance and serum creatinine level. 

The results showed that 4% of the acetylcysteine group and 12% of the control group developed a more than 25% increase in serum creatinine level within 48 hours after contrast administration. This indicates that acetylcysteine significantly reduced the risk of acute contrast-induced nephrotoxicity. Additionally, the acetylcysteine group had lower serum creatinine levels and higher creatinine clearance compared to the control group. These benefits were consistent across various patient subgroups and persisted for at least 7 days. No major adverse events related to the treatment were reported.
