The age of the person with cancer and the caregiver's level of education were also associated with caregiver unmet needs. However, caregiver gender and patient gender did not show any significant associations. 

In conclusion, these findings emphasize the importance of developing tailored programs to provide systematic support to caregivers who are assisting patients during the early stages of cancer treatment.

title: Glucose Sensing in L Cells: A Primary Cell Study
text: The hormone glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) stimulates insulin secretion and improves blood sugar levels in individuals with type 2 diabetes. While there are currently treatments available that are based on GLP-1, our understanding of how to increase the natural release of GLP-1 from L cells is limited. To gain more insight into this cell type, we created transgenic mice that expressed a fluorescent protein specifically in L cells. Through various techniques such as electrophysiology, fluorescence calcium imaging, and expression analysis, we discovered that individual L cells are capable of electrical activity and respond to glucose. Our findings suggest that GLP-1 release is regulated by the activity of sodium glucose cotransporter 1 and ATP-sensitive K(+) channels, which are highly expressed in purified L cells. This research opens up new possibilities for further exploration and development of physiological and therapeutic approaches.

title: Total atherosclerotic burden by whole body magnetic resonance angiography predicts major adverse cardiovascular events.
text:
The aim of this study was to examine the correlation between the Total Atherosclerotic Score (TAS), which measures the overall burden of atherosclerosis in the arterial tree using whole body magnetic resonance angiography (WBMRA), and the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), including cardiac death, myocardial infarction, stroke, and coronary revascularization. The hypothesis was that TAS could predict MACE. 

A total of 305 randomly selected individuals aged 70 (47% women) underwent WBMRA to assess their atherosclerotic burden. Atherosclerotic changes (TAS > 0) were observed in 68% of the subjects. During a mean follow-up period of 4.8 years, MACE occurred in 25 individuals (8.2%). After adjusting for multiple risk factors, TAS was found to be associated with MACE, with an odds ratio of 8.86 for any degree of vessel lumen abnormality (95% confidence interval 1.14-69.11, p = 0.037). Furthermore, the addition of TAS to the Framingham risk score (FRS) improved discrimination and reclassification, as evidenced by an increase in the Receiver Operator Curve (ROC) from 0.681 to 0.750 (p = 0.0421). 

In conclusion, in a population-based sample of 70-year-old men and women, WBMRA with TAS was able to independently predict MACE, regardless of major cardiovascular risk factors.

title: Regulation of ADMP and BMP2/4/7 at Opposite Embryonic Poles Generates a Self-Regulating Morphogenetic Field
text: How is the establishment of a morphogenetic field possible, where embryos can self-regulate and regenerate normal structures after being divided in half? Our research on Xenopus embryos has shown that when ADMP and BMP2/4/7 are simultaneously suppressed, self-regulation is eliminated, resulting in neural induction throughout the ectoderm. ADMP transcription is activated in the Spemann organizer when BMP levels are low. When ventral BMP2/4/7 signals are depleted, Admp expression increases, enabling self-regulation. ADMP functions similarly to BMP and signals through the ALK-2 receptor. However, it is unable to signal dorsally due to inhibition by Chordin. The ventral BMP antagonists Sizzled and Bambi further refine the pattern. Through grafting experiments, we have demonstrated that both the dorsal and ventral poles act as signaling centers capable of inducing histotypic differentiation over significant distances in ADMP/BMP2/4/7-depleted hosts. In conclusion, the opposing transcriptional regulation of dorsal and ventral BMP signals, along with their extracellular antagonists, provides a molecular mechanism for embryonic self-regulation.

title: Genetic control of mosquitoes.
text: Genetics has the potential to offer fresh, environmentally friendly techniques for mosquito control that are specific to each species. The objective of genetic control strategies is either to decrease the number of target mosquito populations or to introduce a new trait that reduces harm. These approaches vary significantly in their characteristics, particularly between self-limiting strategies, where the modification has a limited lifespan, and self-sustaining strategies, which are designed to persist indefinitely in the target population and may spread to other populations. Numerous methods utilizing diverse molecular biology techniques are currently being developed, and the initial field trials have been completed with success.

title: Colorectal Cancers from Distinct Ancestral Populations Show Variations in BRAF Mutation Frequency
text: Research has shown that the occurrence of somatic oncogenic mutations can vary among different ancestral populations for certain types of cancer. In order to investigate if key driver alterations differ in frequency in colorectal cancer, we utilized a high-throughput genotyping platform called OncoMap. This platform allowed us to examine 385 mutations across 33 known cancer genes in the DNA of 83 Asian, 149 Black, and 195 White colorectal cancer patients. Our findings revealed that Asian patients had fewer canonical oncogenic mutations in the tested genes compared to Black and White patients (60% vs 79% for Black patients (P = 0.011) and 77% for White patients (P = 0.015)). Additionally, we observed that BRAF mutations were more prevalent in White patients compared to Asian and Black patients (17% vs 4% for Asian patients (P = 0.004) and 7% for Black patients (P = 0.014)). These results suggest that utilizing genomic approaches to understand the ancestral factors present in different patient populations may lead to more precise and effective treatments for colorectal cancer.

title: Direct neuronal reprogramming: learning from and for development.
text: The identification of key signaling pathways and transcriptional programs that guide neuronal diversity in development has been largely accomplished. In this article, we explore how this knowledge has been effectively utilized to reprogram various cell types into a remarkable range of functional neurons. Additionally, we investigate the degree to which direct neuronal reprogramming mirrors embryonic development and analyze the potential obstacles to reprogramming that may arise due to a cell's specific developmental background. Finally, we present the 'Cook Islands' model, a recently proposed framework for cell specification, and evaluate its suitability based on recent findings in the field of direct reprogramming.

title: Cell fusion hypothesis of the cancer stem cell.
text: Recent cancer research has made a significant breakthrough by discovering tumor cells that possess characteristics similar to stem cells. These cells, known as cancer stem cells (CSCs), are typically found in small numbers within the tumor and have the unique ability to initiate the growth of a diverse tumor. The origin of CSCs is still unknown and likely varies depending on the type of cancer. One potential but often overlooked mechanism for the formation of CSCs is the fusion of stem cells with differentiated cells. This cell fusion hypothesis provides a crucial functional basis for understanding the various roles that cell fusion may play in the development and advancement of cancer.

title: Antidepressant fluoxetine enhances glucocorticoid receptor function in vitro by modulating membrane steroid transporters.
text:
1. The presence of antidepressants during the incubation of LMCAT fibroblast cells enhances glucocorticoid receptor (GR)-mediated gene transcription when dexamethasone and cortisol are present, but not when corticosterone is present. Our research indicates that antidepressants achieve this by blocking the LMCAT cell membrane steroid transporter, which is very similar to the multidrug resistance P-glycoprotein. This inhibition leads to increased intracellular concentrations of dexamethasone or cortisol. However, previous experiments using the antidepressant fluoxetine in combination with dexamethasone did not yield positive results (Pariante et al. (2001). Br. J. Pharmacol., 134, 1335-1343).

2. We have conducted further investigations into the effects of fluoxetine on GR-mediated gene transcription in the presence of dexamethasone. Additionally, we have examined the impact of fluoxetine on GR-mediated gene transcription when cortisol and corticosterone are present, as well as its effect on the accumulation of radioactive cortisol and corticosterone within cells. Lastly, we have studied the influence of fluoxetine on the inhibition of P-glycoprotein activity in Caco-2 cells.

3. Our latest findings reveal that fluoxetine (1-10 micro M) significantly enhances GR-mediated gene transcription when dexamethasone and cortisol are present (increasing it by approximately 140-170%), but not when corticosterone is present. Furthermore, fluoxetine increases the intracellular accumulation of (3)H-cortisol (by 5-15%), but not of (3)H-corticosterone. Additionally, a concentration of 10 micro M of fluoxetine induces approximately 30% inhibition of P-glycoprotein activity in Caco-2 cells.

4. Our results demonstrate that fluoxetine, similar to other antidepressants, inhibits membrane steroid transporters.

title: Physician knowledge levels and barriers to coronary risk prevention in women: survey results from the Women and Heart Disease Physician Education Initiative.
text:
BACKGROUND
There have been limited studies investigating whether the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of physicians contribute to gender disparities in the primary prevention of coronary heart disease (CHD), particularly among obstetricians and gynecologists (OB/GYNs) who care for a large number of reproductive-age women. Our objective was to identify barriers that affect the provision of recommended coronary risk factor therapies in women.

METHODS
We conducted a survey among internists and OB/GYNs who attended Grand Rounds presentations as part of the New York State Women and Heart Disease Physician Education Initiative. This program aimed to improve the screening and management of coronary risk factors in women. Participants were asked to complete a 7-minute questionnaire.

RESULTS
A total of 529 respondents participated, with a mean age of 40.3 years (standard deviation = 12.3). Of the respondents, 75.1% were internists (n=378) and 42.7% (n=226) were women. Physicians answered 71.5% of the 13 knowledge assessment questions on coronary risk prevention correctly (range, 4-13). A significant proportion of internists (one third) and OB/GYNs (half) were unaware that tobacco use was the leading cause of myocardial infarction in young women. When it came to patients who smoked tobacco, only two thirds of internists and 55.4% of OB/GYNs reported suggesting a quit date (p=.007). After adjusting for other factors, physicians who did not perceive time as a barrier were more likely to discuss smoking cessation (odds ratio=1.7 [1.1-2.7]).

CONCLUSIONS
Among the surveyed internists and OB/GYNs, time was perceived as a barrier to implementing risk prevention. Additionally, these physicians underestimated the impact of tobacco use as a risk factor for CHD in young women. To address gender disparities in CHD prevention, both specialties require time-efficient educational programs that take into account their unique characteristics.

title: Separation of mother and daughter cells.
text: This chapter provides a detailed explanation of the procedures used to separate and isolate mothers and daughters in the budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae (S. cerevisiae). The asymmetric division of S. cerevisiae is achieved through budding, with the position of the bud determining the plane of cell division. These protocols have been utilized by researchers investigating various aspects of asymmetric cell division, including aging and bud site selection. The chapter outlines the steps for conducting life span analysis through micromanipulation and the collection of old cells on a large scale. Differentiating between mothers and daughters can be challenging at the beginning and end of a life span. Generally, daughter cells are smaller than their mothers, and mothers tend to bud a second time before their daughters form their first bud. One method, known as a "baby machine," effectively isolates virgin daughter cells from mother cells but does not facilitate the recovery of old mothers. This technique involves attaching mother cells to a membrane and continuously eluting daughter cells through membrane washing.

title: Postnatal development of adipocyte cellularity in the normal rat.
text: Several researchers have demonstrated that the number of adipocytes remains constant in fully developed humans and various rodent species. While techniques like histometry and Coulter counting of osmium-fixed cells can determine the number of new cells in the adipose tissue, they cannot differentiate between the "lipid filling" of existing adipocytes and the creation of new ones. This study utilized in vivo injection of [(3)H]thymidine to show that the production of new adipocytes in Sprague-Dawley rats continues after birth but stops before sexual maturity. Additionally, during the second and third weeks after birth, a group of preadipocytes is formed. It may take up to 30 days for these preadipocytes to develop into mature adipocytes.

title: Withdrawal Symptoms after Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor Discontinuation: A Systematic Review
text:
Background: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) are commonly used in medical practice. However, the full clinical significance of the broad range of symptoms associated with their use has not been fully understood. 

Methods: To conduct a systematic review of the literature, we followed the PRISMA guidelines. We searched for titles, abstracts, and topics using the terms 'withdrawal symptoms' OR 'withdrawal syndrome' OR 'discontinuation syndrome' OR 'discontinuation symptoms', AND 'SSRI' OR 'serotonin' OR 'antidepressant' OR 'paroxetine' OR 'fluoxetine' OR 'sertraline' OR 'fluvoxamine' OR 'citalopram' OR 'escitalopram'. We searched electronic research literature databases including CINAHL, the Cochrane Library, PubMed, and Web-of-Science from the inception of each database to July 2014. 

Results: Our review included 15 randomized controlled studies, 4 open trials, 4 retrospective investigations, and 38 case reports. The prevalence of the syndrome varied, and its estimation was hindered by a lack of case identification in many studies. Symptoms typically appeared within a few days of discontinuing the drug and lasted for a few weeks, even with gradual tapering. However, there were variations, including late onset and/or longer persistence of disturbances. These symptoms could easily be mistaken for signs of an impending relapse. 

Conclusions: Clinicians should consider the possibility of withdrawal symptoms when discontinuing SSRI treatment, along with benzodiazepines, barbiturates, and other psychotropic drugs. The term 'discontinuation syndrome' currently used downplays the potential vulnerabilities induced by SSRIs and should be replaced with 'withdrawal syndrome'.

title: Sphingosine Kinase 1 Regulates the Akt/FOXO3a/Bim Pathway and Contributes to Apoptosis Resistance in Glioma Cells
text: The objective of this study was to investigate how Sphingosine kinase-1 (SPHK1) prevents apoptosis in glioma cancer cells. Our findings demonstrate that when SPHK1 is dysregulated, the sensitivity of glioma cells to apoptosis is altered both in laboratory settings and in living organisms. Further analysis revealed that SPHK1 overexpression in glioma cells leads to the downregulation of the pro-apoptotic protein Bim, while the expression of other Bcl-2 family members remains unaffected. Additionally, SPHK1 was found to alter the transcriptional level of Bim in glioma cells. We also observed a correlation between SPHK1 and Bim expression in primary glioma samples. Notably, increased SPHK1 expression in glioma cells resulted in elevated Akt activity and phosphorylated inactivation of FOXO3a, which ultimately led to the downregulation of Bim. Our pharmacological experiments demonstrated that these effects of SPHK1 were dependent on phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K). Furthermore, the effects of SPHK1 on the Akt/FOXO3a/Bim pathway could be reversed by SPHK1-specific RNA interference or an SPHK1 inhibitor. Overall, our findings suggest that the regulation of the Akt/FOXO3a/Bim pathway may be a novel mechanism by which SPHK1 protects glioma cells from apoptosis, thereby contributing to glioma tumorigenesis.

title: COX-2 and survivin are overexpressed and positively correlated in endometrial carcinoma.
text:
The aim of this study was to investigate the expression of survivin and Cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) in the development of endometrial adenocarcinoma (EC) and their potential correlation. We also examined their association with traditional prognostic factors in EC. This study is the first to explore the relationship between survivin expression and COX-2 in the development of EC. 

We analyzed archived tissue samples from 50 EC cases, 30 endometrial hyperplasia cases, and 20 proliferative endometrium cases using immunohistochemistry to assess survivin and COX-2 expression. 

The results showed that both survivin and COX-2 were overexpressed in hyperplasia and endometrial adenocarcinoma cases compared to proliferative endometrium cases, and this difference was statistically significant (p=0.01, p=0.02, respectively). Among EC cases, 38 (76%) patients had strong positive expression of survivin, and 30 (60%) patients had strong positive expression of COX-2. Furthermore, we found a significant positive correlation between survivin and COX-2 expression (p=0.0001, r=0.46). There was no correlation between survivin or COX-2 expression and traditional prognostic factors such as myometrial invasion, grade, or lymph node metastasis (p>0.05). Additionally, neither COX-2 nor survivin expression had an impact on overall survival (p>0.05). 

In conclusion, both survivin and COX-2 are overexpressed in EC and may be early events in its development. Furthermore, there appears to be a positive correlation between the protein products of these two genes. COX-2 and survivin may share a common molecular pathway or enhance each other's actions in the development of EC. Further research is needed to investigate the molecular basis of this relationship in endometrial carcinogenesis.

title: Structural plasticity of the adult brain: how animal models help us understand brain changes in depression and systemic disorders related to depression
text: The brain processes experiences and converts them into behavioral and physiological reactions. Stressful events are those that are threatening or unexpected, and the body responds in order to adapt through a process known as "allostasis." Allostasis involves various chemical mediators such as cortisol and adrenaline from the adrenal glands, as well as other hormones, neurotransmitters, the parasympathetic and sympathetic nervous systems, and cytokines and chemokines from the immune system. Two important brain structures, the amygdala and hippocampus, play crucial roles in determining what is stressful and deciding appropriate responses. The hippocampus, responsible for memory formation, has receptors that allow it to respond to glucocorticoid hormones in the blood. It can undergo atrophy in certain psychiatric disorders and also exhibits changes in response to stress, such as decreased dendritic branching and a reduction in the number of neurons in the dentate gyrus. The amygdala, which is involved in emotional memories, becomes overactive in conditions like posttraumatic stress disorder and depression. Animal studies suggest that the amygdala may experience growth and hypertrophy in response to stress. The changes in the brain following acute and chronic stress resemble those seen in the metabolic, cardiovascular, and immune systems. Initially, there is short-term adaptation (allostasis), but over time, this can lead to long-term damage (allostatic load), resulting in conditions like atherosclerosis, obesity, bone demineralization, and impaired immune function. Allostatic load is commonly observed in major depressive illness and may also be present in other chronic anxiety and mood disorders.

title: CCR7 provides localized access to IL-2 and defines homeostatically distinct regulatory T cell subsets
text: The precise control of immunosuppressive Foxp3(+) regulatory T (T reg) cells is crucial for immune tolerance and activation. IL-2 plays a significant role in maintaining tolerance and preventing autoimmunity. However, the specific requirement for IL-2 in different populations of peripheral T reg cells is not well understood. Our study demonstrates that IL-2 selectively supports a group of quiescent CD44(lo)CD62L(hi) T reg cells. These cells gain access to IL-2 produced in the T cell zones of secondary lymphoid tissues through their expression of the chemokine receptor CCR7. On the other hand, CD44(hi)CD62L(lo)CCR7(lo) T reg cells, which are found in nonlymphoid tissues, do not have access to IL-2-rich regions in vivo and are not affected by IL-2 blockade. Instead, their maintenance relies on signaling through the co-stimulatory receptor ICOS (inducible co-stimulator). Therefore, we have identified a fundamental division in T reg cell populations based on their location and propose a comprehensive framework for understanding how T reg cell abundance and function are regulated by distinct signals in different tissue environments.

title: Assessing sequence comparison methods with reliable structurally identified distant evolutionary relationships.
text: The effectiveness of pairwise sequence comparison methods has been evaluated using proteins with known relationships from their structures and functions, as documented in the SCOP database [Murzin, A. G., Brenner, S. E., Hubbard, T. & Chothia C. (1995) J. Mol. Biol. 247, 536-540]. The assessment involved testing the programs BLAST [Altschul, S. F., Gish, W., Miller, W., Myers, E. W. & Lipman, D. J. (1990). J. Mol. Biol. 215, 403-410], WU-BLAST2 [Altschul, S. F. & Gish, W. (1996) Methods Enzymol. 266, 460-480], FASTA [Pearson, W. R. & Lipman, D. J. (1988) Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 85, 2444-2448], and SSEARCH [Smith, T. F. & Waterman, M. S. (1981) J. Mol. Biol. 147, 195-197] along with their scoring systems. The use of statistical scores to evaluate matches, rather than relying on percentage identity or raw scores, significantly reduces the error rate of all algorithms. The E-value statistical scores provided by SSEARCH and FASTA are reliable, as the number of false positives detected in our tests aligns well with the reported scores. However, the P-values reported by BLAST and WU-BLAST2 overstate significance by several orders of magnitude. SSEARCH, FASTA ktup = 1, and WU-BLAST2 demonstrate the best performance, successfully detecting nearly all relationships between proteins with sequence identities exceeding 30%. However, their performance diminishes for more distantly related proteins, with only half of the relationships between proteins with 20-30% identity being identified. Due to the low sequence similarity of many homologs, most distant relationships cannot be detected by any pairwise comparison method. Nevertheless, the identified relationships can be confidently utilized.

title: Evaluation of a mental health outreach service for homeless families.
text:
The aim of this study was to examine the characteristics of homeless children and families who received the mental health outreach service (MHOS), assess the impact of the service on the short-term psychosocial functioning of children and parents, and determine perceptions and satisfaction with the service. 

The study included 27 children from 23 families who received the MHOS and 27 children from 23 families living in other hostels without access to such a service. The MHOS was provided by a clinical nurse specialist with expertise in child mental health and included assessments and brief treatments for mental health disorders in children, collaboration with agencies, and training for homeless center staff. 

The results showed that children in the group receiving the MHOS experienced a significant decrease in total scores on the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ). Receiving the intervention was the strongest predictor of improvement in SDQ scores. However, there was no significant impact on parental mental health scores as measured by the General Health Questionnaire. Homeless families and staff expressed high satisfaction with the MHOS. 

In conclusion, the MHOS for homeless families is an innovative intervention that addresses the complex and diverse needs of a vulnerable population who are unable to access mainstream mental health services. While the primary goal of the service was to improve child mental health problems, it also effectively addressed social and practical needs of families in addition to its clinical role.

title: Evaluation of individuals with pulmonary nodules: when is it lung cancer? Diagnosis and management of lung cancer, 3rd ed: American College of Chest Physicians evidence-based clinical practice guidelines.
text:
The aim of this article is to provide updated recommendations for the evaluation and management of individuals with solid pulmonary nodules, as well as to generate new recommendations for those with nonsolid nodules. To achieve this, we conducted literature reviews, synthesized evidence, and followed the methodology outlined in the "Methodology for Development of Guidelines for Lung Cancer" in the American College of Chest Physicians Lung Cancer Guidelines, 3rd edition. 

Based on our findings, we have formulated recommendations for the evaluation of solid pulmonary nodules measuring > 8 mm in diameter, solid nodules measuring ≤ 8 mm in diameter, and subsolid nodules. These recommendations emphasize the importance of assessing the likelihood of malignancy, the usefulness of imaging tests, the need to consider the benefits and risks of different management strategies (such as nonsurgical biopsy, surgical resection, and surveillance with chest CT imaging), and the significance of understanding patient preferences.

In conclusion, individuals with pulmonary nodules should undergo evaluation and management by estimating the probability of malignancy, conducting imaging tests to gain a better understanding of the lesions, evaluating the risks associated with various management options, and considering patient preferences when making decisions about management.

title: AgDscam, a Hypervariable Immunoglobulin Domain-Containing Receptor of the       Anopheles gambiae Innate Immune System
text: The insect's innate immune system relies on a limited number of pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) that can recognize pathogen-associated molecular patterns. In this study, we present a new discovery regarding the role of a gene called Dscam in the immune defense of the malaria-carrying mosquito, Anopheles gambiae. Dscam is an alternatively spliced gene that encodes a hypervariable immunoglobulin domain, and it is responsible for generating a wide range of PRRs involved in immune defense. The AgDscam gene in mosquitoes has a complex genome structure, consisting of 101 exons that can produce over 31,000 potential alternative splice forms. Each splice form has different combinations of adhesive domains and specific interactions. When the mosquito is infected, AgDscam produces specific splice form repertoires in response to the pathogen. Silencing AgDscam temporarily weakens the mosquito's ability to resist bacterial infections and malaria caused by the Plasmodium parasite. AgDscam plays a crucial role in phagocytosis of bacteria, as it can associate with them and defend against them in a splice form-specific manner. Overall, AgDscam is a highly variable PRR that is essential for the innate immune system of A. gambiae.

title: Enterovirus-induced gene expression profile is critical for human pancreatic islet destruction
text: Autoimmune reactions resulting in type 1 diabetes can be caused by viral-induced inflammatory responses, the destruction of beta cells, and the release of beta cell autoantigens. The ability of a virus to induce beta cell death and the immune response it triggers are important factors in determining whether a virus is diabetogenic. Our hypothesis is that enterovirus infections lead to a specific gene expression pattern that causes the destruction of pancreatic islets, and this pattern varies between different strains of the virus. To test this, we studied the changes in gene expression and cytokine profiles in human pancreatic islets infected with lytic or benign enterovirus strains. These strains were either isolated from patients with type 1 diabetes or known to cause a diabetes-like condition in mice. We found that the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokine genes (IL-1-α, IL-1-β, and TNF-α), which contribute to beta cell dysfunction, correlated with the lytic potential of the virus. We also observed an increase in the expression of genes involved in antiviral responses, cytokines, and chemokines for all virus strains studied. In addition, lytic coxsackievirus B5 (CBV-5)-DS infection downregulated genes related to glycolysis and insulin secretion. These findings suggest that enterovirus infections lead to a distinct gene expression pattern that causes the destruction of pancreatic islets and pro-inflammatory effects. However, it is not solely viral replication or cytotoxic cytokine production that leads to necrotic cell death. It is more likely that a combination of these factors, along with cellular energy depletion, contribute to the necrosis of islets induced by enteroviruses.

title: Islet1 derivatives in the heart are of both neural crest and second heart field origin.
text: The purpose of this study was to determine whether the marker Isl1, which is commonly used to identify cardiac progenitor cells derived from the second heart field, is also expressed by cardiac neural crest cells. The researchers used a fate-mapping system to track the lineage of cells expressing Isl1 and found that some Isl1 derivatives in the cardiac outflow tract actually come from neural crest cells. This suggests that Isl1 is not exclusive to second heart field progenitors and may also label neural crest cells. Therefore, caution should be taken when using Isl1 as a marker for second heart field cardiac progenitors, as some Isl1-expressing cells may actually be of neural crest lineage.

title: Review of the secondary injury theory of acute spinal cord trauma with emphasis on vascular mechanisms.
text: In patients with spinal cord injury, the initial trauma rarely causes complete severance of the cord, although it can result in complete loss of function. Furthermore, the cord may experience biochemical and pathological changes that worsen after the injury. To explain these phenomena, the concept of secondary injury has emerged, which suggests various pathophysiological mechanisms. This paper focuses on vascular mechanisms as a key aspect of secondary injury. Evidence is presented to support the theory that posttraumatic ischemia, leading to spinal cord infarction, is a crucial mechanism. Studies using different animal models of acute spinal cord injury have utilized various angiographic methods to assess the microcirculation and measure blood flow in the cord after trauma. These techniques have identified significant systemic and local vascular effects that contribute to the development of secondary injury. Systemic effects include low blood pressure and reduced heart output, while local effects involve the loss of autoregulation in the injured cord segment and a significant decrease in microcirculation in both gray and white matter, particularly in hemorrhagic regions and adjacent areas. This microcirculatory impairment extends a considerable distance from the injury site. Numerous studies have demonstrated a dose-dependent reduction in spinal cord blood flow, which correlates with the severity of the injury, and a progressive decrease in blood flow over time following the injury. Electrophysiological measurements, such as motor and somatosensory evoked potentials, have shown that functional deficits resulting from acute spinal cord injury are directly related to the degree of posttraumatic ischemia. Histologically, early hemorrhagic necrosis occurs, leading to significant infarction at the site of injury. Fortunately, these posttraumatic vascular effects can be addressed. Systemic normotension can be restored through volume expansion or vasopressor administration, while spinal cord blood flow can be improved with dopamine, steroids, nimodipine, or volume expansion. Combining nimodipine and volume expansion has been shown to enhance posttraumatic spinal cord blood flow and improve spinal cord function as measured by evoked potentials. These findings provide compelling evidence that posttraumatic ischemia is a critical secondary mechanism of injury and can be mitigated.

title: Chronophin mediates an ATP-sensing mechanism for cofilin dephosphorylation and neuronal cofilin-actin rod formation.
text: Actin and its main regulatory component, cofilin, are present together in large rod-shaped structures in neurons experiencing energy stress. These structures are also abundant in the brains of individuals with Alzheimer's disease and can be observed in transgenic models of neurodegeneration. When neurons are exposed to insults such as energy loss or oxidative stress, the cellular pool of cofilin undergoes rapid dephosphorylation before assembling into rod-shaped structures. While this suggests that phosphatases play a role in the formation of cofilin rods, the exact mechanism connecting energy stress, phosphocofilin turnover, and subsequent rod assembly has remained unclear. Our study reveals that the cofilin phosphatase chronophin (CIN) interacts with the chaperone hsp90 in an ATP-sensitive manner, forming a biosensor that facilitates cofilin/actin rod formation. Our findings propose a model in which weakened interactions between CIN and hsp90 during ATP depletion enhance CIN-mediated cofilin dephosphorylation and subsequent rod assembly. This mechanism provides an explanation for the development of pathological actin/cofilin aggregates during neurodegenerative energy disturbances.

title: Renal considerations in angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor therapy: a statement for healthcare professionals from the Council on the Kidney in Cardiovascular Disease and the Council for High Blood Pressure Research of the American Heart Association.
text: Angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors are now widely used as antihypertensive drugs. In addition to treating hypertension, they are also used for long-term management of congestive heart failure (CHF), diabetic and nondiabetic nephropathies. While ACE inhibitors generally improve renal blood flow and sodium excretion rates in CHF and slow down progressive renal injury in chronic renal disease, they can also cause "functional renal insufficiency" and/or hyperkalemia. This type of acute renal failure (ARF) typically occurs shortly after starting ACE inhibitor therapy, but can also happen after months or years of use, even without prior issues. ARF is more likely to occur when renal perfusion pressure cannot be maintained due to significant decreases in mean arterial pressure (MAP), or when glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is highly dependent on angiotensin II (Ang II). Preexisting hypotension and low cardiac filling pressures are risk factors for adverse hemodynamic effects of ACE inhibitors in CHF patients. GFR is particularly dependent on Ang II in cases of extracellular fluid (ECF) volume depletion, high-grade bilateral renal artery stenosis, or stenosis of a dominant or single kidney, such as in a renal transplant recipient. Understanding the pathophysiological mechanisms and common risk factors for ACE inhibitor-induced functional ARF is crucial, as preventive strategies exist and, if effectively implemented, may allow for less restricted use of these drugs. Under normal physiological conditions, renal autoregulation adjusts renal vascular resistance to maintain constant RBF and GFR across a wide range of MAPs. This autoregulation mechanism is influenced by Ang II and the sympathetic nervous system. When renal perfusion pressure decreases (as in...

title: Greater clinical benefit of more intensive oral antiplatelet therapy with prasugrel in patients with diabetes mellitus in the trial to assess improvement in therapeutic outcomes by optimizing platelet inhibition with prasugrel-Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction 38.
text:
Patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) have a high risk of experiencing recurrent cardiovascular events after acute coronary syndromes due to increased platelet reactivity. The Trial to Assess Improvement in Therapeutic Outcomes by Optimizing Platelet Inhibition With Prasugrel-Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction 38 (TRITON-TIMI 38) demonstrated that more intensive antiplatelet therapy with prasugrel resulted in a reduction in ischemic events compared to clopidogrel, but with a higher risk of bleeding. In this study, we aimed to compare the effectiveness of prasugrel and clopidogrel specifically among subjects with DM in TRITON-TIMI 38. 

We categorized 13,608 subjects based on their preexisting history of DM and further classified them according to their use of insulin. Using the log-rank test, we compared the primary endpoint (cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke) and key secondary endpoints, including net clinical benefit (death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, and nonfatal TIMI major bleeding). Among the subjects, 3,146 had a preexisting history of DM, with 776 of them receiving insulin. 

The results showed that prasugrel significantly reduced the primary endpoint among subjects without DM (9.2% versus 10.6%; hazard ratio [HR], 0.86; P=0.02) and those with DM (12.2% versus 17.0%; HR, 0.70; P<0.001, P(interaction)=0.09). Among DM subjects, prasugrel provided a benefit for those on insulin (14.3% versus 22.2%; HR, 0.63; P=0.009) and those not on insulin (11.5% versus 15.3%; HR, 0.74; P=0.009). Prasugrel also reduced the incidence of myocardial infarction by 18% among subjects without DM (7.2% versus 8.7%; HR, 0.82; P=0.006) and by 40% among subjects with DM (8.2% versus 13.2%; HR, 0.60; P<0.001, P(interaction)=0.02). 

While there was an increase in TIMI major hemorrhage among subjects without DM on prasugrel (1.6% versus 2.4%; HR, 1.43; P=0.02), the rates were similar between subjects with DM on clopidogrel and prasugrel (2.6% versus 2.5%; HR, 1.06; P=0.81, P(interaction)=0.29). The net clinical benefit with prasugrel was greater for subjects with DM (14.6% versus 19.2%; HR, 0.74; P=0.001) compared to those without DM (11.5% versus 12.3%; HR, 0.92; P=0.16, P(interaction)=0.05). 

In conclusion, subjects with DM experienced a greater reduction in ischemic events without an observed increase in TIMI major bleeding, indicating a greater overall treatment benefit with prasugrel compared to clopidogrel. These findings highlight the particular advantage of more intensive oral antiplatelet therapy provided by prasugrel for patients with DM.

title: Kinetics of early T cell receptor signaling regulate the pathway of lytic granule delivery to the secretory domain.
text: Our study demonstrates that cytolytic granules, responsible for killing virus-infected cells, can take either long or short routes to reach the secretory domain. Despite utilizing the same intracellular molecular events, these paths differ in their spatial and temporal arrangements, which are controlled by the kinetics of Ca(2+)-mediated signaling. When signaling occurs rapidly, the granules quickly concentrate near the microtubule-organizing center (MTOC) and are then delivered directly to the secretory domain by the polarized MTOC, taking the shortest path. On the other hand, when signaling is slower, the granules are recruited later and move along microtubules towards the periphery of the synapse. From there, they move tangentially and fuse at the outer edge of the secretory domain, following a longer path. The shorter pathway is associated with faster granule release and more efficient killing compared to the longer pathway. Therefore, the kinetics of early signaling plays a crucial role in determining the effectiveness of the T cell cytolytic response.

title: Sirtuin-1 is a nutrient-dependent modulator of inflammation
text: Obesity is often accompanied by inflammation and various related conditions such as type 2 diabetes, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, and atherosclerosis. This inflammation is believed to contribute to the development of these conditions, but the exact cellular processes that connect nutrient sensing to inflammation are not fully understood. One protein, called sirtuin-1 (SirT1), is activated when the body is low on energy and plays a crucial role in the body's response to fasting. Recent studies have also suggested that SirT1 is involved in suppressing inflammation. In obese rodents and humans, the expression of SirT1 mRNA and protein is reduced in white adipose tissue. Additionally, when SirT1 is reduced in adipocytes and macrophages, it leads to low-grade inflammation similar to what is observed in obesity. This suggests that the suppression of SirT1 during overnutrition may be a key factor in the development of obesity-related inflammation. SirT1 achieves this effect through various actions, including directly deacetylating NFκB and remodeling the chromatin at inflammatory gene promoters. Our research also shows that diet-induced obesity suppresses SirT1 in macrophages, which play a significant role in metabolic inflammation. Therefore, SirT1 may be a common mechanism through which cells sense nutrient levels and adjust inflammatory signaling networks based on the body's energy availability.

title: A culture-independent sequence-based metagenomics approach to the investigation of an outbreak of Shiga-toxigenic Escherichia coli O104:H4.
text:
The identification of the bacterium responsible for an outbreak is important for disease management. However, traditional culture-based diagnosis can be challenging, especially if there is no specific diagnostic test available for the outbreak strain. The objective of this study was to explore the potential of metagenomics, which involves directly sequencing DNA from complex microbiological samples, as a clinical discovery platform for identifying and characterizing bacterial strains from an outbreak without the need for laboratory culture.

In this retrospective investigation, 45 fecal samples from patients with diarrhea during the 2011 outbreak of Shiga-toxigenic Escherichia coli (STEC) O104:H4 in Germany were selected. These samples underwent high-throughput sequencing, followed by a 3-phase analysis. In phase 1, a draft genome of the outbreak strain was obtained using a de novo assembly approach. In phase 2, the depth of coverage of the outbreak strain genome was determined in each sample. In phase 3, sequences from each sample were compared with sequences from known bacteria to identify pathogens other than the outbreak strain.

The main outcomes and measures of this study were the recovery of genome sequence data for the identification and characterization of the outbreak strain and other pathogens from fecal samples. The results showed that a draft genome of the STEC outbreak strain was obtained during phase 1. In phase 2, the outbreak strain genome was recovered from 10 samples at coverage greater than 10-fold and from 26 samples at coverage greater than 1-fold. Sequences from the Shiga-toxin genes were detected in 27 out of 40 STEC-positive samples (67%). In phase 3, sequences from Clostridium difficile, Campylobacter jejuni, Campylobacter concisus, and Salmonella enterica were also recovered.

In conclusion, these findings suggest that metagenomics has the potential to be a culture-independent approach for identifying bacterial pathogens during an outbreak of diarrheal disease. However, there are challenges that need to be addressed, such as improving diagnostic sensitivity, streamlining workflows, and reducing costs.

title: Biomarkers of endothelial dysfunction and risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus.
text:
The aim of this study was to determine whether elevated levels of certain biomarkers associated with endothelial dysfunction predict the development of type 2 diabetes in women who initially do not have the disease. The study was conducted as a prospective, nested case-control study within the Nurses' Health Study, which began in 1976 in the US. Out of the 121,700 women initially enrolled, 32,826 provided blood samples in 1989-1990. Among those who were free of diabetes, cardiovascular disease, or cancer at baseline, 737 developed incident diabetes by 2000. Controls (n = 785) were selected based on age, fasting status, and race. The main outcome measure was the risk of confirmed clinically diagnosed type 2 diabetes based on baseline levels of E-selectin, ICAM-1, and VCAM-1.

The results showed that the median levels of these biomarkers were significantly higher among cases compared to controls. Elevated levels of E-selectin and ICAM-1 were found to predict the development of diabetes, even after adjusting for various factors such as body mass index, family history of diabetes, smoking, diet score, alcohol intake, activity index, and postmenopausal hormone use. The adjusted relative risks for incident diabetes in the top quintile compared to the bottom quintiles were 5.43 for E-selectin, 3.56 for ICAM-1, and 1.12 for VCAM-1. Further adjustments and exclusions did not change these associations. Therefore, the study concluded that endothelial dysfunction can predict the development of type 2 diabetes in women, independent of other known risk factors such as obesity and subclinical inflammation.

title: Nrf2 protects human alveolar epithelial cells against injury induced by influenza A virus
text:
BACKGROUND: Influenza A virus (IAV) infection primarily targets the cells lining the respiratory tract and can cause a range of clinical outcomes, from mild respiratory infection to severe pneumonia. Recent studies have highlighted the role of antioxidant defense systems in the lungs in protecting against IAV-induced damage. One key player in this defense system is a protein called nuclear factor-erythroid 2 related factor 2 (Nrf2), which activates many antioxidant genes.

METHODS: We isolated alveolar type II (ATII) cells and alveolar macrophages (AM) from human lungs that were not suitable for transplantation but were donated for medical research. In some experiments, we transformed ATII cells into cells resembling alveolar type I cells (ATI-like cells). We infected these alveolar epithelial cells with the PR8 strain of IAV and analyzed various factors, including virus production, levels of influenza A nucleoprotein, generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), and expression of antiviral genes. We used immunocytofluorescence to study the movement of Nrf2 within the cells and performed western blotting to detect Nrf2, HO-1, and cleavage of caspase 1 and 3. We also examined the ingestion of PR8 virus-infected apoptotic ATII cells by AM, measured cytokine levels using ELISA, assessed glutathione levels, and determined levels of necrosis and apoptosis using a TUNEL assay. Additionally, we investigated the importance of Nrf2 by overexpressing it using adenovirus Nrf2 (AdNrf2) or knocking it down using Nrf2 siRNA.

RESULTS: Our findings showed that IAV infection induced oxidative stress, cytotoxicity, and apoptosis in ATI-like and ATII cells. We also observed that AM were able to ingest apoptotic ATII cells induced by PR8 virus (a process called efferocytosis), but not viable cells. In contrast, ATII cells did not ingest these apoptotic cells. PR8 virus infection increased ROS production, as well as the expression and translocation of Nrf2, HO-1, Mx1, and OAS1. Knocking down Nrf2 with siRNA made ATI-like cells and ATII cells more susceptible to IAV-induced injury, while overexpressing Nrf2 with AdNrf2 protected these cells. Furthermore, overexpressing Nrf2 followed by PR8 virus infection reduced virus replication, influenza A nucleoprotein expression, the antiviral response, and oxidative stress. However, AdNrf2 did not increase levels of IFN-λ1 (IL-29).

CONCLUSIONS: Our results demonstrate that IAV infection causes damage to the cells lining the alveoli, and Nrf2 plays a protective role by increasing the expression of antioxidant genes. Understanding the mechanisms involved in protecting cells from injury during influenza infection could be crucial for developing new therapeutic strategies.

title: Dynamics in the plasma membrane: how to combine fluidity and order.
text: The cell membrane is an intriguing structure that not only acts as a barrier between different parts of a cell, but also plays a crucial role in various chemical reactions necessary for the cell's survival and function. In this review, we aim to explore the molecular dynamics and organization of the plasma membrane, which are believed to have significant functional implications. Initially, we will provide an overview of the fundamental principles of Brownian diffusion and the formation of lipid domains in model membranes. Subsequently, we will trace the evolution of ideas and tools in this field, highlighting key findings related to the dynamic processes involved in membrane structure and assembly. Our focus will be on studies that utilize fluorescent labeling and imaging techniques to observe these dynamic processes. Additionally, we will examine a few examples that demonstrate the influence of lateral diffusion on cell signal transduction. Finally, we will outline some future challenges in methodology that need to be addressed in order to answer the remaining questions in this research area.

title: Management of chronic tension-type headache with tricyclic antidepressant medication, stress management therapy, and their combination: a randomized controlled trial.
text:
The aim of this study was to assess the effectiveness of behavioral and pharmacological therapies, both individually and in combination, for chronic tension-type headaches. The study was conducted as a randomized placebo-controlled trial at two outpatient sites in Ohio from August 1995 to January 1998. A total of 203 adults with a diagnosis of chronic tension-type headaches participated in the study. The participants were randomly assigned to one of four groups: tricyclic antidepressant medication, placebo, stress management therapy plus placebo, or stress management therapy plus antidepressant medication. The main outcome measures included monthly headache index scores, number of days with at least moderate pain, analgesic medication use, and Headache Disability Inventory scores. 

The results showed that both tricyclic antidepressant medication and stress management therapy were more effective in reducing headache activity, analgesic medication use, and headache-related disability compared to placebo. However, antidepressant medication led to faster improvements in headache activity. The combination therapy was more likely to result in clinically significant reductions in headache index scores compared to antidepressant medication, stress management therapy, or placebo alone. The combination therapy and its individual components produced similar outcomes on other measures. 

In conclusion, this study suggests that both antidepressant medication and stress management therapy have modest effectiveness in treating chronic tension-type headaches. Combining these therapies may lead to better outcomes compared to using them individually.

title: Maximum likelihood estimates of species trees: how accuracy of phylogenetic inference depends upon the divergence history and sampling design.
text:
Researchers have recognized that gene trees often differ from each other and from the species trees that contain them. This has led to the development of methods that take into account the stochastic nature of genetic processes in phylogenetic estimation. Recently, new methods have been developed that not only consider the retention and sorting of ancestral polymorphism, but also quantify the probabilities of incomplete lineage sorting. These methods are expected to be an improvement over earlier approaches that discard much of the information in gene trees.

However, these new methods have not yet been tested on challenging evolutionary histories, such as those characterized by rapid speciation where incomplete lineage sorting and discord among gene trees are common. In this study, we test a new maximum-likelihood method that incorporates stochastic models of nucleotide substitution and lineage sorting for species-tree estimation. Using simulations, we consider a wide range of species-tree topologies under two scenarios representing moderate and severe incomplete lineage sorting.

Our results show that the maximum-likelihood method produces more accurate species trees than the summary-statistic based approach. This demonstrates that information from discordant gene trees can be effectively extracted using a full probabilistic model. We also find that the shape of the original species tree, specifically the relative lengths of internal branches, significantly affects the accuracy of the estimated species tree. In addition, the accuracy of species-tree estimates is influenced by the variance in relative species divergence times, not just the recent origin of species.

We also show that the number of individuals and/or loci sampled, as well as the ratio of individuals to loci, are important factors affecting the accuracy of species-tree estimates. These factors are also influenced by the relative timing of species divergence. We discuss the challenges of estimating relationships in recent radiations and highlight the limitations of maximum-likelihood estimates that do not consider uncertainty in gene tree estimates.

In conclusion, while there have been significant improvements in phylogenetic approaches, recent radiations still present challenges for accurate species-tree estimation.

title: Relationship of soft drink consumption to global overweight, obesity, and diabetes: a cross-national analysis of 75 countries.
text: Our objectives were to examine the correlation between soft drink consumption and rates of obesity and diabetes on a global scale. To achieve this, we utilized multivariate linear regression to analyze data from 75 countries. We controlled for various factors such as other food consumption, income, urbanization, and aging. Data was collected from the Euromonitor Global Market Information Database, the World Health Organization, and the International Diabetes Federation. As a comparison, we also looked at bottled water consumption, which increased alongside soft drink consumption as per capita income rose. The results showed that soft drink consumption increased globally from 9.5 gallons per person per year in 1997 to 11.4 gallons in 2010. For every 1% increase in soft drink consumption, there was a corresponding increase of 4.8 overweight adults per 100, 2.3 obese adults per 100, and 0.3 adults with diabetes per 100. These findings were consistent across low- and middle-income countries. In conclusion, our study demonstrates a significant association between soft drink consumption and rates of overweight, obesity, and diabetes worldwide, including in low- and middle-income countries.

title: Extensive translation of circular RNAs driven by N6-methyladenosine
text: The human transcriptome contains a large number of circular RNAs (circRNAs) that are generated through extensive pre-mRNA back-splicing. However, the functions of these circRNAs are not well understood. In this study, we have found that N6-methyladenosine (m6A), the most common base modification of RNA, plays a role in promoting protein translation from circRNAs in human cells. We have observed that circRNAs are enriched with consensus m6A motifs, and a single m6A site is sufficient to initiate translation. This m6A-driven translation process requires the involvement of initiation factor eIF4G2 and m6A reader YTHDF3. Additionally, it is enhanced by methyltransferase METTL3/14, inhibited by demethylase FTO, and upregulated during heat shock. Through various analyses, including polysome profiling, computational prediction, and mass spectrometry, we have discovered that m6A-driven translation of circRNAs is widespread, with hundreds of endogenous circRNAs having the potential to be translated into proteins. Our findings expand our understanding of the coding landscape of the human transcriptome and suggest that proteins derived from circRNAs may play a role in cellular responses to environmental stress.

title: Simvastatin reduces CD40 expression in an experimental model of early arterialization of saphenous vein graft.
text:
The failure of saphenous vein grafts (VG) occurs more frequently than arterial grafts, with graft thrombosis being the main cause of early occlusion. The CD40-CD40L pathway, specifically CD40, is believed to be a key link between local inflammation and the coagulation cascade. In this study, we aimed to investigate the role of CD40 and its soluble ligand (sCD40L) in the immediate response of VG to arterial pressures, as well as the potential effects of Simvastatin supplementation. 

We obtained samples of saphenous vein and internal mammary artery (IMA) from sixteen patients who had not received statin therapy. These samples were subjected to pulsatile pressure distension and cultured with or without Simvastatin supplementation. We assessed the levels of CD40 and sCD40L in tissue lysate and culture supernatant, respectively. We also measured sCD40L serum concentrations. 

Throughout the experiment, we observed that CD40 expression was significantly lower in IMA samples compared to both distended and non-distended VG samples. Pressure distension increased CD40 production in VG segments after 24 and 48 hours. Simvastatin supplementation significantly reduced CD40 expression in both venous and arterial samples. This effect was not influenced by treatment with L-NAME, but was reversed by the addition of mevalonic acid. The levels of sCD40L in culture supernatants increased over time, indicating that both platelets and the vessel wall are sources of CD40 and sCD40L. 

In conclusion, Simvastatin treatment can modulate endothelial CD40-sCD40L in both venous and arterial grafts, suggesting its potential as a useful tool in preventing graft failure through pharmacological means.

title: Cancer Cell Membrane-Coated Nanoparticles for Anticancer Vaccination and Drug Delivery
text: The use of nanoparticles derived from cells has gained attention for their ability to imitate the natural properties of the cells they come from. This approach, known as top-down engineering, can be used to develop new therapeutic strategies by retaining complex antigenic information and enabling unique interactions. In this study, we describe the process of biologically modifying polymeric nanoparticles with a layer of cancer cell membrane coating. These resulting core-shell nanostructures contain all the cancer cell membrane antigens and provide a strong foundation for various anticancer therapies. We demonstrate that when these particles are combined with an immunological adjuvant, they can stimulate a specific immune response against tumors, making them suitable for vaccine applications. Additionally, we show that the membrane coating allows for a targeted drug delivery strategy by taking advantage of the natural binding tendencies among tumor cells.

title: Autophagy deficiency leads to protection from obesity and insulin resistance by inducing Fgf21 as a mitokine
text: The role of autophagy in glucose and lipid metabolism remains unclear, despite increasing interest and recent research. To gain more insight, we conducted a study using mice with skeletal muscle-specific deletion of Atg7, a gene related to autophagy. Surprisingly, these mice exhibited reduced fat mass and were resistant to diet-induced obesity and insulin resistance. This was accompanied by an increase in fatty acid oxidation and browning of white adipose tissue, which was attributed to the induction of fibroblast growth factor 21 (Fgf21). The deficiency in autophagy led to mitochondrial dysfunction, which in turn increased Fgf21 expression through the activation of Atf4, a key regulator of the integrated stress response. We also found that inhibiting the mitochondrial respiratory chain resulted in the induction of Fgf21 in an Atf4-dependent manner. Additionally, we observed similar effects in mice with autophagy deficiency in the liver, another insulin target tissue, including the induction of Fgf21, resistance to diet-induced obesity, and improvement in insulin resistance. These findings suggest that autophagy deficiency and subsequent mitochondrial dysfunction promote the expression of Fgf21, which we refer to as a "mitokine." Together, these processes contribute to protection against diet-induced obesity and insulin resistance.

title: Laboratory prediction of the requirement for renal replacement in acute falciparum malaria
text:
Acute renal failure is a common complication of severe malaria in adults, and without renal replacement therapy (RRT), it has a poor prognosis. Delaying the initiation of RRT, even when available, may increase mortality. Identifying patients who will need RRT earlier may improve outcomes. 

To investigate this, data from two intervention studies in adults with severe malaria were analyzed. The focus was on laboratory features on presentation and their association with the later need for RRT. Specifically, laboratory indices of acute tubular necrosis (ATN) and acute kidney injury (AKI) used in other settings were examined. 

The analysis included data from 163 patients. A retrospective assessment, determined by three independent reviewers, was used as the reference to determine whether or not the patients should have received RRT. Of the patients, 43 (26.4%) met the criteria for dialysis, but only 19 (44.2%) were able to receive this intervention due to limited availability of RRT. 

For patients with impaired renal function on admission (creatinine clearance < 60 ml/min) (n = 84), their laboratory indices of ATN/AKI were analyzed. The plasma creatinine level had the highest area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.83 (95% confidence interval 0.74-0.92), which was significantly better than the AUCs for urinary sodium level, the urea to creatinine ratio (UCR), the fractional excretion of urea (FeUN), and the urinary neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalcin (NGAL) level. The AUC for plasma creatinine was also higher than the AUC for blood urea nitrogen level, the fractional excretion of sodium (FeNa), the renal failure index (RFI), the urinary osmolality, the urine to plasma creatinine ratio (UPCR), and the creatinine clearance, although the difference for these variables did not reach statistical significance. 

In conclusion, among adult patients with severe malaria and impaired renal function on admission, none of the evaluated laboratory indices were superior to the plasma creatinine level in predicting the later need for renal replacement therapy.

title: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA).
text: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) are a highly sensitive and specific marker for ANCA-associated systemic vasculitis. By using indirect immunofluorescence on ethanol-fixed neutrophils, two distinct fluoroscopic patterns can be identified: diffuse cytoplasmic staining (C-ANCA) and perinuclear/nuclear staining (P-ANCA). In patients with vasculitis, over 90% of C-ANCA are targeted against proteinase 3 (PR3-ANCA), while approximately 80-90% of P-ANCA recognize myeloperoxidase (MPO-ANCA). Although C-ANCA (PR3-ANCA) is primarily associated with Wegener's granulomatosis (WG), and P-ANCA (MPO-ANCA) with microscopic polyangiitis (MPA), idiopathic necrotizing crescentic glomerulonephritis (iNCGN), and Churg-Strauss syndrome (CSS), there is not absolute specificity. Around 10-20% of patients with classical WG exhibit P-ANCA (MPO-ANCA), and an even larger percentage of patients with MPA or CSS have C-ANCA (PR3-ANCA). Additionally, it is important to note that approximately 10-20% of patients with WG or MPA (and 40-50% of CSS cases) test negative for ANCA. The most accurate diagnosis is achieved when indirect immunofluorescence is combined with PR3 and MPO-specific ELISAs. ANCA with different and unknown antigen specificity can be present in various conditions other than ANCA-associated systemic vasculitis, including inflammatory bowel diseases, other autoimmune diseases, and infections, where their clinical significance remains unclear. Monitoring ANCA levels is useful for assessing disease activity, but it should not be the sole basis for treatment decisions. A significant increase in ANCA titres or the reappearance of ANCA should alert clinicians and prompt closer patient monitoring.

title: Emerging functional cross-talk between the Keap1-Nrf2 system and mitochondria
text: The Nuclear factor erythroid-derived 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) was initially discovered as a positive regulator of drug detoxifying enzyme gene expression when exposed to environmental electrophiles. Presently, it is known that Nrf2 regulates the expression of numerous cytoprotective genes to counteract oxidative stress generated internally or externally. Moreover, when activated by somatic mutations in human tumors, Nrf2 provides growth advantages and resistance to chemotherapy by controlling genes involved in processes like the pentose phosphate pathway, nucleotide synthesis, and antioxidant proteins. Interestingly, emerging evidence suggests that Nrf2 is linked to mitochondrial biogenesis in specific tissues, such as the heart, during environmental stresses. Additionally, SKN-1, a functional equivalent of Nrf2 in C. elegans, is activated by reactive oxygen species in mitochondria and promotes mitochondrial homeostasis, thereby extending lifespan through mitohormesis. Similarly, Nrf2 activation has recently been observed in the hearts of mice lacking the surfeit locus protein 1 (Surf1), which exhibited decreased cellular respiration due to defects in cytochrome c oxidase. In this review, we critically analyze the connection between Nrf2 and mitochondria and argue that the Nrf2 stress pathway closely interacts with mitochondria to uphold cellular homeostasis during oxidative stress.

title: Regulation of pluripotency by RNA binding proteins.
text: The precise coordination of a cell's molecular machinery is crucial for the establishment, maintenance, and exit from pluripotency. Significant progress has been made in understanding various aspects of this complex system, particularly in the fields of epigenetics, transcription, and noncoding RNAs. However, less attention has been given to posttranscriptional regulatory processes, including alternative splicing, RNA processing and modification, nuclear export, regulation of transcript stability, and translation. In this article, we present an overview of RNA binding proteins that play a key role in posttranscriptional regulation of gene expression. We summarize current research and ongoing studies on their functions at different regulatory points, and explore how they contribute to shaping the fate of pluripotent stem cells.

title: The ubiquitin ligase Drosophila Mind bomb promotes Notch signaling by regulating the localization and activity of Serrate and Delta.
text: The Notch pathway, which plays a crucial role in animal development, relies on the receptor Notch and its ligands from the Delta/Serrate/LAG2 (DSL) family. These ligands are regulated by two unrelated RING-type E3 ubiquitin ligases, Drosophila and Xenopus Neuralized, and zebrafish Mind bomb, which promote the endocytosis and signaling activity of Delta. While Neuralized and Mind bomb orthologs are present in most metazoan organisms, their specific contributions to Notch signaling in each organism remain unknown. In this study, we demonstrate that the Drosophila ortholog of Mind bomb (D-mib) is a positive component of Notch signaling, essential for various Neuralized-independent, Notch-dependent developmental processes. Additionally, we find that D-mib physically and functionally interacts with both Serrate and Delta. Our findings indicate that D-mib's ubiquitin ligase activity enhances DSL ligand activity by promoting the endocytosis and degradation of Delta and Serrate. Moreover, we show that D-mib can substitute for Neuralized in cell fate decisions that require Neuralized, highlighting the similar functions of these unrelated ubiquitin ligases in regulating Notch signaling. Overall, our study establishes the ubiquitination of Delta and Serrate by Neuralized and D-mib as a crucial aspect of DSL ligand activation during Drosophila development.

title: Myeloid differentiation factor-88/interleukin-1 signaling controls cardiac fibrosis and heart failure progression in inflammatory dilated cardiomyopathy.
text:
RATIONALE: The activation of self-antigen-presenting cells and expansion of autoreactive CD4(+) T-cells in experimental autoimmune myocarditis, a mouse model of inflammatory heart disease, is mediated by the myeloid differentiation factor (MyD)88/interleukin (IL)-1 axis.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the involvement of MyD88 and IL-1 in the progression of acute myocarditis to end-stage heart failure.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Myocarditis was induced in both wild-type and MyD88(-/-) mice using alpha-myosin heavy chain peptide (MyHC-alpha)-loaded, activated dendritic cells. The distribution of heart-infiltrating cell subsets and CD4(+) T-cell responses were similar in both groups. However, injection of complete Freund's adjuvant (CFA) or MyHC-alpha/CFA into diseased mice resulted in cardiac fibrosis, ventricular dilation, and impaired heart function only in wild-type mice, not in MyD88(-/-) mice. Further experiments using chimeric mice confirmed that fibroblasts replacing inflammatory infiltrates originated from the bone marrow and demonstrated that MyD88 and IL-1 receptor type I signaling on bone marrow-derived cells was crucial for the development of cardiac fibrosis during the progression to heart failure.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight the importance of MyD88/IL-1 signaling in the bone marrow compartment in postinflammatory cardiac fibrosis and heart failure. These findings suggest potential therapeutic strategies for treating inflammatory cardiomyopathy.

title: Mechanisms of Life Span Extension by Rapamycin in the Fruit Fly Drosophila melanogaster
text: The TOR pathway, which is responsible for sensing nutrients, plays a crucial role in determining life span in various organisms, including mammals. By reducing the activity of TOR kinase, the main component of this pathway, through the use of the drug rapamycin, life span can be extended. Rapamycin is a well-known and highly targeted drug that has been approved for human use. In our study, we found that administering rapamycin to adult Drosophila flies resulted in an increase in life span similar to that observed in flies with mutations in the TOR pathway. This life span extension was accompanied by improved resistance to both starvation and paraquat. Further investigation revealed that rapamycin specifically increased longevity through the TORC1 branch of the TOR pathway, by affecting both autophagy and translation. Interestingly, rapamycin was also able to extend the life span of flies with weakened insulin/Igf signaling pathways and those whose life span was already maximized through dietary restriction, suggesting the involvement of additional mechanisms.

title: Conversion of vascular endothelial cells into multipotent stem-like cells
text: The usefulness of mesenchymal stem cells in clinical medicine has been a topic of controversy due to varying results based on isolation methods and tissue source. However, our study reveals that vascular endothelial cells can undergo a transformation into multipotent stem-like cells through a mechanism dependent on the activin-like kinase-2 (ALK2) receptor. In individuals with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP), a condition characterized by heterotopic ossification resulting from ALK2 mutations, or in transgenic mice expressing constitutively active ALK2, chondrocytes and osteoblasts were found to express endothelial markers. Additionally, lineage tracing experiments using a Tie2-Cre construct in mice with heterotopic ossification suggested an endothelial origin for these cell types. When endothelial cells were engineered to express constitutively active ALK2, they underwent endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition and acquired a stem cell-like phenotype. Similar results were observed when untransfected endothelial cells were treated with the ligands transforming growth factor-β2 (TGF-β2) or bone morphogenetic protein-4 (BMP4) in an ALK2-dependent manner. These stem-like cells were capable of differentiating into osteoblasts, chondrocytes, or adipocytes. Our findings suggest that the conversion of endothelial cells into stem-like cells could offer a novel approach to tissue engineering.

title: miR-302 Is Required for Timing of Neural Differentiation, Neural Tube Closure, and Embryonic Viability
text: The miR-302 family of microRNAs, which is conserved throughout evolution, is expressed in the early stages of mammalian embryonic development. In this study, we demonstrate that deleting miR-302a-d in mice leads to a fully penetrant lethal phenotype in late embryonic stages. The embryos lacking miR-302a-d exhibit a defect in the closure of the anterior neural tube, accompanied by a thickened neuroepithelium. The neuroepithelium shows an increase in the proliferation of progenitor cells, a decrease in cell death, and an early differentiation of neurons. Through mRNA profiling at different time points during neurulation, we observe a complex pattern of changing targets. Overexpressing one of these targets, Fgf15, in the neuroepithelium of chick embryos induces an early differentiation of neurons. Additionally, compound mutants with deletions in both mir-302 and the related mir-290 locus display a lethal phenotype before neurulation. Our findings demonstrate that mir-302 plays a role in regulating neurulation by suppressing the expansion of neural progenitor cells and promoting precocious differentiation. Furthermore, our results reveal redundant functions of mir-290 and mir-302 in early embryonic development.

title: Low copy number of the salivary amylase gene predisposes to obesity
text: We conducted a study to examine the impact of gene dosage effects on adiposity by analyzing gene expression levels in adipose tissue. We found a significant association between a multi-allelic copy number variant (CNV) that includes the salivary amylase gene (AMY1) and body mass index (BMI) and obesity. This finding was replicated in a large sample of 6,200 subjects. Higher AMY1 copy number was linked to increased amylase gene expression and serum enzyme levels. Conversely, lower AMY1 copy number was associated with higher BMI and increased risk of obesity. The odds ratio (OR) of 1.19 per copy of AMY1 translates to an eightfold difference in obesity risk between individuals in the top (copy number > 9) and bottom (copy number < 4) 10% of the copy number distribution. This study establishes a genetic connection between carbohydrate metabolism and BMI, highlighting the value of integrated genomic approaches beyond traditional genome-wide association studies.

title: Loss, trauma, and human resilience: have we underestimated the human capacity to thrive after extremely aversive events?
text: At some point in their lives, many individuals encounter loss or potentially traumatic events. Surprisingly, they are able to maintain positive emotional experiences and only experience temporary disruptions in their functioning. However, the field of psychology has primarily focused on individuals seeking treatment or displaying significant distress when studying how adults cope with loss or trauma. As a result, resilience has been seen as rare or abnormal by loss and trauma theorists. The author challenges these assumptions by presenting evidence that resilience is a separate process from recovery, that it is more prevalent than commonly thought, and that there are various unexpected paths to resilience.

title: Role of boundary conditions in an experimental model of epithelial wound healing.
text: Our understanding of the mechanisms that coordinate the behavior of multiple cells in epithelial layers, which is crucial for tissue morphogenesis and homeostasis, is still incomplete. Recent experiments using Madin-Darby canine kidney epithelial monolayers have discovered a wave-like pattern of MAPK activation in response to injury. This activation is essential for collective cell migration during wound healing. To further investigate the effects of different aspects of wound healing on cell sheet migration, we developed a system that allowed us to analyze the classic wound healing assay. We studied Madin-Darby canine kidney sheet migration under three conditions: 1) the classic wound healing assay, 2) empty space induction, where a non-injured monolayer is grown next to a polydimethylsiloxane slab and allowed to migrate after removing the slab, and 3) injury via polydimethylsiloxane membrane peel-off, where an injured monolayer migrates onto a plain tissue culture surface, similar to empty space induction for direct comparison. By tracking the movement of individual cells within the sheet under these three conditions, we demonstrate how the dynamics of individual cell motion coordinate the migration of the entire sheet and are synchronized with the activation of ERK1/2 MAPK. Furthermore, we show that the propagation of MAPK activation waves relies on the generation of reactive oxygen species at the wound edge.

title: Reproductive period and risk of dementia in postmenopausal women.
text:
The objective of this study was to investigate whether a longer reproductive period, indicating longer exposure to endogenous estrogens, is associated with a lower risk of dementia and Alzheimer's disease (AD) in women who experience natural menopause. The study was conducted as part of the Rotterdam Study, a population-based prospective cohort study in the Netherlands. A total of 3601 women aged 55 years or older, without dementia at baseline, were included in the study. The participants were examined in 1990-1993, 1993-1994, and 1997-1999, and were continuously monitored for the development of dementia. The main outcome measures were the incidence of dementia and AD, compared by quartiles of reproductive period among women with natural menopause.
