The complete recovery of the mTEC(high) subset occurs within 10 days and is accompanied by a reduction in the relatively resistant MHC class II(low) mTEC subset (mTEC(low)), which aligns with a previously described precursor-product relationship. Cyclophosphamide and dexamethasone cause even more extensive elimination of thymocytes and stromal cells, but they also severely deplete tolerance-inducing mTEC(high). These findings demonstrate that Aire(+) mTECs are highly susceptible to damage and that the regeneration of mTECs follows a consistent pattern regardless of the specific treatment regimen employed.

title: GATA-3 regulates hematopoietic stem cell maintenance and cell-cycle entry.
text: Maintaining the quiescence of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) is crucial for the continuous production of blood cells throughout life. In a highly enriched pool of long-term repopulating HSCs (LT-HSCs), approximately 75% of cells are in a quiescent state, while only a small percentage are actively dividing. The transcription factor GATA-3 plays a vital role in the development of T cells in the thymus and in the differentiation of Th2 cells in peripheral organs. Although GATA-3 is known to be expressed in HSCs, its role in any prethymic progenitor cell has not been established. This study demonstrates that mice lacking the Gata3 gene produce fewer LT-HSCs, and a smaller proportion of these LT-HSCs are actively dividing. Additionally, Gata3 mutant hematopoietic progenitor cells fail to enter an increased cycling state after myelosuppression induced by 5-fluorouracil. Therefore, GATA-3 is necessary for maintaining a normal number of LT-HSCs and for their progression into the cell cycle.

title: CpG island methylator phenotype predicts progression of malignant melanoma.
text: The purpose of this study was to investigate the CpG island methylator phenotype (CIMP) and its association with the development of malignancy in gastrointestinal cancers and malignant melanoma. The researchers hypothesized that a clinically significant CIMP may exist in cutaneous melanoma progression. They assessed the methylation status of tumor suppressor and tumor-related genes (WIF1, TFPI2, RASSF1A, RARbeta2, SOCS1, and GATA4) and a panel of methylated-in-tumor (MINT) loci (MINT1, MINT2, MINT3, MINT12, MINT17, MINT25, and MINT31) in primary and metastatic tumors of different clinical stages. The results showed an increase in hypermethylation of certain genes with advancing clinical tumor stage, as well as a positive association between the methylation status of certain MINT loci and tumor-related genes. The methylation status of MINT31 was found to be associated with disease outcome in stage III melanoma. These findings highlight the significance of a CIMP pattern in malignant melanoma and suggest that further studies may determine if CIMP-positive primary melanomas are at high risk of metastasis or recurrence.

title: SLC1A5 mediates glutamine transport required for lung cancer cell growth and survival.
text: The purpose of this study was to investigate the role of solute-linked carrier family A1 member 5 (SLC1A5) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and its impact on cell growth and survival. The researchers conducted experiments to analyze the expression of SLC1A5 in lung cancer tissues and cell lines, as well as its involvement in amino acid transportation. They also examined the effects of inhibiting SLC1A5 on cell growth, cell-cycle progression, and growth signaling pathways. The results showed that SLC1A5 was overexpressed in NSCLC, particularly in squamous cell carcinomas, and was associated with male gender. The researchers also found that SLC1A5 played a crucial role in glutamine transport, with 50% of glutamine uptake attributed to SLC1A5 activity. Inhibiting SLC1A5 decreased cell growth and viability, partly through the mTOR signaling pathway. These findings suggest that SLC1A5 is important for controlling the metabolism, growth, and survival of lung cancer cells.

title: Eic1 links Mis18 with the CCAN/Mis6/Ctf19 complex to promote CENP-A assembly
text: The formation of CENP-A chromatin is essential for the assembly of kinetochores. The incorporation of CENP-A at centromeres, which occurs independently of replication, relies on the presence of its chaperone HJURP(Scm3) and Mis18 in both vertebrates and fission yeast. The recruitment of Mis18 and HJURP(Scm3) to centromeres is regulated by the cell cycle. In vertebrates, Mis18 associates with Mis18BP1(KNL2), a crucial protein for the recruitment of Mis18 and HJURP(Scm3). In our study, we have discovered two new proteins in fission yeast, Eic1 and Eic2, which interact with Mis18. Eic1 is essential for maintaining Cnp1(CENP-A) at centromeres and plays a critical role in kinetochore integrity, while Eic2 is not necessary. Eic1 also interacts with other components of the constitutive CCAN/Mis6/Ctf19 complex, namely Fta7(CENP-Q/Okp1), Cnl2(Nkp2), and Mal2(CENP-O/Mcm21). Unlike in vertebrates, fission yeast does not have a Mis18BP1(KNL2) equivalent, so the mechanism by which Mis18 is recruited to centromeres in this organism remains unknown. Our findings suggest that Eic1 functions similarly to Mis18BP1(KNL2) and acts as its counterpart in fission yeast. Eic1 connects with a module within the CCAN/Mis6/Ctf19 complex, allowing the regulated recruitment of the Mis18/Scm3(HJURP) Cnp1(CENP-A) loading factors. These newly identified interactions between CENP-A loading factors and the CCAN/Mis6/Ctf19 complex are likely to contribute to CENP-A maintenance in other organisms as well.

title: INTRANASAL INSULIN IMPROVES COGNITION AND MODULATES β-AMYLOID IN EARLY AD
text:
Background: Patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD) have been found to have reduced brain insulin signaling and low ratios of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) to plasma insulin. Additionally, administering insulin intracerebroventricularly or intravenously has been shown to improve memory, alter evoked potentials, and modulate neurotransmitters, potentially by increasing low brain levels. Insulin-like peptides administered intranasally can reach the brain within 15 minutes by following extracellular pathways. 

Objective: We aimed to test the hypothesis that daily intranasal insulin treatment would enhance cognition in patients with early AD or its prodrome, amnestic mild cognitive impairment (MCI). The primary outcome measure was the proportion of retained verbal information after a delay period. Secondary outcome measures included attention, caregiver rating of functional status, and plasma levels of insulin, glucose, β-amyloid, and cortisol. 

Methods: Twenty-five participants were randomly assigned to receive either placebo (n = 12) or 20 IU twice daily (BID) intranasal insulin treatment (n = 13) using an electronic atomizer. A total of 24 participants completed the study. Treatment assignment was blinded to participants, caregivers, and all clinical evaluators. Cognitive measures and blood samples were collected at baseline and after 21 days of treatment. 

Results: Fasting plasma glucose and insulin levels remained unchanged with treatment. The group receiving insulin treatment retained more verbal information after a delay compared to the placebo group (p = 0.0374). Insulin-treated subjects also showed improved attention (p = 0.0108) and functional status (p = 0.0410). Insulin treatment increased fasting plasma concentrations of the short form of the β-amyloid peptide (Aβ40; p = 0.0471) without affecting the longer isoform (Aβ42), resulting in an increased Aβ40/42 ratio (p = 0.0207). 

Conclusions: The findings of this pilot study support further investigation into the potential benefits of intranasal insulin for patients with Alzheimer's disease. Additionally, intranasal peptide administration may offer a novel approach to treating neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Maternal alloantigens promote the development of tolerogenic fetal regulatory T cells in utero.
text: As the immune system matures, T cells undergo a process of selection or regulation to become tolerant of self antigens and responsive to foreign antigens. In mice, this tolerance is believed to be achieved through the elimination of self-reactive cells. However, our research demonstrates that the human fetal immune system employs an additional mechanism: the production of regulatory T cells (Tregs) that inhibit fetal immune responses. We have discovered that a significant number of maternal cells cross the placenta and take up residence in fetal lymph nodes, triggering the development of CD4+CD25highFoxP3+ Tregs. These Tregs suppress the immune response against maternal antigens and persist until at least early adulthood. These findings unveil a type of antigen-specific tolerance in humans that is induced during fetal development and likely continues to regulate immune responses after birth.

title: β-site amyloid precursor protein-cleaving enzyme 1(BACE1) inhibitor treatment induces Aβ5-X peptides through alternative amyloid precursor protein cleavage
text:
INTRODUCTION
The enzyme β-secretase, also known as β-site amyloid precursor protein-cleaving enzyme 1 (BACE1), plays a crucial role in the production of β-amyloid (Aβ) peptides by cleaving amyloid precursor protein (APP). Therefore, targeting BACE1 is important for potential disease-modifying treatments for Alzheimer's disease. In a previous study investigating Aβ biomarkers, we discovered that treatment with a BACE1 inhibitor led to a decrease in Aβ1-34 levels and an increase in Aβ5-40 levels. This suggests that these Aβ species could serve as novel pharmacodynamic biomarkers in clinical trials. We have now conducted a study to determine if these findings hold true in humans.

METHODS
In an investigator-blind, placebo-controlled, and randomized study, we enrolled 18 healthy subjects who were randomly assigned to receive a single dose of either 30 mg or 90 mg of LY2811376 (a BACE1 inhibitor) or a placebo. We utilized hybrid immunoaffinity-mass spectrometry (HI-MS) and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays to monitor various Aβ peptides.

RESULTS
Our results demonstrate that treatment with the BACE1 inhibitor LY2811376 leads to dose-dependent changes in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) levels of Aβ1-34, Aβ5-40, and Aβ5-X. Both Aβ5-40 and Aβ5-X increase in a dose-dependent manner, as confirmed by two independent measurement techniques. Conversely, Aβ1-34 decreases in a dose-dependent manner.

CONCLUSION
For the first time, we have used HI-MS in a study involving subjects treated with a BACE1 inhibitor. Our findings confirm that CSF Aβ1-34 could be a valuable marker for monitoring target engagement in clinical trials of BACE1 inhibitors. This marker is less hydrophobic than longer Aβ species, making it less susceptible to preanalytical confounding factors and potentially more stable. Additionally, our independent measurement techniques reveal that BACE1 inhibition in humans leads to the production of N-terminally truncated Aβ peptides through a BACE1-independent pathway.

TRIAL REGISTRATION
This study is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov under the identifier NCT00838084. The trial was first received on January 23, 2009, last updated on July 14, 2009, and last verified in July 2009.

title: Cardiovascular diseases in Chinese, Malays, and Indians in Singapore. I. Differences in mortality.
text: The objective of this study was to examine the variations in mortality rates from major cardiovascular diseases (ischaemic heart disease, hypertensive disease, and cerebrovascular disease) among Chinese, Malays, and Indians in Singapore. The study utilized national death registration data from Singapore between 1980 and 1984. The underlying cause of death, classified according to the ninth revision of the International Classification of Diseases, was used for analysis. The study was conducted solely in Singapore, an independent island state with a population of 2.53 million (76.5% Chinese, 14.8% Malays, 6.4% Indians, and 2.3% others). Death registration was considered to be comprehensive. The study focused on all registered deaths in the age range of 30-69 years, categorized by ethnic group. The main findings revealed that Indians had higher mortality rates from ischaemic heart disease compared to the other ethnic groups in both genders. The age-standardized relative risks for Indians versus Chinese were 3.8 for males and 3.4 for females, for Indians versus Malays were 1.9 for males and 1.6 for females, and for Malays versus Chinese were 2.0 for males and 2.2 for females. The excess mortality among Indians decreased with age. Malays had the highest mortality rates from hypertensive disease, with age-standardized relative risks of 3.4 for males and 4.4 for females compared to Chinese, 2.0 for males and 2.5 for females compared to Indians, and 1.6 for males and 1.6 for females compared to Chinese. There were minimal ethnic differences in cerebrovascular disease, except for lower rates in Chinese females. The age-standardized relative risks for Malays versus Chinese were 1.1 for males and 1.9 for females, for Malays versus Indians were 1.0 for males and 1.1 for females, and for Indians versus Chinese were 1.1 for males and 1.7 for females. In conclusion, significant disparities in mortality rates from the three main cardiovascular diseases were observed among different ethnic groups in Singapore.

title: Protein localization in electron micrographs using fluorescence nanoscopy
text: To obtain a comprehensive understanding of a cell, it is necessary to provide a detailed account of its molecular structure, specifically the connection between proteins and specific organelles. Immunocytochemical electron microscopy is a technique that can identify the precise locations of proteins with nanometer precision. However, it is limited by the quality of fixation, the scarcity of antibodies, and the difficulty in accessing antigens. In this study, we introduce a new approach called correlative fluorescence electron microscopy, which allows for the precise localization of proteins at the nanoscale in electron micrographs. To achieve this, we labeled proteins with fluorescent proteins such as Citrine or tdEos and expressed them in Caenorhabditis elegans. The worms were then fixed and embedded in plastic for imaging. We utilized stimulated emission depletion (STED) microscopy or photoactivated localization microscopy (PALM) to capture images of the labeled proteins from ultrathin sections. By correlating the fluorescence signals with the organelles observed in electron micrographs from the same sections, we successfully localized histones, a mitochondrial protein, and a presynaptic dense projection protein.

title: The flavonoid component isorhamnetin in vitro inhibits proliferation and induces apoptosis in Eca-109 cells.
text: Isorhamnetin, a flavonoid component, has been utilized in the treatment of heart disease. Our lab recently investigated the in vitro anti-cancer properties of isorhamnetin on the human esophageal squamous carcinoma cell line Eca-109. When Eca-109 cells were exposed to varying doses of isorhamnetin (0-80 microg/ml) for 48 hours, it was observed that isorhamnetin had a cytostatic effect on the treated cells, with an estimated IC(50) of 40+/-0.08 microg/ml as determined by MTT assay. The inhibition of proliferation by isorhamnetin was confirmed through trypan blue exclusion assay, clone formation test, immunocytochemical assay of PCNA, and (3)H-thymidine uptake analysis. The cell cycle distribution was measured using FCM, and it was found that isorhamnetin significantly hindered the viability of Eca-109 cells. The treated group exposed to isorhamnetin showed an increased population in the G(0)/G(1) phase from 74.6 to 84, while there was a significant reduction in the G(2)/M phase from 11.9 to 5.8 compared to the negative control group. In addition to its cytostatic effect, isorhamnetin also demonstrated a stimulatory effect on apoptosis. Through transmission electron microscope, typical apoptotic morphology such as condensation and fragmentation of nuclei and blebbing membrane of the apoptotic cells were observed. Furthermore, FCM detected a sharp increase in the apoptosis rate from 6.3 to 16.3 between the control and treated group. To investigate the potential molecular mechanisms underlying the growth inhibition and apoptosis stimulatory effects of isorhamnetin, the expressions of six proliferation- and death-related genes were analyzed using FCM. The expressions of bcl-2, c-myc, and H-ras were downregulated, while Bax, c-fos, and p53 were upregulated. However, further in vivo experiments are necessary to confirm the anti-cancer effects of isorhamnetin. In conclusion, isorhamnetin shows promise as a potent drug against esophageal cancer due to its ability to inhibit proliferation and induce apoptosis of Eca-109 cells in vitro.

title: Arachidonic Acid in the Diabetic Rat Kidney
text: This study aimed to investigate the impact of arachidonic acid on renal vasoconstriction in diabetic rats and determine the roles of cyclooxygenase-1/cyclooxygenase-2 and 20-HETE in this process. In the rat isolated perfused kidney, arachidonic acid triggers vasoconstriction through activation of PGH2/TxA2 receptors, and this response is heightened in diabetic rats. We confirmed that the vasoconstrictor effect of arachidonic acid is amplified in diabetic rat kidneys, accompanied by a twofold increase in the release of 6-ketoPGF1alpha, an indicator of cyclooxygenase activity. In diabetic rat kidneys, 1 and 3 micrograms of arachidonic acid raised perfusion pressure by 85+/-37 and 186+/-6 mm Hg, respectively, compared to 3+/-1 and 17+/-8 mm Hg in control rat kidneys. Inhibition of both cyclooxygenase isoforms with indomethacin abolished the vasoconstrictor response to arachidonic acid in both diabetic and control rat kidneys. However, inhibiting cyclooxygenase-2 with nimesulide only reduced perfusion pressure responses to 1 and 3 micrograms of arachidonic acid in diabetic rat kidneys, indicating a threefold increase in renal cortical expression of cyclooxygenase-2. Furthermore, 20-HETE release from diabetic rat kidneys decreased nearly sixfold and did not increase in response to arachidonic acid. These findings demonstrate that the renal vasoconstrictor effect of arachidonic acid relies solely on cyclooxygenase activity, with no contribution from 20-HETE. In diabetic rats, cyclooxygenase-2 activity contributes to the renal vasoconstrictor effect of arachidonic acid.

title: Two sequence motifs from HIF-1alpha bind to the DNA-binding site of p53.
text:
There is evidence suggesting that the interaction between hypoxia-inducible factor-1alpha (HIF-1alpha) and the tumor suppressor p53 exists. In order to understand this potential interaction better, we conducted a study where we examined the binding of the core domain of p53 (p53c) to a range of immobilized peptides derived from HIF-1alpha. Our findings revealed two specific peptide-sequence motifs that exhibited a strong affinity for p53c in solution, with a micromolar binding strength.

Interestingly, one of these sequences was located adjacent to, while the other coincided with, the two proline residues (P402 and P564) within the oxygen-dependent degradation domain. These proline residues are known to act as switches for the oxygen-dependent regulation of HIF-1alpha. Surprisingly, the binding affinity between p53c and these motifs was not influenced by the hydroxylation state of P564.

Further analysis using NMR spectroscopy demonstrated that these sequence motifs bind to the DNA-binding site of p53c. Given that these two sequences are homologous but separated by 120 residues, and one of them is found within a mostly unstructured transactivation domain, we hypothesize that each sequence motif in HIF-1alpha binds to a distinct subunit of the p53 tetramer, resulting in a highly stable binding interaction.

Based on our binding data, we propose that p53 may serve as a pathway for the degradation of HIF-1alpha in hypoxic tumor cells, particularly when HIF-1alpha is not hydroxylated at the two proline residues.

title: A functionally characterized test set of human induced pluripotent stem cells
text: The use of human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) presents exciting opportunities for studying development and modeling diseases in a laboratory setting. However, concerns have been raised about the variability in the behavior of iPSCs, which has raised doubts about their usefulness. To address this issue, we conducted a study where we obtained 16 iPSC lines from seven individuals with different ages, sexes, and health statuses. We extensively analyzed these lines to determine their pluripotency and their ability to differentiate into specialized cells. Using standardized procedures in two separate laboratories, we found that 13 of the iPSC lines were able to generate functional motor neurons with similar efficiency to human embryonic stem cells (ESCs). Although three iPSC lines initially showed resistance to neural differentiation, we were able to rescue their performance by inducing early neuralization. Therefore, all 16 iPSC lines successfully passed a rigorous test of their capacity to differentiate, despite variations in their genetic makeup and the expression of certain markers and transgenes associated with pluripotency. This collection of iPSC and ESC lines serves as a reliable resource for researchers interested in studying the fundamental biology of stem cells and their potential applications.

title: Differential regulation of MAP kinase activation by a novel splice variant of human MAP kinase phosphatase-2.
text: We have discovered a new variant of MAP kinase phosphatase-2 (MKP-2), called MKP-2-S, which lacks the binding site for MAP kinases but still retains the catalytic domain for phosphatase activity. We found that MKP-2-S transcripts and proteins are present in PC3 prostate and MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells, as well as in human prostate biopsies. When MKP-2-S was transfected into cells, it produced a nuclear protein weighing 33kDa that exhibited phosphatase activity similar to the longer form of MKP-2 (MKP-2-L) that was previously described. However, MKP-2-S did not bind to JNK or ERK due to the absence of a kinase interacting motif (KIM), whereas MKP-2-L bound to ERK and to a lesser extent JNK. The turnover rate of MKP-2-S expressed through adenoviral transfection was faster than that of MKP-2-L, making it more susceptible to degradation by the proteasome. MKP-2-S retained its ability to deactivate JNK and inhibit LPS-stimulated COX-2 induction, similar to MKP-2-L. However, unlike MKP-2-L, MKP-2-S was unable to reverse serum-induced ERK activation or significantly inhibit endothelial cell proliferation. These findings suggest the presence of a novel splice variant of MKP-2 that cannot bind to ERK and may play a role in the dysregulation of MAP kinase activity in certain disease states, particularly breast and prostate cancers.

title: Myeloperoxidase acts as a profibrotic mediator of atrial fibrillation
text:
The relationship between atrial fibrillation and inflammation has been well-established through observational clinical and ex vivo studies. However, it remains unclear whether inflammation is the cause or consequence of atrial fibrillation, as well as which specific inflammatory mediators contribute to the atria's susceptibility to fibrillation. In this study, we present experimental and clinical evidence supporting the involvement of myeloperoxidase (MPO), an enzyme expressed by neutrophils, in the pathophysiology of atrial fibrillation. 

Using MPO-deficient mice that were treated with angiotensin II (AngII) to activate leukocytes, we observed lower levels of the MPO product 3-chlorotyrosine in the atrial tissue, reduced activity of matrix metalloproteinases, and less atrial fibrosis compared to wild-type mice. Furthermore, when these MPO-deficient mice underwent right atrial electrophysiological stimulation, they were protected from atrial fibrillation, which could be reversed by restoring MPO. 

In humans with atrial fibrillation, we found higher plasma concentrations of MPO and a greater MPO burden in the right atrial tissue compared to individuals without atrial fibrillation. Additionally, MPO was found to colocalize with increased formation of 3-chlorotyrosine in the atria. 

Overall, our findings demonstrate that MPO plays a crucial role in the structural remodeling of the myocardium, leading to an increased vulnerability to atrial fibrillation.

title: Knowledge and use of secondary contraception among patients requesting termination of pregnancy.
text: A survey conducted at the St. James's University Fertility Control Clinic in England revealed that patients who visited general practitioners had less knowledge compared to those who attended specialist clinics. The survey, which took place between April 1, 1991, and January 31, 1992, highlighted the need for counseling on pill and condom use, as well as protection against sexually transmitted diseases. It also found a lack of knowledge regarding postcoital methods. The respondents included minorities such as Afro-Caribbean (8%) and Asian (9%). Out of the cases, 307 were using a less effective form of contraception at the time of conception, often switching from the pill to condoms. Among the 171 people who reported contraception failure, 93 experienced a split or leaking condom, 13 had a condom fall off during intercourse, 32 had inconsistent condom use, 32 forgot to take contraceptive pills or used antibiotics with the pill, and 1 had a late injection of medroxyprogesterone acetate. Of the 309 people who conceived while using condoms, 45 recognized a potential condom failure, but only 20 attempted emergency contraceptive methods like the postcoital pill. Only 30% of the 171 patients who recognized condom failure and 12% of the 210 who did not use any contraception had adequate knowledge of postcoital pills. Similarly, only 2% of the 171 patients and 2% of the 381 patients had knowledge of postcoital insertion of an intrauterine contraceptive device. When given the choice between an unplanned pregnancy and postcoital contraception, the majority (718 out of 769) preferred using postcoital contraception. Contraceptive information was provided to 501 patients by a general practitioner, 102 by a community family planning clinic, and 163 had no medical advice. There was a range of knowledge regarding postcoital contraceptive methods. Among the 422 patients who had ever used the combined pill, knowledge of how to deal with forgotten pills, severe vomiting, severe diarrhea, and concurrent antibiotic treatment varied. 19% of the 372 patients treated by general practitioners knew 4 correct answers, while 50% of the 50 patients in community family planning clinics answered correctly 4 times. These differences could not be explained by other demographic characteristics.

title: Domestication and Divergence of Saccharomyces cerevisiae Beer Yeasts
text: The domestication of livestock, pets, and crops is well-documented, but the extent to which microbes involved in food production have undergone human selection and the origins of industrial strains remain unclear. In this study, we examine the genomes and characteristics of 157 industrial Saccharomyces cerevisiae yeasts. Our findings reveal that modern industrial yeasts can be categorized into five distinct sublineages that are genetically and phenotypically different from wild strains. These industrial yeasts have evolved from a small number of ancestors through complex processes of domestication and local divergence. Through extensive analysis of their genomes and phenotypes, we also observe strong selection for stress tolerance, sugar utilization, and flavor production in industrial yeasts. However, traits related to survival in natural environments, such as the sexual cycle, show signs of decay, particularly in beer yeasts. These findings provide valuable insights into the origins, evolutionary history, and diversity of industrial yeasts, and offer a valuable resource for the selection of superior strains.

title: The ascendancy of Amblyomma americanum as a vector of pathogens affecting humans in the United States.
text: Until the 1990s, Amblyomma americanum was mainly considered a bothersome species, with little significance as a carrier of diseases that affect humans. However, recent findings of Ehrlichia chaffeensis, Ehrlichia ewingii, and "Borrelia lonestari" have removed any doubt about the public health importance of lone star ticks. It is expected that over the next 25 years, there will be a rise in the number of human diseases caused by A. americanum-associated pathogens. This increase will primarily be driven by biological and environmental factors that alter the spread and intensity of zoonotic pathogens. Additionally, changes in society and demographics that increase the chances of susceptible individuals coming into contact with infected lone star ticks, along with advancements in diagnostic capabilities and national surveillance efforts, will also contribute to the expected rise in reported cases of disease.

title: Biallelic mutations in PALB2 cause Fanconi anemia subtype FA-N and predispose to childhood cancer
text: Recently, PALB2 was discovered to be a nuclear binding companion of BRCA2. When both copies of BRCA2 are mutated, it leads to a specific type of Fanconi anemia called FA-D1 and increases the likelihood of childhood malignancies. In our research, we found harmful mutations in PALB2 (also referred to as FANCN) in seven families who were affected by both Fanconi anemia and early childhood cancer. This discovery demonstrates that when both copies of PALB2 are mutated, it causes a new subtype of Fanconi anemia known as FA-N. Similar to biallelic BRCA2 mutations, biallelic PALB2 mutations also significantly raise the risk of childhood cancer.

title: Long tandem arrays of complex repeat units in Chironomus telomeres.
text:
The telomeres of the Chironomus pallividittatus genome have been identified using in situ hybridization with a cloned 340-bp DNA fragment excised by EcoRI. This fragment has been found to be present at the telomeres as well as the connectives between them. No hybridization was observed in other regions of the chromosomes. Another cloned EcoRI fragment, 525 bp in length, has also been examined. This fragment is a partial duplication of the 340-bp sequence.

Genomic blot hybridization experiments have revealed that the 340-bp sequence is a monomeric unit of tandemly repeated arrays, which make up 1.2% of the Chironomus genome. On average, each telomere contains 300 kb of these repeated arrays. The repeat unit consists of two types of subrepeats, each occurring twice per repeat unit.

Northern blot hybridization experiments have shown that the telomere-associated sequences are transcribed into a discrete RNA species approximately 20 kb in size. The evolution of this telomere-associated DNA is also discussed.

title: Localization of Na+ channel isoforms at the atrioventricular junction and atrioventricular node in the rat.
text: The functional heterogeneity of the atrioventricular node (AVN) and its relationship to distinct cell types and the 3-dimensional structure of the AVN is currently unknown. In order to investigate this, we examined the expression of Na(V)1.5 and other Na+ channel isoforms in the AVN. The AVN in rats was identified using Masson's trichrome staining and marker proteins such as connexin40, connexin43, desmoplakin, atrial natriuretic peptide, and hyperpolarization-activated and cyclic nucleotide-gated channel 4. Immunohistochemistry with isoform-specific Na+ channel antibodies was used to study Na+ channel expression. We found that Na(V)1.1 was distributed similarly to Na(V)1.5, while Na(V)1.2 was not detected. Na(V)1.3 labeling was present in nerve fibers and cell bodies, but not myocytes, and was abundant in the penetrating atrioventricular (AV) bundle and the common bundle, but less abundant in other regions. Na(V)1.5 labeling was abundant in the atrial and ventricular myocardium and the left bundle branch. However, it was absent in the open node, penetrating AV bundle, AV ring bundle, and common bundle, but present at a reduced level in the inferior nodal extension and transitional zone. Na(V)1.6 was not detected. In conclusion, our findings provide molecular evidence of multiple electrophysiological cell types at the AV junction. Impaired AV conduction resulting from mutations in or loss of Na(V)1.5 is likely due to impaired conduction in the AVN inputs (inferior nodal extension and transitional zone) or output (bundle branches), rather than the AVN itself (open node and penetrating AV bundle).

title: Follicular B cell trafficking within the spleen actively restricts humoral immune responses.
text: The separation of follicular (FO) and marginal zone (MZ) B cells within the spleen has long been a mystery. However, we have now discovered that this segregation is dependent on the transcription factor Klf2, which regulates migratory receptors specific to each B cell lineage. Through our study using gene-targeted mice, we have found that altered migration of splenic B cells leads to a gain-of-function phenotype in FO B cells. This includes their ability to rapidly respond to antigens and pathogens associated with the MZ, in a T cell-dependent manner. Our findings reveal that in normal animals, naive FO B cells are actively kept away from the MZ, limiting their ability to combat blood-borne pathogens.

title: Interleukin-2 and inflammation induce distinct transcriptional programs that promote the differentiation of effector cytolytic T cells.
text: During infection, the generation of cytolytic T-lymphocytes (CTLs) is regulated by Interleukin(IL)-2 and inflammation. Our study reveals a complex interaction between IL-2 and inflammatory signals in the differentiation of CTLs. Stimulation with IL-2 leads to the activation of the transcription factor eomesodermin (Eomes), an increase in the transcription of perforin (Prf1), and a suppression of the re-expression of memory CTL markers Bcl6 and IL-7Ralpha. The binding of Eomes and STAT5 to the cis-regulatory regions of Prf1 is associated with the initiation of transcription, as evidenced by an increased recruitment of RNA polymerase II to the Prf1 promoter. Inflammation, induced by CpG and IL-12, enhances the expression of IL-2Ralpha and the transcription factor T-bet. However, it counteracts the late induction of Eomes and perforin, while preventing the repression of IL-7Ralpha by IL-2. In mice infected with lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus, effector CD8(+) T cells lacking IL-2Ralpha expression exhibit increased levels of Bcl6 but decreased levels of perforin and granzyme B. These cells also form fewer KLRG-1(+) and T-bet-expressing CTLs and exhibit impaired killing ability. Therefore, inflammation influences the differentiation of both effector and memory CTLs, while persistent IL-2 stimulation promotes the development of effector CTLs at the expense of memory CTLs.

title: Neighbourhood risk factors for tuberculosis in Hong Kong.
text:
The association between tuberculosis (TB) and poverty, particularly in developing countries, has been widely reported. However, in Hong Kong, an industrialized area with a high incidence of TB, previous studies have produced conflicting results regarding the impact of poverty at the neighborhood level. This study aims to investigate the spatial distribution of TB and its relationship with neighborhood risk factors. 

A total of 17,294 TB cases reported between 2005 and 2007 were analyzed at the District Council Constituency Area (DCCA) level. These cases were indirectly standardized by age and sex using population data from the 2006 census. The standardized TB ratio was then examined in relation to various neighborhood risk factors, including family, ethnicity, economic, and environmental factors. 

The results revealed a diverse spatial pattern in the standardized TB ratio, which was found to be significantly associated with all neighborhood factors in the initial analysis. However, after conducting multivariate analysis, only marital status, place of birth, and low household income remained independently associated with the standardized TB ratio. 

In conclusion, despite the implementation of a comprehensive social assistance scheme that has effectively eradicated absolute poverty, low household income in the neighborhood continues to be significantly linked to TB. This association remains significant even after accounting for other risk factors such as place of birth and marital status.

title: Genomic stability and tumour suppression by the APC/C cofactor Cdh1
text: The APC/C, also known as the anaphase promoting complex or cyclosome, is a protein ligase that works in conjunction with Cdc20 or Cdh1 to target cell-cycle proteins for degradation. Specifically, APC/C-Cdh1 aids in protein degradation during late mitosis and G1. When Cdh1 is absent in mutant embryos, they perish at E9.5-E10.5 due to issues with trophoblast cell endoreduplication and placental dysfunction. However, this lethality can be prevented by expressing Cdh1 in the placenta. Cells lacking Cdh1 experience inefficient proliferation and accumulate numerical and structural chromosomal abnormalities, indicating that Cdh1 plays a role in maintaining genomic stability. Animals with only one copy of the Cdh1 gene exhibit an increased susceptibility to spontaneous tumors, suggesting that Cdh1 acts as a haploinsufficient tumor suppressor. Additionally, these mice display various behavioral defects associated with heightened proliferation of stem cells in the nervous system. These findings demonstrate that Cdh1 is necessary for preventing uncontrolled proliferation of specific progenitor cells and safeguarding mammalian cells against genomic instability.

title: Developing primary palliative care.
text: Despite the fact that 65% of individuals with cancer express a preference to die at home, only around 30% are able to do so. It is crucial for a government committed to patient choice to improve this statistic. Developing palliative care services in primary care is essential in meeting the expectations of those nearing the end of their lives. These services can also provide important opportunities for extending compassionate care to individuals with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, motor neurone disease, and cardiac failure, among others, who also require palliative care. With adequate training, resources, and specialist advice when necessary, primary care professionals have the potential to provide end of life care for the majority of patients. They share common values with palliative care specialists, focusing on holistic, patient-centered care within the context of families and friends. However, until recently, there have been few comprehensive workforce initiatives in primary care that prioritize end of life care, aside from Macmillan general practitioners and nurse facilitators. Many cancer patients and their caregivers experience existential distress long before their death, but this suffering often goes unnoticed or is disregarded by services that primarily focus on the terminal phase of illnesses. Primary care teams have the advantage of knowing patients over extended periods of time and can easily identify those who may benefit from early palliative care by asking themselves a simple question: "Would I be surprised if my patient were to die in the next 12 months?" By proactively identifying such patients, we can simultaneously provide active treatment and patient-centered supportive care through a team with whom many patients have a valued long-term relationship. Palliative care services should be extended to patients with non-malignant conditions who have similar concerns and, in some cases, even greater unmet needs than cancer patients. Progress in palliative medicine is hindered by issues such as uncertainty about the most effective care models, lack of expertise in non-cancer conditions, and concerns about strain on specialist services. General practitioners and community nurses can take the lead in providing a palliative care approach for patients with terminal organ failure illnesses. The first step in this approach is to discuss and agree upon the goals of care, adjusting management plans accordingly. The focus is on effectively controlling symptoms and maintaining quality of life. Unfortunately, the new general medical services contract does not prioritize palliative care, as other developments to achieve quality indicators take precedence during the day. Additionally, the new unscheduled care services, responsible for providing care for 75% of the week, are even less equipped than previous out-of-hours provision to facilitate dying at home. These services specialize in acute emergencies and often struggle to meet the medical, nursing, and social care needs of dying individuals and their families. These changes will greatly impact care for those nearing the end of their lives and may increase the number of hospital admissions. However, there is an important initiative gaining momentum in primary care. The Gold Standards Framework, supported by funding from the Cancer Services Collaborative, Macmillan Cancer Relief, and the National Lottery, provides a detailed guide for organizing proactive palliative care in the community, facilitating effective care. Other recent mechanisms for developing primary palliative care include training general practitioners with a special interest in palliative care and the new end-of-life initiative in England, which aims to improve palliative care provision by generalists and share examples of good practice. To support these developments, it is crucial to have a strong academic foundation for primary palliative care. While conducting research in this field is challenging, progress has been made in recent years in developing conceptual models and research architectures for studying end-of-life issues. Now, we must build upon this work to ensure that the knowledge and insights gained can be translated into effective interventions. Every individual with a progressive illness has the right to receive palliative care. Patients desire the presence of a reassuring professional as they face death. General practitioners and community nurses are trusted by patients and are in a position to provide effective, fair, and accessible palliative care. However, this can only happen if they have sufficient time and resources and work within a system that encourages such care. Patients who receive holistic support in the community are less likely to require costly hospital admissions and often futile treatments at the end of their lives.

title: The effects of self-administering emergency contraception.
text:
BACKGROUND: Emergency postcoital contraception is effective in preventing pregnancy, but currently requires a doctor's prescription and must be taken within 72 hours of intercourse. There is a proposal to make emergency contraception available without a prescription. To investigate the potential impact of this change, we conducted a study to examine how women would behave if provided with a supply of emergency contraceptive pills to keep at home.

METHODS: We divided 553 women into two groups: the treatment group, which received a replaceable supply of hormonal emergency contraceptive pills to take home, and the control group, which obtained emergency contraception by visiting a doctor. After one year, we assessed the frequency of emergency contraception use, the use of other contraceptives, and the incidence of unwanted pregnancies in both groups.

RESULTS: We analyzed data from 549 women in the treatment group and 522 women in the control group. Of these, 379 women in the treatment group (69 percent) and 326 women in the control group (62 percent) provided detailed information at follow-up. Among those who returned the study questionnaire, 47 percent of women in the treatment group used emergency contraception at least once, with 98 percent using it correctly and no serious adverse effects reported. In comparison, 27 percent of women in the control group used emergency contraception at least once (P<0.001). The treatment group did not show a higher likelihood of repeated emergency contraception use, and their use of other contraceptive methods was similar to that of the control group. There were 18 unintended pregnancies in the treatment group and 25 in the control group (relative risk, 0.7; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.4 to 1.2).

CONCLUSIONS: Making emergency contraception more easily accessible does not have any negative effects and may potentially reduce the rate of unwanted pregnancies.

title: A coactivator of pre-mRNA splicing.
text: The monoclonal antibody (mAb) B1C8 recognizes a unique nuclear matrix antigen known as SRm160 (SR-related matrix protein of 160 kD). This antigen is rich in serine (S) and arginine (R) and is associated with splicing complexes. Unlike other splicing factors in the SR family, SRm160 does not possess an RNA recognition motif. SRm160, along with a related protein called SRm300 (the 300-kD nuclear matrix antigen recognized by mAb B4A11), forms a complex that plays a crucial role in the splicing of specific pre-mRNAs. This SRm160/300 complex interacts with splicing complexes and facilitates splicing by interacting with SR family proteins. The binding of SRm160/300 to pre-mRNA is typically dependent on U1 snRNP and is further stabilized by U2 snRNP. Consequently, SRm160/300 establishes multiple interactions with components directly bound to important sites within pre-mRNA. These findings indicate that the nuclear matrix proteins SRm160 and SRm300 function as coactivators of pre-mRNA splicing.

title: Comparison of pioglitazone vs glimepiride on progression of coronary atherosclerosis in patients with type 2 diabetes: the PERISCOPE randomized controlled trial.
text:
The objective of this study was to compare the effects of two different oral glucose-lowering agents, pioglitazone and glimepiride, on the progression of coronary atherosclerosis in patients with type 2 diabetes. The study was conducted as a double-blind, randomized, multicenter trial at 97 academic and community hospitals in North and South America. A total of 543 patients with coronary disease and type 2 diabetes were enrolled in the study.

The patients were randomly assigned to receive either glimepiride (1 to 4 mg) or pioglitazone (15 to 45 mg) for a period of 18 months. The dosage was titrated to the maximum tolerated level. The progression of atherosclerosis was measured using coronary intravascular ultrasonography. A total of 360 patients underwent repeat intravascular ultrasonography examination at the end of the study.

The main outcome measure was the change in percent atheroma volume (PAV) from baseline to study completion. The results showed that the mean PAV increased by 0.73% with glimepiride and decreased by 0.16% with pioglitazone. An alternative analysis, which imputed values for noncompleters based on baseline characteristics, showed similar results.

The baseline HbA(1c) levels were similar in both groups and decreased during treatment with both medications. However, the decrease was greater with pioglitazone compared to glimepiride. Additionally, the pioglitazone group showed improvements in high-density lipoprotein levels and triglyceride levels, while the glimepiride group did not.

Adverse events were also assessed in the study. Hypoglycemia was more common in the glimepiride group, while edema, fractures, and decreased hemoglobin levels occurred more frequently in the pioglitazone group.

In conclusion, the study found that treatment with pioglitazone resulted in a significantly lower rate of progression of coronary atherosclerosis compared to glimepiride in patients with type 2 diabetes and coronary artery disease. The trial was registered under the clinicaltrials.gov Identifier NCT00225277.

title: Staphylococcus aureus RNAIII coordinately represses the synthesis of virulence factors and the transcription regulator Rot by an antisense mechanism.
text: RNAIII, a large regulatory RNA consisting of 514 nucleotides, serves as the intracellular effector of the quorum-sensing system in Staphylococcus aureus. It plays a crucial role in controlling the expression of numerous virulence genes. Our study reveals that the 3' domain of RNAIII acts as an antisense RNA, effectively repressing the expression of mRNAs encoding a specific class of virulence factors involved in early infection processes. Through rapid annealing, the 3' domain forms long RNA duplexes with these mRNAs, leading to repression of translation initiation and subsequent endoribonuclease III hydrolysis. This cascade of events ultimately results in the depletion of the mRNA pool. Furthermore, we demonstrate that RNAIII and its 3' domain mediate translational repression of rot mRNA through a limited number of base pairings, specifically involving two loop-loop interactions. As Rot is a transcriptional regulatory protein, we propose that RNAIII indirectly influences the activation of downstream genes, thereby promoting the synthesis of various exoproteins. These findings highlight the extensive regulatory impact of RNAIII and its 3' domain in establishing a network of virulence factors in S. aureus.

title: Human Cytomegalovirus Latency-Associated Proteins Elicit Immune-Suppressive IL-10 Producing CD4+ T Cells
text: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) is a common herpesvirus that remains in the body for life after initial infection. In healthy individuals, the immune system effectively controls the virus through HCMV-specific T cells. However, the virus is able to establish a state of latency, where viral genes are expressed at low levels, particularly in myeloid cells. In this study, we found that specific T cells targeting two viral genes, UL138 and LUNA, were present in healthy individuals with previous HCMV infection. These T cells were primarily CD4⁺ T cells and were capable of killing infected cells and producing the immune molecule IFNγ during both active and latent infection. Interestingly, unlike CD4⁺ T cells that target genes expressed only during active infection, the UL138 and LUNA-specific T cell responses included cells that secreted the immunosuppressive cytokine cIL-10. We also discovered that cIL-10-producing CD4⁺ T cells targeted other genes expressed during latency, such as US28 and UL111A. Overall, our findings demonstrate that HCMV induces CD4⁺ T cell responses against latency-associated genes, which can exert effector functions against both active and latent infected cells. Importantly, these CD4⁺ T cell populations also include cells that produce the immunosuppressive cytokine cIL-10. This suggests that HCMV manipulates the immune response to latency-associated antigens in a way that promotes immune suppression and allows the virus to persist in the body.

title: Pamidronate induced anti-proliferative, apoptotic, and anti-migratory effects in hepatocellular carcinoma.
text:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: The involvement of small GTPases from the Ras and Rho families in human tumorigenesis and metastasis is well-established. Recent studies have shown that pamidronate, a drug that inhibits the mevalonate pathway necessary for the prenylation of small GTPases, may have potential in the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). 

METHODS: We conducted experiments using five hepatoma cell lines to analyze the effect of pamidronate on cell proliferation. Cell apoptosis was evaluated using DAPI staining and a histone ELISA assay. A cell migration assay was performed using the Modified Boyden Chamber. In vivo, we monitored tumor volumes in nude mice after subcutaneous inoculation of PLC/PRF/5 cells and intraperitoneal injection of pamidronate. 

RESULTS: Pamidronate effectively inhibited cell growth in all hepatoma cell lines. Treatment with pamidronate resulted in reduced levels of membrane-associated Ras and phosphorylated extracellular signal-regulated kinase 2 (ERK 2). Pamidronate also increased apoptosis and cleavage of Caspase-3 and -9. Additionally, pamidronate suppressed membrane-associated RhoA and cell motility. In vivo, pamidronate significantly suppressed tumor volumes at three weeks. 

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that pamidronate has therapeutic potential in inducing anti-proliferative, apoptotic, and anti-migratory effects in HCC.

title: Defective regulation of adipose tissue autophagy in obesity
text:
The aim of this study was to investigate the role of autophagy in obesity and its association with insulin resistance. The study examined both mice and humans to evaluate the effects of weight loss on autophagy in adipose tissue.

In the mouse model, obese mice showed increased markers of autophagy compared to lean mice. However, when the obese mice were subjected to caloric restriction, autophagy decreased while it increased in the lean mice. The reintroduction of normal feeding patterns resulted in a rapid reduction of autophagy in the lean mice and an increase in the obese mice.

In the human study, autophagy was evaluated in the subcutaneous adipose tissue of obese individuals undergoing bariatric surgery for weight loss. Similar to the mouse model, obesity was associated with increased autophagy. However, after weight loss, autophagy in the adipose tissue was attenuated.

The study also examined markers of systemic inflammation and found that obesity was associated with increased levels of inflammation. However, the improvement in metabolic control following weight loss did not have a significant impact on inflammation.

In conclusion, this study suggests that obesity and overeating disrupt the regulation of autophagy in adipose tissue. Weight loss can lead to a reduction in autophagy, which may have implications for improving insulin resistance. Additionally, the study indicates that autophagy and inflammation are regulated independently.

title: Recovery of visual response of injured adult rat optic nerves treated with transglutaminase.
text: The failure of axons in the central nervous system of adult mammals to regenerate on their own after injury is partly due to inhibitory molecules associated with oligodendrocytes. However, in fish, the regeneration of central nervous system axons is linked to the presence of a transglutaminase enzyme. This particular enzyme combines interleukin-2, resulting in a cytotoxic product that affects oligodendrocytes in laboratory settings. When this transglutaminase, derived from nerves, was applied to rat optic nerves that had lost their ability to respond to light due to injury, it promoted the recovery of that response within six weeks. Analysis using transmission electron microscopy also showed the simultaneous appearance of axons in the distal stump of the optic nerve.

title: Cell survival during complete nutrient deprivation depends on lipid droplet-fueled β-oxidation of fatty acids.
text:
The synthesis of triacylglycerols and the formation of lipid droplets (LD) occur in cells exposed to various types of stress. However, the significance of this response in terms of cell function is uncertain. To investigate this further, we used a simple model of stress by completely depriving cells in culture of nutrients. Our aim was to determine whether LD biogenesis plays a protective role in cells that are destined to die.

We observed that complete nutrient deprivation induced LD biogenesis in human LN18 glioblastoma and HeLa cells, as well as in CHO and rat primary astrocytes. In all cell types, the depletion of LD was associated with cell death, and this process was accelerated when LD biogenesis was blocked through the pharmacological inhibition of Group IVA phospholipase A2 (cPLA2α) or the down-regulation of ceramide kinase.

Furthermore, nutrient deprivation also triggered the β-oxidation of fatty acids, which was sensitive to cPLA2α inhibition. Interestingly, cell survival under these conditions became strictly dependent on the catabolism of fatty acids. These findings demonstrate that, during nutrient deprivation, cell viability is sustained by the β-oxidation of fatty acids, which requires the biogenesis and mobilization of LD.

title: Molecular and cytogenetic changes involved in the immortalization of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells by telomerase.
text:
Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a prevalent disease in Hong Kong and southern provinces of China. The development of NPC is believed to be strongly influenced by EBV infection. However, previous studies on the transformation mechanism of EBV genes were mainly conducted on either NPC or nonnasopharyngeal epithelial cells, which may not accurately represent premalignant nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Therefore, it is crucial to establish a representative cell system that can aid in understanding the role of EBV infection in NPC development. 

By using telomerase alone, we successfully created an immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cell line from primary nonmalignant nasopharyngeal biopsies. These telomerase-immortalized cells, known as NP460hTert, mostly exhibit a diploid karyotype. Interestingly, NP460hTert cells harbor genetic alterations commonly found in premalignant and malignant nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. These alterations include the inactivation of p16 through homozygous deletion of the p16(INK4A) locus and the downregulation of RASSF1A expression. The deletion of the p16(INK4A) locus appears to be the most crucial event in the immortalization of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells by telomerase, preceding the downregulation of RASSF1A. 

Furthermore, through detailed analysis using conventional cytogenetics, spectral karyotyping (SKY), and array-based comparative genomic hybridization (CGH), we discovered a gain of a 17q21-q25 fragment on the 11p15 chromosome in all NP460hTert cells. This gain of 17q has been previously observed in NPC. Additionally, we observed the activation of NF-kappaB in immortalized NP460hTert cells at later population doublings, suggesting its potential role in the survival of immortalized NP epithelial cells. The upregulation of Id1, a gene commonly expressed in various human cancers including NPC, was also observed in the immortalized NP460hTert cells. 

In conclusion, the establishment of an immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cell line that harbors common genetic alterations found in premalignant and cancerous nasopharyngeal epithelial cells provides a valuable cell system for studying early events in NPC carcinogenesis. This cell line can particularly aid in elucidating the role of EBV infection in the development of NPC.

title: Cellular nucleic acid binding protein suppresses tumor cell metastasis and induces tumor cell death by downregulating heterogeneous ribonucleoprotein K in fibrosarcoma cells.
text:
The Cellular nucleic acid binding protein (CNBP) has been linked to craniofacial development in vertebrates, as well as the human diseases myotonic dystrophy type 2 (DM2) and sporadic inclusion body myositis (sIBM). It plays a role in cell proliferation and survival, specifically in mediating neural crest expansion. CNBP acts as a nucleic acid chaperone by binding to single-stranded nucleic acid and promoting rearrangements of nucleic acid secondary structure in an ATP-independent manner. 

To investigate the function of CNBP, a variety of methods were employed. These included cell viability assays, wound-scratch assays, chemotaxis assays, invasion assays, circular dichroic (CD) spectroscopy, NMR spectroscopy, chromatin immunoprecipitation, expression and purification of recombinant human CNBP, electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA), surface plasmon resonance (SPR), fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) analyses, luciferase reporter assay, Western blotting, and isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC). 

The results showed that up-regulation of CNBP led to cell death in human fibrosarcoma cells and inhibited their motility and invasiveness. It was discovered that CNBP down-regulated the expression of heterogeneous ribonucleoprotein K (hnRNP K) by converting a G-rich sequence into a G-quadruplex in the promoter of hnRNP K. The G-quadruplex stabilizing ligand tetra-(N-methyl-4-pyridyl) porphyrin (TMPyP4) interacted with and stabilized the G-quadruplex, resulting in the downregulation of hnRNP K transcription. 

In conclusion, overexpression of CNBP induced cell death and suppressed cell metastasis by promoting the formation of G-quadruplex in the promoter of hnRNP K, leading to down-regulation of hnRNP K. This finding has significant implications as it provides a new approach for controlling hnRNP K expression, which could potentially contribute to the design and development of anticancer drugs.

title: The DHR96 nuclear receptor regulates xenobiotic responses in Drosophila.
text: The exposure to substances such as plant toxins, pollutants, or prescription drugs activates a defense mechanism in the body, which leads to the activation of specific genes responsible for detoxification. While the response to these substances has been extensively studied in vertebrates, little attention has been given to utilizing a simple genetic system to understand the underlying molecular mechanisms of this coordinated response. In this study, we demonstrate that around 1000 transcripts in Drosophila are significantly affected by treatment with phenobarbital, a commonly used drug. Furthermore, we show that DHR96, the Drosophila counterpart of the human SXR and CAR xenobiotic receptors, plays a crucial role in this response. A DHR96 mutant lacking the gene exhibits heightened sensitivity to the sedative effects of phenobarbital and the pesticide DDT, as well as abnormalities in the expression of numerous genes regulated by phenobarbital. Additionally, DHR96 is involved in the regulation of metabolic and stress-response genes, suggesting its involvement in coordinating multiple pathways of response. This research establishes a novel model system for studying the genetic regulation of xenobiotic stress responses.

title: A primate virus generates transformed human cells by fusion
text: A proposed model explaining the origin and sporadic nature of cancer suggests that cancer cells are a random outcome of events that lead to genomic and epigenetic variability. The prevailing belief is that these events are mutations that impact the segregation or stability of chromosomes. However, it is also possible for genomic and epigenetic variability to be triggered by cell fusion, often caused by viruses. Despite the perception that cells fused by viruses are harmless because they eventually perish, we present evidence that a primate virus utilizes both viral and exosomal proteins involved in cell fusion to generate transformed and rapidly multiplying human cells. While normal cells typically fail to proliferate after fusion, the expression of an oncogene or a mutated tumor suppressor p53 in just one of the fusion partners is enough to produce diverse offspring. Additionally, we demonstrate that this virus can create viable oncogenically transformed cells by fusing cells that would otherwise die. Consequently, we argue that viruses can contribute to the development of cancer by fusing cells.

title: TAA1-Mediated Auxin Biosynthesis Is Essential for Hormone Crosstalk and Plant Development
text: Plants possess an impressive ability to adapt their growth and development in response to changes in their environment. This remarkable flexibility is achieved through the intricate interplay between hormonal and developmental signals. A prime example of this is the plant's response to the hormone ethylene, which is influenced by factors such as tissue type, developmental stage, and environmental conditions. Through our investigation of the Arabidopsis wei8 mutant, we have discovered that a specific group of genes plays a crucial role in mediating ethylene's effects on different tissues. Further biochemical analysis has revealed that the WEI8 gene encodes an enzyme called tryptophan aminotransferase, also known as TAA1, which is part of the indole-3-pyruvic acid (IPA) branch of the auxin biosynthetic pathway. This branch, although previously uncharacterized genetically, is essential for auxin production. By studying TAA1 and its related genes, we have uncovered a connection between local auxin production, tissue-specific ethylene responses, and organ development. Therefore, the IPA pathway of auxin production plays a crucial role in generating robust auxin gradients in response to both environmental cues and developmental signals.

title: A research agenda for public health workforce development.
text: Over the past few decades, the focus of public health research has primarily been on specific categories rather than broader issues that cut across different areas or systems. There has been a lack of research on the infrastructure needed to support public health programs. This article presents the findings of an interactive process that aimed to develop a research agenda for the development of the public health workforce. The goal was to provide valuable insights to all stakeholders involved in the public health system. This research is defined as a comprehensive field of study that encompasses various disciplines and explores both fundamental and practical aspects. It examines the workforce in terms of costs, quality, accessibility, delivery, organization, financing, and outcomes of public health services. The objective is to enhance knowledge and understanding of the connections between the workforce and the structure, processes, and effects of public health services. Through expert panel meetings held between 2000 and 2003, a logic model and five priority research areas were established. Moving forward, it will be necessary to establish innovative partnerships between public and private entities to advance research that addresses cross-cutting and systems-focused issues.

title: Parallel processing in the mammalian retina
text: The brain receives various types of visual information from our eyes, including outlines, colors, and moving objects. This process is known as parallel processing and begins at the first synapse of the retina, specifically the cone pedicle. At this stage, the molecular makeup of the transmitter receptors in the postsynaptic neurons determines which visual images are transmitted to the inner retina. In the inner plexiform layer, which is the second synaptic layer, intricate circuits with both inhibitory and excitatory interactions act as filters to determine what information is conveyed from the eye to the brain.

title: Oxymetholone Therapy of Fanconi Anemia Suppresses Osteopontin Transcription and Induces Hematopoietic Stem Cell Cycling
text: The use of androgens in treating Fanconi anemia (FA) and other bone marrow failure syndromes is widespread, but we still don't fully understand how they work. To gain insight into the therapeutic effectiveness and mechanism of action of oxymetholone (OXM), we conducted experiments using aged Fancd2(-/-) mice. These mice, at eighteen months old, exhibited key characteristics of FA seen in humans, such as reduced bone marrow cell count, enlarged red blood cells, and overall low blood cell count. Similar to humans, continuous treatment with OXM significantly improved these hematological parameters and stimulated the growth of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells. RNA-Seq analysis revealed that the drug's action may involve the downregulation of osteopontin. The increased proliferation of stem cells was consistent with the chronic OXM therapy, but eventually led to stem cell exhaustion, as demonstrated by competitive repopulation assays. These findings enhance our understanding of how hematopoietic stem cell proliferation is regulated and have direct implications for the clinical treatment of bone marrow failure.

title: A point mutation in KINDLIN3 ablates activation of three integrin subfamilies in humans
text: Monogenic deficiency diseases offer unique opportunities to understand the specific contributions of individual molecules to human physiology and to identify pathologies that arise from their dysfunction. In this study, we present a deficiency disease observed in two siblings, characterized by severe bleeding, frequent infections, and osteopetrosis at an early age. These symptoms are similar to, but more severe than, those seen in individuals with leukocyte adhesion deficiency III (LAD-III). The underlying cause of these symptoms is an inability to activate integrins expressed on hematopoietic cells, such as platelets and leukocytes. Immortalized lymphocyte cell lines obtained from the affected individuals exhibited defects in integrin activation. Interestingly, proteins previously associated with integrin activation, including Ras-associated protein-1 (RAP1) and calcium and diacylglycerol-regulated guanine nucleotide exchange factor-1 (CALDAG-GEF1), were found to be present and functional in these cell lines. Through genetic analysis, we identified a point mutation in the coding region of the KINDLIN3 gene (official gene symbol FERMT3) as the genetic basis for this disease. When the wild-type KINDLIN-3 protein was introduced into the immortalized lymphocytes, their integrins became responsive to activation signals. These findings highlight the critical role of KINDLIN-3 in integrin activation in humans and demonstrate that this genetic disease significantly impacts the health of affected individuals. Additionally, we discovered that allogeneic bone marrow transplantation can alleviate the symptoms of this disease.

title: Fasting Activation of AgRP Neurons Requires NMDA Receptors and Involves Spinogenesis and Increased Excitatory Tone
text: The activity of AgRP neurons is responsible for driving feeding and weight gain, while nearby POMC neurons have the opposite effect. However, we do not know how excitatory glutamatergic input controls these neurons. To investigate this, we created mice that lack NMDA receptors (NMDARs) on either AgRP or POMC neurons. Removing NMDARs from AgRP neurons significantly reduced weight, body fat, and food intake, but deleting them from POMC neurons had no impact. The activation of AgRP neurons during fasting, as indicated by c-Fos, Agrp, and Npy mRNA expression, AMPA receptor-mediated EPSCs, depolarization, and firing rates, required NMDARs. Additionally, only AgRP neurons had dendritic spines, and the increased glutamatergic input onto AgRP neurons caused by fasting was accompanied by an increase in spines, suggesting that fasting induces synaptogenesis and spinogenesis. Therefore, glutamatergic synaptic transmission and its regulation by NMDARs play crucial roles in controlling AgRP neurons and determining the cellular and behavioral response to fasting.

title: Prevalence and Causes of Blindness and Low Vision in Southern Sudan
text: The prevalence and distribution of background blindness and low vision in southern Sudan remain largely unknown. Therefore, our objective was to determine the extent of blindness and low vision, identify the primary causes, and establish targets for programs aimed at preventing blindness in the Mankien payam (district) of southern Sudan.

title: Origin of nitrite and nitrate in nasal and exhaled breath condensate and relation to nitric oxide formation.
text:
The presence of elevated levels of nitrate and nitrite in exhaled breath condensate (EBC) in airway disease suggests an increase in nitric oxide (NO) metabolism. However, the specific sources of nitrate and nitrite in the airways have not been thoroughly investigated. 

To address this, the study measured the fraction of exhaled NO (FE(NO)) at a flow rate of 50 ml/s, as well as nitrite and nitrate levels in EBC, nasal condensate, and saliva. The participants included 17 tracheostomised and 15 non-tracheostomised individuals who were non-smokers without respiratory disease. Tracheal and oral samples were collected from the tracheostomised subjects, while nasal and oral samples were collected from the non-tracheostomised subjects. 

Measurements were taken before and after the ingestion of sodium nitrate (10 mg/kg) and the use of an antibacterial mouthwash (chlorhexidine 0.2%). 

The results showed that in tracheostomised subjects, oral FE(NO) increased by 90% after nitrate ingestion, while tracheal FE(NO) remained unaffected. Oral EBC nitrite levels increased significantly at 60 minutes, whereas tracheal EBC nitrite levels only showed a minor increase. Nitrate levels in both oral and tracheal EBC increased by the same amount. 

In non-tracheostomised subjects, oral FE(NO) and EBC nitrite levels increased after nitrate ingestion, but returned to baseline levels after chlorhexidine mouthwash. Nasal NO, nitrate, and nitrite levels were not affected by nitrate intake or mouthwash. 

Baseline measurements showed that mouthwash with deionised water did not affect nitrite levels in oral EBC or saliva, while antibacterial mouthwash led to significant reductions in nitrite levels. 

In conclusion, besides the salivary glands, the lower airways take up plasma nitrate, but not the nasal airways. Nitrate levels in EBC are influenced by dietary intake. Bacterial activity in the oropharyngeal tract of healthy individuals primarily converts nitrate to nitrite. Only oropharyngeal nitrite appears to contribute to exhaled NO in non-inflamed airways, and there is also a significant contribution of nitrite from the oropharyngeal tract during standard collection of EBC.

title: AZD9150, a next-generation antisense oligonucleotide inhibitor of STAT3 with early evidence of clinical activity in lymphoma and lung cancer
text: The advancements in next-generation sequencing technologies have significantly enhanced our knowledge of cancer genetics. An appealing platform called antisense technology has the potential to utilize these advancements to improve cancer therapeutics. This is because antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) inhibitors can be designed solely based on gene sequence information. Recent clinical data in humans have demonstrated the strong effectiveness of systemically administered ASOs that target genes expressed in the liver. In this article, we discuss the preclinical activity and initial clinical evaluation of a specific class of ASOs that contain constrained ethyl modifications. These ASOs are designed to target the gene responsible for encoding the transcription factor STAT3, which is notoriously challenging to inhibit therapeutically. The systemic delivery of the unformulated ASO, known as AZD9150, has been shown to decrease STAT3 expression in various preclinical cancer models and exhibit antitumor activity in lymphoma and lung cancer models. The preclinical activity of AZD9150 has translated into significant antitumor activity as a single-agent treatment in patients with highly treatment-refractory lymphoma and non-small cell lung cancer, as observed in a phase 1 dose-escalation study.

title: Evidence of a pluripotent human embryonic stem cell line derived from a cloned blastocyst.
text: Recently, the technology known as somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT) has been utilized to create animals with identical genetic compositions. In this particular investigation, we present the development of a pluripotent embryonic stem (ES) cell line (referred to as SCNT-hES-1) derived from a cloned human blastocyst. The SCNT-hES-1 cells exhibited the typical morphology and cell surface markers of ES cells. They demonstrated the ability to differentiate into embryoid bodies in a laboratory setting and form teratomas in vivo, containing cell derivatives from all three embryonic germ layers, when introduced into severe combined immunodeficient mice. Remarkably, even after undergoing more than 70 passages of continuous proliferation, the SCNT-hES-1 cells maintained normal karyotypes and were genetically identical to the somatic nuclear donor cells. While we cannot completely rule out the possibility that the cells originated from parthenogenesis, analyses of imprinting provide support for the SCNT origin of the derived human ES cells.

title: Ultrarapid drug metabolism: PCR-based detection of CYP2D6 gene duplication.
text: The enzyme CYP2D6, also known as debrisoquine 4-hydroxylase, is responsible for metabolizing many commonly used drugs. However, it is highly variable among individuals. Some people have an ultrafast activity of the enzyme, while others have a complete absence of it. This leads to differences in metabolic capacity, resulting in variations in the effectiveness and side effects of drugs at standard doses. In Caucasians, up to 7% of individuals may have ultrarapid drug metabolism due to inherited alleles with multiple functional CYP2D6 genes, leading to higher levels of the enzyme. Identifying individuals with ultrarapid drug metabolism is important for adjusting drug doses in therapy and avoiding misinterpretation of noncompliance. In our study, we used recently developed PCR assays to detect the ultrarapid metabolizer genotype. Among a population of 202 psychiatric patients, we found a prevalence of 3.5% of individuals with duplicate active CYP2D6 genes associated with ultrarapid drug metabolism.

title: The Actions of Synaptically Released Zinc at Hippocampal Mossy Fiber Synapses
text: Zinc ions (Zn2+) are found in high concentrations within the synaptic vesicles of hippocampal mossy fibers. To investigate the physiological function of Zn2+ in this pathway, we utilized Zn2+ chelators and the mocha mutant mouse. Our findings indicate that Zn2+ does not contribute to the distinctive presynaptic plasticities observed at mossy fiber synapses. However, it is co-released with glutamate from these synapses, both spontaneously and with electrical stimulation, exerting a significant modulatory influence on the NMDA receptors. Specifically, Zn2+ consistently occupies the high-affinity binding site of NMDA receptors at mossy fiber synapses, while the lower affinity voltage-dependent Zn2+ binding site is occupied during action potential-driven release. In conclusion, Zn2+ functions as a modulatory neurotransmitter released from mossy fiber synapses, playing a crucial role in shaping the NMDA receptor response at these synapses.

title: Association between folate intake from different food sources in Norway and homocysteine status in a dietary intervention among young male adults.
text:
The purpose of this study was to examine the impact of a dietary intervention that combined nutrition information with increased availability of vegetables, fruits, and wholegrain bread. The researchers wanted to see how this intervention affected the participants' intake of these foods and estimated nutrient levels. Additionally, they investigated whether changes in the sources of folate intake were linked to changes in plasma total homocysteine levels.

The study involved 376 male recruits from the Norwegian National Guard in Vaernes (intervention group) and 105 male recruits from the Norwegian National Guard in Heggelia (control group) over a period of 5 months. The results showed that the intervention led to a significant increase in the consumption of vegetables, fruits, berries, juice, and wholegrain bread. The participants in the intervention group had a greater increase in dietary fiber and folate intake compared to the control group.
