Since high levels can often be easily treated with vitamin supplements, homocyst(e)ine may be considered an independent and modifiable risk factor.

title: Involvement of transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 receptors in protease-activated receptor-2-induced joint inflammation and nociception.
text:
Protease-activated receptor-2 (PAR-2) is a receptor that is activated by proteolytic cleavage and is coupled to G-proteins. It is found on epithelial, endothelial, and inflammatory cells, as well as on neurons expressing the transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) receptor. PAR-2 plays a crucial role in inflammatory and nociceptive processes. However, there is limited information on its function in joints. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the effects of activating PAR-2 within the joint on pain and inflammation.

To assess the impact of intraarticular PAR-2 activation, various measurements were taken in rats and mice. These included secondary hyperalgesia/allodynia, spontaneous weight distribution, swelling, and production of inflammatory cytokines. Additionally, the involvement of TRPV1 ion channels was examined.

The results showed that injecting the PAR-2 receptor agonist SLIGRL-NH(2) into the knee reduced touch sensitivity and weight bearing in the hindlimb on the same side in both species. Furthermore, the TRPV1 antagonist SB366791 significantly reduced secondary mechanical allodynia/hyperalgesia and impaired weight distribution in rats, while genetic deletion of the TRPV1 receptor achieved the same effect in mice.

Interestingly, PAR-2 activation did not cause significant joint swelling but did increase the concentration of IL-1beta, an inflammatory cytokine. This increase was not affected by the absence of the TRPV1 channel. In comparison, injecting SLIGRL-NH(2) into the paw also induced primary mechanical hyperalgesia and impaired weight distribution in both wild-type and TRPV1-deficient mice, but the edema was smaller in the knockout mice. Notably, injecting the inactive peptide LRGILS-NH(2) into either site did not lead to any inflammatory or nociceptive changes.

These findings provide evidence for the significant involvement of TRPV1 receptors in secondary mechanical hyperalgesia/allodynia and spontaneous pain caused by PAR-2 activation in the knee joint. However, primary mechanical hyperalgesia, impaired weight distribution, and IL-1beta production appear to be independent of this channel, although TRPV1 receptors still mediate PAR-2 activation-induced edema in the paw.

title: Relationship between reduced forced expiratory volume in one second and the risk of lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
text:
BACKGROUND
Individuals with severe lung function impairment have a higher risk of developing lung cancer. However, there is controversy surrounding whether milder reductions in forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) also increase the risk of lung cancer. Additionally, there is little consensus on whether men and women have similar risks for lung cancer with similar decreases in FEV1.

METHODS
A search was conducted on PubMed and EMBASE from January 1966 to January 2005 to identify studies that examined the relationship between FEV1 and lung cancer. The search was limited to population-based studies with a prospective design, large sample sizes (> or = 5000 participants), and adjustment for smoking status.

RESULTS
Twenty-eight abstracts were identified, with six not reporting FEV1 and eight not adjusting for smoking. This report includes four studies that reported FEV1 in quintiles. The risk of lung cancer increased as FEV1 decreased. Compared to the highest quintile of FEV1 (> 100% of predicted), the lowest quintile of FEV1 (< approximately 70% of predicted) was associated with a 2.23-fold (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.73 to 2.86) increase in lung cancer risk for men and a 3.97-fold increase for women (95% CI 1.93 to 8.25). Even small decrements in FEV1 (approximately 90% of predicted) increased lung cancer risk by 30% for men (95% CI 1.05 to 1.62) and 2.64-fold for women (95% CI 1.30 to 5.31).

CONCLUSION
Reduced FEV1 is strongly linked to lung cancer. Even a modest reduction in FEV1 is a significant predictor of lung cancer, particularly among women.

title: Functional Architecture of RNA Polymerase I
text: The synthesis of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) by RNA polymerase (Pol) I is the initial stage in the formation of ribosomes and serves as a regulatory switch for cell growth in eukaryotes. In this study, we present the cryo-electron microscopic structure of the complete 14-subunit yeast Pol I at a resolution of 12 A. Additionally, we provide a homology model for the core enzyme and the crystal structure of the subcomplex A14/43. By combining these structures, we have obtained a hybrid structure of Pol I, A14/43, in which the clamp and dock domain interact with promoter-specific initiation factors on a unique surface. The Pol I-specific subunits A49 and A34.5 form a heterodimer near the enzyme funnel, acting as an intrinsic elongation factor similar to the Pol II-associated factor TFIIF. Unlike Pol II, Pol I exhibits a robust 3'-RNA cleavage activity, which relies on the C-terminal domain of subunit A12.2. This activity is crucial for ribosomal RNA proofreading and 3'-end trimming.

title: SWI/SNF-Brg1 regulates self-renewal and occupies core pluripotency-related genes in embryonic stem cells.
text: The SWI/SNF-Brg1 protein is crucial for controlling the cell cycle and promoting differentiation by regulating gene expression. When Brg1 is lost in mice, it leads to early embryonic death. Recent studies have also suggested that Brg1 plays a role in the self-renewal and differentiation of somatic stem cells. However, there is limited knowledge about the function of Brg1 in preimplantation embryos and embryonic stem (ES) cells. In this study, we found that Brg1 is necessary for the self-renewal and pluripotency of ES cells. By using RNA interference to reduce Brg1 levels in blastocysts, we observed abnormal expression of Oct4 and Nanog. In ES cells, knocking down Brg1 resulted in changes that indicated differentiation, as well as a decrease in the expression of genes associated with self-renewal and pluripotency (such as Oct4, Sox2, Sall4, Rest), and an increase in the expression of genes related to differentiation. Through genome-wide promoter analysis, we discovered that Brg1 occupies the promoters of important genes involved in pluripotency, including Oct4, Sox2, Nanog, Sall4, Rest, and Polycomb group (PcG) proteins. Additionally, Brg1 co-occupies a subset of target genes with Oct4, Sox2, Nanog, and PcG proteins. These findings highlight the significant role of Brg1 in regulating self-renewal and pluripotency in ES cells.

title: Rapid induction of Alternative Lengthening of Telomeres by depletion of the histone chaperone ASF1
text: The activation mechanism of the alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT) pathway in maintaining the ends of mammalian chromosomes has been unclear. However, our recent discovery reveals that depleting the histone chaperones ASF1a and ASF1b in human cells induces all the characteristic features of ALT in both primary and cancer cells. These features include the formation of ALT-associated PML (promyelocytic leukemia) bodies (APBs), the presence of extrachromosomal telomeric DNA species, an increased frequency of telomeric sister chromatid exchanges (t-SCE) events, and intertelomeric exchange of an integrated tag. Interestingly, the induction of ALT traits in this scenario also leads to the suppression of telomerase activity. Through our investigation, we found that the proteins RAD17 and BLM positively regulate ALT induction, while EXO1 and DNA2 negatively regulate it. The induction of ALT characteristics as a result of ASF1 depletion strongly supports the hypothesis that ALT arises from dysfunction in histone management.

title: Targeting bromodomains: epigenetic readers of lysine acetylation
text: The regulation of chromatin structure is heavily influenced by lysine acetylation, a crucial mechanism. When acetylation levels are abnormal, it has been associated with the development of various diseases. Acetyl-lysine modifications play a significant role in creating docking sites for bromodomains, which are small interaction modules found on different proteins. Some of these proteins are essential for the assembly of transcriptional regulator complexes, which rely on acetylation. These complexes then initiate transcriptional programs that lead to changes in phenotype. Recently, there has been a breakthrough in the discovery of potent and highly specific inhibitors for the BET family of bromodomains. This discovery has sparked intense research in various therapeutic areas, particularly in oncology. BET proteins, regulated by BET bromodomains, control the expression of crucial oncogenes and anti-apoptotic proteins. Furthermore, targeting BET bromodomains could have potential in treating inflammation and viral infections. In this article, we will discuss the recent advancements in the development of bromodomain inhibitors and their potential applications in drug discovery.

title: Arachidonic acid cytochrome P450 epoxygenase pathway.
text: Cytochrome P450 (CYP) epoxygenases transform arachidonic acid into four epoxyeicosatrienoic acid (EET) regioisomers, namely 5,6-, 8,9-, 11,12-, and 14,15-EET. These EETs act as autacrine and paracrine mediators, inducing vascular relaxation by activating large-conductance Ca2+-activated K+ channels (BKCa) in smooth muscle. Moreover, they possess anti-inflammatory properties in blood vessels and the kidney, promote angiogenesis, and provide protection to ischemic myocardium and brain. CYP epoxygenases also convert eicosapentaenoic acid into vasoactive epoxy-derivatives, and endocannabinoids containing 11,12- and 14,15-EET are formed. Many of the actions of EETs are believed to be initiated by their binding to a membrane receptor, which activates ion channels and intracellular signal transduction pathways. However, EETs can also be taken up by cells, incorporated into phospholipids, and bind to cytosolic proteins and nuclear receptors, suggesting that some functions may occur through direct interaction of EETs with intracellular effector systems. Soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH) converts EETs into dihydroxyeicosatrienoic acids (DHETs), which attenuates many of the functional effects of EETs. Therefore, inhibiting sEH is being investigated as a means to increase and prolong the beneficial actions of EETs.

title: Physical activity at 36 years: patterns and childhood predictors in a longitudinal study.
text:
The objective of this study was to analyze the differences in physical activity patterns between men and women, as well as the impact of socioeconomic factors on participation in sports and recreational activities later in life. The data used in this study was collected from a national birth cohort study, which followed a sample of approximately 3500 individuals from birth until the age of 43. The study was conducted in England, Scotland, and Wales.

The results showed that men reported higher rates of participation in sports, recreational activities, gardening, and do-it-yourself projects, while women reported higher rates of bicycling and walking. Higher levels of education were associated with increased participation in sports. It was also found that individuals often engaged in one type of activity without necessarily participating in others.

The study revealed that those who were most active in sports had excelled in sports during their school years, were more socially outgoing during adolescence, had fewer health problems in childhood, had higher levels of education, and had mothers with a secondary education.

In conclusion, studies examining the relationship between physical activity and chronic disease should consider a wide range of activities rather than focusing on just one area. Additionally, the findings highlight the importance of developing skills and habits related to physical activity during childhood, as well as promoting healthier exercise habits in adults who may have had limited opportunities or low motivation in the past.

title: Residual lifetime risk for developing hypertension in middle-aged women and men: The Framingham Heart Study.
text:
The lifetime risk for developing hypertension is best understood through the lifetime risk statistic. However, the lifetime risk for hypertension and its trends over time are currently unknown. The objective of this study was to estimate the residual lifetime risk for hypertension in older adults in the United States and to assess any changes in this risk over time. 

The study was conducted as a community-based prospective cohort study, involving 1298 participants from the Framingham Heart Study. These participants were between the ages of 55 and 65 and did not have hypertension at the start of the study (1976-1998). 

The main outcome measures of the study were the residual lifetime risk for hypertension, defined as having a blood pressure of 140/90 mm Hg or higher or using antihypertensive medications. 

The results showed that the residual lifetime risks for developing hypertension and stage 1 high blood pressure or higher were both 90% for participants aged 55 and 65. Additionally, there was a 60% probability of receiving antihypertensive medication during their lifetime. 

The risk for hypertension remained unchanged for women, but it was approximately 60% higher for men in the period from 1976 to 1998 compared to the period from 1952 to 1975. On the other hand, the residual lifetime risk for stage 2 high blood pressure or higher was lower in both men and women in the recent period (35%-57% in 1952-1975 vs 35%-44% in 1976-1998). This decrease was likely due to an increase in the treatment of individuals with significantly elevated blood pressure. 

In conclusion, the study found that the residual lifetime risk for hypertension in middle-aged and elderly individuals is 90%, indicating a significant public health burden. While there has been a decline in the lifetime risk for stage 2 high blood pressure or higher, efforts should still be focused on preventing hypertension from occurring in the first place.

title: Mechanism and regulation of DNA end resection in eukaryotes.
text: The process of repairing DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) through homologous recombination (HR) begins with the degradation of the 5'-terminated strands, known as end resection. This degradation produces 3'-single-stranded DNA tails, which serve as substrates for Rad51 to facilitate homologous pairing and DNA strand exchange. Additionally, these tails activate the DNA damage checkpoint. It is widely accepted that end resection occurs in two steps. Firstly, Sae2/CtIP triggers the Mre11-Rad50-Xrs2/Nbs1 (MRX/N) complex to cleave the 5'-terminated DNA strands near the break ends. Secondly, Exo1 and/or Dna2 nucleases extend the resected tracts, resulting in long 3'-ssDNA-tailed intermediates. The initiation of resection commits a cell to repair a DSB through HR, as long ssDNA overhangs are not suitable for non-homologous end joining (NHEJ). Therefore, the initiation of end resection plays a crucial role in determining the repair pathway. In this review, I will discuss recent studies on the mechanism of end resection and how it is regulated to ensure the most appropriate repair outcome.

title: Multiple-dose activated charcoal in acute self-poisoning: a randomised controlled trial
text:
In the rural developing world, intentional self-poisoning has a much higher fatality rate compared to industrialized countries. This is primarily due to the use of highly toxic pesticides and plants. To address this issue, we conducted a study to determine if routine treatment with multiple-dose activated charcoal would be beneficial in interrupting the circulation of toxins in the body. 

The study was an open-label, parallel group, randomized controlled trial conducted in three hospitals in Sri Lanka. A total of 4632 patients were randomly assigned to receive either no charcoal, one dose of charcoal, or six doses of charcoal. Outcomes were available for 4629 patients, with 51% having ingested pesticides and 36% having ingested yellow oleander seeds. The primary outcome measure was mortality, and the analysis was done on an intention-to-treat basis. The trial was registered with controlled-trials.com as ISRCTN02920054. 

The results showed no significant difference in mortality between the groups. In the multiple-dose group, 6.3% of participants died compared to 6.8% in the no charcoal group (adjusted odds ratio 0.96, 95% CI 0.70-1.33). There were also no differences observed for patients who had taken specific poisons, were severely ill upon admission, or presented early. 

Based on these findings, we cannot recommend the routine use of multiple-dose activated charcoal in rural Asia Pacific. However, further studies on early charcoal administration may be beneficial, as there is an urgent need for effective and affordable treatments.

title: Post-prenylation-processing enzymes as new targets in oncogenesis
text: RAS and various other oncogenic proteins undergo a complex sequence of modifications after they are produced, which begins with the addition of an isoprenoid lipid through a process called prenylation. After prenylation, these proteins typically go through endoproteolytic processing by the RCE1 protease and then carboxyl methylation by a unique methyltransferase called isoprenylcysteine carboxyl methyltransferase (ICMT). Although inhibitors targeting the prenylation step are currently being tested in advanced clinical trials, their effectiveness appears to be limited. However, recent discoveries suggest that inhibiting the post-prenylation-processing steps, particularly the methylation catalyzed by ICMT, may offer a more effective approach to controlling the proliferation of cancer cells.

title: Trends in sugar-sweetened beverage consumption among youth and adults in the United States: 1999-2010.
text:
The aim of this study was to examine the trends in sugar-sweetened beverage (SSB) consumption among youth and adults in the United States. The researchers analyzed data from 22,367 youth aged 2-19 years and 29,133 adults aged 20 years and older who participated in a 24-hour dietary recall as part of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) between 1999 and 2010. SSBs included soda, fruit drinks, sports and energy drinks, sweetened coffee and tea, and other sweetened beverages. The study also looked at patterns of SSB consumption, including where and when people consumed these beverages.

The results showed that in 2009-2010, youth consumed an average of 155 calories per day from SSBs, while adults consumed an age-adjusted average of 151 calories per day from SSBs. This represented a decrease from 1999-2000 of 68 calories per day for youth and 45 calories per day for adults. SSBs contributed 8.0% and 6.9% of daily energy intake among youth and adults, respectively, in 2009-2010, which was a decrease compared to 1999-2000. The study also found that SSB consumption decreased both at home and away from home, as well as during meals and snacks, over the 12-year study period.

In conclusion, there was a decrease in SSB consumption among youth and adults in the United States between 1999 and 2010.

title: Ubiquitination on nonlysine residues by a viral E3 ubiquitin ligase.
text: The ubiquitination process regulates a wide range of cellular functions. Enzyme type 3 (E3) ubiquitin ligases control the final step of this pathway. These E3 enzymes are responsible for determining the specific targets and catalyzing the formation of an isopeptide bond between a lysine residue (or the N terminus) of the substrate and ubiquitin. Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus encodes two E3 ubiquitin ligases, MIR1 and MIR2, which are involved in the ubiquitination and subsequent internalization of major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC I) molecules. Our research has revealed that MIR1, but not MIR2, promotes the down-regulation of MHC I molecules that lack lysine residues in their intracytoplasmic domain. In the presence of MIR1, these MHC I molecules undergo ubiquitination, and their association with ubiquitin is sensitive to beta2-mercaptoethanol, unlike lysine-ubiquitin bonds. This type of ubiquitination requires a cysteine residue in the intracytoplasmic tail of MHC I molecules. We also observed that an MHC I molecule containing a single cysteine residue in an artificial glycine and alanine intracytoplasmic domain is endocytosed and degraded when MIR1 is present. Therefore, ubiquitination can occur on proteins that lack accessible lysines or an accessible N terminus.

title: All dosage compensation is local: Gene-by-gene regulation of sex-biased expression on the chicken Z chromosome
text: Recent reports indicate that birds do not possess a comprehensive mechanism for compensating gene dosage on the Z sex chromosome. This finding was unexpected, as other animals with chromosomal sex determination have methods to counteract the effects of gene dosage on the dominant sex chromosome in both males and females. Despite the absence of a global mechanism for avian dosage compensation, there is significant variation in gene expression differences between males and females for individual Z-linked genes. This suggests that certain genes may be individually compensated for dosage, and that some form of local or temporal dosage compensation exists on the avian Z chromosome. To investigate this further, we conducted global gene expression profiling in male and female chickens at various stages of their life cycle, analyzing both somatic and gonadal tissue. The average fold-change in gene expression between males and females varied across different tissue and time-point combinations. Embryonic brain samples exhibited the smallest gene dosage effects, while adult gonadal tissue displayed the highest degree of male bias. Overall, we did not observe any regions of overall dosage compensation on the Z chromosome. These findings suggest that dosage compensation on the Z chromosome is solely regulated on a gene-by-gene basis and can vary depending on the life cycle stage and tissue type. This regulation may reflect the critical functionality of certain genes, as the expression levels of essential genes are tightly controlled to prevent disruption of important pathways and networks with differing expression levels in males and females.

title: Hormone replacement therapy prevents bone loss in patients with inflammatory bowel disease.
text:
A study was conducted to investigate the effectiveness of hormone replacement therapy (HRT) in preventing bone loss in postmenopausal women with inflammatory bowel disease. The study included 47 women aged 44 to 67 years with either ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease. Radial and spinal bone density measurements were taken annually using single photon absorptiometry and quantitative computed tomography, respectively. 

The results showed that the annual change in radial bone density was +1.42%/yr (+0.58 to +2.26; P < 0.005), indicating a positive effect of HRT in preventing bone loss in this area. Similarly, the annual change in spinal bone density was +2.60%/yr (+1.06 to +4.15; p < 0.005), suggesting that HRT also had a positive impact on preventing bone loss in the spine. 

There was no significant correlation between the rates of change in bone density at the two sites, nor between the rates of change and the initial bone density in either the radius or spine. Additionally, the use of prednisolone during the study did not significantly affect the rates of change in spinal bone density. 

The study found no significant differences in the changes in bone density between patients with ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease. Furthermore, the changes in bone density were not influenced by the patients' age or number of years after menopause. 

In conclusion, the study suggests that HRT is effective in preventing bone loss in postmenopausal women with inflammatory bowel disease.

title: Disruption of the 5S RNP–Mdm2 interaction significantly improves the erythroid defect in a mouse model for Diamond-Blackfan anemia
text: Diamond-Blackfan anemia (DBA) is a rare condition characterized by a lack of red blood cell production due to a genetic mutation in ribosomal proteins. This mutation leads to disrupted ribosome formation and triggers a stress response mediated by the p53 protein. However, the exact mechanisms of p53 activation and its impact on the red blood cell defect in DBA are still unclear. Previous research suggests that the inhibition of a protein called Mdm2 by the 5S ribonucleoprotein particle (RNP) is responsible for p53 activation. However, it is uncertain if this mechanism alone is responsible for the p53-related component in DBA. To investigate this further, we conducted experiments using a mouse model of RPS19-deficient DBA and mice with a disrupted 5S RNP-Mdm2 interaction. We found that the disrupted interaction reversed the p53 response, improved the growth of blood cell precursors in the laboratory, and alleviated anemia in live mice. Surprisingly, the disruption of the 5S RNP-Mdm2 interaction also caused a specific defect in red blood cell production. These findings demonstrate the sensitivity of red blood cell precursors to abnormalities in p53 regulation mediated by the 5S RNP-Mdm2 interaction. Additionally, our evidence suggests that the natural activation of the 5S RNP-Mdm2-p53 pathway may contribute to the gradual decline of the hematopoietic system over time in a cell-autonomous manner.

title: Pharmacist participation on physician rounds and adverse drug events in the intensive care unit.
text: The purpose of this study was to determine whether having a pharmacist participate in medical rounds in the intensive care unit (ICU) would reduce preventable adverse drug events (ADEs) caused by ordering errors. The study compared data from before and after the intervention was implemented, as well as compared the ICU unit with a control unit that did not receive the intervention. The study took place in a medical ICU and a coronary care unit in a large urban teaching hospital. A total of 75 patients were randomly selected from each of the three groups: baseline admissions to the study unit, post-intervention admissions to the study unit, and admissions to the control unit. An additional 50 patients were randomly selected from the control unit during the baseline period. The intervention involved a senior pharmacist joining the ICU team for rounds and being available for consultation throughout the day. The main outcome measures were preventable ADEs due to ordering errors and the number, type, and acceptance of interventions made by the pharmacist. The results showed that the rate of preventable ordering ADEs decreased by 66% after the intervention was implemented. In contrast, the rate in the control unit remained essentially unchanged. The pharmacist made 366 recommendations related to drug ordering, and nearly all of them were accepted by physicians. In conclusion, having a pharmacist participate in medical rounds in the ICU as a full member of the patient care team was associated with a significantly lower rate of ADEs caused by prescribing errors, and the majority of the recommendations made by the pharmacist were accepted by physicians.

title: Ligand-target interactions: what can we learn from NMR?
text: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) can be used to study the conformation of a ligand when it is bound to a large macromolecular target. This technique is applicable to both tightly and weakly forming complexes. In the case of weak binding (where the dissociation rate constant, k(off), is greater than 10(4) Hz), NMR can provide structural information about the bound ligand even for very large complexes (>100 kDa), which would otherwise be challenging to study using NMR in the tight binding regime. In this review, I discuss the current state-of-the-art NMR methods used for screening ligands and investigating the structural conformations of bound ligands in both tight and weak binding scenarios. I critically evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of each approach. In recent years, there have been significant advancements in NMR techniques for studying transiently forming complexes, allowing for a more detailed understanding of ligand-target interactions. I thoroughly review novel methods, such as transferred cross-correlated relaxation, for determining the conformation of bound ligands. I discuss the advantages of these new methods compared to established techniques, using the epothilone-tubulin complex as a primary example.

title: MotifMap: integrative genome-wide maps of regulatory motif sites for model species
text:
The challenge in biology is to understand and map gene regulation on a genome-wide level. However, only a small portion of the regulatory elements in a genome have been characterized, and there is a need for computational methods to map and understand these elements. The size of non-coding regions and the complexity of regulatory elements and interactions make this task difficult. Currently, there are no genome-wide catalogs of regulatory elements for all model species. 

The MotifMap system addresses this challenge by using databases of transcription factor binding motifs, refined genome alignments, and a comparative genomic statistical approach. This system provides comprehensive maps of potential regulatory elements in model species' genomes. The system has been used to create new genome-wide maps for yeast, fly, worm, mouse, and human. The human map, for example, contains 519,108 sites for 570 matrices with a False Discovery Rate of 0.1 or less. The accuracy and coverage of these new maps have been validated using experimental data and statistical analysis.

These maps can be integrated with other omic data and are available at http://motifmap.igb.uci.edu/. This integration allows for the analysis of gene regulation on a genome-wide scale and the generation of regulatory pathways and hypotheses. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated using the P53 apoptotic pathway and the Gli hedgehog pathways as examples.

title: Inhibition of apical sodium-dependent bile acid transporter as a novel treatment for diabetes.
text: The aim of this study was to assess the impact of a potent Asbt inhibitor (264W94) on glucose regulation in Zucker Diabetic Fatty (ZDF) rats. By blocking the absorption of bile acids in the intestines, oral administration of 264W94 for two weeks resulted in higher levels of bile acids in feces and increased non-fasting plasma total Glp-1. The treatment with 264W94 significantly reduced HbA1c and glucose levels, and prevented the decline in insulin levels typically observed in ZDF rats, with the effectiveness varying depending on the dosage. An oral glucose tolerance test showed a two-fold increase in plasma total Glp-1 and a three-fold increase in insulin in 264W94-treated ZDF rats, at doses that effectively controlled blood sugar levels. Tissue mRNA analysis revealed reduced activation of the farnesoid X receptor (Fxr) in the small intestines and liver, but co-administration of a Fxr agonist (GW4064) did not diminish the glucose-lowering effects induced by 264W94. In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that inhibiting Asbt leads to higher levels of bile acids in the distal intestine, stimulates the release of Glp-1, and may present a novel therapeutic approach for managing type 2 diabetes mellitus.

title: Early chromatin unfolding by RUNX1: a molecular explanation for differential requirements during specification versus maintenance of the hematopoietic gene expression program.
text: The specific gene expression profile characterizes each regulatory state as development progresses at the cellular level. However, the mechanisms that regulate the priming and maintenance of gene expression within a developmental pathway are not well understood. To address these questions, we focused on the hematopoietic system as an experimental model. In particular, we examined a regulatory circuit involving the transcription factor PU.1, its target gene colony-stimulating-factor 1 receptor (Csf1r), and key upstream regulators like RUNX1, which plays a central role in myelopoiesis. Our findings reveal that chromatin unfolding occurs before the establishment of active histone marks and the formation of stable transcription factor complexes at the Pu.1 locus during ontogeny. We also demonstrate that chromatin remodeling is facilitated by the transient binding of RUNX1 to Pu.1 cis-elements. On the other hand, the reorganization of Csf1r chromatin requires prior expression of PU.1 along with RUNX1 binding. Once the complete hematopoietic program is established, stable transcription factor complexes and active chromatin can be maintained without the presence of RUNX1. These experiments highlight how individual transcription factors function in a stage-specific manner to differentially impact the initiation and maintenance of a developmental program.

title: Whole-genome fingerprint of the DNA methylome during human B cell differentiation
text:
We conducted a thorough analysis of the DNA methylome in ten different subpopulations that cover the entire B cell differentiation process. This analysis involved using whole-genome bisulfite sequencing and high-density microarrays. Our findings revealed that non-CpG methylation disappears once B cell commitment occurs, while CpG methylation undergoes significant changes throughout B cell maturation. These changes follow an accumulative pattern and impact approximately 30% of all measured CpG sites.

During the early stages of differentiation, we primarily observed demethylation of enhancers. This demethylation was associated with the upregulation of key B cell transcription factors and affected multiple genes involved in B cell biology. In contrast, the later stages of differentiation showed extensive demethylation of heterochromatin and a gain in methylation at Polycomb-repressed regions. Interestingly, genes with apparent functional impact in B cells were not affected by these changes. This particular signature, which has previously been associated with aging and cancer, was particularly prevalent in mature cells with an extended lifespan.

When comparing B cell neoplasms to their normal counterparts, we discovered that they frequently acquire methylation changes in regions that already undergo dynamic methylation during normal B cell differentiation.

title: LIN28B induces neuroblastoma and enhances MYCN levels via let-7 suppression
text: LIN28B plays a crucial role in regulating developmental processes by controlling the activity of microRNAs (miRNAs) belonging to the let-7 family. While the involvement of LIN28B in cancer has been suggested, its role in vivo has not been firmly established. In this study, we present evidence that LIN28B exhibits genetic abnormalities and significant overexpression in high-risk neuroblastoma, in contrast to other tumor types and normal tissues. Notably, high levels of LIN28B expression were found to be an independent risk factor for unfavorable outcomes in neuroblastoma. Mechanistically, LIN28B suppressed the activity of let-7 miRNAs, leading to increased expression of the MYCN protein in neuroblastoma cells. This LIN28B-let-7-MYCN signaling axis hindered the differentiation of both normal neuroblasts and neuroblastoma cells. Importantly, these findings were successfully replicated in a mouse model, where LIN28B expression in the sympathetic adrenergic lineage triggered the development of neuroblastomas characterized by reduced let-7 miRNA levels and elevated MYCN protein expression. Targeting this pathway could potentially offer therapeutic opportunities for neuroblastoma treatment.

title: Platelet-derived endothelial cell growth factor expression correlates with tumour angiogenesis and prognosis in non-small-cell lung cancer.
text: Angiogenesis, the formation of new blood vessels, has recently been identified as a prognostic factor in non-small-cell lung cancer. Platelet-derived endothelial cell growth factor (PD-ECGF), which is known to be the enzyme thymidine phosphorylase (TP), has been shown to induce angiogenesis both in laboratory settings and in living organisms. High levels of this enzyme within cells have been linked to increased sensitivity to pyrimidine antimetabolites, a type of chemotherapy drug. In this study, the expression of PD-ECGF/TP was examined in surgically removed tissue samples from 107 patients with operable non-small-cell lung cancer using a specific antibody. It was found that 25% of cases had high expression of PD-ECGF/TP, and this was associated with a high vascular grade. Among tumors with a high vascular grade, 44% showed positive reactivity for PD-ECGF/TP, compared to only 17% of tumors with a low or medium vascular grade. Positive expression was also more common in cases classified as T2 stage compared to T1 stage. Although overall survival was not affected, further analysis revealed that node-negative patients with positive PD-ECGF/TP expression had a worse prognosis. These findings suggest that PD-ECGF/TP may play a significant role in angiogenesis in non-small-cell lung cancer. Up-regulation of this enzyme indicates a more aggressive tumor phenotype in patients without lymph node involvement. Therefore, when designing randomized trials to assess the effectiveness of adjuvant chemotherapy in non-small-cell lung cancer, it is important to consider the assessment of vascular grade and PD-ECGF/TP expression.

title: The association between psychological distance and construal level: evidence from an implicit association test.
text: According to construal level theory, individuals tend to use a more abstract and high-level perspective when evaluating, perceiving, and predicting targets that are psychologically distant. Additionally, they perceive abstract targets as being more psychologically distant. The current study aimed to establish a connection between the level of construal and various dimensions of psychological distance on a conceptual level. Through eight experiments utilizing the Implicit Association Test, the researchers found a correlation between words associated with construal level (low vs. high) and words related to four dimensions of distance (proximal vs. distal): temporal distance, spatial distance, social distance, and hypotheticality. These findings not only support the relationship between construal level and psychological distance but also validate the idea that all four dimensions of psychological distance are interconnected and can be considered as different forms of psychological distance.

title: A load driver device for engineering modularity in biological networks
text: The behavior of gene modules in complex synthetic circuits can often be unpredictable. When modules are combined to form a circuit, downstream elements, such as binding sites for regulatory proteins, can impose a burden on upstream modules, leading to a negative impact on circuit function. In this study, we have developed a genetic device called a load driver to address this issue, and we have demonstrated its effectiveness in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. The load driver operates based on the principle of timescale separation, where its fast phosphotransfer processes enable a slower transcriptional circuit to respond to time-varying input signals, even in the presence of significant load. Without the load driver, we observed a 76% delay in response time and a 25% decrease in system bandwidth due to the load. However, with the inclusion of a load driver, the circuit's performance was almost completely restored. Load drivers will play a crucial role as essential components in the construction of complex, higher-level genetic circuits.

title: Inflammatory monocyte/macrophage modulation by liposome-entrapped spironolactone ameliorates acute lung injury in mice.
text: The aim of this study was to investigate the potential therapeutic and preventive effects of liposome-encapsulated spironolactone (Lipo-SP) on acute lung injury (ALI) and fibrosis. Lipo-SP was prepared using the film-ultrasonic method and its physicochemical and pharmacokinetic properties were characterized for oral administration. In a mouse model of bleomycin-induced ALI, Lipo-SP was administered at doses of 10 and 20 mg/kg for SP-loaded liposomes, and 20 mg/kg for free SP. The results showed that Lipo-SP significantly improved the bioavailability of SP and ameliorated lung pathology. The mechanism of action involved the antagonism of mineralocorticoid receptors by SP, which modulated inflammatory monocyte/macrophage activity and inhibited the M2 polarization of alveolar macrophages directed by Ly6C(hi) monocytosis. Additionally, Lipo-SP at a lower dose of 10 mg/kg showed greater improvement in body weight gain. In conclusion, our findings suggest that Lipo-SP holds promise as a therapeutic and preventive approach for ALI and fibrosis.

title: Passive Surveillance for I. scapularis Ticks: Enhanced Analysis for Early Detection of Emerging Lyme Disease Risk
text:
SUMMARY

Lyme disease (LD) is becoming more prevalent in Canada due to the expansion of the tick vector Ixodes scapularis (Say) into new areas. Detecting these emerging LD risk areas early is crucial for public health responses, but current methods lack specificity on a local scale. Passive tick surveillance has been used in Canada since 1990, but it is not effective in identifying areas where tick populations are established due to the dispersion of ticks by migratory birds. In this study, we developed a logistic regression model using data from 70 field sites in Quebec to estimate the risk of I. scapularis population establishment. The model considered the number of ticks submitted in passive surveillance and an environmental suitability index. By using sensitivity-specificity plots, we determined an optimal threshold value for the model's linear predictor as an indicator of tick population establishment. This value was used to create an "Alert Map" that identified areas in Quebec where passive surveillance data suggested tick establishment. The predictions of the Alert Map were validated through field surveillance at 76 sites. The results showed that the prevalence of established I. scapularis populations was significantly higher in areas predicted as high-risk by the Alert Map compared to moderate-risk areas. This study demonstrates that Alert Maps created using this approach can be a rapid and accurate tool for early identification of emerging LD risk areas, suitable for local disease control and prevention efforts.

title: Reduction of transmission from malaria patients by artemisinin combination therapies: a pooled analysis of six randomized trials
text:
BACKGROUND
Artemisinin combination therapies (ACT) are increasingly being used to treat Plasmodium falciparum malaria. These therapies are more effective against sexual stage parasites (gametocytes) and have the potential to reduce parasite transmission. The size of this effect was estimated in symptomatic P. falciparum infections.

METHODS
Data from six antimalarial trials conducted in The Gambia and Kenya, involving 3,174 patients, were analyzed. Multivariable regression was used to examine the impact of ACT versus non-artemisinin antimalarial treatment, treatment failure, presence of pre-treatment gametocytes, and submicroscopic gametocytaemia on transmission to mosquitoes and the area under the curve (AUC) of gametocyte density during the 28-day follow-up period.

RESULTS
ACT treatment was found to significantly reduce the likelihood of having gametocytes on the day of transmission experiments, transmission to mosquitoes by slide-positive gametocyte carriers, and AUC of gametocyte density. Parasitological treatment failure did not explain the difference between ACT and non-artemisinin impact. The presence of slide-positive gametocytaemia before treatment significantly reduced the impact of ACT on gametocytaemia. Considering submicroscopic gametocytaemia reduced the estimates of ACT impact in a high transmission setting in Kenya, but not in a lower transmission setting in The Gambia.

CONCLUSION
Treatment with ACT significantly reduces the infectiousness of individual patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria compared to previous first-line treatments. Administering ACT to patients before gametocytaemia develops may enhance its impact on transmission.

title: Skeletal Myogenic Progenitors Originating from Embryonic Dorsal Aorta Coexpress Endothelial and Myogenic Markers and Contribute to Postnatal Muscle Growth and Regeneration
text: Skeletal muscle in vertebrates is typically derived from somites, which are epithelial structures found in the paraxial mesoderm. However, there have been reports of myogenic cells appearing in tissues that are not derived from somites. This suggests that these cells may either undergo transdifferentiation or originate from a multipotent progenitor. In this study, we have discovered clonable skeletal myogenic cells in the embryonic dorsal aorta of mouse embryos. We conducted a detailed clonal analysis of different tissue anlagen at various stages of development to confirm this finding. In vitro, these myogenic cells exhibit the same morphology as satellite cells derived from adult skeletal muscle and express several markers associated with both myogenic and endothelial cells. Interestingly, adult satellite cells also express these endothelial markers. Additionally, we were able to clone myogenic cells from the limbs of mutant c-Met-/- embryos, which lack appendicular muscles but have a normal vascular system. When transplanted, these myogenic cells derived from the aorta contribute to postnatal muscle growth and regeneration, and fuse with resident satellite cells. This discovery suggests that the vascular system has the potential to generate skeletal muscle cells, which may explain the occurrence of nonsomite skeletal myogenesis. It also raises the possibility that a subset of satellite cells may originate from the vascular system.

title: Mapping of a gene for severe pediatric gastroesophageal reflux to chromosome 13q14.
text: The hereditary nature of gastroesophageal reflux (GER) has not been widely recognized in the past. However, there have been a few reports indicating that genetics may play a role in the development of severe or chronic forms of GER. The objective of this study was to identify a specific genetic locus that is associated with a severe pediatric GER phenotype in families with multiple affected members. The study involved conducting a genome-wide scan of families affected by severe pediatric GER using microsatellite markers. The research was conducted in a university tertiary care hospital in the United States. The subjects included affected and unaffected family members from five families with multiple individuals affected by severe pediatric GER. The main outcome measures were determining inheritance patterns and linking a genetic locus to the severe pediatric GER phenotype. The results showed that severe pediatric GER followed an autosomal dominant hereditary pattern with high penetrance. A gene for severe pediatric GER was mapped to a specific region on chromosome 13q. The study concluded that a gene for severe pediatric GER is located on chromosome 13q14.

title: Accelerating Policy Decisions to Adopt Haemophilus influenzae Type b Vaccine: A Global, Multivariable Analysis
text:
The adoption of new and underutilized vaccines by national immunization programs is crucial for reducing child mortality. However, policy decisions to adopt these vaccines in high mortality countries often lag behind decisions in high-income countries. This paper focuses on the Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) vaccine and aims to explain the reasons for these delays by analyzing various factors such as economic, epidemiological, programmatic, and policy-related factors at the country level. The role of the Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunisation (GAVI Alliance) is also examined.

To conduct the analysis, data from 147 countries between 1990 and 2007 were used. Accelerated failure time models were employed to identify factors associated with the time it took for countries to decide to adopt the Hib vaccine. The results showed that receiving support from GAVI accelerated the decision-making process by 63%. Additionally, having two or more neighboring countries already adopting the vaccine also sped up the decision-making process. On the other hand, an increase in vaccine price delayed the decision to adopt. Interestingly, global recommendations and local studies did not have a significant impact on the time to decision.

In conclusion, this study confirms previous findings regarding the influence of vaccine price on adoption decisions and provides new evidence suggesting that GAVI eligibility is associated with faster adoption of the Hib vaccine. The study also highlights the importance of neighboring country decisions in influencing adoption rates. Therefore, strategies to promote the adoption of new vaccines should consider both supply- and demand-side factors.

title: Haemolysin coregulated protein is an exported receptor and chaperone of type VI secretion substrates.
text: The discrimination of substrates within the vast pool of proteins in the cytoplasm requires precise mechanisms in secretion systems. However, the factors responsible for recognizing substrates in the type VI secretion system (T6SS) of Gram-negative bacteria, which is a common pathway for transporting effector proteins into target bacterial cells, have not yet been identified. Our findings show that haemolysin coregulated protein (Hcp), a ring-shaped hexamer secreted by all known T6SSs, specifically binds to effector molecules that are compatible with it. Through electron microscopy analysis of an Hcp-effector complex from Pseudomonas aeruginosa, we observed that the effector is bound to the inner surface of Hcp. Further investigations revealed that interaction with the Hcp pore is necessary for the secretion of various effectors with different enzymatic functions. Contrary to previous models that depicted Hcp as a static conduit, our data indicate that it acts as both a chaperone and a receptor for substrates. These distinct roles of a secreted protein highlight fundamental differences between the export mechanism of T6SS and other well-studied secretory pathways.

title: Long-term effects of continuing adjuvant tamoxifen to 10 years versus stopping at 5 years after diagnosis of oestrogen receptor-positive breast cancer: ATLAS, a randomised trial
text: In this study, researchers aimed to evaluate the effects of continuing tamoxifen treatment for 10 years instead of stopping at 5 years in women with early breast cancer. The study included 12,894 women who had completed 5 years of tamoxifen treatment and were randomly assigned to either continue treatment or stop. The researchers recorded any recurrence, second cancer, hospital admission, or death through yearly follow-up forms. The study found that among women with estrogen receptor (ER)-positive disease, continuing tamoxifen reduced the risk of breast cancer recurrence, breast cancer mortality, and overall mortality. The reductions in adverse outcomes were more significant after year 10. The cumulative risk of recurrence and breast cancer mortality was lower in women who continued tamoxifen compared to those who stopped. The study did not find any significant effect on breast cancer outcomes in women with ER-negative disease, and the effect was intermediate in women with unknown ER status. The study also found that continuing tamoxifen did not significantly affect mortality from causes other than breast cancer. However, it was associated with an increased risk of endometrial cancer. The researchers concluded that continuing tamoxifen treatment for 10 years can further reduce recurrence and mortality in women with ER-positive disease, particularly after year 10. These findings suggest that 10 years of tamoxifen treatment can approximately halve breast cancer mortality during the second decade after diagnosis. The study was funded by Cancer Research UK, UK Medical Research Council, AstraZeneca UK, US Army, and EU-Biomed.

title: Roles for MicroRNAs in Conferring Robustness to Biological Processes
text: Biological systems employ various mechanisms to uphold their functions despite disruptions caused by the environment or genetics. Recent findings indicate that microRNAs (miRNAs), in addition to their role in repressing gene expression, play a crucial role in enhancing the stability of biological processes. They achieve this by strengthening transcriptional programs, reducing abnormal transcripts, and potentially mitigating random fluctuations in transcript copy numbers within certain network contexts. These activities have significant implications for normal development, physiology, disease, and evolution. In this article, we will explore instances and principles of miRNAs that contribute to the robustness of animal systems.

title: Six-Year Follow-Up of Impact of Co-proxamol Withdrawal in England and Wales on Prescribing and Deaths: Time-Series Study
text:
The analgesic co-proxamol, which is a combination of paracetamol and dextropropoxyphene, has been linked to numerous fatal poisonings. Due to concerns about its safety and its common use in cases of suicide, it was withdrawn from the market in the UK. Our objective in this study was to examine the relationship between the withdrawal of co-proxamol and prescribing practices, as well as deaths in England and Wales between 2005 and 2010, compared to the period of 1998 to 2004. We also aimed to estimate any potential substitution effects with other analgesics.

To conduct this study, we collected prescribing data from the NHS Health and Social Care Information Centre in England and the Prescribing Services Partneriaeth Cydwasanaethau GIG Cymru in Wales. Mortality data was obtained from the Office for National Statistics. We analyzed the prescribing and death data using interrupted time-series analysis, focusing on deaths related to single analgesics, including suicide, open verdicts, and accidental poisonings.

Following the withdrawal of co-proxamol in 2005, there was a decrease in its prescribing, accompanied by an increase in the prescribing of several other analgesics, such as co-codamol, paracetamol, codeine, co-dydramol, tramadol, oxycodone, and morphine, between 2005 and 2010 compared to 1998 to 2004. These changes were associated with a significant reduction in deaths caused by co-proxamol poisoning, with suicide and undetermined cause verdicts decreasing by 21 deaths per quarter, or approximately 500 fewer suicide deaths (61% reduction) over the 6-year period. When accidental poisoning deaths were included, there was a decrease of 25 deaths per quarter, or approximately 600 fewer deaths (62% reduction). There was little change observed in deaths involving other analgesics, except for an increase in oxycodone poisonings, although the numbers were small. It is important to note that this study only focused on deaths involving single drugs, and we were unable to assess changes in deaths involving prescribed morphine.

In conclusion, the withdrawal of co-proxamol in the UK resulted in a significant reduction in poisoning deaths associated with this drug, without a notable increase in deaths involving other analgesics.

title: Apolipoprotein E genotype and concussion in college athletes.
text: The objective of this study was to examine the relationship between certain variations in the apolipoprotein E (APOE) gene (E2, C/T Arg158Cys; E4, T/C Cys112Arg; and promoter, g-219t) and the occurrence of concussions in college athletes. The hypothesis was that individuals carrying one or more rare alleles of APOE, as assessed in this study, would be more likely to have a history of one or more concussions. This was a cross-sectional study conducted at university athletic facilities, involving 196 male football players and female soccer players who volunteered to participate. The participants completed a written questionnaire about their concussion history and provided saliva samples for genetic testing. The main outcome measures were self-reported documented concussions and the presence of rare APOE genotypes (E2, E4, promoter). The results showed a significant association between carrying all rare APOE alleles and having a previous concussion. Additionally, there was a significant association between carrying the minor allele of the APOE promoter and experiencing two or more concussions. In conclusion, individuals carrying all three rare APOE alleles assessed in this study were nearly ten times more likely to report a previous concussion and may be at a higher risk for concussions compared to non-carriers. Carriers of the minor allele of the APOE promoter were 8.4 times more likely to report multiple concussions and may also be at a higher risk for multiple concussions. Further research with larger sample sizes of individuals with multiple concussions and carriers of multiple rare APOE alleles is recommended.

title: Plasma soluble corin and N-terminal pro-atrial natriuretic peptide levels in pregnancy induced hypertension.
text:
The objective of this study was to investigate the role of salt and water retention in the development of pregnancy induced hypertension. Specifically, we aimed to measure the levels of the proenzyme convertase corin, which is responsible for converting pro-atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) to active ANP, in the plasma of hypertensive pregnant women. 

We compared sixty pregnant women with pregnancy induced hypertension in their second and third trimesters to twenty-eight healthy pregnant women in the same gestational period. We collected urine and plasma samples from both groups to analyze various biochemical parameters. Using enzyme immunoassays, we determined the levels of plasma soluble corin and N-terminal (NT) pro-ANP (1-98) in both groups. 

The results showed that the mean value of plasma soluble corin was significantly higher in the patient group compared to the control group. Additionally, when we divided the patient group based on blood pressure, we found that the mean value of plasma NT pro-ANP was significantly higher in the group with blood pressure of 140/90mmHg or higher compared to the group with blood pressure below 140/90mmHg and the control group. 

In conclusion, the elevated levels of plasma soluble corin and NT pro-ANP in hypertensive pregnant women, especially those with blood pressure of 140/90mmHg or higher, suggest a potential defect in ANP receptor/post receptor signaling. This defect may contribute to the development and worsening of pregnancy induced hypertension.

title: GATA-4 and GATA-6 modulate tissue-specific transcription of the human gene for P450c17 by direct interaction with Sp1.
text: The enzyme Cytochrome P450c17 is responsible for catalyzing the activities of steroidogenic 17alpha-hydroxylase and 17,20 lyase. The expression of the P450c17 gene is dependent on cAMP, specific to certain tissues, programmed during development, and varies among different species. In human NCI-H295A adrenal cells, the binding of Sp1, Sp3, and NF1-C to the first 227 base pairs of the 5'flanking DNA (-227/LUC) is crucial for the basal transcription. However, human placental JEG-3 cells contain Sp1, Sp3, and NF1, but do not express -227/LUC, even when transfected with a vector expressing steroidogenic factor 1 (SF-1). This suggests that other factors are necessary for the basal expression of P450c17. Through Deoxyribonuclease I footprinting and EMSAs, a GATA consensus site at -64/-58 and an SF-1 site at -58/-50 were identified. RT-PCR analysis revealed the presence of GATA-4, GATA-6, and SF-1 in NCI-H295A cells, while GATA-2 and GATA-3 were found in JEG-3 cells, but not GATA-4, GATA-6, or SF-1. Cotransfection experiments showed that the activation of -227/LUC in JEG-3 cells required the presence of either GATA-4 or GATA-6, but not GATA-2 or GATA-3, with or without SF-1. Surprisingly, mutation of the GATA binding site increased the activity induced by GATA-4 or GATA-6, while mutation of the Sp1/Sp3 site decreased it. Additionally, promoter constructs containing the GATA site, but excluding the Sp1/Sp3 site at -196/-188, were not activated by GATA-4 or GATA-6, suggesting an interaction between Sp1/Sp3 and GATA-4 or GATA-6. Further experiments involving glutathione-S-transferase pull-down and coimmunoprecipitation confirmed the interaction between GATA-4 or GATA-6 and Sp1, but not Sp3. Chromatin immunoprecipitation assays confirmed that this interaction occurred at the Sp site in the P450c17 promoter in NCI-H295A cells. Demethylation with 5-aza-2-deoxycytidine allowed JEG-3 cells to express endogenous P450c17, SF-1, GATA-4, GATA-6, and transfected -227/LUC. Therefore, it can be concluded that the regulation of P450c17 expression in adrenal NCI-H295A cells involves the cooperation of GATA-4 or GATA-6 and Sp1, while methylation of P450c17, GATA-4, and GATA-6 silences the expression of P450c17 in placental JEG-3 cells.

title: Performance of an abbreviated version of the Lubben Social Network Scale among three European community-dwelling older adult populations.
text:
The purpose of this study is to evaluate the effectiveness of a shortened version of the Lubben Social Network Scale (LSNS-6) in assessing social networks and social supports, as well as identifying social isolation in older individuals. The study is conducted across three European countries and aims to determine clinical cut-points for identifying those at risk for social isolation based on the concept of lack of redundancy of social ties. 

The results of the study show that the LSNS-6 and its subscales (Family and Friends) have high levels of internal consistency, stable factor structures, and strong correlations with criterion variables across all three samples. The proposed clinical cut-points demonstrate good convergent validity and identify a significant percentage of respondents at risk for social isolation in each country. 

Based on these findings, it is recommended that abbreviated scales like the LSNS-6 be included in the practice protocols of gerontological practitioners. Screening older individuals using the LSNS-6 provides quantitative information about their family and friendship connections and helps identify those at higher risk for social isolation who may benefit from further assessment and targeted interventions.

title: The PneuCarriage Project: A Multi-Centre Comparative Study to Identify the Best Serotyping Methods for Examining Pneumococcal Carriage in Vaccine Evaluation Studies
text:
The pneumococcus is a diverse pathogen that primarily resides in the nasopharynx. There are over 90 different serotypes of the pneumococcus, and it is common for individuals to carry multiple serotypes. Understanding pneumococcal carriage is crucial for assessing the effectiveness of pneumococcal vaccines. However, traditional serotyping methods are cumbersome and inadequate for detecting multiple serotype carriage. Additionally, there is limited data comparing the new methods that have been developed in the past decade.

To address this, we initiated the PneuCarriage project, a large-scale international study aimed at identifying the best pneumococcal serotyping methods for carriage studies. We distributed reference sample sets to 15 research groups for blinded testing. These groups used twenty different serotyping methods to test 81 laboratory-prepared samples that were spiked with pneumococcus. The top five performing methods were then used to test 260 nasopharyngeal samples collected from children in six countries with a high burden of pneumococcal disease.

We determined the sensitivity and positive predictive value (PPV) of the test methods compared to the reference method, which involved traditional serotyping of over 100 colonies from each sample. The overall sensitivity of the alternate serotyping methods ranged from 1% to 99%, while the PPV ranged from 8% to 100% when testing the spiked samples. Fifteen methods had a sensitivity of at least 70% to detect the dominant serotype, while only eight methods had a sensitivity of at least 70% to detect minor serotypes. 

For the field samples, the overall sensitivity ranged from 74.2% to 95.8%, and the PPV ranged from 82.2% to 96.4%. The reference method had a sensitivity of 93.8% and a PPV of 99.6%. The microarray method had the highest sensitivity (95.8%) and a high PPV (93.7%). It is important to note that not all available alternative serotyping methods were included in this study, which is a limitation.

In conclusion, most methods were able to detect the dominant serotype in a sample, but many performed poorly in detecting minor serotype populations. The microarray method, which involved a culture amplification step, was the top-performing method. The results from this comprehensive evaluation will provide valuable insights for future vaccine evaluation and impact studies, particularly in low-income settings where the burden of pneumococcal disease remains high.

title: Ribosome-Mediated Specificity in Hox mRNA Translation and Vertebrate Tissue Patterning
text: In the past, the ribosome was seen as a complex ribozyme that played a constant role in mRNA translation, rather than having regulatory capabilities. However, we have now discovered mutations in the Ribosomal Protein L38 (Rpl38) gene in mice that result in tissue-specific patterning defects, particularly affecting the axial skeleton. Interestingly, these mutations do not affect overall protein synthesis, but instead disrupt the translation of a specific group of Homeobox mRNAs. Our findings indicate that RPL38 acts as a regulatory component of the ribosome, facilitating the formation of 80S complexes on these specific mRNAs to control their translation. We also observed that Rpl38 expression is highly concentrated in the regions of the embryo where these defects occur. Surprisingly, when we screened for the expression of other ribosomal proteins (RPs), we found that their expression is dynamically regulated in the vertebrate embryo. These discoveries suggest that RP activity may be tightly regulated to add a new level of specificity in the control of gene expression and mammalian development.

title: Growth and invasion of human melanomas in human skin grafted to immunodeficient mice.
text: A model of human melanoma was created by injecting malignant cells into human skin that had been grafted onto nude and SCID mice. The melanoma cells grew and spread within the human skin grafts in distinct patterns. In three out of six cases, the melanomas formed multiple nodules and infiltrated the grafts without causing significant changes in the dermis. In the other cases, the melanoma cells invaded the dermis along collagen fibers, accompanied by noticeable endothelial vessels. On the other hand, when melanoma cells were injected into mouse skin, they formed diffuse nodules that did not invade the murine dermis. In the human skin grafts, the melanoma cells stimulated the growth of human blood vessels, while murine vessels were only present at the edges of the grafts. The tumor cells invaded the human vessels, and four out of seven cell lines metastasized to the lungs. These findings suggest that this model can be used to study the interactions between normal and malignant human cells in a live setting.

title: Myeloperoxidase: friend and foe.
text: Neutrophils, also known as neutrophilic polymorphonuclear leukocytes, have a primary function of phagocytosis and destruction of microorganisms. When opsonins, such as complement and/or antibody, coat the microorganisms, they bind to specific receptors on the surface of the neutrophil. This leads to the cell membrane invaginating and incorporating the microorganism into an intracellular phagosome. This process is accompanied by an increase in oxygen consumption, with most, if not all, of the extra oxygen being converted into highly reactive oxygen species. Additionally, the cytoplasmic granules release their contents into the phagosome, resulting in the death of the ingested microorganism. One of the antimicrobial systems formed in the phagosome includes myeloperoxidase (MPO), which is released during the degranulation process, along with hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) produced by the respiratory burst, and a halide, particularly chloride. The initial product of this MPO-H2O2-chloride system is hypochlorous acid, and subsequent formation of chlorine, chloramines, hydroxyl radicals, singlet oxygen, and ozone has been suggested. These toxic agents can also be released outside the cell, potentially causing damage to normal tissue and contributing to disease pathogenesis. This review will discuss the sources of H2O2 for the MPO-H2O2-halide system, the toxic products of the MPO system, the evidence supporting MPO's involvement in neutrophil microbicidal activity, the presence of MPO-independent antimicrobial systems, and the role of the MPO system in tissue injury. Overall, it is concluded that the MPO system plays a significant role in the microbicidal activity of phagocytes.

title: Role of microsomal prostaglandin E synthase-1 in the facilitation of angiogenesis and the healing of gastric ulcers.
text: Understanding the role of PGE synthases (PGESs) in vivo is crucial due to the significance of prostaglandin E(2) in various pathophysiological events. However, there is currently no information on the functional relevance of microsomal PGES-1 (mPGES-1) in the healing processes of gastric ulcers or angiogenesis, which is essential for healing. This study aimed to investigate whether mPGES-1 plays a role in gastric ulcer healing and angiogenesis using mPGES-1 knockout mice (mPGES-1 KO mice) and their wild-type (WT) counterparts. Gastric ulcers were induced by applying 100% acetic acid to the serosal surface, and the ulcer areas were measured. The expression of mPGES-1 and cyclooxygenase-2 was induced in the granulation tissues compared to normal stomach tissues. The healing of acetic acid-induced ulcers was significantly delayed in mPGES-1 KO mice compared to WT mice. This delay was accompanied by reduced angiogenesis in the ulcer granulation tissues, as indicated by lower CD31 mRNA levels determined by real-time PCR and decreased microvessel density. The mRNA levels of proangiogenic growth factors, such as transforming growth factor-β, basic fibroblast growth factor, and connective tissue growth factor, were also reduced in mPGES-1 KO mice compared to WT mice. These findings suggest that mPGES-1 plays a role in enhancing ulcer healing and angiogenesis, and caution should be exercised when using selective mPGES-1 inhibitors in patients with gastric ulcers.

title: Echocardiographic Evidence of Innate Aortopathy in the Human Intracranial Aneurysm
text:
The prevalence of intracranial aneurysm (IA) is higher in patients with coarctation of the aorta or bicuspid aortic valve compared to the general population, suggesting a connection between IA and aortopathy. In this study, we examined the size of the aortic root dimension (ARD) in patients with IA to investigate this possibility. 

Between January 2008 and December 2010, we enrolled 260 consecutive patients with IA who were admitted to our institution for coil embolization or acute stroke management and also underwent echocardiography. Our hypothesis was that patients with large, ruptured, or multiple IAs are more likely to have co-existing aortopathy, as indicated by ARD, compared to patients with small, isolated, unruptured IAs. We classified patients aged <55 years with at least one ruptured aneurysm, an aneurysm ≥7 mm in size, or multiple aneurysms as the eccentric group, while the remaining patients were classified as the non-eccentric group. We compared the clinical, angiographic, and echocardiographic findings of the two groups. 

The results showed that ARD was significantly larger in the eccentric group compared to the non-eccentric group (P = 0.049), and this difference was confirmed by multivariable analysis (P = 0.02). Subgroup analysis of patients aged <55 years also showed a similar result for ARD (P = 0.03), while hypertension was more associated with the non-eccentric group (P = 0.01). Furthermore, after adjusting for age, sex, weight, ARD, smoking status, and number of aneurysms, height was inversely related to aneurysm size (P = 0.004). 

In conclusion, a certain group of IA patients exhibit a common intrinsic wall defect associated with aortopathy. This phenomenon may be attributed to a shared neural crest cell origin.

title: Aortic and large artery compliance in end-stage renal failure.
text:
The study measured pulse wave velocity (PWV) in the aorta, right leg, and arm of 90 control subjects (CS) and 92 hemodialysis patients (HD) who were of the same age and had the same mean arterial pressure (MAP). Blood chemistry, including blood lipids, and echographic dimensions of the aorta were also measured in all participants. The presence of aortic calcification was assessed using abdominal X-ray and echography.

The results showed that while femoral and brachial PWV were slightly increased in HD compared to CS (P < 0.05), aortic PWV was significantly higher in HD (1113 +/- 319 cm/sec) compared to CS (965 +/- 216 cm/sec; P = 0.0016). Aortic diameters were also larger in HD, both at the root of the aorta (32.7 +/- 4 vs. 28.2 +/- 2.8 mm; P < 0.0001) and aortic bifurcation (16.9 +/- 3.1 vs. 14.6 +/- 2.2 mm; P < 0.0001).

Although the MAP was similar in HD (109.9 +/- 19.3 mm Hg) and CS (110.2 +/- 17.2 mm Hg), the pulse pressure was significantly higher in HD patients (76.6 +/- 23.7 vs. 63.9 +/- 22 mm Hg; P = 0.007). In both populations, aortic PWV was found to increase with age (P < 0.0001) and MAP (P < 0.0001). The presence of aortic calcification showed only a weak relationship with the increase in aortic PWV (P = 0.050 in CS and P = 0.069 in HD).

Based on these findings, it can be concluded that aortic wall compliance is decreased in HD, leading to an increase in the pulsatile component of arterial pressure.

title: The DNA polymerase λ is required for the repair of non-compatible DNA double strand breaks by NHEJ in mammalian cells
text: The cellular function of DNA polymerase lambda (polλ) is not yet fully understood. However, our research demonstrates that polλ plays a role in repairing DNA double strand breaks (DSB) through a process called non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) in mammalian cells. We observed that when a catalytically inactive form of polλ (polλDN) is expressed, the frequency of NHEJ events in response to I-Sce-I-induced DSB decreases. In contrast, inactivated forms of polβ and polμ, which are similar to polλ, do not have the same effect. Specifically, only events that require DNA end processing before ligation are affected, resulting in large deletions near the induced DSB. Additionally, cells expressing polλDN show increased sensitivity and genomic instability when exposed to ionizing radiation, similar to cells with defective NHEJ. These findings suggest that polλ is necessary for repairing a specific subset of DSB in genomic DNA, contributing to the maintenance of genetic stability through the NHEJ pathway.

title: Angina with "normal" coronary arteries: sex differences in outcomes.
text:
BACKGROUND Numerous studies have shown that women with nonobstructive coronary disease experience a high rate of subsequent investigations, rehospitalizations for recurrent chest pain, and repeat coronary angiography. However, it remains unclear whether this finding is specific to women. Therefore, we conducted a study to evaluate the differences between men and women in terms of rehospitalization for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or chest pain in patients with "angiographically normal" coronaries.

METHODS We conducted a retrospective cohort study using prospectively collected angiographic and clinical data from all patients in British Columbia, Canada, who underwent their first cardiac catheterization due to suspected ischemic heart disease but had angiographically normal coronaries.

RESULTS Out of 32,856 patients, 7.1% of men and 23.3% of women had angiographically normal coronaries, indicating a significant difference (P < .001). Among patients with angiographically normal coronaries, women were older and more likely to have hypertension, prior stroke, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and peripheral vascular disease compared to men. However, the severity of angina, as measured by the Canadian Cardiovascular Society class, did not differ between the sexes. Within one year, 1.0% of patients died (19 women, 18 men, P = .27), and 0.6% experienced a stroke (13 women, 9 men, P = .91). The readmission rate to the hospital for ACS or chest pain requiring catheterization was significantly higher in women compared to men (adjusted odds ratio 4.06; 95% confidence interval 1.15-14.31).

CONCLUSIONS In a contemporary, population-based cohort undergoing cardiac catheterization for suspected ischemia, women with angiographically normal coronaries were more than four times as likely as men to be readmitted to the hospital for ACS or chest pain within 180 days. This sex difference has important social and economic implications and suggests that traditional diagnostic methods may not be optimal for women.

title: Keratin-dependent regulation of Aire and gene expression in skin tumor keratinocytes
text: The expression of keratin 17 (K17), an intermediate filament protein, is significantly increased in inflammatory skin diseases and various tumors that originate in stratified and pseudostratified epithelia. Our study reveals that autoimmune regulator (Aire), a transcriptional regulator, is induced in human and mouse tumor keratinocytes in a K17-dependent manner. Aire is crucial for the timely onset of Gli2-induced skin tumorigenesis in mice. The induction of Aire mRNA in keratinocytes relies on the functional interaction between K17 and the heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein hnRNP K. Additionally, K17 and Aire protein colocalize in the nucleus of tumor-prone keratinocytes. Both factors are bound to specific promoter regions that contain an NF-κB consensus sequence in a subset of proinflammatory genes that are dependent on K17 and Aire. These findings provide novel insights into the functions of keratin intermediate filaments and Aire, and offer a molecular explanation for the K17-dependent amplification of inflammatory and immune responses in diseased epithelia.

title: Flow-Dependent Regulation of Kruppel-Like Factor 2 Is Mediated by MicroRNA-92a.
text:
BACKGROUND: The transcription factor Krüppel-like factor 2 (KLF2) plays a crucial role in maintaining endothelial function and is upregulated by atheroprotective flow. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are small noncoding RNAs that regulate gene expression posttranscriptionally. In this study, we investigated the role of miRNAs, specifically miR-92a, in the regulation of atheroprotective flow-induced KLF2.
