Our findings suggest that the ability of PcG proteins to compact chromatin in vitro can be determined by the presence of domains with high positive charge, and that this highly charged region is conserved among PRC1 components across various species. These results provide additional evidence for the hypothesis that chromatin compaction is a crucial aspect of PcG function.

title: Angiopoietin-like proteins stimulate ex vivo expansion of hematopoietic stem cells
text: The successful expansion of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) outside of the body would greatly benefit disease treatment and our understanding of stem cell biology. In this study, we used microarray studies to identify specific proteins expressed by HSC-supportive mouse fetal liver CD3+ cells. These proteins, angiopoietin-like 2 (Angptl2) and angiopoietin-like 3 (Angptl3), were found to be present. By culturing highly enriched HSCs in the presence of Angptl2 or Angptl3, along with other growth factors, we observed a significant increase in the number of long-term HSCs. Reconstitution analysis showed a 24- or 30-fold net expansion after 10 days of culture. Additionally, the coiled-coil domain of Angptl2 was found to stimulate HSC expansion. Other proteins, such as angiopoietin-like 5, angiopoietin-like 7, and microfibril-associated glycoprotein 4, also supported HSC expansion in culture.

title: Balancing co-stimulation and inhibition with BTLA and HVEM
text: The interaction between B- and T-lymphocyte attenuator (BTLA) and herpesvirus-entry mediator (HVEM) is unique because it is the only interaction that directly connects these two families of receptors. BTLA is an inhibitory receptor with an extracellular domain that belongs to the immunoglobulin superfamily, while HVEM is a co-stimulatory tumour-necrosis factor receptor. This interaction has raised questions about how receptors from different families can interact and what signaling events may occur as a result. Recent studies have shown that when HVEM engages with its natural ligand (LIGHT) from the tumour-necrosis factor family, it triggers a strong immune response. On the other hand, HVEM interactions with BTLA negatively regulate T-cell responses.

title: Lin28b is sufficient to drive liver cancer and necessary for its maintenance in murine models.
text: Lin28a/b are proteins that bind to RNA and have an impact on the maintenance of stem cells, metabolism, and the development of cancer. In aggressive and poorly differentiated cancers, Lin28 is often overexpressed, but its exact role in the initiation and maintenance of tumors is still uncertain. Our study reveals that overexpression of LIN28B alone is enough to start the development of hepatoblastoma and hepatocellular carcinoma in mice. We also observed increased levels of Lin28b in MYC-driven hepatoblastomas, and when Lin28a/b was specifically deleted in the liver, it resulted in reduced tumor growth, delayed onset, and increased survival. Both intravenous siRNA targeting Lin28b and conditional deletion of Lin28b led to decreased tumor growth and improved survival. Additionally, the upregulation of Igf2bp proteins, particularly Igf2bp3, was found to be necessary for promoting growth in the presence of LIN28B overexpression. Therefore, our findings from various mouse models demonstrate that Lin28b is not only sufficient to initiate liver cancer but also essential for its maintenance.

title: Nanoenzymology of the 20S proteasome: proteasomal actions are controlled by the allosteric transition.
text:
The proteasome is a crucial assembly in eukaryotic cells that plays a vital role in their physiology. We have a good understanding of both the structure and enzymatic properties of the 20S proteasome. However, despite long-standing interest, it has been challenging to integrate the structural and functional aspects of the proteasome into a comprehensive model that explains its enzymatic actions.

Recently, we utilized tapping mode atomic force microscopy (AFM) in a liquid environment to investigate the proteasome. Our findings revealed that the alpha-rings of the proteasome, when imaged from a top-view position, repeatedly transitioned between open and closed conformations. This switching mechanism appeared to regulate access to the central channel.

In addition, we used AFM to examine the proteasome from a side-view position and discovered that the molecules adopted two stable conformations. These conformations were classified as either barrel-like or cylinder-like in shape. The prevalence of each conformation depended on the interactions with ligands. Similar to the closed molecules in the top view, the barrel-like conformers were more abundant in control or inhibited molecules. On the other hand, the cylinder-like conformers and open molecules were more prevalent when the proteasome was observed in the presence of peptide substrates.

Based on these findings, we have developed a two-state model of allosteric transitions to explain the dynamic nature of the proteasomal structure. This model provides a better understanding of the observed properties of the 20S molecule and lays the groundwork for further investigations into the structural dynamics of the proteasome.

title: Changes in plasma copeptin, the c-terminal portion of arginine vasopressin during water deprivation and excess in healthy subjects.
text: The measurement of arginine vasopressin (AVP) can be difficult due to its instability and short half-life. However, copeptin, a more stable peptide derived from the same precursor as AVP, has been found to be a useful indicator of AVP concentration in critically ill patients. The objective of this study was to assess the clinical usefulness of copeptin as a new marker for blood volume and plasma osmolality disorders. The study was conducted in a university hospital and involved 24 healthy adults. Three techniques were used to manipulate plasma osmolality and/or volume, and the results were compared to control studies. Water deprivation led to weight loss, increased plasma osmolality, and elevated copeptin levels. Hypertonic saline infusion and thirsting also resulted in increased copeptin levels. Conversely, hypotonic saline infusion caused a decrease in copeptin levels. These findings suggest that copeptin exhibits similar changes to AVP during water imbalance and could serve as a reliable substitute for measuring AVP levels in clinical practice.

title: Propagation and recovery of intact, infectious Epstein-Barr virus from prokaryotic to human cells.
text: Due to the large size of their genomes, current methods make it challenging to genetically alter herpesviruses. To overcome this obstacle, we have developed a system that enables the cloning of any gamma-herpesvirus onto an F factor-derived plasmid in Escherichia coli. By utilizing this approach, we successfully established immortalized B cell lines using recombinant Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), confirming that the F factor-cloned EBV genome possesses all the characteristics of the wild-type EBV. This experimental technique allows for the genetic analysis of all EBV functions, as E. coli permits any desired genetic modification. Additionally, it is now possible to generate attenuated EBV strains in vitro, facilitating the design of vaccine strains. By incorporating genes for hygromycin resistance and green fluorescent protein into the E. coli cloned EBV genome, we can now investigate the target cells of EBV beyond B lymphocytes, which remains an unanswered question.

title: Chemosensitivity profile assay of circulating cancer cells: prognostic and predictive value in epithelial tumors.
text: The CellSearch technology's ability to detect circulating tumor cells (CTCs) in metastatic breast cancer has raised questions about the significance of this information. We hypothesized that the drug-resistance profile of CTCs could potentially predict how cancer patients would respond to chemotherapy, making it a useful tool for patient selection. To test this, we enrolled 100 patients diagnosed with carcinoma in a prospective trial. CTCs were isolated from their peripheral blood, and positive samples were analyzed for the expression of genes associated with resistance to anticancer drugs. We then correlated the drug-resistance profile with disease-free survival (DFS) for patients in the adjuvant setting and time to progression (TTP) for metastatic patients over a 24-month follow-up period. Objective response correlation was also considered as a secondary endpoint. We found that 51% of patients tested positive for CTCs, while all blood samples from healthy donors were negative. The drug-resistance profile showed a significant correlation with both DFS and TTP (p < 0.001 for both). The test demonstrated a sensitivity of 98% in predicting treatment response and a specificity of 100%, as no samples from healthy subjects showed the presence of CTCs. The positive and negative predictive values were determined to be 96.5% and 100%, respectively. We discovered a drug-resistance profile of CTCs that can predict chemotherapy response, regardless of tumor type or disease stage. This finding could be a crucial first step towards personalized chemotherapy for cancer patients.

title: Trends in heart failure incidence and survival in a community-based population.
text: The investigation of the heart failure epidemic is still incomplete, and there is limited data on the occurrence, survival rates, and sex-specific trends in community populations. The objective of this study was to examine whether the incidence of heart failure has decreased and if survival rates after diagnosis have improved over time, with potential differences between sexes. This population-based cohort study utilized the resources of the Rochester Epidemiology Project in Olmsted County, Minnesota. The study included 4,537 residents of Olmsted County (57% women; average age of 74 years) who were diagnosed with heart failure between 1979 and 2000. The diagnosis was validated using the Framingham criteria and clinical criteria. The main outcomes measured were the occurrence of heart failure and survival rates after diagnosis. The results showed that the occurrence of heart failure was higher in men (378 per 100,000 individuals; 95% confidence interval [CI], 361-395 for men; 289 per 100,000 individuals; 95% CI, 277-300 for women) and did not change over time for either men or women. After an average follow-up period of 4.2 years (ranging from 0 to 23.8 years), there were 3,347 deaths, including 1,930 among women and 1,417 among men. Survival rates after heart failure diagnosis were worse for men compared to women (relative risk, 1.33; 95% CI, 1.24-1.43), but overall, there was an improvement over time (5-year age-adjusted survival rates of 43% in 1979-1984 compared to 52% in 1996-2000, P<.001). However, men and younger individuals experienced greater improvements in survival rates, while women and elderly individuals saw less or no improvement. In conclusion, this cohort study in a community setting found that the occurrence of heart failure did not decrease over a 20-year period, but survival rates after diagnosis increased overall, with less improvement observed among women and elderly individuals.

title: Doxycycline induces apoptosis in PANC-1 pancreatic cancer cells.
text:
BACKGROUND: The mechanism behind the cytotoxic effects of doxycycline on mammalian tumor cells, specifically in terms of cell proliferation, remains unclear.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a study to investigate the antitumor effect of doxycycline on a human pancreatic cancer cell line called PANC-1. Additionally, we examined the impact of doxycycline on the expression of interleukin (IL)-8, a potent proangiogenic factor.

RESULTS: At concentrations exceeding 20 microg/ml, doxycycline demonstrated cytotoxic effects on PANC-1 cells, leading to G(1)-S cell cycle arrest and DNA fragmentation. We consistently observed the activation of p53, p21, and Fas/FasL-cascade-related genes, along with a decrease in the expression of Bcl-xL and Mcl-1. Furthermore, doxycycline at a non-cytotoxic level of 5 microg/ml suppressed both endogenous and paclitaxel-induced IL-8 expression. In a mouse xenograft model, doxycycline treatment resulted in an 80% reduction in tumor growth.

CONCLUSION: Based on these findings, it can be concluded that doxycycline exerts its antitumor effects by activating proapoptotic genes, inhibiting IL-8 expression, and suppressing antiapoptotic genes.

title: Orientationally invariant indices of axon diameter and density from diffusion MRI.
text:
In this study, we propose and evaluate a method for imaging orientationally invariant indices of axon diameter and density in white matter using diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). These indices have the potential to provide more specific information about the microstructure of white matter compared to standard indices obtained from diffusion tensor imaging. The use of orientationally invariant indices allows for their combination with tractography, opening up new possibilities for mapping brain connectivity and quantifying disease processes.

Our technique involves a four-compartment tissue model combined with an optimized multishell high-angular-resolution pulsed-gradient-spin-echo acquisition. We tested the method using simulation, fixed monkey brains with a preclinical scanner, and live human brains with a clinical 3T scanner. The acquisition of human data took approximately one hour.

The simulation experiments demonstrated that both the monkey and human protocols were able to distinguish distributions of axon diameters that naturally occur in white matter. We compared the axon diameter index with the mean axon diameter weighted by axon volume. Although the index differed from this mean and was dependent on the protocol, there was a good correlation for the monkey protocol and a weaker but still discernible correlation for the human protocol. The lower sensitivity to smaller axons in the human protocol was due to greater diffusivity and lower gradient strength.

Maps of axon diameter and density indices obtained from the monkey and human data in the corpus callosum and corticospinal tract reflected known trends observed in histology. This study demonstrated, for the first time, the orientationally invariant sensitivity to natural axon diameter distributions using both specialist and clinical hardware.

These findings highlight the need for further refinement, validation, and evaluation of the precise nature of the indices and the potential influence of confounding factors.

title: IFI16 and cGAS cooperate in the activation of STING during DNA sensing in human keratinocytes
text: During infection, human cells can detect the presence of foreign DNA through a receptor called cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS), which produces a signaling molecule called cyclic GMP-AMP (cGAMP). While other potential DNA receptors have been identified, it remains unclear whether their functions overlap, are specific to certain tissues, or are integrated into the cGAS-cGAMP pathway. In this study, we demonstrate that a protein called interferon-γ inducible protein 16 (IFI16) works together with cGAS in DNA sensing in human keratinocytes. Both cGAS and IFI16 are necessary for the complete activation of the innate immune response against foreign DNA and DNA viruses. Additionally, IFI16 is essential for the activation of STING, a protein involved in immune response, by cGAMP. IFI16 interacts with STING to facilitate its phosphorylation and movement within the cell. Our findings suggest that IFI16 and cGAS collaborate to prevent the inadvertent activation of the type I interferon response.

title: Oncostatic effects of the indole melatonin and expression of its cytosolic and nuclear receptors in cultured human melanoma cell lines.
text: In vitro and in vivo studies have demonstrated that melatonin has inhibitory effects on malignant melanoma. We conducted a study to investigate the growth-suppressing effects of melatonin on four melanoma cell lines (SBCE2, WM-98, WM-164, and SKMEL-188) that represent different growth stages and phenotypes. The melanoma cells were exposed to melatonin concentrations ranging from 10(-12) to 10(-3) M, and their proliferation and clonogenicity were assessed after 12 hours and 14 days, respectively. Additionally, we examined the expression of cytosolic quinone oxidoreductases NQO1, NQO2 (also known as MT3 receptor), and nuclear receptor RORalpha using RT-PCR. Pharmacological concentrations of melatonin (10(-3) to 10(-7) M) suppressed proliferation in all melanoma cell lines. In SKMEL-188 cells cultured in serum-free media, low concentrations of melatonin (10(-12) to 10(-10) M) also slightly reduced proliferation. The effects of pharmacological doses of melatonin were confirmed in the clonogenic assay. NQO1 expression was detected in all cell lines, while NQO2 and nuclear receptor RORalpha, including its isoform RORalpha4, were only present in SBCE2, WM-164, and WM-98. Therefore, melatonin exhibited differential suppression of proliferation in melanoma cell lines with varying behavior. The intensity of the inhibitory response to melatonin may be associated with the specific pattern of melatonin cellular receptors and cytosolic binding protein expression in each cell line.

title: Lysosomal localization of TRPML3 depends on TRPML2 and the mucolipidosis-associated protein TRPML1.
text:
Mucolipidosis type IV is a genetic disorder that affects the lysosomes and leads to severe neurodegeneration, achlorhydria, and visual impairments like corneal opacity and strabismus. The disease is caused by mutations in a specific type of protein called TRPML1, which belongs to a group of proteins known as transient receptor potential (TRP)-related cation channels. In addition to TRPML1, mammals also have two other TRPML proteins called TRPML2 and TRPML3. However, there is limited information about how these proteins interact with each other, where they are located within cells, and the mechanisms that control their movement.

In this study, we show that TRPML proteins can form both homo- and heteromultimers, meaning they can interact with other TRPML proteins of the same or different types. Furthermore, the presence of either TRPML1 or TRPML2 influences the distribution of TRPML3 within cells. Specifically, TRPML1 and TRPML2 are primarily found in lysosomes, while TRPML3 is mainly located in the endoplasmic reticulum. However, when TRPML3 is coexpressed with either TRPML1 or TRPML2, it is redirected to lysosomes. Similarly, when the targeting of TRPML1 and TRPML2 to lysosomes is disrupted, TRPML3 is also mislocalized. On the other hand, TRPML3 does not affect the localization of TRPML1 or TRPML2 in the endoplasmic reticulum. These findings suggest that there is a hierarchical relationship among the TRPML proteins, with TRPML1 and TRPML2 determining the localization of TRPML3, rather than the other way around.

title: Evolution of metastasis revealed by mutational landscapes of chemically induced skin cancers
text: The genetic makeup of human tumors is highly diverse, but we do not yet understand the factors that determine when and how subclones spread and metastasize. To shed light on this, we conducted whole-exome sequencing on 103 skin tumors from genetically diverse mice, including benign, malignant, and metastatic tumors. Our findings suggest that most metastases spread simultaneously from the primary tumor, supporting the idea that parallel evolution, rather than linear progression, is the main model of metastasis. We observed shared mutations between primary carcinomas and their metastases, which had the distinct A-to-T signature of the initiating carcinogen dimethylbenzanthracene. However, non-shared mutations were primarily G-to-T, a signature associated with oxidative stress. Interestingly, some carcinomas in the same host animal metastasized while others did not, indicating that there are intrinsic factors within the tumor that influence metastatic seeding. Additionally, we found that germline polymorphisms play a role in determining allele-specific mutations, and we identified specific somatic genetic alterations related to the initiation of carcinogenesis by Hras or Kras mutations. By using mouse tumors that mimic the genetic diversity seen in human cancers, we can gain insights into the clonal evolution of metastasis and develop realistic models for testing new therapies.

title: A specific inhibitor of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase, 2-(4-morpholinyl)-8-phenyl-4H-1-benzopyran-4-one (LY294002).
text: Phosphatidylinositol (PtdIns) 3-kinase is an enzyme that plays a role in transmitting growth factor signals by interacting with receptor and nonreceptor tyrosine kinases, such as the platelet-derived growth factor receptor. Inhibitors of PtdIns 3-kinase have the potential to enhance our understanding of the enzyme's function and regulatory mechanisms. Quercetin, a naturally occurring bioflavonoid, has previously been found to inhibit PtdIns 3-kinase with an IC50 of 1.3 microgram/ml (3.8 microM), specifically targeting the ATP-binding site of the kinase. Similar compounds to quercetin were examined as PtdIns 3-kinase inhibitors, with the most potent ones displaying IC50 values ranging from 1.7-8.4 micrograms/ml. On the other hand, genistein, a potent tyrosine kinase inhibitor from the isoflavone class, did not significantly inhibit PtdIns 3-kinase (IC50 > 30 micrograms/ml). Quercetin has also been shown to inhibit other PtdIns and protein kinases, leading to the evaluation of other chromones as PtdIns 3-kinase inhibitors while sparing PtdIns 4-kinase and selected protein kinases. One such compound, 2-(4-morpholinyl)-8-phenyl-4H-1-benzopyran-4-one (also known as 2-(4-morpholinyl)-8-phenylchromone, LY294002), completely and specifically abolished PtdIns 3-kinase activity (IC50 = 0.43 microgram/ml; 1.40 microM) without inhibiting PtdIns 4-kinase or tested protein and lipid kinases. Analogues of LY294002 demonstrated a highly selective structure-activity relationship, where even slight changes in structure resulted in significant decreases in inhibition. LY294002 was found to completely eliminate PtdIns 3-kinase activity in fMet-Leu-Phe-stimulated human neutrophils and inhibit the proliferation of smooth muscle cells in cultured rabbit aortic segments. Given the central role of PtdIns 3-kinase in growth factor signal transduction, the development of specific inhibitors against this kinase could be beneficial in treating proliferative diseases and shedding light on its biological role in cellular proliferation and growth factor response.

title: A simple two-step protocol for the purification of human pancreatic beta cells
text: We sought to develop a straightforward approach to isolate pure human beta cells, which would be valuable for various research purposes. However, the lack of specific surface antigens unique to beta cells has posed a significant challenge. Our method involved initially removing ductal cells by targeting their expression of carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9), followed by selectively isolating beta cells based on their expression of polysialic acid-neural cell adhesion molecule (PSA-NCAM). We examined the expression of CA19-9, NCAM, and PSA-NCAM in sections of adult human pancreas and in cultured primary endocrine and exocrine cells to determine their cell type-specific expression. After 4 days of suspension culture, dispersed human islet cells were purified in two steps using magnetic microbeads coupled with antibodies against CA19-9 and PSA-NCAM. NCAM expression was observed in both ducts and islets in the human pancreas, while PSA-NCAM immunoreactivity was only detected in islets. PSA-NCAM staining in dispersed cells revealed its expression in all endocrine cell types but not in duct cells. Purification of dispersed islet cells using PSA-NCAM microbeads alone did not completely eliminate contaminating duct cells. However, by employing CA19-9 microbeads to eliminate duct cells followed by positive sorting of PSA-NCAM-positive cells in five consecutive islet preparations, we achieved a purity of 90 to 98% for endocrine cells, with 89 to 97% being beta cells. In summary, we have developed a simple and reliable method to purify viable human pancreatic beta cells that are free from exocrine acini and ducts.

title: Prev | Table of Contents Reports Embryonic Stem Cell Lines Derived from Human
text: We have discovered human blastocyst-derived cell lines that possess certain characteristics. These cell lines have normal karyotypes, exhibit high levels of telomerase activity, and display specific cell surface markers that are typically found in primate embryonic stem cells but not in other early lineages. Even after undergoing undifferentiated proliferation in a laboratory setting for a period of 4 to 5 months, these cells still retain their ability to develop into various tissues derived from all three embryonic germ layers. These tissues include the gut epithelium (endoderm), cartilage, bone, smooth muscle, and striated muscle (mesoderm), as well as neural epithelium, embryonic ganglia, and stratified squamous epithelium (ectoderm). These cell lines hold great potential for applications in human developmental biology, drug discovery, and transplantation medicine.

title: Ascorbic-acid transporter Slc23a1 is essential for vitamin C transport into the brain and for perinatal survival
text: The only known purpose of ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is to prevent scurvy, likely because it helps stabilize collagen through hydroxylases that are necessary for post-translational modifications. We have successfully generated mice that lack the rat ascorbic-acid transporter Svct2 (also known as solute carrier family 23 member 1 or Slc23a1). When we examined cultured embryonic fibroblasts from these mice, we found that they took up less than 5% of the normal amount of ascorbic acid. Additionally, the blood and tissues of these mice had either undetectable or significantly reduced levels of ascorbic acid. When we supplemented pregnant female mice with ascorbic acid during pregnancy, it did not increase the levels of ascorbic acid in the blood of the Slc23a1-deficient fetuses. This suggests that Slc23a1 plays an important role in transporting ascorbic acid across the placenta. Shortly after birth, the Slc23a1-deficient mice died due to respiratory failure and brain hemorrhage within a few minutes. The lungs did not expand after birth, but the levels of surfactant protein B were normal. The brain hemorrhage cannot be attributed solely to scurvy, as the Slc23a1-deficient mice did not show any hemorrhage in other tissues and their skin had normal levels of 4-hydroxyproline despite low levels of ascorbic acid. In conclusion, Slc23a1 is necessary for the transport of ascorbic acid into various tissues and across the placenta. The absence of this transporter is lethal in newborn mice, revealing a previously unknown requirement for ascorbic acid during the perinatal period.

title: MVP-mediated exosomal sorting of miR-193a promotes colon cancer progression
text: Exosomes play a crucial role in intercellular communication, but little is known about their impact on the cells that release them. To address this, we investigated the expression profiles of exosomal miRNAs in primary mouse colon tumors, liver metastases of colon cancer, and normal colon tissues. We found that in advanced stages of the disease, exosomes contained higher levels of tumor suppressor miRNAs. Specifically, miR-193a was found to interact with a protein called major vault protein (MVP). When MVP was knocked out, miR-193a accumulated in the cells that released the exosomes instead of being encapsulated in the exosomes. This accumulation inhibited tumor progression. Additionally, miR-193a was found to cause cell cycle arrest and suppress cell proliferation by targeting a protein called Caprin1, which in turn upregulated Ccnd2 and c-Myc. In human colon cancer patients with advanced disease, circulating exosomal miR-193a levels were elevated. Overall, our findings demonstrate that the selective sorting of tumor suppressor miRNAs into exosomes by MVP promotes tumor progression.

title: Casual blood pressure and neurocognitive function in children with chronic kidney disease: a report of the children with chronic kidney disease cohort study.
text:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The objective of this study was to investigate the impact of elevated blood pressure (BP) on neurocognitive function in children with chronic kidney disease (CKD). Limited data exists on the potential contribution of hypertension to CKD-associated cognitive deficits in children.

DESIGN, SETTING, PARTICIPANTS, & MEASUREMENTS: This cross-sectional analysis examined the relationship between auscultatory BP and neurocognitive test performance in children aged 6 to 17 years enrolled in the Chronic Kidney Disease in Children (CKiD) project.

RESULTS: Out of 383 subjects, 132 (34%) had elevated BP (systolic BP and/or diastolic BP ≥90th percentile). Children with elevated BP had lower mean scores on the Wechsler Abbreviated Scales of Intelligence (WASI) Performance IQ compared to those with normal BP. The BP index, calculated as the subject's BP divided by the 95th percentile BP, showed an inverse correlation with Performance IQ score. After controlling for demographic and disease-related variables, the association between lower Performance IQ score and increased BP remained significant.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher BP was independently associated with decreased WASI Performance IQ scores in children with mild-to-moderate CKD.

title: Bone marrow failure and developmental delay caused by mutations in poly(A)-specific ribonuclease (PARN).
text:
BACKGROUND: The regulation of RNA function and fate is controlled by deadenylation. Poly(A)-specific ribonuclease (PARN) is an enzyme that removes the poly(A) tail from mRNAs and non-coding RNA. However, the biological significance of germline mutations in PARN remains poorly understood.

METHODS: In this study, we investigated mutations in PARN in patients exhibiting haematological and neurological symptoms. Through genomic, biochemical, and knockdown experiments in human marrow cells and zebrafish, we aimed to elucidate the role of PARN in the development of human disease.

RESULTS: We identified large monoallelic deletions in PARN in four patients who presented with developmental delay or mental illness. One patient, in particular, displayed a severe neurological phenotype characterized by central hypomyelination and bone marrow failure. This patient had an additional missense mutation on the non-deleted allele, resulting in significantly reduced PARN protein levels and deadenylation activity. Furthermore, cells from this patient exhibited impaired oligoadenylation of specific H/ACA box small nucleolar RNAs. Notably, PARN-deficient patient cells displayed shortened telomeres and an abnormal ribosome profile similar to those observed in certain variants of dyskeratosis congenita. Knockdown of PARN in human marrow cells and zebrafish further supported the causal link between PARN deficiency and the development of the human disease.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that large monoallelic mutations in PARN can lead to developmental and mental illness. Additionally, biallelic mutations in PARN can cause severe bone marrow failure and central hypomyelination.

title: The changing epidemiology of malaria in Ifakara Town, southern Tanzania.
text: Between 1995 and 2000, there were significant changes in the occurrence of malaria in Ifakara, a region in southern Tanzania. We conducted various studies involving children up to the age of 5 years, using both parasitological and clinical data, to document these changes. In the community-based cohort studies, we observed a shift towards older ages and a decrease in the prevalence of parasites. Additionally, the incidence of clinical malaria in infants who received a placebo decreased from 0.8 episodes per year in 1995 to 0.43 episodes per year in 2000. This represents a 53% reduction in incidence. On the other hand, there was an increase in the total number of malaria cases requiring hospitalization, with a shift towards older ages. However, despite these changes, the burden of malaria-related deaths remained highest among infants. We discuss how the use of current malaria control measures may have contributed to these changes in malaria epidemiology. It is important to note that hospital-based data may underestimate the impact of anemia on mortality in the community, where most pediatric deaths occur. Even in areas with low to moderate malaria transmission, targeting effective malaria control interventions towards infants could significantly reduce infant mortality caused by malaria.

title: MicroRNA-192 in diabetic kidney glomeruli and its function in TGF-beta-induced collagen expression via inhibition of E-box repressors.
text: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is characterized by the accumulation of certain proteins, such as collagen 1-alpha 1 and -2 (Col1a1 and -2), in the extracellular matrix. Transforming growth factor beta1 (TGF-beta) plays a crucial role in regulating these proteins and is found to be increased in mesangial cells (MC) in DN. Through microarray profiling, we discovered that TGF-beta not only increased the levels of Col1a2 mRNA in mouse MC (MMC), but also decreased the levels of an E-box repressor called deltaEF1. Treatment with TGF-beta or the use of short hairpin RNAs targeting deltaEF1 resulted in an increase in enhancer activity of upstream E-box elements in the Col1a2 gene. Additionally, TGF-beta reduced the expression of Smad-interacting protein 1 (SIP1), which is another E-box repressor similar to deltaEF1. Interestingly, we found that SIP1 is a target of microRNA-192 (miR-192), a highly expressed miR in the kidney. TGF-beta treatment or transfection with miR-192 led to a decrease in endogenous SIP1 expression and reporter activity of a SIP1 3' UTR-containing luciferase construct in MMC. Conversely, inhibition of miR-192 enhanced luciferase activity, confirming SIP1 as a target of miR-192. Furthermore, miR-192 worked together with deltaEF1 short hairpin RNAs to increase Col1a2 E-box-luc activity. Importantly, we observed that miR-192 levels were significantly increased in glomeruli isolated from streptozotocin-injected diabetic mice and diabetic db/db mice compared to nondiabetic controls, along with increased TGF-beta and Col1a2 levels. These findings reveal the role of miRs in the kidney and DN, as they control TGF-beta-induced Col1a2 expression by down-regulating E-box repressors.

title: Activation of PAR(2) receptors sensitizes primary afferents and causes leukocyte rolling and adherence in the rat knee joint.
text: The purpose of this study was to investigate the activation of PAR(2) receptors in the rat knee joint. The researchers examined PAR(2) activation in dorsal root ganglia (DRG) cells in the rat knee joint and conducted electrophysiological recordings from knee joint nerve fibers. They also observed leukocyte kinetics in the synovial vasculature upon PAR(2) activation. The study found that PAR(2) receptors were expressed in a significant percentage of DRG cells and that activating PAR(2) increased joint fiber firing rate and leukocyte rolling and adhesion. These effects were blocked by pre-treatment with selective antagonists for transient receptor potential vanilloid-1 (TRPV1) and neurokinin-1 (NK(1)) receptors. The researchers concluded that PAR(2) receptors play a role in acute inflammation in the knee joint through TRPV1- and NK(1)-dependent mechanisms involving neuronal sensitization and leukocyte trafficking.

title: Polyphosphate kinase 1, a central node in the stress response network of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, connects the two-component systems MprAB and SenX3-RegX3 and the extracytoplasmic function sigma factor, sigma E.
text:
In this study, we investigate the role of polyphosphate (poly P) metabolism in regulating the stress response in mycobacteria. Specifically, we focus on the regulatory architecture of a signal transduction system involving the SenX3-RegX3 two-component system (TCS), the sigma factor sigma E (SigE), and the poly P-synthesizing enzyme polyphosphate kinase 1 (PPK1).

We find that the ppk1 promoter of Mycobacterium tuberculosis is activated during phosphate starvation. However, this activation is diminished when an imperfect palindrome, which likely serves as a binding site for the response regulator RegX3, is deleted. We confirm the binding of phosphorylated RegX3 to this site through electrophoretic mobility shift assay.

Furthermore, we discover that the activity of the ppk1 promoter is abolished when a putative SigE binding site is deleted. Pull-down experiments using biotinylated DNA containing the SigE binding site confirm the likely binding of SigE to the ppk1 promoter. In vitro transcription experiments also support the involvement of SigE in ppk1 transcription.

Additionally, we observe that the overexpression of RseA (anti-SigE) reduces ppk1 expression during phosphate starvation, further supporting the role of SigE in ppk1 transcription. These findings suggest the presence of multiple positive-feedback loops in this signaling circuit, as we have previously shown that PPK1 can regulate sigE expression through the MprAB TCS.

Based on these regulatory elements and the sequestering effect of RseA, we propose that this architecture may contribute to bistability in the system, which could be a crucial factor in the persistence of M. tuberculosis.

title: Natural history of asymptomatic unruptured cerebral aneurysms evaluated at CT angiography: growth and rupture incidence and correlation with epidemiologic risk factors.
text: The purpose of this study was to examine the relationship between the size of aneurysms and epidemiologic risk factors, and their association with growth and rupture using computed tomographic (CT) angiography. The study followed patients with known asymptomatic unruptured intracerebral aneurysms over time, using CT angiographic examinations. Growth was defined as an increase in dimensions and volume by at least 5% using the ABC/2 method. Logistic regression analysis was used to analyze the associations between epidemiologic factors and aneurysm growth and rupture. The study included 165 patients with 258 aneurysms, with a mean follow-up time of 2.24 years. Of the 258 aneurysms, 46 (18%) grew larger. Spontaneous rupture occurred in four of the 228 (1.8%) intradural aneurysms with an average size of 6.2 mm. The risk of aneurysm rupture per patient-year was 2.4% with growth and 0.2% without growth. Growing aneurysms had a 12-fold higher risk of rupture. Tobacco smoking and initial size were independent predictors of growing aneurysms. These findings suggest that all patients with aneurysms, regardless of size, should undergo imaging follow-up. Aneurysm growth, size, and smoking were associated with an increased risk of rupture.

title: A search for the presence of the enteroviral capsid protein VP1 in pancreases of patients with Type 1 (insulin-dependent) diabetes and pancreases and hearts of infants who died of coxsackieviral myocarditis
text: A technique was developed using an antiserum raised to a recombinant coxsackie virus B3 capsid protein, VP1, to detect coxsackie B viruses in infected tissue culture cells that were fixed in formalin and embedded in paraffin. This technique was tested on autopsy heart and pancreas samples from 21 patients suspected to have died from acute coxsackievirus B myocarditis. In 12 out of 20 cases where the heart was available for study, cardiac myocytes were found to be positive for the VP1 protein. Additionally, insulitis was observed in the pancreas of seven of these cases, and all seven cases showed VP1 in the islet endocrine cells. VP1 was rarely found in the exocrine pancreas. Cells containing VP1 in the heart and pancreas typically exhibited signs of necrosis. However, autopsy pancreases from 88 patients who died from clinical presentation of Type 1 diabetes mellitus did not show any evidence of VP1 presence. The ongoing destruction of insulin-secreting B cells observed in the diabetic pancreas at the time of death is unlikely to be caused by a direct cytopathic effect of coxsackie B virus. Nevertheless, this study does not rule out the possibility that a persistent infection of B cells by a defective enterovirus could lead to their destruction through an autoimmune mechanism.

title: Direct reprogramming of mouse fibroblasts to cardiomyocyte-like cells using Yamanaka factors on engineered poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) hydrogels.
text: Direct reprogramming strategies allow for the rapid conversion of somatic cells into cardiomyocytes or cardiomyocyte-like cells without the need for pluripotent state transition. A recent study introduced a protocol that combines Yamanaka factor induction with pluripotency inhibition, followed by BMP4 treatment, to efficiently reprogram mouse fibroblasts into beating cardiomyocyte-like cells. However, the original study utilized Matrigel-coated tissue culture polystyrene (TCPS), a rigid material that also non-specifically absorbs serum proteins. To overcome this limitation, protein adsorption-resistant poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) materials can be modified to present specific concentrations of adhesion proteins or peptides, eliminating the unintended effects of non-specific protein adsorption. In this study, we present an improved protocol that incorporates custom-engineered materials. Initially, we replicated the Efe et al. protocol on Matrigel-coated TCPS, reprogramming adult mouse tail-tip fibroblasts (TTF) and mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEF) into cardiomyocyte-like cells that exhibited striated sarcomeric α-actinin staining, spontaneous calcium transients, and visible beating. Subsequently, we designed PEG hydrogels as culture substrates to enhance MEF adhesion through laminin and RGD-binding integrins. The utilization of PEG hydrogels resulted in improved proliferation and reprogramming efficiency, as evidenced by increased numbers and areas of beating patches, enhanced gene expression, and improved flow cytometry results. Ultimately, this study demonstrates that the use of custom-engineered materials can enhance cellular reprogramming techniques.

title: Effects of risedronate treatment on vertebral and nonvertebral fractures in women with postmenopausal osteoporosis: a randomized controlled trial. Vertebral Efficacy With Risedronate Therapy (VERT) Study Group.
text:
The objective of this study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of risedronate in the treatment of postmenopausal osteoporosis. The study was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial conducted on 2458 postmenopausal women with at least one vertebral fracture. The participants were randomly assigned to receive either risedronate (2.5 or 5 mg/d) or placebo for three years. All subjects also received calcium and vitamin D if necessary. The main outcome measures were the incidence of new vertebral fractures, nonvertebral fractures, and changes in bone mineral density. 

The results showed that treatment with 5 mg/d of risedronate significantly reduced the incidence of new vertebral fractures by 41% over three years compared to placebo. After the first year, there was a 65% reduction in fractures. The cumulative incidence of nonvertebral fractures was also reduced by 39% over three years. Bone mineral density increased significantly in the risedronate group compared to placebo at various sites. The safety profile of risedronate was similar to placebo.

In conclusion, risedronate therapy was found to be effective and well tolerated in the treatment of postmenopausal osteoporosis.

title: Hypoxia — a key regulatory factor in tumour growth
text: When cells are exposed to low oxygen conditions, they experience various biological reactions. These reactions include the activation of signaling pathways that control cell growth, blood vessel formation, and cell death. Cancer cells have adapted these pathways, enabling tumors to not only survive but also thrive in low oxygen conditions. Tumor hypoxia is linked to a negative prognosis and resistance to radiation treatment. Consequently, several components of the hypoxia-response pathway are potential targets for therapeutic intervention.

title: Loss of fibronectin from the aged stem cell niche affects the regenerative capacity of skeletal muscle in mice
text: The function of somatic stem cells has long been thought to be impaired by age-related changes in the niche. In this study, we show that the aged stem cell niche in skeletal muscle has significantly lower levels of fibronectin (FN), which has negative effects on the function and maintenance of muscle stem cells (MuSCs). When we deleted the gene responsible for FN in young regenerating muscles, we observed the same aging effects and a decrease in MuSC numbers. Through an analysis of an extracellular matrix (ECM) library and pathway profiling, we found that FN is a preferred adhesion substrate for MuSCs. We also discovered that integrin-mediated signaling through focal adhesion kinase and the p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase pathway is disrupted in MuSCs from aged mice due to inadequate attachment to the niche. Restoring FN levels in the aged niche resulted in the mobilization of stem cells and rejuvenated muscle regeneration. In conclusion, we have identified the loss of stem cell adhesion to FN in the niche ECM as a previously unknown mechanism of aging.

title: Monitoring starvation-induced reactive oxygen species formation.
text: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) have the potential to harm cells by oxidizing important components such as DNA, proteins, and lipids. However, when present in low levels and tightly regulated, ROS can actually play a beneficial role in various signal transduction pathways, including autophagy. Autophagy has traditionally been linked to oxidative stress, as it helps degrade oxidized proteins and organelles. Recently, it has been suggested that ROS also have a signaling function in the regulation of autophagy, which can lead to either cell survival or death depending on the circumstances. To investigate the impact of ROS on this pathway, it is necessary to determine where the oxidative signal occurs, its intensity, kinetics, and importance in autophagy. Once these characteristics are understood, detecting and manipulating ROS formation could be utilized to monitor and control autophagic activity. This chapter explores different methods for examining ROS within the context of autophagy.

title: Why do patients with multimorbidity in England report worse experiences in primary care? Evidence from the General Practice Patient Survey
text:
The aim of this study was to examine the primary care experiences of individuals in England with multiple long-term conditions. The researchers analyzed questionnaire data from 906,578 participants in the 2012 General Practice Patient Survey. Of these, 583,143 reported having one or more long-term conditions. The data was analyzed using mixed effect logistic regressions, taking into account sociodemographic characteristics and general practice. The researchers also considered the impact of health-related quality of life, measured using the EuroQoL (EQ-5D) scale. 

The results showed that the majority of patients with long-term conditions had positive experiences of care at their general practice. This remained consistent across different types of conditions. However, as the number of comorbid conditions increased, the percentage of patients reporting positive experiences decreased. For example, compared to individuals with no long-term conditions, those with four or more conditions were less likely to report positive experiences. 

However, when the researchers adjusted for health-related quality of life, this relationship was no longer observed. Patients' experiences of care were influenced more by patient-centered measures of health-related quality of life, particularly pain, than by the number of conditions they had. 

In conclusion, patients with multiple long-term conditions tend to have worse experiences in primary care. However, the number of conditions is not the primary factor influencing these experiences. Instead, patient-centered measures of health-related quality of life, particularly pain, play a more significant role.

title: The rice FISH BONE gene encodes a tryptophan aminotransferase, which affects pleiotropic auxin-related processes.
text: Auxin, a crucial plant hormone, plays a vital role in the growth and development of plants, with its localization within organs being of utmost importance. Previous analysis of Arabidopsis mutants lacking auxin biosynthesis revealed that the indole-3-pyruvic acid (IPA) pathway, catalyzed by the TRYPTOPHAN AMINOTRANSFERASE OF ARABIDOPSIS (TAA) and YUCCA (YUC) families, is the primary biosynthetic pathway for indole-3-acetic acid (IAA). However, little is known about the molecular mechanisms of auxin biosynthesis in rice. In this study, we discovered a rice mutant, fish bone (fib), which is related to auxin. The FIB gene, an orthologue of TAA genes, was found to be responsible for various abnormal phenotypes in the mutant, including small leaves with large lamina joint angles, abnormal vascular development, small panicles, abnormal organ identity, and defects in root development. Additionally, the mutant exhibited reduced levels of internal IAA, along with altered auxin sensitivity and polar transport activity. Based on these findings, we propose that FIB plays a crucial role in IAA biosynthesis in rice and that auxin biosynthesis, transport, and sensitivity are closely interconnected.

title: Successful mouse cloning of an outbred strain by trichostatin A treatment after somatic nuclear transfer.
text: Despite being used for various applications and reprogramming research in different species, the somatic cloning technique has been plagued by extremely low success rates for the past decade. In mice, the strains that can be cloned have been limited to hybrid F1 strains like B6D2F1. However, we have recently developed a new and efficient cloning technique using trichostatin A (TSA), which has resulted in a 2-5 fold increase in success rates for cloning B6D2F1 cumulus cells in mice. To further validate the effectiveness of this TSA cloning technique, we attempted to clone the adult ICR mouse, an outbred strain that has never been directly cloned before. Only when TSA was utilized, were we able to successfully clone both male and female mice from cumulus and fibroblast cells of adult ICR mice, with success rates of 4-5%, comparable to the 5-7% success rates of B6D2F1. Therefore, the TSA treatment represents the first cloning technique that allows us to successfully clone outbred mice, demonstrating its ability to improve cloning success rates not only for hybrid strains but also for typically "unclonable" strains.

title: A Genome-wide CRISPR Death Screen Identifies Genes Essential for Oxidative Phosphorylation.
text: Oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) is the primary process by which ATP is produced in humans. Deficiencies in OXPHOS can occur due to mutations in either mitochondrial or nuclear genomes, making it the largest group of inborn errors of metabolism. Currently, we do not have a comprehensive list of human genes and pathways that are essential for OXPHOS. In this study, we present a genome-wide CRISPR "death screen" that identifies dying cells to uncover the human genes necessary for OXPHOS. This approach was inspired by the observation that human cells lacking OXPHOS can survive in glucose but die in galactose. We have identified 191 genes that are highly essential for OXPHOS, including 72 genes associated with known OXPHOS diseases. Our screen has revealed a functional module consisting of NGRN, WBSCR16, RPUSD3, RPUSD4, TRUB2, and FASTKD2, which regulate the mitochondrial 16S rRNA and intra-mitochondrial translation. This study provides a comprehensive catalog of genes required for OXPHOS and demonstrates the effectiveness of death screening for functional genomic analysis.

title: RecQ helicases: caretakers of the genome
text: RecQ helicases exhibit a high level of conservation across various organisms, ranging from bacteria to humans. In humans, germline mutations in three out of the five identified family members result in severe disorders, which include an increased susceptibility to cancer development. Among these disorders, Bloom's syndrome stands out as it uniquely predisposes individuals to various types of cancer. The question then arises: how do RecQ helicases safeguard against cancer? It appears that they play a crucial role in preserving genomic stability by operating at the junction between DNA replication and DNA repair processes.

title: Mortality from causes amenable and non-amenable to medical care: the experience of eastern Europe.
text: The objective of this study was to compare national trends in mortality rates from conditions that can be treated with timely medical care versus those that cannot. The analysis focused on the period from the 1950s to 1987 and included four eastern European nations (Hungary, Czechoslovakia, Poland, the German Democratic Republic), two western European nations (the Federal Republic of Germany and England and Wales), and two North American nations (United States and Canada). The study examined the total populations of these countries during the specified time frame. The main outcome measures were proportional changes in age-standardized mortality rates. Mortality rates from amenable and non-amenable causes were only considered for the age group 0-64. The results showed a divergence in the trends of all-cause mortality between eastern Europe and the western nations around 1970. While mortality rates in western countries steadily declined, those in eastern Europe remained relatively stable. In the age group 0-64, mortality rates from conditions amenable to medical care decreased at a slower pace in eastern Europe compared to the West, especially after 1970. Conversely, mortality rates from non-amenable causes increased in eastern European countries from the late 1960s, while substantial declines were observed in the West. In conclusion, non-amenable causes of death appear to be the main factor contributing to the lack of improvement in all-cause mortality trends in eastern Europe since 1970. The focus of action in this region should prioritize promoting a healthier lifestyle and improving the environment, while also addressing the quality and efficiency of healthcare services.

title: Dynamic regulation of heterochromatin function via phosphorylation of HP1-family proteins.
text: Heterochromatin is identified by the methylation of histone H3 at lysine 9, which is recognized by highly conserved HP1-family proteins. Heterochromatin plays a role in various chromosome functions, such as silencing genes during transcription and maintaining cohesion between sister chromatids. These functions are carried out by different effector proteins that interact with HP1-family proteins. However, the mechanisms that regulate this interaction with the effectors are not well understood. Our recent research has demonstrated that phosphorylation of Swi6, the HP1 homolog in fission yeast, controls the association of transcriptional regulators and alters the activity of heterochromatin, while leaving sister chromatid cohesion unaffected. This study, along with other investigations conducted in different systems, suggests that phosphorylation of HP1/Swi6 offers a dynamic pathway for the selective regulation of heterochromatin in response to signals from both inside and outside the cell.

title: Modeling neurogenesis impairment in Down syndrome with induced pluripotent stem cells from Trisomy 21 amniotic fluid cells.
text: Down syndrome (DS), also known as Trisomy 21 (T21) syndrome, is a common chromosomal abnormality caused by an extra duplication of chromosome 21. When studying neuron development, it is ideal to use experimental models based on human cells for accurate and comprehensive research. To understand the stages of complex neuronal diseases, it is crucial to generate diseased induced pluripotent stem (iPS) cells. In this study, we successfully created human DS iPS cell lines from second trimester amniotic fluid (AF) cells with T21. This was achieved by co-expressing Yamanaka factors through lentiviral delivery, followed by differentiation into neuronal progenitor cells (NPCs) for further analysis. The T21 AF-iPS cells were characterized by their expression of pluripotent markers and their ability to differentiate into all three germ layers, as demonstrated by the formation of embryoid bodies in vitro and teratomas in vivo. The T21 AF-iPS cells maintained their unique pattern of chromosomal karyotypes, with three pairs of chromosome 21. Notably, NPCs derived from T21 AF-iPS cells exhibited a significant increase in amyloid precursor protein levels compared to NPCs from normal AF-iPS cells. Additionally, the expression levels of miR-155 and miR-802 were highly elevated in T21 AF-iPS-NPCs, while MeCP2 expression was low. Furthermore, we observed that T21 iPS-NPCs generated fewer neurons compared to controls, indicating developmental defects during neurogenesis. These findings suggest that T21 AF-iPS cells are a valuable resource for further investigating the impaired neurogenesis in DS and the onset of Alzheimer's disease.

title: Control over DNA replication in time and space.
text: The replication of DNA is carefully controlled in both timing and location to ensure the integrity of the genome. In eukaryotes, replication begins at multiple points along the genome known as origins of replication, and proceeds in two directions. The specific sites and timing of replication initiation are determined by dynamic complexes that are bound to the origins. During late mitosis and the G1 phase of the cell cycle, potential origins are identified and "licensed" by the assembly of pre-replicative complexes (pre-RCs) that contain the MCM2-7 helicases. Then, at the transition from G1 to S phase, a portion of the pre-RCs are activated, leading to the formation of replication forks. The location of origins is influenced by the structure of chromatin and the organization of the nucleus, and the selection of origins is a random process. The regulation of these cell cycle events depends on the periodic changes in the activity of cyclin dependent kinases (CDKs) throughout the cell cycle.

title: MYC/MIZ1-dependent gene repression inversely coordinates the circadian clock with cell cycle and proliferation
text: The circadian clock and the cell cycle are important cellular systems that regulate the overall functioning of the body in a time-dependent manner. It is possible that these two systems, which have potentially conflicting functions, are coordinated. Our study demonstrates that when MYC is overexpressed in U2OS cells, it weakens the circadian clock while promoting cell proliferation. Conversely, when MYC is downregulated, it strengthens the circadian clock and reduces cell proliferation. The inhibition of the circadian clock relies on the formation of repressive complexes between MYC and MIZ1, leading to the downregulation of core clock genes such as BMAL1 (ARNTL), CLOCK, and NPAS2. Additionally, our research reveals an inverse correlation between MYC levels and BMAL1 expression in 102 human lymphomas. These findings suggest that MYC acts as a central coordinator that modulates the impact of the cell cycle and circadian clock on gene expression in opposite directions.

title: Relevance of asystole during head-up tilt testing.
text: The prognosis for patients who experience prolonged asystole during head-up tilt testing is uncertain. Out of 209 consecutive patients with a history of syncope and positive tilt tests, 19 had asystole lasting more than 5 seconds (with an average duration of 15 +/- 10 seconds) in group 1a. When compared to patients without asystole in group 1b, those in group 1a were younger (32 +/- 12 vs 47 +/- 21 years, p < 0.005), but there were no significant differences in the severity of clinical symptoms (the number of syncope episodes [7 +/- 5 vs 8 +/- 6 episodes, p = NS] and injuries during syncope [2 vs 13 patients, p = NS] were similar). During a follow-up period of approximately 2 +/- 1 year, with patients receiving pharmacologic therapy such as beta blockers, ephedrine, theophylline, or disopyramide, the recurrence rate was 11% and 8% in groups 1a and 1b, respectively (p = NS). None of the patients in the asystole group required a pacemaker implantation. Additionally, out of 75 normal volunteers (group 2) with no history of syncope who underwent tilt tests to determine specificity, 3 experienced asystole with an average duration of 10 seconds. Over a follow-up period of more than 1 year, despite receiving no treatment, all 3 volunteers remained symptom-free. Therefore, the presence of asystole during head-up tilt testing does not indicate a more severe outcome or a poor response to pharmacologic therapy. Furthermore, an asystolic response does not improve the specificity of the tilt test as it can also be observed in asymptomatic "normal" volunteers.

title: Increasing informed uptake and non-uptake of screening: evidence from a systematic review.
text:
GOAL: The objective of this study was to present data on the informed uptake of screening tests.

SEARCH STRATEGY: We utilized electronic databases, bibliographies, and consulted experts to identify relevant published and unpublished studies up until August 2000.

INCLUSION CRITERIA: We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs), quasi-RCTs, and controlled trials that focused on interventions aimed at increasing the informed uptake of screening. All participants met the entry criteria of individual screening programs. Studies had to report actual uptake and meet at least three out of four criteria for defining informed uptake.

DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: We independently identified relevant studies, extracted data, and assessed their validity. Outcome data included screening uptake, knowledge, informed decision-making, and attitudes towards screening. We used a random-effects model to calculate individual relative risks and 95% confidence intervals.

MAIN RESULTS: We included six controlled trials (five RCTs and one quasi-RCT) that focused on antenatal and prostate-specific antigen screening. All studies reported on the risks and benefits of screening and assessed knowledge. Two studies also assessed decision-making. Two studies reported on risks and benefits for all randomized groups and evaluated different methods of presenting information. Neither study found that interventions such as videos, information leaflets with decision trees, or touch screen computers provided any additional benefits compared to well-prepared leaflets.

CONCLUSIONS: There is some evidence to suggest that changing the format of informed choice interventions in screening does not impact knowledge, satisfaction, or decisions about screening. The effect of informed choice on screening uptake remains unclear. More well-designed RCTs are needed, and further research should focus on developing a valid instrument for measuring all components of informed choice in screening.

title: Mitochondrial RNA Granules Are Centers for Posttranscriptional RNA Processing and Ribosome Biogenesis.
text: The role of cytoplasmic RNA granules in mRNA metabolism is well-known, but the significance of mitochondrial RNA granules has not been extensively studied. We conducted a thorough analysis of their proteome and discovered that they contain a wide range of proteins dedicated to RNA metabolism. Our investigation focused on four uncharacterized RNA-binding proteins: two RNA helicases, DHX30 and DDX28, and two proteins from the Fas-activated serine-threonine kinase (FASTKD) family, FASTKD2 and FASTKD5. Our findings revealed that both helicases and FASTKD2 are essential for the biogenesis of mitochondrial ribosomes. Through RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) analysis, we determined that DDX28 and FASTKD2 specifically bind to the 16S rRNA. FASTKD5, on the other hand, plays a crucial role in the maturation of precursor mRNAs that lack tRNA flanking sequences, making them unable to undergo processing through the conventional mRNA maturation pathway. Silencing FASTKD5 resulted in a significant reduction in mature COX I mRNA levels, leading to impaired synthesis of COX I and a subsequent defect in complex IV assembly. These findings highlight the importance of mitochondrial RNA granules in posttranscriptional RNA processing and the biogenesis of mitochondrial ribosomes.

title: Controlling nuclear receptors: the circular logic of cofactor cycles
text: The bimodal function of nuclear receptors, as both repressors and activators of gene transcription, plays a crucial role in regulating various important processes in development and homeostasis. It is essential to finely modulate the transcriptional activities of these receptors in order to determine specific and diverse gene expression programs. Recent studies have shed light on the molecular mechanisms involved in switching between repression and activation functions, the collaborative roles of multiple cofactor complexes in mediating transcriptional regulation, and the integration of various signaling pathways at the nuclear level to achieve specific gene expression profiles.

title: Reprogramming fibroblasts into bipotential hepatic stem cells by defined factors.
text: Recent research has shown that fibroblasts can be directly transformed into various types of somatic cells. However, until now, only blood and neuronal lineages have been successfully reprogrammed from stem or progenitor cells. In a previous study, we were able to generate induced hepatocyte-like (iHep) cells by introducing Gata4, Hnf1α, and Foxa3 into p19 Arf null mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs). In this study, we demonstrate that Hnf1β and Foxa3, which are transcription factors involved in liver development, are sufficient to reprogram MEFs into induced hepatic stem cells (iHepSCs). These iHepSCs can be expanded in vitro and have the ability to differentiate into both hepatocytic and cholangiocytic lineages. In the livers of mice lacking fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase (Fah), the repopulating iHepSCs transform into hepatocyte-like cells. Additionally, in mice with DDC-induced bile ductular injury, the iHepSCs engraft as cholangiocytes in the bile ducts. The conversion of lineage into bipotential expandable iHepSCs offers a promising strategy for efficiently deriving both hepatocytes and cholangiocytes, which can be used in disease modeling and tissue engineering.

title: Spatial genome organization: contrasting views from chromosome conformation capture and fluorescence in situ hybridization.
text:
Most studies on genome organization rely on fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) or chromosome conformation capture (3C) methods. FISH allows for direct visualization of the spatial relationship between sequences, but it is limited to a few loci at a time. On the other hand, 3C methods measure the frequency at which sequences are linked together by formaldehyde cross-linking, providing a genome-wide perspective. Higher frequencies indicate shorter distances between sequences. While FISH and 3C should theoretically provide similar views of genome organization, this has not been extensively tested.

To address this, we conducted a study using 3C carbon copy (5C) and FISH techniques on the murine HoxD locus. We examined different developmental and activity states, as well as the presence or absence of epigenetic regulators. We found instances where the data from both methods were consistent, but also identified conditions where the chromatin topographies inferred from 5C or FISH data did not align. This suggests that the products captured by 3C do not always reflect true spatial proximity. In some cases, ligation occurs between sequences that are hundreds of nanometers apart, influenced by the nuclear environment and chromatin composition.

In conclusion, caution must be exercised when interpreting high-resolution results obtained from either 3C methods or FISH alone. Independent validation using alternative methods is necessary to confirm views about genome organization.

title: Development and evaluation of a self-administered computerized 24-h dietary recall method for adolescents in Europe
text:
Objective: The objective of this study was to develop a computerized 24-hour dietary recall method for European adolescents and assess the feasibility of self-administration compared to administration by a dietician.

Methods: A total of 236 adolescents from eight European cities, with a mean age of 14.6 years, completed the 24-hour recall (Young Adolescents Nutrition Assessment on Computer - YANA-C) twice - once through self-report and once through an interview with a dietician.

Results: The self-report method showed a small but significant underestimation in energy (61 kcal) and fat (4.2 g) intake compared to the interview method. However, there were no significant differences in the intake of carbohydrates, proteins, fiber, calcium, iron, and ascorbic acid. Spearman's correlations showed high significance for all nutrients and energy, ranging from 0.86 to 0.91. Agreement in categorizing respondents as consumers and non-consumers for the 29 food groups was also high, with kappa statistics of 0.73 or higher. The average percentage of omissions was 3.7%, and the percentage of intrusions was 2.0%. Spearman's correlations between both modes were high for all food groups, both for the total sample (0.76 or higher) and for consumers only (0.72 or higher). When analyzing only the consumers, approximately 54% of the consumed amounts were exactly the same, with a significant difference found only for the "rice and pasta" group.

Conclusion: The adaptation, translation, and standardization of YANA-C allow for the assessment of dietary intake in adolescents in an international context. Overall, there was good agreement between the self-report and interview methods, with the self-report method offering significant potential for large-scale surveys with limited resources.

title: JTK_CYCLE: an efficient nonparametric algorithm for detecting rhythmic components in genome-scale data sets.
text: Circadian rhythms are natural cycles that occur in physiology, behavior, and metabolism, with a period length of approximately 24 hours. In various organisms, including humans, circadian clock genes have been identified as transcription factors. To study these genes and their regulation, researchers have used microarrays and algorithms to detect cycling patterns in gene expression. This article introduces a new algorithm called JTK_CYCLE, which efficiently identifies and characterizes cycling variables in large data sets. Compared to commonly used methods like COSOPT and Fisher's G test, JTK_CYCLE is more reliable and efficient in distinguishing between rhythmic and nonrhythmic transcripts. It also has increased resistance to outliers, resulting in improved sensitivity and specificity. Additionally, JTK_CYCLE accurately measures the period, phase, and amplitude of cycling transcripts, making it useful for downstream analyses. Notably, JTK_CYCLE is significantly faster than COSOPT, making it suitable for analyzing large-scale data sets. The algorithm was applied to legacy data sets, including NIH3T3 cells with low amplitude oscillations, and successfully identified a novel cluster of RNA-interacting genes regulated by circadian rhythms. These findings demonstrate that JTK_CYCLE is an excellent tool for identifying and characterizing oscillations in genome-scale data sets.

title: Polo-like kinase 1 regulates Nlp, a centrosome protein involved in microtubule nucleation.
text: Most microtubules in animal cells originate from centrosomes. During mitosis, centrosomes undergo a structural reorganization called maturation, which increases microtubule nucleation. This process is regulated by kinases, including Polo-like kinase 1 (Plk1). In this study, we identify a Plk1 substrate called Nlp (ninein-like protein) that is located in centrosomes and appears to play a crucial role in microtubule organization. Nlp interacts with two components of the gamma-tubulin ring complex and promotes microtubule nucleation. Plk1 phosphorylates Nlp, disrupting its association with centrosomes and its interaction with gamma-tubulin. Overexpression of a mutant Nlp lacking Plk1 phosphorylation sites severely disrupts the formation of the mitotic spindle. Our findings suggest that Nlp is important for microtubule organization during interphase, and that Plk1 activation during mitosis triggers the removal of Nlp from centrosomes, allowing the establishment of a mitotic scaffold with increased microtubule nucleation.

title: Consumption of isoflavone-rich soy protein does not alter homocysteine or markers of inflammation in postmenopausal women
text:
Objective: The objective of this study was to examine the impact of soy protein with isoflavones on various biomarkers including homocysteine (Hcy), C-reactive protein (CRP), soluble E-selectin (sE-selectin), soluble vascular adhesion molecule-1 (sVCAM-1), and soluble intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (sICAM-1).

Methods: A total of 34 postmenopausal women participated in a randomized crossover trial. They consumed either soy protein isolate (containing 26±5 g protein and 44±8 mg isoflavones per day) or milk protein isolate (containing 26±5 g protein per day) for 6 weeks each. Fasting blood samples were collected at the end of each diet period and analyzed using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay.

Results: The concentrations of Hcy, CRP, sE-selectin, sVCAM-1, and sICAM-1 did not show any significant differences between the soy and milk diet treatments. These results remained consistent regardless of equol production status or baseline lipid concentration. Adjusting for folate and methionine intake did not affect the Hcy results.

Conclusions: Based on these findings, it can be concluded that soy consumption does not appear to reduce coronary heart disease risk by decreasing vascular inflammation or Hcy concentration.

title: Homogeneously dispersed multimetal oxygen-evolving catalysts
text: Researchers have created catalysts based on abundant first-row transition metals that can facilitate the oxygen-evolution reaction (OER). However, these catalysts require higher overpotentials than what is thermodynamically necessary. By using density functional theory, it was discovered that non-3d metals with high valency, like tungsten, can modify 3d metal oxides to achieve optimal adsorption energies for OER intermediates. A synthesis method was developed to produce gelled oxyhydroxide materials with a uniform distribution of metal atoms at room temperature. These gelled FeCoW oxyhydroxides exhibit the lowest reported overpotential (191 millivolts) at 10 milliamperes per square centimeter in an alkaline electrolyte. The catalyst remains stable even after more than 500 hours of operation. X-ray absorption and computational studies demonstrate that tungsten, iron, and cobalt work together synergistically to create a favorable local coordination environment and electronic structure that enhance the energetics for OER.

title: Global strategy for the diagnosis, management, and prevention of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: GOLD executive summary.
text: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a global health issue. Since 2001, the Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) has been publishing a strategy document for the diagnosis and management of COPD. This summary presents the key points from the second 5-year revision of the GOLD document, which incorporates the extensive knowledge accumulated about COPD in recent years. GOLD now recommends that spirometry is necessary for the clinical diagnosis of COPD to prevent misdiagnosis and accurately assess the severity of airflow limitation. The document emphasizes that evaluating a patient with COPD should include assessing symptoms, severity of airflow limitation, history of exacerbations, and comorbidities. The first three factors help determine the level of symptoms and the risk of future exacerbations, categorizing patients into four groups: A, B, C, and D. The management of COPD, both nonpharmacologic and pharmacologic, aligns with this assessment to alleviate symptoms and reduce the risk of exacerbations based on evidence-based practices. Identifying and treating comorbidities is of utmost importance, and the document includes a separate section on managing comorbidities alongside COPD. Additionally, the revised document includes a new section on COPD exacerbations. The GOLD initiative will continue to raise awareness about COPD among relevant stakeholders and hopefully inspire the development of national and local guidelines for COPD management in the future.

title: Circulating tumor cells: a useful predictor of treatment efficacy in metastatic breast cancer.
text:
The purpose of this study was to investigate the correlation between circulating tumor cells (CTCs) and radiographic disease progression in patients with metastatic breast cancer (MBC). We conducted a prospective study where CTC levels were measured in patients starting a new treatment regimen for progressive MBC. Blood samples were collected at baseline and at regular intervals, and radiographic studies were performed every 9-12 weeks. 

The results showed a significant correlation between CTC levels and radiographic disease progression in patients receiving chemotherapy or endocrine therapy. This correlation was observed at the time of imaging, as well as 3-5 weeks and 7-9 weeks before imaging. The correlation remained significant when the analysis was stratified by type of therapy. 

Furthermore, patients with five or more CTCs at 3-5 weeks and 7-9 weeks after starting treatment had a shorter progression-free survival. 

In conclusion, this study provides the first evidence of a strong correlation between CTC results and radiographic disease progression in patients with MBC receiving chemotherapy or endocrine therapy. These findings suggest that CTC enumeration can be used as an additional method to monitor disease status in MBC.

title: Recovery of supraspinal control of stepping via indirect propriospinal relay connections after spinal cord injury
text: Spontaneous functional recovery after spinal cord injuries (SCIs) in humans and animals is often observed during the initial months following the injury. This recovery is commonly attributed to spared axons that originate from the brain and bypass incomplete lesions, but the exact mechanisms are still uncertain. To investigate the neural basis of this spontaneous recovery, we conducted kinematic, physiological, and anatomical analyses on mice with different combinations of lateral hemisections that were spatially and temporally separated. Some mice also underwent excitotoxic ablation of intrinsic spinal cord neurons. Our study reveals that propriospinal relay connections, which bypass one or more injury sites, can facilitate spontaneous functional recovery and enable supraspinal control of stepping.
