title: Late-life depression and microstructural abnormalities in dorsolateral prefrontal cortex white matter.
text: The aim of this study was to investigate whether there are abnormalities in the microstructure of the white matter in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex that are linked to late-life depression. A total of 17 elderly individuals with depression were compared to 16 elderly individuals without depression. Diffusion tensor imaging was utilized to measure the fractional anisotropy of the white matter in the superior and middle frontal gyri bilaterally in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, with the left occipital lobe serving as a control region. The researchers compared the results between the two groups while taking into account age, sex, and any concurrent medical conditions. The findings revealed significantly lower fractional anisotropy values in the white matter of the right superior frontal gyrus in depressed patients compared to the control group, even after adjusting for age, sex, hypertension, and heart disease. In conclusion, alterations in the microstructure of the white matter in the right superior frontal gyrus are associated with late-life depression. Further research is necessary to understand the role of these changes in the development and progression of depression.

title: Pioglitazone prevents tau oligomerization.
text: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is primarily caused by the aggregation of tau and amyloid β protein (Aβ) deposition. The activation of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ) has been found to regulate Aβ production. In order to investigate whether the PPARγ agonist pioglitazone (PIO) can also prevent tau aggregation in AD, we conducted experiments using a cellular model (M1C cells) overexpressing wild-type tau protein (4R0N) and primary neuronal cultures. PIO effectively reduced both phosphorylated and total tau levels, and inhibited glycogen synthase kinase 3β, a key tau kinase, through Akt activation. Furthermore, PIO decreased the presence of cleaved caspase3 and C-terminal truncated tau species, which are known to contribute to tau aggregation. Fractionation analysis revealed that PIO reduced the levels of high molecular-weight (120 kDa) oligomeric tau species in Tris Insoluble and sarkosyl-soluble fractions. The reduction in tau was reversed when a PPARγ antagonist, GW9662, was added. These findings support the potential therapeutic use of PPARγ agonists in the treatment of AD.

title: Prognostic impact of the mean platelet volume/platelet count ratio in terms of survival in advanced non-small cell lung cancer.
text:
BACKGROUND
Mean platelet volume (MPV) is a measure of platelet size. Traditionally, MPV has been considered a marker of platelet activation. Recent research has shown that MPV, along with the MPV/platelet count (PC) ratio, can predict long-term mortality in patients with ischemic cardiovascular disease. These indices have also been found to be correlated with the pathophysiological characteristics of patients with various disorders, including malignant tumors.

PATIENTS AND METHODS
In this study, we conducted a retrospective analysis of different hematological indices in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The objective was to assess the impact of platelet volume indices on survival in these patients.

RESULTS
A total of 268 patients were included in the study, with a median age of 68 years (range: 31-87 years). We compared various hematological indices between the NSCLC group and a comparator group matched for age and sex. We found that MPV was significantly lower in the NSCLC group compared to the comparator group. Conversely, the PC was significantly higher in the NSCLC group. As a result, the MPV/PC ratio was also lower in the NSCLC group (0.397 vs. 0.501). In receiver operating characteristics (ROC) curve analysis, the MPV/PC ratio showed a sensitivity of 62.3% and a specificity of 74.6% at a cutoff value of 0.408730 (area under the curve [AUC], 0.72492). 

Univariate analysis revealed that overall survival (OS) was significantly shorter in the group with a low MPV/PC ratio compared to the other group (median survival time [MST]: 10.3 months vs. 14.5 months, log-rank, P=0.0245). Multivariate analysis confirmed that a low MPV/PC ratio was an independent unfavorable predictive factor for OS (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.668, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.235-2.271, P=0.0008).

CONCLUSION
These findings clearly demonstrate that the MPV/PC ratio is closely associated with survival in patients with advanced NSCLC.

title: Traceability of biologicals: present challenges in pharmacovigilance.
text:
INTRODUCTION
Traceability plays a crucial role in monitoring the safety of biological products after they have been marketed. Changes in the manufacturing process can introduce specific risks to certain products or batches. As the biosimilar market continues to grow, concerns have arisen about the ability to trace individual products within pharmacovigilance databases.

AREAS COVERED
In this article, the authors address the challenges associated with traceability of biologicals in relation to pharmacovigilance. They examine the processes involved in ensuring traceability, including the existing systems for recording exposure information in clinical practice and the steps required to transfer this data to pharmacovigilance databases.

EXPERT OPINION
While current systems allow for traceability of biologicals up to the manufacturer level in pharmacy records, they do not support the routine recording of batch information. However, anticipated changes in supply chain standards present opportunities to systematically record detailed exposure information. The manual nature of data transfer in spontaneous reporting systems makes them particularly vulnerable in ensuring traceability. Efforts to improve traceability should focus on encouraging healthcare professionals and patients to consistently record and report detailed exposure information in the short term. In the long term, solutions should aim to expand accessibility to exposure data and increase electronic exchange of this information.

title: Regulation of self-ligands for activating natural killer cell receptors.
text: NK cells have the ability to destroy infected and tumor cells without harming healthy cells. The identification of diseased cells by NK cells is controlled by various activating and inhibitory receptors. In this review, we examine multiple pathways that are involved in the control of self-ligands for activating receptors, such as NKG2D, DNAM-1, LFA-1, NKp30, NKp44, NKp46, NKp65, and NKp80, which are present on NK cells and certain T cells. Understanding the regulation of self-encoded ligand expression could potentially lead to new therapeutic approaches for treating infections and cancer.

title: A core Klf circuitry regulates self-renewal of embryonic stem cells
text: ES cells possess the remarkable ability to continuously renew themselves and maintain their pluripotent state. This is made possible by specific transcription factors that control the gene expression program of these cells. By using a combination of four transcription factors - Klf4, Oct4, Sox2, and c-Myc - it has been demonstrated that somatic cells can be reverted back to a pluripotent state. While Oct4, Sox2, and c-Myc are essential for the self-renewal and pluripotency of ES cells, Klf4 is not necessary. However, our research reveals that Krüppel-like factors (Klfs) are crucial for the self-renewal of ES cells. When Klf2, Klf4, and Klf5 are simultaneously depleted, ES cells undergo differentiation. Through chromatin immunoprecipitation and microarray analysis, we have discovered that these Klf proteins share many common targets with Nanog, indicating a close functional relationship between them. Furthermore, our expression analysis after triple RNA interference of the Klfs demonstrates their role in regulating key pluripotency genes, including Nanog. Overall, our study provides valuable insights into how the core Klf circuitry integrates into the Nanog transcriptional network to establish the unique gene expression profile of ES cells.

title: A myeloid hypoxia-inducible factor 1α-Krüppel-like factor 2 pathway regulates gram-positive endotoxin-mediated sepsis.
text: Despite the prevalence of gram-positive infections in sepsis cases, the exact molecular mechanisms behind their effects are still not well understood. Our study aimed to investigate the role of cell wall components of gram-positive bacteria in the development of sepsis. Through experiments conducted on cultured primary macrophages and a cell line, we found that gram-positive bacterial endotoxins stimulate the expression of hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α) mRNA and protein. When macrophages were exposed to live or heat-inactivated gram-positive bacteria, HIF-1 transcriptional activity was induced. Consistent with these findings, the absence of HIF-1α in myeloid cells reduced cellular motility and the expression of proinflammatory genes in response to gram-positive bacterial endotoxins. Conversely, gram-positive bacteria and their endotoxins decreased the expression of the myeloid anti-inflammatory transcription factor Krüppel-like transcription factor 2 (KLF2). Sustained expression of KLF2 reduced the induction of HIF-1α mRNA and protein by gram-positive endotoxins, while KLF2 deficiency enhanced this induction in macrophages. Importantly, KLF2 also attenuated cellular motility and proinflammatory gene expression in myeloid cells stimulated by gram-positive endotoxins. Consistent with these findings, mice lacking myeloid HIF-1α were protected from mortality and clinical symptoms induced by gram-positive endotoxins in sepsis. On the other hand, myeloid KLF2-deficient mice were more susceptible to gram-positive sepsis-induced mortality and clinical symptoms. Overall, our study highlights the critical roles of HIF-1α and KLF2 as regulators of gram-positive endotoxin-mediated sepsis.

title: Autophagy controls Salmonella infection in response to damage to the Salmonella-containing vacuole.
text: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium (S. Typhimurium) is a type of pathogen that can infect various hosts. It invades host cells and resides within a compartment called the Salmonella-containing vacuole (SCV). The bacteria use two separate type III secretion systems (TTSS) to modify the SCV. These systems are known to damage the membranes of eukaryotic cells, and S. Typhimurium is believed to damage the SCV using its Salmonella pathogenicity island (SPI)-1 encoded TTSS. Our study shows that this damage leads to a population of bacteria within the host cells that are targeted by the autophagy system during infection in the lab. Around 20% of the intracellular S. Typhimurium was found to colocalize with the autophagy marker GFP-LC3 one hour after infection. The autophagy of S. Typhimurium depended on the SPI-1 TTSS and bacterial protein synthesis. The bacteria targeted by the autophagy system were often associated with ubiquitinated proteins, indicating that they were exposed to the cytosol. Surprisingly, these bacteria also colocalized with SCV markers. Cells deficient in autophagy were more susceptible to intracellular growth by S. Typhimurium compared to normal cells, allowing increased bacterial growth in the cytosol. We propose a model in which the host autophagy system targets bacteria in damaged SCVs caused by the SPI-1 TTSS. This helps to keep intracellular S. Typhimurium within vacuoles early after infection to prevent colonization of the cytosol. Our findings support the role of autophagy in innate immunity and demonstrate that Salmonella infection is a useful model for studying the autophagy process.

title: PI3K-Akt-mTORC1-S6K1/2 axis controls Th17 differentiation by regulating Gfi1 expression and nuclear translocation of RORγ.
text: The activation, survival, and proliferation of CD4(+) T cells upon stimulation through TCR and CD28 are influenced by the PI3K-Akt-mTORC1 axis. In this study, we show that inhibiting this axis by deleting p85α or using PI3K/mTORC1 inhibitors, as well as deleting raptor (a crucial component of mTORC1) specifically in T cells, hampers Th17 differentiation both in vitro and in vivo in a S6K1/2-dependent manner. The inhibition of the PI3K-Akt-mTORC1-S6K1 axis also prevents the downregulation of Gfi1, a negative regulator of Th17 differentiation. Additionally, we demonstrate that S6K2, a nuclear form of S6K1, is induced by the PI3K-Akt-mTORC1 axis, interacts with RORγ, and transports RORγ to the nucleus. These findings highlight the significant role of the PI3K-Akt-mTORC1-S6K1/2 axis in Th17 differentiation.

title: Disrupted-in-schizophrenia 1 and neuregulin 1 are required for the specification of oligodendrocytes and neurones in the zebrafish brain.
text: Schizophrenia may be caused by subtle abnormalities in brain development due to changes in the functions of certain genes that make individuals more susceptible to the disorder. Two of these genes, Disrupted-in-schizophrenia 1 (DISC1) and Neuregulin 1 (NRG1), have been identified as potential contributors. To gain a better understanding of how DISC1 affects brain development, we studied the expression of the disc1 gene in zebrafish and investigated its role in early embryonic development using a method called morpholino antisense. Our research revealed that disc1 plays a crucial role in the development of oligodendrocytes, a type of brain cell, by promoting the formation of olig2-positive cells in various regions of the brain, including the hindbrain. We also examined the roles of nrg1 and ErbB signaling, which are known to be involved in myelination, another important process in brain development. Interestingly, we found that zebrafish embryos with reduced levels of nrg1 or disc1 displayed similar defects, suggesting that these genes may function in the same or related pathways that control the development of oligodendrocytes and neurons derived from olig2-expressing precursor cells. Furthermore, we discovered that knocking down disc1 or nrg1 resulted in a significant loss of olig2-positive cerebellar neurons, but had no apparent effect on spinal motor neurons. These findings indicate that disc1 and nrg1 are involved in the development of both oligodendrocytes and neurons, and that they may share common pathways. Interestingly, two other genes, OLIG2 and ERBB4, have also been identified as potential susceptibility genes for schizophrenia and are known to be involved in similar processes as DISC1 and NRG1. Therefore, our findings in zebrafish embryos suggest that there may be previously unrecognized connections between these key genes involved in neurodevelopment and the development of schizophrenia. Further investigation using mouse models with altered Disc1 and Nrg1 genes, as well as studies involving genetically defined groups of patients, could help determine the relevance of these connections to the underlying causes of schizophrenia. The GenBank accession number for the disc1 gene in zebrafish is EU273350.

title: Monoclonal antibody targeting of N-cadherin inhibits prostate cancer growth, metastasis and castration resistance
text: The transition from androgen-dependent to castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) is a deadly occurrence with an unclear molecular cause. By comparing gene expression in isogenic androgen-dependent and CRPC xenografts, we discovered a consistent increase in N-cadherin expression. This elevation was also observed in primary and metastatic tumors of individuals with CRPC. When N-cadherin was artificially expressed in nonmetastatic, androgen-dependent prostate cancer models, it resulted in castration resistance, invasion, and metastasis. In laboratory tests, monoclonal antibodies targeting the outer part of N-cadherin reduced the proliferation, adhesion, and invasion of prostate cancer cells. In animal experiments, these antibodies slowed the growth of multiple established CRPC xenografts, prevented local invasion and metastasis, and even caused complete regression at higher doses. The N-cadherin-specific antibodies significantly delayed the emergence of castration resistance, affected tumor histology and angiogenesis, and reduced both AKT serine-threonine kinase activity and the secretion of interleukin-8 (IL-8) in the blood. These findings suggest that N-cadherin plays a major role in both prostate cancer metastasis and castration resistance. Targeting this factor with monoclonal antibodies in therapy could have significant clinical advantages.

title: PP2A regulates tau phosphorylation directly and also indirectly via activating GSK-3beta.
text: Tau hyperphosphorylation is a key factor in the neurofibrillary degeneration seen in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Previous research suggests that a decrease in protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A), the main tau phosphatase in the human brain, contributes to this hyperphosphorylation. However, the specific effects of PP2A down-regulation on site-specific tau hyperphosphorylation are not well understood. In this study, we demonstrated that PP2A dephosphorylates tau at various phosphorylation sites with different efficiencies. Among the sites examined, Thr205, Thr212, Ser214, and Ser262 were the most susceptible to dephosphorylation by PP2A, while Ser199 and Ser404 were the least susceptible. Inhibiting PP2A with okadaic acid in metabolically active rat brain slices resulted in the inhibition of glycogen synthase kinase-3beta (GSK-3beta) by increasing its phosphorylation at Ser9. GSK-3beta phosphorylated tau at multiple sites, with Ser199, Thr205, and Ser396 being the most susceptible in cells. The overall changes in tau phosphorylation caused by PP2A inhibition were a combination of reduced tau dephosphorylation due to direct PP2A inhibition and reduced phosphorylation by GSK-3beta due to its inhibition. Since the effects of tau phosphorylation on its biological activity and neurofibrillary degeneration are specific to certain sites, this study offers new insights into the role of PP2A down-regulation in neurofibrillary degeneration in AD.

title: Human artificial chromosomes containing chromosome 17 alphoid DNA maintain an active centromere in murine cells but are not stable.
text: Human artificial chromosomes (HACs) are independent molecules that can operate and separate like regular chromosomes in human cells. These HACs have been successfully utilized as vectors for gene expression to compensate for genetic deficiencies in human cultured cells. They now provide the opportunity to investigate the regulation and expression of large genes in various cell types from different tissues, as well as correct gene deficiencies caused by inherited diseases in humans. It is also crucial to conduct complementary gene expression studies in mice, particularly in mouse models of human genetic diseases, to determine if large human transgenes can be appropriately expressed from artificial chromosomes. To achieve this, we are developing artificial chromosomes in murine cells as innovative gene expression vectors. Initially, we introduced HAC vectors into murine cells, but were unable to generate new HACs at a reasonable rate. Subsequently, we transferred HACs that were previously established in human HT1080 cells to three different types of murine cells using microcell fusion, followed by positive selection. We observed that the HACs in murine cells bound to centromere protein C (CENP-C), which is a marker of active centromeres, and were detectable under selection. However, they were quickly lost when selection was discontinued. These findings suggest that the HACs maintain a partially functional centromere complex in murine cells, but additional factors are necessary for stability and separation. It may be necessary to incorporate mouse centromeric sequences into artificial chromosomes to enhance stability and maintenance in murine cells.

title: How nascent phagosomes mature to become phagolysosomes.
text: Phagocytosis is responsible for clearing apoptotic bodies and eliminating microbial pathogens. Initially, the phagocytic vacuole formed lacks the ability to kill and degrade microorganisms. However, as the phagosome matures, its membrane and contents undergo progressive remodeling, leading to the formation of phagolysosomes. This maturation process involves the sequential fusion of the phagosomal vacuole with specialized endocytic and secretory compartments. At the same time, the phagosomal membrane undergoes vesiculation, tubulation, and fission, recycling components and maintaining its size. In this summary, we discuss the molecular machinery that controls the complex metamorphosis of phagosome maturation.

title: Purification and structural characterization of bovine cathelicidins, precursors of antimicrobial peptides.
text: Cathelicidins are a new group of antimicrobial peptide precursors found in mammalian myeloid cells. They have a conserved N-terminal region, but the C-terminal antimicrobial domain can vary greatly in both sequence and length. Four cathelicidins, namely proBac5, proBac7, prododecapeptide, and proBMAP-28, have been isolated from bovine neutrophils using simple and fast methods. By comparing the ES-MS data of the purified proteins with their cDNA-deduced sequences, several common features of their primary sequence have been identified, including the presence of N-terminal 5-oxoproline (pyroglutamate) residues and two disulfide bridges arranged in a 1-2, 3-4 pattern. The N-terminal domains of cathelicidins contain one or two Asp-Pro bonds, which are highly susceptible to acid hydrolysis in proBac5 and proBac7, but stable in prododecapeptide. This suggests that the spatial arrangement around these bonds may differ among cathelicidins, leading to varying degrees of hydrolysis. An unexpected finding is that prododecapeptide exists as dimers formed by three possible combinations of its two isoforms. The discovery of a truncated, monomeric form of this protein, lacking the cysteine-containing antimicrobial dodecapeptide, suggests that dimerization occurs through the formation of disulfide bridges in the C-terminal domain, and the dodecapeptide is likely released as a dimer from its precursor. Predictions of secondary structure based on the protein sequence and CD results indicate that cathelicidins have a 30-50% content of extended conformation and less than 20% content of alpha-helical conformation, with the alpha-helical segment located near the N-terminus. Furthermore, similarity searches and structure predictions based on topology highlight a significant sequential and structural similarity between the conserved N-terminal domain of cathelicidins and cystatin-like domains, placing this family within the cystatin superfamily. When tested against cathepsin L, three out of the four cathelicidins show weak inhibitory activity (Ki = 0.6-3 microM), unlike the potent cystatin inhibitors.

title: Tuberculosis mortality in England and Wales during 1982-1992: its association with poverty, ethnicity and AIDS.
text: The purpose of this study is to examine the connection between contemporary tuberculosis (TB) in England and Wales and various potential causes. The study analyzes standardized annual TB mortality rates from 1982 to 1992 for the 403 local authority districts, broken down by age and gender. To calculate Poisson regression models, data from the 1981 and 1991 censuses on social, demographic, and ethnicity measures, as well as standardized annual AIDS-related mortality rates for young men, are utilized. The findings reveal a strong association between all TB mortality groups and overcrowding at the household level. For women, no other factors improved the explanatory power of the models. In multiple regressions, both poverty and AIDS-related mortality accounted for additional variation in the model for younger men. However, the analysis of mortality did not reflect a link between ethnicity and tuberculosis notifications. Once overcrowding was taken into account, there was no evidence of a positive relationship with ethnicity for any group. The significance of household-level overcrowding suggests that prolonged contact is necessary for disease transmission. Regression analysis indicates that overcrowding and poverty among ethnic populations are significant factors in tuberculosis mortality. The fact that the relationship between AIDS and TB is limited to the group most commonly affected by AIDS suggests that AIDS has little impact on the overall level of tuberculosis mortality. Possible explanations for the observed relationship include preferential certification, migration for treatment, and deficiencies in healthcare provision.

title: Noncognate interaction with MHC class II molecules is essential for maintenance of T cell metabolism to establish optimal memory CD4 T cell function.
text: CD4 memory T cells lose their characteristic memory function when they do not have contact with MHC class II molecules. To understand why memory T cells function poorly without MHC class II molecules, we examined the gene expression profiles of resting memory T cells from hosts with or without MHC class II molecules. We focused on five transcripts related to T cell activation, metabolism, and survival, which were found to be less active in resting memory T cells from hosts without MHC class II molecules compared to those with MHC class II molecules. CD4 memory cells from hosts without MHC class II molecules showed changes in their level of differentiation and metabolic activity, even in the presence of dendritic cells expressing antigens. Our findings suggest that the absence of interactions with noncognate MHC class II molecules hinders the accumulation of signals necessary for optimal survival and fitness of activated T cells, as well as shaping the functional capacity of future memory cells. Signals through AKT coordinate survival and metabolic pathways, and may be a crucial factor in connecting interactions with MHC class II molecules to the successful generation of a long-lasting functional memory CD4 T cell population.

title: The kinase TAK1 integrates antigen and cytokine receptor signaling for T cell development, survival and function
text: The role of the kinase TAK1 in innate and B cell immunity is crucial. However, its function in T cells remains unclear. Our study demonstrates that deleting the gene encoding TAK1 specifically in T cells leads to a decrease in thymocyte development, particularly in regulatory T cells that express the transcription factor Foxp3. TAK1 is necessary for the survival of mature thymocytes mediated by interleukin 7, as well as for T cell receptor-induced activation of the transcription factor NF-κB and the kinase Jnk. In effector T cells, TAK1 is not required for T cell receptor-induced NF-κB activation and cytokine production, but it plays a significant role in proliferation and activation of the kinase p38 in response to interleukins 2, 7, and 15. Therefore, TAK1 is essential for integrating signals from the T cell receptor and cytokines to regulate the development, survival, and function of T cells.

title: Caregiver burden in HIV-positive and HIV-negative partners of men with AIDS.
text: This study investigates the factors related to caregiver burden in 82 individuals who are HIV-positive (HIV+) and 162 individuals who are HIV-negative (HIV-) partners of men with AIDS. Our hypothesis was that HIV+ caregivers would experience more burden compared to HIV- caregivers due to the impact of their disease on their resources. The results supported our hypothesis, as HIV+ caregivers reported higher levels of burden. In comparison to HIV- caregivers, HIV+ caregivers were found to be more religious or spiritual, had lower income, and utilized more positive reappraisal, cognitive escape-avoidance, and sought social support as coping mechanisms. When comparing HIV+ caregivers to 61 HIV+ partners of healthy men, most of the differences between HIV+ and HIV- caregivers were attributed to HIV seropositivity rather than caregiving. However, among the variables associated with HIV seropositivity, only religiosity or spirituality independently contributed to caregiver burden in HIV+ caregivers, suggesting a relatively weak connection between HIV seropositivity and caregiver burden. The model accounted for 62% of the variance in burden among HIV+ caregivers and 36% of the variance in burden among HIV- caregivers.

title: Renal Disease and Pregnancy
text: Pregnancy in women with various kidney diseases has significant implications for both the developing fetus and the mother's health. The kidneys and urinary tract undergo significant anatomical, hemodynamic, and endocrine changes to accommodate the pregnancy. Failure to adapt can worsen existing maternal conditions and create an unfavorable environment for fetal development, increasing the risk of complications during childbirth. It is crucial for modern obstetricians to have knowledge and accurate interpretation of renal function tests to avoid misdiagnosing renal disease based solely on specific changes that occur during pregnancy. Proper evaluation of renal function and changes can help identify pathologies that can worsen both the mother's and the baby's conditions. Advances in understanding the pathophysiology of renal function during pregnancy have allowed pregnant women, including those with renal transplants, to have better outcomes. The concept of multidisciplinary teamwork is emphasized in modern medicine, and obstetricians should consider nephrologists as essential members of the team. Pregnant women should be referred to nephrologists for routine renal check-ups in the second or early third trimester, in addition to standard blood and urine analyses. Nephrologists and urologists should be involved in managing severe medical conditions such as preeclampsia, acute and chronic renal failure, as well as the complex management of dialysis or renal transplant patients. During pregnancy, various renal diseases can occur, some preexisting and others developed or directly influenced by pregnancy. This chapter will briefly discuss the basic evaluation of renal status to better understand acute and chronic renal disorders during pregnancy. The focus will be on the most common preexisting diseases in pregnancy, including chronic glomerulonephritis, secondary glomerular nephropathies, interstitial nephropathies (such as chronic pyelonephritis and renal tuberculosis), diabetic nephropathy, solitary kidney, and chronic renal failure. The chapter will also cover renal diseases directly influenced by pregnancy, such as asymptomatic bacteriuria, symptomatic urinary infection, urolithiasis, and acute renal failure. Additionally, the management of dialysis during pregnancy and pregnant women with renal transplants will be discussed.

title: Integrin beta1-mediated matrix assembly and signaling are critical for the normal development and function of the kidney glomerulus.
text: The kidneys in humans filter approximately 180 liters of blood per day through around 2.5 million glomeruli. The glomerular filtration apparatus consists of three layers: fenestrated endothelium, a specialized extracellular matrix called the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), and podocyte foot processes with modified adherens junctions known as the slit diaphragm (SD). In this study, we investigated the role of podocyte beta1 integrin signaling in maintaining normal glomerular function. We used mice with a specific deletion of integrin beta1 in podocytes (podocin-Cre beta1-fl/fl mice), which appeared normal at birth but were unable to complete renal development after birth. These mice exhibited proteinuria on the first day and died within a week. While the glomerular endothelium appeared normal, the kidneys of podocin-Cre beta1-fl/fl mice showed severe defects in the GBM, including multilaminations and splitting, as well as podocyte foot process effacement. Integrin linked kinase (ILK) is a downstream mediator of integrin beta1 activity in epithelial cells. To further investigate the role of integrin beta1-mediated signaling in glomerular filtration, we generated mice lacking ILK specifically in podocytes (podocin-Cre ILK-fl/fl mice). These mice developed normally but exhibited proteinuria at birth and died from renal failure by 15 weeks of age. Overall, our findings demonstrate the critical importance of podocyte beta1 integrin and ILK signaling in the postnatal development and function of the glomerular filtration apparatus.

title: The Aging Epigenome.
text: The decline in health and stress resistance during aging leads to decrepitude, frailty, and ultimately death. The exact timing and mechanisms of this decline are still unknown. Age-dependent decline is primarily caused by changes in transcriptional networks and chromatin state. These changes not only occur during aging but also significantly impact cellular function and stress resistance, contributing to the progression of aging. We believe that the disruption of transcriptional and chromatin networks is a crucial factor in the aging process. By understanding the epigenomic changes that occur with age, we can gain valuable insights into the onset and progression of aging, and potentially develop new therapies to delay or reverse aging and age-related diseases.

title: Cancer chemoprevention: Much has been done, but there is still much to do. State of the art and possible new approaches.
text: In the search for cancer chemoprevention strategies, significant progress has been made in the last thirty years. Understanding the process of cancer cell development has allowed for interventions such as lifestyle changes, natural compounds, and drugs to hinder or reverse this process. Notably, breast and colorectal cancer have seen considerable success. However, these strategies have yet to be widely implemented in clinical settings. This article examines the accomplishments, challenges, and future steps needed to enhance the effectiveness and practicality of chemoprevention strategies. Key areas for improvement include educating physicians to promote the goals and culture of chemoprevention, finding the optimal balance between risks and benefits, determining the minimum effective doses and intermittent schedules, tailoring interventions based on individual characteristics, and managing the costs of public and private health prevention programs.

title: Secreted Frizzled-related Protein 5 Diminishes Cardiac Inflammation and Protects the Heart from Ischemia/Reperfusion Injury.
text: The aim of this study was to examine the role of Secreted frizzled-related protein 5 (Sfrp5) in the heart during ischemic stress. Sfrp5 is known to inhibit non-canonical Wnt signaling and is found in high levels in white adipose tissue. To investigate its function, Sfrp5 knockout (KO) mice and wild-type (WT) mice were subjected to ischemia/reperfusion (I/R). At baseline, there were no observable differences between Sfrp5-KO and WT mice. However, after I/R, Sfrp5-KO mice had larger infarct sizes, increased cardiac myocyte apoptosis, and reduced cardiac function compared to WT mice. The ischemic lesions in Sfrp5-KO mice also had more Wnt5a-positive macrophages and higher expression of inflammatory cytokines and chemokines. In experiments with bone marrow-derived macrophages, Wnt5a activated JNK and increased inflammatory gene expression, but treatment with Sfrp5 blocked these effects. These findings suggest that Sfrp5 plays a role in suppressing inflammatory responses in the heart after I/R, potentially through non-canonical Wnt5a/JNK signaling.

title: Asymptomatic spinal cord lesions predict disease progression in radiologically isolated syndrome.
text: The advancement of neuroimaging technology has led to the discovery of incidental anomalies in the central nervous system (CNS). This includes the identification of unexpected brain abnormalities and asymptomatic spinal cord lesions in patients undergoing neuroimaging for reasons unrelated to multiple sclerosis (MS). The objective of this study was to determine if asymptomatic spinal cord lesions are associated with clinical progression in individuals with radiologically isolated syndrome (RIS). A retrospective review of RIS cases at the University of California, San Francisco Multiple Sclerosis Center was conducted. The presence of asymptomatic cervical spinal cord lesions on MRI was analyzed as a potential predictor for clinical progression. The results showed that out of 71 subjects with RIS, 25 had findings in the cervical spine that strongly suggested demyelinating disease. Of these subjects, 21 (84%) experienced clinical progression to either clinically isolated syndrome or primary progressive MS within a median time of 1.6 years from the date of RIS identification. The sensitivity, specificity, and positive predictive value of an asymptomatic spinal cord lesion for subsequent development of a demyelinating attack or primary progressive MS were 87.5%, 91.5%, and 84%, respectively. The odds ratio of clinical progression was 75.3, indicating a significant association. This association remained significant even after adjusting for potential confounders. In conclusion, these findings suggest that the presence of asymptomatic spinal cord lesions puts individuals with RIS at a high risk of developing acute or progressive events, independent of brain lesions on MRI.

title: YqhC regulates transcription of the adjacent Escherichia coli genes yqhD and dkgA that are involved in furfural tolerance
text: Previous findings have shown that the increased tolerance to furfural in an E. coli strain EMFR9 is attributed to the silencing of neighboring genes, yqhD and dkgA, which encode NADPH-dependent furfural oxidoreductases [Miller et al., Appl Environ Microbiol 75:4315–4323, 2009]. It has now been discovered that this gene silencing occurs due to the spontaneous insertion of an IS10 element into the coding region of yqhC, an upstream gene. YqhC shares similarities with transcriptional regulators from the AraC/XylS family and has been identified as a positive regulator of the adjacent operon that encodes YqhD and DkgA. This regulation was confirmed through the deletion of yqhC in the chromosome, the use of a firefly luciferase reporter plasmid for yqhC, and a direct comparison of furfural resistance and NADPH-dependent furfural reductase activity. Other closely related bacteria also possess orthologs of yqhC, yqhD, and dkgA in the same arrangement as in E. coli LY180, while more distantly related Gram-negative bacteria also contain orthologs of yqhC. Disrupting yqhC presents a valuable strategy for enhancing furfural tolerance in bacteria.

title: A direct role for Met endocytosis in tumorigenesis
text: The compartmentalization of signals produced by receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) endocytosis has become a significant factor in various cellular functions. In this study, we establish a direct connection between endocytosis and tumorigenicity using Met-activating mutations associated with tumors. These Met mutants display heightened endocytosis/recycling activity and reduced degradation, resulting in their accumulation on endosomes. This accumulation leads to the activation of the GTPase Rac1, the loss of actin stress fibers, and an increase in cell migration. By blocking endocytosis, we were able to inhibit the mutants' ability to grow independently of anchorage, as well as their capacity for in vivo tumorigenesis and metastasis, while still maintaining their activation. Interestingly, one mutant that was resistant to inhibition by a Met-specific tyrosine kinase inhibitor was found to be sensitive to endocytosis inhibition. Therefore, the oncogenicity of Met mutants arises not only from their activation but also from the alterations in their endocytic trafficking. This suggests that endosomal signaling may play a crucial role in regulating RTK-dependent tumorigenesis.

title: Immediate effects of droperidol
text: The researchers observed and recorded the subjective and behavioral reactions of 20 healthy individuals who took droperidol 5 mg as part of a cognitive challenge program. All participants experienced some form of akathisia. Half of the subjects felt dysphoric, but the causes of their dysphoria seemed to differ, and various other effects were also observed, such as sedation, dissociative experiences, changes in sensation, and subtle changes in appearance. The duration of these effects varied, lasting from a few hours to over a week. During the initial phase, participants had mixed understanding of the cause of their experiences. These findings have implications for the interpretation of cognitive challenge tests, the understanding of akathisia, clinical treatments, and the development of drugs. (© 1998 John Wiley & Sons, Ltd.)

title: Toxicity of Nerium oleander in the monkey (Cebus apella).
text:
The toxic effects of Nerium oleander were assessed in capuchin monkeys (Cebus apella) through the examination of various factors including clinical signs, hematologic and serum chemical values, and gross and microscopic lesions. The monkeys were administered dried and ground oleander leaves at intervals of 48 hours, with doses of 30, 7.5, and 3 mg/kg body weight. The cumulative lethal dose varied between 30 and 60 mg/kg body weight for monkeys receiving doses of 30 and 7.5 mg/kg body weight. However, monkeys that were given doses of 3 mg/kg body weight (total cumulative dose: 60 mg/kg) managed to survive. 

The observed clinical signs included vomiting, salivation, excessive urination, slow heart rate, vaginal bleeding, abortion, loss of appetite, constipation, weight loss, drowsiness, restlessness, weakness, and shallow and rapid breathing. Changes in blood values included an increase in white blood cell count, an increase in neutrophils, elevated levels of potassium, glutamic-oxalacetic transaminase, glutamic-pyruvic transaminase, blood urea nitrogen, and α-globulins, a decrease in calcium, glucose, total serum protein, albumin, and γ-globulin levels, as well as a decrease in reticulocyte count.

title: Plzf regulates limb and axial skeletal patterning
text: We have generated Zfp145−/− mice to investigate the role of the promyelocytic leukaemia zinc finger (Plzf) protein, which is encoded by the gene Zfp145 and belongs to the POZ/zinc-finger family of transcription factors. Our findings demonstrate that Plzf is crucial for the development of the limb and axial skeleton. Inactivation of Plzf leads to defects in the patterning of all skeletal structures in the limb, resulting in the transformation of anterior skeletal elements into posterior structures. We have also discovered that Plzf functions as a growth-inhibitory and pro-apoptotic factor in the limb bud. Furthermore, we have observed changes in the expression of genes from the abdominal b (Abdb) Hox gene complex and bone morphogenetic proteins (Bmps) in the developing limb of Zfp145−/− mice. Interestingly, Plzf regulates the expression of these genes independently of known patterning genes and without any abnormal polarizing activity. Additionally, Zfp145−/− mice exhibit homeotic transformations in the axial skeleton, with a shift towards anterior-directed patterning and corresponding alterations in Hox gene expression. Overall, our findings highlight the role of Plzf as a mediator of anterior-to-posterior (AP) patterning in both the axial and appendicular skeleton, and as a regulator of Hox gene expression.

title: Requirement for the ERI/DICER complex in endogenous RNA interference and sperm development in Caenorhabditis elegans.
text: Gene expression is regulated by small regulatory RNAs, with one class known as endogenous small interfering RNAs (endo siRNAs). These endo siRNAs are believed to negatively regulate cellular transcripts through a mechanism called endogenous RNA interference (endo RNAi). In the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans, the ERI/DICER complex, consisting of ERI-1/3/5, RRF-3, and DICER proteins, is responsible for mediating endo RNAi processes. To further understand the machinery involved in endo RNAi, we conducted a genetic screen and discovered two important components. The first is eri-9, which encodes a novel protein that interacts with DICER. The second is a missense mutation in the helicase domain of DICER, known as DCR-1(G492R). Animals lacking ERI-9 or carrying the DCR-1(G492R) mutation showed defects in endo siRNA expression and an inability to regulate mRNAs that share sequence homology with these endo siRNAs. This suggests that ERI-9 and the helicase domain of DICER play crucial roles in the endo RNAi pathway in C. elegans. We also identified a subset of Eri mutant animals (eri-1, rrf-3, eri-3, and dcr-1, but not eri-9 or ergo-1) that displayed temperature-sensitive, sperm-specific sterility and defects in X chromosome segregation. These mutants exhibited various abnormalities in sperm development, starting from cytokinesis and continuing through terminal differentiation. These findings not only uncover new components of the endo RNAi machinery but also reveal different requirements for the Eri factors in the germline responsible for sperm production. Additionally, they provide insights into the functional role of the ERI/DICER complex in sperm development.

title: Drug-induced thrombocytopenia: pathogenesis, evaluation, and management.
text: Although drugs are a frequent cause of acute immune-mediated thrombocytopenia in adults, the initial recognition of drug-induced thrombocytopenia (DITP) is often overlooked. Most cases of DITP are a result of drug-dependent antibodies that specifically target the drug's structure and tightly bind to platelets through their Fab regions, but only when the drug is present. A comprehensive database, accessible at www.ouhsc.edu/platelets, contains 1301 published reports detailing 317 drugs and provides information on the level of evidence supporting a causal relationship with thrombocytopenia. Typically, DITP occurs within 1 to 2 weeks after starting a new drug or suddenly after a single dose if the drug had been taken intermittently in the past. However, severe thrombocytopenia can immediately manifest after the initial administration of antithrombotic agents that inhibit fibrinogen binding to platelet GP IIb-IIIa, such as abciximab, tirofiban, and eptifibatide. Recovery from DITP usually begins within 1 to 2 days of discontinuing the drug and is typically complete within a week. Drug-dependent antibodies can persist for many years, underscoring the importance of confirming the drug's role and subsequently avoiding its use.

title: Costs and financial feasibility of malaria elimination
text: The lack of empirical evidence makes it difficult to determine the costs and benefits of transitioning malaria programs from control to elimination. In order to address this gap, we propose a conceptual framework to evaluate the economics of elimination, focusing on potential short-term and medium-term financial savings. Despite a lack of existing evidence, we conducted a review and calculated the net present value of elimination in five different locations, comparing it to effective control. The results showed that the probability of cost-saving over a 50-year period ranged from 0% to 42%, with only one site achieving cost-savings in the base case. These findings suggest that financial savings should not be the primary motivation for pursuing elimination, but rather the overall benefits should outweigh the marginal costs. It is crucial to conduct robust research to better understand the benefits of elimination and make informed decisions.

title: Expression of the angiogenic factors vascular endothelial cell growth factor, acidic and basic fibroblast growth factor, tumor growth factor beta-1, platelet-derived endothelial cell growth factor, placenta growth factor, and pleiotrophin in human primary breast cancer and its relation to angiogenes
text: The role of angiogenesis as a prognostic factor in breast cancer is significant, but the specific factors that control angiogenesis in the body are not well understood. We have studied the expression of seven angiogenic polypeptides in primary human breast cancers and also examined their relationship with estrogen receptor and vascular density. These polypeptides include vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and its four isoforms, transforming growth factor (TGF)-beta1, pleiotrophin, acidic and basic fibroblast growth factor (FGF), placental growth factor, and thymidine phosphorylase. We used RNase protection analysis to quantify their expression, and ELISA to measure beta-FGF. We also analyzed the estrogen receptor (ER), epidermal growth factor receptor, and vascular density in 64 primary breast cancers. We found that all tumors expressed at least six different vascular growth factors, with VEGF being the most abundant and the 121-amino acid form being the most prevalent. Thymidine phosphorylase and TGF-beta1 were also expressed at high levels. The expression of most angiogenic factors did not correlate with that of ER or vascular density, except for thymidine phosphorylase which showed a correlation coefficient of 0.3 (P = 0.03). We also observed significant associations between pleiotrophin and acidic FGF expression (P = 0.001), and between TGF-beta and platelet-derived endothelial cell growth factor expression (P = 0.001), suggesting a coordinated regulation of some vascular growth factors. In univariate analysis, high VEGF expression, as well as ER and epidermal growth factor receptor expression, were associated with poor prognosis (P = 0.03). We also measured basic FGF using ELISA and found that it was more highly expressed in tumors compared to normal breast tissues. These findings have implications for therapy, suggesting that agents targeting common features of these angiogenic factors, such as antagonism of heparin-binding activity, may be useful. Additionally, inhibiting endothelial migration or using agents directly toxic to endothelium could be beneficial in a combined approach to therapy.

title: Cnn1 inhibits the interactions between the KMN complexes of the yeast kinetochore
text:
The kinetochores are responsible for attaching the replicated chromosomes to the mitotic spindle and ensuring their proper transmission to the daughter cells. This process is facilitated by the KNL1Spc105, MIS12Mtw1, and NDC80Ndc80 complexes, collectively known as the KMN network, which mediate the binding between the kinetochores and the spindle. The attachment of the KMN network to the spindle is regulated by the Aurora BIpl1 and MPS1Mps1 kinases. However, it remains unclear if there are other mechanisms that support the activity of the KMN network during the cell cycle. 

In our study using budding yeast, we have discovered that a kinetochore protein called Cnn1 localizes to the base of the Ndc80 complex and plays a crucial role in maintaining a functional configuration of the KMN network. Cnn1 regulates the activity of the KMN network in a spatial and temporal manner by inhibiting the interaction between its complexes. The activity of Cnn1 reaches its peak during anaphase and is driven by the Cdc28, Mps1, and Ipl1 kinases.

title: Origin and functions of tissue macrophages.
text: Macrophages are present in various tissues throughout the body and play a role in maintaining balance and combating diseases. Recent findings indicate that most macrophages in adult tissues originate during embryonic development rather than from circulating monocytes. Each tissue has a unique combination of macrophages derived from embryonic and adult sources, but it remains uncertain whether macrophages from different origins can perform the same functions or if they have distinct roles in a stable condition. This new understanding also prompts a reevaluation of the role of circulating monocytes. Classical Ly6c(hi) monocytes patrol the spaces between cells in resting organs, while Ly6c(lo) nonclassical monocytes patrol the blood vessels. Inflammation triggers the differentiation of monocytes into macrophages, but it is unclear whether resident and newly recruited macrophages have similar functions during inflammation. In this article, we discuss the methods used to identify the complex origins of tissue macrophages and explore the relative contributions of the tissue environment and developmental origin in regulating macrophage functions during both stable and inflammatory conditions.

title: Treatment outcome of an unselected cohort of tuberculosis patients in relation to human immunodeficiency virus serostatus in Zomba Hospital, Malawi.
text: Limited information is available regarding the treatment outcomes of patients with smear-negative pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) or extrapulmonary tuberculosis (EPTB) in subsaharan Africa under routine program conditions. To address this gap, a prospective study was conducted at Zomba General Hospital in Malawi to assess the treatment outcomes of a diverse cohort of TB patients. Between July 1 and December 31, 1995, a total of 827 adult TB patients (451 men and 376 women) were enrolled in the study. The standardized treatment outcomes, including treatment completion, death, default, and transfer to another district, were evaluated based on the type of TB, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) serostatus, age, and gender. By the end of treatment, 254 patients (31%) had died, with half of the deaths occurring within the first month. The death rates were 19% among 386 patients with smear-positive PTB, 46% among 211 patients with smear-negative PTB, and 37% among 230 patients with EPTB. Additionally, 77% of the patients were HIV-positive. Among new patients, those who were HIV-positive had higher death rates compared to HIV-negative patients (hazard ratio [HR] 2.5; 95% confidence interval [95% CI] 1.6-3.8). Smear-negative patients had the highest death rates (HR 3.9; 95% CI 2.7-5.5 compared to smear-positive patients), followed by EPTB patients (HR 2.6, 95% CI 1.8-3.7 compared to smear-positive patients). Furthermore, death rates increased with age but were similar between men and women. The findings highlight the low treatment completion and high death rates among adult patients in Malawi with smear-negative PTB and EPTB, which are strongly associated with high levels of HIV infection. Consequently, national TB control programs in regions with a high prevalence of HIV should prioritize monitoring and improving treatment outcomes for patients with smear-negative PTB or EPTB.

title: Statin use and risk of gallstone disease followed by cholecystectomy.
text:
The prevalence of gallstone disease is high in western countries and has significant economic implications. Statins, which reduce cholesterol production in the liver, may lower the risk of cholesterol gallstones by decreasing cholesterol levels in the bile. However, there is limited data on this association in humans. 

The objective of this study was to examine the relationship between the use of statins, fibrates, or other lipid-lowering agents and the risk of developing gallstone disease requiring cholecystectomy. The study utilized a case-control analysis using the UK-based General Practice Research Database. Incident patients between 1994 and 2008 were identified, along with four controls per patient, matched on various factors. The study population consisted of 76% women, with a mean age of 53.4 years. Conditional logistic regression was used to estimate the odds ratio (OR) of developing gallstones requiring cholecystectomy in relation to exposure to lipid-lowering agents, taking into account exposure timing and duration. The ORs and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were adjusted for various factors such as smoking, body mass index, ischemic heart disease, stroke, and estrogen use. 

The main outcome measure was the adjusted OR (AOR) for developing gallstone disease requiring cholecystectomy in relation to exposure to lipid-lowering agents. 

The results showed that out of the total 27,035 patients who underwent cholecystectomy, 2,396 had used statins, compared to 8,868 controls. Current statin use (with the last prescription recorded within 90 days before the first-time diagnosis of the disease) was found to be 1.0% for patients and 0.8% for controls (AOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.95-1.27) for 1 to 4 prescriptions; 2.6% vs 2.4% (AOR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.77-0.93) for 5 to 19 prescriptions, and 3.2% vs 3.7% (AOR, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.59-0.70) for 20 or more prescriptions. The AORs for current use of statins defined as 20 or more prescriptions were consistent across different age, sex, and body mass index categories, as well as across different statin classes. 

In conclusion, long-term use of statins was found to be associated with a reduced risk of gallstones requiring cholecystectomy.

title: Chromatin remodeling in embryonic stem cells: regulating the balance between pluripotency and differentiation.
text: Embryonic stem cells possess boundless potential for self-renewal, while also being pluripotent, meaning they can differentiate into three distinct germ layers and ultimately give rise to various cell lineages. Specific factors responsible for pluripotency ensure that ES cells maintain an undifferentiated phenotype, while factors specific to each lineage counteract this to facilitate cell specialization. Alongside these crucial transcriptional regulators, epigenetic modifiers significantly contribute to regulating the equilibrium between pluripotency and differentiation by inducing alterations in chromatin structure.

title: The National Advisory Group on Immunization (NAGI) of the Republic of South Africa.
text: The National Advisory Group on Immunization (NAGI), formerly known as the National Immunization Technical Advisory Group (NITAG), was established in 1993 in South Africa. Its primary purpose is to provide guidance and advice to the National Department of Health (DoH) on matters pertaining to vaccination. Meetings are convened as necessary, but occur at least twice a year. The group's mandate encompasses vaccines, immunization, and other pertinent issues related to infectious diseases. NAGI is also responsible for making recommendations on vaccine schedules and formulations. The DoH and the Chairman of NAGI collaborate to set the meeting agendas. NAGI brings together experts from various fields relevant to vaccines and vaccinations, serving as a valuable resource in guiding the Expanded Program of Immunization (EPI) in South Africa.

title: Effect of n-3 long chain polyunsaturated fatty acid supplementation in pregnancy on infants’ allergies in first year of life: randomised controlled trial
text: The objective of this study was to determine if supplementing pregnant women at high risk of allergic disease with dietary n-3 long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids (LCPUFA) reduces the occurrence of immunoglobulin E associated eczema or food allergy in their infants at 1 year of age. The study followed up on infants at high hereditary risk of allergic disease who were part of the Docosahexaenoic Acid to Optimise Mother Infant Outcome (DOMInO) randomized controlled trial in Adelaide, South Australia. The intervention group received fish oil capsules providing 900 mg of n-3 LCPUFA daily from 21 weeks' gestation until birth, while the control group received vegetable oil capsules without n-3 LCPUFA. The main outcome measure was immunoglobulin E associated allergic disease at 1 year of age. The results showed no significant difference in the overall percentage of infants with immunoglobulin E associated allergic disease between the two groups. However, the percentage of infants diagnosed with atopic eczema and egg sensitization was lower in the n-3 LCPUFA group. The study concluded that n-3 LCPUFA supplementation during pregnancy did not reduce the overall incidence of immunoglobulin E associated allergies in the first year of life, but may have a positive effect on atopic eczema and egg sensitization. Further research is needed to determine the long-term effects of supplementation on respiratory allergic diseases and aeroallergen sensitization in childhood. The trial was registered in the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry under ACTRN12610000735055 (DOMInO trial: ACTRN12605000569606).

title: ModLoop: automated modeling of loops in protein structures.
text:
ModLoop is a web server designed to automate the modeling of loops in protein structures. Users can input the atomic coordinates of the protein structure in the Protein Data Bank format, along with the starting and ending residues of the segments they want to model. These segments should not exceed a total of 20 residues. The server then provides the coordinates of the non-hydrogen atoms in the modeled segments. 

To use ModLoop, users simply access the server through a user-friendly web interface and submit their input. The output is then sent to them via email. The server utilizes the loop modeling routine in MODELLER, which predicts loop conformations by satisfying spatial restraints, rather than relying on a database of known protein structures. 

To ensure a quick response time, ModLoop runs on a cluster of Linux PC computers. The server is freely accessible to academic users and can be found at http://salilab.org/modloop.

title: What is the best way to help caregivers in cancer and palliative care? A systematic literature review of interventions and their effectiveness.
text: Informal caregivers who provide care for cancer and palliative care patients often have significant needs and experience psychological distress. However, there is a lack of targeted interventions available for these caregivers, as identified in a literature review. To address this gap, a systematic review was conducted to identify interventions for caregivers of patients receiving home cancer and palliative care services. The review searched various databases including Medline, CancerLit, Psycinfo, and Cinahl using keywords such as carer(s), caregiver(s), palliative, and cancer. The selected papers focused on interventions for adult caregivers who were actively providing informal care for noninstitutionalized cancer and palliative care patients. A total of 22 interventions were identified, which included home nursing care, respite services, social networks and activity enhancement, problem solving and education, and group work. Among these interventions, nine were specifically targeted towards caregivers. Only six of the interventions had been evaluated, with two using a randomized control trial (RCT), three using a single group methodology, and one evaluated using facilitator feedback. The evaluation designs had limitations such as small sample sizes and a reliance on intervention descriptions and formative evaluations. Therefore, alternative approaches to RCTs should be considered due to methodological challenges. The current evidence primarily focuses on the feasibility and acceptability of the interventions rather than their effectiveness. It is crucial for practitioners and evaluators to prioritize the further development of intervention studies in this area.

title: Brief Internet-Based Intervention Reduces Posttraumatic Stress and Prolonged Grief in Parents after the Loss of a Child during Pregnancy: A Randomized Controlled Trial
text:
Background: The loss of a child during pregnancy can cause significant emotional distress for women and their partners, and may result in long-term psychiatric disorders. Internet-based interventions that utilize exposure techniques and cognitive restructuring have been shown to be effective for treating posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and prolonged grief. This study aimed to compare the effects of an Internet-based intervention for parents who have experienced prenatal loss with a waiting list condition (WLC).

Methods: Symptoms of PTSD were assessed using the Impact of Event Scale - Revised, while depression, anxiety, and general mental health were assessed using the Inventory of Complicated Grief and the Brief Symptom Inventory. A total of 228 participants (92% female) were randomly assigned to either a treatment group (TG; n = 115) or a WLC group (n = 113). The TG received a 5-week cognitive behavioral intervention that included self-confrontation, cognitive restructuring, and social sharing.

Results: The TG showed significant reductions in symptoms of posttraumatic stress, prolonged grief, depression, and anxiety compared to the WLC control group. Intention-to-treat analysis revealed treatment effects ranging from d = 0.84 to d = 1.02 for posttraumatic stress and prolonged grief from pre- to posttreatment. Further significant improvements in all symptoms of PTSD and prolonged grief were observed from the posttreatment evaluation to the 12-month follow-up. The attrition rate of 14% was relatively low.

Conclusions: The Internet-based intervention proved to be a feasible and cost-effective treatment, effectively reducing symptoms of posttraumatic stress, grief, depression, anxiety, and general mental health following pregnancy loss. It is recommended that low-threshold e-health interventions be further evaluated and routinely implemented to enhance psychological support for individuals who have experienced pregnancy loss.

title: Up-regulation of PPAR-gamma mRNA expression in the liver of obese patients: an additional reinforcing lipogenic mechanism to SREBP-1c induction.
text: The accumulation of triglycerides in the liver is an early characteristic of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) in individuals with obesity. NAFLD is a complex syndrome, and its underlying mechanisms are starting to be understood. This study aimed to measure the expression of liver peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ (PPAR-γ) mRNA as a signaling mechanism related to steatosis in obese patients with NAFLD. The researchers also examined the levels of sterol receptor element-binding protein 1c (SREBP-1c) mRNA, serum total adiponectin, high molecular weight (HMW)-adiponectin, and insulin resistance (IR) evolution in these patients. The study included 22 obese NAFLD patients (16 with steatosis and six with steatohepatitis) who underwent subtotal gastrectomy with gastrojejunal anastomosis in Roux-en-Y, as well as 16 nonobese subjects who underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy (controls). The results showed that liver PPAR-γ mRNA levels were significantly higher in obese patients with steatosis and steatohepatitis compared to the control group. These patients also exhibited increased levels of SREBP-1c, IR, and lower levels of serum total adiponectin and HMW-adiponectin. Liver PPAR-γ expression was positively associated with SREBP-1c mRNA levels, serum insulin levels, and IR, and negatively correlated with total adiponectin and HMW-adiponectin levels in serum. In conclusion, PPAR-γ is up-regulated in the liver of obese patients with NAFLD, which contributes to the development of hepatic steatosis along with SREBP-1c induction.

title: Ribosomal protein S17 gene (RPS17) is mutated in Diamond-Blackfan anemia.
text: Diamond-Blackfan anemia (DBA) is a congenital condition characterized by a specific type of anemia where there is a deficiency in red blood cell precursors in the bone marrow. This results in a normochromic macrocytic anemia. Additionally, around 40% of DBA patients also exhibit physical abnormalities. Currently, two genes, ribosomal protein (RP) S19 and RPS24, are known to be associated with the DBA phenotype. Mutations in these genes are found in 25% and approximately 1.4% of DBA patients, respectively. In this study, we have identified a mutation in another ribosomal protein, RPS17. This mutation affects the start codon for the translation of RPS17 protein, resulting in a change from T to G (c.2T>G). As a result, the natural start of RPS17 protein biosynthesis is eliminated. RNA analysis showed that the mutated allele was expressed, and a downstream start codon at position +158 was found to produce a short peptide consisting of only four amino acids (Met-Ser-Arg-Ile). This mutation occurred spontaneously, as all healthy family members carried the normal alleles. The discovery of a mutation in the third ribosomal protein of the small ribosomal subunit in DBA patients further supports the theory that impaired translation may be the primary cause of DBA pathogenesis.

title: An overview of the effective combination therapies for the treatment of breast cancer.
text: Breast cancer (BC) is typically categorized based on the presence of certain receptors on the cell nucleus, including hormone receptors like progesterone (PR) and estrogen (ER), as well as HER2. Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a form of cancer that lacks these three receptor proteins (ER/PR/HER2). Tumor cells with this type of cancer often display resistance to drugs, which reduces the effectiveness of chemotherapy. Drug resistance is generally caused by abnormal gene expression, but there are various types of drug resistance, such as efflux pumps that decrease drug concentration in cells, changes in membrane lipids that hinder drug uptake, altered drug targets, metabolic changes to the drug, inhibition of apoptosis, DNA repair, and alterations to cell cycle checkpoints. "Combination therapy" is widely recognized as an effective approach to treating breast cancer and other diseases. In this review, we provide examples of different nanocarriers used to simultaneously deliver multiple therapeutics (chemotherapeutic agents and nucleic acids) to drug-resistant tumor cells. Finally, we offer recommendations for future directions in co-delivery treatments.

title: Disturbed sleep in bipolar disorder is related to an elevation of IL-6 in peripheral monocytes.
text: Bipolar disorder is a serious mental illness characterized by persistent changes in sleep patterns, including the quality, duration, and structure of sleep. The reasons behind these sleep alterations in bipolar disorder are not fully understood, making management challenging yet crucial. Sleep is influenced by various cytokines, such as IL-6. Higher levels of IL-6 have been linked to poorer sleep quality and similar sleep architecture changes seen in bipolar disorder. The therapeutic use of Interferon, which increases IL-6 levels in the spinal cord, has been found to worsen sleep quality. Conversely, blocking IL-6 with tocilizumab in rheumatoid arthritis has been associated with improved sleep quality. In bipolar disorder, IL-6 levels are elevated, particularly in the mRNA coding for IL-6 found in peripheral monocytes. We propose that the sleep changes observed in bipolar disorder are connected to the increased IL-6 levels and the heightened expression of mRNA coding for IL-6 in peripheral monocytes.

title: Targeted blockade of TGF-β and IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 pathways inhibits lung cancer growth promoted by bone marrow-derived myofibroblasts
text: To investigate the interaction between myofibroblasts (MFs) and lung cancer cells, the role of TGF-β and IL-6 was examined. Two lung cancer cell lines (Lewis and CTM-167) were stimulated with IL-6, MF-conditioned medium (MF-CM), or MFs, with or without inhibitors for TGF-β signaling (SB431542) and JAK2/STAT3 signaling (JSI-124). Similarly, MFs were stimulated with TGF-β, cancer cell-conditioned medium (cancer cell-CM), or cancer cells, with or without SB431542 and JSI-124. Various parameters such as cell proliferation, cytokine levels, mRNA and protein expression were measured. Mice with xenograft tumors were treated with SB431542 or JSI-124 and monitored for 45 days. In co-culture systems, MFs secreted high levels of IL-6, while cancer cells produced high levels of TGF-β. Recombinant IL-6 and MF-CM activated STAT3 and upregulated TGF-β in cancer cells. Conversely, cancer cell-CM or TGF-β stimulated MFs to produce IL-6. Inhibition of JAK2/STAT3 and TGF-β signaling significantly reduced cell proliferation in vitro and tumor growth in vivo in lung cancer cells. Our study revealed a positive feedback signaling loop between the TGF-β and IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 pathways, mediating the interactions between MFs and lung cancer cells. Targeting this signaling loop could be a promising approach for lung cancer prevention and therapy.

title: Production of cloned mice and ES cells from adult somatic cells by nuclear transfer: how to improve cloning efficiency?
text: Despite advancements in cloning technology over the past decade, the success rate for producing live offspring through cloning remains low, with less than 5% of cloned embryos reaching full development. This low success rate is believed to be due to epigenetic errors, such as abnormal DNA hypermethylation, but the process of "reprogramming" these errors is not well understood. However, we have made progress in developing a stable cloning method in mice, where donor nuclei are directly injected into oocytes using a precise micromanipulator. While only a few labs are currently able to clone mice from adult somatic cells, this technique holds promise for future research in basic biology. One potential application is the generation of embryonic stem cell lines from a patient's own somatic cells, known as NT-ES cells. We have demonstrated that NT-ES cells are comparable to ES cells derived from fertilized embryos and can be relatively easily generated from various mouse genotypes and cell types. Although direct cloning may be more challenging, the NT-ES cell technique has potential applications in regenerative medicine and the preservation of genetic resources. This review explores methods to improve cloning efficiency, establish NT-ES cells, and explore further applications.

title: Recruitment of Tat to heterochromatin protein HP1 via interaction with CTIP2 inhibits human immunodeficiency virus type 1 replication in microglial cells.
text: We have discovered that the Tat protein of HIV-1, which is responsible for activating viral gene expression, can be effectively blocked in human microglial cells by a nuclear receptor cofactor called chicken ovalbumin upstream promoter transcription factor-interacting protein 2 (CTIP2). When CTIP2 is overexpressed, it suppresses HIV-1 replication by inhibiting Tat-mediated activation. On the other hand, CTIP1, a related protein, does not have any effect on Tat function or viral replication. Through the use of confocal microscopy, we observed that overexpression of CTIP2, but not CTIP1, disrupts the nuclear localization of Tat and causes it to accumulate in ball-like structures induced by CTIP2 in the nucleus. Furthermore, our research shows that CTIP2 interacts and colocalizes with a protein called HP1alpha, which is associated with heterochromatin. The CTIP2 protein contains two domains, 145-434 and 717-813, that are responsible for interacting with Tat and HP1, respectively. CTIP2 and HP1alpha form a complex with Tat, where the 145-434 domain of CTIP2 interacts with the N-terminal region of Tat, and the 717-813 domain binds to HP1. We confirmed the importance of this Tat binding interface and Tat's relocation within the nucleus through analysis of CTIP2 deletion mutants. Our findings suggest that CTIP2 inhibits HIV-1 expression by recruiting Tat into CTIP2-induced structures and relocating it to inactive regions of the chromatin through the formation of the Tat-CTIP2-HP1alpha complex. This discovery reveals a novel mechanism of Tat inactivation through subnuclear relocation, which could potentially lead to the inhibition of viral pathogenesis.

title: Cryptochrome Mediates Circadian Regulation of cAMP Signaling and Hepatic Gluconeogenesis
text:
During periods of fasting, mammals maintain normal levels of glucose in their bodies by stimulating the production of glucose in the liver, a process known as hepatic gluconeogenesis. This is triggered by the increase in two hormones, glucagon and epinephrine, which activate hepatic gluconeogenesis. These hormones cause the phosphorylation of a protein called cAMP response element-binding protein (Creb) and the dephosphorylation of another protein called Creb-regulated transcription coactivator-2 (Crtc2). These two proteins are key regulators of the gluconeogenesis process.

The regulation of hepatic gluconeogenesis is also influenced by the circadian clock, which helps coordinate glucose metabolism with changes in the external environment. The circadian control of gene expression is achieved through the action of two transcriptional activators, Clock and Bmal1. These activators stimulate the production of repressor proteins called cryptochrome (Cry1 and Cry2) and Period (Per1, Per2, and Per3), which then feedback on the activity of Clock and Bmal1.

In this study, we demonstrate that the activity of Creb during fasting is modulated by Cry1 and Cry2, which are rhythmically expressed in the liver. Cry1 expression is elevated during the transition from night to day, and it reduces the expression of genes involved in fasting gluconeogenesis by blocking the increase in intracellular cAMP levels and the phosphorylation of Creb mediated by glucagon. Through biochemical experiments, we found that Cry1 inhibits the accumulation of cAMP in response to activation of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), but not in response to forskolin, a direct activator of adenyl cyclase. Cry proteins appear to directly modulate GPCR activity by interacting with G(s)α.

Furthermore, when Cry1 is overexpressed in the liver of insulin-resistant db/db mice, it leads to lower blood glucose levels and improved insulin sensitivity. This suggests that compounds that enhance the activity of cryptochrome proteins may have therapeutic benefits for individuals with type 2 diabetes.

title: Toll-like receptor 4 gene Asp299Gly polymorphism in myocardial infarction: a meta-analysis of 15,148 subjects.
text: The association between the toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) gene Asp299Gly (+896 A/G) polymorphism and the risk of myocardial infarction (MI) remains controversial. Therefore, a comprehensive meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate the potential association between this gene variant and the risk of MI. Various databases including PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CBMdisc, CNKI, and Google Scholar were searched until February 6, 2013. Statistical tests were performed using Stata 11.0. A total of 10 studies from nine articles were included in the final meta-analysis, encompassing 8299 MI cases and 6849 controls. Overall, the results showed no significant association between the TLR4 gene Asp299Gly polymorphism and the risk of MI. Specifically, when comparing the G allele with the A allele, the odds ratio (OR) was 0.95 (95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.74-1.22, p = 0.71). Similarly, no significant association was found when comparing G/G with A/A (OR = 1.03, 95% CI = 0.54-1.98, p = 0.93), G/G with A/G+A/A (OR = 1.05, 95% CI = 0.55-2.03, p = 0.87), and G/G+A/G with A/A (OR = 0.92, 95% CI = 0.75-1.13, p = 0.42). Subgroup analysis based on the source of controls also revealed a lack of evidence for a significant association between the TLR4 gene Asp299Gly polymorphism and the risk of MI. In conclusion, this meta-analysis suggests that the TLR4 gene Asp299Gly polymorphism is not associated with the risk of MI.

title: Matrix metalloproteinase and proinflammatory cytokine production by chondrocytes of human osteoarthritic cartilage: associations with degenerative changes.
text:
