These measures were assessed over a four-week baseline period, after four and eight weeks of treatment, and at one, six, and twelve months following the treatment. Prior to the study, each patient completed the MMPI questionnaire. The results of split-plot ANOVAs indicated that, compared to the baseline, the frequency of headache episodes, analgesic consumption, and the headache index significantly decreased over time at one month after treatment and during the twelve-month follow-up. However, there was no significant difference between the effects of acupuncture and placebo treatment. None of the individual scales of the MMPI questionnaire predicted the response to treatment. However, the average MMPI profile of acupuncture non-responders showed the presence of 'Conversion V'.

title: TCR stimulation with modified anti-CD3 mAb expands CD8+ T cell population and induces CD8+CD25+ Tregs.
text: Modified anti-CD3 monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) are being explored as a potential method to promote immunologic tolerance in conditions like transplantation and autoimmunity, such as type 1 diabetes. In a study involving patients with type 1 diabetes, we observed that those who responded positively to treatment with a modified anti-CD3 mAb [hOKT3gamma1(Ala-Ala)] showed an increase in the number of CD8+ cells in their peripheral blood. Our findings demonstrate that the anti-CD3 mAb activated CD8+ T cells both in laboratory settings and in the patients themselves, leading to the generation of regulatory CD8+CD25+ T cells. These regulatory cells suppressed the responses of CD4+ cells to the mAb and to antigens. The regulatory CD8+CD25+ cells expressed CTLA4 and Foxp3 and required physical contact to exert their inhibitory effects. Furthermore, during mAb treatment, Foxp3 expression was also induced in CD8+ T cells of the patients, suggesting a potential mechanism by which the anti-CD3 mAb modulates the immune response through the generation of a specific subset of regulatory CD8+ T cells.

title: Interactions between Non-Physician Clinicians and Industry: A Systematic Review
text:
BACKGROUND
As restrictions on interactions between physicians and the industry increase, industry marketing may shift towards targeting other healthcare professionals. Recent health policy developments have made the decision-making of non-physician clinicians even more important. This systematic review aims to examine the types and implications of interactions between non-physician clinicians and the industry in clinical practice.

METHODS AND FINDINGS
We conducted a search of MEDLINE and Web of Science from January 1, 1946, to June 24, 2013, following PRISMA guidelines. Non-physician clinicians eligible for inclusion were Registered Nurses, nurse prescribers, Physician Assistants, pharmacists, dieticians, and physical or occupational therapists. Trainee samples were excluded. Fifteen studies met the inclusion criteria. The data were qualitatively synthesized into eight outcome domains: nature and frequency of industry interactions; attitudes towards industry; perceived ethical acceptability of interactions; perceived marketing influence; perceived reliability of industry information; preparation for industry interactions; reactions to industry relations policy; and management of industry interactions. Non-physician clinicians reported interacting with the pharmaceutical and infant formula industries. Clinicians from various disciplines regularly met with pharmaceutical representatives and relied on them for practice information. They frequently received industry "information," attended sponsored "education," and distributed similar materials to patients. Clinicians generally considered this ethical and believed they could detect promotional content while benefiting from industry information. Free samples were among the most common and accepted ways that clinicians interacted with the industry. The included studies were observational and varied in methodological rigor, so the findings may not be generalizable. However, this review is the first, to our knowledge, to provide a descriptive analysis of this literature.

CONCLUSIONS
Non-physician clinicians generally have positive attitudes towards industry interactions, despite recognizing issues related to bias. This suggests that industry interactions are normalized in clinical practice across non-physician disciplines. Industry relations policy should address all disciplines and be consistently implemented to mitigate conflicts of interest and address the potential impact of these interactions on patient care. Please refer to the Editors' Summary for more information.

title: Emtricitabine-tenofovir concentrations and pre-exposure prophylaxis efficacy in men who have sex with men.
text: The determination of drug concentrations that provide protection against HIV-1 acquisition has not yet been established. We conducted a study within the iPrEx trial to assess drug concentrations in men who have sex with men. In this trial, men were given daily oral doses of emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP). We found that the presence of the drug was less frequent in the blood plasma and viable cryopreserved peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) of HIV-infected individuals compared to controls at the same time point of the study. Additionally, the drug was less frequently detected in the 90 days leading up to the discovery of HIV in these cases. An intracellular concentration of the active form of tenofovir, called tenofovir-diphosphate (TFV-DP), of 16 fmol per million PBMCs was associated with a 90% reduction in HIV acquisition compared to the placebo group. Another study, the STRAND trial, examined directly observed dosing and found that TFV-DP concentrations corresponding to two doses per week resulted in a 76% reduction in HIV risk, four doses per week resulted in a 96% reduction, and seven doses per week resulted in a 99% reduction. These findings suggest that prophylactic benefits can be achieved with a range of doses and drug concentrations, providing insights for optimizing PrEP regimens for this population.

title: Clinical outcomes following institution of the Canadian universal leukoreduction program for red blood cell transfusions.
text: Several countries have implemented a policy of universal leukoreduction in their blood supply, but its impact on postoperative mortality and infection is not clear. The objective of this study was to evaluate the clinical outcomes after the adoption of a national universal prestorage leukoreduction program for blood transfusions. The study was conducted from August 1998 to August 2000 in 23 hospitals in Canada, enrolling 14,786 patients who received red blood cell transfusions following cardiac surgery, hip fracture repair, or intensive care after surgery or trauma. The intervention was the introduction of a universal prestorage leukoreduction program by two Canadian blood agencies. The main outcome measures were in-hospital mortality and serious nosocomial infections occurring after the first transfusion and at least 2 days after the procedure or ICU admission. Secondary outcomes included rates of posttransfusion fever and antibiotic use. The results showed that unadjusted in-hospital mortality rates were significantly lower after the introduction of leukoreduction compared to the control period. The adjusted odds of death following leukoreduction were also reduced. However, serious nosocomial infections did not decrease. The frequency of posttransfusion fevers and antibiotic use decreased significantly following leukoreduction. In conclusion, a national universal leukoreduction program may be associated with decreased mortality, as well as decreased fever episodes and antibiotic use after red blood cell transfusion in high-risk patients.

title: Failure of continuous venovenous hemofiltration to prevent death in paraquat poisoning.
text: Paraquat poisoning is characterized by the failure of multiple organs and the development of pulmonary fibrosis, leading to respiratory failure. Within three days of ingesting paraquat, many individuals experience circulatory collapse, which is a major cause of early death. Recent studies have suggested that continuous venovenous hemofiltration (CVVH) may play a role in treating multiorgan failure by promoting hemodynamic stability. To investigate this further, we conducted a study involving 80 patients with paraquat poisoning between August 1996 and February 1999. The average amount ingested was 2.1 +/- 1.0 mouthfuls of 20% concentrate. All patients received hemoperfusion (HP) within 24 hours of ingestion, with an average duration of 6.4 +/- 3.0 hours. They were then randomly assigned to either the HP-alone group or the HP-CVVH group. Forty-four patients underwent HP alone, while 36 patients underwent CVVH (average duration of 57.4 +/- 31.3 hours; ultrafiltration volume of 40.2 +/- 4.8 L/d) after HP. The results showed that the time to death after ingestion was significantly longer in the HP-CVVH group compared to the HP group (5.0 +/- 5.0 days versus 2.5 +/- 2.1 days; P < 0.05). However, there was no difference in mortality rates between the two groups (66.7% versus 63.6%; P = 0.82). In the HP group, early circulatory collapse was the primary cause of death, while in the HP-CVVH group, late respiratory failure was the main cause. In conclusion, prophylactic CVVH following HP prevented early death caused by circulatory collapse and extended survival time. However, it did not prevent late death caused by respiratory failure and did not provide a survival advantage in cases of acute paraquat poisoning.

title: The antidiabetic effect of mesenchymal stem cells is unrelated to their transdifferentiation potential but to their capability to restore Th1/Th2 balance and to modify the pancreatic microenvironment.
text:
Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is a chronic metabolic disease caused by the autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing cells. Previous studies on animal models of T1DM have shown that the administration of multipotent mesenchymal stromal cells, also known as mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), can regenerate pancreatic islets. However, the mechanisms behind this effect are not well understood. Our objective was to investigate whether donor MSCs can differentiate into pancreatic β-cells and modify the systemic and pancreatic markers of T1DM. 

We conducted an experiment where syngeneic MSCs were intravenously administered to mice with T1DM. We observed that the mice's hyperglycemia was reversed, but no insulin-producing cells derived from the donor MSCs were found. Instead, we found that the MSCs engrafted into secondary lymphoid organs 7 and 65 days after transplantation. This was accompanied by a decrease in autoaggressive T cells and an increase in regulatory T cells, both systemically and locally. Furthermore, in the pancreas of MSC-treated mice with T1DM, we observed a shift in the cytokine profile from proinflammatory to anti-inflammatory. Although MSC transplantation did not reduce pancreatic cell apoptosis, it did restore local expression and increase circulating levels of epidermal growth factor, a pancreatic trophic factor. 

Therefore, the antidiabetic effect of intravenously administered MSCs is not due to their ability to differentiate into pancreatic β-cells, but rather their capacity to restore the balance between Th1 and Th2 immune responses and modify the pancreatic microenvironment. These findings are important to consider when designing clinical trials to evaluate MSC transplantation in T1DM patients, as the presence of endogenous precursors appears to be crucial for restoring glycemic control.

title: Tmem27: a cleaved and shed plasma membrane protein that stimulates pancreatic beta cell proliferation.
text: The mechanisms that control the replication of fully developed beta cells are not yet understood. In this study, we present the discovery and analysis of a transmembrane protein called Tmem27 (also known as collectrin) in pancreatic beta cells. We found that the expression of Tmem27 is decreased in Tcf1(-/-) mice and increased in mouse models with hypertrophy of the endocrine pancreas. Tmem27 forms dimers and its extracellular domain is glycosylated, cleaved, and released from the surface of beta cells. This cleavage process is specific to beta cells and does not occur in other cell types. When full-length Tmem27 is overexpressed, there is an increase in thymidine incorporation, indicating enhanced cell replication. Conversely, silencing Tmem27 using RNA interference leads to a reduction in cell replication. Additionally, transgenic mice with elevated Tmem27 expression in pancreatic beta cells show an increase in beta cell mass. These findings highlight the role of Tmem27 as a transmembrane protein that regulates the growth of pancreatic islets.

title: The ATM missense mutation p.Ser49Cys (c.146C>G) and the risk of breast cancer.
text:
Ataxia telangiectasia is caused by a homozygous mutation in the ATM gene, while individuals with a heterozygous mutation may have a higher risk of developing breast cancer. Our study examined a total of 22 different variants of the ATM gene. Out of these, 18 variants were analyzed in two large population-based studies conducted in the United States and Poland. Additionally, four variants were analyzed in a total of 2,856 breast cancer cases and 3,344 controls from both studies.

One of the variants, known as the Ser49Cys (c.146C>G, p. S49C) missense mutation, was found in approximately 2% of the subjects. This mutation was more prevalent in the breast cancer cases compared to the controls in both study populations. The combined odds ratio (OR) for this mutation was 1.69 (95% CI, 1.19-2.40; P=0.004).

Another missense mutation, known as Phe858Leu (c.2572T>C, p. F858L), was also found in approximately 2% of the subjects. This mutation was associated with a significantly increased risk of breast cancer in the U.S. study, but not in the Polish study. The combined odds ratio for this mutation was 1.44 (95% CI, 0.98-2.11; P=0.06).

These findings provide strong evidence that missense mutations in the ATM gene, particularly the p. S49C mutation, may be linked to an increased susceptibility to breast cancer. However, due to their low frequency, larger sample sizes are needed to further confirm these associations.

title: A diffusion tensor magnetic resonance imaging study of corpus callosum from adult patients with migraine complicated with depressive/anxious disorder.
text:
The objective of this study was to examine the potential abnormalities in the microstructure of the corpus callosum (CC) in adult patients with migraine without aura who also have depressive/anxious disorder. Emotional disorders, particularly depression and anxiety, are more common in individuals with migraine. However, the underlying mechanism of migraine complicated with depressive/anxious disorder is not well understood. 

The study utilized diffusion tensor magnetic resonance imaging to assess 12 adult patients with simple migraine (without aura and without depressive/anxious disorder) (S-M group), 12 adult patients with complicated migraine (without aura but complicated with depressive/anxious disorder) (Co-M group), and 12 healthy subjects of similar age and sex (Control group). Fractional anisotropy (FA) and apparent diffusion coefficient were measured at different regions of the CC. 

The results showed significant differences in FA values at all CC locations among the three groups. Both the S-M and Co-M groups had significantly lower FA values compared to the control group (P < .05 and P < .01, respectively). The Co-M group also had significantly lower FA values than the S-M group (P < .01). However, there were no significant differences in apparent diffusion coefficient values among the groups (P > .05). 

Furthermore, negative correlations were observed between FA values of the genu of the CC and disease duration, as well as FA values of the genu and body of the CC and headache frequency (P < .05). Negative correlations were also found between FA values at all CC locations and Hamilton anxiety and Hamilton depression scores (both P < .05). 

In conclusion, this study suggests that there may be changes in the integrity of neurofibrotic microstructures in the CC of migraine patients with depressive/anxious disorder, which could serve as a potential neuroanatomical basis for these conditions.

title: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma agonists for the Prevention of Adverse events following percutaneous coronary Revascularization--results of the PPAR study.
text:
BACKGROUND
Patients who have metabolic syndrome are at a higher risk for cardiovascular complications. Our objective was to determine if peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma agonists had any positive impact on patients with metabolic syndrome who were undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).

METHODS
We conducted a study with 200 patients who had metabolic syndrome and were undergoing PCI. These patients were randomly assigned to receive either rosiglitazone or a placebo, and they were followed for a period of 1 year. We measured carotid intima-medial thickness (CIMT), inflammatory markers, lipid levels, brain natriuretic peptide, and clinical events at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months.

RESULTS
There was no significant difference in CIMT between the two groups. The 12-month composite end point of death, myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, or any recurrent ischemia was not different between the groups (31.4% vs 30.2%, P = .99). The rate of death, MI, or stroke at 12 months was slightly lower in the rosiglitazone group (11.9% vs 6.4%, P = .19). There was a trend towards a greater decrease over time in high-sensitivity C-reactive protein values compared to baseline in the rosiglitazone group compared to the placebo group at both 6 months (-35.4% vs -15.8%, P = .059) and 12 months (-40.0% vs -20.9%, P = .089). Additionally, there was a higher increase in high-density lipoprotein (+15.5% vs +4.1%, P = .05) and a lower decrease in triglycerides (-13.9% vs +14.9%, P = .004) in the rosiglitazone group. There was a trend towards a lower incidence of new onset diabetes in the rosiglitazone group (0% vs 3.3%, P = .081), and no cases of symptomatic hypoglycemia were reported. There was no increase in new onset clinical heart failure in the rosiglitazone group, and there was no significant change in brain natriuretic peptide levels.

CONCLUSIONS
Patients with metabolic syndrome who undergo PCI are at a higher risk for future cardiovascular events. In this population, rosiglitazone treatment for 12 months did not appear to have an effect on CIMT. However, it did show beneficial effects on high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, high-density lipoprotein, and triglyceride levels. Further research on the use of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor agonists in patients with metabolic syndrome undergoing PCI may be necessary.

title: Accumulation of hydroxyethyl starch in human and animal tissues: a systematic review
text:
A systematic review was conducted to examine the clinical and preclinical data on the storage of hydroxyethyl starch (HES) in tissues. The search was performed on MEDLINE (PubMed) and abstracts were screened based on specific criteria to identify articles with original data on HES tissue accumulation. A total of 48 studies were included in the review, consisting of 37 human studies with 635 patients and 11 animal studies.

The most common reason for fluid infusion, accounting for 282 patients (45.9%), was surgery. The studies showed that HES was localized in various tissues, with 17 studies demonstrating its presence in the skin, 12 in the kidney, 8 in the liver, and 5 in the bone marrow. HES deposition was also found in other sites such as lymph nodes, spleen, lung, pancreas, intestine, muscle, trophoblast, and placental stroma. Among the major organs, the highest concentration of HES was found in the kidney.

The uptake of HES into intracellular vacuoles was observed within 30 minutes after infusion. The storage of HES in tissues was cumulative and increased in proportion to the dose administered. However, in 15% of patients, storage and associated symptoms were observed even at the lowest cumulative doses (0.4 g kg−1). Some HES deposits were found to be extremely long-lasting, persisting for 8 years or more in the skin and 10 years in the kidney.

Pruritus, or itching, associated with HES storage was described in 17 studies, and renal dysfunction was reported in ten studies. In one randomized trial included in the review, HES infusion resulted in osmotic nephrosis-like lesions, indicating HES storage (p = 0.01), and also increased the need for renal replacement therapy (odds ratio, 9.50; 95% confidence interval, 1.09–82.7; p = 0.02).

The distribution of HES in tissues was generally similar between animals and humans. The review concluded that HES storage in tissues is widespread, rapid, cumulative, often long-lasting, and potentially harmful.

title: Cationic host defense (antimicrobial) peptides.
text: Cationic host defense peptides, which are part of the antimicrobial peptide family, are found in a wide range of organisms, including insects, plants, mammals, and non-mammalian vertebrates. While they have been shown to directly combat bacteria, fungi, parasites, and viruses, it is now understood that these peptides also play a crucial role in regulating the innate immune response. Recent studies have revealed that these peptides can act as effective adjuvants, work in synergy with other immune factors, influence the adaptive response, and promote wound healing. Furthermore, ongoing research is uncovering the mechanisms by which these peptides function, allowing for the development of more efficient therapeutic agents based on these natural compounds.

title: A mental health intervention for schoolchildren exposed to violence: a randomized controlled trial.
text: The effectiveness of psychological interventions for children with symptoms of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) resulting from witnessing or being exposed to violence has not been studied through randomized controlled trials. This study aimed to assess the effectiveness of a school-based intervention, collaboratively designed, in reducing symptoms of PTSD and depression in children exposed to violence. The study was conducted during the 2001-2002 academic year and involved sixth-grade students from two large middle schools in Los Angeles who reported exposure to violence and had clinically significant levels of PTSD symptoms. The intervention consisted of a 10-session standardized cognitive-behavioral therapy called the Cognitive-Behavioral Intervention for Trauma in Schools, delivered by trained school mental health clinicians. The students were randomly assigned to either an early intervention group or a wait-list delayed intervention comparison group. The main outcome measures included child-reported symptoms of PTSD and depression, parent-reported psychosocial dysfunction, and teacher-reported classroom problems. The results showed that after three months of intervention, the early intervention group had significantly lower scores on symptoms of PTSD, depression, and psychosocial dysfunction compared to the wait-list delayed intervention group. However, there were no significant differences between the two groups in teacher-reported classroom problems. At six months, after both groups received the intervention, there were no significant differences between the groups in symptoms of PTSD, depression, psychosocial function, and teacher-reported classroom behaviors. In conclusion, a standardized 10-session cognitive-behavioral group intervention can effectively reduce symptoms of PTSD and depression in students exposed to violence and can be delivered by trained school-based mental health clinicians on school campuses.

title: Knowledge gaps and misconceptions about coronary heart disease among U.S. South Asians.
text:
BACKGROUND: Despite the higher risk of coronary heart disease (CHD) among South Asians compared to other racial/ethnic groups in the US, there is a lack of research addressing this disparity. 

PURPOSE: This study aimed to develop culturally targeted CHD prevention messages for the rapidly growing South Asian community by examining their knowledge and beliefs about CHD. 

METHODS: Data collected from January to July 2008 in a cross-sectional study of 270 South Asian adults in Illinois were analyzed in 2009. Standardized questionnaires were used for interviews conducted in English, Hindi, or Urdu. Multivariate regression models were employed to explore the associations between sociodemographics and CHD knowledge, as well as attitudes about preventability. 

RESULTS: The study found that 81% of respondents had one or more CHD risk factors. The majority (89%) reported having little or no knowledge about CHD. Stress was the most commonly mentioned risk factor (44%), while few mentioned controlling blood pressure (11%), cholesterol (10%), or diabetes (5%) for prevention. Additionally, 53% believed that heart attacks are not preventable. Lower education level, being interviewed in Urdu or Hindi, and low level of acculturation were associated with less knowledge and the belief that CHD is not preventable. 

CONCLUSIONS: The study revealed that a majority of South Asians believed CHD is not preventable and had limited awareness of modifiable risk factors. To address this, CHD education should focus on filling knowledge gaps that may impact risk factor control and behavior change. It may be necessary to tailor educational messages to specific subgroups (e.g., based on education and language) for maximum effectiveness.

title: Innate host defense requires TFEB-mediated transcription of cytoprotective and antimicrobial genes.
text: The expression of defense genes in animals to fight off infections is crucial and must occur at the right place and time. To understand how this control is achieved, we investigated the involvement of transcription factors in host defense using the model organism Caenorhabditis elegans. Our unbiased approach led us to discover that a transcription factor called HLH-30 (known as TFEB in mammals) plays a key role in host defense. HLH-30 was activated shortly after infection with Staphylococcus aureus and was responsible for driving nearly 80% of the host response, including the expression of antimicrobial and autophagy genes that are essential for the host's ability to tolerate the infection. We also observed rapid activation of TFEB in murine macrophages upon S. aureus infection, where it was necessary for the proper induction of several proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines. These findings suggest that TFEB is an important, yet previously underestimated, transcription factor in the host's response to infection, and it has likely been conserved throughout evolution.

title: DAP kinase regulates JNK signaling by binding and activating protein kinase D under oxidative stress
text: The cellular responses to oxidative stress are mediated by the stress-activated kinase JNK. In this study, we demonstrate that DAP kinase (DAPk), a protein kinase that promotes cell death, plays a crucial role in the JNK signaling pathway induced by oxidative stress. We have identified protein kinase D (PKD) as a new target of DAPk and have shown that DAPk physically interacts with PKD in response to oxidative stress. Additionally, we have found that DAPk activates PKD in cells and that the phosphorylation of JNK by ectopically expressed DAPk can be reduced by decreasing PKD expression or inhibiting its catalytic activity. Furthermore, when DAPk expression is knocked down, there is a significant decrease in JNK activation under oxidative stress, indicating that DAPk is essential for JNK signaling activation in these conditions. Finally, we have discovered that DAPk is necessary for cell death under oxidative stress, and this process exhibits the characteristics of caspase-independent necrotic cell death. Overall, our findings highlight the important role of DAPk and its specific interaction with PKD in regulating the JNK signaling network during oxidative stress.

title: The changes of antioxidant defense system caused by quercetin administration do not lead to DNA damage and apoptosis in the spleen and bone marrow cells of rats.
text: The purpose of this study was to investigate the effects of quercetin on oxidative activity in the bone marrow and spleen cells of rats. Quercetin has been found to have both anti-oxidant and pro-oxidant properties. The rats in the experiment were given daily doses of either 8 or 80mg/kg of quercetin for 40 days. The levels of ferric ion reducing antioxidant power (FRAP) and malonodialdehyde were measured to assess the intracellular redox state. The expression of HO-1 mRNA was examined using real-time PCR. DNA damage was evaluated using the alkaline-labile comet assay. The potential pro-apoptotic effects of quercetin were determined using the FITC-Annexin V kit. The concentrations of quercetin and isorhamnetin in the serum were analyzed using HPLC-ECD. The results showed that the levels of MDA and FRAP were significantly reduced in the spleen and bone marrow cells of rats treated with 80mg/kg of quercetin compared to the control rats. No significant changes were observed when a lower dose of quercetin was administered. The expression of HO-1 mRNA in the bone marrow cells increased in a dose-dependent manner with quercetin treatment. Quercetin did not cause DNA damage or apoptosis in the examined cells. These findings suggest that quercetin-induced changes in antioxidant activity do not lead to DNA damage or pro-apoptotic effects in vivo.

title: Mutated KRAS results in overexpression of DUSP4, a MAP-kinase phosphatase, and SMYD3, a histone methyltransferase, in rectal carcinomas.
text: Mutations in the KRAS oncogene can indicate resistance to antibodies targeting the epithelial growth factor receptor in colorectal cancer patients. To address this challenge, we can potentially introduce drugs that inhibit signaling pathways activated by KRAS mutations. To comprehensively identify these pathways, we analyzed biopsies and normal mucosa from 65 patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, 30 of whom had mutated KRAS, using gene expression microarrays. By comparing tumor tissues exclusively to matched normal mucosa, we enhanced assay sensitivity and discovered 22,297 differentially expressed features between normal mucosa and cancer, including potential rectal cancer genes. Using this comprehensive description of the rectal cancer transcriptome as a baseline, we identified 13 upregulated genes (adjusted P-value <0.05) significantly correlated with activating KRAS mutations, including DUSP4, a MAP-kinase phosphatase, and SMYD3, a histone methyltransferase. Previous studies have shown that inhibiting the expression of both genes can be achieved using the MEK1-inhibitor PD98059 and the antibacterial compound Novobiocin, respectively. These findings suggest a potential strategy to overcome resistance to antibodies targeting the epithelial growth factor receptor in patients with KRAS-mutant rectal carcinomas.

title: Clinicopathological and prognostic significance of Bmi-1 expression in human cervical cancer.
text:
The objective of this study was to investigate the clinical significance of Bmi-1 expression as a prognostic marker for cervical cancer. The study design involved retrospectively collecting data from a population-based cohort at Jiangsu Province Hospital. The population consisted of 88 women diagnosed with cervical carcinoma between 2000 and 2003.

Methods included performing RT-PCR assays to determine Bmi-1 mRNA expression in 18 cervical cancer and noncancerous tissue samples, as well as immunohistochemistry to detect Bmi-1 protein expression in 88 cervical cancer samples. The correlation between Bmi-1 expression and clinicopathological factors was analyzed, and statistical analyses were conducted to test for prognostic associations. RNA interference was used to downregulate Bmi-1 expression in a cervical cancer cell line (HeLa). In vitro cytotoxicity was measured using the methylthiazoletetrazolium and colony formation assays. The effects of Bmi-1 inhibition on in vivo growth of cancer cells were detected by the tumorigenicity assay. Cell cycle distribution and cell apoptosis were measured using flow cytometry.

The main outcome measures included evaluating the levels of Bmi-1 mRNA and protein expression in tissues using RT-PCR and Western Blot assays. The results showed that the level of Bmi-1 mRNA expression in cervical cancer tissues was significantly higher than that in corresponding noncancerous tissues. High Bmi-1 expression was significantly correlated with poor tumor differentiation, advanced International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage, and positive lymph node metastasis. Patients with high Bmi-1 expression had shorter overall survival than those with low expression. Univariate and multivariate analyses demonstrated that high Bmi-1 expression was an independent prognostic factor.

In conclusion, RNA interference-mediated Bmi-1 inhibition was found to inhibit in vitro and in vivo growth, enhance apoptosis, and induce cell cycle arrest of cervical cancer cells. Bmi-1 may serve as an independent prognostic marker for cervical cancer patients.

title: Dexamethasone decreases vomiting by children after tonsillectomy.
text: We conducted a study to assess the impact of dexamethasone on vomiting following elective tonsillectomy in 133 healthy children aged 2-12 years. The study was conducted in a randomized, stratified, blocked, double-blind, placebo-controlled manner. General anesthesia was induced either through inhalation of N2O and halothane or intravenously with propofol. Anesthesia was maintained using N2O and halothane. Prior to surgery, the children were administered either dexamethasone at a dose of 150 micrograms/kg (up to a maximum of 8 mg) or a placebo intravenously. Additionally, all patients received 1.5 mg/kg of codeine intramuscularly during the surgery. The perioperative intravenous fluids, management of vomiting, postoperative pain, and hospital discharge criteria were standardized. The groups were similar in terms of the number of participants, age, weight, duration of surgery, and estimated blood loss during surgery. The administration of dexamethasone significantly reduced the overall incidence of vomiting from 72% in the placebo group to 40% (P < 0.001). The prophylactic use of dexamethasone also led to a decrease in vomiting both during the hospital stay and after discharge. Each episode of vomiting during the hospital stay prolonged the time until discharge by an average of 13 +/- 2 minutes (mean +/- standard deviation, P < 0.001). In conclusion, the administration of dexamethasone effectively reduced vomiting in healthy children undergoing elective tonsillectomy in an ambulatory hospital setting.

title: A Conserved Histidine in the RNA Sensor RIG-I Controls Immune Tolerance to N1-2'O-Methylated Self RNA.
text: The cytosolic helicase known as retinoic acid-inducible gene-I (RIG-I) is responsible for initiating immune responses against most RNA viruses. It achieves this by detecting viral RNA that is 5'-triphosphorylated (pppRNA). However, even though endogenous mRNA also possesses this 5'-triphosphorylation, modifications to its backbone and the presence of a 5'-ppp-linked methylguanosine ((m7)G) cap prevent it from being recognized by the immune system. In our study, we demonstrate that the methylation status of the first nucleotide (N1) at the 5'-terminal of endogenous capped mRNA is crucial in preventing RIG-I activation. Furthermore, we have identified a single conserved amino acid (H830) in the RNA binding pocket of RIG-I that acts as a mediator, excluding N1-2'O-methylated RNA through steric hindrance. By altering this amino acid to H830A (RIG-I(H830A)), we were able to restore the binding of N1-2'O-methylated pppRNA. As a result, endogenous mRNA activated the RIG-I(H830A) mutant, but not the wild-type RIG-I. Similarly, when we knocked down the endogenous N1-2'O-methyltransferase, we observed significant stimulation of RIG-I in the absence of external stimuli. Through our studies involving the yellow-fever-virus-encoded 2'O-methyltransferase and RIG-I(H830A), we have discovered that viruses exploit this mechanism to evade detection by RIG-I. Our findings shed light on a new role for cap N1-2'O-methylation in enabling RIG-I to tolerate self-RNA.

title: lumi: a pipeline for processing Illumina microarray.
text: The Illumina microarray, which is not labeled, is gaining popularity as a microarray platform. Unlike other microarray technologies, the BeadArray technology from Illumina has unique preprocessing and quality control methods. However, most analyses have not utilized these unique properties and have instead used preprocessing methods designed for Affymetrix microarrays. To address this, the lumi Bioconductor package was specifically developed to process Illumina microarray data. This package includes functions for data input, quality control, variance stabilization, normalization, and gene annotation. One notable feature is the variance-stabilizing transformation (VST) algorithm, which takes advantage of the technical replicates available on every Illumina microarray. The package also offers various normalization methods and multiple quality control plots. To enhance the annotation of Illumina data, a vendor-independent nucleotide universal identifier (nuID) was created to identify the probes on the microarray. The nuID annotation packages and the output of lumi processed results can easily be integrated with other Bioconductor packages to construct a statistical data analysis pipeline for Illumina data. The lumi Bioconductor package is available at www.bioconductor.org.

title: Large scale replication and meta-analysis of variants on chromosome 4q25 associated with atrial fibrillation.
text:
AIMS: In a recent study, a specific genetic pattern on chromosome 4q25 was found to be linked to atrial fibrillation (AF). Our goal was to replicate this finding in four separate groups of participants.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We conducted our research using two community-based longitudinal studies, the Framingham Heart Study and the Rotterdam Study, as well as two case-control studies, the Vanderbilt AF Registry and the German AF Network (AFNet). We compared participants with AF (n = 3508) to a control group (n = 12,173). We found that individuals with AF were more likely to be male and older than those in the control group (Framingham 82 +/- 10 vs. 71 +/- 13 years; Rotterdam 73 +/- 8 vs. 69 +/- 9 years; Vanderbilt 54 +/- 14 vs. 57 +/- 14 years; AFNet 62 +/- 12 vs. 49 +/- 14 years). In all four cohorts, a specific genetic marker called rs2200733 was associated with AF, with odds ratios (ORs) ranging from 1.37 in Rotterdam [95% confidence interval (CI) 1.18-1.59; P = 3.1 x 10(-5)] to 2.52 in AFNet (95% CI 2.22-2.8; P = 1.8 x 10(-49)). There was also a significant association between AF and another genetic marker, rs10033464, in the Framingham (OR 1.34; 95% CI 1.03-1.75; P = 0.031) and AFNet (OR 1.30; 95% CI 1.13-1.51; P = 0.0002) cohorts, but not in Vanderbilt (OR 1.16; 95% CI 0.86-1.56; P = 0.33). A meta-analysis of our findings and previous studies on AF showed that rs2200733 had an OR of 1.90 (95% CI 1.60-2.26; P = 3.3 x 10(-13)), and rs10033464 had an OR of 1.36 (95% CI 1.26-1.47; P = 6.7 x 10(-15)).

CONCLUSION: Our study confirms that two specific genetic markers, rs2200733 and rs10033464, are strongly associated with AF in four groups of individuals of European descent. These findings provide further evidence of the significant relationship between AF and specific genetic variants on chromosome 4.

title: Ecological analysis of ethnic differences in relation between tuberculosis and poverty.
text:
The aim of this study was to investigate the impact of ethnicity on the relationship between tuberculosis and deprivation. The study design was a retrospective ecological study that compared the incidence of tuberculosis in white and south Asian residents of the 39 electoral wards in Birmingham, taking into account ethnic-specific measures of deprivation. The study was conducted in Birmingham between 1989 and 1993, and included 1516 notified cases of tuberculosis. The main outcomes measured were rates of tuberculosis and levels of deprivation.

The results of the study showed that there were significant associations between tuberculosis rates and various measures of deprivation for the entire population (P<0.01), as well as with the proportion of the population of south Asian origin (P<0.01). All measures of deprivation were positively correlated with each other, but when multiple regression analysis was conducted, it was found that higher levels of overcrowding were independently associated with tuberculosis rates. In the white population, overcrowding was associated with tuberculosis rates even after controlling for other variables (P=0.0036). However, no relationship between deprivation and tuberculosis was found for the south Asian population in either single or multivariable analyses.

In conclusion, poverty is significantly associated with tuberculosis in the white population, but this association does not exist for individuals of Asian ethnicity. These findings suggest that the causal factors and potential interventions for tuberculosis will differ between ethnic groups.

title: Reduced expression of oestrogen receptor beta in invasive breast cancer and its re-expression using DNA methyl transferase inhibitors in a cell line model.
text:
In order to understand the potential role of oestrogen receptor (ER) beta in the development of breast cancer, we conducted immunohistochemical analysis on 512 breast tissue samples. These samples included normal breast tissue (n = 138), pure ductal carcinoma in situ (n = 16), invasive cancers (n = 319), lymph node metastases (n = 31), and recurrences (n = 8). Additionally, we used real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) to investigate the methylation status of the ER beta gene in two breast cancer cell lines, SkBr3 and MDA-MB-435, which were negative for ER beta.

Our findings revealed a gradual decrease in ER beta expression as the transition occurred from normal and pre-invasive lesions to invasive cancers. However, complete loss of ER beta expression was not observed, with only 21% of invasive cancer cases lacking ER beta. This reduction in ER beta expression was more prominent in invasive ductal carcinomas compared to lobular carcinomas. Notably, a significantly higher proportion of lobular carcinomas (91%) retained ER beta expression compared to invasive ductal carcinomas (74%) (p = 0.0004).

Furthermore, when we examined paired primary cancers and their corresponding axillary lymph node metastases, we found that if ER beta was present in the primary tumor, it persisted in the metastasis. This suggests that the presence or absence of ER beta in the primary tumor is maintained during metastasis.

To investigate the potential mechanism behind the loss of ER beta expression, we treated ER beta-negative cell lines with DNA methyl transferase inhibitors. This treatment resulted in the restoration of ER beta expression, indicating that the silencing of ER beta in breast carcinomas may be due to promoter hypermethylation.

Overall, our results suggest that the loss of ER beta expression is a characteristic feature of breast cancer development and that it may be a reversible process involving methylation.

title: Atopy risk in infants and children in relation to early exposure to fish, oily fish, or long-chain omega-3 fatty acids: a systematic review.
text:
There are two primary groups of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), known as n-6 and n-3 families. It has been suggested that there is a cause-and-effect relationship between n-6 PUFA consumption and allergic disease. There are plausible biological mechanisms involving eicosanoid mediators of the n-6 PUFA arachidonic acid that could explain this connection. On the other hand, fish and fish oils are rich sources of long-chain n-3 PUFAs, which counteract the effects of n-6 PUFAs. Therefore, it is believed that n-3 PUFAs can protect against atopic sensitization and the clinical symptoms of atopy.

To examine this hypothesis, evidence has been gathered from epidemiological studies that investigate the associations between fish consumption during pregnancy, lactation, infancy, and childhood, and atopic outcomes in infants and children. Additionally, intervention studies have been conducted using fish oil supplements during these periods to assess their impact on atopic outcomes. Out of the five epidemiological studies examining the effect of maternal fish consumption during pregnancy, all concluded that it had a protective association with atopic or allergic outcomes in infants and children. However, a study investigating the effects of maternal fish consumption during lactation did not find any significant associations.

The evidence from epidemiological studies investigating the effects of fish consumption during infancy and childhood on atopic outcomes is inconsistent. However, the majority of these studies (nine out of 14) showed a protective effect of fish consumption during infancy or childhood on atopic outcomes in infants and children. Providing fish oil supplements during pregnancy, lactation, or infancy results in higher levels of n-3 PUFAs in infants and children. Fish oil provision to pregnant women is associated with immunological changes in cord blood, which may persist. Studies conducted so far indicate that providing fish oil during pregnancy may reduce sensitization to common food allergens and decrease the prevalence and severity of atopic dermatitis in the first year of life. These effects may persist until adolescence, resulting in a reduction in eczema, hay fever, and asthma.

Fish oil provision to infants or children may also lead to immunological changes in the blood, but it is unclear if these changes have clinical significance or if they persist. While fish oil supplementation in infancy may decrease the risk of developing certain manifestations of allergic disease, this benefit may not last as other factors come into play. The effectiveness of fish oil in treating children with asthma is also uncertain, as the two studies conducted to date have produced conflicting results.

Further studies are needed to better understand the immunological and clinical effects of increased provision of long-chain n-3 PUFAs during pregnancy, lactation, and infancy. These studies should aim to identify protective and therapeutic effects, as well as their persistence, in infants and children.

title: Dietary quality among men and women in 187 countries in 1990 and 2010: a systematic assessment
text:
BACKGROUND: The promotion of healthy dietary patterns is a global priority in order to reduce non-communicable diseases. However, there is a lack of established knowledge regarding worldwide dietary patterns and their trends over time. The objective of this study was to analyze global changes in dietary patterns at the national and regional levels, and to assess variations based on age, sex, national income, and type of dietary pattern.

METHODS: In this systematic assessment, we examined the consumption of key dietary items (foods and nutrients) globally, by region, nation, age, and sex in 1990 and 2010. Consumption data from 325 surveys (71.7% nationally representative) covering 88.7% of the global adult population were evaluated. Two types of dietary patterns were analyzed: one characterized by greater consumption of ten healthy dietary items, and the other based on lesser consumption of seven unhealthy dietary items. The mean intakes of each dietary factor were divided into quintiles and assigned an ordinal score, with higher scores indicating healthier diets (range 0-100). Hierarchical linear regression was used to assess the dietary patterns, taking into account country, age, sex, national income, and time as exploratory variables.

FINDINGS: Between 1990 and 2010, diets based on healthy items improved globally (by 2.2 points, 95% uncertainty interval (UI) 0.9 to 3.5), while diets based on unhealthy items worsened (-2.5, -3.3 to -1.7). In 2010, the global mean scores were 44.0 (SD 10.5) for the healthy pattern and 52.1 (18.6) for the unhealthy pattern, with weak intercorrelation (r=-0.08) between countries. On average, older adults had better diets compared to younger adults, and women had better diets compared to men (p<0.0001 each). High-income nations had better diets based on healthy items compared to low-income nations (+2.5 points, 95% UI 0.3 to 4.1), but significantly poorer diets based on unhealthy items (-33.0, -37.8 to -28.3). Dietary patterns and their trends varied greatly across world regions. For instance, both types of dietary patterns improved in high-income countries, but worsened in some low-income countries in Africa and Asia. Middle-income countries showed the greatest improvement in dietary patterns based on healthy items, but the largest deterioration in dietary patterns based on unhealthy items.

INTERPRETATION: The consumption of healthy items improved globally, while the consumption of unhealthy items worsened, with variations across regions and countries. These findings provide the most up-to-date estimates of nutrition transitions worldwide and can inform policies and priorities aimed at reducing the health and economic burdens associated with poor diet quality.

FUNDING: This study was funded by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and the Medical Research Council.

title: The epidemiology of major depressive disorder: results from the National Comorbidity Survey Replication (NCS-R).
text:
The purpose of this study was to provide comprehensive data on the prevalence and factors associated with major depressive disorder (MDD) based on the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fourth Edition (DSM-IV) criteria. Additionally, the study aimed to examine treatment patterns and adequacy of treatment for MDD using data from the National Comorbidity Survey Replication (NCS-R).

The study was conducted through face-to-face household surveys between February 2001 and December 2002 in the 48 contiguous United States. The participants included 9090 household residents aged 18 years or older who responded to the NCS-R survey.

The main outcome measures included the prevalence and factors associated with MDD using the World Health Organization's Composite International Diagnostic Interview (CIDI), 12-month severity assessed with the Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology Self-Report (QIDS-SR), and the level of disability measured by the Sheehan Disability Scale (SDS) and the World Health Organization disability assessment scale (WHO-DAS). Clinical reinterviews were conducted using the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV.

The results showed that the lifetime prevalence of CIDI MDD was 16.2% (32.6-35.1 million US adults) with a 95% confidence interval [CI] of 15.1-17.3. The 12-month prevalence was 6.6% (13.1-14.2 million US adults) with a 95% CI of 5.9-7.3. Almost all 12-month cases identified by CIDI were classified as clinically significant using the QIDS-SR, with 10.4% classified as mild, 38.6% as moderate, 38.0% as severe, and 12.9% as very severe. The average duration of an episode was 16 weeks (95% CI, 15.1-17.3). Role impairment, as measured by SDS, was significant, with 59.3% of 12-month cases experiencing severe or very severe role impairment. The majority of lifetime (72.1%) and 12-month (78.5%) cases had comorbid CIDI/DSM-IV disorders, with MDD rarely being the primary disorder. Although 51.6% (95% CI, 46.1-57.2) of 12-month cases received healthcare treatment for MDD, only 41.9% (95% CI, 35.9-47.9) of these cases received adequate treatment, resulting in only 21.7% (95% CI, 18.1-25.2) of 12-month MDD cases being adequately treated. The study also found that sociodemographic factors had a limited impact on treatment compared to prevalence.

In conclusion, MDD is a common disorder that affects a significant portion of the population and is associated with severe symptoms and role impairment. While there has been an increase in treatment rates, inadequate treatment remains a concern. It is crucial to focus on screening and expanding treatment options while also improving the quality of treatment provided.

title: The Pain Catastrophizing Scale: Further Psychometric Evaluation with Adult Samples
text: The reliability and structure of the Pain Catastrophizing Scale (PCS) have been supported by previous studies involving undergraduates. In this study, we aimed to assess the reliability and validity of the PCS in adult community and pain outpatient samples. Both groups demonstrated a high internal consistency when using the PCS. Confirmatory factor analyses conducted with data from the community sample indicated that the PCS measures a single construct consisting of three interconnected dimensions. Gender differences were observed in the total PCS score for both the community and outpatient samples. Additionally, significant differences were found between the community and outpatient samples in terms of the PCS total score and subscales. Overall, the results provide strong evidence of criterion-related, concurrent, and discriminant validity for the PCS in the community sample. The limitations of this study are also discussed.

title: Temsirolimus, interferon alfa, or both for advanced renal-cell carcinoma.
text: In this phase 3 trial, 626 patients with previously untreated metastatic renal-cell carcinoma were randomly assigned to receive different treatments. The primary goal was to compare overall survival between the groups. The results showed that patients who received temsirolimus alone had longer overall survival and progression-free survival compared to those who received interferon alone. However, the combination therapy of temsirolimus and interferon did not significantly improve overall survival compared to interferon alone. The most common side effects in the temsirolimus group were rash, peripheral edema, hyperglycemia, and hyperlipidemia, while asthenia was more common in the interferon group. The study concluded that temsirolimus improved overall survival in patients with metastatic renal-cell carcinoma and a poor prognosis compared to interferon alone, but the addition of temsirolimus to interferon did not provide any survival benefit.

title: Macrophage Diversity Enhances Tumor Progression and Metastasis
text: There is compelling clinical and experimental proof indicating that macrophages play a significant role in the development and advancement of cancer. In the initial stages of tumor formation, they create an inflammatory environment that is both mutagenic and supportive of tumor growth. As tumors progress and become malignant, macrophages stimulate the formation of new blood vessels, facilitate the migration and invasion of tumor cells, and suppress the body's natural defense against cancer. In metastatic sites, macrophages prepare the surrounding tissue for the arrival of tumor cells, and then a distinct subgroup of macrophages aids in the extravasation, survival, and subsequent growth of these cells. Targeting specific subgroups of macrophages could potentially offer promising therapeutic opportunities.

title: Ankle brachial index as a predictor of cognitive impairment in the general population: ten-year follow-up of the Edinburgh Artery Study.
text:
The aim of this study was to investigate whether the ankle brachial index (ABI), a marker of generalized atherosclerosis, is associated with cognitive impairment in older individuals after a 10-year period. The study was conducted as a cohort study called the Edinburgh Artery Study, involving participants from eleven general practices in Edinburgh, Scotland. A total of 717 men and women aged 55 to 74 from the general population were followed for 10 years. The ABI was measured at the beginning of the study, and major cognitive functions were assessed after 10 years, including premorbid function using the National Adult Reading Test (NART).

The results showed that after adjusting for age and sex, a low ABI was associated with lower scores on Raven's Matrices, Verbal Fluency, and the Digit Symbol Test. This suggests that a low ABI is predictive of poorer performance in nonverbal reasoning, verbal fluency, and information processing speed. The association between ABI and the Digit Symbol Test remained significant even after further adjustment for premorbid cognitive function, indicating that a low ABI is also predictive of decline in information processing speed as individuals age.

In conclusion, the ABI may be a useful tool for identifying older individuals who are at a higher risk of cognitive impairment. In the future, preventive measures targeting individuals with a low ABI should not only focus on reducing cardiovascular events but also aim to reduce vascular-related cognitive decline. This could help reduce the incidence and consequences of subsequent cognitive impairment and dementia.

title: PTEN Regulates PI(3,4)P2 Signaling Downstream of Class I PI3K
text: The PI3K signaling pathway plays a crucial role in regulating cell growth and movement, and it is frequently mutated in cancer. Class I PI3Ks are responsible for synthesizing a lipid messenger called PI(3,4,5)P3. This messenger can be dephosphorylated by either 3-phosphatases or 5-phosphatases, with the latter producing PI(3,4)P2. The PTEN tumor suppressor is known to primarily function as a 3-phosphatase for PI(3,4,5)P3, thereby limiting the activation of this pathway. However, our research demonstrates that PTEN also acts as a 3-phosphatase for PI(3,4)P2, both in laboratory experiments and in living organisms. In the cytosol of Mcf10a cells, PTEN is a major phosphatase for PI(3,4)P2, and the simultaneous loss of PTEN and INPP4B, a known 4-phosphatase for PI(3,4)P2, leads to a synergistic accumulation of PI(3,4)P2. This accumulation is associated with an increase in invadopodia formation in cells stimulated by epidermal growth factor (EGF). In a mouse model of prostate cancer, the deletion of PTEN results in elevated levels of PI(3,4)P2, and this increase is inversely correlated with PI(3,4)P2 levels in various EGF-stimulated prostate and breast cancer cell lines. These findings suggest that PI(3,4)P2 plays a role in the phenotypic changes caused by loss-of-function mutations or deletions in PTEN.

title: Genetic analysis of an ARS element from the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
text: We have conducted a detailed study on ARS (autonomously replicating sequence) elements, which are fragments of DNA that can initiate DNA replication in yeast. Specifically, we focused on ars1, an ARS element found in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe. Through a series of experiments involving deletion mutations, we discovered that the minimal DNA fragment containing ars1 is surprisingly large. Any fragment smaller than 650 base pairs did not exhibit significant ARS activity. Further analysis of deletion and substitution mutations across the minimal ars1 revealed that a single 50 base pair segment (segment 1) is essential for efficient ARS activity. Only one other 50 base pair mutation resulted in a 5-fold reduction in activity, while most deletions had no effect. Therefore, the minimal ars1 consists of two types of genetic elements: a small segment that is crucial for ARS activity and a larger region that can tolerate internal structural changes. By examining segment 1 at a higher resolution, we identified a critical 30 base pair A/T-rich segment that appears to contain redundant genetic elements. Interestingly, when introduced into the budding yeast S.cerevisiae, Schizosaccharomyces pombe ars1 promoted high frequency transformation, but this activity did not depend on segment 1. Our findings suggest that the functional elements necessary for ARS function in S.pombe and S.cerevisiae are distinct from each other.

title: N terminus of Swr1 binds to histone H2AZ and provides a platform for subunit assembly in the chromatin remodeling complex.
text: The regulation of gene expression involves variant histone H2AZ-containing nucleosomes. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the deposition of histone H2AZ onto chromatin is facilitated by the SWR1 complex, which consists of fourteen subunits. This complex catalyzes the ATP-dependent exchange of nucleosomal histone H2A for H2AZ. Previous research has focused on seven SWR1 subunits (Swr1 ATPase, Swc2, Swc3, Arp6, Swc5, Yaf9, and Swc6) and their role in maintaining complex integrity and H2AZ histone replacement activity. In this study, we investigated the function of three additional SWR1 subunits: Bdf1, Arp4, and Swc7. We analyzed mutant SWR1 complexes that were purified based on their affinity and observed that the depletion of Arp4 (arp4-td) significantly affected the association of Bdf1, Yaf9, and Swc4. On the other hand, the loss of either Bdf1 or Swc7 had minimal impact on the overall integrity of the complex. Additionally, the in vitro H2AZ histone replacement activity of SWR1 required Arp4 but not Bdf1 or Swc7. Therefore, it appears that Bdf1, Swc7, and Swc3 (previously identified) have auxiliary roles in the basic histone replacement activity, out of the fourteen SWR1 subunits. The N-terminal region of the Swr1 ATPase subunit is crucial for the association of Bdf1, Swc7, Arp4, Act1, Yaf9, and Swc4. This region also contains a separate binding site for H2AZ-H2B, which is distinct from the binding site of the Swc2 subunit that was previously identified. These findings suggest that one SWR1 enzyme may be capable of binding two H2AZ-H2B dimers and provide further understanding of the hierarchy and interdependency of molecular interactions within the SWR1 complex.

title: Role of the cytoskeleton during leukocyte responses
text: The cytoskeleton is a complex network of molecules that controls various cellular functions involved in the immune response. These functions include cell movement, antigen recognition, activation, and phagocytosis by different types of immune cells. Recent studies have identified numerous components and regulators of the cytoskeleton in immune cells. In this article, we explore the composition, regulation, and significance of these cytoskeletal elements in immune responses.

title: Integration of mental health into primary healthcare in low-income countries: avoiding medicalization.
text: Since 2008, the World Health Organization (WHO) has been working on integrating mental health into non-specialized healthcare, specifically primary healthcare, through its mental health Gap Action Programme. While this initiative has generated renewed interest in delivering mental health services, it has also faced criticism. Some concerns include the potential medicalization of social and psychological issues and the narrow focus on primary care without adequately strengthening other levels of the healthcare system, such as community-based and district-level care. This paper explores seven essential elements to prevent unintentionally promoting a narrow biomedical approach to mental healthcare when integrating it into non-specialized healthcare. These elements include utilizing task shifting within a stepped care system, ensuring that primary mental healthcare incorporates brief psychotherapeutic interventions, promoting community-based recovery-oriented interventions for individuals with chronic mental disorders, viewing training as an ongoing process to enhance clinical competencies through supervision, involving communities as partners in psychosocial interventions, incorporating shifts to primary mental healthcare within broader health policy reforms, and promoting inter-sectoral approaches to address the social determinants of mental health.

title: Comparison of clomiphene citrate, metformin, or the combination of both for first-line ovulation induction and achievement of pregnancy in 154 women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
text:
The objective of this study was to compare the effectiveness of two first-line medications for ovulation induction and pregnancy achievement in patients with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), and to determine if any patient characteristics are associated with a better response to treatment. The study design was an observational comparative study conducted at a fertility clinic. The study included 154 infertile women with oligomenorrhea and hyperandrogenism. 

The interventions consisted of three groups: Group 1 received clomiphene citrate (CC) 50 mg from days 5-9 of the cycle, Group 2 received 500 mg of metformin three times a day, and Group 3 received both medications. The main outcome measures were ovulation and pregnancy rates. 

The results showed that patients receiving metformin alone had a higher ovulation rate compared to those receiving CC alone (75.4% vs. 50%). The ovulation rates in the metformin group were similar to those in the combination group (75.4% vs. 63.4%). Pregnancy rates were similar in all three groups. The response to metformin was not influenced by body weight or dose. Additionally, nonsmoking was associated with a better ovulatory response overall, as well as lower fasting glucose levels for CC and lower androgen levels for metformin. 

In conclusion, metformin is more effective than CC alone for ovulation induction and equally effective for achieving pregnancy. Based on these findings, we recommend using metformin as the first-line medication for ovulation induction in PCOS patients, regardless of their weight and insulin levels, due to its efficacy and known safety profile.

title: Pulmonologist involvement, stage-specific treatment, and survival in adults with non-small cell lung cancer and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
text:
RATIONALE: A significant number of lung cancer patients also have chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), which can limit their eligibility for appropriate treatment and lead to a lack of treatment. However, pulmonologist-guided management may help mitigate the negative impact of COPD.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate the relationship between pulmonologist management and the likelihood of receiving recommended treatment and overall survival among patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and preexisting COPD.

METHODS: The researchers identified cases of early- and advanced-stage NSCLC diagnosed between 2002 and 2005, with a prior COPD diagnosis, using data from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results tumor registry linked to Medicare claims. The study assessed the receipt of recommended treatment and overall survival as outcomes. Pulmonologist management was considered present if there were one or more Evaluation and Management visit claims with a pulmonologist specialty within 6 months after NSCLC diagnosis. The association between pulmonologist management and treatment received was tested using stage-specific multivariate logistic regression. Cox proportional hazard models were used to examine the independent association between pulmonologist care and mortality. Two-stage residual inclusion instrumental variable (2SRI-IV) analyses were conducted to account for potential confounding factors.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The study included 5,488 patients with early-stage NSCLC and 6,426 patients with advanced-stage NSCLC and preexisting COPD. Pulmonologist management was documented for 54.9% of patients with early-stage NSCLC and 35.7% of patients with advanced-stage NSCLC. Among patients with pulmonologist involvement, 58.5% of those with early-stage NSCLC received surgical resection, and 43.6% of those with advanced-stage NSCLC received chemotherapy. Pulmonologist management after NSCLC diagnosis was associated with higher rates of surgical resection for early-stage NSCLC and increased rates of chemotherapy for advanced-stage NSCLC. Pulmonologist management was also linked to a reduced risk of mortality for patients with early-stage NSCLC, but not for those with advanced-stage NSCLC.

CONCLUSIONS: Pulmonologist management was positively associated with rates of stage-specific treatment and overall survival in early-stage NSCLC. These findings support the recent guidelines that highlight the role of pulmonologists in managing lung cancer.

title: Divalent cations differentially regulate integrin alphaIIb cytoplasmic tail binding to beta3 and to calcium- and integrin-binding protein.
text: We conducted experiments using recombinant or synthetic alphaIIb and beta3 integrin cytoplasmic peptides to investigate their ability to form complexes and bind ligands in vitro using surface plasmon resonance. We observed that alpha.beta heterodimerization occurred in a 1:1 ratio with a weak KD in the micromolar range. The association of alpha.beta complex did not require divalent cations, but their presence stabilized the complex by reducing the dissociation rate. However, the R995A substitution or the KVGFFKR deletion in alphaIIb impaired the formation of the alpha.beta complex, while the beta3 S752P mutation did not have an effect. We also found that the recombinant calcium- and integrin-binding protein (CIB), which specifically binds to alphaIIb, interacted with the alphaIIb cytoplasmic peptide independently of Ca2+ or Mn2+ ions in a one-to-one reaction with a KD value of 12 microM. In contrast, when CIB was tested for binding to intact alphaIIbbeta3 in a liquid phase, it showed a preference for Mn2+-activated alphaIIbbeta3 conformers. This was demonstrated by enhanced coimmunoprecipitation of CIB with PAC-1-captured Mn2+-activated alphaIIbbeta3. These findings suggest that Mn2+ activation of intact alphaIIbbeta3 exposes a CIB-binding site, which is already exposed by the free alphaIIb peptide. Importantly, CIB did not stimulate PAC-1 binding to inactive alphaIIbbeta3 or prevent the occupancy of activated alphaIIbbeta3 by PAC-1. Therefore, we conclude that CIB does not regulate the inside-out signaling of alphaIIbbeta3, but rather plays a role in a post-receptor occupancy event involving alphaIIbbeta3.

title: Lethal autoimmune myocarditis in interferon-gamma receptor-deficient mice: enhanced disease severity by impaired inducible nitric oxide synthase induction.
text: The role of interferon-gamma (IFN-gamma) in inflammatory heart disease is not well understood. In this study, we investigated the effects of IFN-gamma on myocarditis, an inflammatory heart condition. We used mice that lacked the IFN-gamma receptor (IFN-gammaR(-/-)) and found that when these mice were immunized with a peptide derived from cardiac alpha-myosin heavy chain, they developed severe myocarditis with high mortality. In contrast, wild-type mice showed a decrease in myocarditis after 3 weeks. However, the IFN-gammaR(-/-) mice continued to have persistent disease. This persistent inflammation was accompanied by strong CD4 T-cell responses in vitro and impaired expression of inducible nitric oxide synthase, which is responsible for nitric oxide production in the heart. We also found that treating wild-type mice with an inhibitor of nitric oxide synthase enhanced CD4 T-cell proliferation and prevented healing of myocarditis. These findings suggest that IFN-gamma protects mice from lethal autoimmune myocarditis by promoting the expression of inducible nitric oxide synthase and suppressing T-cell responses.

title: Association between CYP2D6 polymorphisms and outcomes among women with early stage breast cancer treated with tamoxifen.
text: The aim of this study was to investigate whether variations in the CYP2D6 enzyme, which is responsible for metabolizing tamoxifen, are linked to clinical outcomes in women receiving adjuvant tamoxifen for breast cancer. The study involved a retrospective analysis of German and US cohorts of patients with early stage breast cancer who were treated with adjuvant tamoxifen. The patients had hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, no metastatic disease at diagnosis, and did not receive chemotherapy. The patients were classified into three groups based on their CYP2D6 metabolism: extensive metabolizers, heterozygous extensive/intermediate metabolizers, and poor metabolizers. The main outcome measures were time to recurrence, event-free survival, disease-free survival, and overall survival. The results showed that patients with decreased CYP2D6 activity had worse clinical outcomes compared to those with normal CYP2D6 activity. Specifically, heterozygous extensive/intermediate metabolizers and poor metabolizers had a higher risk of recurrence and worse event-free survival and disease-free survival. However, there was no significant difference in overall survival between the groups. In conclusion, variations in the CYP2D6 enzyme are associated with clinical outcomes in women receiving tamoxifen for breast cancer, with better outcomes observed in patients with normal CYP2D6 activity.

title: Long-term, nightly benzodiazepine treatment of injurious parasomnias and other disorders of disrupted nocturnal sleep in 170 adults.
text:
The purpose of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness, stability of dosage, safety, and potential for abuse of long-term benzodiazepine treatment for chronic sleep disorders. The study included 170 adult patients who were referred to one author over a 12-year period. These patients had been experiencing sleep-disruptive disorders such as sleepwalking, sleep terrors, rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder, severe insomnia, and restless legs syndrome/periodic limb movement disorder for at least 6 months. 

The results showed that 86% of the patients achieved complete or substantial control of their sleep disorders. Only 8% experienced adverse effects that required changes in medication, while 2% had relapses of alcohol or chemical abuse that required hospitalization. Another 2% occasionally misused their medications. The majority of patients (136) received clonazepam on a nightly basis for an average of 3.5 years, with no significant difference in the initial and final mean dose. Similar results were observed with chronic alprazolam treatment and other benzodiazepine treatments.

In conclusion, long-term benzodiazepine treatment for injurious parasomnias and other sleep disorders showed sustained efficacy in most cases, with a low risk of dosage tolerance, adverse effects, or abuse. However, it is important to note that the data from this study on the treatment of chronic, severe insomnia cannot be generalized to all insomnia patients.

title: Decreased proteasomal activity causes age-related phenotypes and promotes the development of metabolic abnormalities.
text: The proteasome is an enzyme complex that breaks down normal and damaged proteins. A decline in proteasomal activity with age has been linked to various age-related diseases. However, the connection between decreased proteasomal activity and aging is still unclear due to a lack of suitable animal models. In this study, we created a transgenic mouse model with reduced proteasomal chymotrypsin-like activity. These mice had a shorter lifespan and showed signs of aging. They also had an accumulation of polyubiquitinated and oxidized proteins, as well as changes in the expression of certain cellular proteins. When fed a high-fat diet, the transgenic mice developed more severe obesity and liver fat accumulation compared to normal mice. The expression of a protein involved in lipid droplet formation was also increased in their livers. Interestingly, the obesity and liver fat accumulation induced by the high-fat diet were more pronounced in older normal mice, and these mice also had higher levels of the lipid droplet protein. This suggests that the metabolic abnormalities observed in the transgenic mice mimic those seen in older mice. Overall, our findings provide the first evidence that reduced proteasomal chymotrypsin-like activity affects lifespan and worsens age-related metabolic disorders like obesity and liver fat accumulation.

title: Orai1/CRACM1 overexpression suppresses cell proliferation via attenuation of the store-operated calcium influx-mediated signalling pathway in A549 lung cancer cells.
text:
The protein Orai1/CRACM1 is a key component of calcium channels that are activated when the body's calcium stores are depleted. This calcium influx is closely linked to inflammatory reactions, immune regulation, and cell growth. Epidermal growth factor (EGF), which is involved in cell growth regulation, can activate these calcium channels. However, the effects of overexpressing Orai1/CRACM1 in EGF-mediated lung cancer cell growth are not well understood.

To investigate the role of Orai1/CRACM1 in EGF-mediated lung cancer cell proliferation, we introduced Orai1/CRACM1 plasmids into the cells using a lipofection technique. We then used various methods, including cell proliferation assays, immunofluorescence staining, flow cytometry, and real-time polymerase chain reaction, to monitor cell growth. We also examined calcium influx signals using a fluorescent-based calcium assay.

Our results showed that introducing Orai1/CRACM1 plasmids inhibited EGF-mediated cell proliferation. Overexpression of Orai1/CRACM1 also inhibited the phosphorylation of ERK1/2 and Akt, which are proteins involved in cell signaling. Additionally, the expression of p21, a protein that regulates the cell cycle, was increased in the cells overexpressing Orai1/CRACM1, while the expression of cyclin D3, another cell cycle regulator, was reduced. Flow cytometry analysis revealed that Orai1/CRACM1 overexpression caused cell cycle arrest in the G0/G1 phase. Importantly, overexpressing Orai1/CRACM1 significantly reduced EGF-mediated calcium influx through the channels. Furthermore, when we applied a store-operated calcium channel inhibitor called 2-APB, it inhibited EGF-mediated cancer cell proliferation.

In conclusion, our findings suggest that overexpressing Orai1/CRACM1 reduces calcium influx through the channels, which in turn blocks EGF-mediated signaling for cell growth and leads to cell cycle arrest.

title: Oxidative stress in cancer associated fibroblasts drives tumor-stroma co-evolution: A new paradigm for understanding tumor metabolism, the field effect and genomic instability in cancer cells.
text: Loss of caveolin-1 (Cav-1) in stromal fibroblasts is a strong predictor of poor prognosis in breast cancer patients. It is associated with early tumor recurrence, lymph node metastasis, and resistance to tamoxifen. To understand how the absence of Cav-1 in stromal fibroblasts leads to a harmful tumor micro-environment, we developed a new co-culture system. Our proposed model suggests that cancer cells induce oxidative stress in cancer-associated fibroblasts, which then drives tumor-stroma co-evolution, DNA damage, and aneuploidy in cancer cells. We found that the loss of Cav-1 expression in fibroblasts causes mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and aerobic glycolysis. Additionally, we propose that oxidative stress induces autophagy/mitophagy in fibroblasts, leading to the removal of defective mitochondria.
