This process provides nutrients, like lactate, to adjacent cancer cells, promoting mitochondrial biogenesis and oxidative metabolism (known as the "Reverse Warburg Effect"). Our evidence suggests that oxidative stress in cancer-associated fibroblasts can induce genomic instability in neighboring cancer cells, potentially increasing their aggressiveness. We also demonstrate that the over-production of nitric oxide (NO), due to Cav-1 loss, is the main cause of mitochondrial dysfunction in cancer-associated fibroblasts. Treatment with antioxidants or NO inhibitors can reverse many of the fibroblast phenotypes we describe. Therefore, cancer cells utilize oxidative stress in adjacent fibroblasts to fuel their own survival and drive their mutagenic evolution towards a more aggressive phenotype. We also present evidence that the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and NO by stromal fibroblasts may contribute to the "field effect" in cancer biology. Fibroblasts expressing endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) can downregulate Cav-1 and induce mitochondrial dysfunction in neighboring fibroblasts lacking eNOS. This suggests that stromal oxidative stress can spread from cell-to-cell, promoting widespread DNA damage like a contagious virus, and creating an oncogenic/mutagenic field.

title: Telomeres and telomerase: more than the end of the line
text: Initial studies on telomerase suggested that the maintenance of telomeres is achieved through a simple and highly conserved mechanism of telomerase-mediated replication. However, further research has revealed that while the mechanism is indeed elegant, it is not as straightforward as initially believed. It has also become apparent that although many species utilize similar DNA sequences for their telomeres, they exhibit their own unique characteristics in terms of regulating these sequences and potentially imposing additional tasks on their telomeric DNA. The remarkable similarities observed between telomeres in different species have provided valuable insights into chromosome ends, while the differences have proven to be equally enlightening. Furthermore, apart from the variations between telomerase-utilizing species, there are a few exceptional organisms with unconventional telomeres that do not exhibit any telomerase activity. This review focuses on recent studies, the valuable insights they offer, and the important questions they raise.

title: Reduced osteoblastic population and defective mineralization in osteopetrotic (op/op) mice.
text: The bone remodeling process is impaired in osteopetrotic (op/op) mice due to a defective formation of osteoclasts caused by a deficiency in macrophage colony-stimulating factor. This study aimed to investigate the role of osteoblasts and bone mineralization in relation to osteoclasts and bone resorption in op/op mice. The op/op mice exhibited an expansion of trabecular bones from the junction between cartilage and bone to the diaphyseal region. In the metaphyses of the femur in op/op mice, there were numerous alkaline phosphatase (ALPase)-positive osteoblasts near the erosion zone of the growth plates. Von Kossa's staining revealed scattered mineralized nodules and a fine network of mineralized bone matrices, whereas the wild-type littermates had well-mineralized trabeculae aligned with the longitudinal axis. In contrast, some diaphyses in op/op mice showed flattened osteoblasts with weak ALPase activity, while others had bone surfaces without any osteoblast coverage. This suggests that the population and activity of osteoblasts were reduced in the diaphyses of op/op mice. Despite being an osteopetrotic model, von Kossa's staining revealed areas of unmineralized bone in the op/op diaphyses, indicating defective mineralization due to a lower population and/or activity of osteoblasts. Transmission electron microscopy showed few osteoblasts on the diaphyseal bones, with bone marrow cells and vascular endothelial cells often attached to the unmineralized bone. Osteocytes were embedded within the unmineralized bone matrix. Therefore, it appears that osteoclasts play a role not only in the population and activity of osteoblasts but also in subsequent bone mineralization.

title: Interleukin 18 function in atherosclerosis is mediated by the interleukin 18 receptor and the Na-Cl co-transporter
text: Interleukin-18 (IL18) is involved in the development of atherosclerosis through various potential mechanisms. In mice, inhibiting IL18 activity reduces the occurrence of atherosclerosis. However, our research demonstrates that the absence of the IL18 receptor (IL18r) does not impact atherosclerosis in mice lacking apolipoprotein E (Apoe−/−), nor does it affect IL18's ability to bind to or signal in endothelial cells. Through co-immunoprecipitation with IL18, we discovered that IL18 interacts with the Na-Cl co-transporter (NCC), a protein responsible for ion transport and primarily found in the kidney. NCC is present in atherosclerotic lesions and co-localizes with IL18r. In Apoe−/− mice, the combined deficiency of IL18r and NCC, but not the deficiency of either protein alone, protects against atherosclerosis. Macrophages from Apoe−/− mice, as well as those lacking IL18r or NCC, exhibit IL18 binding, cell signaling induction, and expression of cytokines and chemokines. However, macrophages from Apoe−/− mice with the combined deficiency of IL18r and NCC display a diminished response. Co-immunoprecipitation revealed an interaction between NCC and IL18r on macrophages. IL18 binds to the cell surface of NCC-transfected COS-7 cells, which do not express IL18r, and induces cell signaling and cytokine expression. This study identifies NCC as an IL18-binding protein that collaborates with IL18r in cell signaling, the expression of inflammatory molecules, and the development of atherosclerosis in experimental models.

title: Notch promotes survival of pre–T cells at the β-selection checkpoint by regulating cellular metabolism
text: The functional outcomes of T cell receptor β-selection, such as differentiation, proliferation, and rescue from apoptosis, rely on Notch signals. However, the mechanism behind this requirement for T cell development remains unknown. In this study, we demonstrate that the interaction between Notch receptor and Delta-like 1 ligand is crucial for the survival of CD4−CD8− pre–T cells. This interaction maintains cell size, glucose uptake, and metabolism, thereby promoting cell survival. Additionally, the trophic effects of Notch signaling are mediated by the phosphatidylinositol-3-OH kinase pathway and the kinase Akt. Interestingly, the expression of active Akt can bypass the need for Notch in β-selection. Overall, our findings highlight the involvement of Notch receptor–ligand interactions in the regulation of cellular metabolism, which enables the autonomous signaling capacity of the pre–T cell receptor complex.

title: Blood pressure, salivary cortisol, and inflammatory cytokine outcomes in senior female cancer survivors enrolled in a tai chi chih randomized controlled trial
text:
Older individuals who have survived cancer are a vulnerable group because they are more likely to develop chronic diseases, such as cardiovascular disease. This risk is further compounded by the effects of cancer treatment and declines in physical functioning. Therefore, it is important to implement interventions that can reduce the risk factors for chronic diseases in this population. One such intervention is Tai Chi Chih (TCC), a mind-body exercise that has been shown to decrease the risk factors for chronic diseases. However, its effects on older cancer survivors have not been studied.

In a feasibility randomized controlled trial, we investigated the secondary outcomes of blood pressure, salivary cortisol, and inflammatory cytokines (specifically interleukin (IL)-6, IL-12, tumor necrosis factor-α, IL-10, IL-4) in relation to chronic diseases. We recruited sixty-three senior female cancer survivors (with an average age of 67 years and a standard deviation of 7.15) who had limitations in physical functioning (SF-12 physical functioning ≤80 or role-physical ≤72). These participants were randomly assigned to either a 12-week TCC program (consisting of 60-minute sessions, three times a week) or a Health Education control (HEC) program. We collected resting blood pressure measurements, 1-day salivary cortisol samples, and fasting plasma samples for cytokine multiplex assays at baseline and one week after the intervention.

After controlling for baseline values, we found that the TCC group had significantly lower systolic blood pressure (SBP) (p = 0.002) and cortisol area-under-curve (AUC) (p = 0.02) compared to the HEC group at the post-intervention assessment. However, there was no significant effect of the intervention on inflammatory cytokines (p’s > 0.05). These results suggest that the TCC program in this feasibility trial led to significant reductions in SBP and cortisol AUC in senior female cancer survivors. However, larger and more definitive trials are needed to confirm these findings. It is clear that senior cancer survivors are at an increased risk for chronic diseases, but TCC interventions may help reduce the associated risk factors.

title: Heart failure admissions in adults with congenital heart disease; risk factors and prognosis.
text:
BACKGROUND: Congenital heart disease (CHD) in adults can lead to heart failure (HF), a serious complication often resulting in death. Our study aimed to determine the frequency of HF admissions and identify risk factors for both first HF admission and mortality after the first HF admission in adults with CHD.

METHODS: We linked the Dutch CONCOR registry with the Hospital Discharge Registry and National Mortality Registry to gather data on HF admissions and mortality. Cox regression models were used to assess risk factors for HF admission and mortality.

RESULTS: Out of 10,808 adult patients (49% male), 274 (2.5%) were admitted for HF during a median follow-up period of 21 years. The incidence of first HF admission was 1.2 per 1000 patient-years, but the overall incidence of HF is likely higher. Main defect, multiple defects, and childhood surgical interventions were identified as independent risk factors for HF admission. Patients admitted for HF had a five-fold higher risk of mortality compared to those not admitted (hazard ratio (HR) = 5.3; 95% confidence interval 4.2-6.9). One- and three-year mortality rates after the first HF admission were 24% and 35%, respectively. Independent risk factors for three-year mortality after the first HF admission included male gender, pacemaker implantation, admission duration, non-cardiac medication use, and high serum creatinine.

CONCLUSIONS: The incidence of HF admission in adults with CHD is 1.2 per 1000 patient-years. Mortality risk significantly increases after HF admission, highlighting the importance of identifying high-risk patients. These patients may benefit from closer monitoring and earlier medical interventions. The identified risk factors can aid in surveillance efforts.

title: New pathologic classification of lung cancer: relevance for clinical practice and clinical trials.
text:
The 2011 International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer/American Thoracic Society/European Respiratory Society (IASLC/ATS/ERS) lung adenocarcinoma classification has led to significant changes in the pathologic classification of lung cancer. This classification was developed by a panel of international experts from IASLC, ATS, and ERS, including oncologists/pulmonologists, pathologists, radiologists, molecular biologists, and thoracic surgeons. 

Due to the fact that 70% of lung cancer patients are diagnosed at advanced stages, a new approach to small biopsies and cytology has been implemented. This approach includes specific terminology and criteria to differentiate between squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma, as well as molecular testing for EGFR mutations and ALK rearrangement. Tumors that were previously classified as non-small-cell carcinoma, not otherwise specified, due to the lack of clear squamous or adenocarcinoma morphology, should now undergo a limited immunohistochemical workup to preserve tissue for molecular testing. The terms "bronchioloalveolar carcinoma" and "mixed subtype adenocarcinoma" have been discontinued.

For resected adenocarcinomas, new concepts of adenocarcinoma in situ and minimally invasive adenocarcinoma have been introduced. These concepts define patients who, if they undergo complete resection, will have a 100% disease-free survival. Invasive adenocarcinomas are now classified based on the predominant pattern observed after comprehensive histologic subtyping, including lepidic, acinar, papillary, and solid patterns. Additionally, a new histologic subtype called micropapillary has been added, which is associated with a poor prognosis. Former mucinous bronchioloalveolar carcinomas are now referred to as "invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma."

Given the rapid advancements in the field of lung cancer, particularly in the molecular arena, this classification provides a much-needed standard for pathologic diagnosis. It is not only beneficial for patient care, but also for clinical trials and TNM classification.

title: Polymorphisms in EGFR and IL28B are associated with spontaneous clearance in an HCV-infected iranian population
text: The purpose of this study was to identify genes associated with spontaneous clearance of the hepatitis C virus (HCV) in Iranian patients. We examined 110 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in 59 candidate genes in a group of 107 HCV-infected individuals who cleared the infection on their own and 176 individuals whose infection persisted. We found that three of the SNPs, rs11506105 in the EGFR gene, and rs11881222 and rs12979860 in the IL28B gene, were associated with HCV outcome (P-values<0.03). Using multivariate logistic regression, we determined that individuals with the A/A genotypes in both rs11506105 (EGFR) and rs11881222 (IL28B), as well as the C/C genotype in rs12979860 (IL28B), were more likely to clear the HCV infection (recessive model: odds ratio (OR)=2.06, 95% confidence interval (95% CI)=1.09–3.88, P=0.025; OR=2.09, 95% CI=1.23–3.60, P=0.007; and OR=1.95, 95% CI=1.15–3.35, P=0.014 for rs11506105, rs12979860, and rs11881222, respectively). In conclusion, these SNPs in the EGFR and IL28B genes serve as strong independent predictors of spontaneous clearance of the HCV.

title: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing variables reflect the degree of diastolic dysfunction in patients with heart failure-normal ejection fraction.
text: The aim of this study was to compare the results obtained from echocardiography with tissue Doppler imaging (TDI) and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPX) in patients with heart failure (HF) and normal ejection fraction (NEF). A total of 32 patients with HF-NEF underwent both tests to determine various variables related to cardiac function and exercise capacity. The results showed that the ratio between mitral early velocity (E) and mitral annular velocity (E') was significantly correlated with peak oxygen uptake, ventilatory efficiency, resting and peak end-tidal carbon dioxide levels, and heart rate recovery at 1 minute. Left ventricular mass and end systolic volume did not show any correlation with CPX variables, while ejection fraction was correlated with heart rate recovery at 1 minute. The study suggests that E/E' can accurately reflect left ventricular filling pressure and provide insights into diastolic function. Additionally, CPX may be a valuable clinical assessment tool for evaluating cardiac dysfunction in patients with HF-NEF.

title: Radical prostatectomy for pathological Gleason 8 or greater prostate cancer: influence of concomitant pathological variables.
text: The purpose of this study was to assess the long-term outcomes of radical prostatectomy for patients with prostate cancer classified as Gleason score 8 or higher, and to determine the prognostic significance of other pathological variables. A total of 6,419 patients who underwent radical prostatectomy between 1987 and 1996 were included in the study. Among them, 407 patients had pathological Gleason score 8 or higher, with 8 in 48%, 9 in 49%, and 10 in 3% of cases. Adjuvant treatment was administered to 45% of patients, including hormonal therapy in 38% of cases. Progression-free survival, including local or systemic progression and/or prostate specific antigen (PSA) levels of 0.4 ng/ml or higher, as well as cancer-specific survival, were analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method. The impact of pathological grade and stage, preoperative PSA levels, DNA ploidy, margin status, tumor dimension, seminal vesicle invasion, and adjuvant treatment were evaluated through univariate and multivariate analyses. The results showed that 26% of patients had pathological stage pT2, 48% had pT3, and 27% had pTxN+. The overall and progression-free survival rates at 10 years were 67% and 36%, respectively, while the cancer-specific survival rate was 85%. Univariate analysis revealed that adjuvant treatment, pathological stage, preoperative PSA levels, and pathological grade were significant predictors of progression-free survival (p<0.05). Pathological stage, margin status, and ploidy were associated with cancer-specific survival. The 10-year progression-free survival rate was 52% for patients who received adjuvant treatment, compared to 23% for those who did not. In the multivariate analysis, pathological grade (p=0.02), preoperative PSA levels (p<0.0001), adjuvant therapy (p<0.0001), and pathological stage (p=0.036) were identified as significant independent predictors of progression-free survival. In conclusion, radical prostatectomy can effectively control high-grade prostate cancer in some patients with localized disease, resulting in a 10-year cause-specific survival rate of 96%. The predictors of outcomes for patients with Gleason score 8 or higher are similar to those established for all grades. Although adjuvant hormonal therapy appears to improve disease progression rates after radical prostatectomy based on this nonrandomized study, its impact on prostate cancer death rates within 10 years for patients with high-grade cancer remains uncertain.

title: Successful establishment of long-term bone marrow cultures in 103 patients with myelodysplastic syndromes.
text: Instead of using mononuclear cells, we utilized bone marrow biopsies to establish long-term cultures from 103 patients representing all five sub-categories of myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS), as well as 12 normal controls. By the fourth week, the cultures reached a confluency of 30-50%, which could be maintained for up to 12 weeks with a confluency of 100%. The predominant cell types observed were fibroblasts, macrophages, endothelial cells, and adipocytes. Lineage confirmation was achieved through immunohistochemical and electron microscopic studies. The MDS stroma provided robust support for normal hematopoiesis. The growth potency was not correlated with either the FAB classification or cytogenetics. Morphologically and functionally, the MDS stroma appeared to be normal.

title: [Acupuncture combined with auricular point sticking therapy for post stroke depression:a randomized controlled trial].
text: The objective of this study was to observe the clinical effects of combining acupuncture with auricular point sticking in the treatment of post-stroke depression (PSD) alongside western medication. Sixty patients with PSD were randomly assigned to either an acupuncture plus auricular application group (combination group) or a medication group, with 30 patients in each group. The medication group received 20 mg of paroxetine hydrochloride orally once a day for 8 weeks. In addition to this treatment, the combination group received 30-minute acupuncture sessions three times a week for 8 weeks at specific acupuncture points, including Baihui (GV 20), Sishencong (EX-HN 1), Shenting (GV 24), Yintang (GV 29), Shenmen (HT 7), Neiguan (PC 6), Taichong (LR 3), Hegu (LI 4), Zusanli (ST 36), Sanyinjiao (SP 6), and Fenglong (ST 40). The combination group also received auricular point sticking therapy for 8 weeks at shenmen (TF4), pizhixia (AT4), xin (CO15), and gan (CO12), with pressing three times a day and once every 3-5 days. The total score and individual factor scores of Hamilton's depression scale (HAMD) were observed before and after treatment, and the Asberg's antidepressant side-effect rating scale (SERS) and clinical effect were evaluated. The results showed that both groups experienced a decrease in total HAMD scores after treatment (both P<0.05), with the combination group showing a better effect (P<0.05). The combination group also had lower scores in the anxiety/somatization factor, sleep disturbance factor, and hopelessness factor compared to the medication group (all P<0.05). The total effective rate was higher in the combination group (86.7%) compared to the medication group (66.7%) (P<0.05). The SERS score was also lower in the combination group compared to the medication group (P<0.05). In conclusion, acupuncture combined with auricular point sticking is a safe and effective treatment for PSD, improving clinical symptoms.

title: Selective enhancement of endothelial BMPR-II with BMP9 reverses pulmonary arterial hypertension
text: Genetic evidence suggests that the loss of bone morphogenetic protein type II receptor (BMPR-II) signaling in the endothelium is a key factor in the development of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). However, the potential of targeting this signaling pathway using BMP ligands as a therapeutic strategy has not been explored. In this study, we have identified BMP9 as the preferred ligand for preventing cell death and improving the integrity of the endothelial monolayer in both pulmonary arterial endothelial cells and blood outgrowth endothelial cells from PAH patients with mutations in the BMPR2 gene. To further investigate the role of BMPR-II deficiency in PAH, we created a mouse model with a human BMPR2 mutation (R899X) and found that these mice spontaneously developed PAH. Treatment with BMP9 effectively reversed established PAH in these mice, as well as in two other experimental PAH models induced by monocrotaline or VEGF receptor inhibition combined with chronic hypoxia. These findings highlight the potential of enhancing endothelial BMP signaling as a promising therapeutic approach for PAH.

title: Coordinated actions of SLX1-SLX4 and MUS81-EME1 for Holliday junction resolution in human cells.
text: Holliday junctions (HJs) are DNA intermediates that form during homologous recombination and are crucial for proper chromosome segregation. In this study, we demonstrate that there are two pathways for resolving HJs in human cells, involving three structure-selective endonucleases: SLX1-SLX4, MUS81-EME1, and GEN1. The GEN1 pathway is responsible for one pathway of HJ resolution, while SLX1-SLX4 and MUS81-EME1 constitute a separate and genetically distinct pathway called SLX-MUS. Depletion of proteins from either the SLX-MUS or GEN1 pathway leads to severe defects in chromosome segregation and reduced cell survival. At the G2/M transition, SLX1-SLX4 and MUS81-EME1 form a stable complex called SLX-MUS holoenzyme, which is facilitated by CDK-mediated phosphorylation. This SLX-MUS holoenzyme can be reconstituted in vitro. Biochemical analysis reveals that SLX-MUS acts as a HJ resolvase, coordinating the active sites of two different endonucleases during HJ resolution. This cleavage reaction is more efficient and controlled compared to the activity of SLX1-SLX4 alone, which exhibits a promiscuous nickase activity on various DNA secondary structures.

title: Prevalence of frequent headache in a population sample.
text:
The purpose of this study was to examine the prevalence and characteristics of frequent headaches in the general population. While patients with daily or near-daily headaches are often seen in neurology practices and headache subspecialty centers, there is limited information on how common this condition is among the general population. This study aimed to fill that gap by conducting the first US-based study on the topic.

The study was conducted in Baltimore County, Maryland, where 13,343 individuals between the ages of 18 and 65 were randomly selected through telephone interviews. Participants were asked about their headaches, and those who reported experiencing 180 or more headaches per year were classified as having frequent headaches. The researchers identified three distinct subtypes of frequent headaches: frequent headaches with migrainous features, chronic tension-type headaches, and unclassified frequent headaches.

The overall prevalence of frequent headaches in the general population was found to be 4.1%, with a higher prevalence among females (5.0%) compared to males (2.8%). The female to male ratio was 1.8:1. Caucasians had a higher prevalence of frequent headaches (4.4%) compared to African Americans (3.3%). Additionally, the lowest educational category had the highest prevalence of frequent headaches in both males and females.

Among those with frequent headaches, more than half met the criteria for chronic tension-type headaches (52% of females, 56% of males), while almost one third met the criteria for frequent headaches with migrainous features (33% of females, 25% of males). The remaining individuals were classified as unclassified frequent headaches (15% of females, 19% of males). Overall, 30% of females and 25% of males with frequent headaches met the criteria for migraine according to the International Headache Society.

In conclusion, frequent headaches are common in the general population, with higher prevalence among Caucasians and those with lower levels of education. Chronic tension-type headaches are more common than frequent headaches with migrainous features, although the latter is more disabling. While females have a higher prevalence of frequent headaches compared to males, the difference is less pronounced than in migraines. The sex ratio also varies depending on the subtype of frequent headaches.

title: HTLV-I/II associated disease in England and Wales, 1993-7: retrospective review of serology requests.
text: Besides HIV, there are two retroviruses that infect humans, known as human T cell leukaemia viruses type I (HTLV-I) and type II (HTLV-II). HTLV-I infection is prevalent in Japan, the Caribbean, Africa, and Melanesia, and can also be found among immigrants from these regions in Europe. HTLV-I infection is linked to a 1-5% lifetime risk of adult T cell leukaemia/lymphoma, a 0.25% lifetime risk of HTLV-I associated myelopathy, and other inflammatory conditions such as uveitis, alveolitis, and arthritis. On the other hand, HTLV-II infection is endemic among certain native American and African populations, as well as injecting drug users, and has been associated with neurological disease. In the United Kingdom, between 1986 and 1992, there were 100 cases of HTLV-I associated myelopathy and 44 cases of adult T cell leukaemia/lymphoma diagnosed. Adult T cell leukaemia/lymphoma was first reported in 1977, and patients with this condition typically have a mean life expectancy of only six months, suggesting that most of the 44 cases were newly occurring incidents.

title: Lentiviral vector design and imaging approaches to visualize the early stages of cellular reprogramming.
text: The process of creating induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) involves transferring reprogramming transcription factors into somatic cells. The effectiveness of forming iPSC colonies is influenced by the expression levels of these factors, but there may also be additional factors at play. In this study, we used specially designed lentiviral vectors that express optimized reprogramming factors using a strong retroviral promoter. This promoter is quickly silenced in iPSCs. We used fluorescence microscopy and live-cell imaging to track the conversion of fibroblasts into iPSCs and analyze the formation of early iPSC clusters. Our results show that the lentiviral vectors are typically silenced before or at the same time as the induction of an Oct4-EGFP pluripotency marker. Around 7 days after transduction, a subset of cells in clonal colonies expressed Oct4-EGFP and rapidly expanded. Tracking individual cells in iPSC colonies supported the idea that stochastic epigenetic changes are necessary for reprogramming. We also observed that iPSC colonies can be a mix of cells from different clusters. By improving vector design and using continuous cell tracking, we have created a powerful system to study the intricate dynamics of early reprogramming events.

title: EIF2AK3, encoding translation initiation factor 2-α kinase 3, is mutated in patients with Wolcott-Rallison syndrome
text: Wolcott-Rallison syndrome (WRS) is a rare genetic disorder characterized by insulin-dependent diabetes that develops in newborns or infants. As the affected individuals grow older, they may also experience bone and growth abnormalities, such as epiphyseal dysplasia, osteoporosis, and growth retardation. Additionally, WRS can lead to various other health issues, including liver and kidney dysfunction, intellectual disability, and heart problems. Through the study of two families with a history of consanguinity, researchers were able to identify a specific region on chromosome 2p12 that is associated with WRS. Within this region, they found the gene EIF2AK3, which codes for a protein involved in the initiation of protein synthesis. Further investigation revealed distinct mutations in EIF2AK3 that were present in each of the families affected by WRS. One mutation resulted in a truncated protein lacking the catalytic domain, while the other mutation altered an amino acid within the catalytic domain that is highly conserved among related kinases. These findings provide strong evidence for the involvement of EIF2AK3 in WRS and may contribute to a better understanding of more common forms of diabetes and other pathological manifestations associated with WRS.

title: Beta oscillations in a large-scale sensorimotor cortical network: directional influences revealed by Granger causality.
text: Previous research has indicated that synchronized beta frequency oscillations in the primary motor cortex play a role in maintaining steady contractions of arm and hand muscles on the opposite side of the body. However, there is limited understanding of how postcentral cortical areas contribute to motor maintenance and how they interact with the motor cortex. To address this gap, we conducted a study in which we examined the functional relationships of beta-synchronized neuronal assemblies in pre- and postcentral areas of two monkeys. During a visual discrimination task, the monkeys pressed a hand lever during a wait period. Through power and coherence spectral analysis, we identified a large-scale network that linked pre- and postcentral areas and exhibited beta synchronization. We then used Granger causality spectra to measure the directional influences among the recording sites. In both monkeys, we observed strong Granger causal influences from the primary somatosensory cortex to both the motor cortex and the inferior posterior parietal cortex. Additionally, the inferior posterior parietal cortex exerted Granger causal influences on the motor cortex. However, in one monkey, the Granger causal influences from the motor cortex to the postcentral sites were weak, and in the other monkey, they were not observed at all. These findings are the first, to our knowledge, to demonstrate in awake monkeys that synchronized beta oscillations connect multiple sensorimotor areas into a large-scale network during motor maintenance behavior. Furthermore, these oscillations carry Granger causal influences from the primary somatosensory and inferior posterior parietal cortices to the motor cortex.

title: Aging, frailty and age-related diseases
text: The understanding of frailty as a distinct medical syndrome has developed through the observations of geriatricians and is widely recognized in clinical practice. Frailty is a state of vulnerability that is not specific to any particular illness, but rather reflects changes in multiple physiological systems. These changes, which may not always reach the level of a diagnosable disease, can make individuals, particularly the very elderly, frail without a specific life-threatening condition. It is now believed that frailty is influenced not only by physical factors, but also by psychological, cognitive, and social factors, all of which should be considered in its definition and treatment. The presence of these signs and symptoms suggests a reduced ability to cope with stressors and a decline in overall resilience, even in the absence of external stressors. As a result, frail elderly individuals are at a higher risk for accelerated physical and cognitive decline, disability, and death. These characteristics of frailty can also be applied to the general aging process, and there is limited consensus in the literature regarding the physiological and biological pathways that contribute to or determine frailty. However, chronic systemic inflammation is widely believed to be a major factor. This review will explore the relationship between aging, frailty, and age-related diseases, and will discuss potential interventions to reduce the occurrence and impact of frailty in older adults.

title: A case of paraquat intoxication caused by intravenous injection.
text: Paraquat intoxication is a life-threatening issue. While most cases occur due to oral ingestion, we present a case where death resulted from intravenous injection of paraquat. Limited clinical data exists regarding paraquat exposure through injection, and we provide details of this case and its fatal progression. Shortly after the injection, the patient experienced toxic symptoms and severe impairment of organ function. Various treatments were attempted, including repeated activated charcoal hemoperfusion with pulse steroids, cyclophosphamide, and antioxidants. Unfortunately, the patient succumbed to multiple organ failure three days after the intoxication. This case highlights the grim prognosis associated with even minimal amounts of paraquat intoxication via intravenous injection.

title: Genome-wide association study identifies variants at CLU and CR1 associated with Alzheimer's disease
text:
Apolipoprotein E (APOE) is the only confirmed susceptibility gene for late-onset Alzheimer's disease, located on chromosome 19. In order to identify other genetic risk factors, we conducted a large-scale study involving 2,032 individuals from France diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease (cases) and 5,328 controls. We examined markers outside of APOE that showed suggestive evidence of association (P < 10−5) in additional collections from Belgium, Finland, Italy, and Spain, which included a total of 3,978 Alzheimer's disease cases and 3,297 controls.

Our study revealed two loci that consistently showed evidence of association. The first locus is within the CLU gene (also known as APOJ) on chromosome 8, which encodes clusterin or apolipoprotein J. The specific marker rs11136000 showed an odds ratio (OR) of 0.86, with a 95% confidence interval (CI) of 0.81–0.90, and a combined data p-value of 7.5 × 10−9. The second locus is within the CR1 gene on chromosome 1, which encodes the complement component (3b/4b) receptor 1. The marker rs6656401 showed an OR of 1.21, with a 95% CI of 1.14–1.29, and a combined data p-value of 3.7 × 10−9.

Previous biological studies have provided support for the roles of CLU and CR1 in the clearance of β amyloid (Aβ) peptide, the main component of amyloid plaques. These plaques are a major characteristic of Alzheimer's disease in the brain.

title: Identification and characterization of subpopulations in undifferentiated ES cell culture.
text:
Embryonic stem (ES) cells are a type of pluripotent cells that originate from the inner cell mass (ICM) and the epiblast. They are believed to be a uniform group of cells with characteristics that fall between the ICM and the epiblast. These cells express two genes, Oct3/4 and Rex1, which serve as markers for identifying undifferentiated ES cells. Oct3/4 is present in both totipotent and pluripotent cells throughout the mouse life cycle, while Rex1 is only found in the ICM and is downregulated in pluripotent cells during later stages, such as the epiblast and primitive ectoderm (PrE).

To investigate whether ES cells are a homogeneous population representing a specific developmental stage of pluripotent cells or a heterogeneous population consisting of cells at different stages of differentiation, we created knock-in ES cell lines. These lines contained genes for fluorescent proteins inserted into the Rex1 and Oct3/4 gene loci, allowing us to visualize the expression of these genes. Our findings revealed that undifferentiated ES cells actually consist of at least two distinct populations: Rex1(+)/Oct3/4(+) cells and Rex1(-)/Oct3/4(+) cells. Interestingly, these populations were capable of converting into each other when exposed to LIF.

Based on our assumption that Rex1(+)/Oct3/4(+) cells resemble ICM and early-PrE cells, we observed that these cells primarily differentiated into primitive ectoderm and contributed to the formation of chimeras. On the other hand, Rex1(-)/Oct3/4(+) cells exhibited a higher efficiency in differentiating into somatic lineage cells compared to non-fractionated ES cells in vitro. However, they displayed a limited ability to contribute to chimera formation. These results confirmed that undifferentiated ES cell cultures contain subpopulations that correspond to the ICM, epiblast, and PrE.

In summary, our study demonstrates that undifferentiated ES cells are not a homogeneous population but rather consist of distinct subpopulations representing different stages of pluripotent cell development.

title: Isolation of intact nuclei of high purity from mouse liver.
text: The current methods used to isolate nuclei from the liver involve disrupting the plasmalemmae by homogenization and separating the nuclei using high centrifugal force (HCF) with sucrose gradients for up to 80 minutes. However, this prolonged use of HCF increases the risk of nuclear damage and degradation by endogenous proteases. In this study, we compared four different modifications to the traditional nuclear isolation methods. We gently crushed mouse liver through a fine mesh, with or without in vivo perfusion with collagenase. The resulting cell suspension was then centrifuged at 600 g to remove large debris, followed by centrifugation at moderate centrifugal force (MCF, 16,000 g) or high centrifugal force (HCF, 70,000 g) through sucrose gradients for 30 minutes. We assessed the biological and morphological purity of the isolated nuclei, including analyzing marker proteins for nuclei and cytoplasm. The results showed that using MCF without collagenase provided the highest integrity and purity of the nuclei. However, if the priority is to maximize yield, using MCF with collagenase is a viable option. This method is particularly suitable for small samples and can facilitate studies using human liver biopsies and mouse livers, which are commonly used for gene targeting research.

title: Two structurally independent domains of E. coli NusG create regulatory plasticity via distinct interactions with RNA polymerase and regulators.
text:
NusG is a regulatory protein that is highly conserved and plays a role in modulating transcription in various ways. It interacts with elongation complexes (ECs) of RNA polymerase, DNA, and RNA. In Escherichia coli, NusG has multiple functions. It suppresses pausing and increases the rate of elongation. It also enhances termination by E. coli rho and phage HK022 Nun protein, and promotes antitermination by lambdaN and in ribosomal RNA operons.

Our study focuses on NMR studies of E. coli NusG. We have found that it is composed of two distinct structural domains, namely NTD and CTD. These domains are largely independent of each other. Through tests conducted in vivo and in vitro, we have determined that the NTD alone is sufficient to suppress pausing and enhance transcript elongation in vitro. However, neither domain alone can enhance rho-dependent termination or support antitermination. This suggests that both domains need to interact with ECs in order for these processes to occur.

We propose that the NTD of NusG interacts with RNA polymerase, while the CTD interacts with rho and other regulators. This allows NusG to have different combinations of interactions, which in turn lead to different regulatory outcomes.

title: Cytochemistry and C-values: the less-well-known world of nuclear DNA amounts.
text:
In the field of plant sciences, there are two commonly used technologies for measuring nuclear DNA content: Feulgen absorbance cytophotometry and flow cytometry (FCM). While FCM is becoming increasingly popular among plant scientists, absorbance-cytophotometric techniques are losing popularity. This is problematic as it limits the available methods, which is not ideal. Both approaches have their advantages, but static cytophotometry seems to have more difficulties with instruments and materials compared to FCM. As a result, Feulgen-based data in the literature are often less reliable than expected. 

The purpose of this article is to provide an overview of nuclear DNA content measurement, specifically C-values, focusing on the technical difficulties caused by biological materials and discussing the photometrical aspects of the work. It has been known for over 20 years that plant polyphenols interfere with Feulgen DNA cytophotometry, leading to unreliable results. However, there is limited information available about the specific chemical classes of plant metabolites that interfere with DNA staining and the mechanisms of their inhibition. Plant slimes are also a concern. 

Recently, research in FCM has started to investigate the effects of secondary metabolites on measurement results. In particular, the analysis of variation in genome size within a species requires a rigorous methodology that takes inhibitors into account. FCM tests should be mandatory to assess the inhibitory effects of endogenous metabolites. The use of dry seeds for harvesting embryo and endosperm nuclei for FCM and Feulgen densitometry can often bypass staining inhibitors. The importance of internal standardization is emphasized. The goal is to better understand the interactions between phytochemicals and cytochemicals in plant DNA photometry for the benefit of studying plant genome sizes.

title: Integrins and cell proliferation: regulation of cyclin-dependent kinases via cytoplasmic signaling pathways.
text: The progression of the cell cycle in mammalian cells is tightly controlled by two factors: adhesion to the extracellular matrix through integrins and the binding of growth factors to their receptors. This control is achieved through G1 phase cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs), which are influenced by signaling pathways that are regulated by both integrins and growth factor receptors. Recent advancements have revealed a wide range of integrin-dependent signals that contribute to the regulation of G1 phase CDKs. The regulation of cyclin D1 by the ERK pathway serves as an example of how cell adhesion can impact cell cycle progression.

title: Interplay between microtubule bundling and sorting factors ensures acentriolar spindle stability during C. elegans oocyte meiosis
text: The absence of centrioles in many species leads to unique mechanisms for oocyte meiosis, including microtubule organization, spindle assembly, and chromosome segregation. Our research focuses on C. elegans KLP-15 and KLP-16, two closely related proteins from the kinesin-14 family. These proteins are found in the acentriolar oocyte spindle and play a role in bundling microtubules during spindle assembly. When KLP-15/16 is depleted, microtubule bundles initially form but then collapse into a disorganized arrangement. However, we discovered that during anaphase, the microtubules are able to reorganize into bundled arrays that facilitate chromosome segregation, despite the initial defect. This allowed us to identify factors that promote microtubule organization during anaphase, which are normally not detectable in wild-type worms. We found that SPD-1 (PRC1) bundles microtubules and KLP-18 (kinesin-12) likely arranges these bundles in a functional orientation for chromosome segregation. Our findings demonstrate the interplay between different mechanisms that contribute to spindle formation and chromosome segregation in the absence of centrioles.

title: Development of a questionnaire to measure heart disease risk knowledge in people with diabetes: the Heart Disease Fact Questionnaire.
text: This paper presents a study on a questionnaire that assesses knowledge of heart disease risk in individuals with diabetes. The questionnaire, called the Heart Disease Fact Questionnaire (HDFQ), consists of 25 items that aim to measure respondents' understanding of major risk factors for coronary heart disease (CHD), with a focus on diabetes-related factors. The study analyzed responses from 524 people with diabetes to evaluate the psychometric properties of the HDFQ. The questionnaire is designed to be easily readable and understandable, even for an average 13-year old, and does not impose a significant burden on respondents. It demonstrates good content and face validity, as well as adequate internal consistency, with a Kuder-Richardson-20 formula of 0.77 and strong item-total correlations. Item analysis revealed desirable P-values. In discriminant function analyses, HDFQ scores successfully differentiated respondents based on their knowledge of their own cardiovascular health, use of lipid lowering medications, health insurance status, and educational attainment, indicating good criterion-related validity. This questionnaire provides a concise and user-friendly measure of heart disease risk knowledge, making it suitable for both research and practical applications. The paper also suggests the need for establishing norms and further investigating the questionnaire's test-retest reliability and predictive validity in future research.

title: Prevalence of Multiple Sclerosis in Isfahan, Iran
text:
Background: The prevalence of multiple sclerosis (MS) varies greatly worldwide. According to Kurtzke, Iran has a low prevalence of MS. 

Objective: To determine the period prevalence and risk factors of MS in Isfahan, a region in central Iran. 

Methods: A cross-sectional case register study was conducted between 2004 and 2005. All patients with confirmed MS during this period, who were alive, residing in Isfahan, and members of the Isfahan MS Association, were included in the study. Demographic and case-related information was collected. A total of 1,391 patients with definite MS (308 men and 1,083 women) were identified from the Isfahan MS Association. The diagnosis was confirmed by a neurologist and radiologist using clinical information and MRI findings. Patients were interviewed and completed a questionnaire. Population data were obtained from the 1999 Iran Census. The mean age of participants was 32.5 years, with an average disease duration of 6.4 years for men and 6.9 years for women. 

Results: The period prevalence of MS in Isfahan was 35.5 per 100,000 (95% CI: 33.6–37.3) in a population of 3,923,255. The prevalence was higher in women [54.5 (95% CI: 51.1–57.8)] compared to men [14.9 (95% CI: 13.3–16.6)]. The female-to-male ratio was 3.6 (95% CI: 3.2–4.1). The direct age-adjusted period prevalence was 59.5 per 100,000 (95% CI: 44.8–75.2) for women and 17.0 per 100,000 (95% CI: 8.9–25.1) for men. MS rates were highest among individuals aged 30-39 and decreased with increasing age. The most common initial symptoms were sensory disturbances (51.1%, 95% CI: 48.4–53.7) and visual disturbances (47.0%, 95% CI: 44.4–49.7). 

Conclusion: Isfahan has a medium to high risk of MS, which contradicts the gradient hypothesis.

title: A kinetochore-independent mechanism drives anaphase chromosome separation during acentrosomal meiosis
text: Although extensive research has been conducted on the assembly of acentrosomal meiotic spindles, there is limited knowledge regarding the segregation of chromosomes on these spindles. In this study, we present evidence in Caenorhabditis elegans oocytes that the kinetochore protein, KNL-1, plays a crucial role in the assembly of meiotic kinetochores that orient chromosomes. However, unlike in mitosis, the separation of chromosomes during meiotic anaphase is not dependent on kinetochores. Prior to anaphase, both meiotic kinetochores and spindle poles disassemble, along with the microtubules on the side of chromosomes facing the pole. During anaphase, microtubules then form between the separating chromosomes. Functional analysis has identified a group of proteins that localize to a ring-shaped domain between kinetochores during pre-anaphase spindle assembly and anaphase separation. The localization of these proteins is regulated by the chromosomal passenger complex, which controls the loss of meiotic chromosome cohesion. Therefore, the process of meiotic segregation in C. elegans can be divided into two stages, where kinetochores orient chromosomes but are not required for their separation. We propose that separation is governed by a meiosis-specific chromosomal domain that coordinates the removal of cohesin and the segregation of chromosomes.

title: Association between the Medicare Modernization Act of 2003 and patient wait times and travel distance for chemotherapy.
text:
The Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement, and Modernization Act of 2003 (MMA) made changes to reimbursements for outpatient chemotherapy drugs and drug administration services. There have been concerns that these changes may have negatively impacted access to chemotherapy for Medicare beneficiaries. This study aimed to compare patient wait times and travel distances for chemotherapy before and after the enactment of the MMA. 

The researchers analyzed a nationally representative 5% sample of claims from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services from 2003 to 2006. The study included Medicare beneficiaries with incident breast cancer, colorectal cancer, leukemia, lung cancer, or lymphoma who received chemotherapy in inpatient hospital, institutional outpatient, or physician office settings. 

The main outcomes measured were the number of days from incident diagnosis to the first chemotherapy visit and the distance traveled for treatment. The analysis controlled for various factors such as age, sex, race/ethnicity, cancer type, geographic region, comorbid conditions, and year of diagnosis and treatment. 

The study found that there were 5082 incident cases in 2003, 5379 cases in 2004, 5116 cases in 2005, and 5288 cases in 2006. Around 70% of patients received treatment in physician office settings each year. There was a small but significant change in treatment settings from 2003 to 2006, with a decrease in the proportion of patients receiving chemotherapy in inpatient settings and an increase in institutional outpatient settings. The proportion in physician offices remained consistent. 

The median time from diagnosis to initial chemotherapy visit was similar across the years. In multivariate analyses, average wait times for chemotherapy were slightly longer in 2005 compared to 2003, but not significantly different in 2006. Median travel distance also remained relatively consistent across the years. However, after adjustment, average travel distance was slightly longer in 2004, 2005, and 2006 compared to 2003. 

In conclusion, there have not been significant changes in travel distance and patient wait times for chemotherapy in the Medicare population since 2003, the year before the MMA-related changes in reimbursement.

title: 20-year outcomes following conservative management of clinically localized prostate cancer.
text: The appropriate treatment for men with clinically localized prostate cancer is uncertain. A recent study found that the mortality rate for prostate cancer increases for men who survive more than 15 years after diagnosis. The objective of this study was to estimate the 20-year survival rate for men diagnosed with clinically localized prostate cancer and treated with observation or androgen withdrawal therapy alone, based on a competing risk analysis. The study included 767 men aged 55 to 74 years with clinically localized prostate cancer diagnosed between 1971 and 1984. The patients were treated with observation or immediate or delayed androgen withdrawal therapy, with a median observation period of 24 years. The main outcome measures were the probability of mortality from prostate cancer or other medical conditions, based on the patient's age at diagnosis and tumor grade. The results showed that the prostate cancer mortality rate was 33 per 1000 person-years during the first 15 years of follow-up and 18 per 1000 person-years after 15 years of follow-up. These rates were not statistically different after adjusting for tumor histology. Men with low-grade prostate cancers had a minimal risk of dying from prostate cancer during 20 years of follow-up, while men with high-grade prostate cancers had a high probability of dying from prostate cancer within 10 years of diagnosis. Men with intermediate-grade tumors had an intermediate risk of prostate cancer death. In conclusion, the annual mortality rate from prostate cancer appears to remain stable after 15 years from diagnosis, suggesting that aggressive treatment may not be necessary for localized low-grade prostate cancer.

title: Role of beta adrenergic receptor polymorphisms in heart failure: systematic review and meta-analysis.
text: Heart failure (HF) is a prevalent condition that leads to significant illness and death. The main way that cardiac function is affected is through the activation of beta adrenergic receptors (betaAR). Long-term activation of beta(1)AR is believed to contribute to the development of HF, and blocking betaAR has been shown to improve survival in individuals with left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Certain variations in the genes that code for beta adrenergic receptors (ADRB) have been linked to different types of HF and how individuals respond to beta blockers. However, these associations have not consistently been found in multiple studies. This review examines the evidence for the involvement of ADRB variations in the development, progression, and response to beta blockers in HF. Additionally, a meta-analysis of three studies is presented, which shows that individuals with a specific ADRB1 Arg389Gly variation experience a 5% improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction when treated with beta blockers. This suggests that this particular variation may have a different response to beta blockers. In the future, identifying specific genotypes may help identify individuals who are at a higher risk of developing HF, those whose HF may worsen quickly, or those who may not benefit from beta blockers. These individuals could then receive more targeted and aggressive treatment.

title: New development of the yolk sac theory in diabetic embryopathy: molecular mechanism and link to structural birth defects.
text: Maternal diabetes mellitus is a significant risk factor for structural birth defects, such as congenital heart defects and neural tube defects. The increasing prevalence of type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity in women of childbearing age has made diabetes-induced birth defects a growing public health concern. In both live subjects and laboratory settings, maternal diabetes mellitus and high glucose levels cause damage to the yolk sac, resulting in cell morphological changes and disruptions to organelle dynamics. The yolk sac vascular system, which is the first system to develop during embryogenesis, is particularly sensitive to high blood sugar levels. This can lead to impaired nutrient transportation due to vasculopathy. While the exact relationship between yolk sac vasculopathy and structural birth defects is not yet fully understood, a recent study suggests that the quality of yolk sac vasculature is inversely related to rates of embryonic malformations. Animal studies have identified key molecular factors involved in diabetic yolk sac vasculopathy, including hypoxia-inducible factor-1α, apoptosis signal-regulating kinase 1, thioredoxin-1 (its inhibitor), c-Jun-N-terminal kinases, nitric oxide, and nitric oxide synthase. Abnormalities in arachidonic acid and myo-inositol are also associated with yolk sac vasculopathy. Dietary supplementation with fatty acids that restore lipid levels in the yolk sac has been shown to reduce diabetes-induced malformations. Although the role of the human yolk sac in embryogenesis is not as extensive as in rodents, maternal diabetes mellitus still has a negative impact on human embryonic vasculogenesis. Mechanistic studies have identified potential targets for future interventions to address yolk sac vasculopathy, birth defects, and other complications associated with diabetic pregnancies.

title: Hepatitis B and C in HIV-infected patients. Prevalence and prognostic value.
text:
The prevalence and impact of coinfection with hepatitis B (HBV) or hepatitis C (HCV) on the clinical course of HIV-infected patients is not well understood. In this study, we aimed to investigate the prevalence of HBV and HCV markers in HIV-infected patients and assess their influence on disease progression.

A total of 232 HIV-infected patients were included in the study, with an average age of 37 years. Follow-up data was available for these patients, and their CD4 counts (a measure of immune function) were recorded. Of the patients, 46% had AIDS.

Samples from these patients were analyzed for markers of HBV and HCV infection, including HBsAg, HBeAg, HBV-DNA, Anti-HBs, anti-HBc, anti-HCV, and HCV-RNA.

The results showed that 23% of the patients were positive for anti-HCV, and 78% of these had detectable HCV-RNA. Additionally, 9% of the patients had chronic HBV infection, with 82% of these having detectable HBeAg and 86% having HBV-DNA.

The presence of HCV-RNA, HBeAg, and the amount of HBV-DNA were found to be associated with the degree of immunodeficiency in these patients. Compared to the control group without HBV or HCV infection, HIV-infected patients with either HBV or HCV showed a direct correlation between a decrease in CD4 counts and reduced cholinesterase activity.

Furthermore, in patients with AIDS, coinfection with HBV or HCV was associated with a reduced survival rate compared to controls. The median survival time for patients with HBV was 212 days, for HCV it was 267 days, and for controls it was 439 days.

In conclusion, coinfection of HIV and HBV or HCV is common among HIV-infected patients. Our findings suggest that in the context of prolonged survival in HIV-infected patients, coinfection with either HBV or HCV is associated with a reduced survival rate.

title: Requirement of endogenous stem cell factor and granulocyte-colony-stimulating factor for IL-17-mediated granulopoiesis.
text: IL-17 is a unique cytokine that is restricted to CD4+ T cells. It has been found to stimulate the production of blood cells and specifically leads to an increase in mature granulocytes. In our research, we have discovered that IL-17-induced granulopoiesis relies on the release of G-CSF and the presence of a specific form of stem cell factor (SCF). Interestingly, IL-17 also offers protection against neutropenia caused by neutralizing G-CSF. When G-CSF was neutralized, the expansion of bone marrow progenitor cells induced by IL-17 was completely reversed. However, the reduction in splenic CFU-GM/CFU-granulocyte-erythrocyte-megakaryocyte-monocyte was only 50% in both Sl/Sld and control mice. This suggests that IL-17 has a significant effect on splenic granulopoiesis that is independent of SCF and G-CSF, resulting in the preservation of mature granulocytes in circulation. IL-17 is a cytokine that has the potential to connect the immune responses of lymphocytes and myeloid cells, making it a promising target for therapeutic development.

title: The expression of immediate early gene X-1 (IEX-1) is differentially induced by retinoic acids in NB4 and KG1 cells: possible implication in the distinct phenotype of retinoic acid-responsive and -resistant leukemic cells
text: The early response gene immediate early gene X-1 (IEX-1) plays a role in growth control and modulation of apoptosis, depending on the cell type and stimulus. This study focuses on two acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) cell lines, NB4 and KG1, which have different responses to retinoic acids (RAs). The researchers found that IEX-1 expression is rapidly induced by all-trans- or cis-RA in both cell lines, independent of other signal transduction mediators. In NB4 cells, the increase in IEX-1 expression is temporary and reversible, leading to cell cycle arrest, ongoing differentiation, and reduced sensitivity to anti-cancer drug-induced apoptosis. On the other hand, in KG1 cells, the RA-induced IEX-1 expression persists over several days, accompanied by continued cell cycle progression and increased sensitivity to apoptosis. The researchers also identified two functional RA-response elements in the IEX-1 promoter. These findings suggest that IEX-1 is a unique transcriptional target of the X–RARα fusion receptors, which have different responses to RAs. The different time course of direct transcriptional induction by PML–RARα and PLZF–RARα in NB4 and KG1 cells, respectively, suggests that IEX-1 expression may contribute to the modified actions of these receptors and the distinct characteristics of APL cells.

title: Comorbidity between ADHD and obesity: exploring shared mechanisms and clinical implications.
text: New research suggests a link between attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and obesity. In this article, we conducted a thorough review of existing evidence on the prevalence of ADHD in obese patients and the weight status of individuals with ADHD. We searched for relevant articles in PubMed, PsychInfo, and ISI Web of Science from January 1980 to June 2010. Our findings indicate that there is a high occurrence of ADHD in clinical samples of patients seeking treatment for obesity. Additionally, studies show that individuals with ADHD have higher body mass index z scores and a significantly higher prevalence of obesity compared to those without ADHD. Three possible explanations for the association between ADHD and obesity have been proposed: 1) obesity or factors related to it, such as sleep-disordered breathing, may present as ADHD-like symptoms; 2) ADHD and obesity may share common biological dysfunctions; and 3) ADHD may contribute to the development of obesity. In terms of clinical implications, our findings suggest that it is important to screen for ADHD in obese patients and to consider abnormal eating behaviors as potential contributing factors to obesity in individuals with ADHD. Based on initial findings, appropriate treatment for ADHD may improve the weight status of individuals with both obesity and ADHD.

title: Rapamycin treatment augments motor neuron degeneration in SOD1(G93A) mouse model of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
text:
The exact mechanisms behind the contribution of aberrant protein misfolding to the development of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) are not well understood. However, our previous research has shown that autophagy, a process involved in cellular waste removal, is altered in a mouse model of ALS. In this study, we aimed to investigate the relationship between autophagic changes and the degeneration of motor neurons (MNs) in ALS mice.

Our findings demonstrate a significant increase in the autophagic protein marker LC3-II specifically in the MNs of the spinal cord in ALS mice. Through electron microscopy and immunochemistry studies, we observed a significant accumulation of autophagic vacuoles in the dystrophic axons of spinal cord MNs in ALS mice. These changes were first observed at 90 days of age when the ALS mice displayed mild clinical symptoms, and became more prominent at 120 days. The severity of clinical symptoms correlated with the progression of MNs degeneration.

Additionally, we found a progressive accumulation of p62/SQSTM1, indicating a potential impairment in the autophagic flux in the SOD1(G93A) mice. Surprisingly, treatment with the autophagy enhancer rapamycin accelerated MNs degeneration, shortened the lifespan of ALS mice, and had no significant effect on the accumulation of SOD1 aggregates. Furthermore, rapamycin treatment in ALS mice led to more severe mitochondrial impairment, higher levels of Bax (a protein involved in apoptosis), and increased caspase-3 activation.

These findings suggest that the selective degeneration of MNs in ALS is associated with impaired autophagy, and that rapamycin treatment may worsen the pathological processes through apoptosis and other mechanisms in ALS mice.

title: Improvements in survival and clinical benefit with gemcitabine as first-line therapy for patients with advanced pancreas cancer: a randomized trial.
text:
The purpose of this study was to assess the effectiveness of gemcitabine in patients with advanced pancreas cancer who experience pain and have limited daily activities due to tumor-related symptoms. Previous treatments have not had a significant impact on the disease. Early studies with gemcitabine showed improvement in disease-related symptoms in patients with pancreas cancer. Based on these findings, a definitive trial was conducted.

A total of 126 patients with advanced symptomatic pancreas cancer participated in the study. They completed a lead-in period to characterize and stabilize their pain and were then randomly assigned to receive either gemcitabine or fluorouracil (5-FU). Gemcitabine was administered at a dose of 1,000 mg/m2 weekly for 7 weeks, followed by 1 week of rest, and then weekly for 3 weeks every 4 weeks thereafter. 5-FU was given at a dose of 600 mg/m2 once weekly.

The primary measure of effectiveness was clinical benefit response, which included assessments of pain (analgesic consumption and intensity), Karnofsky performance status, and weight. Clinical benefit was defined as a sustained improvement in at least one parameter for at least 4 weeks without worsening in any others. Other measures of effectiveness included response rate, time to progressive disease, and survival.

The results showed that 23.8% of gemcitabine-treated patients experienced a clinical benefit response, compared to only 4.8% of 5-FU-treated patients. The median survival durations were 5.65 months for gemcitabine-treated patients and 4.41 months for 5-FU-treated patients. The survival rate at 12 months was 18% for gemcitabine patients and 2% for 5-FU patients. The treatment was well tolerated.

In conclusion, this study demonstrates that gemcitabine is more effective than 5-FU in alleviating some disease-related symptoms in patients with advanced, symptomatic pancreas cancer. Gemcitabine also provides a modest survival advantage over treatment with 5-FU.

title: Endothelial-myofibroblast transition contributes to the early development of diabetic renal interstitial fibrosis in streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice.
text: Diabetic nephropathy is the primary cause of chronic renal failure. Myofibroblasts play a significant role in the production and release of extracellular matrix in diabetic renal fibrosis. Emerging evidence suggests that endothelial cells may undergo a transition to myofibroblasts under both normal and abnormal conditions. Therefore, this study aims to investigate whether this transition occurs and contributes to the development of diabetic renal interstitial fibrosis. Diabetes was induced in Tie2-Cre;LoxP-EGFP mice, a mouse line with traceable endothelial lineage, by administering streptozotocin. The study also examined the transition in MMECs (a mouse pancreatic microvascular endothelial cell line) and primary cultures of CD31+/EYFP- endothelial cells isolated from normal alpha-smooth muscle actin promoter-driven-EYFP mouse kidneys. Confocal microscopy revealed that 10.4 +/- 4.2% and 23.5 +/- 7.4% of renal interstitial myofibroblasts (alpha-SMA+) in 1- and 6-month streptozotocin-induced diabetic kidneys originated from endothelial cells (EGFP+/alpha-SMA+ cells), compared to only 0.2 +/- 0.1% in vehicle-treated Tie2-Cre;LoxP-EGFP mice (P < 0.01). Confocal microscopy and real-time PCR demonstrated that transforming growth factor (TGF)-beta1 induced the expression of alpha-SMA and the loss of VE-cadherin and CD31 in MMECs and primary cultures of renal endothelial cells in a time- and dose-dependent manner. These findings indicate that the transition from endothelial cells to myofibroblasts occurs and contributes to the early development and progression of diabetic renal interstitial fibrosis, suggesting that targeting this transition may be a potential therapeutic approach.

title: Effect of phosducin silencing on the photokinetic motile response of Blepharisma japonicum.
text: The coloured ciliate Blepharisma japonicum exhibits changes in swimming velocity (known as positive photokinesis) and elongates its body when exposed to prolonged illumination. We have recently suggested that changes in the phosphorylation level of a protein called phosducin (Pdc) in the ciliate may be responsible for the light-induced cell elongation. This, in turn, affects the interaction between the βγ-dimer of G-proteins (Gβγ) and β-tubulin, leading to cytoskeletal remodeling. However, the specific cellular mechanism behind the photokinetic effect in this ciliate remains unclear. In this study, we used real-time PCR to show that the levels of Pdc mRNA in ciliate cells treated with Pdc-RNAi were significantly lower compared to cells fed with bacteria carrying an empty vector (control cells). Western immunoblotting confirmed that Pdc-RNAi-treated cells expressed a much lower level of the Pdc protein. Furthermore, our assay revealed that ciliates treated with Pdc-RNAi and exposed to light had a reduced cytosolic level of Gβ (~36 kDa), while the level of Gβ localized to the membrane (~32 kDa) was increased compared to control cells. Additionally, behavioral analysis of the cells showed a significant decrease in photokinesis. These findings contribute to our understanding of the functional properties of the ciliate Pdc protein and suggest a potential role for this phosphoprotein in the photokinetic phenomenon observed in the ciliate protist Blepharisma.

title: Alzheimer’s disease and NGF signaling
text: The degeneration of basal forebrain cholinergic neurons (BFCNs) in Alzheimer's disease (AD) is an early and significant contributor to cognitive decline. The proper functioning and structure of BFCNs rely on the supply of nerve growth factor (NGF) from the cortex and hippocampus. Numerous experiments have demonstrated that a reduced supply of NGF to BFCN cell bodies leads to the loss of neuronal markers and shrinkage, similar to what is observed in AD. The delivery of adequate NGF signals to BFCN cell bodies depends on various factors, including the synthesis and release of NGF, the synthesis and expression of NGF receptors by BFCNs, the normal signaling and retrograde transport of the NGF-receptor complex, and the effective induction of gene expression by NGF. Recent research has revealed that the decreased levels of NGF at the BFCN cell bodies are primarily due to failed retrograde transport, rather than reduced synthesis, binding, or expression of NGF receptors in the BFCN terminals. In this article, we will discuss the in vivo evidence supporting the decreased retrograde transport of NGF in a mouse model with BFCN degeneration and attempt to correlate these findings with our studies on postmortem human AD brains. Furthermore, we will speculate on the potential mechanisms underlying the failed retrograde transport of NGF and its relationship to AD pathology.

title: Echocardiographic assessment of left ventricular hypertrophy: comparison to necropsy findings.
text:
The purpose of this study was to assess the accuracy of echocardiographic measurements in detecting and quantifying left ventricular (LV) hypertrophy. The researchers compared the results of blind readings of antemortem echocardiograms with LV mass measurements obtained during necropsy in 55 patients. LV mass was calculated using M-mode LV measurements according to the Penn and American Society of Echocardiography (ASE) conventions, as well as cube function and volume correction formulas in 52 patients.

The study found that Penn-cube LV mass closely correlated with necropsy LV mass (r = 0.92, p < 0.001) and only overestimated it by 6%. The sensitivity for detecting LV hypertrophy (defined as necropsy LV mass > 215 g) was 100% (18 out of 18 patients), with a specificity of 86% (29 out of 34 patients). ASE-cube LV mass also correlated well with necropsy LV mass (r = 0.90, p < 0.001), but consistently overestimated it by an average of 25%. However, this overestimation could be corrected using the equation: LV mass = 0.80 (ASE-cube LV mass) + 0.6 g. The use of ASE measurements in the volume correction formula resulted in a systematic underestimation of necropsy LV mass by an average of 30%.

In a subset of 9 patients, where 3 had technically inadequate M-mode echocardiograms, 2-dimensional echocardiographic LV mass using two methods also showed a significant correlation with necropsy LV mass (r = 0.68, p < 0.05 and r = 0.82, p < 0.01). Among other measures of LV anatomy, only the measurement of myocardial cross-sectional area was found to be sufficiently accurate for quantifying LV mass (r = 0.80, p < 0.001) or diagnosing LV hypertrophy (sensitivity = 72%, specificity = 94%).

In conclusion, this study demonstrates that echocardiographic measurements, particularly using the Penn-cube method, are highly accurate in detecting and quantifying LV hypertrophy. However, adjustments may be necessary when using the ASE-cube method or volume correction formulas. Additionally, the measurement of myocardial cross-sectional area shows promise as a reliable indicator of LV mass and hypertrophy.

title: R93W mutation in Orai1 causes impaired calcium influx in platelets.
text: Calcium store release and store-operated calcium entry (SOCE) regulate the intracellular Ca(2+) concentration in many nonexcitable cells. In platelets, the main calcium sensor expressed in the endoplasmic reticulum is STIM1. To investigate the role of the SOC channel component, Orai1, in platelet SOCE, we created mice that only expressed a mutated, inactive form of Orai1 in blood cells (Orai1(R93W)). Platelets with Orai1(R93W) exhibited significantly reduced SOCE and impaired increases in [Ca(2+)](i) when stimulated by agonists. These platelets also displayed decreased integrin activation and impaired degranulation under static conditions with low agonist concentrations. However, this defect did not significantly impact the ability of Orai1(R93W) platelets to aggregate or adhere to collagen under arterial flow conditions in an ex vivo setting. On the other hand, these adherent Orai1(R93W) platelets showed a deficiency in surface phosphatidylserine exposure, indicating that Orai1 plays a crucial role in the platelets' procoagulant response rather than other Ca(2+)-dependent cellular responses.

title: [Efficacy on post-stroke depression treated with acupuncture at the acupoints based on ziwuliuzhu and prozac].
text:
The objective of this study was to observe the effects of acupuncture treatment on post-stroke depression using the acupoints based on the ziwuliuzhu theory. Ninety-three patients were randomly assigned to three groups: a comprehensive group, a ziwuliuzhu group, and a prozac group, with 31 patients in each group. In the ziwuliuzhu group, acupuncture was administered once a day, five times a week, targeting the acupoints based on the ziwuliuzhu theory. In the prozac group, patients were prescribed fluoxetine hydrochloride (prozac) for oral administration, once a day, at a dosage of 20 mg. In the comprehensive group, acupuncture based on ziwuliuzhu was combined with oral administration of prozac, with the same treatment frequency as the ziwuliuzhu and prozac groups. The treatment duration was four weeks per session, and a total of six sessions were required. The clinical efficacy, Hamilton depression rating scale (HAMD) score, and adverse reactions were compared among the three groups. 

The results showed that the total effective rate was 96.8% in the comprehensive group, which was higher than the ziwuliuzhu group (83.9%) and the prozac group (80.6%). The HAMD score significantly decreased after 4, 12, and 24 weeks of treatment in all three groups. The comprehensive group had lower HAMD scores compared to the other two groups at each time point after treatment. There were no significant differences between the ziwuliuzhu group and the prozac group at 4 and 12 weeks of treatment, but at 24 weeks, the ziwuliuzhu group had a lower HAMD score than the prozac group. Regarding adverse reactions, there were 2 cases in the comprehensive group, 6 cases in the prozac group, and no cases in the ziwuliuzhu group. 

In conclusion, the comprehensive therapy of acupuncture based on ziwuliuzhu and oral administration of prozac showed superior clinical efficacy and improvements in depressive state compared to either the simple oral administration of prozac or ziwuliuzhu acupuncture alone. In terms of clinical efficacy, simple ziwuliuzhu acupuncture was not significantly different from the simple oral administration of prozac, but it was better in terms of long-term HAMD score and safety.

title: Linkage with methadone treatment upon release from incarceration: a promising opportunity.
text: People who use injection drugs are more likely to contract HIV, viral hepatitis, and tuberculosis. They also make up over 25% of the incarcerated population in the United States. Methadone maintenance treatment for opiate addiction has proven to be very successful in reducing drug use, drug-related crimes, and the risk of HIV transmission. Individuals who have recently been released from prison are especially vulnerable to overdoses and disease transmission. Connecting them to methadone treatment right after their release presents a hopeful chance to prevent disease transmission, help them reintegrate into society, and decrease the likelihood of them returning to prison.

title: The Diabetes Prevention Program: baseline characteristics of the randomized cohort. The Diabetes Prevention Program Research Group.
text:
The objective of the Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP) is to assess the effectiveness and safety of interventions that can delay or prevent the onset of type 2 diabetes in individuals at a higher risk. The research design and methods involved enrolling participants who were at least 25 years old, had a BMI of 24 kg/m2 or higher (22 kg/m2 or higher for Asian-Americans), and had impaired glucose tolerance with a fasting plasma glucose level between 5.3-6.9 mmol/l (or less than or equal to 6.9 mmol for American Indians). The randomization process for the DPP was completed over a period of 2.7 years, ending in June 1999.
