These findings highlight the critical role of specific sites on CTCF's C terminus in binding to cohesin and carrying out insulator functions. Notably, the only direct interaction between CTCF and cohesin occurs through contact with SA2, which is located outside the cohesin ring. This suggests that SA2 may bind first, followed by the assembly of the cohesin ring during the recruitment process.

title: Interleukin 6 plays a key role in the development of antigen-induced arthritis.
text:
In order to investigate the direct impact of interleukin (IL) 6 on the development of rheumatoid arthritis, we conducted a study using IL-6-deficient (IL-6 -/-) mice. These mice were bred for eight generations with C57BL/6 mice, a strain known to be susceptible to antigen-induced arthritis (AIA). We compared the histological and immunological characteristics of IL-6-deficient mice with their wild-type (IL-6 +/+) littermates after inducing AIA.

The results showed that while all IL-6 +/+ mice developed severe arthritis, IL-6 -/- mice only exhibited mild arthritis. Safranin O staining revealed that the articular cartilage in IL-6 -/- mice remained intact, whereas it was completely destroyed in IL-6 +/+ mice. Furthermore, we found comparable mRNA expression levels of IL-1beta and tumor necrosis factor alpha in the inflamed joints of IL-6 -/- mice, but not for IL-6. This suggests that IL-6 may play a more significant role in cartilage destruction compared to IL-1beta or tumor necrosis factor alpha.

In terms of immunological comparisons, IL-6 -/- mice exhibited reduced antigen-specific in vitro proliferative response in lymph node cells and in vivo antibody production, compared to IL-6 +/+ mice. However, IL-6 -/- mice produced a higher amount of Th2 cytokines in lymph node cells when stimulated in vitro, regardless of whether the stimulation was antigen-specific or nonspecific.

Overall, these findings indicate that IL-6 may play a crucial role in the development of AIA, both during the initiation and execution phases. Blocking IL-6 could potentially be beneficial in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis.

title: Relation between renal function within the normal range and central and peripheral arterial stiffness in hypertension.
text: The relationship between glomerular filtration rate (GFR) within the normal range and arterial stiffness in chronic kidney disease has not been well studied. To investigate this, a study was conducted on 305 patients with untreated essential hypertension who were free from cardiovascular disease. The patients had serum creatinine values below 1.4 mg/dL for men and below 1.2 mg/dL for women. Noninvasive measurements of aortic and upper-limb pulse wave velocity (PWV) were taken to assess arterial stiffness. The results showed that aortic PWV was strongly correlated with age, while upper-limb PWV had a weaker, nonlinear relationship with age. Glomerular filtration rate was found to be inversely correlated with both aortic and peripheral artery stiffness. In a multivariate analysis, age, mean arterial pressure, and GFR were independent predictors of aortic PWV, while GFR and mean arterial pressure were predictors of upper-limb PWV. These findings suggest that in hypertensive patients with normal renal function, there is an inverse relationship between GFR and stiffness of both central elastic and peripheral muscular arteries, independent of age, sex, and blood pressure.

title: Comparative gene expression profiling of in vitro differentiated megakaryocytes and erythroblasts identifies novel activatory and inhibitory platelet membrane proteins.
text: In order to discover platelet receptors that were previously unknown, we conducted a comparison of the transcriptomes of in vitro differentiated megakaryocytes (MKs) and erythroblasts (EBs). We obtained RNA from purified MK and EB cultures that were biologically paired, and then used cDNA microarrays to compare them. By performing bioinformatical analysis on the up-regulated genes in MKs, we identified 151 transcripts that encoded proteins with transmembrane domains. While some of these transcripts were already known platelet genes, we also found a number of previously unidentified or poorly characterized ones. Several of these transcripts, such as G6b, G6f, LRRC32, LAT2, and the G protein-coupled receptor SUCNR1, encoded proteins that had structural features or functions suggesting their involvement in the modulation of platelet function. We confirmed the presence of these encoded proteins through immunoblotting on platelets, and their expression on the surface of platelets through flow cytometric analysis of G6b, G6f, and LRRC32. By comparing their expression in platelets and other blood cells, we demonstrated that G6b, G6f, and LRRC32 were specific to the platelet lineage, while LAT2 and SUCNR1 were also found in other blood cells. The discovery of the succinate receptor SUCNR1 in platelets is particularly interesting, as it was shown that physiologically relevant concentrations of succinate can enhance the effect of low doses of various platelet agonists.

title: Topographic mapping of VMH → arcuate nucleus microcircuits and their reorganization by fasting
text:
We conducted a study to investigate the activation of anorexigenic neuronal pathways in the hypothalamic arcuate nucleus (ARC) by neurons in the ventromedial hypothalamic nucleus (VMH), which is known to be involved in satiety. Specifically, we wanted to determine if these VMH neurons project excitatory inputs to pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons and/or inhibitory inputs to neuropeptide-Y (NPY) neurons in the ARC, as POMC neurons inhibit feeding while NPY neurons stimulate feeding.

Using laser scanning photostimulation in brain slices from transgenic mice, we discovered that POMC and NPY neurons, although interspersed in the ARC, are regulated by different synaptic inputs. POMC neurons received strong excitatory input from the medial VMH (mVMH), whereas NPY neurons did not receive such input. Instead, NPY neurons only received weak inhibitory input from within the ARC. Furthermore, we observed that the strength of the excitatory input from the mVMH to POMC neurons decreased during fasting.

These findings reveal a newly identified circuit that is molecularly defined and dynamically regulated by the nutritional state, aligning with the established role of the VMH as a satiety center.

title: The human immunodeficiency virus type 1 nonnucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor resistance mutation I132M confers hypersensitivity to nucleoside analogs.
text: We have previously discovered a rare mutation, I132M, in the reverse transcriptase (RT) of human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1). This mutation provides high-level resistance to nonnucleoside RT inhibitors (NNRTIs) such as nevirapine and delavirdine. In this study, we aimed to further understand the impact of this mutation on viral replication capacity and resistance to other RT inhibitors. Surprisingly, our findings indicate that I132M actually makes the virus and enzyme highly susceptible to nucleoside analogs like lamivudine (3TC) and tenofovir. Through mutagenesis studies, we discovered that the mutation in the p51 subunit of RT is responsible for this increased sensitivity to the drugs. Transient kinetic analyses revealed that I132M reduces the enzyme's affinity for the natural dCTP substrate but increases its affinity for 3TC-triphosphate, explaining the hypersusceptibility. Additionally, HIV-1 with I132M experiences a significant decrease in replication capacity. However, this decrease can be partially or completely compensated for by the A62V or L214I mutation, respectively. These findings shed light on why the selection of I132M is rare in patients who are failing NNRTI regimens. They also demonstrate that a single mutation outside of the polymerase active site, specifically within the p51 subunit of RT, can have a significant impact on nucleotide selectivity.

title: AFF1 and AFF4 differentially regulate the osteogenic differentiation of human MSCs
text:
The AFF (AF4/FMR2) family of proteins, including AFF1 and AFF4, play a role as scaffolding proteins that connect two transcription elongation factors, P-TEFb and ELL1/2, in super elongation complexes (SECs). These proteins are involved in gene transcription through elongation and chromatin remodeling. However, their specific function in the osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) is not yet understood. This study aimed to investigate the impact of AFF1 and AFF4 on MSCs' osteogenic differentiation.

Using small interfering RNA (siRNA), we depleted AFF1 in human MSCs and observed increased alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, enhanced mineralization, and upregulated expression of osteogenic-related genes. Conversely, depletion of AFF4 significantly inhibited the osteogenic potential of MSCs. Furthermore, we found that overexpression of AFF1 and AFF4 had different effects on osteogenic differentiation in vitro and MSC-mediated bone formation in vivo.

Mechanistically, we discovered that AFF1 regulates the expression of DKK1 by binding to its promoter region. Depletion of DKK1 in MSCs overexpressing HA-AFF1 reversed the impairment of osteogenic differentiation. Additionally, we observed that AFF4 is enriched in the promoter region of ID1. Knockdown of AFF4 reduced the BRE luciferase activity, SP7 expression, and ALP activity induced by BMP2 treatment.

In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that AFF1 and AFF4 play distinct roles in regulating the osteogenic differentiation of human MSCs.

title: Markers of myocardial damage and inflammation in relation to long-term mortality in unstable coronary artery disease. FRISC Study Group. Fragmin during Instability in Coronary Artery Disease.
text:
In patients with unstable coronary artery disease, the levels of troponin T, C-reactive protein, and fibrinogen in the blood are associated with the short-term risk of death. To assess their usefulness in predicting long-term risk of death from cardiac causes, we analyzed data from the Fragmin during Instability in Coronary Artery Disease trial. We examined the levels of C-reactive protein and fibrinogen at enrollment, as well as the maximum troponin T level within 24 hours of enrollment, in 917 patients. These patients were followed for an average of 37.0 months.

During the follow-up period, we found that patients with higher troponin T levels had a higher risk of death from cardiac causes. Specifically, 1.2% of patients with troponin T levels less than 0.06 microg per liter died, compared to 8.7% of patients with levels between 0.06 and 0.59 microg per liter, and 15.4% of patients with levels of at least 0.60 microg per liter. Similar trends were observed for C-reactive protein and fibrinogen levels, with higher levels associated with a higher risk of death from cardiac causes.

In a multivariate analysis, both troponin T and C-reactive protein levels were found to be independent predictors of the risk of death from cardiac causes. These markers have additive effects with each other and other clinical indicators of risk.

In conclusion, elevated levels of troponin T and C-reactive protein are strongly associated with the long-term risk of death from cardiac causes in patients with unstable coronary artery disease. These markers are independent risk factors and can provide valuable information for predicting patient outcomes.

title: Loss of lamin B1 results in prolongation of S phase and decondensation of chromosome territories.
text: LMNB1, a crucial protein in the lamina mesh, plays a significant role in the structure of the nucleus. To investigate its function, we used RNA interference to silence LMNB1 expression in the colon cancer cell line DLD-1. This led to a notable redistribution of H3K27me3, a histone modification, from the periphery of the nucleus to a more uniform distribution throughout. Additionally, we observed telomere attrition, an increased occurrence of micronuclei and nuclear blebs. Through 3D-FISH analysis, we found that LMNB1-depleted cells had larger chromosome territories in terms of volume and surface area, indicating that LMNB1 is necessary for maintaining chromatin condensation in interphase nuclei. These changes resulted in a prolonged S phase due to the activation of Chk1. Furthermore, silencing LMNB1 caused significant alterations in alternative splicing of multiple genes and an increased number of enlarged nuclear speckles. Overall, our findings suggest that the nuclear lamina plays a crucial role in organizing chromosome territories, preserving genome integrity, and facilitating proper gene splicing.

title: Human artificial chromosomes with alpha satellite-based de novo centromeres show increased frequency of nondisjunction and anaphase lag.
text: We have utilized human artificial chromosomes to study the requirements for human chromosome segregation and investigate the characteristics of sequences necessary for centromere function. Normal human centromeres rely on specialized chromatin, which consists of alpha satellite DNA combined with modified histones and centromere-specific proteins. Although various types of alpha satellite DNA have been used to create artificial centromeres in experiments, it remains unclear to what extent they accurately replicate the function of natural centromeres. In our study, we employed two types of alpha satellite DNA, DXZ1 (from the X chromosome) and D17Z1 (from chromosome 17), to generate human artificial chromosomes. While these artificial chromosomes remained stable during extended periods in culture, our examination of their segregation during individual cell divisions using an anaphase assay revealed that they exhibited more errors in segregation compared to natural human chromosomes (P < 0.001). Additionally, naturally occurring abnormal small ring chromosomes derived from chromosome 17 and the X chromosome also displayed higher rates of missegregation compared to normal chromosomes. This suggests that overall chromosome size and/or structure play a role in the accuracy of chromosome segregation. Furthermore, as different artificial chromosomes exhibited varying rates of missegregation, our data indicates that the content of centromeric DNA and/or the process of epigenetic assembly can influence the behavior of artificial chromosomes during mitosis.

title: Identification of a human HLA-E-restricted CD8+ T cell subset in volunteers immunized with Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi strain Ty21a typhoid vaccine.
text: Our previous research on individuals who received the Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi (S. Typhi) vaccine has indicated that CD8+ T cells play a crucial role in defending the host. In this study, we introduce a new subset of nonclassical human HLA-E-restricted CD8+ T cells that specifically target S. Typhi. These cells were isolated from the peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) of individuals who received the Ty21a typhoid vaccine. The CD3+CD8+CD4-CD56- T cells effectively killed S. Typhi-infected cells, regardless of whether they shared classical HLA class I molecules. This killing mechanism was independent of FAS and relied on the release of granzyme B from granules. The blocking effects of concanamycin and strontium ions further supported this mechanism. The expression of HLA-E antigens on the membrane of S. Typhi-infected cells made them susceptible to lysis, while CD1-a, -b, or -c did not have the same effect. Additionally, the presence of anti-HLA-E antibodies partially inhibited these responses. We also found that presenting S. Typhi antigens through HLA-E stimulated the production of IFN-gamma. When targets were coated with peptides containing S. Typhi GroEL HLA-E binding motifs, there was an increase in the frequency of IFN-gamma spot-forming cells. These findings suggest that HLA-E can bind nonamer peptides from bacterial proteins, triggering CD8+-mediated lysis and IFN-gamma production when exposed to infected cells. This novel effector mechanism may contribute to the host's defense against intracellular bacterial infections.

title: Costs and cost-effectiveness of alternative tuberculosis management strategies in South Africa--implications for policy.
text:
The objective of this study was to analyze the economic aspects of the Hlabisa community-based directly observed therapy management strategy for tuberculosis and estimate the costs of three alternative strategies. The study was conducted in the Hlabisa health district in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. 

The methods involved comparing the current tuberculosis management strategy in Hlabisa with three alternative strategies: the Hlabisa strategy prior to 1991 which relied on hospitalization, the national strategy, and sanatorium care. The comparison was based on costs to both the health service and the patients, as well as cost-effectiveness.

The results showed that the current Hlabisa strategy was the most cost-effective, with a cost of R3799 per patient cured. In comparison, the strategy used prior to 1991 had a cost of R98307, the national strategy had a cost of R9940, and sanatorium care had a cost of R11145. The health service bore between 71% and 88% of the treatment costs, with hospitalization being the most expensive component at R119 per day. Prolonged hospitalization was found to be extremely expensive, while community care was more affordable, with a community clinic visit costing R28 and a community health worker visit costing R7. 

Under the current Hlabisa strategy, the total cost of supervising a patient in the community was R503, which is equivalent to 4.2 days in the hospital. The cost of drugs was R157, equivalent to just 1.3 days in the hospital.

In conclusion, the use of community-based directly observed therapy for tuberculosis can significantly reduce costs for both the health service and the patients. This strategy is not only cost-effective but also has important implications at a national level, supporting the goals of the new tuberculosis control program.

title: Interleukin-18 null mutation increases weight and food intake and reduces energy expenditure and lipid substrate utilization in high-fat diet fed mice
text:
The aim of this study was to investigate the effects of the proinflammatory cytokine interleukin-18 (IL-18) on food intake and energy metabolism in animals fed a high-fat diet. The researchers wanted to determine whether IL-18 affects basal metabolic rate and metabolic processes in living organisms. They conducted experiments on IL-18 knockout mice and compared their food intake, whole-body metabolism, and motor activity to those of wildtype mice. They also administered IL-18 intracerebroventricularly to mice with different IL-18 receptor genotypes to assess its anorectic effects. 

The results showed that IL-18 knockout mice, which were fed a regular chow diet, were overweight at 6 months of age and gained excess weight on both low-fat and high-fat diets. They consumed more high-fat diet and had reduced whole-body energy expenditure and increased respiratory exchange ratios. These reductions in energy expenditure were observed in various conditions, such as fasting vs. feeding, low- vs. high-fat diets, and high vs. low levels of physical activity and times of day, indicating an effect on basal metabolic rate. The circadian amplitude of energy expenditure was also blunted in IL-18 knockout mice. However, IL-18 administration in the central nervous system only reduced high-fat diet intake in wildtype mice, not in mice lacking the IL-18 receptor. 

In conclusion, the findings suggest that endogenous IL-18 suppresses appetite and promotes energy expenditure and lipid fuel substrate utilization in healthy adults consuming high-fat diets, not just during sickness.

title: Notch activation promotes cell proliferation and the formation of neural stem cell-like colonies in human glioma cells
text: Given the critical role of Notch signaling in stem cells and oncogenesis, we hypothesized that it may also play a role in cancer stem cells and cancer cells with a stem cell-like phenotype. To investigate this, we examined the potential functions of the Notch pathway in the development of cancer stem cells using human glioma as a model. Through RT-PCR analysis, we observed that most human astrogliomas of varying grades expressed Notch receptors and ligands at moderate to high levels. Additionally, we detected mRNA of Hes5, a downstream molecule of the Notch pathway, but not Hes1. In human glioma cell lines BT325, U251, SHG-44, and U87, we found mRNA encoding different types of Notch receptors, but the active form of Notch1 (NIC) was only present in SHG-44 and U87, as confirmed by Western blot analysis. Interestingly, the proliferation of these two glioma cell lines was faster compared to the other two lines where NIC was not detected. To further investigate the effects of Notch signaling on glioma cells, we over-expressed NIC of Notch1 in SHG-44 cells through constitutive transfection. Our results demonstrated that the over-expression of NIC in SHG-44 cells promoted cell growth and colony-forming activity. Moreover, we observed an increase in the formation of neurosphere-like colonies in the presence of growth factors. These colonies expressed nestin and could be induced to differentiate into cells expressing neuron-, astrocyte-, or oligodendrocyte-specific markers, resembling neural stem cells. These findings suggest that Notch signaling plays a role in promoting the formation of cancer stem cell-like cells in human glioma.

title: Rodent models in bone-related research: the relevance of calvarial defects in the assessment of bone regeneration strategies.
text: Animal models, particularly rodent models, have long been favored in bone-related biomedical research due to their ability to provide valuable data on physiological and pathological conditions. This data is crucial for developing more effective clinical interventions. The calvarial defect model, in particular, has been widely used in both basic and applied research for regenerating bone tissue. However, there is ongoing debate about whether critical size defects (defects that do not heal spontaneously) or subcritical size defects should be used in these applications. This review aims to examine the advantages and limitations of using rodent models in bone-related research, with a focus on the problematic issues surrounding the use of calvarial critical and subcritical size defects. Additionally, the article provides surgical protocols for creating both types of defects in rat calvarial bone and describes the most commonly used techniques for assessing bone tissue repair.

title: The transcriptional responses of Mycobacterium tuberculosis to inhibitors of metabolism: novel insights into drug mechanisms of action.
text: To generate a dataset of 430 microarray profiles, we monitored the differential transcriptional response of Mycobacterium tuberculosis to drugs and growth-inhibitory conditions. By unbiased grouping of these profiles, we were able to accurately cluster agents with known mechanisms of action and successfully predict the mechanisms of action for several unknown agents. We validated these predictions biochemically for two agents, pyridoacridones and phenothiazines, which were previously uncategorized. Additionally, our analysis of the dataset revealed 150 clusters of genes that are coordinately regulated, providing a glimpse into the full metabolic potential of this organism. A subset of these gene clusters was able to classify all known agents based on their mechanisms of action. By conducting transcriptional profiling of both crude and purified natural products, we can gather critical information on mechanism and detoxification before purification, which can guide the drug discovery process. In fact, the transcriptional profile generated by a crude marine natural product accurately predicted the mechanism of action of the pure active component. Furthermore, the underlying gene clusters offer valuable insights into the metabolic response of bacteria to drug-induced stress and serve as a rational basis for selecting critical metabolic targets for screening new agents with improved activity against this significant human pathogen.

title: Electron microscopic studies of macrophages in early human yolk sacs.
text: The distribution and structure of macrophages were examined in 10 human embryos during the 6th and 7th week of pregnancy, ranging from 5.5 to 12 mm in length from crown to rump. Prior to the emergence of bone marrow and lymphatic tissues, macrophages were already present in the extravascular mesenchymal tissues and intravascular spaces of the yolk sac. Alongside the macrophages, fibroblastic cells and cells involved in erythropoiesis were also observed in the extravascular area. The macrophages displayed a range of cellular structures, indicating a transition from immature cells lacking heterophagolysosomes to mature cells engaged in phagocytosis. The mature macrophages actively engulfed primitive erythroblasts and occasionally platelets. They exhibited positive staining for lysosomal enzymes and were characterized by numerous pleomorphic heterophagolysosomes at various stages of digesting phagocytized blood cells. The intravascular macrophages may have originated from either migrated extravascular macrophages or phagocytic endothelial cells. The phagocytosis and breakdown of erythroblasts appeared to be a primary function of the yolk sac macrophages. The presence of macrophages undergoing mitosis suggests their proliferation in their current location.

title: Urban malaria and anaemia in children: a cross-sectional survey in two cities of Ghana.
text:
AIM: This study aims to provide an overview of the epidemiology of urban malaria, a growing issue in sub-Saharan Africa.

METHOD: Cross-sectional surveys were conducted in Accra and Kumasi, Ghana, to investigate the risk factors for malaria infection and anemia in children aged 6-60 months.

RESULTS: The prevalence of malaria varied significantly among urban communities, ranging from 2% to 33%. Additionally, 47.1% of the children were found to be anemic (Hb<11.0 g/dl). Factors such as low socio-economic status, age, and anemia were associated with higher malaria prevalence. The attributable risks of anemia and severe anemia (Hb<8.0 g/dl) caused by malaria were 5% and 23%, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: The study revealed that urban malaria exhibits a diverse and complex nature, distinct from its rural counterpart, which has important implications for malaria control strategies. The significant variation within cities emphasizes the need for targeted interventions in specific areas or districts. Priority should be given to the urban poor, who are the most vulnerable group, when designing control measures. To develop an effective integrated control program, a thorough assessment of the malaria risk pattern in each city is essential.

title: Nitrite infusions to prevent delayed cerebral vasospasm in a primate model of subarachnoid hemorrhage.
text: The aim of this study was to investigate whether infusions of nitrite could prevent delayed cerebral vasospasm, which can lead to permanent neurological deficits or death in patients who have undergone successful treatment for ruptured intracranial aneurysm. The study involved 14 anesthetized cynomolgus monkeys, who had a blood clot placed around their right middle cerebral artery. Cerebral arteriography was performed before clot placement and on days 7 and 14 to assess vasospasm. The monkeys were divided into three groups: one group received a 90-mg sodium nitrite intravenous solution infused over 24 hours plus a 45-mg sodium nitrite bolus daily, another group received a 180-mg sodium nitrite intravenous solution infused over 24 hours, and the control group received a saline solution infusion. The infusions were administered continuously for 14 days. The main outcome measures were nitrite, S-nitrosothiol, and methemoglobin levels in blood and cerebrospinal fluid, as well as the degree of arteriographic vasospasm. The results showed that in the control group, cerebrospinal fluid nitrite levels decreased significantly over time, and all monkeys in this group developed significant vasospasm, with one experiencing stroke and death. In contrast, the monkeys in the nitrite infusion groups had increased nitrite and methemoglobin levels in their blood and cerebrospinal fluid, without experiencing systemic hypotension. Nitrite infusion prevented the development of vasospasm, with no animals in the nitrite-treated groups developing significant vasospasm. There was a negative correlation between the concentration of nitrite in cerebrospinal fluid and the degree of cerebral vasospasm. The infusion of nitrite also led to the formation of S-nitrosothiol in cerebrospinal fluid. There were no signs of nitrite toxicity in terms of clinical or pathological evidence. In conclusion, subacute sodium nitrite infusions were found to prevent delayed cerebral vasospasm in a primate model of subarachnoid hemorrhage.

title: Developmental gene networks: a triathlon on the course to T cell identity
text: Cells acquire their final identities by activating combinations of transcription factors that initiate and maintain the expression of specific genes for each cell type. The development of T cells relies on the progression of precursor cells through three main stages. Each stage is associated with distinct sets of transcription factors that regulate the recruitment of these cells to the thymus, their growth, commitment to a specific lineage, and their ability to respond to signals from the T cell receptor. Only after these processes are complete can the cells be assigned to specific effector programs. All three stages are crucial for proper T cell development, as well as the mechanisms that establish the boundaries between them. If a cell fails to deactivate one group of regulators before activating the next gene network phase, it becomes more susceptible to developing leukemia.

title: A tumor necrosis factor-α–mediated pathway promoting autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
text: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) is a genetic condition caused by mutations in either the PKD1 or PKD2 genes, which produce polycystin-1 and polycystin-2 proteins, respectively. In this study, we demonstrate that tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), an inflammatory molecule found in the fluid-filled cysts of individuals with ADPKD, disrupts the normal localization of polycystin-2 to the cell membrane and primary cilia. This disruption is mediated by a protein called FIP2, which is induced by TNF-α. When mouse kidney tissue was treated with TNF-α, cysts formed, and this effect was more pronounced in kidneys with heterozygous mutations in the Pkd2 gene (Pkd2+/−). TNF-α also promoted cyst formation in Pkd2+/− mice in vivo. However, when Pkd2+/− mice were treated with a TNF-α inhibitor called etanercept, cyst formation was prevented. These findings highlight a pathway involving TNF-α, polycystins, and cyst formation, which may be activated when the levels of functional polycystin-2 fall below a critical threshold, leading to the cellular changes observed in ADPKD.

title: Inappropriate inhaler use: assessment of use and patient preference of seven inhalation devices. EDICI.
text: The aim of this study was to evaluate patients' use of different inhaler devices and determine if patient preference is a reliable indicator of ease of use. We also wanted to assess if current inhaler use had any impact on technique or preference. One hundred patients were taught how to use seven different inhaler devices in a random order. Their inhaler technique was then assessed using predetermined criteria. Patients were asked to identify their top three preferred inhalers and indicate which inhaler they currently used. Breath-actuated inhalers, specifically the Easi-Breathe and Autohaler, had the best technique scores, with 91% of patients demonstrating good technique. The pressurized metered dose inhaler (pMDI) performed poorly, with only 79% of patients showing good technique, despite being the most commonly prescribed. The Easi-Breathe was the most popular device among patients, followed closely by the Autohaler, Clickhaler, and Accuhaler. Although the majority of patients (55%) currently used the pMDI, it did not score highly in terms of preference or technique. Only 79% of patients were able to effectively use the pMDI even after receiving expert instruction, yet it continues to be widely prescribed. This has significant implications for drug delivery and disease control. Prescribing a patient's preferred device may increase cost, but it can improve efficiency and ultimately be cost-effective in the long run. Using a less expensive device (pMDI) when technique is good and the patient's preferred inhaler when it is not may optimize drug delivery and potentially reduce costs.

title: Hemoperfusion-hemodialysis ineffective for paraquat removal in life-threatening poisoning?
text: We present a case study of a patient who underwent hemoperfusion-hemodialysis (HP-HD) for severe paraquat poisoning. This treatment approach was chosen due to its potential to enhance overall drug removal through a combination of adsorption and dialysis. Upon admission, the patient's blood paraquat level was measured at 15.8 micrograms/ml. The patient received conventional treatment along with HP-HD, which began within 3 hours of ingesting the chemical and lasted for 5 hours. Blood samples were collected during and after the HP-HD procedure. Specifically, samples were taken before the charcoal column, between the charcoal column and the artificial kidney, and after the artificial kidney. The blood clearances of paraquat were determined to be 116 +/- 32 ml/min (n=6) for the charcoal column (HP), 90 +/- 54 ml/min (n=6) for the artificial kidney (HD), and 151 +/- 37 ml/min (n=6) for the combined systems (HP-HD). Following the HP-HD treatment, there was a slight increase in blood paraquat levels. One day after admission, the patient developed renal and hepatic failure and unfortunately passed away after 5 days. Tissue samples were collected to measure paraquat levels (microgram/g wet tissue), which were found to be: skeletal muscle 9.4, pancreas 6.0, prostate 5.6, thyroid 4.2, lungs 4.0, bone marrow 4.0, kidney 3.1, spleen 2.9, adrenal 2.9, heart 2.8, liver 2.3, and stomach and testis below 1.0. Blood level measurements demonstrated the effective clearance of paraquat from the central (plasma) compartment with HP-HD. However, these findings align with previous reports suggesting that the efficacy of short-term HP-HD in treating severe paraquat poisoning is questionable, as paraquat levels in the peripheral (tissue) compartment remain elevated.

title: Cancer treatment and survivorship statistics, 2014.
text: Due to the aging and growth of the population, as well as advancements in early detection and treatment, the number of cancer survivors is steadily increasing. To better support these survivors, the American Cancer Society and the National Cancer Institute collaborated to estimate the current and future number of survivors using data from the SEER program registries. Additionally, treatment patterns for the most common types of cancer are described based on information from the National Cancer Data Base and the SEER and SEER-Medicare linked databases, including a brief overview of treatment-related side effects. As of January 1, 2014, there were approximately 14.5 million Americans with a history of cancer who were still alive, and by January 1, 2024, this number is projected to reach nearly 19 million. The three most prevalent cancers among males are prostate cancer (43%), colorectal cancer (9%), and melanoma (8%), while among females, the most common are breast cancer (41%), uterine corpus cancer (8%), and colon and rectum cancer (8%). The age distribution of survivors varies significantly depending on the type of cancer. For instance, the majority of prostate cancer survivors (62%) are aged 70 years or older, whereas less than one-third (32%) of melanoma survivors fall into this older age group. It is crucial for clinicians to comprehend the unique medical and psychosocial needs of cancer survivors and to actively assess and address these concerns. Fortunately, there is a growing number of resources available to assist patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers in navigating the different phases of cancer survivorship.

title: Massive activation of archaeal defense genes during viral infection.
text: Archaeal viruses exhibit an unusually wide range of genetic and morphological variations. The study of these viruses has been crucial in expanding our knowledge of viral diversity and evolution. One particular virus, the Sulfolobus islandicus rod-shaped virus 2 (SIRV2), serves as a model for investigating virus-host interactions in Archaea. SIRV2 is a lytic virus that utilizes a unique method of exiting the host cell by forming distinctive pyramidal structures on the cell envelope. In this study, we utilized whole-transcriptome sequencing to create a comprehensive map of host and viral gene expression during the infection cycle of SIRV2 in its hyperthermophilic host S. islandicus LAL14/1. This information, combined with a yeast two-hybrid analysis of SIRV2 protein interactions, advanced our understanding of viral gene functions. As a result of SIRV2 infection, over one-third of S. islandicus genes exhibited differential regulation in their transcription. Genes involved in cell division showed decreased expression, while those involved in antiviral defense were highly activated. Specifically, genes related to toxin-antitoxin and clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeat (CRISPR)-Cas systems were prominently expressed. The varying levels of activation in different CRISPR-Cas systems highlight their specialized functions. This data on individual gene expression and activation of antiviral defense systems will be valuable for future studies aiming to understand the intricate functions and interactions of these systems in vivo.

title: Impact of human immunodeficiency virus infection on the histological features of chronic hepatitis C: a case-control study. The MULTIVIRC group.
text: The Hepatitis C virus (HCV) is commonly found in individuals who are also infected with the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) due to shared transmission routes. Previous research has indicated that HIV infection can accelerate the progression of chronic hepatitis C, leading to cirrhosis at a faster rate. However, these studies did not consider other factors that contribute to the advancement of liver fibrosis, such as alcohol consumption, sexual behavior, age at infection, and duration of HCV infection. In our study, we examined liver biopsy samples from two groups of 58 patients: one group infected with both HCV and HIV, and the other group infected with HCV alone. We matched the two groups based on the aforementioned risk factors and evaluated the biopsy results using the METAVIR criteria. We found that HIV-positive patients had higher levels of liver activity compared to HIV-negative patients. Cirrhosis was more prevalent in HIV-positive patients with a CD4 count of 200 cells/microL or less (45%) compared to HIV-negative patients (10%) (P = .003). Additionally, cirrhosis was more common in HIV-positive patients with a CD4 count of 200 cells/microL or less (45%) compared to HIV-positive patients with a CD4 count above 200 cells/microL (17%) (P = .04). These differences, which were associated with HIV status, may be attributed to increased HCV replication during HIV infection or other immune mechanisms that require further investigation.

title: Relation of plasma leptin concentrations to sex, body fat, dietary intake, and peak oxygen uptake in young adult women and men.
text: The aim of this study was to investigate the connection between leptin and metabolic and dietary factors in college-age adults. A total of 32 young adult women and men participated in the study. They underwent various tests to measure their body mass index, body composition, peak oxygen consumption (VO2peak), dietary intake, and levels of leptin and insulin in their plasma. The results showed that women had significantly higher levels of ln leptin compared to men (2.1 ng/mL versus 1.2 ng/mL, respectively). This difference remained significant even after taking into account fat mass and fat-free mass as covariates in separate analyses. Men had higher VO2peak values than women, and this difference remained significant even after adjusting for differences in fat-free mass and total body mass. There were significant correlations between ln leptin and indicators of fat mass in both women and men, with stronger correlations observed in men. Ln leptin showed a significant inverse relationship with VO2peak in men only. However, after adjusting for body fat mass, ln leptin was not significantly associated with any of the measured variables. On the other hand, when ln leptin was normalized using fat mass as the divisor (a less reliable statistical analysis method), men showed significant correlations between ln leptin and dietary intake and VO2peak. Although women had higher plasma leptin values, stronger associations between leptin and metabolic and dietary factors were found in men compared to women.

title: Expression of a human cytomegalovirus latency-associated homolog of interleukin-10 during the productive phase of infection.
text: The UL111A region of the human cytomegalovirus is active during both productive and latent stages of infection. In the productive stage, the virus produces two proteins: ORF79, which has oncogenic properties, and cmvIL-10, a functional equivalent of human IL-10. In the latent stage, a modified version of cmvIL-10 called latency-associated (LA) cmvIL-10 has been previously discovered in myeloid progenitor cells. To investigate if LAcmvIL-10 is transcribed during productive infection, we conducted 5' and 3' RACE experiments to map UL111A-region transcripts in human foreskin fibroblasts (HFFs) infected with the virus. Our analysis revealed the presence of a single-spliced UL111A-region transcript that is likely to encode LAcmvIL-10. This transcript was expressed in HFFs with early (beta) kinetics, which is different from the timing of ORF79 (alpha kinetics) and cmvIL-10 (gamma kinetics). These findings demonstrate the existence and location of a transcript that encodes a latency-associated version of IL-10, which is produced by the virus during the productive phase of infection.

title: Kruppel-like factor 4 is essential for inflammatory monocyte differentiation in vivo.
text: This study demonstrates the importance of Kruppel-like factor (KLF) family of transcription factors in the differentiation, survival, and trafficking of blood and immune cell types. Our findings show that hematopoietic cells from KLF4(-/-) fetal livers (FL) have normal numbers of functional hematopoietic progenitor cells and perform well in competitive repopulation assays. However, when these KLF4(-/-) fetal liver cells are transplanted into lethally irradiated wild-type mice, the resulting "KLF4(-/-) chimeras" lack circulating inflammatory monocytes and have reduced numbers of resident monocytes. Although peritoneal macrophages are unaffected, bone marrow monocytic cells from KLF4(-/-) chimeras show lower levels of key trafficking molecules and increased apoptosis. These findings demonstrate that KLF4 is essential for the differentiation of mouse inflammatory monocytes and plays a role in the differentiation of resident monocytes. Additionally, we found that inducible expression of KLF4 in the HL60 human acute myeloid leukemia cell line promotes monocytic differentiation and enhances macrophage differentiation, but inhibits granulocytic differentiation. The specific effects of loss-of-KLF4 and gain-of-KLF4-induced monocytic differentiation in HL60 cells highlight KLF4 as a crucial regulator of monocytic differentiation and a potential target for immune modulation.

title: A population-based, case–control study of green tea consumption and leukemia risk in southwestern Taiwan
text: This study aimed to examine the connection between leukemia and green tea consumption. A total of 252 cases (90.3% response rate) and 637 controls (53.4% response rate) were included in the study. Controls were selected to match cases in terms of age and gender. Participants' living habits, including tea consumption, were recorded. Green tea was used as a reference to estimate the total amount of catechins consumed by each individual. The consumption of catechins was divided into four levels. Conditional logistic regression models were used to assess the relationship between leukemia and catechin consumption in two age groups: 0-15 years and 16-29 years. The results showed a significant inverse association between green tea consumption and leukemia risk in individuals aged 16-29 years, while no significant association was observed in the younger age groups. In the older group with higher tea consumption (>550 units of catechins), the adjusted odds ratio (OR) compared to the group without tea consumption was 0.47 [95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.23-0.97]. After adjusting for smoking status and medical irradiation exposure, the overall OR for all participants was 0.49 (95% CI = 0.27-0.91), indicating a negative relationship between high catechin intake and leukemia. Drinking sufficient amounts of tea, particularly green tea which has higher catechin content compared to oolong tea and black tea, may potentially lower the risk of leukemia.

title: Specific HDV RNA-templated transcription by pol II in vitro.
text: The role of RNA polymerase II in RNA-templated RNA synthesis during viroid and Hepatitis Delta Virus (HDV) replication is not well understood. To address this, we have developed an in vitro transcription system using HeLa cell nuclear extract (NE). In this system, a specific segment of antigenomic RNA from the left-hand tip region of the HDV rod-like structure serves as a template for efficient and specific RNA synthesis. The accumulation of the unique RNA product is highly sensitive to alpha-amanitin in HeLa NE, indicating the involvement of RNA polymerase II. However, NE from PMG cells, which contain an alpha-amanitin-resistant subunit of pol II, only partially inhibits the synthesis of this RNA product, further supporting the involvement of pol II. Detailed analysis of the RNA product reveals that it is a chimeric molecule consisting of a newly synthesized transcript attached to the 5' half of the RNA template. The selection of the transcription start site is highly specific and depends on the secondary structure of the RNA template rather than its primary sequence. This reaction shares similarities with the RNA cleavage-extension process observed in pol II-arrested complexes in vitro. We discuss the potential role of this reaction in HDV replication.

title: Pulmonary vascular lesions in end-stage idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: Histopathologic study on lung explant specimens and correlations with pulmonary hemodynamics.
text: In patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), the changes in pulmonary vessels are well understood in fibrotic areas but have not been accurately assessed in the areas of preserved lung tissue. Additionally, the relationship between pulmonary vessel lesions and pulmonary hemodynamics is not well understood. Therefore, we conducted a retrospective study using lung explant specimens from 26 patients who had undergone lung transplantation and had a confirmed diagnosis of IPF. Our objectives were to (1) describe the vascular lesions, particularly in preserved lung areas, and (2) examine their correlation with pulmonary hemodynamics. In dense fibrotic regions, all patients exhibited thickening of the arterial and venous walls with significant narrowing of the lumen. In architecturally preserved lung regions, 65% of patients showed occlusion of venules and small pulmonary veins, although there were only minor changes in muscular pulmonary arteries. We discovered a significant positive correlation between the extent of lung fibrosis and mean pulmonary artery pressure. However, we did not find a relationship between mean pulmonary artery pressure and venous/venular lesions in nonfibrotic areas. Our study highlights that many patients with IPF have occlusive venopathy in nonfibrotic lung areas, the significance of which remains unknown.

title: Maternal and perinatal outcome in severe pregnancy-related liver disease.
text: Acute fatty liver of pregnancy (AFLP) and the syndrome of hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme levels, and low platelet count (HELLP) are uncommon but significant disorders that occur during the third trimester of pregnancy. Over a span of 10 years, our Liver Failure Unit received 46 women (median age, 30 years; range, 17-41 years) with severe hepatic dysfunction. The majority of these women were having their first pregnancy, and 5 were carrying twins. The median gestational age at admission was 35 weeks (range, 24-40 weeks). Upon admission, 70% of the patients were diagnosed with preeclampsia, and 46% were experiencing encephalopathy and/or required ventilation. Among the patients, 70% exhibited clinical features and laboratory values consistent with AFLP, while 15% had HELLP syndrome. One patient experienced preeclamptic liver rupture and required a liver transplant. In 6 other patients, severe liver dysfunction unrelated to pregnancy was identified as the cause. Infectious complications were observed in 53% of AFLP patients and 29% of HELLP syndrome patients. Major intra-abdominal bleeding occurred in 12 women (10 with AFLP), and 9 of them required laparotomies for clot removal. Four AFLP patients (12.5%) had fatal outcomes, resulting in a perinatal mortality rate of 9%. No maternal or perinatal deaths were associated with HELLP syndrome. In contrast to previous studies, this large series suggests a relatively positive outcome for mothers and babies affected by severe AFLP and HELLP syndrome. Further improvements in outcome can be achieved by preventing bleeding and infectious complications associated with these disorders.

title: Circadian rhythms and the regulation of metabolic tissue function and energy homeostasis.
text: The coordination of physiological processes with cyclic changes in the physical environment relies heavily on circadian oscillators. Recent clinical and molecular studies have indicated that circadian biology may have a crucial role in regulating the functions of adipose and other metabolic tissues. This discussion aims to propose the hypothesis that circadian dysfunction could be implicated in the development of obesity, type 2 diabetes, and the metabolic syndrome.

title: Large-scale gene function analysis with the PANTHER classification system
text: The PANTHER classification system is a comprehensive tool that allows biologists to analyze large-scale genomic data from sequencing, proteomics, or gene expression experiments. It combines gene function, ontology, pathways, and statistical analysis tools. The system is built with 82 complete genomes organized into gene families and subfamilies, and their evolutionary relationships are represented in phylogenetic trees, multiple sequence alignments, and statistical models. Genes are classified based on their function, with families and subfamilies annotated with ontology terms and sequences assigned to PANTHER pathways. The PANTHER website offers a range of tools for browsing and querying gene functions, as well as analyzing experimental data using statistical tests. It is widely used by scientists in various fields. In the 2013 release, the website interface was redesigned to enhance user experience and analytical capabilities. This protocol provides a detailed guide on how to analyze genome-wide experimental data using the PANTHER classification system.

title: Periostin, a novel marker of intramembranous ossification, is expressed in fibrous dysplasia and in c-Fos-overexpressing bone lesions.
text: Fibrous dysplasia is a non-cancerous bone condition caused by a mutation in the gene responsible for the Gs alpha protein, which leads to elevated levels of cyclic adenosine monophosphate. Histologically, fibrous dysplasia is characterized by the production of fibrous tissue and the deposition of abnormal type I collagen and other bone-related proteins. Additionally, irregular woven bone is formed, often with Sharpey fibers containing type I collagen. Fibrous dysplasia is also associated with increased expression of c-Fos/c-Jun, which are known targets of cyclic adenosine monophosphate signaling. In this study, we investigated the presence of periostin, a protein involved in bone formation, and its receptor integrin alpha v beta 3 (CD51/61), in both normal bones and fibrous dysplasia. Through immunohistochemistry and in situ hybridization, we found that periostin was present in the extracellular matrix during the formation of woven bone, but not during endochondral ossification. It was also found in the fibrous component of fibrous dysplasia, with all cells surrounding periostin-positive areas expressing CD51/61. Notably, periostin was highly localized to Sharpey fibers. To further understand the role of c-Fos, we studied transgenic mice that overexpressed c-fos and developed sclerotic lesions similar to those seen in fibrous dysplasia. In these lesions, transformed osteoblasts expressed high levels of periostin, while normal osteoblasts did not. Our findings suggest that periostin could serve as a new marker for woven bone formation and may be a potential diagnostic or therapeutic target for fibrous dysplasia. Furthermore, the Gs alpha-cyclic adenosine monophosphate-c-Fos pathway may contribute to the up-regulation of periostin in fibrous dysplasia, leading to the abnormal collagen formation characteristic of this disease.

title: FGF-2 enhances intestinal stem cell survival and its expression is induced after radiation injury.
text:
The role of fibroblast growth factors (FGFs) in various cell types and developmental processes is well-established. FGF-2, in particular, has been found to regulate the migration and replication of intestinal epithelial cells. However, its effects on intestinal epithelial stem cells during normal renewal or regeneration after injury are not well understood. To address this, we conducted a study on the expression of FGF-2 in the mouse small intestine after irradiation and its impact on crypt stem cell survival following radiation injury.

We observed that the expression of FGF-2 mRNA and protein increased starting from 12 hours after gamma-irradiation, with peak levels observed between 48 and 120 hours post-irradiation. Throughout this period, the higher molecular mass isoform of FGF-2 (approximately 24 kDa) was the predominant form expressed in the small intestine. Immunohistochemical analysis revealed that FGF-2 was mainly present in the mesenchyme surrounding regenerating crypts after radiation injury.

Furthermore, we found that the administration of exogenous recombinant human FGF-2 (rhFGF-2) significantly improved the survival of crypt stem cells when given prior to irradiation. This suggests that FGF-2 expression is induced by radiation injury and that rhFGF-2 can enhance the survival of crypt stem cells following subsequent injury.

In summary, our study demonstrates the induction of FGF-2 expression after radiation injury and highlights the potential of rhFGF-2 in promoting the survival of crypt stem cells after injury.

title: Caspase inhibitors promote alternative cell death pathways.
text: The discovery of alternative cell death programs for apoptosis has been made possible through the use of caspase inhibitors. One such inhibitor, zVAD-fmk, has been found to modulate the three main types of cell death. By adding zVAD-fmk, apoptotic cell death is blocked, cells become more susceptible to necrotic cell death, and autophagic cell death is induced. Research has shown that the kinase RIP1 and the adenosine nucleotide translocator (ANT)-cyclophilin D (CypD) complex play a crucial role in necrotic cell death. The mechanism behind zVAD-fmk's ability to sensitize cells to necrotic cell death involves inhibiting caspase-8-mediated proteolysis of RIP1 and disrupting the ANT-CypD interaction. RIP1 is also involved in autophagic cell death. Studies using caspase inhibitors and knockdown techniques have revealed that catalase and caspase-8 have negative roles in autophagic cell death. The involvement of RIP1 and caspase-8 in both necrotic and autophagic cell death suggests that these two types of cell death are interconnected. Necrotic cell death is a rapid response by cells that involves the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in mitochondria, a decrease in adenosine triphosphate concentration, and other cellular damage. On the other hand, autophagic cell death initially begins as a survival mechanism to remove ROS-damaged mitochondria. However, when this process becomes excessive, autophagy itself becomes toxic and leads to autophagic cell death. Gaining a better understanding of the molecular mechanisms behind these alternative cell death pathways could lead to therapeutic strategies for combating cell death in neurodegenerative diseases, ischemia-reperfusion pathologies, and infectious diseases. Additionally, it may aid in the development of alternative cytotoxic approaches for cancer treatment.

title: Nucleosome stability mediated by histone variants H3.3 and H2A.Z.
text: In vivo, nucleosomes containing the histone variant H3.3 are often found clustered near active genes and regulatory elements. However, it has been unclear whether these H3.3-containing nucleosomes have unique properties that impact transcription. Our findings reveal that H3.3 nucleosomes isolated from vertebrates, regardless of their partnership with H2A or H2A.Z, are remarkably susceptible to disruption by salt, resulting in the loss of H2A/H2B or H2A.Z/H2B dimers. Immunoprecipitation studies of nucleosome core particles (NCPs) demonstrate that NCPs containing both H3.3 and H2A.Z are even less stable than those containing H3.3 and H2A. Interestingly, NCPs containing H3 and H2A.Z exhibit similar stability to H3/H2A NCPs. These findings establish a hierarchy of stabilities for native nucleosomes carrying different variants and suggest that H2A.Z may have distinct roles depending on its partners within the NCP. Furthermore, these results support the notion that H3.3 actively maintains accessible chromatin structures in enhancer and transcribed regions. Consistently, promoters, enhancers, and coding regions of highly expressed genes contain nucleosomes carrying both H3.3 and H2A.Z, making them highly susceptible to disruption.

title: Increased growth after long-term oral 1alpha,25-vitamin D3 in childhood renal osteodystrophy.
text:
We conducted a study on six prepubescent children with renal osteodystrophy who had previously been treated with vitamin D2. The children were given oral 1,25-vitamin D3 therapy for up to 26 months, with doses ranging from 14 to 41 ng per kilogram per day. The goal of the therapy was to correct hypocalcemia and reverse bone disease.

Before the treatment, the serum levels of 1,25-vitamin D3 were initially reduced, averaging at 15 +/- 5 pg per milliliter. However, after the treatment, these levels increased to 54 +/- 13. Similarly, the serum calcium levels rose from 7.5 +/- 1.6 mg per deciliter to 9.8 +/- 0.6 after one month (P less than 0.02). Additionally, the alkaline phosphatase activity decreased from 536 +/- 298 to 208 +/- 91 IU per liter after 12 months (P less than 0.05). The serum immunoreactive parathyroid levels also decreased from 900 +/- 562 microliter eq per milliliter to 411 +/- 377.

We observed healing of rickets and subperiosteal erosions, indicating that the bone was remineralizing. This was confirmed by the photon absorption technique. In four of the patients, we evaluated their growth velocity for 12 months before and after the therapy. We found that their growth velocity increased from 2.6 +/- 0.8 to 8.0 +/- 3.2 cm per year. Furthermore, their growth velocity per year improved from being below the third percentile to ranging from the 10th to 97th percentile after the therapy. The height increment ranged from 27 to 113 percent of the expected change in chronological age and 40 to 114 percent of the expected change in bone age after the therapy.

This trial demonstrates that oral 1,25-vitamin D3 can effectively reverse renal bone disease and promote growth in children with uremia.

title: Rapid progression of familial amyloidotic polyneuropathy: a multinational natural history study.
text:
The aim of this study was to examine the relationship between the severity of neuropathy and disease stage, as well as estimate the rate of neuropathy progression in patients with familial amyloidotic polyneuropathy (FAP) from multiple countries. The researchers assessed the severity and progression of neuropathy in patients with FAP from France, the United States, Portugal, and Italy. They collected data on Neuropathy Impairment Scores (NIS), time from symptom onset to NIS measurement, polyneuropathy disability (PND) scores, FAP disease stage, and manual grip strength. The researchers used Loess Fit and Gompertz Fit models to estimate neuropathy progression. 

The study included 283 patients with a mean age of 56.4 years. They found that there was variation in the transthyretin (TTR) mutation among the different countries, with the majority of patients in Portugal having early-onset Val30Met-FAP. There was also variation in PND score, FAP stage, and TTR stabilizer use among the countries. The researchers found that NIS was associated with PND score and FAP stage, indicating that the severity of neuropathy increased with higher scores and stages. There was also a relationship between NIS and TTR genotype. The estimated rate of NIS progression for a population with a median NIS of 32 was 14.3 points per year, and for the modified NIS+7, it was 17.8 points per year. 

In conclusion, this multinational study of patients with FAP showed that neuropathy progressed rapidly and that the severity of neuropathy was associated with functional scales of locomotion.

title: The BRRF1 early gene of Epstein-Barr virus encodes a transcription factor that enhances induction of lytic infection by BRLF1.
text: The transition from the latent to the lytic form of Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection is facilitated by the viral immediate-early (IE) proteins, BZLF1 (Z) and BRLF1 (R). Within the BRLF1 intron, there is an EBV early protein called BRRF1 (Na), but its role in the viral life cycle remains unknown. In this study, we demonstrate that Na enhances the R-mediated induction of lytic EBV infection in 293 cells that are latently infected with a recombinant EBV (R-KO) lacking the expression of both R and Na. Additionally, Na also enhances R-induced lytic infections in a gastric carcinoma line (AGS) carrying the R-KO virus, but it has no effect in a Burkitt lymphoma line (BL-30) that is stably infected with the same mutant virus. Our findings reveal that Na functions as a transcription factor that enhances the ability of R to activate Z expression from the R-KO viral genome in 293 cells. Furthermore, Na alone can activate the Z promoter (Zp) in cells that are not infected with EBV. The activation of Zp by Na requires a CRE motif (ZII), and a consensus CRE motif is sufficient to confer Na responsiveness to the heterologous E1b promoter. Moreover, we demonstrate that Na enhances the transactivator function of a Gal4-c-Jun fusion protein, but it does not enhance the transactivator function of other transcription factors (such as ATF-1, ATF-2, and CREB) that are known to bind CRE motifs. The expression of Na in cells leads to increased levels of a hyperphosphorylated form of c-Jun, suggesting a mechanism by which Na activates c-Jun. Overall, our results indicate that Na is a transcription factor that activates the EBV Zp IE promoter through its interaction with c-Jun, and it suggests that Na works in conjunction with BRLF1 to induce the lytic form of EBV infection in specific cell types.

title: Stromal p16 expression differentiates endometrial polyp from endometrial hyperplasia
text: Endometrial polyps are common non-cancerous growths in the lining of the uterus, but their cause is not well understood, although some studies suggest they may be benign tumors of the supportive tissue. While it is easy to diagnose endometrial polyps through a surgical sample, it can be challenging to differentiate them from endometrial hyperplasia in a biopsy or curettage sample. Currently, there is no immunohistochemical marker that can help with this distinction. In this study, we investigated the expression of a protein called p16 in 35 endometrial polyps and 33 cases of endometrial hyperplasia, which included 16 simple hyperplasias, 14 complex atypical hyperplasias, and 3 complex hyperplasias without atypia. The expression of p16 in the supportive tissue differed significantly between the two groups; it was present in 31 (89%) of the endometrial polyps, but only in 1 (3%) of the endometrial hyperplasia cases. The percentage of supportive cells that showed p16 expression ranged from 10% to 90% (average of 47%), and these positive cells tended to be located around the glands. We also examined six cases of endometrial hyperplasia within an endometrial polyp, and all of them showed p16 expression in the supportive tissue. There was no difference in p16 expression in the glandular cells between endometrial polyps (33 cases, 94%) and hyperplasia (27 cases, 82%). The presence of p16-immunoreactivity was mostly limited to metaplastic epithelial cells in both groups. The expression of p16 in the supportive tissue may be a unique characteristic of endometrial polyps and could serve as a useful marker for diagnosis, particularly in fragmented samples from biopsies or curettage. This expression of p16 in the supportive tissue may reflect a process called p16-induced cellular senescence, which has been observed in various non-cancerous mesenchymal tumors.

title: A systematic review of mortality in schizophrenia: is the differential mortality gap worsening over time?
text: Despite improvements in mental health services in recent years, it is still unclear whether the risk of mortality in individuals with schizophrenia has changed over time. The objective of this study was to examine the distribution of standardized mortality ratios (SMRs) for people with schizophrenia. To gather data, a comprehensive search was conducted using various databases and search terms. A total of 37 articles from 25 different countries were included in the analysis. The median SMR for all-cause mortality was found to be 2.58, with a pooled SMR of 2.50. No significant difference was observed between sexes. Suicide had the highest SMR, but other causes of death were also elevated in individuals with schizophrenia. Furthermore, the SMRs for all-cause mortality have increased in recent years. These findings highlight a significant disparity in mortality rates between individuals with schizophrenia and the general population, and this gap has worsened over time. Given the potential negative impact of certain medications on mortality rates, it is crucial to prioritize the overall health of individuals with schizophrenia.

title: Antioxidant Defenses in the Rat Placenta in Late Gestation: Increased Labyrinthine Expression of Superoxide Dismutases, Glutathione Peroxidase 3, and Uncoupling Protein 21
text: Placental oxidative stress plays a crucial role in the development of placenta-related disorders, particularly preeclampsia (PE) and intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR). Oxidative stress occurs when reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulate and cause damage to DNA, proteins, and lipids. This damage is limited by antioxidant enzymes, and mitochondrial uncoupling protein 2 (UCP2) may also reduce ROS production and limit oxidative stress. In this study, we examined the antioxidant defenses of the placenta during normal gestation and after inducing IUGR with glucocorticoids. Placentas were collected from rats on Days 16 and 22 of a normal pregnancy (term = Day 23), as well as on Day 22 after treatment with dexamethasone starting on Day 13. We measured the expression of several genes that encode antioxidant enzymes (Sod1, Sod2, Sod3, Cat, Gpx3, Txn1, Txnrd1, Txnrd2, and Txnrd3) and Ucp2 using quantitative RT-PCR in two regions of the placenta: the labyrinth (LZ) and the junctional zone (JZ). We found that the expression of Sod1 and Ucp2 mRNA, as well as the activity of xanthine oxidase (a source of ROS), increased from Days 16 to 22 in both placental zones. Sod2 and Gpx3 expression increased only in the rapidly growing LZ. However, Sod3 and Txnrd1 expression decreased in the LZ during this period, while total superoxide dismutase activity remained stable. Treatment with dexamethasone reduced fetal-placental growth and LZ expression of Ucp2, but increased JZ expression of Txn1. Measures of placental oxidative damage (TBARS, F2-isoprostanes, and 8-OHdG) did not change with gestational age or dexamethasone treatment, indicating sufficient antioxidant protection. Overall, our findings suggest that the rat placenta is protected from oxidative stress through the dynamic expression of antioxidant defense genes, which varies depending on the region and stage of development.

title: Emerging role of bisphosphonates in the clinic--antitumor activity and prevention of metastasis to bone.
text: Bisphosphonates are currently utilized to treat bone metastases, and emerging evidence suggests that they may also possess antitumor properties. Preclinical research has shown that zoledronic acid can hinder the growth of blood vessels, invasion and attachment of tumor cells, as well as overall tumor progression. Furthermore, there is emerging data indicating that these agents may hinder the development of skeletal metastases. In a recent clinical study involving patients with metastatic bone disease, the levels of vascular endothelial growth factor, a crucial factor for blood vessel formation, were significantly reduced in patients receiving zoledronic acid. This suggests that zoledronic acid may have clinically relevant antiangiogenic properties. Early clinical data on the prevention of bone metastases using the older-generation bisphosphonate clodronate have shown promising results in patients with breast cancer. Currently, trials are underway to evaluate the effectiveness of clodronate in this context. Similarly, the newer-generation bisphosphonate zoledronic acid has demonstrated efficacy in preventing bone metastases in small pilot studies involving patients with high-risk solid tumors. Additionally, in a separate trial spanning five years, patients with multiple myeloma who received zoledronic acid as part of their standard treatment regimen had a higher overall survival rate compared to those who received standard treatment alone. These encouraging early clinical findings have prompted the initiation of larger randomized trials that are currently ongoing.

title: LIF/STAT3 controls ES cell self-renewal and pluripotency by a Myc-dependent mechanism.
text: The LIF/STAT3-dependent signaling pathway is responsible for maintaining murine ES cells as a pluripotent, self-renewing population. However, the specific downstream effectors of this pathway have not been previously identified. In this study, we have discovered that the Myc transcription factor is a key target of the LIF self-renewal pathway. We found that STAT3 directly regulates the expression of Myc in murine ES cells. These cells express high levels of Myc, but when LIF is withdrawn, Myc mRNA levels decrease and Myc protein is phosphorylated on threonine 58 (T58), leading to its degradation through GSK3beta. However, if stable Myc (T58A) expression is maintained, self-renewal and pluripotency can occur independently of LIF. On the other hand, a dominant negative form of Myc inhibits self-renewal and promotes differentiation. The transcriptional control by STAT3 and suppression of T58 phosphorylation are crucial for regulating Myc activity in ES cells and promoting self-renewal. Overall, our findings provide insight into how LIF and STAT3 regulate the self-renewal and pluripotency of ES cells.

title: Chronic renal failure accelerates atherogenesis in apolipoprotein E-deficient mice.
text: Patients with chronic renal failure (CRF) have a significantly higher risk of cardiovascular mortality, which is 10 to 20 times greater compared to individuals without CRF. These patients also have numerous risk factors for atherosclerosis. However, the exact cause of cardiovascular disease in CRF is still unknown. To investigate the impact of CRF on the development of atherosclerosis, researchers examined male mice deficient in apolipoprotein E. The mice were divided into three groups: those that underwent 5/6 nephrectomy to induce CRF, those that underwent unilateral nephrectomy, and those that did not undergo any surgery. After twenty-two weeks, the mice with CRF showed a significant increase in aortic plaque area, aortic cholesterol content, and aortic root plaque area compared to the mice that did not undergo surgery. The plaques in the uremic mice contained macrophages and exhibited strong staining for nitrotyrosine. Systolic blood pressure and plasma homocysteine concentrations were similar in both uremic and nonuremic mice. However, plasma urea and cholesterol concentrations were significantly higher in the CRF mice. These variables were positively correlated with aortic plaque area and with each other. Multiple linear regression analysis revealed that only plasma urea was a significant predictor of aortic plaque area. In conclusion, these findings suggest that uremia greatly accelerates the development of atherosclerosis in apolipoprotein E-deficient mice. This effect cannot be fully explained by changes in blood pressure, plasma homocysteine levels, or total plasma cholesterol concentrations. Therefore, the CRF apolipoprotein E-deficient mouse model can be used to study the pathogenesis of accelerated atherosclerosis in uremia.

title: Left ventricular function and exercise capacity.
text: The role of left ventricular function in predicting exercise capacity and its impact on age and sex differences is not well understood. The objective of this study was to determine the impact of measures of cardiac function assessed by echocardiography on exercise capacity and to investigate if these associations are influenced by sex or advancing age. The study was a cross-sectional analysis of patients who underwent exercise echocardiography with routine measurements of left ventricular systolic and diastolic function using 2-dimensional and Doppler techniques. The researchers analyzed the data to identify the strongest factors associated with exercise capacity and to examine the interactions between age, sex, and these variables. The study took place at a large tertiary referral center in Rochester, Minnesota in 2006, and included a total of 2867 patients who underwent exercise echocardiography using the Bruce protocol. Patients with evidence of exercise-induced ischemia, ejection fractions below 50%, or significant valvular heart disease were excluded from the study. The main outcome measure was exercise capacity measured in metabolic equivalents (METs). The results showed that diastolic dysfunction was strongly and inversely associated with exercise capacity. After adjusting for other factors, patients with moderate/severe resting diastolic dysfunction had a significantly lower exercise capacity (-1.30 METs), as did those with mild resting diastolic dysfunction (-0.70 METs). Variation in left ventricular systolic function within the normal range did not have a significant association with exercise capacity. However, higher left ventricular filling pressures, as measured by resting E/e' of 15 or greater or postexercise E/e' of 15 or greater, were both associated with a reduction in exercise capacity. Furthermore, individuals with impaired relaxation or resting E/e' of 15 or greater experienced a greater reduction in exercise capacity with advancing age. Other factors independently associated with exercise capacity were age, female sex, and a body mass index greater than 30. In conclusion, this study found that abnormalities in left ventricular diastolic function were independently associated with exercise capacity in a large group of patients referred for exercise echocardiography.

title: A dynamic population model to investigate effects of climate on geographic range and seasonality of the tick Ixodes scapularis.
text:
We developed a population model for Ixodes scapularis, the tick that transmits various tick-borne diseases in North America. The model aimed to simulate the impact of temperature on tick survival and activity patterns. We used temperature data from specific meteorological stations to calculate temperature-dependent time delays for tick development. The model also took into account the influence of temperature on the tick's ability to find hosts. By using data from stations near areas with endemic tick populations, the model was able to accurately replicate the seasonal activity patterns observed in the field. 

When we ran simulations using data from meteorological stations in central and eastern Canada, we found that the maximum number of ticks at equilibrium decreased as the station location moved further north. In fact, the simulated tick populations died out at the most northerly stations. This die-out was due to an increase in mortality across all life stages as temperature decreased, rather than a specific threshold event in the tick's life cycle. 

To assess the temperature conditions at the meteorological stations, we used linear regression to analyze the mean annual number of degree-days above 0 degrees Celsius (DD>0 degrees C). This index provided a useful measure of temperature conditions for the model. We found a strong association between the maximum number of ticks at equilibrium and the mean DD>0 degrees C. Additionally, when accounting for the province of origin of the meteorological station, we observed that Quebec had a higher number of ticks compared to Ontario. 

The regression models also provided theoretical limits for the establishment of I. scapularis in Canada. Maps based on these limits indicated that the range of southeast Canada, where temperature conditions are currently suitable for the tick, is wider than the actual distribution of I. scapularis. This suggests that there is potential for the tick to spread further. We also discussed the future applications of the model in studying the effects of climate change on I. scapularis.

title: Inflammatory cytokines in depression: neurobiological mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
text: There is growing evidence suggesting that inflammatory cytokines play a role in the development of depression, both in individuals with medical conditions and those who are medically healthy. Cytokines are crucial for brain development and normal brain function, and they have the ability to influence the neurocircuitry and neurotransmitter systems that affect behavior.
