Additionally, our study demonstrates that TMPyP4 induces anaphase bridges in sea urchin embryos, whereas telomestatin does not have this effect. This leads us to conclude that the selectivity of telomestatin for intramolecular G-quadruplex structures and TMPyP4 for intermolecular G-quadruplex structures plays a crucial role in mediating different biological effects. Stabilization of intramolecular G-quadruplex structures leads to telomerase inhibition and accelerated telomere shortening, while facilitation of intermolecular G-quadruplex structure formation induces the formation of anaphase bridges.

title: Targeting oxidative stress to treat endometriosis.
text:
INTRODUCTION
Endometriosis affects approximately 10% of women in their reproductive years. It is characterized by the presence of active endometrial tissue outside the uterus. The exact cause of endometriosis is still uncertain, although several theories have been proposed. Given its prevalence, there is a strong demand for new treatments for this condition. Recent studies have shed light on the pathological characteristics of endometriosis, revealing a vicious cycle in which oxidative stress (OS) plays a key role in the implantation of ectopic endometrium. This cycle is further exacerbated by the generation of reactive oxygen species. 

AREAS COVERED
This article explores the evidence linking OS and endometriosis. The author discusses various antioxidant agents that have been specifically investigated in endometriosis patients, including Vitamins C and E, melatonin, resveratrol, xanthohumol, and epigallocatechin-3-gallate. The review highlights the significant impact of these antioxidants on endometriosis.

EXPERT OPINION
Targeting the reduction of OS as a treatment strategy for endometriosis shows promise. However, since most of the studies conducted so far have been either in vitro or animal-based, further research involving human subjects is necessary to fully understand the effects of reducing OS in patients with endometriosis.

title: Interferon alpha for the treatment of chronic hepatitis C in patients infected with human immunodeficiency virus. Hepatitis-HIV Spanish Study Group.
text: Liver disease caused by hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection is becoming a major cause of illness and death in individuals who have contracted human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) through injection drug use, hemophilia, or blood transfusions. We conducted a study to assess the effectiveness of interferon (IFN) alpha therapy in these patients and identify factors that predict a positive response to this treatment. Our study included 119 patients with chronic hepatitis C, 90 of whom were also infected with HIV and 29 who were not. The patients received subcutaneous injections of IFN-alpha three times a week for three months, followed by a lower dose for an additional nine months for those who responded well. Of the 107 patients who completed the study, 26 (32.5%) of the HIV-infected patients and 10 (37.0%) of the non-HIV-infected patients achieved a complete response, with normal liver enzyme levels and no detectable HCV RNA in their blood after treatment. In HIV-infected patients, two factors were independently associated with a positive response: a CD4+ T lymphocyte count of over 500 x 10(6)/L and a baseline HCV viral load of less than 10(7) copies/mL. In the year following treatment, relapses occurred in 30.8% of the HIV-infected patients and 12.5% of the non-HIV-infected patients.

title: Vanishing cerebellar infarcts in a migraine patient.
text: Recent studies conducted on the general population have indicated that migraine may increase the risk of developing infarct-like lesions in the posterior circulation area. These lesions are believed to be genuine vascular infarcts due to their size, location, and characteristics observed through magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). However, since there have been no postmortem studies conducted to determine the underlying cause of these MRI findings, their true origin remains unknown. In this case, a patient with migraine is presented, who initially displayed what appeared to be cerebellar infarcts on MRI. However, these lesions disappeared upon repeat imaging after 16 days, raising doubts about their origin as vascular ischemic infarcts.

title: A novel viral transcript with homology to human interleukin-10 is expressed during latent human cytomegalovirus infection.
text: The latent phase of human cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection occurs in hematopoietic cells, specifically granulocyte-macrophage progenitors (GM-Ps). During this phase, the virus remains in a nonreplicating state, although some limited transcriptional activity has been observed. To further investigate viral gene expression during latency, we conducted a study using an experimental model. Primary human GM-Ps were latently infected with CMV strain Toledo, and RNA was extracted and subjected to reverse transcription-PCR using CMV gene-specific primers. Through this method, we identified transcription from the UL111.5A region of the viral genome. This transcription was also observed in GM-Ps latently infected with AD169 and Towne strains, indicating that expression was not dependent on the CMV strain. Importantly, we also detected UL111.5A-region transcripts in mononuclear cells from healthy bone marrow and mobilized peripheral blood allograft donors, demonstrating expression during natural latent infection. Mapping experiments using RNA from latently infected GM-Ps revealed the expression of a novel UL111.5A region transcript with a different splicing pattern compared to productive infection of permissive cells. This transcript is predicted to encode a 139-amino-acid protein that shares similarities with the potent immunosuppressor interleukin-10 (IL-10) and the viral IL-10 homolog expressed during productive CMV infection. The expression of this latency-associated cmvIL-10 may enable the virus to evade immune recognition and clearance during the latent phase of infection.

title: Treatments for somnambulism in adults: assessing the evidence.
text: Sleepwalking, also known as somnambulism, is a sleep disorder characterized by the performance of wakeful movements during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep. If sleepwalking causes distress or poses a danger despite safety precautions, medical or psychological intervention may be necessary. Healthcare professionals must evaluate the available evidence on treatment options. To gather relevant information, searches were conducted in MEDLINE, EMBASE, PsycINFO, and the Ovid Evidence-Based Medicine Reviews (EBM) multifile databases. Unfortunately, no adequately powered and rigorously controlled trials were found for the treatment of sleepwalking in adults. However, seven reports were identified, which included small trials with some form of control group or retrospective case series involving 30 or more patients. Due to the lack of high-quality evidence supporting specific treatments for somnambulism, it is recommended to engage in thorough discussions with patients. It is crucial to conduct well-designed clinical trials with sufficient sample sizes, potentially through multi-center collaborations, to address this research gap.

title: Premature chromosome condensation: evidence for in vivo cell fusion in human malignant tumours.
text: The study examined premature chromosome condensation (PCC) in tissue samples from patients with haematological diseases and various types of carcinomas. PCC was observed in 6 out of 166 malignancies (128 haematological cases, 35 carcinomas, and 3 malignant effusions) using the GTG-technique. Chromosome analysis revealed PCC in both S-phase and G1-phase in each case, with PCC occurring in 1, 4, and 8.6% of the metaphases analyzed. These findings suggest that PCC chromosomes, which indicate cell fusion in the body, are not uncommon in naturally occurring human malignancies and may impact the malignant phenotype. Additionally, along with other factors, they may contribute to the heterogeneity of tumor cell populations.

title: Blockade of the angiotensin system improves mental health domain of quality of life: A meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
text:
Objective: The objective of this study was to determine the impact of angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors and angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) blockers on the mental health domain of quality of life. 

Study Design: A meta-analysis of published literature was conducted using data from the PubMed and clinicaltrials.gov databases. The most recent search was conducted in January 2017. 

Study Selection: Randomized controlled trials that compared any angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor or AT1R blocker with placebo or non-angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor or non-AT1R blocker were selected. The study participants were adults without any major physical symptoms. The meta-analysis reporting methods as per PRISMA and the Cochrane Collaboration were followed. 

Data Synthesis: A total of eleven studies were included in the analysis. When compared with placebo or other antihypertensive medications, AT1R blockers and angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors were found to be associated with improved overall quality of life, positive wellbeing, mental health, and anxiety domains of quality of life. However, no significant difference was found for the depression domain. 

Conclusions: The use of angiotensin blockers and inhibitors for the treatment of hypertension in otherwise healthy adults is linked to improved mental health domains of quality of life. It is important to note that mental health quality of life was a secondary outcome in the included studies. Further research specifically designed to analyze the effectiveness of drugs that block the angiotensin system is necessary to properly evaluate this novel psychiatric target.

title: The role of epigenetics in aging and autoimmunity.
text: As individuals age, their immune system becomes less effective, leading to a higher occurrence of autoimmune diseases. This process, known as immunosenescence, is characterized by a decline in the functioning of T and B cells, as well as the presence of mild, long-term inflammation. Recent research suggests that epigenetics, the study of inherited changes in gene expression that are not determined by DNA sequence, also undergoes changes with age. Interestingly, epigenetics appears to play a significant role in various human diseases, including inflammatory and cancerous conditions. In this article, we will explore the potential mechanisms behind the increased autoimmune responses observed in older individuals. Specifically, we will examine how epigenetic modifications, such as DNA methylation and histone acetylation, accumulate during the aging process and contribute to the risk of developing autoimmune disorders.

title: A framework for understanding and targeting residual disease in oncogene-driven solid cancers
text: The potential of molecular targeted therapy to significantly enhance the survival rates of cancer patients is undeniable. However, it is important to acknowledge that achieving complete and long-lasting responses to targeted therapy is uncommon among individuals with advanced-stage solid cancers. Even the most effective targeted therapies typically fail to induce a complete eradication of tumors, leading to the persistence of residual disease and the progression of tumors, which ultimately limits patient survival. In light of this, we believe it is crucial to gain a deeper understanding of the molecular foundations of residual disease. This understanding will serve as a foundation for developing therapeutic strategies aimed at minimizing or eliminating residual disease, thereby enabling us to transition from temporary control of the disease to a more chronic control or even a cure for patients with advanced-stage solid cancers. Ultimately, we propose a shift in approach, moving away from the current reactive paradigm of analyzing and treating acquired drug resistance, and towards a pre-emptive paradigm that focuses on identifying the mechanisms responsible for residual disease. By targeting and limiting this reservoir of disease, we can significantly improve patient outcomes.

title: Long-term inhibition of dipeptidyl peptidase-4 in Alzheimer's prone mice.
text: In this study, we examined the effects of long-term inhibition of dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) using sitagliptin on the accumulation of amyloid-beta in the brain and memory-related behavioral deficits in a mouse model of Alzheimer's disease (AD). The mice used in the study were double transgenic mice B6*Cg-Tg(APPswe,PSEN1dE9)85Dbo/J. Sitagliptin treatment was initiated when the mice reached 7 months of age. Three different doses of sitagliptin (5, 10, and 20 mg/kg) were administered daily for a period of 12 weeks through gastric gavage. The sitagliptin treatments had several positive effects, including: (i) improvement in memory impairment as assessed by the contextual fear conditioning test; (ii) increased levels of GLP-1 in the brain; (iii) significant reduction in nitrosative stress and inflammation markers in the brain; and (iv) a significant decrease in the number and total area of betaAPP and Abeta deposits. These effects were most pronounced with the highest dose of sitagliptin (20 mg/kg). Overall, our findings suggest that long-term inhibition of endogenous DPP-4 enzymes with sitagliptin can effectively delay certain aspects of AD pathology, such as amyloid deposition, when administered early in the disease progression in a transgenic mouse model of AD.

title: Structural and mechanistic insights into phospholipid transfer by Ups1–Mdm35 in mitochondria
text: In order to achieve specific lipid compositions within membrane-bounded organelles, eukaryotic cells rely on lipid trafficking. Our focus was on the Ups1-Mdm35 system, which facilitates the transfer of phosphatidic acid (PA) between the outer and inner mitochondrial membranes. Through X-ray analysis, we determined the structures of Mdm35 and Ups1-Mdm35, both with and without PA. The Ups1-Mdm35 complex consists of a single domain with a deep pocket and a flexible Ω-loop lid. By analyzing the structure, we found that a basic residue at the bottom of the pocket and the Ω-loop lid play crucial roles in extracting PA from the membrane after Ups1 binding. The binding of Ups1 to the membrane is enhanced by the dissociation of Mdm35. Additionally, we discovered that basic residues around the entrance of the pocket are important for Ups1 binding to the membrane and PA extraction. These findings provide a structural foundation for understanding the mechanism of PA transfer between mitochondrial membranes.

title: Redox regulation of cell migration and adhesion.
text: The migration and adhesion of cells are influenced by reactive oxygen species (ROS), specifically hydrogen peroxide, and the proteins that regulate them. When cell surface receptors are stimulated by growth factors and chemoattractants, ROS are generated and transmit signals from the cell surface to important signaling proteins within the cell. ROS play a role in promoting migration within cells and also affect the behavior of migrating cells in nonmigrating cells. Additionally, hydrogen peroxide has been proposed to act as a chemoattractant itself, attracting immune cells to wounds. In this discussion, we explore recent advancements in understanding how organisms utilize ROS and the extent to which they rely on them in the processes of cell migration and adhesion.

title: Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome, Quick Sequential Organ Function Assessment, and Organ Dysfunction: Insights From a Prospective Database of ED Patients With Infection
text:
The proposed revision of sepsis definitions has eliminated the systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) and instead defined organ dysfunction as a rise in the Sequential Organ Function Assessment (SOFA) score of at least 2. They have also introduced the concept of "qSOFA" (quick SOFA) as a bedside indicator of organ dysfunction. The objectives of this study were to (1) assess the prognostic impact of SIRS, (2) compare the diagnostic accuracy of SIRS and qSOFA for organ dysfunction, and (3) compare the standard (Sepsis-2) and revised (Sepsis-3) definitions for organ dysfunction in emergency department (ED) patients with infection. 

Over a period of 3 years, we enrolled 8,871 ED patients who were admitted with suspected infection. We collected sufficient observational data to calculate SIRS, qSOFA, SOFA, comorbidity, and mortality. Of the enrolled patients, 4,176 (47.1%) had SIRS. We found that SIRS was associated with a higher risk of organ dysfunction (relative risk [RR] 3.5) and mortality in patients without organ dysfunction (odds ratio [OR] 3.2). Both SIRS and qSOFA had similar accuracy in predicting organ dysfunction (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve: 0.72 vs 0.73). However, qSOFA had high specificity but poor sensitivity for organ dysfunction (96.1% and 29.7%, respectively). The mortality rate for patients with organ dysfunction was similar between Sepsis-2 and Sepsis-3 (12.5% and 11.4%, respectively), although 29% of patients with Sepsis-3 organ dysfunction did not meet Sepsis-2 criteria. We also found that an increasing number of Sepsis-2 organ system dysfunctions were associated with higher mortality. 

In conclusion, SIRS was linked to organ dysfunction and mortality, suggesting that abandoning this concept may be premature. A qSOFA score of at least 2 had high specificity but limited sensitivity, which may restrict its usefulness as a bedside screening tool. Although mortality for organ dysfunction was comparable between Sepsis-2 and Sepsis-3, the Sepsis-2 criteria provided more prognostic and clinical information regarding the number and type of organ dysfunctions. The recalibration of the SOFA score may be necessary.

title: Requirement of NAD and SIR2 for life-span extension by calorie restriction in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
text: The life-span of various organisms can be prolonged through calorie restriction. While it has been proposed that this restriction may reduce the production of reactive oxygen species during respiration, the exact mechanism by which it slows down aging remains uncertain. In this study, we replicated calorie restriction in yeast using either physiological or genetic methods and observed a significant increase in life-span. However, this increase was not observed in yeast strains that were mutated for SIR2 (the gene responsible for producing the silencing protein Sir2p) or NPT1 (a gene involved in the synthesis of NAD, the oxidized form of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide). These findings suggest that the prolonged longevity resulting from calorie restriction relies on the activation of Sir2p through NAD.

title: Pathways disrupted in human ALS motor neurons identified through genetic correction of mutant SOD1.
text: Although there are numerous mutations in various genes that are known to cause Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), it is still not well understood how these mutations specifically affect motor neuron biology and whether they all lead to neuronal degeneration through common pathways. In this study, we have combined reprogramming and stem cell differentiation techniques with genome engineering and RNA sequencing to investigate the transcriptional and functional changes induced in human motor neurons by a mutant form of SOD1. The mutant SOD1 protein caused a transcriptional signature that indicated increased oxidative stress, impaired mitochondrial function, altered subcellular transport, and activation of the ER stress and unfolded protein response pathways. Functional experiments showed that these pathways were disrupted in a manner that depended on the specific SOD1 mutation. Additionally, we examined motor neurons derived from ALS patients with a repeat expansion in C9orf72 and found that at least some of these changes were also present in this subset of ALS cases.

title: Effect of enalapril on 12-year survival and life expectancy in patients with left ventricular systolic dysfunction: a follow-up study.
text:
In the SOLVD studies, it was found that enalapril reduced mortality in patients with symptomatic left ventricular systolic dysfunction but not in those with asymptomatic dysfunction. To determine if the mortality reduction with enalapril persisted among patients with heart failure and if there was a subsequent reduction in mortality among those with asymptomatic dysfunction, we conducted a 12-year follow-up of SOLVD. 

We tracked the vital status of 5165 individuals who were alive at the completion of the SOLVD prevention and treatment trials out of the 6797 patients initially enrolled. Follow-up was conducted through direct contacts in Belgium and by linking with national death registries and federal beneficiary or historic tax summary files in the USA and Canada. 

The follow-up was nearly complete, with a 99.8% (6784/6797) completion rate. In the prevention trial, 50.9% (1074/2111) of the enalapril group had died compared to 56.4% (1195/2117) of the placebo group (generalised Wilcoxon p=0.001). In the treatment trial, 79.8% (1025/1285) of the enalapril group had died compared to 80.8% (1038/1284) of the placebo group (generalised Wilcoxon p=0.01). The reductions in cardiac deaths were significant and similar in both trials. 

When the data from the prevention and treatment trials were combined, the hazard ratio for death was 0.90 for the enalapril group compared to the placebo group (95% CI 0.84-0.95, generalised Wilcoxon p=0.0003). Enalapril extended median survival by 9.4 months in the combined trials (95% CI 2.8-16.5, p=0.004). 

In conclusion, treatment with enalapril for 3-4 years resulted in a sustained improvement in survival beyond the original trial period for patients with left ventricular systolic dysfunction, leading to a significant increase in life expectancy.

title: TGFbeta/activin/nodal signaling is necessary for the maintenance of pluripotency in human embryonic stem cells.
text:
Little is currently known about the signaling pathways that control the pluripotent nature of human embryonic stem cells (hESCs), which have the ability to self-renew indefinitely and differentiate into various cell types. In this study, we focused on investigating the role of TGFbeta superfamily signaling in hESCs, as it is known to play a significant role in early embryonic development.

Our findings indicate that the TGFbeta/activin/nodal branch of signaling is active in undifferentiated hESCs, mediated by the signal transducer SMAD2/3. On the other hand, the BMP/GDF branch (SMAD1/5) is only active in mitotic cells that are isolated. As hESCs undergo early differentiation, SMAD2/3 signaling decreases, while SMAD1/5 signaling becomes activated.

To further understand the functional significance of TGFbeta/activin/nodal signaling in hESCs, we conducted experiments and discovered that it is necessary for maintaining the expression of markers associated with the undifferentiated state. Additionally, we found that SMAD2/3 activation is dependent on WNT signaling, which we have previously shown to be sufficient for maintaining the undifferentiated state of hESCs.

Interestingly, our study also revealed that SMAD2/3 signaling is crucial for maintaining the inner cell mass in ex vivo mouse blastocyst cultures, which is the source of stem cells. These findings highlight the importance of TGFbeta signaling in the early stages of determining cell fate and demonstrate a connection between TGFbeta and WNT signaling in these contexts.

title: The structure and expression of a novel gene activated in early mouse embryogenesis.
text: We have successfully cloned and determined the sequence of the mouse H19 gene. In mice, this gene is controlled by two trans-acting loci called raf and Rif. These loci regulate the levels of H19 mRNA and alpha-fetoprotein mRNA in adult mice. Our analysis of the H19 gene's sequence and structure reveals that it is not related to the alpha-fetoprotein gene. This suggests that the H19 gene acquired its regulation by raf and Rif independently. Additionally, we found that the H19 gene has a unique structure. It consists of five exons, with sizes of 1307, 135, 119, 127, and 560 bp, and four small introns totaling 270 bases. The largest open reading frame in the gene, which can encode a protein of approximately 14 kd, is located entirely within the first exon, 680 bases downstream of the mRNA's cap site. Before the translation initiation codon, there are four ATG codons, each followed by translation terminator codons. The remaining part of the gene, which includes all five exons, is likely untranslated. We propose that the long 5' untranslated region may play a role in regulating mRNA translation, based on our in vitro translation studies. Furthermore, our experiments using mesodermal lineage tissue culture cell lines suggest that the H19 gene is activated early during muscle cell differentiation.

title: Diminished linear growth during intermittent calcitriol therapy in children undergoing CCPD.
text: The use of daily calcitriol therapy has been shown to improve the growth of children with renal bone disease. 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D is an important regulator of chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation. While large intermittent doses of calcitriol can reduce levels of parathyroid hormone (PTH) and reverse skeletal changes caused by secondary hyperparathyroidism, the effect of intermittent calcitriol therapy on growth in children is not known. Therefore, we conducted a study on 16 pre-pubertal patients with secondary hyperparathyroidism confirmed by bone biopsy. These patients completed a 12-month clinical trial of intermittent calcitriol therapy. We compared the biochemical results and growth data obtained during intermittent therapy to those from the previous 12 months of daily therapy for each patient. After one year of intermittent calcitriol therapy, we also assessed changes in bone histology. Z-scores for height did not change during the 12 months of daily calcitriol therapy. However, during intermittent therapy, the Z-scores for height decreased from -1.8 +/- 0.32 to -2.0 +/- 0.33 (P < 0.01). Most patients showed improvement in the skeletal lesions caused by secondary hyperparathyroidism, but those who developed adynamic bone lesions after 12 months of treatment experienced the largest reductions in Z-scores for height. During intermittent calcitriol therapy, the change in Z-scores for height correlated with serum PTH levels (r = 0.71, P < 0.01) and alkaline phosphatase levels (r = 0.67, P < 0.01), but this correlation was not observed during daily therapy. These findings suggest that high-dose intermittent calcitriol therapy has a negative impact on linear growth, especially in patients with adynamic lesions. It is possible that the higher doses of calcitriol or the intermittent schedule of administration directly inhibit chondrocyte activity in the growth plate cartilage of children with end-stage renal disease.

title: Comparison of pain syndromes associated with nervous or somatic lesions and development of a new neuropathic pain diagnostic questionnaire (DN4)
text: There have been limited studies comparing the clinical features of neuropathic and non-neuropathic pains. To address this, the French Neuropathic Pain Group created a questionnaire called DN4, which includes sensory descriptors and signs related to bedside sensory examination. This questionnaire was used in a study of 160 patients with pain caused by a neurological or somatic lesion. The most common causes of neurological lesions were traumatic nerve injury, post herpetic neuralgia, and post stroke pain. Non-neurological lesions included osteoarthritis, inflammatory arthropathies, and mechanical low back pain. Each patient was evaluated by two experts to confirm the diagnosis of neuropathic or non-neuropathic pain. The prevalence of pain descriptors and sensory dysfunctions were compared between the two groups. The psychometric properties of the DN4 questionnaire were analyzed, including face validity, inter-rater reliability, factor analysis, and logistic regression. We discovered that a small number of items were enough to differentiate neuropathic pain. The 10-item questionnaire developed in this study is a new diagnostic tool that can be useful in both clinical research and daily practice.

title: Changing the density of alcohol outlets to reduce alcohol-related problems.
text: The issue of whether the number and concentration of alcohol establishments impact alcohol consumption and related harm has become a focal point in legal and political discussions surrounding the granting of new liquor licenses. However, the current state of evidence on this matter remains uncertain. In this edition of the Harm Reduction Digest, Livingston, Chikritzhs, and Room critically examine the existing research literature to explore the effects of alcohol sales outlet density on alcohol consumption and associated issues. They propose a fresh perspective on understanding these relationships and delve into the implications for mitigating alcohol-related harm.

title: [Pharmacokinetics and biotransformation of the antimycotic drug ciclopiroxolamine in animals and man after topical and systemic administration].
text:
1. After applying a 1% aqueous cream containing the carbon-14 labelled broad spectrum antimycotic 6-cyclohexyl-1-hydroxy-4-methyl-2(1H)-pyridone, 2-aminoethanol salt (ciclopiroxolamine, Hoe 296, Batrafen) to healthy human dorsal skin, it was found that approximately 1.3% of the applied dose was absorbed through the skin. The cream was left on for 5 hours with an occlusive dressing, and the penetration time was 6 hours. The highest concentrations of the antimycotic were found in the horny layer of the skin, ranging from 2300-4500 microgram/cm3. These concentrations remained consistent throughout the penetration period, indicating that the antimycotic was able to penetrate the skin effectively. Histoautoradiography studies showed that ciclopirox can penetrate the skin through the epidermis and hair follicles. In dogs, the percutaneous absorption was higher, ranging from 5-15% of the applied dose, compared to humans.

2. When bitches were treated with a vaginal application of ciclopirox-14C-olamine in the form of a 1% aqueous cream (1 mg/kg), between 42 and 97% of the dose was excreted in the urine and feces. The remaining amount of the compound was found in the tampon used to close the vagina.

3. Both dogs and humans excrete ciclopirox primarily in the urine as a glucuronide. In humans, another glucuronide with similar properties to the original substance was detected, along with two conjugated, relatively non-polar metabolites in small amounts. The metabolite patterns were similar after oral and dermal application. In humans, ciclopirox binds to serum proteins at a rate of 96 +/- 2% in a concentration range of 0.01-11.0 microgram/ml.

4. Placental transfer of ciclopirox was found to be low in rats. Although the mother animal showed good absorption of the compound, the radioactivity in the fetal tissues was always lower than that in the maternal blood.

title: Maximizing the diagnostic utility of endoscopic biopsy in dogs and cats with gastrointestinal disease.
text: This article examines the usefulness of flexible endoscopy in diagnosing gastrointestinal diseases in small animals. It discusses the importance of performing the techniques carefully to ensure meaningful results. The article also covers practical and technical considerations for endoscopic biopsy, the best instruments for collecting mucosal specimens, the correlation between endoscopic indices and clinical activity and histopathologic findings, and new advancements in the endoscopic diagnosis of GI disease. Recent studies have established guidelines for the number and quality of diagnostic specimens from different parts of the gut. These studies have also highlighted the significance of ileal biopsy in diagnosing chronic enteropathies in dogs and cats. Additionally, they have demonstrated the value of endoscopic biopsy specimens in immunohistochemical, microbiological, and molecular studies, going beyond routine histopathological analysis with hematoxylin and eosin staining.

title: Age-structured red blood cell susceptibility and the dynamics of malaria infections.
text: The interaction between malaria parasites and immune responses in an infected human takes place on a dynamic landscape. This landscape is shaped by a population of replicating parasites that depletes a population of replenishing red blood cells (RBCs). Although these underlying dynamics have received little attention, they provide valuable insights into the mechanisms that control most malaria infections. In this study, we specifically focus on the observation that three out of the four malaria parasite species that infect humans are limited to specific age groups of RBCs. We incorporate this observation into our models of infection dynamics to differentiate between common and species-specific pressures on host immune responses. Our findings reveal that age structuring has significant impacts on the progression of infection. In certain conditions, all four species of parasites can persist at low densities or be cleared even without an immune response. Even with the two species that only attack the youngest RBCs, catastrophic anemia can occur, despite only a small fraction of cells being parasitized at any given time. Additionally, in these two species, compensatory erythropoietic responses in the host accelerate the growth of the parasite population. These differences in outcomes are characterized by a "basic reproduction rate."

title: Helicobacter pylori AlpA and AlpB bind host laminin and influence gastric inflammation in gerbils.
text: Helicobacter pylori is a bacterium that colonizes humans and can cause various health issues such as gastritis, ulcers, and gastric cancer. It has been observed that when H. pylori adheres to the gastric epithelium, it enhances inflammation. However, only a few adhesins of H. pylori have been identified as binding to specific targets in the host tissue. One such adhesin is encoded by the alpAB locus, which is involved in adherence to human gastric tissue. Our study reveals that when the genes for AlpA and AlpB in H. pylori are deactivated, the binding of the bacterium to laminin is reduced. On the other hand, when alpA or alpB genes are introduced into Escherichia coli through plasmids, the bacteria gain the ability to bind to laminin. Interestingly, an H. pylori strain lacking only AlpB also shows a deficiency in laminin binding. Therefore, we conclude that both AlpA and AlpB contribute to the binding of H. pylori to laminin. Surprisingly, in gerbils, the H. pylori SS1 mutant lacking AlpA and AlpB causes more severe inflammation compared to the wild-type strain. This finding contradicts our expectations. The identification of laminin as the target for AlpA and AlpB will aid in further investigations of the interactions between the host and the pathogen during H. pylori infection.

title: A quantitative analysis of kinase inhibitor selectivity
text: Kinase inhibitors are a novel type of drugs that have the ability to inhibit multiple targets. However, the effects of this multi-kinase activity on biological systems are not well understood. To gain insight into the relationship between selectivity, efficacy, and safety, it is crucial to study how these inhibitors interact with the human kinome. In this study, we present interaction maps for 38 kinase inhibitors tested against a panel of 317 kinases, which represents more than 50% of the predicted human protein kinome. This dataset is the most comprehensive study of kinase inhibitor selectivity to date and reveals a wide range of interaction patterns. To facilitate a global analysis of the results, we introduce a selectivity score as a general tool to quantify and distinguish the observed interaction patterns. Additionally, we examine the impact of panel size and find that small assay panels are not reliable for measuring selectivity.

title: Ribosomal protein S9 is a novel B23/NPM-binding protein required for normal cell proliferation.
text: B23, also known as NPM or nucleophosmin, is a versatile protein found in the nucleolus. It belongs to the nucleoplasmin superfamily of acidic histone chaperones. B23 is crucial for normal embryonic development and plays a significant role in maintaining genomic stability, ribosome production, and preventing cell death. Changes in B23 protein expression or genetic mutations are observed in various types of cancer. Despite being described as multifunctional, the exact molecular function of B23 remains unclear. In this study, we demonstrate that B23 interacts with a protein complex consisting of ribosomal proteins and ribosome-associated RNA helicases. We also investigate a novel interaction between B23 and ribosomal protein S9 (RPS9) that does not involve RNA. Our findings reveal that the binding of S9 to B23 requires an intact B23 oligomerization domain. When S9 is depleted using small interfering RNA, protein synthesis decreases, and cells are arrested in the G(1) phase of the cell cycle. This arrest is accompanied by the activation of p53 target genes. We also discover that S9 is a short-lived protein in the absence of ribosome production, and inhibiting the proteasome increases its protein levels. Overexpressing B23 promotes the storage of S9 in the nucleolus, while reducing B23 levels leads to a decrease in nucleolar S9. Based on our results, we propose that B23 selectively stores and protects ribosomal protein S9 in the nucleolus, thereby facilitating ribosome production.

title: Vasculature-associated cells expressing nestin in developing bones encompass early cells in the osteoblast and endothelial lineage.
text: Nestin-positive (Nes(+)) cells play a crucial role in supporting hematopoiesis in adult bone marrow. However, the origin of these cells during the development of endochondral bone remains unknown. Research using mice that express GFP under the control of the nestin promoter/enhancer (Nes-GFP) has shown that there are distinct endothelial and nonendothelial Nes(+) cells in the embryonic perichondrium. The nonendothelial cells are early cells of the osteoblast lineage that descend from their progenitors upon the action of Indian hedgehog and the expression of Runx2. As vascular invasion occurs and ossification centers form, these Nes(+) cells become closely associated with each other and their numbers increase progressively. Interestingly, when tamoxifen-inducible cre recombinase driven by the nestin enhancer (Nes-creER) is used to target cells in developing bone marrow, predominantly endothelial cells are affected. Furthermore, Nes(+) cells in postnatal bones are a heterogeneous population that includes various cells in the osteoblast and endothelial lineages. These findings highlight the complexity of stromal populations and demonstrate that Nes(+) cells are associated with vasculature and are early cells in the osteoblast and endothelial lineages.

title: Public health, academic medicine, and the alcohol industry's corporate social responsibility activities.
text: In the context of public health theory on corporate social responsibility, we examined the evolving connections between the alcohol industry, academic medicine, and the public health community. Our analysis focused on the sponsorship of scientific research, attempts to shape public perception of research, dissemination of scientific information, and industry-funded policy efforts. As scientific evidence increasingly supports the need for regulatory and legal measures to reduce alcohol consumption, the academic community has found itself at odds with the alcohol industry. Our findings indicate that the alcohol industry has intensified its scientific and policy-related endeavors, often under the guise of corporate social responsibility initiatives, which primarily serve the industry's economic interests.

title: RET, ROS1 and ALK fusions in lung cancer
text:
We conducted a comprehensive screening of 1,529 lung cancers using a combined molecular and histopathology approach. Our aim was to identify fusions involving the anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) and c-ros oncogene 1, receptor tyrosine kinase (ROS1). Among the samples analyzed, we found 44 cases with ALK-fusion and 13 cases with ROS1-fusion in adenocarcinomas. Interestingly, we also discovered two previously unknown kinase fusions, KIF5B-RET and CCDC6-RET, in 14 adenocarcinomas. These findings suggest potential targets for molecular-targeted therapies. 

Furthermore, we performed a multivariate analysis on 1,116 adenocarcinomas, including the 71 cases with kinase fusions. This analysis revealed four independent factors associated with poor prognosis: age ≥50 years, male sex, advanced pathological stage, and absence of kinase fusions.

title: Genetic and biochemical interactions among Yar1, Ltv1 and Rps3 define novel links between environmental stress and ribosome biogenesis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
text: The coordination of ribosome assembly in the yeast S. cerevisiae is influenced by environmental conditions through the regulation of genes involved in ribosome biogenesis. In this study, we demonstrate that two nonessential stress-responsive genes, YAR1 and LTV1, are involved in the production of the 40S subunit. Through genetic and biochemical analysis, we establish that Yar1, a small ankyrin-repeat protein, physically interacts with RpS3, a component of the 40S subunit, as well as with Ltv1, a recently identified protein found in a 43S preribosomal particle. Our findings reveal that cells lacking YAR1 or LTV1 are more sensitive to specific protein synthesis inhibitors and display abnormal polysome profiles, characterized by a decrease in the number of 40S subunits and an excess of free 60S subunits. Interestingly, both mutants also exhibit heightened sensitivity to various environmental stress conditions. Overexpression of RPS3 alleviates the stress sensitivity and ribosome biogenesis defect in YAR1 mutants, but fails to rescue these defects in LTV1 mutants. Based on these observations, we propose that YAR1 and LTV1 have distinct, nonessential roles in 40S subunit production. The increased sensitivity to environmental stress in strains lacking these genes suggests a previously unknown connection between ribosome biogenesis factors and stress sensitivity.

title: Rational design of acridine-based ligands with selectivity for human telomeric quadruplexes.
text: Using structure-based modeling methods, a series of acridine compounds linked by disubstituted triazoles were designed to target human telomeric quadruplex DNAs. To validate the selectivity of these compounds, a focused library was created using click chemistry. The concept of selectivity was then tested against two promoter quadruplexes from the c-kit gene, which have known molecular structures, as well as duplex DNA using a FRET-based melting method. The lead compounds were found to have minimal impact on the thermal stability of the c-kit quadruplexes and duplex DNA structures. Further investigation through competition experiments confirmed that binding to duplex DNA was very low, even at high ratios of duplex to telomeric quadruplex. Selectivity towards the c-kit quadruplexes was more complex, with some evidence of their stabilization at higher concentrations compared to human telomeric quadruplex DNA. This selectivity is attributed to the dimensions of the triazole-acridine compounds, specifically the separation of the two alkyl-amino terminal groups. Additionally, both lead compounds exhibited selective inhibitory effects on the proliferation of cancer cell lines compared to normal cell lines. One of the compounds was also shown to inhibit the activity of the telomerase enzyme, which is selectively expressed in tumor cells and plays a crucial role in maintaining telomere integrity and cellular immortalization.

title: Hospital volume and the outcomes of mechanical ventilation.
text:
BACKGROUND: The impact of patient volume on survival rates in high-risk medical and surgical conditions has been well-documented. However, the relationship between hospital volume and outcomes for critically ill patients remains unclear.

METHODS: We conducted a study using data from the Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation clinical information system, analyzing information from 20,241 nonsurgical patients who received mechanical ventilation at 37 acute care hospitals between 2002 and 2003. Multivariate analyses were performed to account for differences in illness severity and case mix.

RESULTS: Our analysis revealed that higher hospital volume was associated with improved survival rates for patients receiving mechanical ventilation in both the intensive care unit (ICU) and the hospital as a whole. Patients admitted to hospitals in the highest quartile of volume (over 400 patients receiving mechanical ventilation per year) had a 37 percent lower adjusted odds of death in the ICU compared to those admitted to hospitals in the lowest quartile (150 or fewer patients receiving mechanical ventilation per year, p<0.001). In-hospital mortality rates were similarly reduced (adjusted odds ratio, 0.66; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.52 to 0.83; p<0.001). A patient in a low-volume hospital would have an adjusted in-hospital mortality rate of 34.2 percent, while a patient in a high-volume hospital would have a rate of 25.5 percent. Length of stay in the ICU or hospital did not show significant differences among survivors.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that mechanical ventilation in hospitals with higher case volumes is associated with lower mortality rates. Further research is needed to understand the underlying mechanisms behind this relationship for critically ill patients.

title: A meta-analysis of depression during pregnancy and the risk of preterm birth, low birth weight, and intrauterine growth restriction.
text: The aim of this study was to estimate the risk of preterm birth (PTB), low birth weight (LBW), and intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) associated with antenatal depression. The researchers conducted a search for relevant articles in various databases and included 29 studies that met their criteria. They calculated pooled relative risks (RRs) using random-effects methods and found that studies using a categorical depression measure showed significantly larger effect sizes for PTB, LBW, and IUGR compared to studies using a continuous depression measure. The risk of LBW associated with antenatal depression was higher in developing countries compared to the United States or European social democracies. Categorically defined antenatal depression tended to be associated with an increased risk of PTB among women of lower socioeconomic status in the United States. The researchers concluded that women with depression during pregnancy are at increased risk for PTB and LBW, and it is important to identify and treat antenatal depression through universal screening.

title: ES cell pluripotency and germ-layer formation require the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling component BAF250a.
text: ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling complexes are a group of epigenetic modifiers that use ATP hydrolysis to alter the structure of chromatin, thereby changing its accessibility to nuclear factors. BAF250a (ARID1a) is a unique subunit of the BAF chromatin remodeling complex that plays a crucial role in chromosome alterations during development. Our research demonstrates that removing BAF250a in early mouse embryos leads to developmental arrest at around embryonic day 6.5 and the absence of the mesodermal layer, indicating its importance in early germ-layer formation. Additionally, the deficiency of BAF250a compromises the pluripotency of ES cells, inhibits self-renewal, and promotes differentiation into primitive endoderm-like cells under normal feeder-free culture conditions. Interestingly, this phenotype can be partially rescued by the presence of embryonic fibroblast cells. Through DNA microarray, immunostaining, and RNA analyses, we have discovered that BAF250a-mediated chromatin remodeling is essential for the proper expression of numerous genes involved in ES cell self-renewal, such as Sox2, Utf1, and Oct4. Furthermore, the defects in pluripotency observed in BAF250a mutant ES cells seem to be specific to certain cell lineages. For instance, our experiments with embryoid bodies have shown that BAF250a-ablated stem cells struggle to differentiate into fully functional mesoderm-derived cardiomyocytes and adipocytes, but they can still differentiate into ectoderm-derived neurons. These findings suggest that BAF250a is a critical component of the gene regulatory machinery in ES cells, governing self-renewal, differentiation, and cell lineage choices.

title: Metabolic shutdown in Escherichia coli cells lacking the outer membrane channel TolC.
text: TolC, an outer membrane channel in Escherichia coli, plays a crucial role in multidrug efflux and type I secretion transporters. When TolC is mutated and deactivated, cells become highly vulnerable to antibiotics and experience difficulties in secreting protein toxins. Surprisingly, despite the impairment in various transport functions, cells lacking TolC do not exhibit any growth defects. However, our research has revealed that the absence of TolC significantly hampers cell division and growth in minimal glucose medium. This growth deficiency is further intensified when the ygiB and ygiC genes, which are expressed in the same operon as tolC, and their homologues yjfM and yjfC located elsewhere on the chromosome, are also lost. Our findings indicate that this growth deficiency is caused by a depletion of the critical metabolite NAD(+) and an imbalance in NADH/NAD(+) ratios. The increased levels of PspA and reduced rates of NADH oxidation in Delta tolC membranes suggest membrane stress and a dissipation of the proton motive force. In conclusion, the deactivation of TolC triggers a metabolic shutdown in E. coli cells grown in minimal glucose medium. However, this Delta tolC phenotype can be partially rescued by YgiBC and YjfMC, which have parallel functions independent of TolC.

title: Acyl and total ghrelin are suppressed strongly by ingested proteins, weakly by lipids, and biphasically by carbohydrates.
text:
CONTEXT: Ghrelin, a hormone that increases body weight, is known to increase before meals and decrease after eating. Understanding how different types of macronutrients affect ghrelin regulation could help in designing weight-reducing diets.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to investigate the effects of carbohydrates, proteins, and lipids on acyl and total ghrelin levels in humans. We hypothesized that lipids might be less effective in suppressing ghrelin levels compared to carbohydrates or proteins.

DESIGN: This study was a randomized, within-subjects cross-over study.

SETTING: The study took place at a University Clinical Research Center.

PARTICIPANTS: Sixteen healthy human subjects participated in the study.

INTERVENTIONS: Participants were provided with isocaloric, isovolemic beverages primarily composed of carbohydrates, proteins, or lipids.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The study measured the extent to which total and acyl ghrelin levels were suppressed after consuming the beverages, using a novel acyl-selective, two-site ELISA.

RESULTS: All beverages led to a suppression of plasma acyl and total ghrelin levels. There was a significant effect of macronutrient class on the extent of suppression, with protein having a greater effect than carbohydrates, and carbohydrates having a greater effect than lipids. Total ghrelin levels were significantly lower after consuming carbohydrate and protein beverages compared to lipid beverages. In the first 3 hours after consumption, the suppression of acyl and total ghrelin was greatest with carbohydrates, followed by protein, and then lipids. However, in the subsequent 3 hours, there was a significant rebound in acyl and total ghrelin levels after consuming carbohydrates alone.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide insights into the mechanisms behind the effects of high-protein/low-carbohydrate diets for weight loss and high-fat diets for weight gain.

title: Hydrogen sulfide increases nitric oxide production with calcium-dependent activation of endothelial nitric oxide synthase in endothelial cells.
text:
Recent research has revealed that hydrogen sulfide (H(2)S) is produced in mammalian tissues through various enzymes. Numerous studies have demonstrated that H(2)S has beneficial effects on the cardiovascular system, such as vasodilation and antihypertensive properties. However, the specific intracellular mechanisms of H(2)S-induced vasodilation and its interactions with other endothelium-derived relaxing factors, like nitric oxide (NO), are still not fully understood. In this study, we aimed to investigate whether H(2)S directly regulates the activity of endothelial NO synthase (eNOS) and the production of NO in endothelial cells.

To achieve this, we used NaHS, a donor of H(2)S, and observed that it dose-dependently increased the production of NO in cultured endothelial cells. Interestingly, this effect was abolished when we used a calcium chelator (BAPTA-AM), indicating the involvement of calcium signaling. However, the absence of extracellular calcium did not affect the NaHS-induced increase in NO production. We also found that the inhibitors of ryanodine receptor (dantrolene) or inositol 1,4,5-triphosphate receptor (xestospongin C) partially blocked the NaHS-induced increase in NO production, suggesting the involvement of these receptors in the process. Furthermore, NaHS significantly elevated intracellular calcium concentrations, and this effect was attenuated by dantrolene or xestospongin C. Additionally, NaHS induced the phosphorylation of eNOS at the activating phosphoserine residue 1179. Importantly, the NaHS-induced eNOS phosphorylation and NO production were not affected by a PI3K/Akt inhibitor (wortmannin).

Based on these findings, our study suggests that H(2)S directly acts on endothelial cells to activate eNOS and promote NO production by releasing calcium from the intracellular store in the endoplasmic reticulum. This mechanism may contribute to the vasodilator function of H(2)S.

title: Fear of falling and visual field loss from glaucoma.
text:
The objective of this study was to determine if glaucoma-related visual field (VF) loss is linked to an increased fear of falling. The study design was prospective and observational. The participants included 83 glaucoma subjects with bilateral VF loss and 60 control subjects with good visual acuity and no significant VF loss. The control subjects were recruited from patients who were being monitored for suspected glaucoma. The fear of falling was compared between the two groups using the University of Illinois at Chicago Fear of Falling Questionnaire. The extent of fear of falling was assessed using Rasch analysis, with lower scores indicating a greater fear of falling and less ability to perform tasks without fear. 

The results showed that the glaucoma subjects had more severe VF loss compared to the control subjects. However, there were no significant differences between the two groups in terms of age, race, gender, employment status, presence of other adults in the home, body mass index (BMI), grip strength, cognitive ability, mood, or comorbid illness. In multivariate models, the glaucoma subjects reported a greater fear of falling compared to the controls. The fear of falling also increased with the severity of VF loss. Other factors that predicted a greater fear of falling included female gender, higher BMI, living with another adult, and greater comorbid illness. 

In conclusion, bilateral VF loss resulting from glaucoma is associated with a higher fear of falling, which has a greater impact than numerous other risk factors. Screening for and developing interventions to minimize fear of falling in patients with VF loss could lead to significant improvements in their quality of life, considering the physical and psychological consequences associated with this fear.

title: Repeat instability: mechanisms of dynamic mutations
text: Disease-causing repeat instability is a significant and distinct type of mutation that is associated with over 40 neurological, neurodegenerative, and neuromuscular disorders. Mutations in DNA repeats expand and persist in tissues and across generations. The patterns of instability, which can be inherited or specific to certain tissues, are influenced by both gene-specific elements within the DNA and proteins involved in DNA metabolism. The process of repeat instability likely involves the formation of abnormal DNA structures during DNA replication, repair, and recombination. Recent experimental advancements have enhanced our understanding of the mechanisms behind repeat instability, revealing unexpected ways in which metabolic pathways can either promote or safeguard against this type of mutation.

title: Demographic Risk Factors for Alcohol-Related Aggression In and Around Licensed Venues.
text: There have been few studies that have explored the impact of gender and both area-level and individual socio-economic status (SES) as independent predictors of alcohol-related aggression (ARA) in and around licensed venues. The purpose of this study was to examine the relationship between gender, area-level SES, individual SES (measured by occupational category), and ARA in and around licensed venues. The study included 697 men and 649 women aged 16-47 who participated in a survey as part of a larger study on alcohol-related problems in the night-time economy. The results of binary logistic regression analyses showed that age, gender, occupational category, area-level SES, and level of intoxication at the time of the survey were all significant predictors of involvement in ARA. Being male doubled the likelihood of being involved in ARA, while age was found to be a protective factor. Blue collar workers had more than double the odds of being involved in ARA compared to professionals, and individuals living in socio-economically disadvantaged areas were over twice as likely to report experiencing ARA compared to those in advantaged areas. However, when examining the predictive model by gender, the effects of age, occupational category, and area-level SES were only significant for male participants, with greater intoxication no longer being predictive. In conclusion, ARA was more likely to occur among male patrons, those in blue collar occupations, and individuals living in low SES areas, suggesting that both individual and area-level disadvantage may contribute to ARA.

title: Schizophrenia susceptibility pathway neuregulin 1–ErbB4 suppresses Src upregulation of NMDA receptors
text: The hypothesis suggests that cognitive dysfunction in individuals with schizophrenia may be caused by a decrease in the activity of a specific type of glutamate receptor called N-methyl D-aspartate receptor (NMDAR). This decrease in NMDAR activity is believed to be a result of excessive signaling from the schizophrenia-linked genes NRG1 and ERBB4. However, our findings indicate that the signaling between neuregulin 1β–ErbB4 (NRG1β-ErbB4) does not lead to a general decrease in NMDAR activity. Instead, we discovered that NRG1β-ErbB4 signaling actually suppresses the enhancement of synaptic NMDAR currents by a protein called Src, specifically in the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex. This signaling also prevents the strengthening of connections between neurons in the hippocampus and inhibits the Src-dependent enhancement of NMDAR responses during a specific type of stimulation. Additionally, NRG1β-ErbB4 signaling prevents the phosphorylation of a specific subunit of the NMDAR called GluN2B, which is normally induced by the stimulation. Based on these findings, we propose that NRG1-ErbB4 signaling contributes to cognitive dysfunction in schizophrenia by abnormally suppressing the Src-mediated enhancement of synaptic NMDAR function.

title: Intestinal bacteria and the regulation of immune cell homeostasis.
text: The human gut is inhabited by approximately 100 trillion bacteria. While some of these bacteria play a crucial role in maintaining normal bodily functions, others have been linked to the development of various inflammatory diseases such as IBD and asthma. This article explores how signals from intestinal bacteria impact the balance of the immune system in both healthy and diseased individuals. It delves into the composition of gut bacteria in mammals, the immunoregulatory molecules they produce, and the innate immune receptors in mammals that recognize these molecules. The article also discusses how bacterial signals affect the function of immune cells and the mechanisms through which they influence the progression of inflammatory diseases. Finally, it examines the current achievements and future obstacles in utilizing bacterial communities or their byproducts for the prevention and treatment of human ailments.

title: Sympathetic activation during early pregnancy in humans.
text:
Increased sympathetic activity has been observed in normotensive pregnant women, and it is even more pronounced in women with gestational hypertension and preeclampsia at term. However, it is unclear whether sympathetic overactivity develops early in pregnancy and remains high throughout gestation, or if it only occurs at term and contributes to hypertensive disorders. To investigate this, we conducted a study to test the hypothesis that sympathetic activation occurs early in pregnancy in humans.

We recruited eleven healthy women (average age 29 ± 3 years) with no history of hypertensive pregnancies. We measured muscle sympathetic nerve activity (MSNA) and hemodynamics while the participants were in a supine position, at a 30-degree tilt, and at a 60-degree tilt for 5 minutes each. We also collected blood samples to measure catecholamines, direct renin, and aldosterone levels. The participants were tested during the mid-luteal phase (PRE) and early pregnancy (EARLY; 6.2 ± 1.2 weeks of gestation).

Our results showed that MSNA was significantly higher during EARLY compared to PRE (supine: 25 ± 8 vs. 14 ± 8 bursts min(-1), 60 deg tilt: 49 ± 14 vs. 40 ± 10 bursts min(-1); main effect, P < 0.05). Resting diastolic pressure showed a trend towards being lower (P = 0.09), heart rate was similar, total peripheral resistance decreased (2172 ± 364 vs. 2543 ± 352 dyne s cm(-5); P < 0.05), and sympathetic vascular transduction was blunted (0.10 ± 0.05 vs. 0.36 ± 0.47 units a.u.(-1) min(-1); P < 0.01). Additionally, both renin (supine: 27.9 ± 6.2 vs. 14.2 ± 8.7 pg ml(-1), P < 0.01) and aldosterone (supine: 16.7 ± 14.1 vs. 7.7 ± 6.8 ng ml(-1), P = 0.05) levels were higher during EARLY compared to PRE.

These findings suggest that sympathetic activation is a common characteristic of early pregnancy in humans, despite lower diastolic pressure and total peripheral resistance. These results challenge conventional understanding of blood pressure regulation during pregnancy, as they demonstrate significant sympathetic activation within the first few weeks of conception. This early sympathetic activation may contribute to cardiovascular complications associated with pregnancy.

title: Psychological adaptation in children with idiopathic short stature treated with growth hormone or placebo.
text:
The impact of being short in height on the psychological well-being of children and adolescents is a topic of debate. Currently, growth hormone (GH) is used to treat children with idiopathic short stature (ISS), also known as non-GH-deficient short stature. This study is the first of its kind to investigate the effects of GH on the psychological adaptation of children and adolescents with ISS. The participants were treated with GH until they reached their adult height. 

The study included sixty-eight children (53 males, 15 females) between the ages of 9 and 16, who had significant ISS (height measurement or predicted adult height of -2.5 standard deviations or less). They were randomly assigned to receive either GH (0.074 mg/kg) or a placebo subcutaneously three times a week until their height velocity decreased to less than 1.5 cm per year. The parents completed the Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL), while the children completed the Self-Perception Profile (SPP) and Silhouette Apperception Technique at the beginning of the study and annually thereafter. 

The baseline scores for behavioral and emotional adjustment (CBCL) and self-concept (SPP) of children with ISS were found to be within the normal range. During the first two years of the study, both groups showed similar behavioral and self-concept profiles (CBCL). However, in the third and fourth years, the GH-treated group showed a decrease in behavior problems (internalizing, externalizing, and total problems) compared to the placebo-treated group. There were no significant differences between the two groups in terms of competency domains (CBCL) and the SPP throughout the study. 

This long-term, placebo-controlled study found no evidence that short stature among children with ISS is associated with psychological adaptation or self-concept issues, as measured by the psychological instruments used. However, GH treatment showed a trend towards improving problem behaviors, as reported by the parents through questionnaires (CBCL). It is still unclear whether GH treatment has a significant impact on adaptation, psychosocial functioning, or quality of life in children with ISS.

title: Distinct and essential roles of transcription factors IRF-3 and IRF-7 in response to viruses for IFN-alpha/beta gene induction.
text: The induction of the interferon (IFN)-alpha/beta gene transcription in cells infected with viruses is a crucial event in innate immunity. Mice that lack the transcription factor IRF-3 are more susceptible to virus infections. In embryonic fibroblasts, the levels of virus-induced IFN-alpha/beta gene expression are decreased, and the types of IFN-alpha mRNA are changed. Additionally, cells that also have a defect in IRF-7 expression completely fail to activate these genes in response to infections by any of the tested virus types. However, when both IRF-3 and IRF-7 are coexpressed, a normal pattern of IFN-alpha/beta mRNA induction can be achieved in these cells. These findings highlight the crucial and distinct roles of these two factors in ensuring the efficiency and diversity of IFN-alpha/beta gene transcription for the antiviral response.

title: Interleukin-2- and interferon-gamma-secreting T cells in normal and diseased human intestinal mucosa.
text: We utilized a sensitive reverse haemolytic plaque assay and Northern blot analysis to investigate the production of interferon-gamma (IFN-gamma) and interleukin-2 (IL-2) in the mucosa of children with Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis (UC), as well as in histologically normal mucosa from patients without inflammatory bowel disease. Our findings showed that IL-2- and IFN-gamma-secreting cells were either absent or present at low levels in the mucosa of most UC patients and control individuals. However, in patients with Crohn's disease, we observed readily detectable lymphokine-secreting cells (3-18%). Furthermore, Northern blot analysis revealed the presence of IFN-gamma mRNA in 5 out of 6 Crohn's tissues, but only in 1 out of 5 UC samples and none of the nine control mucosa samples. These results indicate an ongoing cell-mediated immune response in the mucosa of individuals with Crohn's disease.

title: Metabolic reprogramming of stromal fibroblasts through p62-mTORC1 signaling promotes inflammation and tumorigenesis.
text: The role of the tumor microenvironment in cancer progression is crucial, but we have limited understanding of how stromal cells affect the epithelium. In this study, we discovered that p62 levels were decreased in the stroma of various tumors. Additionally, when p62 was lost in the tumor microenvironment or stromal fibroblasts, it led to enhanced tumorigenesis of epithelial prostate cancer cells. This effect was mediated by the regulation of cellular redox through the mTORC1/c-Myc pathway of stromal glucose and amino acid metabolism. Consequently, there was an increase in stromal IL-6 production, which is necessary for promoting tumor growth in the epithelial compartment. Therefore, p62 acts as an anti-inflammatory tumor suppressor by modulating metabolism in the tumor stroma.

title: Drosophila RNAi screen reveals CD36 family member required for mycobacterial infection.
text: Certain pathogens, like Mycobacterium tuberculosis, are able to survive within the hostile environment inside a macrophage. In order to identify the factors in the host that are necessary for the entry and survival of mycobacteria within macrophages, we conducted a comprehensive RNA interference screen in Drosophila macrophage-like cells using Mycobacterium fortuitum. Through this screen, we discovered factors that are essential for general phagocytosis, as well as those specifically required for mycobacterial infection. One particular factor, known as Peste (Pes), is a member of the CD36 family and is necessary for the uptake of mycobacteria, but not for Escherichia coli or Staphylococcus aureus. Additionally, scavenger receptors (SRs) belonging to the mammalian class B have been found to facilitate the uptake of bacteria into nonphagocytic cells. Among these receptors, SR-BI and SR-BII are uniquely responsible for the uptake of M. fortuitum, indicating a conserved role for class B SRs in pattern recognition and innate immunity.

title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practice on second primary cancer screening among cancer survivors: a qualitative study.
text:
The aim of this study was to investigate the understanding, attitude, and behavior towards second cancer screening among individuals who have previously had cancer. To achieve this, thirteen cancer survivors who were free of disease in the stomach, colorectal, breast, and thyroid were interviewed in three focus groups. Recurring themes were identified and categorized accordingly. 

The results revealed that none of the participants were familiar with the term "SPC" and were unable to distinguish it from "recurrence" or "metastasis." The survivors believed that they had been cured and were unaware of their increased risk of developing a second cancer. While they had a good understanding of cancer screening, they struggled to differentiate it from routine surveillance tests following cancer treatment. The participants expressed a desire to have undergone screening for SPC if they had been aware of it, and they considered physicians to be the most reliable source of information regarding screening. 

In conclusion, the study found that cancer survivors had limited knowledge about SPC, and the lack of information was the primary barrier to SPC screening. The findings suggest that an educational intervention would be beneficial in helping cancer survivors understand their risk of developing a second cancer and the importance of screening after their initial cancer diagnosis.

title: LncRNA HANR Promotes Tumorigenesis and Increase of Chemoresistance in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
text:
Background/Aims: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the fifth most prevalent cancer globally and the third leading cause of cancer-related death. Recent studies have highlighted the significant role of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in various cancers, including HCC. However, the impact and mechanism of lncRNAs in HCC tumorigenesis and resistance to chemotherapy remain poorly understood. 

Methods: In this study, we identified a lncRNA called HANR (HCC associated long non-coding RNA) that is expressed in HCC. HANR was identified through microarray analysis and its up-regulated expression was confirmed using quantitative PCR. We conducted RNA pull-down and pathway analyses to assess the physical and functional interactions involving HANR. In vivo experiments were performed to evaluate tumorigenesis and chemoresistance. Additionally, we detected HANR expression in HCC specimens using FISH. We also constructed xenograft and orthotopic mice models to observe the effects of HANR on tumorigenesis and chemoresistance in vivo. 

Results: HANR was found to be up-regulated in HCC patients and HCC cell lines. Increased HANR expression in HCC was associated with shorter patient survival. Knocking down HANR significantly inhibited cell proliferation, suppressed HCC tumor growth in xenograft/orthotopic models, induced apoptosis, and increased sensitivity to doxorubicin. Conversely, overexpression of HANR had the opposite effects. We discovered that HANR binds to GSKIP, thereby regulating the phosphorylation of GSK3β in HCC. 

Conclusion: Our findings demonstrate that HANR plays a role in HCC development and represents a promising therapeutic target for enhancing the sensitivity of HCC cells to doxorubicin. This discovery may have significant implications for future therapeutic interventions.

title: Dissection of signaling cascades through gp130 in vivo: reciprocal roles for STAT3- and SHP2-mediated signals in immune responses.
text: We created a series of knockin mouse lines by replacing the mouse gp130 gene with mutant human gp130 cDNAs. This disrupted the cytokine receptor gp130-dependent STAT3 and/or SHP2 signals. The mice lacking the SHP2 signal (gp130F759/F759) were born without any abnormalities but developed splenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, and an enhanced acute phase reaction. On the other hand, the mice lacking the STAT3 signal (gp130FXQ/FXXQ) died shortly after birth, similar to the gp130-deficient mice (gp130D/D). The gp130F759/F759 mice exhibited prolonged activation of STAT3 induced by gp130, suggesting that SHP2 plays a negative regulatory role. In these mice, there was an increase in Th1-type cytokine production, as well as IgG2a and IgG2b production. Conversely, the gp130FXXQ/FXXQ immune system showed a decrease in these immune responses. These findings demonstrate that the balance between positive and negative signals mediated by gp130 is crucial in regulating immune responses.

title: Viral interleukin-10 expressed by human cytomegalovirus during the latent phase of infection modulates latently infected myeloid cell differentiation.
text:
We investigated the impact of the human cytomegalovirus UL111A gene on the differentiation of latently infected myeloid progenitors. This gene codes for interleukin-10 (IL-10) homologs and is expressed during both latent and productive infections. Our study focused on determining whether viral IL-10 expressed during latency affects the differentiation process. 

Comparing latent infection with a virus lacking the gene encoding viral IL-10 to infection with the parental virus or a mock infection, we observed an upregulation of cytokines associated with dendritic cell (DC) formation. Additionally, the proportion of myeloid DCs increased in the latent infection with the IL-10-deleted virus. 

These findings indicate that viral IL-10 hinders the differentiation of latently infected myeloid progenitors into DCs. Moreover, they highlight the immunomodulatory role of viral IL-10, which may impede the host's ability to eliminate latent virus.

title: Bortezomib enhances dendritic cell (DC)-mediated induction of immunity to human myeloma via exposure of cell surface heat shock protein 90 on dying tumor cells: therapeutic implications.
text: Most chemotherapy drugs used to treat cancer suppress the immune system and cause tumor cells to die in a way that does not trigger an immune response. However, bortezomib, a drug that inhibits a specific protein complex called the 26S proteasome, has shown effectiveness in treating various human tumors, including myeloma. In this study, we demonstrate that when myeloma cells are killed by bortezomib, they can be taken up by dendritic cells (DCs), a type of immune cell. This uptake leads to the activation of an immune response against the tumor cells, even without the use of additional immune-stimulating substances. The transfer of signals from the dying tumor cells to the DCs relies on direct contact between the two cell types and is facilitated by the exposure of a protein called heat shock protein 90 (hsp90) on the surface of the dying cells, which is induced by bortezomib. Interestingly, when bortezomib is combined with geldanamycin, an inhibitor of hsp90, it causes more tumor cell death but eliminates their ability to trigger an immune response. These findings highlight the importance of drug-induced exposure of heat shock proteins on the surface of dying tumor cells as a mechanism for making human tumors more susceptible to immune attack. By specifically targeting bortezomib to tumors, we may be able to enhance their immunogenicity and promote the activation of an effective antitumor immune response.

title: Survivin depletion preferentially reduces the survival of activated K-Ras-transformed cells.
text: In order to find specific targets for cancer treatment, we conducted a study using a small interfering RNA (siRNA) library that targeted around 4,000 individual genes. Our focus was on enhancing the killing of cells in the DLD-1 colon carcinoma cell line, which carries an activated form of the K-Ras oncogene. Through this study, we discovered that siRNAs targeting the baculoviral inhibitor of apoptosis repeat-containing 5 (survivin) significantly reduced the survival of cells transformed by activated K-Ras, compared to their normal counterparts where the mutant K-Ras gene had been disrupted (DKS-8). Furthermore, the use of survivin siRNA led to a temporary arrest in the G(2)-M phase of the cell cycle and the development of polyploidy, accompanied by increased activation of caspase-3 in the activated K-Ras cells. These findings suggest that tumors expressing the activated K-Ras oncogene may exhibit heightened sensitivity to inhibitors targeting the survivin protein.

title: Small molecules enable cardiac reprogramming of mouse fibroblasts with a single factor, Oct4.
text: Recently, it was demonstrated that mouse fibroblasts can be transformed into cardiac cells through the forced expression of multiple transcription factors and microRNAs. However, in order to apply this reprogramming strategy for cell-based therapy or cardiac regeneration in vivo, it would be highly desirable to reduce or eliminate the need for genetic manipulations by using small molecules. In this study, we have identified a specific combination of small molecules that can efficiently convert mouse fibroblasts into cardiac cells using only one transcription factor, Oct4, without inducing pluripotency. These small-molecule-induced cardiomyocytes exhibit spontaneous contraction and display characteristics of ventricular cells. Additionally, these induced cardiomyocytes go through a cardiac progenitor stage. This research serves as a foundation for future pharmacological reprogramming methods and provides a small-molecule condition for investigating the mechanisms involved in the cardiac reprogramming process.

title: A switch from white to brown fat increases energy expenditure in cancer-associated cachexia.
