text: Cancer-associated cachexia (CAC) is a condition characterized by weight loss, inflammation, and the wasting of white adipose tissue (WAT) and skeletal muscle. Currently, there are limited treatment options available and the underlying mechanisms are not well understood. However, our research reveals that in the early stages of CAC, there is a transition from WAT to brown fat, known as WAT browning, before skeletal muscle atrophy occurs. This transition is accompanied by an increase in the expression of uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1), which redirects mitochondrial respiration towards thermogenesis rather than ATP synthesis. As a result, there is an increase in lipid mobilization and energy expenditure in cachectic mice. We have also found that chronic inflammation and the cytokine interleukin-6 contribute to the upregulation of UCP1 in WAT. Furthermore, treatments that reduce inflammation or block β-adrenergic receptors can inhibit WAT browning and alleviate the severity of cachexia. Importantly, we have observed UCP1 staining in WAT samples from CAC patients. Therefore, targeting WAT browning shows promise as a potential approach to improve cachexia in cancer patients.

title: Potential Mechanisms of Action of Lithium in Bipolar Disorder
text: Lithium has been used for more than 50 years as a treatment for bipolar disorder, known for its ability to stabilize mood. Despite its long history of use, the specific ways in which lithium works to stabilize mood are not well understood. This paper aims to summarize the current knowledge on lithium's effects, ranging from its impact on mood, cognition, and brain structure, to its effects on neurotransmission and molecular pathways. A thorough search of databases was conducted, and the findings were reviewed and synthesized. Many studies have shown that lithium is effective in treating acute mania and maintaining mood stability over the long term, but its efficacy in treating depression is less clear. However, lithium does possess unique properties that make it effective in preventing suicide. In terms of cognition, research suggests that lithium may help reduce cognitive decline in patients, but more investigation is needed using various methods. Interestingly, lithium appears to have a neuroprotective effect, preserving or even increasing the volume of brain structures involved in emotional regulation. At the neuronal level, lithium reduces excitatory neurotransmission (dopamine and glutamate) while increasing inhibitory neurotransmission (GABA). However, these effects are part of a complex system that strives to maintain balance. At the intracellular and molecular level, lithium targets second-messenger systems that further modulate neurotransmission. For example, it affects pathways such as adenyl cyclase and phospho-inositide, as well as protein kinase C, to reduce excessive excitatory neurotransmission. In addition to these mechanisms, it is believed that lithium's neuroprotective effects play a crucial role in its therapeutic actions. It reduces oxidative stress associated with manic and depressive episodes, increases protective proteins, and inhibits processes that lead to cell death. Overall, the therapeutic actions of lithium are complex and likely interconnected.

title: The role of autophagy in cancer development and response to therapy
text: Autophagy is a cellular process characterized by dynamic changes in subcellular membranes, resulting in the breakdown of cellular proteins and cytoplasmic organelles. This mechanism plays a crucial role in responding to stress or starvation. Numerous studies have contributed to our understanding of autophagy's significance in cancer. However, it remains uncertain whether autophagy inhibits tumor formation or serves as a rescue mechanism for cancer cells during unfavorable conditions. Consequently, the current state of knowledge regarding autophagy's role in cancer development and response to therapy is unclear. Additionally, exploring how the autophagic process can be manipulated to enhance anticancer treatments is essential.

title: The quest to overcome resistance to EGFR-targeted therapies in cancer
text: Patients with metastatic lung, colorectal, pancreatic, or head and neck cancers who initially respond well to epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-targeted therapies eventually develop resistance. The increasing understanding of the various resistance mechanisms highlights the immense difficulty in eliminating tumors that are resistant to EGFR inhibitors. However, our expanding knowledge of these resistance pathways presents an opportunity to develop new inhibitors and combination therapies that are specifically designed to prevent or overcome therapeutic resistance in tumors. In this comprehensive review, we explore the resistance pathways to EGFR-targeted therapies in lung, colorectal, and head and neck cancers, and discuss therapeutic strategies that aim to bypass resistance.

title: An organ culture model for the study of metanephric development.
text: We developed a culture system using mouse embryos to study the developmental aspects of nephrogenesis in mammals. At 13.5 +/- 0.4 days gestation, we removed the metanephros and ureteric bud from CFI albino mouse embryos. These tissues were then grown in Dulbecco's modified Eagle's Minimal Essential Medium supplemented with 20% donor bovine serum at 37C in a mixed air--5% CO2 environment. Our experimental conditions allowed for the development of organotypic tubular and glomerular epithelial structures in the metanephric explants. By 72 hours of culture, a well-developed proximal tubule with microvilli, intracellular organelles, and intercellular junctions had formed. By 120 hours of culture, devascularized glomeruli consisting of parietal and visceral epithelial layers had developed. The glomerular visceral epithelial cells formed foot processes and slit pore diaphragms, and produced islands of basement membrane. Throughout the organ culture development, there were no endothelial or mesangial elements present, indicating that advanced nephrogenesis can occur without vascularization. This whole organ culture model system allows us to study renal structural development in a controlled environment, separate from the influences of perfusion and urine formation. It provides an opportunity to investigate normal and abnormal mammalian renal development under highly controlled experimental conditions.

title: Molecular layers underlying cytoskeletal remodelling during cortical development
text: During the process of neural development, the cytoskeleton of newly formed neurons undergoes significant and dynamic changes to support the sequential stages of neurogenesis, cell migration, and terminal differentiation. Through studying the mechanisms that trigger these functions, it becomes evident that different arrangements of the cytoskeleton play a crucial role in ensuring the successful completion of each step. Additionally, these arrangements determine groups of proteins that are essential for controlling neuronal migration but not terminal differentiation. The coordination of these protein functions is also influenced by regulated gene expression and the precise localization of their protein products within specific subcellular regions. In this article, we delve deeper into this perspective by examining recent data on how the cytoskeleton is regulated during the maturation of cortical neurons in the developing brain.

title: Strong bias in the bacterial CRISPR elements that confer immunity to phage.
text: The CRISPR-Cas systems, known as Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats, offer adaptive immunity against phages by using CRISPR RNAs that are encoded with spacers complementary to invasive nucleic acids. In this study, we conducted an experiment where we exposed Streptococcus thermophilus to a bacteriophage and used PCR-based metagenomics to track the phage-derived spacers over a period of 15 days in two separate trials. We found that spacers targeting the host chromosome were rare and strongly discouraged, indicating that autoimmunity is lethal. In experiments where we recovered over half a million spacers, we observed that a few specific spacer sub-populations dominated early on and there were rapid fluctuations in their abundances. This pattern was consistent across two CRISPR systems and in replicate experiments, with a small number of spacers accounting for the majority of sequences. Additionally, we discovered that almost all phage locations targeted by the acquired spacers had a specific motif called a proto-spacer adjacent motif (PAM), suggesting that PAMs play a role in spacer acquisition. Furthermore, we identified a significant and consistent bias in the locations within the phage genome from which the spacers were derived. This bias may indicate a selection process based on the location and effectiveness of the spacers.

title: Chronic hypoxia induces modification of the N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor in rat brain.
text: This study investigated the effects of intermittent hypobaric hypoxia on the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor in the cerebral cortex, hippocampus, and corpus striatum of 3-week-old rats. The binding of [3H]MK-801 to the NMDA receptor was examined in membranes prepared from these brain regions and compared to normoxic controls. The results revealed a significant reduction in binding sites (Bmax) in the cortex, hippocampus, and striatum of hypoxic animals, with decreases of 36%, 35%, and 31% respectively. Additionally, there was a decrease in the dissociation constant (Kd), indicating increased affinity, of 29%, 32%, and 17% in these brain regions. In the cerebral cortex, the binding of 3[H]MK-801 was enhanced by glutamate and glycine, with a two to three-fold increase. However, the coagonist glutamate had a higher EC50 in the hypoxic cortical membranes compared to controls, while no significant differences were observed in the EC50 of glycine. These findings suggest that the NMDA receptor is altered in multiple brain regions of rats exposed to a hypoxic environment during development.

title: Cannabinoids in Clinical Practice
text: The potential clinical use of cannabis is often overshadowed by unreliable and purely anecdotal reports. The main psychoactive cannabinoid found in cannabis is tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), but there are also other cannabinoids such as cannabidiol (CBD) and cannabigerol (CBG). Not all of the observed effects can be attributed to THC alone, as the other constituents may also influence its actions. For example, CBD can reduce anxiety caused by THC. To maximize the benefits in practice, standardized extracts of the herb are being considered, and clinical trials have been designed to evaluate their effectiveness. Although the mechanism of action is not fully understood, cannabinoid receptors have been identified and natural ligands have been discovered. Patients with multiple sclerosis (MS) often use cannabis to alleviate muscle spasms and pain, and studies on an experimental model of MS have shown that low doses of cannabinoids can relieve tremors. Most controlled studies have focused on THC rather than the whole cannabis herb, so they may not accurately reflect the typical clinical situation. However, small clinical studies have confirmed the analgesic properties of THC, and CBD and CBG have also shown analgesic and anti-inflammatory effects. This suggests that there is potential for developing drugs that do not have the psychoactive properties of THC. Patients who take the synthetic derivative nabilone for neurogenic pain have reported that they prefer cannabis herb because it not only relieves pain but also alleviates associated depression and anxiety. Cannabinoids have been found to be effective in treating chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting, and nabilone has been approved for this use for several years. Currently, the synthetic cannabinoid HU211 is being tested as a protective agent for brain trauma. There have been anecdotal reports of cannabis being used to treat conditions such as migraine, Tourette's syndrome, asthma, and glaucoma. Apart from the risks associated with smoking, cannabis has a relatively good safety profile. However, adverse reactions such as panic or anxiety attacks are more common in the elderly and women, and less likely in children. While cannabis use has been linked to psychosis, a study of psychiatric hospital admissions did not find evidence of this, although it may worsen existing symptoms. The slow elimination of cannabinoids from the body has safety implications for cognitive tasks, particularly driving and operating machinery. Although cannabis-related impairment while driving is moderate, there is a significant interaction with alcohol. Natural cannabis materials can vary greatly, so standardization of multiple components is necessary to ensure consistent effects. Pure natural and synthetic compounds do not have these variations, but they may not have the same overall therapeutic effect as the whole herb.

title: Large deformation of red blood cell ghosts in a simple shear flow.
text: Red blood cells have the ability to change their shape in response to the flow conditions in their surroundings. This deformability affects both the physiological function of the red blood cells and the way blood flows through the body. To study these interactions between the cell membrane and the fluid, researchers use the immersed boundary method, which allows them to simulate the three-dimensional flow of the membrane and the fluid. In these simulations, the cells are assumed to have the same internal and external fluid viscosities. The validity of this method has been confirmed for small deformations of a spherical capsule in shear flow, using both the neo-Hookean and the Evans-Skalak membrane models. The simulations also include initially oblate spheroidal capsules, and it is observed that the red blood cell membrane behaves asymptotically as the ratio of the dilation modulus to the extensional modulus increases. Additionally, a good approximation of local area conservation is achieved. The simulations also reveal the occurrence of tank treading behavior, and the period of this behavior is calculated.

title: Preoperative C-reactive protein predicts long-term mortality and hospital length of stay after primary, nonemergent coronary artery bypass grafting.
text:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies have shown that preoperative C-reactive protein (CRP) levels above 10 mg/l are linked to higher morbidity and mortality rates after cardiac surgery. In this study, we aimed to assess the predictive value of preoperative CRP levels below 10 mg/l for long-term, all-cause mortality and hospital length of stay in patients undergoing primary, nonemergent coronary artery bypass graft-only surgery.

METHODS: We analyzed data from 914 patients who were prospectively enrolled for primary, nonemergent coronary artery bypass graft-only surgery. Preoperative CRP levels were categorized into four groups: < 1, 1-3, 3-10, and > 10 mg/l. We used a proportional hazards regression model to examine the association between these CRP categories and 7-year all-cause mortality and hospital length of stay.

RESULTS: During a mean follow-up period of 4.8 +/- 1.5 years, 87 patients (9.5%) died. After adjusting for proportional hazards, the 3-10 mg/l and > 10 mg/l preoperative CRP groups were associated with increased long-term mortality (hazard ratios [95% CI]: 2.50 [1.22-5.16], P = 0.01 and 2.66 [1.21-5.80], P = 0.02, respectively) and extended hospital length of stay (1.32 [1.07-1.63], P < 0.001 and 1.27 [1.02-1.62], P = 0.001, respectively).

CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that even preoperative CRP levels as low as 3 mg/l are linked to higher long-term mortality and extended hospital length of stay in patients undergoing primary, nonemergent coronary artery bypass graft-only surgery with relatively lower acuity. These findings have important implications for risk stratification of patients undergoing uncomplicated surgical coronary revascularization.

title: Transcript assembly and quantification by RNA-Seq reveals unannotated transcripts and isoform switching during cell differentiation.
text: Cufflinks, an open-source software program, introduces algorithms that can overcome the limitations of prior gene annotations and account for alternative transcription and splicing. By using Cufflinks, we were able to analyze over 430 million paired 75-bp RNA-Seq reads from a mouse myoblast cell line undergoing differentiation. Our analysis revealed 13,692 known transcripts and 3,724 previously unannotated ones. Of these, 62% were supported by independent expression data or homologous genes in other species. Throughout the differentiation process, we observed complete switches in the dominant transcription start site (TSS) or splice isoform for 330 genes, while 1,304 other genes showed more subtle shifts. These findings demonstrate the regulatory flexibility and complexity in muscle development and highlight how Cufflinks can enhance transcriptome-based genome annotation.

title: Sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease in the United Kingdom: analysis of epidemiological surveillance data for 1970-96.
text:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to examine the potential relationship between the occurrence of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease and the epidemic of bovine spongiform encephalopathy.

DESIGN: This study involved epidemiological surveillance of the United Kingdom population for Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease. Suspected cases were referred by neurologists, neuropathologists, and neurophysiologists, and death certificates were also considered.

SETTING: The study was conducted in England and Wales from 1970 to 1984, and in the entire United Kingdom from 1985 to 1996.

SUBJECTS: A total of 662 patients identified as sporadic cases of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease were included in the study.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The main outcome measures included the age distribution of patients, age-specific time trends of the disease, occupational exposure to cattle, and potential exposure to the causative agent of bovine spongiform encephalopathy.

RESULTS: The number of sporadic cases of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease recorded annually in England and Wales increased from 1970 to 1996. The greatest increase was observed among individuals aged over 70. There was a statistically significant excess of cases among dairy farm workers and their spouses, as well as among individuals at an increased risk of contact with live cattle infected with bovine spongiform encephalopathy. From 1994 to 1996, there were six deaths from sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease in the United Kingdom in patients under the age of 30.

CONCLUSIONS: The increase in the incidence of sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease and its high occurrence among dairy farmers in the United Kingdom may not be related to bovine spongiform encephalopathy. The most notable change in the pattern of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease after the epidemic of bovine spongiform encephalopathy was the incidence in a group of unusually young patients with a consistent and unusual neuropathological profile. The results of mouse transmission studies and the future incidence of the disease in the United Kingdom and other countries will be crucial in determining whether the agent causing bovine spongiform encephalopathy has infected humans.

title: Documented head injury in early adulthood and risk of Alzheimer's disease and other dementias.
text:
BACKGROUND: The relationship between previous head injuries and Alzheimer's disease (AD) is not consistent.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the connection between head injuries in early adulthood, as recorded in military hospital records, and the development of dementia later in life. Additionally, the study aimed to assess how head injuries and the APOE epsilon4 gene interact as risk factors for dementia.

METHODS: The study utilized a population-based prospective historical cohort design. It included male veterans from the Navy and Marine Corps who served in World War II and were hospitalized during their military service for either a nonpenetrating head injury or an unrelated condition. In 1996 to 1997, military medical records were examined to gather information on the occurrence and specifics of closed head injuries. The entire sample was then evaluated for dementia and AD using a multistage procedure. The study included 548 veterans with head injuries and 1228 without head injuries who completed all stages of the study. The authors used proportional hazards models to estimate the risk of dementia, specifically AD.

RESULTS: The study found that both moderate head injuries (hazard ratio [HR] = 2.32; CI = 1.04 to 5.17) and severe head injuries (HR = 4.51; CI = 1.77 to 11.47) were associated with an increased risk of AD. Similar results were observed for dementia in general. The findings for mild head injuries were inconclusive. When the authors analyzed the data based on the number of APOE epsilon4 alleles, they noticed a trend towards a stronger association between AD and head injuries in men with more epsilon4 alleles, although this trend was not statistically significant.

CONCLUSIONS: This study suggests that moderate and severe head injuries in young men may be linked to a higher risk of developing AD and other forms of dementia later in life. However, the authors acknowledge that there may be other unmeasured factors that could influence this association.

title: Transient receptor potential channels as drug targets: from the science of basic research to the art of medicine.
text: The Trp gene family is responsible for encoding transient receptor potential (TRP) proteins, which create unique ion channels that selectively allow cations to pass through. In mammals, there have been 28 identified Trp channel genes. TRP proteins have a wide range of permeation and gating properties and play a crucial role in numerous physiological functions that greatly impact cellular sensing and signaling pathways. Mutations in human genes that encode TRP channels, known as "TRP channelopathies," are responsible for various hereditary diseases that affect the musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, genitourinary, and nervous systems. This review provides an overview of the functional characteristics of mammalian TRP channels, discusses their involvement in acquired and hereditary diseases, and explores their potential as targets for therapeutic intervention.

title: Identification of genes associated with the astrocyte-specific gene Gfap during astrocyte differentiation.
text: The arrangement of chromosomes and genes within the nucleus of mammalian cells is not random. Gene clustering plays a crucial role in regulating transcription. However, the importance of gene clustering and their expression in the transformation of neural precursor cells (NPCs) into astrocytes is not well understood. To address this, we conducted a comprehensive analysis using enhanced circular chromosomal conformation capture (e4C) to identify genes associated with the astrocyte-specific gene glial fibrillary acidic protein (Gfap) during astrocyte differentiation. We discovered 18 genes that were specifically linked to Gfap and expressed in astrocytes derived from NPCs. These findings provide further support for the functional significance of gene clustering in regulating transcription during NPC differentiation.

title: Ketamine reduces LPS-induced HMGB1 via activation of the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway and NF-κB suppression.
text:
In this study, we aimed to investigate the potential anti-inflammatory effect of ketamine, an anesthetic agent. Specifically, we focused on its ability to inhibit the release of high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1), a cytokine associated with sepsis, in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated macrophages. We also examined the role of heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1) induction in mediating this effect.

To conduct the study, macrophages were first preincubated with different concentrations of ketamine and then exposed to LPS. We collected the cell culture supernatants to measure the levels of various inflammatory mediators, including HMGB1, nitric oxide, tumor necrosis factor-α, and interleukin 1β, using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Additionally, we analyzed the expression of HO-1 protein, the phosphorylation and degradation of IκB-α, and the nuclear translocation of nuclear factor E2-related factor 2 and nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) p65 through Western blot analysis. To further understand the role of HO-1 in this process, we used tin protoporphyrin (SnPP), an HO-1 inhibitor.

Our results showed that ketamine treatment dose-dependently reduced the levels of proinflammatory mediators (HMGB1, nitric oxide, tumor necrosis factor α, and interleukin 1β) and increased the expression of HO-1 protein in LPS-activated macrophages. Furthermore, ketamine inhibited the phosphorylation and degradation of IκB-α, as well as the LPS-induced nuclear translocation of NF-κB p65 in macrophages. We also observed that ketamine induced HO-1 expression through the nuclear translocation of nuclear factor E2-related factor 2 in macrophages. Importantly, the inhibitory effects of ketamine on LPS-induced proinflammatory cytokine production were partially reversed by the HO inhibitor tin protoporphyrin (SnPP).

In conclusion, our study demonstrates that ketamine can inhibit the release of HMGB1 in LPS-stimulated macrophages. This effect is at least partly mediated by the activation of the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway and suppression of NF-κB.

title: Association Between Early Screening for Patent Ductus Arteriosus and In-Hospital Mortality Among Extremely Preterm Infants.
text:
The importance of screening and treating patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) in extremely preterm infants is currently a topic of debate. There is a lack of consensus on the best approach, with some observing a decrease in pharmacological closure and an increase in supportive management without sufficient evidence to support these changes. 

The objective of this study was to assess the association between early screening echocardiography for PDA and in-hospital mortality. The study was conducted as part of the EPIPAGE 2 national prospective population-based cohort study, which included all preterm infants born at less than 29 weeks of gestation and hospitalized in 68 neonatal intensive care units in France from April to December 2011. Two main analyses were performed to account for potential selection bias: propensity score matching and the use of neonatal unit preference for early screening echocardiography as an instrumental variable. 

The infants were divided into two groups: those who underwent early screening echocardiography before day 3 of life and those who did not. The primary outcome measured was death between day 3 and discharge, while the secondary outcomes included major neonatal morbidities such as pulmonary hemorrhage, severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia, severe cerebral lesions, and necrotizing enterocolitis. 

Out of the 1513 preterm infants included in the study, 847 were screened for PDA and 666 were not. After matching, 605 infants from each group were paired. The exposed infants who underwent screening were more likely to receive treatment for PDA during their hospitalization compared to the non-exposed infants (55.1% vs 43.1%). However, the exposed infants had a lower rate of hospital death (14.2% vs 18.5%) and pulmonary hemorrhage (5.6% vs 8.9%) compared to the non-exposed infants. There were no significant differences in rates of necrotizing enterocolitis, severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia, or severe cerebral lesions between the two groups. 

The instrumental variable analysis yielded an adjusted odds ratio for in-hospital mortality of 0.62, suggesting a potential benefit of early screening echocardiography. However, the results of this analysis are not definitive, and further evaluation is needed to provide a clearer understanding of the long-term effects. 

In conclusion, this study found that early screening echocardiography for PDA in extremely preterm infants was associated with lower in-hospital mortality and a reduced likelihood of pulmonary hemorrhage. However, there were no significant differences in other major neonatal morbidities. The results of the instrumental variable analysis are not conclusive, and more research is required to fully understand the implications of early screening echocardiography for PDA in this population.

title: Role of birthweight in the etiology of breast cancer.
text: Breast cancer may have its origins during fetal development. We have examined the available evidence regarding the connection between birthweight and the risk of breast cancer. So far, 26 research papers have been published on this topic. The majority of these studies have found a positive correlation between birthweight and the risk of premenopausal breast cancer, but not postmenopausal breast cancer. When considering all studies that included both pre- and postmenopausal breast cancer, the relative risk estimate for women with high birthweight compared to those with low birthweight was 1.23 (with a 95% confidence interval of 1.13-1.34). The reasons behind this association are likely related to increased levels of growth factors, which may lead to a higher number of vulnerable stem cells in the mammary gland or initiate tumors through DNA mutations. Loss of imprinting (LOI) of growth hormone genes, such as insulin-like growth factor 2 (IGF2), which are important for fetal growth, can result in abnormally high hormone levels, as seen in high birthweight babies. LOI of IGF2 has also been observed in mammary tumor tissue. The impact of environmental factors that trigger this epigenetic regulation of gene expression is still not fully understood.

title: An activator of the cAMP/PKA/CREB pathway promotes osteogenesis from human mesenchymal stem cells.
text: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) possess the ability to differentiate into various cell types, including osteoblasts, adipocytes, and chondrocytes. Controlling the differentiation of MSCs could have significant implications in regenerative medicine and cell-based therapies. In the pursuit of developing a novel drug for osteoporosis treatment, the identification of a small molecule that triggers the osteogenic differentiation of MSCs would be highly beneficial. Our research has led us to discover CW008, a pyrazole-pyridine derivative, which effectively stimulates the differentiation of human MSCs into osteoblasts and enhances bone formation in mice that have undergone ovariectomy. The mechanism behind CW008's osteogenic properties involves the activation of the cAMP/PKA/CREB signaling pathway and the inhibition of leptin secretion. These findings indicate that CW008 acts as an agonist for the cAMP/PKA/CREB pathway during osteogenic differentiation, making it a promising candidate for the treatment of bone-related diseases and for further exploration in the field of bone biology.

title: Magnesium sulphate for women at risk of preterm birth for neuroprotection of the fetus.
text:
BACKGROUND: There is evidence from epidemiological and basic science studies suggesting that administering magnesium sulphate before birth may have neuroprotective effects on the fetus.

OBJECTIVES: The objective of this study was to evaluate the effects of magnesium sulphate as a neuroprotective agent in women at risk of preterm birth.

SEARCH STRATEGY: We conducted a search in the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group's Trials Register as of August 31, 2008.

SELECTION CRITERIA: We included randomized controlled trials that examined the use of antenatal magnesium sulphate therapy in women who were likely to give birth before 37 weeks of gestational age. Studies were categorized based on their primary intent, including "neuroprotective intent," "maternal neuroprotective - pre-eclampsia," or "tocolytic."

DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS: Two authors assessed trial eligibility and quality, and extracted data.

MAIN RESULTS: A total of five trials involving 6145 babies were included in this review. Antenatal magnesium sulphate therapy significantly reduced the risk of cerebral palsy in children born to women at risk of preterm birth (Relative Risk (RR) 0.68; 95% Confidence interval (CI) 0.54 to 0.87; five trials; 6145 infants). There was also a significant reduction in the rate of substantial gross motor dysfunction (RR 0.61; 95% CI 0.44 to 0.85; four trials; 5980 infants). However, there was no significant effect on paediatric mortality (RR 1.04; 95% CI 0.92 to 1.17; five trials; 6145 infants) or other neurological impairments or disabilities in early childhood. Overall, there were no significant effects on combined rates of mortality with cerebral palsy, although there were significant reductions in the neuroprotective groups (RR 0.85; 95% CI 0.74 to 0.98; four trials; 4446 infants), but not in the other intent subgroups. Minor maternal side effects were more common in the magnesium groups, but there were no significant effects on major maternal complications.

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Antenatal magnesium sulphate therapy has been established as a neuroprotective treatment for preterm fetuses in women at risk of preterm birth. The number needed to treat to prevent one case of cerebral palsy is 63 (95% confidence interval 43 to 87). Further evaluation of outcomes in later childhood is needed to determine any potential long-term neurological effects, particularly on motor or cognitive function, given the beneficial effects on gross motor function in early childhood.

title: The growing landscape of lysine acetylation links metabolism and cell signalling
text: Lysine acetylation is a well-preserved modification of proteins after translation, connecting acetyl-coenzyme A metabolism and cellular signaling. Recent advancements in mass spectrometry have improved our comprehension of lysine acetylation, revealing its involvement in numerous biological processes by regulating protein interactions, activity, and localization. Additionally, proteins often undergo other types of acylations, such as formylation, butyrylation, propionylation, succinylation, malonylation, myristoylation, glutarylation, and crotonylation. The intricate relationship between lysine acylation and cellular metabolism has been elucidated through the discovery of several metabolite-sensitive acylations and their targeted removal by sirtuin deacylases. These emerging discoveries shed light on new roles for various lysine acylations and deacylating enzymes, while also highlighting the mechanisms through which acetylation governs diverse cellular processes.

title: COMPASS, a histone H3 (Lysine 4) methyltransferase required for telomeric silencing of gene expression.
text: The maintenance of a particular gene expression pattern in certain organisms relies on the trithorax (Trx) family of proteins. Our recent study focused on the identification and analysis of COMPASS, a complex consisting of multiple proteins including Set1, a Trx-related protein found in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Our findings reveal that COMPASS is capable of methylating the fourth lysine of histone H3 in laboratory conditions. Furthermore, we have discovered that Set1 and other components of COMPASS are essential for histone H3 methylation in living organisms, as well as for the transcriptional silencing of a gene located near a chromosome telomere.

title: Free water elimination diffusion tractography: A comparison with conventional and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery, diffusion tensor imaging acquisitions.
text: The aim of this study was to assess the effectiveness of free water elimination (FWE) diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) methods in reducing the adverse effects of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) partial volume effects (PVEs) on white matter tractography reconstructions. Ten healthy individuals underwent "traditional," FLAIR (fluid-attenuated inversion recovery), and FWE DTI scans. Deterministic tractography was used to reconstruct the fornix, corpus callosum, and cingulum bundles. The FWE DTI scan was performed twice to match the total acquisition time (long FWE) and number of measurements (encoding directions, short FWE) of the FLAIR and "traditional" DTI scans. The resolution of PVE was determined based on the volume of the reconstructed tracts. Blinded review was conducted to assess anatomical correctness, symmetry, and completeness of the reconstructions. The results showed that the FWE and FLAIR scans produced more complete and anatomically plausible reconstructions of the fornix compared to "traditional" DTI. Furthermore, the tract reconstructions using FWE-DTI were significantly larger than those using FLAIR with DTI. Both FLAIR and FWE methods led to reductions in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), with FLAIR showing a greater reduction compared to FWE. There was no significant difference between the long and short FWE acquisitions for any of the reconstructed tracts. In conclusion, the FWE diffusion model effectively overcomes CSF PVE without the drawbacks of time, SNR, and volumetric coverage associated with FLAIR DTI.

title: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials of acupuncture in the treatment of depression.
text: Acupuncture has gained popularity as a complementary and alternative treatment for depression. This review aimed to analyze randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that investigated the effects of acupuncture on depression. The researchers located RCTs on depression treatment with acupuncture using various databases. They assessed the methodology of the RCTs using the Jadad criteria and quantified elements of research design for systematic comparisons. Out of the nine RCTs examined, five were considered to be of low quality based on the Jadad criteria. The odds ratios derived from comparing acupuncture with control conditions within the RCTs provided some evidence for the effectiveness of acupuncture in treating depression. Overall, acupuncture modalities appeared to be as effective as antidepressants in the limited studies available for comparison. However, placebo acupuncture treatment often showed no significant difference from the intended verum acupuncture. The RCTs had limitations such as small sample sizes, imprecise enrollment criteria, issues with randomization and blinding, short study duration, and lack of long-term follow-up. In conclusion, although the odds ratios from existing literature suggest a potential role for acupuncture in depression treatment, the evidence is inconclusive. Nonetheless, efforts are underway to standardize complementary approaches for depression treatment, and further systematic research is needed.

title: Genome-Wide Gene-Sodium Interaction Analyses on Blood Pressure: The Genetic Epidemiology Network of Salt-Sensitivity Study.
text:
We conducted a study to investigate the genetic loci that interact with sodium to affect blood pressure (BP) in a Chinese population. We used various tests, including single-marker-based tests and gene-based tests, on data from 1876 participants in the Genetic Epidemiology Network of Salt-Sensitivity (GenSalt) study. Sodium excretion was estimated using the average of 3 urine samples, and BP was measured using a random zero sphygmomanometer. We imputed 2.05 million single-nucleotide polymorphisms using Affymetrix 6.0 genotype data and the Chinese Han of Beijing and Japanese of Tokyo HapMap reference panel. Promising findings from the GenSalt study were then replicated in 775 participants from the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA). The results from both studies were combined to determine genome-wide significance. 

The single-marker-based tests identified an interaction between the UST rs13211840 variant and diastolic BP. The 2 df tests additionally found associations between the CLGN rs2567241 variant, the LOC105369882 rs11104632 variant, and systolic BP. The CLGN rs2567241 variant was also associated with diastolic BP and mean arterial pressure. 

In the gene-based analysis, we identified several genes, including MKNK1, C2orf80, EPHA6, SCOC-AS1, SCOC, CLGN, MGAT4D, ARHGAP42, CASP4, and LINC01478, that were associated with at least one BP phenotype. 

Overall, we discovered 8 new and 1 previously reported BP loci through the examination of interactions between single-nucleotide polymorphisms, genes, and sodium.

title: Percentile curves for hemoglobin and red cell volume in infancy and childhood.
text: We calculated percentile curves for hemoglobin and mean corpuscular volume in children aged 0.5 to 16 years. These curves were based on data from non-indigent white children living near sea level. Children with laboratory evidence of iron deficiency, thalassemia minor, and/or hemoglobinopathy were excluded from the reference population. The final reference populations consisted of 9,946 children for the hemoglobin curves and 2,314 for the MCV curves. These percentile curves are especially useful for diagnosing and screening iron deficiency and thalassemia minor.

title: Preservation of pancreatic beta-cell function and prevention of type 2 diabetes by pharmacological treatment of insulin resistance in high-risk hispanic women.
text: We conducted a study to investigate whether improving insulin resistance could help preserve pancreatic beta-cell function and delay or prevent the onset of type 2 diabetes in high-risk Hispanic women. We randomly assigned women with previous gestational diabetes to either a placebo group or a group receiving the insulin-sensitizing drug troglitazone (400 mg/day) in a double-blind manner. Fasting plasma glucose levels were measured every 3 months, and oral glucose tolerance tests (OGTTs) were performed annually to detect diabetes. Intravenous glucose tolerance tests (IVGTTs) were conducted at the beginning of the study and 3 months later to identify early metabolic changes associated with potential protection from diabetes. Women who did not develop diabetes during the trial returned for follow-up OGTTs and IVGTTs 8 months after stopping the study medications. Over a median follow-up period of 30 months on blinded medication, the average annual incidence rates of diabetes were 12.1% in the placebo group and 5.4% in the troglitazone group among the 236 women who returned for at least one follow-up visit (P < 0.01). The protective effect of troglitazone was closely linked to the reduction in endogenous insulin requirements observed 3 months after randomization, persisted even after stopping the study medications for 8 months, and was associated with the preservation of beta-cell compensation for insulin resistance. Treatment with troglitazone effectively delayed or prevented the onset of type 2 diabetes in high-risk Hispanic women. This protective effect was attributed to the preservation of pancreatic beta-cell function and appeared to be mediated by a reduction in the secretory demands placed on beta-cells due to chronic insulin resistance.

title: Androgen regulation of micro-RNAs in prostate cancer.
text:
BACKGROUND: Androgens play a crucial role in the growth of both androgen-dependent and castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC). However, only a small number of micro-RNAs (miRNAs) have been identified as potentially regulated by androgens. Our objective is to identify miRNAs that are regulated by androgens.

METHODS: We utilized a model derived from the LNCaP cell line, which overexpresses the androgen receptor (AR), as well as the VCaP cell line, and 13 intact-castrated prostate cancer (PC) xenograft pairs. We also analyzed clinical specimens of untreated PC and CRPC. The expression of miRNAs was analyzed using microarrays and quantitative RT-PCR (Q-RT-PCR). We also performed transfection experiments using pre-miR-141 and anti-miR-141.

RESULTS: Upon treatment with dihydrotestosterone (DHT), 17 miRNAs showed more than a 1.5-fold up- or downregulation in the cell lines, and 42 miRNAs showed similar changes after castration in the AR-positive xenografts. Only four miRNAs (miR-10a, miR-141, miR-150*, and miR-1225-5p) exhibited similar androgen regulation in both cell lines and xenografts. Among these, miR-141 was found to be expressed at higher levels in PC and CRPC compared to benign prostate hyperplasia. Furthermore, overexpression of miR-141 enhanced the growth of parental LNCaP cells, while inhibition of miR-141 by anti-miR-141 suppressed the growth of the LNCaP subline that overexpresses AR.

CONCLUSIONS: Only a small number of miRNAs were found to be regulated by androgens in both cell lines and xenograft models. Among these, miR-141 was upregulated in cancer and its overexpression promoted the growth of LNCaP cells, suggesting that it may contribute to the progression of PC.

title: Relationship between drug treatment services, retention, and outcomes.
text:
The aim of this study was to analyze the connections between treatment processes and outcomes in community-based drug treatment programs. A longitudinal approach was used, and a total of 1,939 patients from 36 outpatient drug-free and residential treatment programs in 13 California counties were included. The patients were assessed at intake, discharge, three months after admission, and nine months after admission. Path analyses were conducted to examine the relationship between the quantity and quality of services received in the first three months of treatment, treatment retention, and outcomes at the nine-month follow-up. Patients were considered to have a favorable outcome if they abstained from drug use, criminal activity, and lived in the community for at least 30 days before the follow-up assessment. The analyses took into account the patients' baseline characteristics. 

The results showed that higher service intensity and satisfaction were associated with either completing the treatment or having longer treatment retention, which in turn led to favorable treatment outcomes. Patients with more severe problems received more services and were more satisfied with their treatment. These patterns were consistent for patients in both outpatient drug-free programs and residential programs. 

In conclusion, the study suggests that there is a strong positive relationship between process measures, such as higher levels of service intensity, satisfaction, treatment completion or retention, and treatment outcomes. Therefore, improving these key elements of the treatment process is likely to enhance treatment outcomes.

title: Breast cancer mortality trends in the United States according to estrogen receptor status and age at diagnosis.
text:
The purpose of this study was to examine breast cancer mortality trends in the United States based on estrogen receptor (ER) status and age. It has been observed that overall breast cancer mortality rates in the US have decreased by 24% since 1990, which is attributed to mammography screening and adjuvant systemic therapy. However, the effectiveness of these treatments may vary depending on ER expression and age. 

To conduct the study, data from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) program from 1990 to 2003 was analyzed. Trends in incidence-based mortality (IBM), annual hazard rates for breast cancer deaths after diagnosis, and relative hazard rates for women with ER-positive and ER-negative tumors were calculated. Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess relative hazard rates, taking into account stage and grade, and stratified by age at diagnosis.

The results showed that during the study period, both IBM and annual hazard rates for breast cancer deaths decreased for women with ER-positive and ER-negative tumors. However, the decline was more significant for those with ER-positive tumors. Among women under 70 years old, the relative hazard rates decreased by 38% for those with ER-positive tumors compared to 19% for those with ER-negative tumors. Among women aged 70 or older, the relative hazard rates decreased by 14% for those with ER-positive tumors, while there was no significant decline for those with ER-negative tumors.

In conclusion, breast cancer mortality rates have decreased in the United States for women with both ER-positive and ER-negative tumors, with greater declines observed among younger women and those with ER-positive tumors. However, the mortality rates in all groups are still considered unacceptably high. Therefore, it is important to focus on improving outcomes for breast cancer patients over the age of 70 and for patients of all ages with ER-negative tumors.

title: An adenovirus mutant that replicates selectively in p53-deficient human tumor cells.
text: The E1B gene of the human adenovirus codes for a protein weighing 55 kilodaltons, which deactivates the cellular tumor suppressor protein p53. This study demonstrates that a modified adenovirus lacking this viral protein can reproduce and destroy p53-deficient human tumor cells, but not cells with functional p53. However, when the 55-kilodalton EIB protein is artificially expressed in the latter cells, they become susceptible to infection by the modified virus. When the mutant virus was injected into p53-deficient human cervical carcinomas grown in nude mice, it resulted in a significant reduction in tumor size and complete regression of 60 percent of the tumors. These findings suggest that mutant adenoviruses may have potential in the treatment of specific human tumors.

title: Immune reconstitution after cord blood transplantation: peculiarities, clinical implications and management strategies.
text: Umbilical cord blood (UCB) is now commonly used as an alternative source of hematopoietic stem cells for patients who do not have closely matched adult donors. However, UCB transplantation has traditionally been associated with delayed engraftment, weak immune reconstitution, and an increased risk of infection. Recent clinical studies, however, suggest that the conditioning regimens used and the omission of in vivo T-cell depletion may play a crucial role in promoting T-cell expansion after UCB transplantation, leading to a faster immune recovery. This article describes the unique characteristics of UCB cells, the importance of thymic function, and the impact of conditioning regimens and graft-versus-host disease on immune reconstitution. The final part of the review discusses available data on UCB and a new approach called third-party peripheral blood derived anti-viral cell therapy, which can help UCB recipients with viral complications during the post-transplant period.

title: OVEREXPRESSION OF BOTH CLOCK AND BMAL1 INHIBITS ENTRY TO S PHASE IN HUMAN COLON CANCER CELLS.
text: The circadian rhythm, controlled by the biological clock, regulates various physiological, biochemical, and behavioral processes in organisms ranging from bacteria to mammals. The core circadian oscillator consists of a feedback loop involving CLOCK and BMAL1, which act as positive regulators. The relationship between the "cell cycle" and "cell rhythm" mechanisms in a cell is still debated. This study aimed to investigate the impact of Clock and Bmal1 on the cell cycle, particularly the G1 phase, using vectors with the tetracycline operator-repressor system. The results showed that simultaneous induction of Bmal1 and Clock had a significant effect on the cell cycle in SW480/T-REx/Clock/Bmal1 cells, where both Clock and Bmal1 could be induced by tetracycline. The induction of Clock and Bmal1 inhibited cell growth and increased the proportion of cells in the G1 phase, suggesting that the entry from G1 to S phase was hindered. Moreover, overexpression of Clock and Bmal1 prevented the cells from entering the G2/M phase induced by Paclitaxel, making them more resistant to the agent. In conclusion, the overexpression of Clock and Bmal1 suppressed cell growth and potentially played a role in preventing cells from transitioning from G1 to S phase by suppressing CyclinD1 expression, thereby conferring resistance to Paclitaxel.

title: Composition of gall bladder stones associated with octreotide: response to oral ursodeoxycholic acid.
text:
Octreotide, a highly effective treatment for acromegaly, has been found to cause gall bladder stones in a significant percentage of patients (ranging from 13% to 60%). Understanding the composition of these stones is crucial for studying their development, treatment, and prevention. To investigate this, a study was conducted on 14 acromegalic patients who were treated with octreotide and had gall stones. 

Chemical analysis of gall stones removed during cholecystectomy from two patients revealed that they consisted of 71% and 87% cholesterol by weight. In the remaining 12 patients, localized computed tomography of the gall bladder showed that eight had stones with maximum attenuation scores of less than 100 Hounsfield units. This indicates that these stones were likely cholesterol-rich and dissolvable. Gall bladder bile samples were obtained from six patients using ultrasound-guided, fine needle puncture. All six patients had bile that was supersaturated with cholesterol, with a mean cholesterol saturation index of 1.19 (SEM) and abnormally rapid cholesterol microcrystal nucleation times (less than 4 days). In four of these patients, cholesterol microcrystals were present immediately after sampling.

Out of the 12 patients considered for oral treatment with ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA), two had a blocked cystic duct and were not started on UDCA, while one patient was lost to follow-up. After one year of treatment, five out of the remaining nine patients showed either partial (three patients) or complete (two patients) dissolution of their gall stones, indicating that their stones were primarily composed of cholesterol. This corresponds to a gall stone dissolution rate of 58.3% (15.9%) based on actuarial (life table) analysis.

In conclusion, gall stones induced by octreotide treatment are typically small, multiple, and predominantly composed of cholesterol. However, similar to spontaneous gall stone disease, some patients may present with a blocked cystic duct and stones containing calcium.

title: Imiquimod 5% cream for the treatment of superficial basal cell carcinoma: results from a randomized vehicle-controlled phase III study in Europe.
text:
Imiquimod is a medication that enhances the immune response by activating toll-like receptor 7, leading to the production of cytokines and an immune response involving both innate and adaptive cells. Previous studies have shown that imiquimod 5% cream can effectively clear superficial basal cell carcinoma (sBCC) both clinically and histologically. 

The objective of this study was to assess the safety and efficacy of imiquimod 5% cream for the treatment of sBCC in a multicentre, randomized, double-blind, phase III clinical trial conducted at 26 centres in Europe. Participants with at least one confirmed sBCC tumor were randomly assigned to apply either imiquimod or a vehicle cream to the tumor once daily for 6 weeks. The location of the target tumor was marked before treatment initiation. 

At 12 weeks post-treatment, the treated tumor site was evaluated for treatment response and then excised for histological evaluation. The efficacy of the treatment was assessed based on composite response rates (clinical and histological clearance) as well as histological clearance rates alone. Safety assessments, including adverse events and local skin reactions, were conducted throughout the study. 

A total of 166 participants were enrolled in the study. The results showed a significant difference between the imiquimod and vehicle groups in terms of both composite clearance rates and histological clearance rates. Composite clearance was observed in 77% of participants treated with imiquimod compared to only 6% in the vehicle group. Histological clearance was achieved in 80% of participants treated with imiquimod compared to 6% in the vehicle group. 

The most commonly reported safety findings were local skin reactions, which were more frequent in the imiquimod group. In conclusion, the study demonstrated that imiquimod 5% cream, applied once daily for 6 weeks, is a safe and effective treatment for sBCC when compared to the vehicle cream.

title: Changing the course of pancreatic cancer--Focus on recent translational advances.
text: Over the past ten years, significant advancements in preclinical research have greatly improved our understanding of pancreatic cancer. While the majority of pancreatic cancers have a KRAS mutation, not all tumors respond equally to KRAS-targeting therapies. However, there is hope in the development of 'synthetic lethal' approaches for treatment. The role of the pancreatic cancer stromal microenvironment is complex, as it can both hinder drug delivery and protect the tumor. Clinical trials are currently underway to manipulate different components of the stroma. Pancreatic tumors with BRCA mutations have shown increased susceptibility to DNA damaging agents and PARP-inhibition. This suggests that DNA repair-targeting agents may have broader applications beyond just germ line BRCA mutations. Immune strategies are also being actively explored in pancreatic cancer research. While initial trials of single-agent checkpoint inhibitors have been disappointing, combination therapies involving immune-modifying agents and vaccines show promise. The ultimate goal is to identify a profile of pancreatic cancer that is responsive to immune-therapy.

title: Swc2 is a widely conserved H2AZ-binding module essential for ATP-dependent histone exchange
text: The specific incorporation of the histone variant H2AZ in chromatin plays a role in modulating chromosome functions. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the SWR1 complex, a multiprotein complex, is responsible for depositing histone H2AZ by replacing nucleosomal histone H2A with H2AZ in an ATP-dependent manner. In this study, we investigated the interactions between the components of the SWR1 complex and H2AZ, and identified a connection between the ATPase domain of Swr1 and three subunits that are necessary for H2AZ binding. Our findings revealed that Swc2 directly binds to H2AZ and is essential for its transfer. Swc6 and Arp6 are required for the association of Swc2 and for binding to the nucleosome, while Swc5 and Yaf9 are necessary for H2AZ transfer but not for binding to either H2AZ or the nucleosome. Additionally, we found that the C-terminal α-helix of H2AZ is crucial for its recognition by SWR1. These discoveries shed light on the initial steps involved in histone exchange.

title: Detection, characterization, and spontaneous differentiation in vitro of very small embryonic-like putative stem cells in adult mammalian ovary.
text: The purpose of this study was to identify and examine the differentiation potential of stem cells in the ovarian surface epithelium (OSE) of adult rabbits, sheep, monkeys, and menopausal humans. Two different populations of putative stem cells (PSCs) were found in the scraped OSE. One population was smaller, measuring 1-3 μm, and exhibited pluripotent characteristics with nuclear Oct-4 and cell surface SSEA-4. The other population was larger, measuring 4-7 μm, and showed cytoplasmic Oct-4 localization and minimal SSEA-4 expression, suggesting they were tissue committed progenitor stem cells. Reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction revealed the presence of pluripotent gene transcripts in human and sheep OSE, including Oct-4, Oct-4A, Nanog, Sox-2, TERT, and Stat-3. The PSCs underwent spontaneous differentiation into various structures, such as oocyte-like structures, parthenote-like structures, embryoid body-like structures, cells with neuronal-like phenotype, and embryonic stem cell-like colonies. Additionally, the epithelial cells transformed into a mesenchymal phenotype through epithelial-mesenchymal transition after three weeks of OSE culture. Germ cell markers were also found in the oocyte-like structures. These findings challenge the traditional belief that the OSE is only capable of producing oocytes and granulosa cells, as they suggest the presence of distinct PSCs and tissue committed progenitor stem cells in mammalian ovaries that can develop into oocyte-like structures in vitro. Further research at the single-cell level, including comprehensive gene expression profiling, is necessary to confirm whether postnatal oogenesis is a common occurrence in adult mammals.

title: Rearrangement of CRLF2 is associated with mutation of JAK kinases, alteration of IKZF1, Hispanic/Latino ethnicity, and a poor outcome in pediatric B-progenitor acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
text: The gene expression profiling of 207 children with high-risk B-progenitor acute lymphoblastic leukemia who received uniform treatment showed that 29 cases (14%) had significantly increased expression of CRLF2 (cytokine receptor-like factor 2). All 29 cases had a genomic rearrangement of CRLF2: 18 cases (62%) had a translocation of the immunoglobulin heavy chain gene IGH@ on 14q32 to CRLF2 in the pseudoautosomal region 1 of Xp22.3/Yp11.3, while 10 cases (34%) had a 320-kb interstitial deletion centromeric of CRLF2, resulting in a P2RY8-CRLF2 fusion. One case had both IGH@-CRLF2 and P2RY8-CRLF2 rearrangements, and another case had a new CRLF2 rearrangement. Only 2 of the 29 cases had Down syndrome. CRLF2 rearrangements were significantly associated with activating mutations of JAK1 or JAK2, deletion or mutation of IKZF1, and Hispanic/Latino ethnicity (Fisher exact test, P < .001 for each). Among this group, patients with CRLF2 rearrangements had much worse treatment outcomes compared to those without CRLF2 rearrangements (35.3% vs 71.3% relapse-free survival at 4 years; P < .001). These findings suggest that the activation of CRLF2 expression, mutation of JAK kinases, and alterations of IKZF1 work together to promote B-cell leukemogenesis, highlighting these pathways as important targets for therapy in this disease.

title: Substrate requirements for ErmC' methyltransferase activity.
text: ErmC' is an enzyme that provides resistance to a group of antibiotics called macrolide-lincosamide-streptogramin B by methylating a specific adenine residue (A-2085 in Bacillus subtilis; A-2058 in Escherichia coli) in the 23S rRNA. The gene for ErmC' was cloned and expressed at a high level in E. coli, and the resulting protein was purified to almost complete purity. Research on the requirements of ErmC' substrate revealed that a 262-nucleotide RNA fragment within domain V of B. subtilis 23S rRNA can be efficiently methylated at A-2085. Kinetic studies on the monomethylation reaction demonstrated that the apparent Km of this 262-nucleotide RNA fragment was 26 times higher than the value determined for full-size and domain V 23S rRNA. Additionally, the Vmax for this fragment increased sevenfold. Based on the kinetic data, a model of RNA-ErmC' interaction involving multiple binding sites is proposed.

title: Validity of the World Health Organization Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS) Screener in a representative sample of health plan members.
text: The effectiveness of the six-question World Health Organization Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS) Screener was evaluated in a group of individuals who were subscribed to a large health plan in the United States. A subset of 668 subscribers was conveniently selected to take the ASRS Screener twice to determine its reliability, and then a third time alongside a clinical interviewer to assess adult ADHD according to DSM-IV criteria. The data was adjusted to account for differences in socio-demographics and past medical claims between the sample and the overall population. The continuous ASRS Screener demonstrated good internal consistency reliability, with values ranging from 0.63 to 0.72, and the test-retest reliability (measured by Pearson correlations) ranged from 0.58 to 0.77. The four-category version of the ASRS Screener showed strong agreement with clinician diagnoses, as indicated by an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.90. The brevity of the six-question ASRS Screener, along with its ability to accurately distinguish between individuals with and without DSM-IV adult ADHD, makes it a valuable tool for both community-based epidemiological surveys and clinical initiatives aimed at identifying and assisting individuals with ADHD.

title: The body-mass index of twins who have been reared apart.
text:
In order to determine the impact of genetics and environment on body-mass index (BMI), we conducted a study using samples of identical and fraternal twins who were either raised together or apart. The samples included 93 pairs of identical twins raised apart, 154 pairs of identical twins raised together, 218 pairs of fraternal twins raised apart, and 208 pairs of fraternal twins raised together. 

For identical twins raised apart, the correlation coefficients for BMI were 0.70 for men and 0.66 for women. These coefficients provide direct estimates of the influence of genetics (heritability) on BMI and were only slightly lower than those for twins raised together in this and previous studies. Maximum-likelihood model-fitting analyses yielded similar estimates of heritability, with coefficients of 0.74 for men and 0.69 for women. Nonadditive genetic variance, particularly among men, played a significant role in the heritability estimates. 

Among the potential environmental influences, only those unique to the individual, rather than those shared by family members, were found to be important, accounting for approximately 30% of the variance. The shared childhood environment did not contribute to the similarity in BMI among twins later in life. 

Based on these findings, we can conclude that genetic factors have a substantial impact on BMI, while the childhood environment has little to no influence. These results support and expand upon previous studies involving twins and adoptees.

title: A study of high cell density cultivation process of recombinant Helicobacter pylori multi-epitope vaccine engineering bacteria.
text:
GOAL: To develop a process for cultivating recombinant Helicobacter pylori multi-epitope vaccine engineering bacteria BIB at high cell density.

METHODS: The shake flask fermentation results were used to scale up the process in a 50 L fermenter. Various factors affecting the protein yield, such as fermentation medium, seed inoculation amount, inducer concentration, induction timing and duration, inducer addition method, and feeding strategy, were optimized and verified.

RESULTS: The BIB working seed was activated in modified TB medium at 37°C for 8 hours. It was then inoculated at a 5% (v/v) concentration and induced for another 11 hours using a final lactose concentration of 5 mmol/L. During the growth phase, glucose was used as the carbon source at a rate of 80 ml/h, while glycerol was used at a rate of 40 ml/h during the induction phase. Ammonia water was added dropwise to maintain a pH of approximately 7.0, and the revolution speed was adjusted to maintain a dissolved oxygen level above 30%. Ultimately, the bacterial biomass reached 70 g/L, and the protein expression amount was approximately 32%.

CONCLUSION: The high cell density cultivation of the recombinant engineering bacteria led to a significant increase in the expression and yield of the target protein rBIB.

title: Phorbol esters and cytokines regulate the expression of the NEMO-related protein, a molecule involved in a NF-kappa B-independent pathway.
text: The NF-kappaB signaling pathway is vital for immune, inflammatory, and apoptotic responses. Our recent discovery of the NF-kappaB Essential Modulator (NEMO) as a crucial component of this pathway has been significant. NEMO serves as a structural and regulatory subunit of the high molecular kinase complex (IKK), responsible for phosphorylating NF-kappaB inhibitors. During our search in the database, we isolated a cDNA that encodes a protein called NRP (NEMO-related protein), which shares a strong resemblance to NEMO. Surprisingly, we found that NRP exists in a unique high molecular weight complex that does not contain any known members of the IKK complex. Consequently, we did not observe any impact of NRP on NF-kappaB signaling. However, we did discover that treatment with phorbol esters leads to NRP phosphorylation and a decrease in its half-life. This phosphorylation event could only be inhibited by K-252a and stauroporin. Furthermore, we demonstrated that interferon and tumor necrosis factor alpha can induce the expression of NRP, and these two stimuli have a synergistic effect on NRP expression. Additionally, we observed that endogenous NRP is associated with the Golgi apparatus. Similar to NEMO, we found that NRP forms a complex with two kinases, suggesting that NRP may play a comparable role in another signaling pathway.

title: Tailoring Nutritional Advice for Mexicans Based on Prevalence Profiles of Diet-Related Adaptive Gene Polymorphisms
text: The prevalence of diet-related adaptive gene (DRAG) polymorphisms in specific populations has been linked to chronic disorders in individuals carrying these adaptive alleles. This is due to changes in dietary and lifestyle patterns that have occurred in recent times. In Mexico, the population consists of Amerindians (AM) and Mestizos, who have varying degrees of AM, European (EUR), and African genetic ancestry. As a result, they face an increased risk of nutrition-related chronic diseases. To address this issue, it is necessary to develop preventive and therapeutic strategies based on the Mexican genome and traditional food culture. Therefore, our objective was to determine the prevalence of several DRAG polymorphisms in the Mexican population, including subpopulations in Central West (CW) Mexico. We created geographic heat maps using ArcGIS10 software, which were based on published data for the MTHFR C677T (rs1801133), ABCA1 Arg230Cys (rs9282541), APOE T388C (rs429358)/C526T (rs7412), LCT C-13910T (rs4988235) polymorphisms, as well as AMY1 copy number variation (CNV). Additionally, we included new data obtained through allelic discrimination-real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) assays for the MTHFR, ABCA1, and APOE polymorphisms, as well as the AMY1 CNV in the CW Mexico subpopulations with varying proportions of AM and EUR ancestry. In the CW region, the highest frequency of the MTHFR 677T, ABCA1 230C, and APOE ε4 adaptive alleles was observed in the AM groups, followed by Mestizos with intermediate AM ancestry. The LCT-13910T allele frequency was highest in Mestizos-EUR but extremely low in AM, while the AMY1 diploid copy number was 6.82 ± 3.3 copies. Overall, the heat maps revealed a diverse distribution of the DRAG polymorphisms, with the AM groups exhibiting the highest frequencies of the adaptive alleles, followed by Mestizos. Given these genetic differences, it is important to provide genome-based nutritional advice that is tailored to the regional and individual needs of the population. This approach should take into account the available foods and the traditional food culture in Mexico, with the aim of promoting a healthier dietary pattern.

title: Prevention of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Through Inhibition of the Renin-Angiotensin System
text:
The prevalence of type 2 diabetes mellitus is rapidly increasing, making it a significant health problem associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Therefore, preventing the disease should be a key objective in the near future. In addition to lifestyle changes, various pharmacological treatments have proven effective in clinical trials, including antidiabetic drugs like metformin, acarbose, and troglitazone, as well as antiobesity agents like orlistat.

Arterial hypertension, a condition commonly associated with insulin resistance, is strongly linked to type 2 diabetes and can precede the disease by several years. While certain antihypertensive medications may worsen insulin resistance and impair glucose tolerance, newer agents have neutral or slightly positive metabolic effects. Clinical trials investigating the effects of ACE inhibitors or angiotensin II receptor antagonists (ARAs) on insulin sensitivity in hypertensive patients, with or without diabetes, have yielded inconsistent results. Some studies with ACE inhibitors in hypertensive nondiabetic individuals have shown a slight but significant increase in insulin sensitivity, while others have not found any significant change. The effects of ARAs on insulin sensitivity are generally neutral in most studies.

The mechanisms by which the renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibition improves glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity are complex. They may involve improving blood flow and microcirculation in skeletal muscles, enhancing insulin and glucose delivery to insulin-sensitive tissues, facilitating insulin signaling at the cellular level, and improving insulin secretion by beta cells.

Several recent large-scale clinical studies have consistently reported a reduction in the incidence of type 2 diabetes in hypertensive patients treated with ACE inhibitors or ARAs for 3-6 years compared to other medications or placebo. The relative risk reduction ranged from 14% to 34% in these studies. These findings have led to the initiation of two large, prospective, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trials aimed at preventing type 2 diabetes: the DREAM trial with the ACE inhibitor ramipril and the NAVIGATOR trial with the ARA valsartan. Additionally, the ONTARGET trial will investigate whether blocking the RAS with an ACE inhibitor, an ARA, or a combination of both can prevent the development of type 2 diabetes as a secondary endpoint.

These promising observations highlight the need for further research to uncover various aspects of the pathogenesis, prevention, and treatment of type 2 diabetes. From a practical standpoint, they offer a new strategy to reduce the ongoing epidemic and burden of the disease.

title: Randomized dose-finding clinical trial of oncolytic immunotherapeutic vaccinia JX-594 in liver cancer
text: The combination of oncolytic viruses and active immunotherapeutics have different ways of working in tumors, but both have the ability to multiply within the tumor. However, the effect of the dosage on the outcome for patients is not clear. JX-594 (Pexa-Vec) is a vaccinia virus that acts as both an oncolytic and immunotherapeutic treatment. In order to determine the best dosage of JX-594 for patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), a randomized phase 2 trial was conducted with 30 participants. Radiologists injected either a low or high dose of JX-594 into liver tumors on days 1, 15, and 29. The injections resulted in the detection of JX-594 genomes in the blood vessels. The response rates for intrahepatic Modified Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (mRECIST) (15%) and Choi (62%) were similar in both injected and non-injected tumors at both doses. The replication of JX-594 and the expression of granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) occurred before the induction of anticancer immunity. Unlike the response rate and immune endpoints, the duration of survival for patients was significantly influenced by the dosage (with a median survival of 14.1 months for the high dose compared to 6.7 months for the low dose; hazard ratio 0.39; P = 0.020). JX-594 demonstrated its ability to act as an oncolytic and immunotherapeutic treatment, with tumor responses and survival rates being dose-dependent in individuals with HCC.

title: Misread protein creates membrane channels: an essential step in the bactericidal action of aminoglycosides.
text: The bactericidal action of aminoglycosides is attributed to their irreversible uptake and inhibition of initiating ribosomes. However, the exact contributions of translational misreading and membrane damage, as well as the mechanism of that damage, have remained uncertain. Our study provides evidence that the incorporation of misread proteins into the membrane is responsible for the observed membrane damage. This suggests that the bactericidal action occurs through a sequence of essential steps: initial entry of the antibiotic, interaction with ribosomes causing misreading, incorporation of misread proteins into the membrane leading to abnormal channels, increased entry through these channels, further misreading and channel formation, and finally, blockade of initiating ribosomes. This mechanism explains several previously unexplained observations, such as the requirement of protein synthesis for streptomycin uptake during the lag phase before membrane damage, the ability of streptomycin-resistant cells to take up streptomycin after treatment with another aminoglycoside, and the effects of puromycin on streptomycin uptake. Puromycin, which prematurely releases polypeptides of normal sequence, also creates channels and promotes streptomycin uptake in resistant cells. These findings suggest that membrane proteins must not only have a hydrophobic anchoring surface but also fit tightly into the membrane.

title: Rate of cervical cancer, severe intraepithelial neoplasia, and adenocarcinoma in situ in primary HPV DNA screening with cytology triage: randomised study within organised screening programme.
text: The objective of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of primary human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA screening with cytology triage compared to conventional cytology in detecting cervical cancer and severe pre-cancerous lesions. The study was a randomized trial conducted in southern Finland from 2003 to 2005, involving 58,076 women aged 30-60 who were invited to participate in the routine population-based screening program for cervical cancer. The interventions included primary HPV DNA testing with cytology triage for positive results, or conventional cytological screening as the reference. The main outcome measures were the rates of cervical cancer, cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) grade III, and adenocarcinoma in situ (referred to as CIN III+) during the period of 2003-2007. The results showed that the relative rate of CIN III+ was higher in the HPV arm compared to the conventional arm, both among all women invited for screening and among those who attended. Among women with a normal or negative test result, the rate of subsequent CIN III+ was lower. The rate of cervical cancer was similar between the two arms. In conclusion, primary HPV screening with cytology triage was more sensitive than conventional cytology in detecting CIN III+ lesions when incorporated into an organized screening program. The findings have implications for cancer prevention. The trial was registered with Current Controlled Trials (ISRCTN23885553).

title: Metabolic syndrome as a risk factor for diabetes.
text: Initially described as a syndrome of insulin resistance, the metabolic syndrome is characterized by the presence of multiple metabolic traits such as high triglycerides, low levels of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, high blood pressure, abdominal obesity, and varying degrees of impaired glucose regulation. Although different consensus groups have developed various definitions, epidemiological studies consistently show that the metabolic syndrome is associated with a similar cardiometabolic risk, particularly for diabetes, with the risk ranging from three to twenty times higher depending on the number of components and the inclusion of impaired fasting glucose, impaired glucose tolerance, or both.
