These cultures were then analyzed for their tumorigenicity, expression of tumor stem cell markers, and ability to differentiate into multiple cell types, confirming their enrichment in TICs.

We exposed the TIC cultures to increasing concentrations of erlotinib and gefitinib and monitored their survival over a period of 1-4 days. In most cases, we observed a time- and concentration-dependent cell death. However, GBM 2 showed complete insensitivity to both drugs, while GBM 7 only responded to the highest concentrations tested. Radioligand binding assays revealed that all GBM TICs expressed EGFR. Furthermore, erlotinib and gefitinib inhibited EGFR and ERK1/2 phosphorylation/activation in all GBMs, regardless of the observed antiproliferative response.

Interestingly, GBM 2 exhibited high Akt phosphorylation under basal conditions, which remained unaffected by the drugs. On the other hand, GBM 7 showed complete insensitivity to gefitinib, and Akt inactivation only occurred at the highest concentration of erlotinib tested. This finding suggests a direct correlation between Akt inhibition and the antiproliferative effects of erlotinib. Additionally, we observed a significant down-regulation of phosphatase and tensin homolog expression in GBM 2, which may explain its insensitivity to the drugs.

In conclusion, our study demonstrates that glioma TICs are responsive to anti-EGFR drugs. However, the expression of phosphatase and tensin homolog and Akt inhibition appear to be crucial for the effectiveness of these drugs.

title: Structural features of the interaction of the 3'-untranslated region of mRNA containing exosomal RNA-specific motifs with YB-1, a potential mediator of mRNA sorting.
text: Previously, we demonstrated that YB-1 is the sole protein in the cytoplasmic extract of HEK293 cells that specifically interacts with RNA hairpins containing the motifs ACCAGCCU (1), CAGUGAGC (2), and UAAUCCCA (3). These motifs are frequently found in exosomal RNA and are believed to act as cis-acting elements that target RNAs into exosomes. In this study, we investigated the interactions between YB-1 and a fragment of the 3'-untranslated region (UTR) of septin 14 mRNA (SEPT14 RNA), which contains all three motifs. We demonstrated that YB-1 is present among the proteins pulled down from the HEK293 cell extract using biotinylated SEPT14 RNA. Using recombinant YB-1, we found that SEPT14 RNA can bind up to 5 moles of protein per mole of RNA in a cooperative manner, primarily facilitated by the presence of the aforementioned motifs. RNA hairpins with motifs 1 and 2 competed with SEPT14 RNA for binding to YB-1, while motif 3 was less competitive, consistent with YB-1's affinity for these RNA hairpins. Hydroxyl radical attack experiments revealed that nucleotides within all three motifs were protected when bound to YB-1, although hairpins with motif 2 and motif 1 contained additional protected nucleotides outside the motifs. This suggests that the specific environments surrounding these motifs significantly contribute to YB-1 binding. Analysis of the 3' UTRs of HEK293 cell mRNA obtained from RNA-seq data led us to conclude that YB-1 primarily binds to hairpins in the 3' UTRs that contain a portion of the motif along with its specific surroundings. We derived consensus sequences for these hairpins. Overall, our findings provide new insights into the structural basis of the interactions between YB-1 and mRNAs carrying the aforementioned motifs.

title: Periodic screening for breast cancer: the HIP Randomized Controlled Trial. Health Insurance Plan.
text: This paper presents the findings of the initial breast cancer screening trial, which began in December 1963 to investigate the effectiveness of screening. Women between the ages of 40 and 64 were chosen from participants in the Health Insurance Plan (HIP) of Greater New York and were randomly assigned to either the study or control groups. The study group women were invited to undergo screening, including an initial examination and three annual reexaminations. The screening process involved film mammography (cephalocaudal and lateral views of each breast) and a clinical examination of the breasts. The researchers analyzed breast cancer cases and mortality rates from breast cancer based on the treatment group (study vs. control) and the age group at the time of entry. After 18 years, the study group had a breast cancer mortality rate approximately 25% lower than the control group among women aged 40-49 and 50-59 at the time of entry. However, the majority of the difference in the 40-49 age group occurred in women who were diagnosed with breast cancer after turning 50, raising doubts about the effectiveness of screening women in their forties.

title: Staphylococcus aureus infections.
text: Micrococcus, when present in limited amounts and activity, can cause acute suppurative inflammation (phlegmon). However, when it becomes more extensive and intense in its effects on the human body, it can lead to highly virulent forms of septicaemia and pyaemia. In 1880 and 1882, Ogston conducted a series of clinical observations and laboratory studies that shed light on staphylococcal disease, its role in sepsis, and the formation of abscesses. Even after more than a century, Staphylococcus aureus remains a versatile and dangerous pathogen for humans. The incidence of both community-acquired and hospital-acquired staphylococcal infections has been steadily increasing, with little change in overall mortality rates. The treatment of these infections...

title: Structural overview of the nuclear receptor superfamily: insights into physiology and therapeutics.
text: The nuclear hormone receptors, known as ligand-regulated transcription factors, are highly desirable targets for drug development. They possess internal pockets that can bind to hydrophobic molecules similar to drugs, and they undergo specific conformational changes when bound to ligands, which in turn recruit transcriptional coregulators to specific regions of DNA. However, a major challenge in targeting these receptors is the identification of ligands that selectively act on specific genes, rather than affecting the entire set of genes regulated by the receptor. This selectivity is crucial for impacting disease outcomes through a specific subset of target genes. In this article, we provide an overview of the current understanding and progress in developing steroidal and nonsteroidal receptor ligands. This includes the use of crystal structures, high-throughput screening methods, and rational design approaches to discover therapeutic molecules. To overcome the difficulties in finding selective receptor modulators, it is necessary to gain a deeper understanding of the communication between different regions of the receptor, posttranslational modifications, and interactions between the receptor and other proteins. This knowledge can be utilized to exploit specific interactions and achieve target gene selectivity.

title: Differential assembly of inwardly rectifying K+ channel subunits, Kir4.1 and Kir5.1, in brain astrocytes.
text: The distribution and function of the inwardly rectifying K+ channel subunit Kir5.1 in the brain are still largely unknown, despite its abundant expression. We conducted a study comparing the biochemical and immunological properties of Kir5.1 and Kir4.1 in the mouse brain, as Kir5.1 is co-expressed with Kir4.1 in retinal glial Muller cells. Immunoprecipitation experiments revealed the presence of at least two subsets of Kir channels in the brain: heteromeric Kir4.1/5.1 and homomeric Kir4.1. Immunolabeling using specific antibodies showed that channels containing Kir4.1 and Kir5.1 subunits were assembled in specific regions. Heteromeric Kir4.1/5.1 was found in the neocortex and the glomeruli of the olfactory bulb, while homomeric Kir4.1 was limited to the hippocampus and thalamus. Homomeric Kir5.1 was not detected. Both Kir4.1/5.1 and Kir4.1 were associated with PDZ domain-containing syntrophins, which may play a role in targeting these astrocyte Kir channels to specific subcellular locations. The distinct ion channel properties of heteromeric Kir4.1/5.1 and homomeric Kir4.1 suggest that these channels may have different physiological roles in the K+ buffering function of brain astrocytes, depending on the specific region.

title: Low-grade serous ovarian cancer: a unique disease.
text: Approximately 10% of all serous ovarian carcinomas are classified as low-grade serous carcinomas. Recent research has highlighted significant differences in both clinical and molecular characteristics between these tumors and high-grade serous ovarian carcinomas. Patients with low-grade serous ovarian tumors tend to be diagnosed at a younger age, have a longer overall survival, and show lower response rates to conventional chemotherapy. Furthermore, low-grade serous ovarian carcinomas possess distinct pathologic and molecular features that are similar to serous tumors of low malignant potential. This suggests a shared pathogenesis and a continuum of disease from serous tumors of low malignant potential to low-grade serous carcinomas. To effectively treat this disease, further investigation specifically targeting low-grade serous carcinomas is necessary to determine the efficacy of alternative chemotherapeutic agents, hormonal therapy, or targeted biologic agents.

title: Renal outcomes with different fixed-dose combination therapies in patients with hypertension at high risk for cardiovascular events (ACCOMPLISH): a prespecified secondary analysis of a randomised controlled trial.
text: The ACCOMPLISH trial demonstrated that starting treatment for high blood pressure with a combination of benazepril and amlodipine is more effective in reducing cardiovascular morbidity and mortality compared to benazepril and hydrochlorothiazide. We conducted a study to evaluate the impact of these drug combinations on the progression of chronic kidney disease. The trial was a double-blind, randomized study conducted in five countries, with 11,506 hypertensive patients at high risk for cardiovascular events. Patients were randomly assigned to receive either benazepril plus amlodipine or benazepril plus hydrochlorothiazide, with doses adjusted to achieve recommended blood pressure goals. The primary endpoint was the progression of chronic kidney disease, defined as a doubling of serum creatinine concentration or end-stage renal disease. The trial was terminated early due to the superior efficacy of benazepril plus amlodipine. The analysis showed that the benazepril plus amlodipine group had a lower incidence of chronic kidney disease progression compared to the benazepril plus hydrochlorothiazide group. The most common adverse event in patients with chronic kidney disease was peripheral edema, which was more frequent in the benazepril plus amlodipine group. Angioedema was also more common in this group. In patients without chronic kidney disease, dizziness, hypokalemia, and hypotension were more frequent in the benazepril plus hydrochlorothiazide group. Based on these findings, initial treatment with benazepril plus amlodipine should be considered over benazepril plus hydrochlorothiazide as it slows the progression of nephropathy to a greater extent. The study was funded by Novartis.

title: Effects of exercise training on health status in patients with chronic heart failure: HF-ACTION randomized controlled trial.
text:
The aim of this study was to examine the effects of exercise training on the health status of patients with heart failure. The study involved 2331 outpatients with stable heart failure and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 35% or less. The patients were randomly assigned to either receive usual care plus aerobic exercise training or usual care alone. The main outcome measures were assessed using the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) at various time points over a period of up to 4 years.

The results showed that after 3 months, the group receiving exercise training had a greater improvement in the KCCQ overall summary score compared to the usual care group. This improvement was statistically significant. However, there were no further significant changes in the KCCQ score for either group after 3 months. Overall, the exercise training group had a sustained and greater improvement in health status compared to the usual care group. The results were consistent across different subscales of the KCCQ and there were no differences between subgroups.

In conclusion, exercise training led to modest but statistically significant improvements in self-reported health status among patients with heart failure compared to usual care alone. These improvements were observed early and persisted over time. The study was registered on clinicaltrials.gov with the identifier NCT00047437.

title: Acute respiratory failure in patients with severe community-acquired pneumonia: a prospective randomized evaluation of noninvasive ventilation.
text: A study was conducted to compare the effectiveness of noninvasive positive pressure ventilation (NPPV) in combination with standard treatment versus standard treatment alone in patients with severe community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) and acute respiratory failure (ARF). Patients who met the criteria for severe CAP and ARF were included in the study, while those with severe hemodynamic instability, need for emergency cardiopulmonary resuscitation, home mechanical ventilation or long-term oxygen supplementation, severe comorbidities with a low life expectancy, inability to expectorate, or contraindications to using a mask were excluded. A total of 56 patients were enrolled, with 28 in each group, and both groups were similar at the start of the study. The use of NPPV was well tolerated and safe, and it resulted in a significant reduction in respiratory rate, need for endotracheal intubation, and duration of stay in the intensive care unit (ICU). The two groups had similar nursing care workload, time to endotracheal intubation, duration of hospitalization, and hospital mortality. Among patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), those who received NPPV had a lower nursing care workload and improved 2-month survival. In conclusion, NPPV was effective in reducing the need for endotracheal intubation and ICU stay in selected patients with severe CAP and ARF. Patients with COPD also experienced a survival advantage.

title: Smallest angiosperm genomes found in lentibulariaceae, with chromosomes of bacterial size.
text: The size of nuclear holoploid genomes (C-values) in angiosperms can vary greatly, with a range of about 800-fold. The smallest recorded 1C-value is 157 Mbp in Arabidopsis thaliana. However, in the carnivorous family Lentibulariaceae, three taxa have been discovered with significantly smaller genome sizes. Genlisea margaretae has a 1C-value of 63 Mbp, G. aurea has 64 Mbp, and Utricularia gibba has 88 Mbp. In G. aurea, the smallest mitotic anaphase chromatids are only 2.1 Mbp, which is comparable to the size of bacterial genomes (e.g., E. coli has around 4 Mbp). Some Utricularia species have genome sizes that are lower or similar to A. thaliana. The largest 1C-value observed in Lentibulariaceae is in Genlisea hispidula, with 1510 Mbp, resulting in a 24-fold variation within Genlisea and the Lentibulariaceae. With these new measurements, the variation in genome size among angiosperms is now almost 2000-fold. Genlisea and Utricularia are positioned at the terminal branches of the eudicots' phylogeny, making these findings relevant for understanding genome miniaturization. Additionally, the Genlisea-Utricularia clade has one of the highest mutational rates in several genomic regions among angiosperms, which may be linked to specialized patterns of genome evolution. Pinguicula, the sister group of the Genlisea-Utricularia clade, does not exhibit accelerated mutational rates and does not have ultrasmall genomes. C-values in Pinguicula only vary by 1.7-fold, ranging from 487 to 829 Mbp.

title: Parasite multiplication potential and the severity of Falciparum malaria.
text: We compared the multiplication rates and invasiveness of Plasmodium falciparum parasites obtained from adult Thai patients hospitalized with uncomplicated malaria (n=34) to those from individuals with severe malaria (n=42). In order to simulate severe malaria and control for host effects, the in vitro cultures were adjusted to 1% parasitemia and utilized the same red blood cell donor. The P. falciparum isolates from individuals with severe malaria displayed initial cycle multiplication rates in vitro that were three times higher than those from uncomplicated malaria (median [95% confidence interval], 8.3 [7.1-10.5] vs. 2.8 [1.7-3.9]; P=.001). The parasites causing severe malaria demonstrated unrestricted invasion of red blood cells, while those from uncomplicated malaria were limited to infecting a geometric mean of 40 (31%-53%) of red blood cells. P. falciparum parasites causing severe malaria exhibited less selectivity and multiplied more at high parasitemias compared to those causing uncomplicated malaria.

title: PHD3-dependent hydroxylation of HCLK2 promotes the DNA damage response.
text: The DNA damage response (DDR) is a complex regulatory network that plays a crucial role in maintaining the integrity of the genome. Posttranslational modifications are commonly used to tightly control the flow of signals within this network. However, the DDR's response to environmental cues, such as changes in oxygen levels, is not well understood. Our research focused on a key component of the ATR/CHK1 signaling pathway called HCLK2, which is the human equivalent of a protein called CLK-2 found in Caenorhabditis elegans, a type of roundworm. We discovered that HCLK2 interacts with and is modified by a protein called PHD3, specifically through a process called hydroxylation. This hydroxylation of HCLK2 is necessary for its interaction with ATR and the subsequent activation of the ATR/CHK1/p53 pathway. When we inhibited PHD3 using a compound called dimethyloxaloylglycine (DMOG) or through exposure to low oxygen levels (hypoxia), the ATR/CHK1/p53 pathway was not activated, and apoptosis (cell death) caused by DNA damage was reduced. These findings were further supported by our experiments on mice lacking PHD3, which showed increased resistance to the effects of ionizing radiation and decreased thymic apoptosis, a marker of genomic integrity. By identifying HCLK2 as a substrate of PHD3, we have uncovered a mechanism by which hypoxia inhibits the DDR. This suggests that targeting the hydroxylation of HCLK2 could be a potential therapeutic strategy for regulating the ATR/CHK1/p53 pathway.

title: Economic implications of nighttime attending intensivist coverage in a medical intensive care unit.
text: Our goal was to evaluate the financial implications of transitioning from an on-demand presence to a mandatory 24-hour in-house critical care specialist staffing model in the intensive care unit (ICU). We conducted a pre-post comparison study, analyzing data from patients admitted to our medical ICU one year before and one year after the staffing change. We categorized the data based on the severity of illness and whether patients were admitted during the day or at night. We used a generalized linear model with log-link and γ-distributed errors to model the costs. The study took place at a large academic center in the Midwest. We included all adult patients admitted to the medical ICU between January 1, 2005, and December 31, 2006, excluding those who received care under both staffing models. The intervention involved changing the ICU staffing model to require a 24-hour in-house critical care specialist presence. We calculated the total cost estimates of hospitalization for each patient from the day of ICU admission to the day of hospital discharge. Adjusted mean total cost estimates were found to be 61% lower in the post period compared to the pre period for patients admitted during night hours (7 pm to 7 am) who were in the highest severity quartile according to the Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation III. No significant differences were observed at other severity levels. The unadjusted length of stay in the ICU decreased in the post period compared to the pre period (3.5 vs. 4.8), with no change in non-ICU length of stay. In conclusion, our findings indicate that implementing a 24-hour ICU intensivist staffing model reduces lengths of stay and cost estimates for the most severely ill patients admitted at night. However, the costs associated with implementing such a staffing model should be carefully considered in relation to the potential savings for smaller ICUs that primarily care for lower-acuity patients.

title: GENOTYPING OF THALASSEMIA IN MICROCYTIC HYPOCHROMIC ANEMIA PATIENTS FROM SOUTHWEST REGION OF IRAN
text:
Objective: The objective of this study was to assess the prevalence of α-gene, s-gene, and hemoglobin variants in individuals with Microcytic hypochromic anemia.

Methodology: A total of 340 subjects with microcytic hypochromic anemia (MCV<80fl; MCH<27pg) from the Southwest region of Iran were included in this study. The research was conducted at the Research Center of Thalassemia and Hemoglobinopathies (RCTH), the only center specializing in hematology and oncology in the Southwest (Khuzestan) region of Iran. The study population consisted of 325 individuals, including 171 with Beta-thalassemia trait, 88 with Alpha-thalassemia trait, 13 with thalassemia major, 11 with hemoglobin variants (HbS, HbC, and HbD Punjab), and 42 with iron-deficiency anemia. The remaining 15 patients had no definitive etiology for their condition.

Results: Genotyping for -α 3.7, -α 4.2, – α PA, - α 5NT, and - - MED was performed using gap-PCR. The overall frequency of - α 3.7 deletion in the 325 individuals was found to be 20%. Genotyping for the 23 most common s-gene mutations was conducted using direct mutation analysis by Amplification Refractory Mutation System (ARMS). The most prevalent mutations were CD 36/37, IVS II-I, and IVS I-110, with frequencies of 9.7%, 11.7%, and 3.5% respectively, among the 340 patients. There was a statistically significant difference in MCV (p-value = 0.25) and MCH (p-value = 0.23) indices between individuals with Beta-thalassemia trait and Beta-thalassemia Major, as well as in MCH index between individuals with Beta-thalassemia trait and Hb Variants (p-value = 0.04).

Conclusion: The prevalence of α-gene and s-gene mutations is high in the Southwest region of Iran. Molecular genotyping of α-thalassemia and s-thalassemia can aid in the diagnosis of unexplained microcytosis, thereby preventing unnecessary iron supplementation.

title: Systemic biomarkers in exacerbations of COPD: the evolving clinical challenge.
text:
BACKGROUND: Exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) continue to be a significant cause of mortality and morbidity. Despite advancements in understanding their underlying mechanisms, diagnosing and predicting exacerbations primarily relies on clinical presentation, which can be inconsistent. Numerous biomarkers have been studied in this context, with some showing promise.

METHODS: A comprehensive online search was conducted for articles published until December 2010, using specific terms related to COPD exacerbations, biomarkers, and sampling methods. The potential roles of biomarkers in diagnosing and confirming exacerbations, assessing etiology and severity, predicting prognosis, and guiding treatment decisions were evaluated.

RESULTS: Various systemic biomarkers have been measured during COPD exacerbations, with most showing an increase at onset and a decrease during the course of exacerbations. While correlations among these biomarkers have been reported, establishing direct associations with clinical variables has proven challenging. However, certain biomarkers, such as C-reactive protein for identifying exacerbations and procalcitonin for guiding antibiotic treatment, may offer clinically relevant information. Despite some limitations, these biomarkers show promise.

CONCLUSIONS: Although no single biomarker has gained widespread acceptance, some provide valuable clinical information. Further investigation through large decision-making studies is expected to focus on evaluating these biomarkers in the near future.

title: Preoperative Predictors of Weight Loss Following Bariatric Surgery: Systematic Review
text: Obesity affects approximately 32% of adults in the United States. While surgery can lead to significant weight loss, around 20-30% of individuals do not achieve successful results. Our goal was to identify psychosocial factors before surgery that are associated with weight loss following bariatric surgery. We conducted a thorough search of PubMed® and the Cochrane Database of Reviews of Effectiveness from 1988 to April 2010. We focused on articles that discussed bariatric surgery and weight loss, specifically looking at predictors such as body mass index (BMI), preoperative weight loss, eating disorders, and psychiatric disorder/substance abuse. We reviewed a total of 1,007 titles, screened 534 articles, and included 115 in our analysis. Our findings suggest that certain factors may have a positive or negative association with weight loss after surgery. For example, mandatory preoperative weight loss was found to be positively associated with weight loss in 7 out of 14 studies. On the other hand, preoperative BMI was negatively associated with weight loss in 37 out of 62 studies, super-obesity in 24 out of 33 studies, and personality disorders in 7 out of 14 studies. A meta-analysis revealed that super-obese patients experienced a decrease of 10.1% in excess weight loss (EWL) with a 95% confidence interval (CI) of [3.7-16.5%]. However, there was significant heterogeneity in the meta-analysis. Additionally, patients with binge eating showed an increase of 5.9% in EWL at 12 months after surgery, with a 95% CI of [1.9-9.8%]. Further research is needed to determine if preoperative factors can reliably predict significant differences in weight loss after bariatric surgery. Identifying these predictive factors could enhance patient selection and guide the development of interventions tailored to individual needs.

title: The tumor necrosis factor receptor stalk regions define responsiveness to soluble versus membrane-bound ligand.
text: The immune response is regulated by a network of tumor necrosis factor receptors (TNFRs) and their ligands. Different members of this receptor family have varying responses to soluble and membrane-bound ligands, but the reasons for this diversity are not yet understood. To investigate this, we used a system of chimeric TNFRs and new ligand variants that mimic the bioactivity of membrane-bound TNF. Our findings reveal that the extracellular stalk regions of TNFR1 and TNFR2 play a crucial role in determining responsiveness to soluble TNF. Specifically, the stalk region of TNFR2 inhibits the receptor's clustering in specific areas of the cell membrane and prevents ligand-independent receptor preassembly, thus blocking signaling induced by soluble TNF. This is in contrast to the stalk region of TNFR1. These results not only have implications for other TNFR family members, but also suggest potential targets for therapeutic intervention.

title: A bird's-eye view of sex chromosome dosage compensation.
text: Studying a small number of species with XX/XY sex chromosomes has provided some generalizations about how sex chromosome dosage compensation works. However, these generalizations do not apply well to ZZ/ZW sex chromosome systems found in birds. The unequal distribution of sex chromosome genes between males and females has led to the development of mechanisms in birds that balance gene dosage across the entire sex chromosome and in comparison to autosomal genes. Recent advancements in our understanding of avian genomes have prompted a reevaluation of sex-specific dosage compensation in birds, which is not as effective as in known XX/XY systems. The study of dosage compensation in birds has revealed both similarities and differences compared to XX/XY species, offering new insights into the evolution of sex-specific dosage compensation.

title: The role of CHMP2BIntron5 in autophagy and frontotemporal dementia.
text: Charged multivesicular body protein 2B (CHMP2B) is a crucial component of the endosomal complex required for transport-III (ESCRT-III). It plays a vital role in membrane deformation functions in autophagy and endolysosomal trafficking. A dominant mutation in CHMP2B, known as CHMP2BIntron5, is associated with a specific type of heritable frontotemporal dementia called FTD-3, which is linked to chromosome 3. ESCRT-III recruits Vps4, an AAA-ATPase that cuts the membrane during various cellular processes, including autophagy and intraluminal vesicle formation. The CHMP2BIntron5 mutation leads to a truncation at the C-terminus, removing an important Vps4 binding site and eliminating the normal autoinhibitory resting state of CHMP2B. CHMP2B is expressed in most cell types, but it appears to be particularly crucial for proper neuronal function. The phenotypes associated with CHMP2BIntron5 include misregulation of transmembrane receptors, accumulation of multilamellar structures, abnormal lysosomal morphology, downregulation of a brain-specific microRNA (miRNA-124), abnormal dendritic spine morphology, decrease in dendritic arborization, and cell death. Currently, researchers are using transgenic fly, mouse, and human cell lines to gain a better understanding of the diverse phenotypes and develop therapeutic approaches for FTD-3 caused by CHMP2BIntron5. This article is part of a Special Issue focused on autophagy.

title: Restless legs syndrome and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a review of the literature.
text:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to examine the connection between restless legs syndrome (RLS) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), explore the potential mechanisms behind this association, and consider the implications for shared pharmacologic treatments when both conditions co-occur.

METHOD: A search was conducted on PubMed.

RESULTS: Clinical samples have shown that up to 44% of individuals with ADHD also have RLS or RLS symptoms, while up to 26% of individuals with RLS have ADHD or ADHD symptoms. Various mechanisms could explain this association. Sleep disruption caused by RLS may result in inattentiveness, mood swings, and excessive activity. Diurnal manifestations of RLS, such as restlessness and inattention, may resemble symptoms of ADHD. Alternatively, RLS and idiopathic ADHD could be comorbid conditions. Subjects with RLS and a subset of those with ADHD may share a common dopamine dysfunction. Limited evidence suggests that certain dopaminergic agents, including levodopa/carbidopa, pergolide, and ropinirole, may be effective in treating RLS symptoms associated with ADHD.

CONCLUSIONS: Although the evidence is still limited, clinical studies have demonstrated an association between RLS and ADHD or ADHD symptoms. Further clinical studies using standardized criteria and procedures are necessary to better understand the extent of this association. Epidemiologic studies are needed to assess the relationship between ADHD and RLS symptoms in nonclinical populations. Future research should focus on investigating the underlying mechanisms linking RLS and ADHD. Several dopaminergic agents show promise as potential treatments for RLS symptoms associated with ADHD. However, the absence of randomized and blinded controlled studies currently prevents evidence-based recommendations.

title: Impact of the KU80 pathway on NHEJ-induced genome rearrangements in mammalian cells.
text: We investigated the impact of non-homologous end-joining (NHEJ) on mammalian chromosome rearrangements by using a substrate to measure deletion or inversion of an I-SceI-excised fragment, as well as accurate and inaccurate rejoining. Regardless of the DNA ends structure, deletion was found to be 2- to 8-fold more efficient than inversion. Accurate rejoining was controlled by KU80, while in the absence of KU, mutagenic rejoining, particularly microhomology-mediated repair, occurred efficiently. In cells that carried both the NHEJ and a homologous recombination (HR) substrate containing a third I-SceI site, we observed that NHEJ was at least 3.3-fold more efficient than HR. Translocation of the I-SceI fragment from the NHEJ substrate locus into the HR-I-SceI site was possible, but it occurred 50- to 100-fold less frequently than deletion. Both deletions and translocations showed both accurate and inaccurate rejoining, indicating a combination of KU-dependent and KU-independent processes. Therefore, these processes likely play significant roles in DSB-induced genetic instability in mammalian cells.

title: The multi-zinc finger protein ZNF217 contacts DNA through a two-finger domain.
text: Classical zinc finger proteins, specifically C2H2 zinc finger proteins, are highly abundant transcription factors in eukaryotes. The mechanisms by which they identify their target genes have been extensively studied. Typically, a sequence-specific DNA recognition requires a tandem array of three fingers separated by characteristic TGERP links. However, there are zinc finger proteins that lack this hallmark three-finger array, which raises the question of how they interact with DNA. In this study, we focused on ZNF217, a multi-finger protein containing eight classical zinc fingers. ZNF217 is known to be involved in oncogenesis and repression of the E-cadherin gene. Our findings reveal that two of its zinc fingers, 6 and 7, are capable of contacting DNA. We investigated its potential recognition site in the E-cadherin promoter and found it to be suboptimal. Through NMR analysis, mutagenesis, and fluorescence anisotropy titrations, we determined the DNA binding surface of ZNF217 and examined the specificity of its DNA binding activity. Furthermore, our sequence analysis indicates that other multi-finger proteins also possess two-finger units, suggesting the existence of a distinct subclass of DNA recognition motif.

title: Knowledge, attitudes, risk perception, and cancer screening behaviors among cancer survivors.
text:
The knowledge, attitudes, and risk perception surrounding second primary cancer (SPC) screening and its impact on screening practices in cancer survivors are not well understood. To address this, we recruited 326 cancer survivors who had completed primary treatment for cancer over a year ago from six oncology care outpatient clinics in the Republic of Korea. We assessed their knowledge, attitudes, perceived risk, and screening practices, as well as their sociodemographic, behavioral, and clinical characteristics. Using multivariate logistic regression, we examined the behavioral factors associated with completing all appropriate SPC screening according to national guidelines. 

Our findings showed that approximately 37.7% of survivors had undergone all appropriate SPC screening tests. These survivors had a high perceived risk of SPC, believed in the benefits of screening, and had positive attitudes towards cancer screening. However, their knowledge about SPC screening tests was limited, and only a few had received a recommendation from a physician to undergo SPC screening. While there was no association between perceived risk and positive attitudes with screening behavior, we found that higher knowledge was significantly associated with completing all appropriate SPC screening (adjusted odds ratio, 1.81; 95% confidence interval, 1.03-3.33). 

In conclusion, our study revealed that cancer survivors have limited knowledge about second cancer screening tests, which may contribute to lower rates of completion of screening practices in this population.

title: Ria1p (Ynl163c), a protein similar to elongation factors 2, is involved in the biogenesis of the 60S subunit of the ribosome in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
text:
RIA1 (YNL163c) is a gene that is considered to be essential, but not completely necessary for survival. It encodes a protein that shares many similarities with elongation factors 2. When there are small deletions in the protein's C-terminal region, it causes a significant growth defect. However, if there is a deletion of 22 amino acids in the C-terminal region, this defect can be reversed by mutations within the RIA1 gene itself or by dominant mutations in TIF6. TIF6 is believed to play a role in the formation of the 60S subunit of the ribosome. These dominant TIF6 mutations can also alleviate the negative effects associated with a complete deletion of the RIA1 gene.

When Ria1p is depleted, it has a profound impact on the polysome profile. The level of 80S monosomes is greatly reduced, causing an imbalance in the ratio of 40S to 60S subunits, and the appearance of halfmers. Further investigation revealed that the depletion of Ria1p specifically reduces the amount of 60S subunits. Localization experiments using HA-tagged derivatives of Ria1p did not show any stable association between Ria1p and ribosome subunits, 80S monosomes, or polysomes. Cell fractionation experiments demonstrated that Ria1p is present in both the cytoplasmic and nuclear fractions. Based on these findings, it can be inferred that Ria1p plays a role in the formation of the 60S subunit of the ribosome.

title: The Intestinal Immune System in Obesity and Insulin Resistance.
text: Chronic inflammation in metabolic tissues like adipose tissue and the liver is linked to obesity and insulin resistance. Recent studies have shown that the intestinal immune system plays a significant role in metabolic diseases. Obesity leads to changes in intestinal immunity, including alterations in gut microbiota, intestinal barrier function, immune cells residing in the gut, and tolerance to luminal antigens. Therefore, targeting the gut immune system could be a new approach to treating systemic inflammation in insulin resistance. This review explores the emerging field of intestinal immunity in obesity-related insulin resistance and its impact on metabolic disease.

title: Human placental lactogen and unconjugated estriol concentrations in twin pregnancy: monitoring of fetal development in intrauterine growth retardation and single intrauterine fetal death.
text: The concentrations of human placental lactogen and unconjugated estriol in maternal serum were assessed in 100 twin pregnancies without complications. These values were then compared to those observed in 16 twin pregnancies that were associated with either intrauterine growth retardation or the death of one fetus. In pregnancies with intrauterine growth retardation (n = 8), human placental lactogen levels were found to be at the lower end of the normal range for singleton pregnancies, while estriol levels were mostly within the normal range. In cases where one fetus had died before the 33rd week of pregnancy (n = 5), both human placental lactogen and estriol levels were low and similar to levels seen in singleton pregnancies. However, when intrauterine fetal death occurred after the 36th week of pregnancy (n = 3), both hormone levels remained normal until delivery. Therefore, human placental lactogen is a better indicator of intrauterine growth retardation in twin pregnancies compared to estriol. Both human placental lactogen and estriol are useful for monitoring the surviving fetus in cases of single intrauterine fetal death.

title: Low antioxidant enzyme gene expression in pancreatic islets compared with various other mouse tissues.
text: The gene expression of superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase, and glutathione peroxidase was examined in pancreatic islets and compared to various other mouse tissues (liver, kidney, brain, lung, skeletal muscle, heart muscle, adrenal gland, and pituitary gland) using a sensitive Northern blot hybridization technique. Generally, the gene expression of the antioxidant enzymes in the pancreatic islets was within a range of +/- 50% of that in the liver. However, the gene expression in the pancreatic islets was significantly lower compared to other tissues. Specifically, the cytoplasmic Cu/Zn SOD and mitochondrial Mn SOD gene expression levels were approximately 30-40% of those in the liver. Glutathione peroxidase gene expression was only 15%, and catalase gene expression was undetectable in the pancreatic islets. These findings suggest that the low levels of antioxidant enzyme gene expression in the pancreatic beta cells may explain their heightened vulnerability to cytotoxic damage caused by diabetogenic compounds and the development of diabetes in humans and animals.

title: Cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterase isozymes expressed in mouse skeletal muscle.
text: In order to comprehend the changes in cyclic nucleotide metabolism in muscle diseases, we examined the expression of phosphodiesterase (PDE) isozymes in normal mouse leg muscle. We generated four subcellular fractions through differential centrifugation at 10,000 x g and 100,000 x g. The activity of cAMP PDE was predominantly found in the soluble fractions, while the activity of cGMP PDE was more evenly distributed among soluble and particulate fractions. Through the use of pharmacological inhibitors, we discovered that PDE4 is the primary enzyme responsible for hydrolyzing cAMP, while PDE2 is the major enzyme for hydrolyzing cGMP in mouse leg muscle. PDE1 is expressed at low levels, while PDE3 and PDE5 are expressed at intermediate levels. Approximately 20 to 40% of the total PDE activity remained even in the presence of inhibitors for PDE1-PDE5, suggesting that other PDE families also contribute to the overall PDE pool. Our conclusion was supported by reverse-transcription PCR using family-specific primers, which revealed the expression of mRNA for PDE7-PDE9. Furthermore, we observed elevated levels of total PDE activity in tissue extracts from a mouse model of Duchenne's muscular dystrophy.

title: Exercise-induced asthma.
text: The impact of exercise on respiratory function was examined in a group of seven asthma patients. Out of the seven, three experienced a noticeable decrease in forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV 1) following exercise. The extent of hyperventilation during exercise was found to be correlated with the decrease in FEV 1 after exercise. Additionally, all asthma patients experienced a decrease in FEV 1 when voluntarily hyperventilating at rest. When these patients breathed in 5.6 percent carbon dioxide instead of regular air during voluntary hyperventilation, they exhibited increased ventilation and a greater decrease in FEV 1. On the other hand, exercise and voluntary hyperventilation did not have any significant impact on FEV 1 in individuals with normal respiratory function or those with chronic bronchitis. The decrease in FEV 1 caused by both exercise and hyperventilation was inhibited by prior administration of isoproterenol, but not by atropine. It is hypothesized that exercise-induced asthma is likely a result of hyperventilation-induced asthma. There are several potential mechanisms that could explain the development of airway obstruction in this context.

title: An antimicrobial protein of the gut symbiont Bacteroides fragilis with a MACPF domain of host immune proteins.
text:
Bacteroidales, which are Gram-negative bacteria found in the human intestinal microbiota, are incredibly abundant and make up over half of the bacteria in many individuals. While some factors that allow these bacteria to establish and thrive in this ecosystem have been identified, there is still much to learn about ecological competition, particularly interference competition where one organism directly harms another. In order to gain a better understanding of this ecological principle and its relevance to these prevalent gut bacteria, we conducted a study on Bacteroides fragilis to investigate the production of antimicrobial molecules.

Our findings revealed that the production of extracellularly secreted antimicrobial molecules is widespread in Bacteroides fragilis. The first molecule we identified, which is described in this manuscript, contains a membrane attack complex/perforin (MACPF) domain. This domain is also found in host immune molecules that kill bacteria and virally infected cells by creating pores. Mutations in key residues of this domain rendered the molecule inactive. We have named this antimicrobial molecule BSAP-1.

BSAP-1 is secreted from the cell in outer membrane vesicles, and no additional proteins are necessary for its secretion, processing, or immunity of the producing cell. This study provides valuable insight into the secreted molecules that promote competitive interference among Bacteroidales strains in the human gut.

title: Directional perception of distributed sound sources.
text:
Two listening experiments were conducted in anechoic conditions to investigate the perception of spatially distributed sound sources. In the first experiment, 13 loudspeakers were evenly distributed in the frontal horizontal plane, emitting incoherent noise signals. The sound sources had gaps in their distribution and emitted pink noise. The results showed that the exact loudspeaker distribution could not be accurately perceived, and the width of the distribution was perceived to be narrower than it actually was. Only up to three spatially distributed loudspeakers emitting sound could be individually perceived, and the number of loudspeakers indicated as emitting sound was smaller than the actual number. 

In the second experiment, a reference with 13 loudspeakers and test cases with fewer loudspeakers were presented, and their perceived spatial difference was rated. The researchers were particularly interested in the effect of noise bandwidth. They used noise with different bandwidths centered around 500 and 4000 Hz. The results revealed that when the number of loudspeakers increased from four to seven, the perceived auditory event was very similar to that perceived with 13 loudspeakers, regardless of the bandwidth. However, the perceived differences were larger in wideband noise compared to narrow-band noise.

title: Adoptive T cell transfer for cancer immunotherapy in the era of synthetic biology.
text: The field of adoptive T cell transfer for cancer and chronic infection is rapidly advancing and showing promise in recent trials. One key breakthrough is the use of synthetic-biology-based engineering to enhance T lymphocytes and overcome immune tolerance, a major obstacle in immunotherapy-based strategies. This has allowed for a broader evaluation of the technology, transitioning it from a niche application to a potentially mainstream approach. However, a significant challenge remains in increasing the specificity of engineered T cells for tumors, as targeting shared antigens can result in unintended toxicities. As the field continues to evolve, the focus is now shifting towards developing automated cell culture systems to make this approach more accessible beyond specialized academic centers.

title: Bruce treadmill test in children: normal values in a clinic population.
text: The Bruce treadmill protocol can be used for children as young as 4 years old. The duration of maximum endurance can be used as the only measure of exercise capacity, and normal values were established using 327 children with innocent heart murmurs. On average, boys' endurance time increased from 10.4 minutes at ages 4 to 5, to 14.1 minutes at ages 13 to 15. Girls' endurance time increased from 9.5 minutes at ages 4 to 5, to 12.3 minutes at ages 10 to 12. The average maximum heart rate ranged from 193 to 206 beats per minute. There were minimal differences in average maximum and submaximal heart rates based on age. There were negative correlations between endurance time and the weight-to-height ratio. Additionally, there were negative correlations between heart rates during treadmill stages 1 to 3 and endurance times. The correlation coefficient between endurance time and maximal oxygen uptake was 0.88, but for clinical purposes, endurance time alone is a satisfactory indicator of exercise performance.

title: Immunoproteasome and LMP2 polymorphism in aged and Alzheimer's disease brains.
text: This study aimed to examine the presence and function of the immunoproteasome and its LMP2 subunit polymorphism at codon 60 in Alzheimer's disease (AD). The immunoproteasome was detected in brain regions such as the hippocampus and cerebellum, and it was localized in neurons, astrocytes, and endothelial cells. Interestingly, AD patients exhibited higher levels of immunoproteasome expression in the brain compared to non-demented elderly individuals, while its expression was negligible or absent in young brains. Additionally, regions affected by AD displayed a partial reduction in proteasome trypsin-like activity. The investigation of the LMP2 polymorphism (R/H) revealed that it did not impact LMP2 expression, both at the mRNA and mature protein levels, in brain tissue. However, control brain areas of AD patients with the RR genotype exhibited increased proteasome activity compared to RH carriers. To explore whether this genotype effect might be associated with AD onset, a genetic study was conducted. Surprisingly, the study found no association between the LMP2 codon 60 polymorphism and AD onset, despite its influence on proteasome activity in the human brain.

title: The centrosome and its mode of inheritance: the reduction of the centrosome during gametogenesis and its restoration during fertilization.
text: The complete understanding of the restoration and reduction of the centrosome during fertilization and gametogenesis is still lacking, but these events play a crucial role in development. In each somatic cell cycle, the chromosomes, cytoplasm, and centrosomes duplicate in interphase, and all three divide in two during cell division. It has been known for a long time that both the sperm and the egg contribute equal haploid genomes during fertilization, with the majority of the cytoplasm coming from the egg. However, the relative contributions of the centrosome from each gamete are still uncertain. This article examines the inheritance patterns of the centrosome and discusses nine essential and secondary activities of this structure. Boveri once proposed that the egg has all the necessary elements for development except for an active division center, while the sperm possesses such a center but lacks the necessary protoplasmic substratum. Therefore, the union of the egg and sperm in syngamy restores the missing element required for further development to each gamete. This article reviews evidence from 11 experimental strategies used to test this theory. Although most of these approaches support the hypothesis that the sperm introduces the centrosome during fertilization, it is not a universal pattern, as parthenogenesis can occur naturally and be induced artificially. Additionally, the centrosome and centriole can form de novo in extracts from unfertilized eggs, and in some systems, such as mice, the centrosome is derived from maternal sources during fertilization. The article proposes models of the centrosome and speculative mechanisms that may explain the masking of the maternal centrosome during oogenesis and the retention of this structure by the paternal centrosome during spermatogenesis. Proteins essential for microtubule nucleation, like gamma-tubulin, are retained in the cytoplasm during oogenesis but mostly lost during spermatogenesis. It is also suggested that the restoration of the zygotic centrosome during fertilization involves the attraction of maternal centrosomal components, particularly gamma-tubulin and the 25S "gamma-some" particle, to the paternal reproducing element. This, combined with post-translational modifications such as phosphorylation, disulfide reduction, and calcium ion binding, creates a functional zygote centrosome by incorporating both maternal and paternal constituents.

title: Aggregation of vascular risk factors and risk of incident Alzheimer disease.
text:
BACKGROUND: The prevalence of Alzheimer's disease (AD) is rising among the elderly population, and there is evidence to suggest that vascular risk factors may contribute to its development. 

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the association between the accumulation of vascular risk factors and the risk of developing AD. 

METHODS: The study followed 1,138 individuals without dementia at the start of the study (with a mean age of 76.2) for an average of 5.5 years. The presence of vascular risk factors was assessed in relation to the occurrence of possible and probable AD. 

RESULTS: When analyzed individually, four risk factors (diabetes, hypertension, heart disease, and current smoking) were found to be associated with a higher risk of AD (p < 0.10). The risk of AD increased as the number of risk factors increased (diabetes + hypertension + heart disease + current smoking). The adjusted hazards ratio for probable AD in individuals with three or more risk factors was 3.4 (95% CI: 1.8, 6.3; p for trend < 0.0001) compared to those with no risk factors. Diabetes and current smoking were identified as the strongest risk factors, both individually and when combined with other risk factors. However, hypertension and heart disease also contributed to an increased risk of AD when clustered with diabetes, smoking, or each other. 

CONCLUSIONS: The risk of developing Alzheimer's disease increased with the accumulation of vascular risk factors. Diabetes and current smoking were identified as the most significant risk factors, but the presence of hypertension and heart disease, either individually or in combination with other risk factors, also increased the risk of AD. These associations are unlikely to be due to misclassification of the outcome, as strong associations were observed when only probable AD cases were considered.

title: Hotspot mutations in H3F3A and IDH1 define distinct epigenetic and biological subgroups of glioblastoma.
text: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a type of brain tumor that has a very poor prognosis and shows significant variability. Recently, we have discovered recurring mutations in the H3F3A gene, specifically affecting two important amino acids (K27 and G34) of the histone H3.3 protein, in around one-third of pediatric GBM cases. Our research reveals that each H3F3A mutation defines a distinct subgroup of GBM based on epigenetic characteristics, including a unique pattern of global methylation. These mutations are mutually exclusive with IDH1 mutations, which define another subgroup based on a different set of mutations. Additionally, we have identified three more epigenetic subgroups that are enriched with genetic events commonly found in adult GBM, as well as established transcriptomic signatures. Furthermore, our findings demonstrate that the two H3F3A mutations give rise to GBMs in different parts of the brain, with varying regulation of transcription factors OLIG1, OLIG2, and FOXG1, suggesting potential differences in the cellular origins of these tumors.

title: Glucocorticoid with cyclophosphamide for paraquat-induced lung fibrosis.
text: Paraquat is a widely used herbicide that is effective but also highly toxic. In many developing countries, it is easily accessible and inexpensive, making it difficult to prevent poisoning. However, most cases of paraquat poisoning occur as a result of suicide attempts. The standard treatment for paraquat poisoning involves preventing further absorption and reducing the amount of paraquat in the blood through haemoperfusion or haemodialysis. However, these treatments have limited effectiveness. The immune system plays a role in worsening lung fibrosis caused by paraquat. Researchers are currently studying the use of immunosuppressive treatment with glucocorticoid and cyclophosphamide to assess its effects on mortality in patients with paraquat-induced lung fibrosis. To find relevant studies, various databases were searched, including the Cochrane Injuries Group's Specialised Register, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Chinese biomedical literature databases. The selection criteria for this review included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) where patients received standard care plus either glucocorticoid with cyclophosphamide or a control intervention. Data from the selected studies were analyzed, and the results showed that patients who received glucocorticoid with cyclophosphamide in addition to standard care had a lower risk of death compared to those receiving standard care alone. Based on these findings, it is suggested that glucocorticoid with cyclophosphamide may be a beneficial treatment for patients with paraquat-induced lung fibrosis. Further research is needed, and hospitals may consider providing this treatment as part of an RCT with allocation concealment to study its effects on patients with moderate to severe paraquat poisoning.

title: Hydroxyethyl starch (HES) versus other fluid therapies: effects on kidney function.
text:
BACKGROUND: Hydroxyethyl starches (HES) are commonly used synthetic colloids for fluid resuscitation, but there is controversy surrounding their impact on kidney function.

OBJECTIVES: This study aims to examine the effects of HES on kidney function compared to other fluid resuscitation therapies in different patient populations.

SEARCH STRATEGY: We conducted a search in various databases including the Cochrane Renal Group's specialised register, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE, EMBASE, MetaRegister, and reference lists of articles.

SELECTION CRITERIA: We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and quasi-RCTs that compared HES to alternate fluid therapies for the prevention or treatment of effective intravascular volume depletion. Primary outcomes were renal replacement therapy (RRT), author-defined kidney failure, and acute kidney injury (AKI) as defined by the RIFLE criteria. Secondary outcomes included serum creatinine and creatinine clearance.

DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS: Two authors screened, selected, extracted data, and assessed the quality of each retrieved article using standardized forms. Authors were contacted for additional data if necessary. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses were performed using a random effects model.

MAIN RESULTS: The review included 34 studies with a total of 2607 patients. Overall, HES-treated individuals had a higher risk of author-defined kidney failure (RR 1.50, 95% CI 1.20 to 1.87; n = 1199) and a slightly higher risk of requiring RRT (RR 1.38, 95% CI 0.89 to 2.16; n = 1236) compared to other fluid therapies. Subgroup analyses suggested a higher risk in septic patients compared to non-septic (surgical/trauma) patients. However, the non-septic patient studies were smaller and had lower event rates, so the subgroup differences may be due to lack of statistical power. Limited data was available for analysis of kidney outcomes using the RIFLE criteria. The methodological quality of the studies was generally good, but subjective outcomes may be biased due to lack of blinding in most studies.

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: The potential for increased risk of AKI should be considered when weighing the risks and benefits of using HES for volume resuscitation, especially in septic patients. Large studies with adequate follow-up are needed to evaluate the renal safety of HES products in non-septic patient populations. Future studies should apply the RIFLE criteria to evaluate kidney function and re-analyze previously published studies if data is available. There is currently insufficient clinical data to support claims of safety differences between different HES products.

title: Dietary fat and obesity: evidence from epidemiology.
text: The available evidence suggests that a high-fat diet may contribute to the development of obesity, but it is not definitive. This paper aims to review different epidemiological methods used to address this issue and provide an updated summary of the existing evidence. Ecological studies, which examine dietary fat intake and obesity at a population level, yield mixed results and are likely influenced by confounding factors and variations in data quality across different populations. Cross-sectional studies generally agree that a higher fat concentration in the diet is associated with higher relative weight. However, prospective studies on diet and subsequent weight change produce inconsistent findings, possibly due to behavioral factors like dieting in response to weight gain. Moreover, these studies rarely consider the potential interaction between genetic predisposition and dietary fat in promoting weight gain. Intervention studies on free-living individuals show consistent but short-lived periods of active weight loss on low-fat diets. Experimental evidence on this relationship is more conclusive than epidemiological evidence, although the biological mechanisms involved remain controversial. Future epidemiological research should focus on longitudinal studies of dietary fat intake as a predictor of growth in children, observational studies examining the relationship between total dietary fat and specific types of fat with overall and regional adiposity, and randomized intervention studies investigating the effects of low-fat diets, with a particular emphasis on familial predisposition to obesity and other potential modifying factors.

title: Uncoupling of leading- and lagging-strand DNA replication during lesion bypass in vivo.
text: DNA is often attacked by various agents, which can cause damage that hinders normal replication. To overcome this, specialized DNA polymerases temporarily replace the usual replicative polymerase and copy past the damaged areas. Unfortunately, this process can lead to mutations, which are a major factor in the development of cancer. In our study, we observed the replication kinetics of both strands of DNA molecules in Escherichia coli that contained a single replication block in either the leading or lagging strand. Surprisingly, even with a block in the leading strand, synthesis on the lagging strand continued, suggesting a temporary separation of the two processes. Replicating through the damaged area requires the involvement of specialized DNA polymerases and occurs at similar rates and efficiencies in both strands.

title: Phosphoinositide 3-kinase signalling--which way to target?
text: This abstract discusses the importance of phosphoinositide 3-kinases (PI3Ks) in regulating cell growth, proliferation, and survival. These kinases play a crucial role in the progression of tumors by activating various proteins, including phosphoinositide-dependent kinase, protein kinase B, and the target of rapamycin. Additionally, PI3Ks are involved in controlling cell motility and cardiovascular parameters. Given their significant role in these processes, PI3Ks have the potential to be targeted for the treatment of cancer, chronic inflammation, allergy, and cardiovascular failure. However, it is important to consider that PI3Ks also play a role in metabolic control and nutrient uptake. This article provides mechanistic data and mouse phenotypic analyses to support the potential therapeutic inhibition of specific PI3K isoforms.

title: Determination of the time course of capacitation in mouse spermatozoa using a chlortetracycline fluorescence assay.
text:
The heads of mouse spermatozoa, collected 5 minutes after being released from the excised caudae epididymides, displayed a distinct fluorescence pattern when exposed to the fluorophore chlortetracycline (CTC). The entire head exhibited uniform fluorescence, with approximately half of the sperm population showing a brighter line of fluorescence across the equatorial segment. This pattern was labeled as "F". 

After being incubated for 90 minutes in a culture medium (CM) containing 2% bovine serum albumin, most of the sperm heads displayed a dark band of nonfluorescence over the equatorial and postequatorial segment, while the anterior part of the head exhibited bright fluorescence. This pattern was designated as "B". The disappearance of pattern F coincided with the appearance of pattern B, with a half-time of 30 minutes. The transformation was complete after 90 minutes. 

As the incubation time in CM increased, the percentage of spermatozoa displaying pattern B decreased. The fluorescence over the entire head was lost, which is characteristic of acrosome-reacted sperm. Mouse sperm exhibiting pattern B were capable of undergoing the acrosome reaction, either spontaneously or when induced by acid-solubilized zonae pellucidae from mouse eggs. This reaction was inhibited by the specific inhibitor 3-quinuclidinyl benzilate (QNB). 

On the other hand, mouse sperm displaying pattern F could not be induced to undergo the acrosome reaction when exposed to solubilized zonae. This suggests that the transition from fluorescence pattern F to pattern B corresponds to changes in the sperm that render them susceptible to the acrosome reaction. This change occurs within the previously determined time frame required for capacitation of mouse sperm in vitro in CM. 

These findings indicate that spermatozoa exhibiting CTC fluorescence pattern B can be considered capacitated, and that the ability to rapidly undergo the acrosome reaction when treated with acid-solubilized zonae pellucidae serves as a functional definition for capacitation. The CTC fluorescence assay provides a novel method to monitor the time course of epididymal mouse sperm capacitation in vitro.

title: [Detection of CRISPR and its relationship to drug resistance in Shigella].
text:
The aim of this study was to identify clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) in Shigella and examine their association with drug resistance. A total of 60 Shigella strains were analyzed using four pairs of primers designed based on sequences in the CRISPR database. CRISPR Finder software was used to analyze the CRISPR structures, and the susceptibilities of the Shigella strains were tested using the agar diffusion method. Additionally, the relationship between drug resistance and a specific CRISPR structure, CRISPR-S4, was investigated. 

The results showed that 95% of the Shigella strains had convincing CRISPR structures. The four CRISPR loci formed 12 spectral patterns (A-L), with all patterns containing convincing CRISPR structures except for type K. The study also identified one new repeat and 12 new spacers. The rate of multi-drug resistance among the Shigella strains was found to be 53.33%. No significant difference was observed between CRISPR-S4 and drug resistance. However, the repeat sequence of CRISPR-S4 in multi- or TE-resistance strains predominantly had AC deletions in the 3' end, and the spacer sequences of CRISPR-S4 in multi-drug resistance strains were mainly Sp5.1, Sp6.1, and Sp7. 

In conclusion, CRISPR structures were commonly found in Shigella. Variations in repeat sequences and diversities of spacer sequences may be associated with drug resistance in Shigella.

title: The helicase DDX41 senses intracellular DNA mediated by the adaptor STING in dendritic cells
text: The recognition of harmful DNA is crucial for triggering antiviral responses. In this study, we have discovered a DNA sensor called DDX41, which belongs to the DEXDc family of helicases, in myeloid dendritic cells (mDCs). By using short hairpin RNA to reduce DDX41 expression, we observed that mDCs lost their ability to produce type I interferon and cytokine responses when exposed to DNA and DNA viruses. Interestingly, when both DDX41 and the membrane-associated adaptor STING were overexpressed, they had a synergistic effect in enhancing the activity of the Ifnb promoter. DDX41 was found to bind to both DNA and STING, and it localized in the cytosol alongside STING. Furthermore, knocking down DDX41 expression hindered the activation of the mitogen-activated protein kinase TBK1, as well as the transcription factors NF-κB and IRF3, by B-form DNA. These findings suggest that DDX41 is an additional DNA sensor that relies on STING to detect harmful DNA.

title: Radiotherapy plus concomitant and adjuvant temozolomide for glioblastoma.
text:
In this study, we compared the effectiveness and safety of radiotherapy alone versus radiotherapy combined with temozolomide for patients with newly diagnosed glioblastoma, the most common primary brain tumor in adults. The current standard treatment involves surgical removal of the tumor, followed by adjuvant radiotherapy. 

A total of 573 patients from 85 medical centers were randomly assigned to receive either radiotherapy alone or radiotherapy plus temozolomide. The radiotherapy consisted of daily fractions of 2 Gy given 5 days per week for 6 weeks, totaling 60 Gy. The group receiving radiotherapy plus temozolomide also took a daily dose of 75 mg per square meter of body-surface area throughout the course of radiotherapy, followed by six cycles of adjuvant temozolomide. Each cycle involved taking 150 to 200 mg per square meter for 5 days every 28 days. 

The primary goal of the study was to assess overall survival. After a median follow-up of 28 months, the median survival was 14.6 months for the radiotherapy plus temozolomide group and 12.1 months for the radiotherapy alone group. The hazard ratio for death in the radiotherapy-plus-temozolomide group was 0.63, indicating a significant survival benefit. The two-year survival rate was 26.5 percent for the radiotherapy plus temozolomide group and 10.4 percent for the radiotherapy alone group. 

The addition of temozolomide to radiotherapy did result in some hematologic toxic effects, specifically grade 3 or 4 toxicity in 7 percent of patients. However, these effects were considered minimal and did not outweigh the survival benefit observed. 

In conclusion, the combination of temozolomide with radiotherapy for newly diagnosed glioblastoma showed a significant improvement in survival with minimal additional toxicity.

title: Drug interactions between oral contraceptives and antibiotics.
text:
The objective of this study was to assess the evidence regarding potential drug interactions between antibiotics and oral contraceptives (OCs) that could result in OC failure. The data sources included MEDLINE and Lexis/Nexis Medical Library searches from 1966 to 1999 using the keyword "oral contraceptives," cross-referenced with the terms "antibiotics," "adverse effects," and "pregnancy." An additional MEDLINE search was conducted using the MeSH term "drug interactions." No language restrictions were applied. 

A total of 167 articles were analyzed, and an additional 32 articles were identified through reference review. The selection criteria included articles that provided information on the relationship between antibiotic therapy and OC efficacy in compliant users (women with unplanned pregnancies who reported adherence to their OC regimen). Studies that directly measured the effects of antibiotics on the pharmacokinetics of OC components or analyzed the effects of antibiotics on ovulation in OC users were also included. 

The analysis revealed at least 30 reported cases of pregnancies in women using OCs and antibiotics, particularly rifampin. Approximately 20% of pregnant women seeking family planning or abortion services reported concurrent use of OCs and antibiotics. Adverse event reporting databases supported the findings from case reports and clinical surveys, accounting for about one-third of reported cases. Retrospective surveys, primarily from dermatology practices, reported 24 pregnancies in OC users receiving antibiotic therapy, most commonly tetracyclines and penicillins. The apparent OC failure rates in clinical surveys were consistent with the expected rates for typical use. 

In pooled results from small populations, oral antibiotics, except for rifampin, did not significantly affect the pharmacokinetics of ethinyl estradiol, levonorgestrel, and norethindrone or reduce the serum concentrations of gonadotropins. However, individual patients were identified who experienced significant decreases in the plasma concentration of these OC components and appeared to ovulate. 

In conclusion, rifampin reduces the effectiveness of OCs. Pharmacokinetic studies of other antibiotics did not show any consistent interaction with OC steroids. However, certain antibiotics, such as tetracycline and penicillin derivatives, have been associated with significant decreases in the plasma concentrations of ethinyl estradiol in individual patients. Therefore, a cautious approach is recommended due to the inability to identify these women in advance.

title: Male Japanese quails with female brains do not show male sexual behaviors.
text:
The brain's sexual differentiation in higher vertebrates is believed to be influenced by gonadal steroid hormones, specifically androgens and estrogens, during embryonic development. This process occurs in the heterogametic sexes, such as males in mammals and females in birds. On the other hand, the brain differentiation in the homogametic sexes is thought to happen naturally, without the need for sex hormones. In gallinaceous birds like the Japanese quail, it is believed that female brain organization occurs through estrogen-dependent demasculinization of a default male brain phenotype.

To investigate this further, we conducted experiments using Japanese quail embryos before their gonads had differentiated. We performed various types of transplantation, including male donor-to-female host (MF), female-to-male (FM), male-to-male (MM), and female-to-female (FF) isotopic, isochronic transplantation of the forebrain primordium. In these brain chimeras, the forebrain, including the hypothalamus, originated solely from the donor cells.

The MM, FF, and MF chimeras all exhibited sexual behavior based on the genetic sex of the host. However, the FM chimeras, which had a genetically female forebrain but genetically male tissues in other parts of the body, showed no mounting behavior and only rudimentary crowing behavior. While all chimeras produced typical levels of steroid hormones during embryonic life, only the FM chimeras were hypogonadal, had abnormally low levels of circulating testosterone in adulthood, and displayed reduced crowing or complete absence of mounting behavior. Additionally, the morphological features of the medial preoptic nucleus, a sexually dimorphic brain area, were not male-like in FM males.

These findings indicate that there is an inherent, genetically determined component within the brain that influences the production of sex-specific gonadal hormones in adulthood. This calls for a reassessment of the mechanisms involved in brain sexual differentiation in other higher vertebrate species.

title: DNA joint dependence of pol X family polymerase action in nonhomologous end joining.
text:
The repair process known as nonhomologous end-joining (NHEJ) is responsible for directly rejoining DNA double strand breaks (DSBs). In order for accurate NHEJ to occur, nucleases and polymerases are necessary to assist when the terminal bases of the DSB are damaged. However, these same enzymes can also contribute to imprecise rejoining and the joining of incompatible ends, which can lead to mutagenic events. Previous research has indicated that the Pol X family polymerase Pol4 is required for certain NHEJ events that involve gap filling in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, although not all events require its presence.

In this study, we conducted a systematic analysis of DSB end configurations and discovered that the presence of gaps on both strands and the polarity of overhangs are the main factors that determine whether Pol4 is necessary for a joint to be repaired. DSBs with 3'-overhangs and gaps on each strand heavily relied on Pol4 for repair, while DSBs with 5'-overhangs of the same sequence did not require its presence. Interestingly, Pol4 was not needed when 3'-overhangs only contained a gap on one strand. Additionally, Pol4 was equally necessary for 3'-overhangs of all lengths within the NHEJ-dependent range, but was not essential outside of this range, indicating its specificity to NHEJ.

The absence of Pol4 did not impact the rejoining of DSBs that utilized a recessed microhomology or DSBs with 5'-hydroxyls but no gap. Finally, we found that mammalian Pol X polymerases were able to complement a pol4 mutation in a differential manner depending on the structure of the joint, suggesting that these polymerases can participate in yeast NHEJ with distinct properties.

title: ABC of burns. Introduction.
text: Burns are a devastating condition that affects patients physically and psychologically. It can occur at any age and is a problem worldwide. Even a small burn can cause severe pain, but larger burns have long-lasting effects, both visible and invisible. Medical and paramedical staff face diverse challenges in managing burn injuries, requiring a multidisciplinary approach. This series aims to provide an overview of burn injuries for healthcare workers in both hospital and non-hospital settings. The accompanying image shows a child with extensive burns who required intensive care and treatment, but ultimately made a good recovery.

title: DNA methylation is a critical cell-intrinsic determinant of astrocyte differentiation in the fetal brain.
text: The activation of a transcription factor called STAT3 plays a crucial role in the differentiation of astrocytes, which occurs late in brain development. Our research demonstrates that astrocytes, as indicated by the expression of glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), do not originate from neuroepithelial cells on embryonic day (E) 11.5, even when STAT3 is activated. This is in contrast to E14.5 neuroepithelial cells. We have observed that a specific CpG dinucleotide within a STAT3 binding element in the GFAP promoter is heavily methylated in E11.5 neuroepithelial cells. However, this CpG site becomes demethylated in cells that are responsive to the activation signal of STAT3, resulting in the expression of GFAP. The methylation of this CpG site prevents STAT3 from binding to the element. Based on our findings, we propose that the methylation of a gene promoter that is specific to a particular cell type is a critical event in regulating the determination of cell lineages during brain development.

title: DNMT1 Inhibition Reprograms Pancreatic Cancer Stem Cells via Upregulation of the miR-17-92 Cluster.
text: The hierarchical organization of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and other carcinomas involves cancer stem cells (CSC) at the top, driving tumor progression, metastasis, and chemoresistance. Despite sharing the same genetic background as non-CSC, we propose that differences in epigenetics explain the significant functional disparities between these two cell populations. Epigenetic mechanisms, like DNA methylation, play a crucial role in maintaining pluripotency and regulating stem cell differentiation. However, the role of DNA methylation in pancreatic CSC remains unclear. In this study, we examined the genome-wide DNA methylation profile of PDAC CSC and assessed the importance of DNA methyltransferases for CSC maintenance and tumorigenicity.
