Through high-throughput methylation analysis, we found that sorted CSCs exhibit higher levels of DNA methylation, regardless of the heterogeneity or polyclonality of the CSC populations within the tumors studied. Mechanistically, CSCs expressed higher levels of DNMT1 compared to non-CSCs. Targeting DNMT1 in CSCs, either through pharmacological or genetic means, reduced their self-renewal ability and in vivo tumorigenic potential, suggesting DNMT1 as a potential therapeutic target for CSCs. This inhibitory effect was partially mediated by the epigenetic reactivation of previously silenced miRNAs, particularly the miR-17-92 cluster. Overall, our findings highlight the importance of DNA methylation in CSC biology and provide a rationale for developing epigenetic modulators to target CSC plasticity and improve the prognosis of PDAC patients.

title: Mutation spectrum in the nephrin gene (NPHS1) in congenital nephrotic syndrome.
text: Congenital nephrotic syndrome, known as Finnish type (CNF or NPHS1), is a hereditary condition characterized by excessive protein in the urine and the development of nephrotic syndrome shortly after birth. While the disease is most prevalent in Finland, cases have also been identified in other populations. The underlying cause of CNF is mutations in the nephrin gene, which plays a crucial role in the glomerular ultrafilter and the podocyte slit diaphragm. To date, a total of 30 mutations in the nephrin gene have been reported in individuals with congenital nephrotic syndrome worldwide. In the Finnish population, two primary mutations have been identified, accounting for over 94% of all mutations in Finland. In non-Finnish patients, the mutations primarily consist of missense mutations, but also include nonsense and splice site mutations, as well as deletions and insertions. This mutation update provides a comprehensive overview of previously reported nephrin mutations and introduces 20 newly discovered mutations identified in our laboratory.

title: The HSA domain binds nuclear actin-related proteins to regulate chromatin-remodeling ATPases
text: The primary binding platform for nuclear actin-related proteins (ARPs) and actin is identified as the helicase-SANT–associated (HSA) domain. The HSA domains from various chromatin remodelers (RSC, yeast SWI-SNF, human SWI-SNF, SWR1, and INO80) or modifiers (NuA4) can reconstitute their respective ARP–ARP or ARP–actin modules. In the case of RSC, the HSA domain is located on the catalytic ATPase subunit Sth1. The presence of Sth1 HSA is crucial for its function in vivo, and its absence leads to the specific loss of ARPs and a moderate decrease in ATPase activity. Through genetic selections for arp suppressors, gain-of-function mutations in two new domains in Sth1, namely the post-HSA domain and protrusion 1, were discovered. These domains are essential for RSC function in vivo but not for ARP association. In summary, the role of the HSA domain is defined, and evidence is provided for a regulatory relationship involving the ARP–HSA module and two new conserved functional domains found in remodeler ATPases containing ARPs.

title: Increased dendritic complexity and axonal length in cultured mouse cortical neurons overexpressing methyl-CpG-binding protein MeCP2
text: Loss-of-function mutations in the gene that encodes the methyl DNA-binding factor MeCP2 are responsible for causing Rett syndrome. In Rett patients, there is a decrease in brain mass and neuronal complexity. To investigate whether MeCP2 has a direct impact on the morphological complexity of developing neurons, we conducted experiments. Our findings indicate that cultured mouse neurons that overexpress MeCP2beta (MECP2A) exhibit more intricate morphologies, with longer axonal and dendritic processes, as well as an increased number of axonal and dendritic terminal endings. Subsequently, we examined whether overexpressing a mutant form of MeCP2beta, which lacks its carboxyl terminus, would produce the same effects. Interestingly, while neurons overexpressing this mutant did not enhance the elongation of axonal and dendritic processes, the complexity of their axonal and dendritic processes remained significantly elevated. Overall, these results support the hypothesis that MeCP2 directly regulates the maturation of neurons and/or synaptogenesis. Furthermore, they provide evidence that MeCP2 may influence the elongation of neurites and the branching of processes through distinct mechanisms.

title: Folate affects apoptosis in human trophoblastic cells.
text: The study investigated the impact of folate deficiency on apoptosis in human cytotrophoblastic cells. Apoptosis levels were measured in these cells after being cultured in three different mediums: 1. a control medium, 2. a folate-free medium, and 3. a folate-free medium supplemented with 10% fetal calf serum. The results showed that apoptosis rates were significantly higher in cells cultured in mediums 2 and 3 compared to those in the control medium (P<0.02 and P<0.03, respectively). Therefore, it can be concluded that human cytotrophoblastic cells experience a notable increase in apoptosis when cultured in a folate-free medium. This finding suggests a potential link between folate deficiency and pregnancy complications.

title: Role of KRAS and EGFR as biomarkers of response to erlotinib in National Cancer Institute of Canada Clinical Trials Group Study BR.21.
text:
The purpose of this study was to assess the impact of KRAS and epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) genotype on the response to erlotinib treatment in the BR.21 trial, which was a placebo-controlled trial. A total of 206 tumors were analyzed for KRAS mutation, 204 tumors for EGFR mutation, and 159 tumors for EGFR gene copy using fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH). Two highly sensitive techniques were used to reanalyze EGFR deletion/mutation in samples with 5% to 10% tumor cellularity. KRAS mutation was analyzed through direct sequencing. 

The results showed that 15% of patients had KRAS mutations, 17% had EGFR exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R mutations, and 38% had high EGFR gene copy (FISH positive). The response rates were 10% for wild-type KRAS and 5% for mutant KRAS, 7% for wild-type EGFR and 27% for mutant EGFR, and 5% for EGFR FISH-negative and 21% for FISH-positive patients. These differences in response rates were statistically significant. 

Patients with wild-type KRAS and EGFR FISH positivity had a significant survival benefit from erlotinib therapy. However, patients with mutant KRAS, wild-type EGFR, mutant EGFR, and EGFR FISH negativity did not show a significant survival benefit from erlotinib therapy. In multivariate analysis, only EGFR FISH-positive status was found to be prognostic for poorer survival and predictive of differential survival benefit from erlotinib. 

In conclusion, EGFR mutations and high copy number are predictive of response to erlotinib. EGFR FISH is the strongest prognostic marker and a significant predictive marker of differential survival benefit from erlotinib.

title: Immune dysregulation in major depression: a critical review of existing evidence.
text: The connection between depression and immune dysregulation is now widely accepted. However, it remains unclear whether this immune dysregulation contributes to the development of major depression or if it makes depressed individuals more susceptible to immune-related disorders. This article provides a thorough examination of the existing evidence on immune dysregulation in major depression, including changes in leucocyte trafficking, lymphocyte function, and markers of immune activation. Additionally, potential factors that may contribute to immune dysregulation in major depression are briefly discussed. Lastly, the relationship between major depression and various medical conditions such as infection, allergy and autoimmune disorders, cardiovascular diseases, cancer, and AIDS is critically evaluated.

title: Regulation of E2Fs and senescence by PML nuclear bodies.
text: The protein PML, which suppresses tumor growth, controls the processes of cellular senescence and terminal differentiation. These processes involve a permanent exit from the cell cycle. Our research reveals that PML induces this permanent cell cycle exit and activates p53 and senescence by recruiting E2F transcription factors and retinoblastoma (Rb) proteins to PML nuclear bodies. These bodies are rich in heterochromatin proteins and protein phosphatase 1α. By blocking the functions of the Rb protein family or reintroducing E2Fs to cells expressing PML, we can reverse their defects in E2F-dependent gene expression and cell proliferation, thereby inhibiting the senescent phenotype. In benign prostatic hyperplasia, a neoplastic disease that exhibits senescence-like characteristics, PML is up-regulated and forms nuclear bodies. However, prostate cancers rarely display PML bodies. This newly identified PML/Rb/E2F pathway may help differentiate between benign tumors and cancers. Additionally, it suggests that E2F target genes could be potential targets for inducing senescence in human tumors.

title: The International Classification of Headache Disorders.
text: A society without laws can be compared to a collection of medical disorders that lack a proper classification system and diagnostic criteria. This absence leads to confusion and disorder, with the potential for disastrous consequences. Hence, the International Classification of Headache Disorders (ICHD) is considered a groundbreaking achievement in the field of headache medicine, perhaps the most significant in the past half-century. The ICHD establishes a logical and hierarchical framework, identifying and categorizing over a hundred different types of headaches. Moreover, it provides explicit diagnostic criteria for each listed disorder. The ICHD swiftly gained universal acceptance, with minimal criticism compared to other disease classification systems. In the two decades since its initial publication, headache research has experienced remarkable progress, despite limited resources allocated to this endeavor. In conclusion, the ICHD has achieved widespread international acceptance and significantly facilitated both clinical research and care in the realm of headache medicine.

title: Call to Develop a Standard Acquisition Charge Model for Kidney Paired Donation
text: We are suggesting the implementation of a Medicare Demonstration Project that aims to establish a standard acquisition charge for kidney paired donation. This is necessary because Medicare and commercial insurance companies are not currently able to directly cover the costs associated with living donors, specifically those intended for the transplantation of a beneficiary who is insured by a different provider. In the past, there were similar limitations in the recovery and placement of deceased donor organs until the 1970s, when organ procurement organizations were given the authority to act as financial intermediaries. They would cover the upfront recovery expenses for deceased donor kidneys without knowing the identity of the recipient. Similarly, kidney paired donation requires the evaluation of living donors before a recipient can be identified. This process involves additional financial barriers such as tissue typing, crossmatching, and transportation of living donors or their kidneys. Additionally, the organizations responsible for identifying and coordinating kidney paired donation transplantation also incur administrative expenses that need to be reimbursed, similar to organ procurement organizations. In order to make kidney paired donation more accessible to a larger number of patients, we propose a reimbursement model that mirrors the successful strategy used for over 30 years to cover the costs of deceased donor solid organ transplantation in the United States.

title: Oxidant stress promotes disease by activating CaMKII.
text: The activation of CaMKII occurs through the oxidation of methionine residues located in the regulatory domain. Recent studies have implicated oxidized CaMKII (ox-CaMKII) in the development of cardiovascular and pulmonary diseases as well as cancer. This comprehensive review examines the existing evidence regarding the involvement of ox-CaMKII in disease, identifies important gaps in our understanding, and proposes new avenues for further investigation.

title: Genetic diagnosis and prognosis of Alzheimer's disease: challenges and opportunities.
text: Alzheimer's disease (AD), the most prevalent form of dementia in western societies, is a complex disease with diverse pathological and clinical characteristics, influenced by genetic factors. Recent advancements in high-throughput genome technologies have revolutionized our understanding of the genetic basis of AD susceptibility. These technologies enable the rapid analysis of millions of genetic variations in large populations, leading to the identification of over 20 disease-associated regions through genome-wide association, whole-exome sequencing, and whole-genome sequencing studies. These findings shed light on the molecular mechanisms underlying AD development and offer potential targets for novel therapeutic interventions. This review article discusses the challenges and opportunities associated with utilizing genomic information for the diagnosis and prognosis of AD.

title: WNT5A regulates adipose tissue angiogenesis via antiangiogenic VEGF-A165b in obese humans.
text: Experimental studies have indicated that WNT5A, a protein associated with metabolic dysfunction in obesity, is a proinflammatory secreted protein. The impaired angiogenesis in fat depots has been linked to the development of adipose tissue capillary rarefaction, hypoxia, inflammation, and metabolic dysfunction. Our recent research has shown that the impaired adipose tissue angiogenesis is connected to the overexpression of the antiangiogenic factor VEGF-A165b in both human fat and the systemic circulation. In this study, we hypothesized that the upregulation of WNT5A is associated with angiogenic dysfunction and investigated its role in regulating VEGF-A165b expression in human obesity. We obtained subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissue samples from 38 obese individuals during planned bariatric surgery and analyzed the protein expression of VEGF-A165b and WNT5A using Western blot analysis. We found a strong correlation between VEGF-A165b expression and WNT5A protein in both subcutaneous and visceral fat. In subcutaneous adipose tissue, where angiogenic capacity is higher than in the visceral depot, the addition of exogenous human recombinant WNT5A increased VEGF-A165b expression in both whole adipose tissue and isolated vascular endothelial cell fractions. This increase was associated with a significant reduction in angiogenic capillary sprout formation in human fat pad explants. Furthermore, the recombinant WNT5A also increased the secretion of soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1, a negative regulator of angiogenesis, in the sprout media. However, the use of a VEGF-A165b-neutralizing antibody and secreted frizzled-related protein 5, which acts as a decoy receptor for WNT5A, improved capillary sprout formation and reduced soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 production. Our findings demonstrate a significant regulatory connection between WNT5A and antiangiogenic VEGF-A165b in the adipose tissue of obese individuals, which is associated with angiogenic dysfunction. The elevated expression of WNT5A in obesity may act as a negative regulator of angiogenesis. In summary, our study highlights the role of WNT5A in negatively regulating adipose tissue angiogenesis through VEGF-A165b in human obesity.

title: At least 1400 base pairs of 5'-flanking DNA is required for the correct expression of the HO gene in yeast.
text:
The aim of this study is to examine the factors that influence HO gene transcription in homothallic yeast cells. Specifically, the researchers investigate the impact of cell type (a, alpha, and a/alpha), cell age (mother or daughter), and the cell cycle on HO transcription. To do this, they replace the genomic DNA with in vitro mutated copies and analyze the resulting sequences.

The researchers find that a region known as URS1, located between -1000 and 1400, is crucial for transcription. Additionally, they identify a "TATA"-like region at -90 that is also necessary for transcription. Interestingly, the 900 bp of DNA that separates URS1 from the "TATA" box is not required for transcription or for a/alpha repression and some level of mother/daughter control. However, this region is essential for proper cell cycle control.

title: Inflammation and its role in neuroprotection, axonal regeneration and functional recovery after spinal cord injury.
text: Injuries to the central nervous system (CNS) lead to inflammation within the brain and spinal cord, as well as activation of the body's immune system. This immune response can worsen damage to the nerves and also trigger processes that aid in tissue repair. Although we still have much to learn about how these different functions are regulated, there is growing interest in using immune-based treatments for trauma-related conditions. This article will explore the intricate nature of post-traumatic neuroinflammation, with a specific focus on the spinal cord. Furthermore, we will discuss the current therapies that aim to target the cascades of neuroinflammation.

title: Order of intron removal influences multiple splice outcomes, including a two-exon skip, in a COL5A1 acceptor-site mutation that results in abnormal pro-alpha1(V) N-propeptides and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome type I.
text:
Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDS) type I, also known as the classical variety, is a connective-tissue disorder that is inherited dominantly and genetically heterogeneous. Several individuals with EDS type I have been found to have mutations in the COL5A1 and COL5A2 genes, which are responsible for encoding type V collagen. These mutations typically affect either the triple-helical domain of the protein or the expression of one allele of COL5A1.

In our study, we discovered a new mutation (IVS4-2A-->G) in the N-propeptide-encoding region of COL5A1 in a patient with EDS type I. This mutation had a complex effect on the outcome. The major product resulted in the skipping of both exons 5 and 6, while a small amount of other products skipped only exon 5, and an even smaller amount used cryptic acceptor sites within exon 5. Importantly, all of these products were in frame.

The abnormal N-propeptides of pro-alpha1(V) chains were secreted and incorporated into the extracellular matrix, leading to significant alterations in collagen fibril structure. The two-exon skip occurred in transcripts where intron 5 was removed quickly compared to introns 4 and 6, resulting in a large composite exon that could be entirely skipped. Transcripts that skipped only exon 5 were derived from those where intron 6 was removed before intron 5. The use of cryptic acceptor sites in exon 5 happened in transcripts where intron 4 was removed after introns 5 and 6.

These findings indicate that the order of intron removal plays a crucial role in the outcome of splice-site mutations. They also provide a model that explains why a single splice site mutation can lead to multiple products.

title: Kruppel-like factor KLF10 targets transforming growth factor-beta1 to regulate CD4(+)CD25(-) T cells and T regulatory cells.
text: The role of CD4(+)CD25(+) regulatory T cells (T regs) in maintaining self-tolerance and immune suppression is well-established, but the mechanisms governing their development and suppressor function are not fully understood. In this study, we present evidence that Kruppel-like factor 10 (KLF10/TIEG1) is a key regulator of T reg suppressor function and CD4(+)CD25(-) T cell activation through distinct mechanisms involving transforming growth factor (TGF)-beta1 and Foxp3. Overexpression of KLF10 in CD4(+)CD25(-) T cells led to increased expression of both TGF-beta1 and Foxp3, resulting in reduced expression of T-Bet (a Th1 marker) and Gata3 (a Th2 marker). Conversely, CD4(+)CD25(-) T cells lacking KLF10 showed enhanced differentiation along both Th1 and Th2 pathways and produced higher levels of Th1 and Th2 cytokines. Additionally, KLF10(-/-) CD4(+)CD25(-) T cell effectors were not effectively suppressed by wild-type T regs. Surprisingly, KLF10(-/-) T regs exhibited reduced suppressor function, independent of Foxp3 expression, due to decreased expression and production of TGF-beta1. However, this effect was completely reversed by exogenous treatment with TGF-beta1. Mechanistic studies revealed that KLF10 can activate both TGF-beta1 and Foxp3 promoters in response to TGF-beta1, suggesting a positive feedback loop that may contribute to cell-intrinsic control of T cell activation. Furthermore, KLF10(-/-) CD4(+)CD25(-) T cells promoted atherosclerosis by approximately 2-fold in ApoE(-/-)/scid/scid mice, characterized by increased accumulation of leukocytes and peripheral pro-inflammatory cytokines. Overall, our findings highlight the critical role of KLF10 in regulating TGF-beta1 in CD4(+)CD25(-) T cells and T regs, and its involvement in atherosclerotic lesion formation in mice.

title: Synchrotron radiation solution X-ray scattering study of the pH dependence of the quaternary structure of yeast pyruvate decarboxylase.
text: We conducted a study on the pH dependence of the quaternary structure of pyruvate decarboxylase from yeast within the pH range of 6.2 to 8.4. Our findings revealed an equilibrium point around pH 7.5, where tetramers and dimers coexist. The enzyme's catalytic activity is influenced by the volume fraction of tetramers. This equilibrium serves as an additional regulatory mechanism, alongside substrate activation. If pyruvate accumulates, the pH decreases, leading to an increase in the concentration of the catalytically active tetramer. During X-ray scattering experiments, radiation damage occurs, causing a shift in this equilibrium and the formation of octamers. However, we were able to overcome these effects and analyze them using experimental and data processing methods that can be applied to other radiation-sensitive systems. By utilizing spherical harmonics, we determined the low-resolution shapes of the dimers and tetramers from the scattering curves. Our results indicate that a conformational change takes place in the dimers when tetramers are formed, which aligns with previous circular dichroism measurements.

title: Enhancement of anxiety-like responsiveness to the cannabinoid CB(1) receptor agonist HU-210 following chronic stress.
text: This study aimed to examine the impact of chronic unpredictable stress on the anxiety-like response caused by the cannabinoid receptor agonist HU-210 in the elevated plus maze. Male Long-Evans rats were divided into two groups: unstressed and subjected to a 21-day regimen of chronic unpredictable stress. Afterward, they were further divided into three testing groups (vehicle, 10 and 50 microg/kg of HU-210) and assessed on the elevated plus maze. The results revealed that in unstressed animals, a low dose of HU-210 produced a calming effect, while a high dose induced anxiety. Conversely, in stressed animals, both low and high doses of HU-210 resulted in anxiety. These findings suggest that chronic stress may enhance the responsiveness of cannabinoid receptors or other systems involved in emotional states.

title: Cardiac glycosides inhibit TNF-α/NF-κB signaling by blocking recruitment of TNF receptor-associated death domain to the TNF receptor
text: The potent blocking of the TNF-α/NF-κB signaling pathway by digitoxin and similar cardiac glycoside drugs has led us to investigate the underlying mechanism. Our hypothesis is that a systematic search for selective inhibitory action throughout the pathway may reveal the answer. Our findings indicate that these drugs share a common action, which is to prevent the binding of TNF receptor 1 to TNF receptor-associated death domain in a TNF-α-dependent manner. This effect can be observed in native cells, such as HeLa, as well as in reconstituted systems using HEK293 cells. It appears that all other anti-inflammatory effects of digitoxin on the NF-κB and c-Jun N-terminal kinase pathways stem from the inhibition of this initial upstream signaling event.

title: Zinc supplementation during lactation: effects on maternal status and milk zinc concentrations.
text:
The study aimed to investigate the effects of a zinc supplement on the zinc levels in lactating mothers and their breast milk for a period of at least 7 months. A total of 71 lactating women participated in the study, with 40 receiving a daily 15-mg zinc supplement (ZS group) and 31 receiving a placebo (NZS group). The supplementation or placebo was initiated within 2 weeks after giving birth, and the study followed a double-blind, randomized design.

The average daily zinc intake was 13.0 +/- 3.4 mg for the NZS group and 25.7 +/- 3.9 mg (including the supplement) for the ZS group. The plasma zinc concentrations in the ZS group were significantly higher compared to the NZS group (P = 0.05). Although milk zinc concentrations decreased throughout the study for all participants, the zinc supplementation did not have an impact on these concentrations.

The findings suggest that the dietary zinc intake in the group without supplementation was sufficient to maintain normal zinc levels in both the mothers and their breast milk for at least 7 months of lactation. However, further controlled intervention trials in populations with poorer nutrition are needed to assess the effects of lower zinc intakes on milk zinc concentrations.

title: DMSO as a vehicle for central injections: tests with feeding elicited by norepinephrine injected into the paraventricular nucleus.
text: The use of Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) as a vehicle for central injections is gaining popularity. This study aimed to determine if the vehicle used for solubilizing substances for central injection would affect the stimulatory response to norepinephrine (NE) injected into the paraventricular nucleus (PVN) and its impact on short-term food intake. To assess its suitability, we compared the effects of repeated unilateral injections of NE dissolved in two different vehicles (100% artificial CSF or 75% DMSO, 25% artificial CSF) in separate groups of animals over a 30-day period, with injections every 48 hours. The results showed that NE (40 nmol) significantly increased food intake by approximately sevenfold compared to either vehicle alone, and this effect was similar regardless of whether artificial CSF or 75% DMSO was used as the vehicle. Additionally, the stimulatory effect of NE on feeding remained consistent across multiple tests. These findings suggest that 75% DMSO is a suitable vehicle for delivering NE (and potentially other water-insoluble substances) in small volumes of 0.3 microliters to specific brain regions.

title: Dodecameric structure and ATPase activity of the human TIP48/TIP49 complex.
text:
TIP48 and TIP49 are two closely related and highly conserved proteins found in eukaryotes. They play a crucial role in important pathways that are closely associated with cancer. These proteins are part of chromatin-modifying complexes that are highly conserved. Although they share similarities with a bacterial protein called RuvB, their specific biochemical role and mechanism are still unknown. 

To investigate their activity, recombinant human TIP48 and TIP49 were combined to form a stable complex with a high molecular mass. In vitro testing showed that the formation of the TIP48/TIP49 complex led to a synergistic increase in ATPase activity. However, the presence of single-stranded, double-stranded, or four-way junction DNA did not stimulate ATP hydrolysis, and no DNA helicase or branch migration activity was observed. 

Further analysis revealed that the TIP48/TIP49 complex required both proteins to have ATPase activity, as complexes with catalytic defects in either TIP48 or TIP49 showed no ATPase activity. 

The structure of the TIP48/TIP49 complex was examined using negative stain electron microscopy. The reconstruction showed that the complex consisted of two stacked hexameric rings with C6 symmetry. Interestingly, the top and bottom rings had noticeable structural differences. Additionally, TIP48 was found to form oligomers in the presence of adenine nucleotides, while TIP49 did not. 

These findings suggest that there are biochemical differences between TIP48 and TIP49, which may explain the structural disparities between the two hexameric rings. These differences could be significant for the specialized functions that these proteins perform individually.

title: Associations between work-related factors and specific disorders of the shoulder--a systematic review of the literature.
text:
Our objective was to quantitatively assess the relationship between work-related physical and psychosocial factors and the occurrence of specific shoulder disorders in occupational populations. To achieve this, we conducted a systematic review of the literature on the associations between type of work, physical load factors, and psychosocial aspects at work, and the occurrence of tendinitis of the biceps tendon, rotator cuff tears, subacromial impingement syndrome (SIS), and suprascapular nerve compression. The associations between work factors and shoulder disorders were measured using odds ratio (OR) or relative risk (RR).

The results showed that SIS was associated with force requirements exceeding 10% of maximal voluntary contraction (MVC), lifting weights over 20 kg more than 10 times per day, and high levels of hand force for over 1 hour per day (OR 2.8-4.2). Repetitive movements of the shoulder, repetitive motion of the hand/wrist for over 2 hours per day, hand-arm vibration, and working with the hand above shoulder level were also associated with SIS (OR 1.04-4.7). Additionally, upper-arm flexion of 45 degrees or more for at least 15% of the time (OR 2.43), and a duty cycle of forceful exertions for at least 9% of the time or a duty cycle of forceful pinch for any amount of time (OR 2.66) showed an association with SIS. High psychosocial job demand was also linked to SIS (OR 1.5-3.19).

Jobs in the fish processing industry had the highest risk for both tendinitis of the biceps tendon and SIS (OR 2.28 and 3.38, respectively). Work in a slaughterhouse and as a betel pepper leaf culler were associated with the occurrence of SIS only (OR 5.27 and 4.68, respectively). However, none of the included articles described the association between job title/risk factors and the occurrence of rotator cuff tears or suprascapular nerve compression.

In conclusion, highly repetitive work, forceful exertion, awkward postures, and high psychosocial job demand are all associated with the occurrence of SIS.

title: Altered TCR signaling from geometrically repatterned immunological synapses.
text: The immunological synapse, a specialized junction between cells, is still not fully understood in terms of its formation and function, despite being characterized by large-scale spatial patterns of receptors and signaling molecules. To gain more insight, we conducted experiments using supported bilayer membranes and nanometer-scale structures on the underlying substrate to create geometric constraints on immunological synapse formation. By analyzing the resulting synapses with alternative patterns, we discovered a cause-and-effect relationship between the radial position of T cell receptors (TCRs) and signaling activity. Specifically, TCR microclusters that were mechanically trapped in the outer regions of the synapse exhibited prolonged signaling. These findings support a model of the synapse where the spatial movement of TCRs directly regulates signaling.

title: Molecular regulation of histone H3 trimethylation by COMPASS and the regulation of gene expression.
text: We conducted a comprehensive proteomic screen to investigate the role of the yeast complex COMPASS, which is similar to the human MLL complex, in histone trimethylation. Our findings reveal that both Cps60 and Cps40 components of COMPASS are crucial for the accurate trimethylation of histone H3, but not for the regulation of telomere-associated gene silencing. When Cps60 is absent from purified COMPASS, it can only perform mono- and dimethylation, but not trimethylation of H3(K4). Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) studies demonstrate that the loss of COMPASS subunits necessary for histone trimethylation does not impact the localization of Set1 to chromatin in the tested genes. Overall, our results indicate that multiple components of COMPASS are required for proper histone H3 trimethylation and the regulation of telomere-associated gene expression, highlighting the diverse roles of different forms of histone methylation by COMPASS.

title: Mitosis-specific anchoring of gamma tubulin complexes by pericentrin controls spindle organization and mitotic entry.
text: The primary function of centrosomes is to nucleate microtubules, with this process being mediated by gamma tubulin ring complexes (gamma TuRCs). However, there is limited knowledge regarding the molecules responsible for anchoring these complexes to centrosomes. In this study, we demonstrate that the coiled-coil protein pericentrin plays a crucial role in anchoring gamma TuRCs at spindle poles through its interaction with gamma tubulin complex proteins 2 and 3 (GCP2/3). Silencing pericentrin in somatic cells using small interfering RNAs disrupted the localization of gamma tubulin and the organization of spindles during mitosis, but had no impact on gamma tubulin localization or microtubule organization during interphase. Similarly, overexpressing the GCP2/3 binding domain of pericentrin disrupted the natural interaction between pericentrin and gamma TuRCs, leading to disturbances in astral microtubules and spindle bipolarity. When introduced to Xenopus mitotic extracts, this domain caused the separation of gamma TuRCs from centrosomes, inhibited the assembly of microtubule asters, and induced the rapid disassembly of preassembled asters. All observed phenotypes were significantly reduced in a pericentrin mutant with weakened GCP2/3 binding, and were specific to mitotic centrosomal asters, as there was minimal effect on interphase asters or asters assembled through the Ran-mediated centrosome-independent pathway. Furthermore, silencing or overexpressing pericentrin resulted in G2/antephase arrest followed by apoptosis in many cell types, although not all. In conclusion, the anchoring of gamma tubulin complexes at centrosomes in mitotic cells by pericentrin is essential for proper spindle organization, and the loss of this anchoring mechanism triggers a checkpoint response that prevents mitotic entry and leads to apoptotic cell death.

title: High levels of viral replication contrast with only transient changes in CD4(+) and CD8(+) cell numbers during the early phase of experimental infection with simian immunodeficiency virus SIVmnd-1 in Mandrillus sphinx.
text: The early stages of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infections are believed to indicate the ability of the host to control the infection. We conducted a study on the early virus and host parameters during the initial phase of simian immunodeficiency virus (SIVmnd-1) nonpathogenic infection in its natural host, the Mandrillus sphinx (mandrill). Four mandrills were intentionally infected with a primary strain of SIVmnd-1 obtained from a naturally infected mandrill. Additionally, two uninfected mandrills were observed for comparison. Blood and lymph nodes were collected at three time points prior to infection, twice a week during the first month, and at days 60, 180, and 360 after infection. Anti-SIVmnd-1 antibodies were detected between days 28 and 32 after infection. There were no signs of elevated temperature or increased lymph node size. The viral load in plasma reached its peak between days 7 and 10 after infection, ranging from 2 x 10(6) to 2 x 10(8) RNA equivalents/ml. Viremia then decreased by 10- to 1,000-fold, stabilizing between days 30 and 60 after infection. The viral levels during the chronic phase of infection were similar to those in the naturally infected mandrill donor, at 2 x 10(5) RNA equivalents/ml. The numbers and percentages of CD4(+) cells in blood and lymph nodes slightly decreased (<10%) during the primary infection, while CD8(+) cell numbers experienced a temporary increase. However, all values returned to pre-infection levels by day 30 after infection. The numbers or percentages of CD8(+) cells in peripheral blood and lymph nodes did not increase throughout the one-year follow-up period. In conclusion, SIVmnd-1 has the ability to replicate rapidly and extensively in mandrills. Despite high levels of viremia, the numbers of CD4(+) and CD8(+) cells remained stable during the post-acute phase of infection, raising questions about the susceptibility of mandrill T cells to activation and/or cell death in response to SIVmnd-1 infection in vivo.

title: Vascular endothelial growth factor stimulates bone repair by promoting angiogenesis and bone turnover.
text: During the process of fracture repair, various growth factors are expressed in specific patterns over time and space. One of these factors, known as vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), is particularly intriguing due to its ability to stimulate the formation of new blood vessels (angiogenesis). In order to determine the importance of VEGF in bone repair, we conducted experiments using a unique mouse model. We inhibited VEGF activity during both the healing of secondary bone fractures through cartilage formation (endochondral ossification) and the direct repair of bone (intramembranous ossification). By treating the mice with a soluble VEGF receptor that neutralizes its effects, we observed a decrease in angiogenesis, bone formation, and the mineralization of the callus in femoral fractures. Additionally, inhibiting VEGF had a significant impact on the healing of a tibial cortical bone defect, which supports our finding that VEGF plays a direct role in the differentiation of osteoblasts. In separate experiments, we found that the introduction of exogenous VEGF enhanced the formation of blood vessels, ossification, and the maturation of new bone in femur fractures of mice, as well as the bridging of a segmental gap defect in the radius of rabbits. Our findings at specific time points throughout the healing process highlight the role of VEGF in different types of bone formation (endochondral vs. intramembranous ossification) and in both skeletal development and bone repair. The positive responses to exogenous VEGF observed in two different model systems and species suggest that a slow-release formulation of VEGF, applied directly to the site of bone damage, could potentially be an effective therapy for promoting bone repair in humans.

title: Psychiatric comorbidity in chronic daily headache.
text: According to clinical evidence, there is a link between psychopathologies and chronic daily headache (CDH), with previous studies mainly focusing on migraine. In order to examine this connection, we conducted a study using the DSM-IIIR criteria, involving a group of 88 patients (18 males, 70 females) who were affected by CDH, with an average duration of 7.4 +/- 8.7 years. Our findings revealed that 90% of this population had a psychiatric disorder. The most common diagnosis was a combination of anxiety and mood disorders. The coexistence of psychiatric disorders and headaches has significant implications for treatment strategies.

title: An Expanded Oct4 Interaction Network: Implications for Stem Cell Biology, Development, and Disease
text: Oct4, a transcription factor, plays a crucial role in determining the identity and reprogramming of embryonic stem cells. Understanding its interactions with other proteins can shed light on how the pluripotent state is established and controlled. In this study, we have identified a significantly expanded group of proteins that bind to Oct4 in mouse embryonic stem cells. These proteins include regulators of gene expression and modulators of Oct4's function. Interestingly, half of these partners are regulated by Oct4 itself or other transcription factors involved in stem cell biology, while one-third of them show significant changes in expression during cell differentiation. It is worth noting that most of the Oct4-associated proteins studied so far have been found to cause early lethal phenotypes when mutated. Additionally, some of the human counterparts of these proteins are associated with inherited developmental disorders or are known to be causative factors in cancer. The Oct4 interactome serves as a valuable resource for unraveling the mechanisms underlying Oct4's function, gaining insights into pluripotency and development, and identifying potential factors involved in reprogramming.

title: Reproductive and lifestyle determinants of anti-Müllerian hormone in a large population-based study.
text:
CONTEXT: Anti-müllerian hormone (AMH) is a marker used in clinical practice to assess ovarian reserve. However, there is a lack of large-scale studies examining the factors that influence AMH levels.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the impact of reproductive and lifestyle factors on AMH levels in a large population-based cohort of women.

DESIGN: A cross-sectional study was conducted, and age-specific AMH percentiles were calculated using a statistical model called CG-LMS. The study included women from the general community who were participating in the Doetinchem Cohort study.

PARTICIPANTS: A total of 2,320 premenopausal women were included in the study.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: The study examined how female reproductive and lifestyle factors affected shifts in age-specific AMH percentiles.

RESULTS: Women who were using oral contraceptives (OC), had menstrual cycle irregularities, or were pregnant had significantly lower age-specific AMH percentiles compared to women with regular menstrual cycles. The decrease in percentiles was 11 for OC users, 11 for women with cycle irregularities, and 17 for pregnant women (P < .0001 for all). Age at menarche and age at first childbirth did not have a significant association with age-specific AMH percentiles. However, higher parity was associated with a 2 percentile increase in age-specific AMH (P = .02). Among the lifestyle factors examined, current smoking was associated with a 4 percentile decrease in age-specific AMH (P = .02), regardless of the amount smoked. Body mass index, waist circumference, alcohol consumption, physical exercise, and socioeconomic status did not show a significant association with age-specific AMH percentiles.

CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the influence of reproductive and lifestyle factors on age-specific AMH levels. The decrease in AMH levels associated with OC use and smoking appears to be reversible, as it was only observed in current users. These findings emphasize the importance of considering these factors when interpreting AMH levels in a clinical setting and making decisions about patient management based on AMH.

title: Primary care and health insurance among women released from New York City jails.
text: The study examined the factors related to primary care usage and health insurance coverage among 511 women who were released from jail in New York City between 1997 and 2001. One year after their release, approximately half of the participants reported using primary care services (47%) and having health insurance coverage (56%). The presence of diabetes, asthma, or depression did not make it more likely for the women to utilize primary care or have health insurance coverage. However, those who received public benefits, had health insurance coverage, had moderate social support, avoided illegal activities, and were HIV positive were more likely to use primary care services. Health insurance coverage was associated with receiving public benefits, being hospitalized, using primary care services, and avoiding re-arrest. The study revealed that a majority of women leaving jail, even those with chronic illnesses, did not have access to primary care. These findings emphasize the importance of planning for continuity of care from correctional facilities to the community and suggest that providing health benefits and social support can help facilitate this process.

title: The effects of prion protein proteolysis and disaggregation on the strain properties of hamster scrapie.
text: Different strains of native mammalian prions have distinct clinical, pathological, and biochemical characteristics. The diversity of prion strains is linked to variations in the conformation of PrP(Sc), but it is still unclear which physical properties of PrP(Sc) molecules are necessary to determine the phenotypes of mammalian prion strains. In this study, we tested prion-infected brain samples from three different hamster scrapie strains by subjecting them to either proteinase K digestion or sonication, and then injected the modified samples into healthy hamsters. The results showed that the specific clinical features and neuropathological profiles of the injected animals were not affected by either treatment. Similarly, the strain-specific biochemical characteristics of the PrP(Sc) molecules, such as their electrophoretic mobility, glycoform composition, conformational stability, and susceptibility to protease digestion, remained unchanged after proteolysis or sonication of the original samples. These findings suggest that the infectious properties of native prion strains are not altered by disaggregation of PrP(Sc), and that the N-domain (approximately residues 23-90) of the protease-resistant PrP(Sc) molecules or protease-sensitive PrP(Sc) molecules are not required to maintain these properties.

title: Methylation of histone H3 lysine-79 by Dot1p plays multiple roles in the response to UV damage in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
text: Proteins have been discovered to have dual roles in repairing UV damaged DNA and silencing heterochromatin in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Specifically, the factors involved in the methylation of lysine-79 of histone H3 by Dot1p have been linked to both processes, suggesting a two-fold function for this modification. Our research reveals that a dot1 null mutation and a histone H3 point mutation at lysine-79 lead to increased sensitivity to UV radiation, indicating the importance of lysine-79 methylation in efficient repair of UV damage. Epistasis analysis between dot1 and various UV repair genes demonstrates that lysine-79 methylation plays overlapping roles in nucleotide excision, post-replication, recombination repair pathways, and RAD9-mediated checkpoint function. Conversely, epistasis analysis with the H3 lysine-79 point mutation suggests that the substitution of lysine with glutamic acid specifically affects nucleotide excision repair and post-replication repair pathways, implying that this allele disrupts only a subset of lysine-79 methylation functions. Overall, these findings highlight the distinct and separable roles of histone H3 lysine-79 methylation in the response to UV damage, potentially coordinating the various repair processes.

title: Unmet need for personal assistance with activities of daily living among older adults.
text: The purpose of this study was to examine the occurrence, factors, and negative effects of not receiving sufficient personal assistance for daily activities among older adults. The researchers analyzed data from the 1994 National Health Interview Survey's Supplement on Aging, which was representative of individuals aged 70 years and above who were not living in institutions. The results showed that 20.7% of those who required assistance with one or more activities of daily living (ADLs) reported not receiving adequate help, which equated to an estimated 629,000 individuals. The prevalence of unmet need varied for different ADLs, ranging from 10.2% for eating to 20.1% for transferring. Factors such as lower household income, multiple difficulties with ADLs, and living alone were associated with a higher likelihood of having unmet needs. Additionally, almost half of those with unmet needs reported experiencing negative consequences, such as being unable to eat when hungry, due to their lack of assistance. These findings suggest that targeted efforts should be made to reduce the occurrence and negative effects of unmet need for assistance with ADLs among elderly individuals.

title: Multi-stage chemical carcinogenesis in mouse skin: Fundamentals and applications
text: The study of epithelial carcinogenesis and the evaluation of modifying factors have relied on the chemical induction of tumors in mouse skin for over 60 years. In the traditional two-stage skin carcinogenesis model, the initiation phase involves applying a sub-carcinogenic dose of a carcinogen. This is followed by repeated treatment with a tumor-promoting agent to elicit tumor development. The initiation protocol can be completed within 1-3 hours, depending on the number of mice used. The promotion phase requires twice weekly treatments (1-2 hours) and once weekly tumor palpation (1-2 hours) throughout the study. By following this protocol, a highly reproducible papilloma burden can be expected within 10-20 weeks, with some tumors progressing to squamous cell carcinomas within 20-50 weeks. Unlike complete skin carcinogenesis, the two-stage model allows for a greater yield of premalignant lesions and separates the initiation and promotion phases.

title: Preventing deaths by drowning in children in the United Kingdom: have we made progress in 10 years? Population based incidence study.
text: The collection of detailed information on drowning in children is not a regular practice for national statistical offices. Limited studies have been conducted in the United Kingdom, and none have specifically examined British children abroad. In 1988-9, two of the authors (AMK and JRS) gathered data from national statistical offices, police forces (Royal Life Saving Society), and a press cutting service (Royal Society for Prevention of Accidents) to conduct a thorough analysis of child drowning deaths. This analysis revealed that 149 children had drowned in the United Kingdom during 1998-9. It also highlighted the need for a safety agenda, focusing on young children in garden ponds and pools, as well as older children swimming without supervision. In the past decade, efforts have been made to improve children's safety in water, particularly in swimming. We obtained similar information for 1998-9 to identify any changes that have occurred.

title: Hypoxic heterogeneity in human tumors: EF5 binding, vasculature, necrosis, and proliferation.
text: We conducted a study to assess the levels and distribution of hypoxia in 31 human tumors using fluorescent immunohistochemical detection of binding by the 2-nitroimidazole, EF5. Our findings revealed that hypoxia is not a uniform characteristic of human tumors, but rather a heterogeneous property. In most cases, necrosis was observed in close proximity to the areas with the highest level of binding within an individual patient's tumor. However, it was also observed that hypoxia can occur without necrosis. Among the tumors examined, the most common relationship between blood vessels (PECAM/CD31) and EF5 staining indicated diffusion-limited hypoxia, while acute hypoxia was infrequent. Within a specific patient's tumor, there was an inverse correlation between regions of proliferation (Ki-67) and regions of hypoxia. However, when analyzing these parameters across a group of patients, the absence of proliferation did not reliably predict the presence of hypoxia. The relationships between hypoxia and other biological endpoints are intricate, but within the spatial relationships of a given tumor, they align with established physiological principles. Therefore, our data highlight the fact that the relationships between hypoxia and other biological parameters can vary between patients. Necrosis, proliferation, and blood vessel distribution cannot serve as reliable predictors of the level or presence of hypoxia in an individual patient's tumor.

title: The Sp1-like protein BTEB3 inhibits transcription via the basic transcription element box by interacting with mSin3A and HDAC-1 co-repressors and competing with Sp1.
text: Sp1-like proteins possess three conserved zinc finger motifs at their C-terminus, which bind to GC-rich sequences in the promoters of various genes crucial for maintaining the balance of mammalian cells. These proteins can function as either transcriptional activators or repressors. While there is substantial knowledge about the molecular mechanisms of Sp1-like activators, little is understood about the mechanisms of repressor proteins. In this study, we present the functional analysis of BTEB3, a widely expressed Sp1-like transcriptional repressor. Through GAL4 assays, we demonstrate that the N-terminus of BTEB3 contains regions that act as direct repressor domains. Immunoprecipitation assays reveal that BTEB3 interacts with the co-repressor mSin3A and the histone deacetylase protein HDAC-1. Gel shift assays demonstrate that BTEB3 specifically binds to the BTE site, a well-known GC-rich DNA element, with a similar affinity to Sp1. Reporter and gel shift assays conducted in Chinese hamster ovary cells show that BTEB3 can also repress gene expression by competing with Sp1 for BTE binding. Therefore, the characterization of BTEB3 expands the group of BTEB-like members within the Sp1 family involved in transcriptional repression. Additionally, our findings suggest a repression mechanism for BTEB3, involving direct repression by the N-terminus through interaction with mSin3A and HDAC-1, as well as competition with Sp1 through the DNA-binding domain.

title: Perceptual limits in a simulated "Cocktail party".
text:
We conducted a study to examine how people judge the number of simultaneous talkers. Participants were asked to report the number of talkers they heard, which varied from 1 to 13. We manipulated the spatial location of the talkers (1 or 6 locations), the duration of their voices (0.8 s, 5.0 s, and 15.0 s), and the arrangement of their genders in four different experiments.

Across all experiments, we found that the accuracy of numerosity judgments decreased as the number of talkers increased. We defined perceptual limits as the number of talkers at which the proportion of correct judgments was 0.5. On average, these limits ranged from 3 to 5 talkers, depending on the listening conditions. Perceptual limits were significantly higher when the talkers were spatially separated, when their voices were longer, and when they consisted of a mix of genders (Experiments 1, 2, and 3).

Furthermore, in Experiment 4, we observed that response times for numerosity judgments increased as the number of talkers increased from one to four.

These findings suggest that listeners perceptually separate talkers before counting them to make numerosity judgments. They also indicate that our ability to perceive simultaneous voices is limited to, at most, three to five talkers, depending on the listening situation. We discuss possible reasons for these perceptual limits in light of these results.

title: The MOS social support survey.
text: This paper discusses the creation and assessment of a concise, multidimensional, self-administered survey on social support. The survey was specifically developed for patients participating in the Medical Outcomes Study (MOS), a two-year study focusing on individuals with chronic conditions. The aim of this survey was to encompass the latest understanding of the various aspects of social support while also distinguishing itself from similar measures. The authors provide an overview of the key conceptual considerations taken into account when selecting items for the social support survey. They describe the items included in the survey and present findings based on data collected from 2987 patients aged 18 and above. Through multitrait scaling analyses, the authors confirm the existence of four functional support scales: emotional/informational, tangible, affectionate, and positive social interaction. They also construct an overall functional social support index. These measures of support differ from structural measures of social support and other health-related measures. The reliability of these measures is high, with all Alphas exceeding 0.91, and they demonstrate reasonable stability over time. Furthermore, the authors find support for selected hypotheses regarding the construct validity of the survey.

title: Can hematological parameters discriminate malaria from nonmalarious acute febrile illness in the tropics?
text:
BACKGROUND: Malaria is the primary potential cause of acute febrile illness in tropical regions, and it has been observed that various hematological parameters are altered in patients with malaria.

AIM: The aim of this study was to determine if specific hematological parameters can increase the likelihood of malaria in patients with acute febrile illnesses.

SETTINGS AND DESIGN: This was a prospective cohort study conducted in a hospital setting.

METHODS AND MATERIAL: All consecutive inpatients with a fever lasting less than seven days were included in the study. Patients with a known cause for their fever were excluded. Hematological parameters (hemoglobin, red cell distribution width (RDW), leukocyte count, and platelet counts) were measured using an automated counter. Peripheral smear examination for malarial parasites was used as the gold standard for diagnosing malaria.

STATISTICAL ANALYSIS USED: Diagnostic accuracy was assessed by calculating sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and likelihood ratios. The precision of these estimates was evaluated using 95% confidence intervals.

RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: A total of 184 patients were included in the study, and 70 (38%) had a positive peripheral smear for malarial parasites. Thrombocytopenia alone (platelet count less than 150,000/mm3) was found to be a predictor for malaria (sensitivity 60%, specificity 88%, positive likelihood ratio 5.04). When combined with anemia (hemoglobin less than 10 g/dl), it was the next best parameter (sensitivity 69%, specificity 74%, positive likelihood ratio 2.77). RDW and leukocyte count were not predictive. In conclusion, the presence of thrombocytopenia in a patient with acute febrile illness increases the likelihood of malarial infection.

title: 14q deletions are associated with trisomy 12, NOTCH1 mutations and unmutated IGHV genes in chronic lymphocytic leukemia and small lymphocytic lymphoma.
text: Deletions of chromosome 14's long arm (del(14q)) are not common but are frequently seen in mature B-cell neoplasms, especially in chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). To gain a better understanding of this abnormality, we examined 81 cases with del(14q): 54 of CLL and 27 of small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL), making it the largest reported series to date. Through karyotype and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), we found that the most common additional abnormality was trisomy 12 (tri12), which was observed in 28 out of 79 (35%) cases. This was followed by del13q14 (12 out of 79, 15%), delTP53 (11 out of 80, 14%), delATM (5 out of 79, 6%), and del6q21 (3 out of 76, 4%). Among 53 patients, 41 (77%) had unmutated IGHV genes, with a high occurrence of IGHV1-69 (21 out of 52, 40%). The NOTCH1 gene was mutated in 14 out of 45 (31%) patients. There were no significant differences in cytogenetic and molecular abnormalities between CLL and SLL. Further investigations using FISH and SNP-array revealed that the size of the 14q deletions varied. However, we identified a group with the same del(14)(q24.1q32.33) in 48% of cases. In this group, tri12 (P = 0.004) and NOTCH1 mutations (P = 0.02) were significantly more common compared to other patients. In CLL patients with del(14q), the median treatment-free survival (TFS) was 27 months. In conclusion, del(14q) is linked to tri12 and unfavorable prognostic factors, including unmutated IGHV genes (with a higher presence of the IGHV1-69 repertoire), NOTCH1 mutations, and a shorter TFS.

title: Rapid DNA methylation changes after exposure to traffic particles.
text:
RATIONALE: Exposure to particulate air pollution has been linked to increased hospitalization and mortality, particularly from cardiovascular disease. Lower levels of DNA methylation in the blood have been associated with processes related to cardiovascular outcomes, such as oxidative stress, aging, and atherosclerosis.

OBJECTIVES: Our objective was to investigate whether particulate pollution affects DNA methylation in heavily methylated sequences that are widely represented throughout the human genome.

METHODS: We analyzed DNA methylation of long interspersed nucleotide element (LINE-1) and Alu repetitive elements in 1,097 blood samples from 718 elderly participants in the Boston area Normative Aging Study. We used quantitative polymerase chain reaction-pyrosequencing and covariate-adjusted mixed models to account for within-subject correlation in repeated measures. We examined the effects of ambient particulate pollutants (black carbon, particulate matter with aerodynamic diameter ≤ 2.5 microm [PM2.5], or sulfate) in various time windows (ranging from 4 hours to 7 days) prior to the examination. We expressed the effects as standardized regression coefficients (beta), indicating the fraction of a standard deviation change in DNA methylation associated with a standard deviation increase in exposure.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Repetitive element DNA methylation varied in relation to time-related variables, such as the day of the week and season. LINE-1 methylation decreased following recent exposure to higher levels of black carbon (beta = -0.11; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.18 to -0.04; P = 0.002) and PM2.5 (beta = -0.13; 95% CI, -0.19 to -0.06; P < 0.001 for the 7-day moving average). In models considering two pollutants, only black carbon, which serves as a tracer for traffic particles, showed a significant association with LINE-1 methylation (beta = -0.09; 95% CI, -0.17 to -0.01; P = 0.03). No association was observed with Alu methylation (P > 0.12).

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that exposure to traffic particles leads to decreased methylation of repetitive elements. However, further research is needed to determine whether decreased methylation mediates the health effects associated with exposure.

title: Incidence of adverse drug events and potential adverse drug events. Implications for prevention. ADE Prevention Study Group.
text:
GOALS: The aim of this study was to evaluate the occurrence and preventability of adverse drug events (ADEs) and potential ADEs. Additionally, the study sought to analyze preventable events in order to develop strategies for prevention.

METHODS: This study was conducted as a prospective cohort study. The participants included all 4031 adult admissions to 11 medical and surgical units in two tertiary care hospitals over a period of six months. The units consisted of two medical and three surgical intensive care units, as well as four medical and two surgical general care units. 

OUTCOMES: The main outcomes measured were adverse drug events and potential ADEs.

PROCEDURE: Incidents were identified through stimulated self-reporting by nurses and pharmacists, as well as through daily chart reviews conducted by nurse investigators. Two independent reviewers then classified the incidents as either ADEs or potential ADEs, and assessed their severity and preventability.

RESULTS: Over the course of six months, a total of 247 ADEs and 194 potential ADEs were identified. Extrapolating these rates, it was estimated that there were approximately 6.5 ADEs and 5.5 potential ADEs per 100 nonobstetrical admissions, resulting in an average of 1900 ADEs and 1600 potential ADEs per year per hospital. Of all the ADEs, 1% were fatal (none of which were preventable), 12% were life-threatening, 30% were serious, and 57% were significant. Twenty-eight percent of the ADEs were deemed preventable. Among the life-threatening and serious ADEs, 42% were preventable, compared to 18% of the significant ADEs. Errors leading to preventable ADEs most commonly occurred during the ordering stage (56%) and administration stage (34%), while transcription errors (6%) and dispensing errors (4%) were less frequent. Errors were more likely to be caught if they occurred earlier in the process, with 48% being intercepted at the ordering stage compared to 0% at the administration stage.

CONCLUSION: Adverse drug events were found to be common and often preventable, with serious ADEs being more likely to be preventable. Most errors occurred during the ordering stage, but a significant number also occurred during the administration stage. Therefore, prevention strategies should target both stages of the drug delivery process.

title: Induction of galactokinase in Saccharomyces cerevisiae: kinetics of induction and glucose effects.
text: The effects of glucose on the synthesis of galactokinase have been studied in yeast cells that were made permeable by treatment with dimethyl sulfoxide. It was discovered that the response of uninduced cells to galactose depends on the carbon source used in the culture before exposure to galactose. Cells grown on glucose showed a long delay before induction, while cells grown on lactate exhibited induced synthesis within 8 minutes. The optimal concentration for induction was found to be 0.5% galactose. When glucose was added to yeast cultures growing on galactose, there was a temporary repression of synthesis followed by a slower rate of synthesis, indicating a weaker permanent catabolite repression. Neither 2-deoxygalactose nor fucose acted as unnecessary inducers of the pathway, nor did they serve as substrates for galactokinase.

title: Gene--nutrition interactions in coronary artery disease: correlation between the MTHFR C677T polymorphism and folate and homocysteine status in a Korean population.
text:
INTRODUCTION
Elevated levels of total homocysteine in the blood are a significant risk factor for coronary artery disease (CAD). The Methyltetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) enzyme plays a crucial role in homocysteine metabolism, and a common mutation in the MTHFR gene (C677T) leads to reduced enzyme activity, resulting in increased homocysteine levels and decreased folate levels. In this study, we aimed to determine the frequency of MTHFR C677T alleles in a Korean population, establish genotype-specific threshold levels of folate and vitamin B12, and investigate the association between the TT genotype and CAD risk.

MATERIALS AND METHODS
We recruited 163 CAD patients and 50 control subjects for our study. We used real-time PCR with melting point analysis to screen for the MTHFR C677T polymorphism. Additionally, we measured plasma levels of homocysteine, folate, and vitamin B12. We then determined the genotype-specific threshold values of folate and vitamin B12 required to maintain normal homocysteine levels for individuals with each MTHFR C677T genotype.

RESULTS
The frequency of the TT genotype was 18% in the control group and 26% in the patient group (P>0.05). Individuals with the TT genotype had significantly higher homocysteine levels (P<0.05). The genotype-specific threshold level of folate was significantly higher in individuals with the TT genotype compared to those with the CC or CT genotypes. The odds ratio (OR) for individuals with low folate levels and the TT genotype, estimating the relative risk of CAD, was 2.2. The OR for individuals with high folate levels and the TT genotype was 1.5 (95% CI, 0.5-9.6 and 0.7-3.2, respectively).

CONCLUSION
Our study identified a gene-nutrient interaction that indicates a higher risk of CAD based on specific threshold levels of folate required by different MTHFR C677T genotypes in the Korean population.

title: Human bone marrow adipocytes block granulopoiesis through neuropilin-1-induced granulocyte colony-stimulating factor inhibition.
text: Adipocytes, although their role in hematopoiesis is still uncertain in humans, are a part of the hematopoietic microenvironment. Our previous research has shown that the accumulation of fat cells in the femoral bone marrow is associated with increased expression of neuropilin-1 (NP-1), while its expression is weak in the hematopoietic iliac crest bone marrow. Based on this observation, we hypothesized that adipocytes may have a negative impact on hematopoiesis through NP-1. To test this hypothesis, we established an experimental model using bone marrow adipocytes differentiated into fibroblast-like fat cells (FLFC), which share similar characteristics with primitive unilocular fat cells. As expected, FLFCs consistently produced macrophage colony-stimulating factor and induced the differentiation of CD34(+) cells into macrophages, regardless of cell-to-cell contact. However, granulopoiesis was hindered by cell-to-cell contact, but could be restored in transwell culture conditions along with the production of granulocyte colony-stimulating factor. Both functions were also restored when FLFCs cultured in contact with CD34(+) cells were treated with an antibody that neutralizes NP-1, indicating its critical involvement in contact inhibition. Inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin-1 beta or dexamethasone were able to modulate FLFC properties and restore granulopoiesis. These findings provide the first evidence that primary adipocytes play a regulatory role in hematopoiesis, which may be implicated in certain pathological processes. Any potential conflicts of interest are disclosed at the end of this article.

title: The transcriptome profile of human embryonic stem cells as defined by SAGE.
text: We have successfully created human embryonic stem (ES) cell lines that possess the remarkable ability to renew themselves and transform into specific cell types. However, the precise molecular mechanisms behind this self-renewal and differentiation process remain largely unknown. To shed light on this, we conducted a study comparing the transcriptome profiles of two exclusive human ES cell lines (HES3 and HES4, ES Cell International) with those of mouse ES cells and other human tissues. Interestingly, we discovered that human and mouse ES cells share certain expressed gene products, although there are notable differences between them. For instance, the leukemia inhibitory factor pathway is inactive in human ES cells, and there is a higher prevalence of crucial genes like POU5F1 and SOX2 in human ES cells. By compiling a list of known ES-specific genes and potential new candidates, we have identified markers that can indicate the presence of human ES cells and contribute to their "stemness" phenotype. Notably, we observed a decrease in DNMT3B and LIN28 mRNAs during the differentiation of ES cells, which is of particular interest. The similarities and differences in gene expression profiles between human and mouse ES cells provide a solid foundation for further investigation into the intricate molecular and cellular mechanisms that govern their pluripotency, directed differentiation, and remarkable ability to renew themselves.

title: Small-molecule antagonists of p53-MDM2 binding: research tools and potential therapeutics.
text: p53 plays a crucial role in safeguarding normal tissues against tumor development caused by various types of stress. When stress is absent, the growth-suppressing and proapoptotic functions of p53 are hindered by MDM2, which binds to p53 and negatively regulates its activity and stability. By targeting MDM2, it is possible to activate p53 and potentially introduce a new and innovative therapeutic approach to cancer treatment. Recently, we have discovered a group of highly effective and selective small molecules called Nutlins, which inhibit the binding between MDM2 and p53. These Nutlins activate the p53 pathway and effectively inhibit tumor growth both in laboratory settings and in living organisms. They serve as valuable tools for studying the p53 pathway and its abnormalities in cancer. Nutlins induce apoptosis in human cancer cells in a p53-dependent manner, while exhibiting a cytostatic effect on normal cells that are actively dividing. Their remarkable efficacy against osteosarcoma xenografts suggests that MDM2 antagonists could be clinically beneficial in treating tumors with wild-type p53.

title: Slipped (CTG)•(CAG) repeats can be correctly repaired, escape repair or undergo error-prone repair
text: The expansion of (CTG)•(CAG) repeats, which is responsible for causing 14 or more diseases, is believed to occur when slipped DNAs escape repair. Our study focuses on the accuracy of slipped-DNA repair using human cell extracts and DNAs containing slip-outs of (CAG)20 or (CTG)20. We observed three possible outcomes: correct repair, escaped repair, and error-prone repair. The repair pathway chosen depended on the location of the nick and the composition of the slip-out (CAG or CTG). We also discovered a new type of error-prone repair, where excess repeats were not completely removed, leading to expansions rather than deletions. Neuron-like cell extracts exhibited all three repair outcomes, suggesting that these processes play a role in the instability of (CTG)•(CAG) repeats in post-mitotic brain cells of patients. Mismatch repair (MMR) and nucleotide excision repair (NER) proteins hMSH2, hMSH3, hMLH1, XPF, XPG, or polymerase β were not necessary for this instability, indicating that their involvement may occur before slip-out processing. The differential processing of slipped repeats may explain the variations in mutation patterns observed in different disease loci or tissues.

title: High Dub3 expression in mouse ESCs couples the G1/S checkpoint to pluripotency.
text: The exact molecular process that allows mouse embryonic stem cells (ESCs) to bypass the G1/S checkpoint is still unknown. When DNA damage occurs, it prevents the entry of ESCs into the S phase by inhibiting the CDK2 kinase through the destruction of its activator, the Cdc25A phosphatase. However, our observations have shown that even after DNA damage, there are high levels of Cdc25A present in the G1 phase of mouse ESCs. We have also discovered that Dub3, a deubiquitylase that regulates the abundance of Cdc25A protein, is expressed at higher levels in these cells. Additionally, we have found that the Dub3 gene is directly controlled by Esrrb, a crucial transcription factor in the self-renewal process. During neural conversion, we have observed a significant decrease in Dub3 expression, which precedes the destabilization of Cdc25A. Furthermore, when Dub3 expression is forced in ESCs, it becomes lethal upon differentiation, coinciding with changes in the cell cycle and commitment to a specific lineage. Finally, when either Dub3 or Cdc25A is knocked down, ESCs undergo spontaneous differentiation. Overall, these findings demonstrate a connection between the self-renewal process and cell cycle regulation in ESCs through the action of a deubiquitylase.

title: Paracrine effects of direct intramyocardial implantation of bone marrow derived cells to enhance neovascularization in chronic ischaemic myocardium.
text: The aim of this study was to determine the most effective types of bone marrow (BM) cells and their mechanisms of action for promoting new blood vessel formation in chronically ischemic heart tissue. The researchers compared the functional effects, angiogenic potential, and cytokine expression of direct intramyocardial implantation of autologous BM CD31-positive endothelial progenitor cells (EPC), BM mononuclear cells (MNCs), and saline in a swine model of chronic ischemic myocardium. Autologous BM cells were harvested and injected directly into the ischemic heart tissue using catheter-based electromechanical mapping guidance. After 12 weeks, the injection of BM-MNCs resulted in significant improvements in left ventricular dP/dt, left ventricular pressure, and regional microsphere myocardial perfusion over the ischemic endocardium and epicardium. No significant effects were observed following the injection of BM-EPCs or saline. The BM-MNC group also showed significantly higher capillary density and expression of mRNA of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and angiopoietin-2 in the ischemic myocardium compared to the saline group. Capillary density in the ischemic myocardium was positively correlated with VEGF expression. In conclusion, catheter-based direct intramyocardial injection of BM-MNCs enhanced angiogenesis more effectively than BM-EPCs or saline, possibly through a paracrine effect involving increased expression of VEGF, leading to improved cardiac performance in ischemic myocardium.

title: Endogenous miRNA sponge lincRNA-RoR regulates Oct4, Nanog, and Sox2 in human embryonic stem cell self-renewal.
text: The regulatory circuitry of embryonic stem cells (ESCs) is controlled by various factors, including core transcription factors (TFs), microRNAs (miRNAs), and other regulators. However, the role and mechanism of large intergenic noncoding RNAs (lincRNAs) in this circuitry are still unclear. In this study, we investigate the function of a specific lincRNA called linc-RoR, which may act as a competing endogenous RNA to connect miRNAs and core TFs such as Oct4, Sox2, and Nanog. Our findings reveal that linc-RoR contains miRNA-response elements that prevent miRNA-mediated suppression of these core TFs in self-renewing human ESCs. We propose that linc-RoR forms a feedback loop with core TFs and miRNAs to regulate the maintenance and differentiation of ESCs. These results provide valuable insights into the functional interactions of genetic network components during development and may have implications for the development of new therapies for various diseases.

title: Foxp3(+) T cells regulate immunoglobulin a selection and facilitate diversification of bacterial species responsible for immune homeostasis.
text: The maintenance of immune tolerance relies heavily on Foxp3(+) T cells. Our study in mice reveals that these cells are crucial for diversifying the gut microbiota, particularly the Firmicutes species. Foxp3(+) T cells control the indigenous bacteria by performing regulatory functions both inside and outside germinal centers (GCs). This includes suppressing inflammation and regulating the selection of immunoglobulin A (IgA) in Peyer's patches. The diversified and selected IgAs contribute to maintaining a balanced and diverse microbiota, which in turn promotes the expansion of Foxp3(+) T cells, the induction of GCs, and IgA responses in the gut. This symbiotic regulatory loop is facilitated by the adaptive immune system, which utilizes cellular and molecular components to ensure immune tolerance and diversify and select the antibody repertoire. Ultimately, this regulation of bacterial communities is essential for maintaining homeostasis.

title: The isolation and characterization of a cDNA encoding phospholipid-specific inositol polyphosphate 5-phosphatase.
text:
We have successfully cloned and characterized a new human inositol polyphosphate 5-phosphatase (5-phosphatase) through cDNA analysis.
