This particular enzyme stands out from previously known members of its gene family due to its unique substrate specificity. While other members hydrolyze water soluble inositol phosphates, this enzyme exclusively targets lipid substrates, specifically phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate and phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate. The isolated cDNA consists of 3110 base pairs and predicts a protein product of 644 amino acids with a molecular weight of 70,023.

We have designated this 5-phosphatase as type IV. It is a highly basic protein with a pI value of 8.8. Among all known 5-phosphatases, it exhibits the highest affinity towards phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate. Its K(m) value is 0.65 micrometer, which is one-tenth of the K(m) value of SHIP (5.95 micrometer), another 5-phosphatase that hydrolyzes phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate. The activity of 5-phosphatase type IV is influenced by the presence of detergents in the in vitro assay. It can hydrolyze lipid substrates without detergents or in the presence of n-octyl beta-glucopyranoside or Triton X-100. However, it cannot hydrolyze phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate in the presence of cetyltriethylammonium bromide, a detergent commonly used in other studies.

Interestingly, SHIP, which was previously characterized as a 5-phosphatase that only hydrolyzes substrates with d-3 phosphates, also demonstrated the ability to hydrolyze phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate in the presence of n-octyl beta-glucopyranoside but not cetyltriethylammonium bromide. To identify the 5-phosphatase type IV enzyme in human tissues, we utilized antibodies generated against a peptide predicted by the cDNA. Western blotting revealed high expression levels of this enzyme in the brain. We also conducted Western blotting on mouse tissues and observed high expression levels in the brain, testes, and heart, with lower expression levels in other tissues. Furthermore, mRNA of this enzyme was detected in various tissues and cell lines through Northern blotting.

title: Lack of Absent in Melanoma 2 (AIM2) expression in tumor cells is closely associated with poor survival in colorectal cancer patients.
text: Functional studies on colorectal cancer cells have shown that the interferon-inducible dsDNA sensor Absent in Melanoma 2 (AIM2) plays a protective role in cancer progression. In this study, we aimed to investigate the relationship between AIM2 expression in tumor cells and patient prognosis over a 5-year follow-up period. A total of 476 matched tissue pairs (colorectal tumor and adjacent normal colon epithelium) were analyzed using a tissue microarray by two independent observers. We excluded samples from 62 patients due to missing follow-up information or neo-adjuvant therapy prior to tissue sampling. Among the remaining 414 tissue pairs, 279 (67.4%) showed reduced AIM2 expression in cancer cells compared to their normal epithelial cells. Additionally, 38 patients (9.18%) had completely lost AIM2 expression in tumor cells. After adjusting for various factors including sex, age, cancer stage, tumor site, tumor grade, and chemotherapy, we found that complete lack of AIM2 expression was associated with a 3-fold increase in overall mortality (HR=2.40; 95% CI=1.44-3.99) and disease-specific mortality (HR=3.14; 95% CI=1.75-5.65) compared to AIM2-positive tumor samples. These results strongly support the notion that AIM2 expression is closely linked to poor outcomes in colorectal cancer. Further research is needed to determine whether lack of AIM2 expression can serve as a biomarker for identifying colorectal cancer patients with a poor prognosis.

title: VSL#3 probiotic upregulates intestinal mucosal alkaline sphingomyelinase and reduces inflammation.
text:
The background information provided states that alkaline sphingomyelinase is an enzyme found only in bile and the intestinal brush border. It breaks down sphingomyelin into ceramide, sphingosine, and sphingosine-1-phosphate, which leads to epithelial apoptosis. Reduced levels of alkaline sphingomyelinase have been observed in premalignant and malignant intestinal epithelia, as well as in ulcerative colitis tissue. Probiotic bacteria, such as VSL#3, can serve as a source of sphingomyelinase. 

The objective of the study was to investigate the impact of VSL#3 probiotic therapy on mucosal levels of alkaline sphingomyelinase in both a mouse model of colitis and patients with ulcerative colitis. 

In the mouse model, interleukin-10 gene-deficient (IL10KO) mice and wild type control mice were treated with VSL#3 for three weeks. Afterward, the activity of alkaline sphingomyelinase was measured in the ileal and colonic tissue. Additionally, 15 patients with ulcerative colitis were treated with VSL#3 for five weeks, and alkaline sphingomyelinase activity was measured through biopsies. The ulcerative colitis disease activity index scores were also compared before and after treatment. 

The results showed that IL10KO mice had lower levels of alkaline sphingomyelinase in the colon and ileum compared to controls. However, treatment with VSL#3 increased mucosal alkaline sphingomyelinase activity in both the colon and ileum of these mice. In human patients with ulcerative colitis, VSL#3 treatment reduced the disease activity index scores and increased mucosal alkaline sphingomyelinase activity. 

In conclusion, the study found that mucosal alkaline sphingomyelinase activity is decreased in the intestines of IL10KO mice with colitis and in humans with ulcerative colitis. However, VSL#3 probiotic therapy can upregulate mucosal alkaline sphingomyelinase activity.

title: Nodal/Activin signaling predicts human pluripotent stem cell lines prone to differentiate toward the hematopoietic lineage.
text: The potential for differentiating into specific lineages varies among different human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC) lines. Therefore, it is important to identify which hPSC lines have the highest potential for differentiation into a particular lineage. In this study, we compared the hematopoietic potential of 14 human embryonic stem cell (hESC)/induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) lines. We analyzed the emergence of hemogenic progenitors, primitive and mature blood cells, and colony-forming unit (CFU) potential at different time points. We observed significant differences in the ability of hPSCs to differentiate into blood cells: some hPSCs had a strong potential for blood differentiation, while others had a limited capacity. Correlation studies showed that CFU potential strongly correlated with hemogenic progenitors and primitive blood cells, but not mature blood cells. The expression of mesoendodermal and hematopoietic transcription factors did not correlate with the efficiency of hematopoietic initiation or maturation. Microarray studies revealed distinct gene expression profiles between hPSCs with good and poor hematopoietic potential. While genes associated with neuroectoderm were downregulated in hPSCs prone to hematopoietic differentiation, genes involved in Nodal/Activin signaling were upregulated, suggesting that this signaling pathway predicts hPSC lines with good blood differentiation potential. Loss- and gain-of-function assays confirmed the association between Nodal/Activin signaling and hematopoietic differentiation potential. Our findings highlight the importance of comparative studies to determine the lineage-specific differentiation potential of different hPSCs and suggest that Nodal/Activin signaling can predict hPSC lines prone to hematopoietic specification.

title: Addition of a Gastrointestinal Microbiome Modulator to Metformin Improves Metformin Tolerance and Fasting Glucose Levels.
text:
BACKGROUND: The adverse effects of metformin primarily stem from gastrointestinal (GI) intolerance, which can hinder the administration of an effective dose or lead to discontinuation of the medication. As some of these side effects may be linked to changes in the GI microbiome, we conducted a study to determine if combining a GI microbiome modulator (GIMM) with metformin could alleviate GI symptoms.

METHODS: We employed a 2-period crossover study design, with two treatment sequences: placebo in period 1 followed by GIMM in period 2, or vice versa. Each study period lasted for 2 weeks, with a 2-week washout period in between. During the first week, patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) who experienced GI intolerance with metformin took 500 mg of metformin along with their assigned NM504 (GIMM) or placebo treatment during breakfast and dinner. In the second week, the 10 subjects took 500 mg of metformin three times a day, with GIMM or placebo consumed with the first and third daily metformin doses. Subjects were allowed to discontinue metformin dosing if it became intolerable.

RESULTS: The combination of metformin and GIMM treatment resulted in significantly better tolerance to metformin compared to the placebo combination (6.78 ± 0.65 [mean ± SEM] versus 4.45 ± 0.69, P = .0006). Mean fasting glucose levels were significantly lower with the metformin-GIMM combination (121.3 ± 7.8 mg/dl) than with metformin-placebo (151.9 ± 7.8 mg/dl) (P < .02).

CONCLUSION: Combining a GI microbiome modulator with metformin may enable the increased use of metformin in T2D patients and improve the treatment of the disease.

title: Diverse tumorigenic pathways in ovarian serous carcinoma.
text: The purpose of this study was to examine genetic changes in 108 sporadic serous ovarian neoplasms in order to understand how ovarian serous carcinogenesis occurs. Our findings reveal that K-ras mutations are present in approximately 50% of serous borderline tumors (SBTs), non-invasive micropapillary serous carcinomas (MPSCs), and invasive micropapillary serous carcinomas. These types of tumors represent a continuum of tumor progression in terms of their appearance. Additionally, we observed a gradual increase in the degree of allelic imbalance in chromosomes 1p, 5q, 8p, 18q, 22q, and Xp when comparing serous borderline tumors to non-invasive and invasive micropapillary serous carcinomas. On the other hand, high-grade tumors (conventional serous carcinoma) had wild-type K-ras in all 23 cases studied and a high frequency of allelic imbalance, even in small primary tumors similar to those found in advanced stage tumors. Based on these findings, we propose a dualistic model for ovarian serous carcinogenesis. One pathway involves a stepwise progression from SBT to non-invasive and then invasive MPSC. The other pathway is characterized by rapid progression from the ovarian surface epithelium or inclusion cysts to a conventional (high-grade) serous carcinoma.

title: Tissue-inherent fate of GPI revealed by GPI-anchored GFP transgenesis.
text: In order to better understand what happens to glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) in mammals, we created a fusion protein called enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP-GPI) that is anchored to GPI. We then introduced this protein to cultured cells and observed that it was correctly sorted to plasma membranes and microsomes, depending on GPI biosynthesis. Additionally, we developed transgenic mice that carried the EGFP-GPI fusion construct. These mice exhibited widespread expression of the transgene. Through histological analysis, we discovered that the EGFP-GPI protein was prominently localized in a polarized manner in various epithelial tissues, the nervous system, liver, and was also secreted from some exocrine glands. In non-epithelial tissues, the protein was present in a non-polarized manner, indicating that the sorting of GPI is specific to each tissue.

title: Essential role for the SANT domain in the functioning of multiple chromatin remodeling enzymes.
text: The SANT domain, which bears resemblance to the DNA binding domain of c-myb, is a newly discovered motif present in various eukaryotic transcriptional regulatory proteins. In this study, we demonstrate the crucial role of the SANT domain in the biological functions of yeast Swi3p, Ada2p, and Rsc8p, which are subunits of distinct chromatin remodeling complexes. Additionally, we observe that the SANT domain of Ada2p is indispensable for the histone acetyltransferase activity of native HAT complexes containing Gcn5p. Moreover, our kinetic analyses reveal that an intact SANT domain is necessary for Ada2p to enhance the binding of histone tails and catalytic activity of Gcn5p. These findings support the notion that SANT domains play a general role in functional interactions with histone N-terminal tails.

title: Mechanisms of pancreatic beta-cell death in type 1 and type 2 diabetes: many differences, few similarities.
text:
The failure of beta cells is a common characteristic of both type 1 and type 2 diabetes. In both forms of the disease, beta cell death is primarily caused by apoptosis. It has been proposed that the activation of a final common pathway involving interleukin (IL)-1beta, nuclear factor (NF)-kappaB, and Fas is responsible for nutrient- and cytokine-induced beta cell death in type 2 and type 1 diabetes, respectively. This review examines the similarities and differences in the mechanisms of beta cell death between type 1 and type 2 diabetes.

In type 1 diabetes, the insulitis lesion is characterized by the infiltration of immune cells that produce cytokines such as IL-1beta, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-alpha, and interferon (IFN)-gamma. These cytokines, along with IL-1beta and/or TNF-alpha plus IFN-gamma, induce beta cell apoptosis by activating beta cell gene networks controlled by the transcription factors NF-kappaB and STAT-1. NF-kappaB activation leads to the production of nitric oxide (NO) and chemokines, as well as the depletion of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) calcium. Beta cell death is then executed through the activation of mitogen-activated protein kinases, triggering ER stress, and the release of mitochondrial death signals.

In type 2 diabetes, chronic exposure to high levels of glucose and free fatty acids (FFAs) can lead to beta cell dysfunction and apoptosis. High glucose has dual effects, initially causing "glucose hypersensitization" and later apoptosis through different mechanisms. However, high glucose does not induce or activate IL-1beta, NF-kappaB, or inducible nitric oxide synthase in rat or human beta cells in vitro or in vivo in Psammomys obesus. FFAs may induce beta cell apoptosis through ER stress, which is independent of NF-kappaB and NO.

Therefore, the mechanisms of beta cell death triggered by cytokines and nutrients are fundamentally different. Cytokines activate an NF-kappaB-dependent mechanism that ultimately leads to caspase-3 activation, while nutrients act through an NF-kappaB-independent mechanism. This suggests that a unified hypothesis for the mechanisms of beta cell death in type 1 and type 2 diabetes is unlikely, and different approaches will be needed to prevent beta cell death in each type of diabetes.

title: Health-related quality of life among children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
text:
The aim of this study was to measure the health-related quality of life (HRQL) of children undergoing treatment for acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and identify specific disabilities that could be addressed. The study included two groups: ALL patients aged 5 years and older in a multi-center clinical trial, and a control group from the general population. The patients were assessed during all four major phases of treatment and approximately 2 years after treatment. The HEALTH UTILITIES INDEX® (HUI®) Mark 2 (HUI2) and Mark 3 (HUI3) were used to measure health status and HRQL. HRQL scores were used to calculate quality-adjusted life years (QALYs). Excess disability rates were used to identify areas for improvement. 

The study collected HUI assessments from 749 participants during the five phases. The mean HRQL increased from the induction phase to the post-treatment phase (P < 0.001). There were no significant effects of demographics or treatment on HRQL, except for the type of asparaginase used during continuation therapy (P = 0.005 for HUI2 and P = 0.007 for HUI3). During the active treatment phases, there were significant differences in mean HRQL scores between patients and controls (P < 0.001), but not during the post-treatment phase. Patients lost approximately 0.2 QALYs during active treatment compared to controls. Disability was observed in mobility/ambulation, emotion, self-care, and pain, but improved over time. 

In conclusion, patients with ALL experienced significant but decreasing deficits in HRQL during active treatment phases, equivalent to losing approximately 2 months of life in perfect health. HRQL within the 2-year post-treatment phase was similar to that of controls. The challenge for policymakers is to develop new treatment protocols that result in fewer disabilities in mobility/ambulation, emotion, self-care, and pain, without compromising survival.

title: JUVENILE MORTALITY INCREASES WITH CLUTCH SIZE IN A NEOTROPICAL BIRD
text:
The variation in the number of eggs laid by birds at different latitudes is a well-known example of how geographic location can affect certain traits in vertebrates. There are several theories as to why tropical birds tend to have smaller clutch sizes, including the risk of nest predation, limited food availability for nestlings, and higher mortality rates for young birds after they leave the nest. To test these hypotheses, we conducted an experiment in central Panama, where we manipulated the number of eggs in the nests of Spotted Antbirds.

We found that the activity of the parents at the nests did not have an impact on the rate of nest predation, and the parents were able to successfully feed their nestlings even in larger broods. While larger broods did produce more young birds that successfully fledged, these individuals were less likely to survive until they dispersed compared to those from smaller broods. As a result, the overall productivity of the nests did not vary depending on the number of eggs.

We also discovered that the mortality of young birds after they left the nest was not related to their weight two to three days before they fledged. Instead, it seemed that the allocation of parental care per juvenile in different-sized broods influenced the probability of survival for the young birds. These findings suggest that the care provided by parents during the period after the young birds leave the nest may be a crucial factor in the evolution of smaller clutch sizes in tropical birds.

title: Diagnosis of rotator cuff tears.
text: Almost half of all major shoulder injuries are caused by rotator cuff tears, but diagnosing them can be challenging. In order to improve the accuracy of diagnosis, we conducted a prospective study where we compared the results of 23 clinical tests performed on 400 patients, both with and without rotator cuff tears. From our findings, we identified three simple tests that were highly indicative of a rotator cuff tear: weakness in the supraspinatus muscle, weakness in external rotation, and impingement. If all three tests were positive, or if two tests were positive and the patient was 60 years old or older, there was a 98% likelihood of a rotator cuff tear. Conversely, the absence of these features ruled out the diagnosis of a rotator cuff tear.

title: Increased susceptibility to UV-induced skin carcinogenesis in polymerase eta-deficient mice.
text: Patients with Xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XPV) who have mutations in the DNA polymerase eta (pol eta) gene are extremely sensitive to sunlight and have a significantly higher susceptibility to developing skin cancer caused by sun exposure. The absence of Pol eta in XPV cells reduces their ability to replicate DNA damaged by UV light, making them more vulnerable to UV-induced cell death and genetic mutations. To gain a better understanding of Pol eta's functions, we conducted experiments using mice lacking this enzyme. These mice, which carry two copies of a non-functioning pol eta gene, are viable, fertile, and do not exhibit any noticeable defects within the first year of their lives. However, fibroblasts derived from these mutant mice are highly sensitive to UV light and all of the Pol eta-deficient mice develop skin tumors after being exposed to UV radiation, unlike their wild-type counterparts who do not develop such tumors. These findings, along with biochemical studies on how mouse Pol eta performs translesion synthesis, suggest that Pol eta's ability to bypass cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers plays a crucial role in preventing UV-induced skin cancer in mice. Additionally, 37.5% of mice carrying only one functional copy of the pol eta gene also developed skin cancer within a 5-month period after being exposed to UV light, indicating that humans who are heterozygous for pol eta mutations may also face an increased risk of developing skin cancer.

title: Hydrogen sulfide interacts with nitric oxide in the heart: possible involvement of nitroxyl.
text: The aim of this study is to investigate the interaction between nitric oxide (NO) and hydrogen sulfide (H2S), two important gaseous mediators in rat hearts. In order to do this, the researchers measured intracellular calcium levels in isolated cardiomyocytes using a spectrofluorometric method with Fura-2. They also measured myocyte contractility using a video edge system. The results showed that NaHS, an H2S donor, had no significant effect on resting calcium levels, electrically induced calcium transients, or cell contractility in ventricular myocytes. However, stimulating endogenous NO production or applying NO donors decreased myocyte twitch amplitudes and slowed down cell contraction and relaxation. Surprisingly, NaHS reversed these negative effects of NO-increasing agents. Additionally, the mixture of SNP (a NO donor) and NaHS increased resting calcium levels and calcium transient amplitudes, while SNP alone decreased them. Angeli's salt, a nitroxyl anion (HNO) donor, had similar effects to SNP + NaHS on calcium handling and myocyte contractility. Three thiols, N-acetyl-cysteine, l-cysteine, and glutathione, abolished the effects of HNO and SNP + NaHS on myocyte contraction. The inhibitors Rp-cAMP and Rp-cGMP did not affect the effects of SNP + NaHS, suggesting a mechanism independent of cAMP/PKA or cGMP/PKG. In conclusion, H2S may interact with NO to form a thiol sensitive molecule (possibly HNO) that produces positive effects on myocyte contraction. These findings provide insights into the interaction between NO and H2S and may offer new approaches for treating cardiovascular diseases.

title: A novel mechanism of rapid nuclear neutrophil extracellular trap formation in response to Staphylococcus aureus.
text: Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) are webs of DNA covered with antimicrobial molecules that make up a newly discovered killing mechanism in the innate immune defense. Previous studies have shown that it takes 3-4 hours for NETs to form through an oxidant-dependent process that involves the death of neutrophils. However, in this study, we observed a unique response of neutrophils to Staphylococcus aureus, where NET formation occurred without neutrophil death or breach of the plasma membrane. The nucleus of the neutrophils rapidly changed shape and condensed, leading to the separation of the inner and outer nuclear membranes and the formation of vesicles filled with nuclear DNA. These vesicles were then released intact into the extracellular space, where they ruptured and released chromatin. This entire process happened very quickly, within 5-60 minutes, and did not rely on oxidants. Mitochondrial DNA played a minimal role in these NETs, which exhibited some proteolytic activity and were able to kill S. aureus. Over time, the nuclear envelope ruptured, allowing DNA to fill the cytoplasm, potentially for later production of lytic NETs, but this was different from the vesicular release mechanism. Supernatants containing NET-inducing activity were found to contain Panton-Valentine leukocidin, autolysin, and a lipase, with Panton-Valentine leukocidin being the main inducer of NETs. This study describes a new, rapid mechanism of NET release that contributes to the trapping and killing of S. aureus.

title: 131-I radioiodine therapy for hyperthyroidism in patients with Graves' disease, uninodular goitre and multinodular goitre.
text:
We conducted a study on 201 consecutive patients who were given a consistent dose of radioiodine for the treatment of hyperthyroidism between 1981 and 1986. Among the patients with Graves' disease (170), the initial treatment involved an average dose of 369 (10) MBq 131-I. The remission rate at 6 months was 94%, with a cumulative relapse rate of 12% at one year and 21% at five years. The cumulative incidence of hypothyroidism was 26% at 3 months, 55% at 6 months, 61% at 1 year, and 66% at 5 years. 

For patients with a uninodular goitre (10), the initial treatment included an average dose of 438 (85) MBq 131-I. The remission rate at 6 months was 100%, with no relapse at 1 year but a relapse rate of 17% at 5 years. The cumulative incidence of hypothyroidism was 26% at 3 months, 30% at 6 months, 40% at 1 year, and 40% at 5 years. 

Patients with a multinodular goitre (21) received an initial treatment with an average dose of 613 (77) MBq 131-I. The remission rate at 6 months was 79%, with a cumulative relapse rate of 26% at 1 year and 39% at 5 years. The cumulative incidence of hypothyroidism was 5% at 3 months, 14% at 6 months, 24% at 1 year, and 24% at 5 years.

title: Enteral nutrition in the critically ill patient.
text: The outcome of critically ill patients can be influenced by the timing and method of nutrition they receive. Research has demonstrated that providing early enteral nutrition can specifically reduce the risk of infectious complications in these patients. However, a subset of patients who are malnourished upon admission to the intensive care unit can benefit from parenteral nutrition.

title: Genomewide analysis of nucleosome density histone acetylation and HDAC function in fission yeast.
text:
We have conducted a comprehensive study on four histone deacetylases (HDACs) in fission yeast (Schizosaccharomyces pombe), representing three different phylogenetic classes. Our investigation focused on enzymatic specificity, expression profiles, and binding locations of these HDACs. By comparing nucleosome density, histone acetylation patterns, and HDAC binding in both intergenic and coding regions with gene expression profiles, we made several significant findings.

Firstly, we discovered that Sir2 (class III) and Hos2 (class I) play a role in preventing histone loss. Additionally, Clr6 (class I) is the primary enzyme responsible for repression localized at promoters. Surprisingly, Hos2 also promotes high expression of growth-related genes by deacetylating H4K16Ac in their open reading frames.

Furthermore, we found that Clr3 (class II) works in cooperation with Sir2 throughout the genome, including silent regions such as rDNA, centromeres, mat2/3, and telomeres. The most significant acetylation sites were H3K14Ac for Clr3 and H3K9Ac for Sir2 at their respective genomic targets. Clr3 also influences subtelomeric regions, which contain stress- and meiosis-induced genes that are clustered.

In conclusion, our combined genomic approach has revealed distinct roles for fission yeast HDACs in the repression and activation of gene expression, particularly in the silent regions.

title: In vitro antimicrobial activity of mangrove plant Sonneratia alba.
text: The aim of this study was to investigate the antimicrobial properties of the mangrove plant Sonneratia alba (S. alba). The antimicrobial activity was assessed using disc diffusion and microdilution methods against six different microorganisms. The extraction process involved using a series of solvents, starting with n-hexane, followed by ethyl acetate and methanol in increasing order of polarity. The results showed that the methanol extract was the most effective, while the n-hexane extract had no activity. The antimicrobial activities were observed against the gram positive bacteria Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) and Bacillus cereus (B. cereus), the gram negative Escherichia coli (E. coli), and the yeast Cryptococcus neoformans. However, no inhibition zone was observed for Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Candida albicans, suggesting that they were not sensitive to the concentrations tested. Among the sensitive strains, E. coli (17.5 mm) showed the highest sensitivity, followed by S. aureus (12.5 mm) and B. cereus (12.5 mm). In conclusion, this study demonstrates that S. alba possesses antimicrobial properties against certain microorganisms.

title: Obesity induces a phenotypic switch in adipose tissue macrophage polarization.
text: During obesity, adipose tissue macrophages (ATMs) infiltrate the adipose tissue and contribute to insulin resistance. Our hypothesis was that the macrophages migrating to the adipose tissue due to high-fat feeding may differ from those already present under normal diet conditions. Our research revealed a new population of ATMs, identified as F4/80(+)CD11c(+), in the adipose tissue of obese mice, which was not observed in lean mice. ATMs from lean mice expressed several genes associated with M2 or "alternatively activated" macrophages, including Ym1, arginase 1, and Il10. However, diet-induced obesity reduced the expression of these genes in ATMs while increasing the expression of genes encoding TNF-alpha and iNOS, which are characteristic of M1 or "classically activated" macrophages. Interestingly, ATMs from obese C-C motif chemokine receptor 2-KO (Ccr2-KO) mice exhibited M2 markers at levels similar to those from lean mice. The anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10, which was overexpressed in ATMs from lean mice, protected adipocytes from TNF-alpha-induced insulin resistance. Therefore, diet-induced obesity causes a shift in the activation state of ATMs from an M2-polarized state in lean animals, which may protect adipocytes from inflammation, to an M1 proinflammatory state that contributes to insulin resistance.

title: Psychological Outcome 4 Years after Restrictive Bariatric Surgery
text: Severe psychiatric and physical health issues are commonly associated with extreme obesity, leading to impaired psychosocial functioning. Bariatric surgery is considered the most effective treatment for weight loss and addressing obesity-related illnesses. The impact of this surgery on psychological and psychosocial well-being in the long term, however, remains unclear. This study aimed to assess the relationship between weight loss and psychological variables such as depression, anxiety, health-related quality of life (HRQOL), and self-esteem up to four years after obesity surgery. A total of 148 patients (47 males, 101 females) with a mean age of 38.8 ± 10.2 years were evaluated using standardized questionnaires before surgery (T1), and at 1 year (T2), 2 years (T3), and 4 years (T4) post-surgery. On average, participants lost 24.6% of their initial weight after one year, 25.1% after two years, and 22.3% after four years. Statistical analysis revealed significant improvements in depressive symptoms, physical aspects of quality of life, and self-esteem, with the greatest improvements observed one year after surgery. These improvements were largely maintained over time. There were also significant correlations between weight loss and improvements in depression, physical aspects of HRQOL (at T2, T3, and T4), and self-esteem (at T3). Mental health aspects showed significant improvement during the four-year follow-up period, corresponding to the substantial weight loss achieved through bariatric surgery. However, there was a gradual decline in psychological improvements over time, which was not statistically significant.

title: Dynamics of Microvillus Extension and Tether Formation in Rolling Leukocytes.
text: Leukocyte rolling under flow conditions is facilitated by the binding of P-selectin glycoprotein ligand-1 (PSGL-1) to P-selectin. PSGL-1 molecules are located on the surface ruffles, known as microvilli, of human neutrophils, which are a type of leukocyte in the innate immune system. When a P-selectin-PSGL-1 bond is formed, it can exert a pulling force on the microvillus, causing it to deform. The extent of deformation depends on the strength of the bond force, with the microvillus either extending or forming a thin membrane cylinder called a tether. In this study, we propose a Kelvin-Voigt viscoelastic material as a more accurate model for microvillus extension. Using a modified version of our Event-Tracking Model of Adhesion (ETMA), we show how load-bearing P-selectin-PSGL-1 bonds shape microvillus deformation during neutrophil rolling at low shear conditions. Specifically, we investigate a wall shear rate of 50 s(-1) and a P-selectin site density of 150 molecules μm(-2). Additionally, we explore the impact of microvillus deformability on neutrophil rolling. Our findings reveal that, on average, 65% of the total extension of the microvillus-tether complex is due to microvillus extension. Furthermore, we observe that the rolling neutrophil may never fully come to a rest. By comparing these results with those obtained from non-deformable microvilli, we support the notion that the ability of the microvillus to deform plays a role in stabilizing cell rolling.

title: Female Gender and Reproductive Factors Affecting Risk, Relapses and Progression in Multiple Sclerosis
text: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic disease of the central nervous system that causes inflammation, damage to the protective covering of nerve fibers, and degeneration. It is a common cause of neurological disability in young adults, and there has been an increase in the number of women affected in recent decades. While being female and of child-bearing age increases the risk of developing relapsing remitting MS, it also seems to offer some protection against cognitive decline and the progressive form of the disease, which is a negative factor for long-term disability. The risk of MS in women has been linked to an earlier age at menarche (the onset of menstruation), but studies have shown that the number of children a woman has does not affect her risk of developing MS. However, recent research suggests that having more children may actually reduce the risk of experiencing a first episode of demyelination, which is a potential early sign of MS. Pregnancy in women with MS has been associated with a lower rate of relapse and fewer neurological symptoms, particularly in the third trimester. Although there is an increased risk of relapse in the postpartum period, giving birth does not appear to have a negative impact on the long-term course of the disease. Fertility treatments in women with MS have been linked to a higher risk of relapse in the three months following the procedure, especially when gonadotrophin-releasing hormone agonists are used and pregnancy does not occur. Overall, there is strong evidence supporting the role of sex steroid hormones in regulating MS, although the specific mechanisms are not yet fully understood. In conclusion, the higher risk of MS in women and the changes in relapse and progression risk associated with reproductive events indicate complex interactions between the immune, neuroendocrine, and reproductive systems in MS.

title: Spatial release from masking based on binaural processing for up to six maskers.
text:
We conducted an experiment to measure Spatial Release from Masking (SRM) for the identification of a female target word in the presence of male masker words. The target words were presented from a single loudspeaker located at the center, while two, four, or six masker words were presented either from the same source as the target or from spatially separated masker sources. All masker words were presented from loudspeakers symmetrically placed around the centered target source in the front hemisphere. We used three different masking conditions: speech-in-speech masking (which includes both informational and energetic masking), speech-in-noise masking (which involves only energetic masking), and filtered speech-in-filtered speech masking (which involves only informational masking). 

To analyze the results, we used psychophysical measures and created three-point psychometric functions that showed the proportion of correct word identification in relation to the target-to-masker ratio (in decibels) for both the cases of co-located and spatially separated target and masker sources. By comparing the slopes and intercepts of these functions, we calculated the SRM. 

We found that as the number of symmetrically placed masker sources increased from two to six, the SRM decreased. This decrease was consistent across all types of masking, and for six masker sources, there was almost no SRM measured. These findings suggest that when binaural processing is the primary factor influencing SRM, it is effectively limited to fewer than six sound sources.

title: Nephrin mutations cause childhood- and adult-onset focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.
text: Congenital nephrotic syndrome of the Finnish type, which manifests before the age of 3 months, is caused by mutations in the NPHS1 gene. Recently, these mutations have also been found in childhood-onset steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome and less severe forms of the disease. However, their role in adults with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis is still unknown. In this study, we developed a scoring matrix to assess the pathogenicity of amino acid substitutions by considering the biophysical and biochemical differences between the wild-type and mutant amino acids, the evolutionary conservation of the amino acid residue in related species, and specific domains, along with contextual information. We analyzed mutations in 97 patients from 89 unrelated families, 52 of whom developed steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome after the age of 18. We identified compound heterozygous or homozygous NPHS1 mutations in five familial and seven sporadic cases, including one patient who was 27 years old when the disease began. Using our in silico approach, we classified the substitutions as either 'severe' or 'mild'. Our findings suggest that patients with two 'severe' mutations tend to develop the disease at an earlier age compared to those with at least one 'mild' mutation. The discovery of mutations in a patient with adult-onset focal segmental glomerulosclerosis suggests that NPHS1 analysis should be considered for patients with a later onset of the disease.

title: Use of clomifene during early pregnancy and risk of hypospadias: population based case-control study.
text: Clomifene is commonly used to stimulate ovulation.1 It is structurally similar to diethylstilbestrol, a substance that has been associated with vaginal and cervical clear cell adenocarcinoma in women exposed to it while in the womb. The negative effects are less severe in males, although there have been reports linking it to testicular cancer and urogenital abnormalities, such as epididymal cysts.2 3 Recent research has also discovered an increased risk of hypospadias in males whose mothers were exposed to diethylstilbestrol during pregnancy.4 Clomifene has a half-life of approximately five days, but its byproducts have been detected in blood samples on day 22 of the menstrual cycle and in feces up to six weeks after administration.5 The occurrence of hypospadias may be on the rise, but little is known about the risk of this condition in boys born to women who have used clomifene to induce ovulation. ### Methods and results Our study, a case-control investigation, was conducted in the Danish counties of North Jutland, Aarhus, Viborg, and ...

title: Association of aspirin and NSAID use with risk of colorectal cancer according to genetic variants.
text: The use of aspirin and other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) has been found to be important in reducing the risk of colorectal cancer. The objective of this study was to identify genetic markers that may determine the effectiveness of aspirin or NSAID chemoprevention. The study involved analyzing data from 5 case-control and 5 cohort studies conducted between 1976 and 2003 in the United States, Canada, Australia, and Germany. The participants were of European descent and included colorectal cancer cases and matched controls. The study looked at genome-wide single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and information on regular use of aspirin and/or NSAIDs, as well as other risk factors. The results showed that regular use of aspirin and/or NSAIDs was associated with a lower risk of colorectal cancer compared to nonregular use. One specific SNP, rs2965667, near the MGST1 gene, showed a significant interaction with aspirin and/or NSAID use. Individuals with the rs2965667-TT genotype had a lower risk of colorectal cancer with aspirin and/or NSAID use, while those with the TA or AA genotypes had a higher risk. Another SNP, rs16973225, near the IL16 gene, also showed a significant interaction with aspirin and/or NSAID use. Individuals with the rs16973225-AA genotype had a lower risk of colorectal cancer with regular use, while those with the AC or CC genotypes did not show a significant association. These findings suggest that the effectiveness of aspirin and/or NSAIDs in reducing colorectal cancer risk may vary depending on genetic variation. Further research is needed to validate these findings and develop targeted prevention strategies for colorectal cancer.

title: Intravaginal ring eluting tenofovir disoproxil fumarate completely protects macaques from multiple vaginal simian-HIV challenges.
text: The use of topical preexposure prophylaxis can prevent the transmission of HIV at the site of mucosal exposure. Vaginal gels containing the HIV-1 reverse transcriptase inhibitor tenofovir have shown some protection in pigtailed macaques, depending on the timing of viral challenge in relation to gel application. However, clinical trials have shown limited or no protection. Intravaginal rings (IVRs) may improve effectiveness by providing sustained drug delivery, resulting in constant levels of antiretroviral medication at the mucosal site and improving adherence. Although a few IVRs have been tested in clinical trials, achieving 100% efficacy in a repeated macaque vaginal challenge model has not yet been accomplished. In this study, we present a reservoir IVR technology that continuously delivers the tenofovir prodrug tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) over a period of 28 days. By changing the IVR every month in the repeated challenge model, we consistently achieved protective drug levels with the TDF IVRs. All macaques treated with TDF IVRs (n = 6) remained free of infection and showed no simian-HIV RNA after 16 weekly vaginal exposures to 50 tissue culture infectious dose SHIV162p3. In contrast, 11 out of 12 control macaques became infected, with an average of four exposures assuming a 7-day period from infection to virus RNA detection. The protection observed was correlated with tenofovir levels in vaginal fluid [average 1.8 × 10(5) ng/mL (range 1.1 × 10(4) to 6.6 × 10(5) ng/mL)] and the antiviral activity of cervicovaginal lavage samples. These findings support further development of TDF IVRs and suggest that long-lasting drug delivery devices delivering topical antiretrovirals could be effective in preventing the sexual transmission of HIV in humans.

title: Epithelial and mesenchymal subpopulations within normal basal breast cell lines exhibit distinct stem cell/progenitor properties.
text: The suggestion has been made that epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in mammary epithelial cells and breast cancer cells leads to the development of stem cell characteristics. It has also been proposed that the presence of EMT characteristics in claudin-low breast tumors indicates that they originate from basal stem cells. However, it is still unknown whether EMT is a natural property of normal basal stem cells and whether a mesenchymal-like phenotype is necessary for maintaining all their stem cell properties. To investigate this, we used non-tumorigenic basal cell lines as models of normal stem cells/progenitors. Our study revealed that these cell lines contain an epithelial subpopulation (referred to as "EpCAM+," which means epithelial cell adhesion molecule positive [EpCAM(pos)]/CD49f(high)) that spontaneously generates mesenchymal-like cells (referred to as "Fibros," which means EpCAM(neg)/CD49f(med/low)) through EMT. Importantly, stem cell/progenitor properties such as regenerative potential, high aldehyde dehydrogenase 1 activity, and the ability to form three-dimensional acini-like structures are predominantly found within EpCAM+ cells, while Fibros exhibit invasive behavior and the ability to form mammospheres. A meta-analysis of gene expression profiling showed that EpCAM+ cells have a luminal progenitor-like expression pattern, while Fibros are most similar to stromal fibroblasts but not stem cells. Furthermore, Fibros exhibit some myoepithelial traits and strong similarities with claudin-low breast cancer cells. Finally, we demonstrated that the EMT-inducers Slug and Zeb1 control the progenitor and mesenchymal-like phenotype in EpCAM+ cells and Fibros, respectively, by inhibiting luminal differentiation. In conclusion, non-tumorigenic basal cell lines have the inherent ability to undergo EMT, but a mesenchymal-like phenotype does not necessarily correlate with the acquisition of overall stem cell/progenitor features. Based on our findings, we propose that EMT in normal basal cells and claudin-low breast cancers reflects abnormal/incomplete myoepithelial differentiation.

title: Involvement of members of the Rab family and related small GTPases in autophagosome formation and maturation
text: Macroautophagy, a process in which cytosolic components and organelles are engulfed and broken down by a double-membrane structure, can be seen as a specialized, multi-step membrane transport process. It intersects with the pathways of exocytic and endocytic membrane trafficking. Several Rab GTPases, which regulate the traffic of secretory and endocytic membranes, have been found to have critical or accessory roles in autophagy. The formation of the pre-autophagosomal isolation membrane, also known as the phagophore, relies on the functionality of Rab1. A non-traditional mode of autophagosome generation from the trans-Golgi or endosome requires Rab9. Other Rabs, including Rab5, Rab24, Rab33, and Rab7, have been shown to be necessary or involved at different stages of autophagosomal formation and maturation. Recently, RalB, another small GTPase, was discovered to induce the formation and maturation of the isolation membrane by interacting with the exocyst complex, a known Rab effector. In this article, we summarize the current knowledge about the involvement of Rabs in autophagy and discuss potential mechanisms and future perspectives.

title: Comparative risk of new-onset diabetes mellitus for antihypertensive drugs: A network meta-analysis.
text: The aim of this study was to compare different antihypertensive drugs in terms of their effect on new-onset diabetes mellitus (NOD). NOD refers to the development of diabetes mellitus during the treatment of other diseases like hypertension. A network meta-analysis was conducted to analyze the advantages and disadvantages of these drugs in relation to NOD, focusing on their respective effect rates. The study included 38 articles with a total of 224,140 patients to evaluate the preventive effect of hypertension drugs on NOD. The results of the network meta-analysis showed that both angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers were associated with a lower risk of developing NOD compared to placebo. The ranking probabilities for these treatments were 79.81% and 72.77%, respectively. On the other hand, β-blockers and calcium channel blockers were found to significantly increase the probability of developing NOD. The odds ratio for β-blockers was 2.18 (95% credible intervals: 1.36-3.50), while for calcium channel blockers it was 1.16 (95% credible intervals: 1.05-1.29). In conclusion, angiotensin receptor blockers were found to have an advantage over other treatments in terms of preventing NOD.

title: Transformation of mammalian cells by constitutively active MAP kinase kinase.
text: The activation of mitogen-activated protein (MAP) kinase kinase (MAPKK) triggers the activation of MAP kinase in a pathway that facilitates cellular responses to growth and differentiation factors. Certain oncogenes, such as ras, src, raf, and mos, have been suggested to transform cells by extending the activated state of MAPKK and other components in the signaling pathway. To investigate this theory, researchers developed constitutively active MAPKK mutants with basal activities that were up to 400 times higher than the unphosphorylated wild-type kinase. When these mutants were expressed in mammalian cells, they activated AP-1-regulated transcription. The cells formed transformed foci, grew effectively in soft agar, and exhibited high tumorigenicity in nude mice. These findings demonstrate that the continuous activation of MAPKK alone is sufficient to promote cell transformation.

title: Psychological treatment of malignant vasovagal syncope due to bloodphobia.
text: We conducted a study on a 17-year-old boy who frequently fainted due to blood-injury phobia. In our syncope unit, we examined his cardiovascular reflexes and recorded a 50-second period of asystole. The Pediatric Psychosocial Department treated him using systematic desensitization techniques involving muscular tension and cognitive approaches. Since then, he has not encountered any further syncopal events.

title: QT and QTc dispersion are accurate predictors of cardiac death in newly diagnosed non-insulin dependent diabetes: cohort study.
text: Patients diagnosed with non-insulin dependent diabetes mellitus face an increased risk of cardiovascular disease-related mortality. A small study indicated that a prolonged QT interval could potentially predict cardiac death in patients with diabetic nephropathy who have undergone insulin treatment. However, it remains uncertain whether this holds true for newly diagnosed diabetes patients without any apparent complications. Additionally, QT dispersion, a recently discovered electrocardiographic variable, has been found to predict cardiac death in patients with chronic heart failure, peripheral vascular disease, or essential hypertension. Our investigation aimed to determine whether it also had predictive value for cardiac death in diabetic patients. The study included 182 patients with non-insulin dependent diabetes mellitus (103 men; average age 52.8 years) from the Dundee cohort of the United Kingdom prospective diabetes study, recruited between 1982 and 1988. These patients were followed up for an average of 10.3 years.

title: Recombinant human IL-10 prevents the onset of diabetes in the nonobese diabetic mouse.
text: The impact of IL-10 on the development of autoimmune diabetes mellitus was examined in the nonobese diabetic (NOD) mouse. The study focused on three aspects of diabetes: the occurrence of high blood sugar levels, the presence of inflammation in the pancreas, and the production of insulin by beta cells. Initially, researchers investigated the effect of antibodies against certain cytokines on the disease's development. The findings revealed that a monoclonal anti-IFN-gamma antibody significantly reduced the likelihood of high blood sugar in female NOD mice, while antibodies against IL-4, IL-5, and IL-10 had no effect. Subsequent experiments involved administering IL-10, a potent inhibitor of IFN-gamma production by TH1 T cells, to 9 and 10-week-old NOD mice through daily subcutaneous injections. This treatment delayed the onset of the disease and notably decreased the occurrence of diabetes. Histopathology analysis of pancreatic tissue showed that IL-10 treatment lessened the severity of inflammation, prevented infiltration of islet cells by immune cells, and promoted normal insulin production by beta cells. Overall, these findings suggest that IL-10 suppresses the initiation and progression of autoimmune pathogenesis associated with diabetes mellitus, indicating its potential as a therapeutic cytokine for this autoimmune disease.

title: Arterial hypertension and progression of chronic kidney disease in children during 10-year ambulatory observation.
text: The objective of this study was to analyze the long-term progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD) in children, focusing on the impact of hypertension (HTN). Patients with HTN exhibited a higher average rate of CKD progression compared to those without HTN. The treatment of hypertension necessitates the use of multidrug regimens, which should be intensified as the duration of CKD increases.

title: Exercise blood flow patterns within and among rat muscles after training.
text:
The purpose of this study was to examine how a long-term, moderate-intensity treadmill training program affects blood flow distribution in the muscles of rats during exercise. One group of male Sprague-Dawley rats trained for 1 hour per day for 13-17 weeks at a speed of 30 meters per minute on a motor-driven treadmill (referred to as the T group). Another group of rats (referred to as the UT group) underwent conditioning for 10 minutes per day for 4 weeks at the same speed. The researchers measured the activity of succinate dehydrogenase, an enzyme involved in muscle metabolism, and found that it was higher in the T group compared to the UT group, indicating a significant training effect.

To assess blood flow, the researchers used radiolabeled microspheres to measure blood flows in 32 hindlimb muscles or muscle parts, as well as other selected organs, during pre-exercise and while the rats ran on the treadmill for 30 seconds, 5 minutes, or 15 minutes at a speed of 30 meters per minute. The data revealed several key findings: 1) there were no differences in total hindlimb muscle blood flow between the UT and T groups at any time; however, 2) the T group had higher heart rates before exercise and higher blood flows in the deep red extensor muscles, suggesting a greater anticipatory response to exercise; 3) the T group showed faster increases in blood flow in the red extensor muscles at the start of exercise; 4) during exercise, the T group had higher blood flows in red extensor muscles, while the UT group had higher blood flows in white muscles; and 5) the T group maintained higher blood flows in the visceral organs during exercise.

These findings demonstrate that exercise training leads to changes in the distribution of blood flow within and among muscles, as well as among organs, during exercise. Specifically, the data suggest that the high-oxidative motor units, which are primarily recruited during the initial stages of moderate treadmill exercise, receive higher blood flows in trained rats. This likely contributes to increased resistance to fatigue.

title: Serious infections after unrelated donor transplantation in 136 children: impact of stem cell source.
text: The comparative infection risks following umbilical cord blood (UCB) and bone marrow (BM) transplantation remain unknown. To address this, we conducted a study comparing serious infections in the two years following pediatric myeloablative unrelated donor transplantation using unmanipulated BM (n = 52), T cell-depleted (TCD) BM (n = 24), or UCB (n = 60) for the treatment of hematologic malignancy. Overall, the cumulative incidence of one or more serious infections was similar across all groups (BM, 81%; TCD, 83%; UCB, 90%; P = .12). Additionally, when considering all serious infections and using unmanipulated BM as the reference, there were no significant differences between groups (TCD relative risk [RR], 1.6; P = .10; UCB RR, 1.0; P = .84). The only notable difference was a higher risk of viral infections in TCD recipients during the first 42 days (RR, 3.5; P = .02). After day 180, TCD recipients had a significantly increased infection risk (RR, 3.1; P = .03), while the risk in UCB recipients (RR, 0.5; P = .23) was comparable to that in BM recipients. Other factors associated with an increased infection risk within the two years post-transplantation included age ≥ 8 years, graft failure, and severe acute graft-versus-host disease. These findings suggest that the risk of serious infection following pediatric UCB transplantation is similar to that observed with unmanipulated BM.

title: The NBS1–Treacle complex controls ribosomal RNA transcription in response to DNA damage
text: The mechanisms involved in the transient silencing of ribosomal RNA synthesis caused by chromosome breakage have been unclear. However, we have now discovered a signaling mechanism that triggers the silencing of rRNA transcription throughout the nucleus in response to DNA damage. This mechanism involves the temporary recruitment of the Nijmegen breakage syndrome protein 1 (NBS1), a key regulator of DNA damage responses, into the nucleoli. Additionally, we have found that TCOF1 (also known as Treacle), a factor involved in ribosome production and mutated in Treacher Collins syndrome, interacts with NBS1. We have demonstrated that the translocation and accumulation of NBS1 in the nucleoli is dependent on Treacle. Finally, we have provided evidence that Treacle-mediated recruitment of NBS1 into the nucleoli regulates the silencing of rRNA in response to distant chromosome breaks.

title: Inflammatory T cells rapidly induce differentiation of human bone marrow stromal cells into mature osteoblasts.
text: The destruction of bone associated with rheumatoid arthritis is largely caused by osteoclastogenic cytokines secreted by activated T cells. While the impact of T cells on osteoclastogenesis has been extensively studied, their effect on osteoblast formation and activity remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate whether activated T cells contribute to increased bone turnover in chronic inflammation by promoting osteoblastic differentiation. The results demonstrate that T cells produce soluble factors that stimulate alkaline phosphatase activity in bone marrow stromal cells and increase the expression of mRNA for Runx2 and osteocalcin. This suggests that T cell derived factors have the ability to induce the differentiation of bone marrow stromal cells into osteoblasts. RANKL mRNA was not detected in highly purified bone marrow stromal cells under any conditions. However, it was consistently expressed in primary osteoblasts and only moderately up-regulated by activated T cell conditioned medium. Interestingly, both bone marrow stromal cells and osteoblasts expressed mRNA for RANK, which was strongly up-regulated in both cell types by activated T cell conditioned medium. Although mRNA for the RANKL decoy receptor, osteoprotegerin, was also up-regulated by activated T cell conditioned medium, its inhibitory effects may be counteracted by an increase in the osteoprotegerin competitor TNF-related apoptosis-inducing ligand. Based on these findings, it is proposed that T cells regulate bone loss during chronic inflammation through a dual mechanism involving direct stimulation of osteoclastogenesis via production of osteoclastogenic cytokines, and indirect induction of osteoblast differentiation and up-regulation of bone turnover through coupling.

title: Prevention of coronary heart disease with pravastatin in men with hypercholesterolemia. West of Scotland Coronary Prevention Study Group.
text:
BACKGROUND: The purpose of this study was to determine if administering pravastatin to men with high cholesterol levels and no history of heart attack could reduce the risk of nonfatal heart attacks and death from coronary heart disease. 

METHODS: A total of 6595 men between the ages of 45 and 64, with an average plasma cholesterol level of 272 +/- 23 mg/dL (7.0 +/- 0.6 mmol/L), were randomly assigned to receive either pravastatin (40 mg each evening) or a placebo. The study lasted for an average of 4.9 years, and clinical endpoints were determined using medical records, electrocardiographic recordings, and the national death registry. 

RESULTS: Pravastatin reduced plasma cholesterol levels by 20% and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels by 26%, while there was no change with the placebo. In the placebo group, there were 248 definite coronary events (nonfatal heart attacks or death from coronary heart disease), compared to 174 in the pravastatin group (a 31% relative reduction in risk with pravastatin; 95% confidence interval, 17 to 43%; P < 0.001). Similar reductions in risk were observed for nonfatal heart attacks (31% reduction, P < 0.001), death from coronary heart disease (definite cases alone: 28% reduction, P = 0.13; definite plus suspected cases: 33% reduction, P = 0.042), and death from all cardiovascular causes (32% reduction, P = 0.033). There was no increase in deaths from noncardiovascular causes in the pravastatin group. Additionally, a 22% reduction in the risk of death from any cause was observed in the pravastatin group (95% confidence interval, 0 to 40%; P = 0.051). 

CONCLUSIONS: Treatment with pravastatin significantly reduced the occurrence of heart attacks and death from cardiovascular causes in men with moderate hypercholesterolemia and no history of heart attack, without negatively impacting the risk of death from noncardiovascular causes.

title: Validation of a migraine-specific questionnaire for use in family studies.
text: Having valid migraine-specific questionnaires available is crucial when analyzing a large number of migraine patients. The Finnish Migraine-Specific Questionnaire has undergone a two-stage validation process. In the first stage, a clinical diagnosis of migraine was made in 100 consecutive patients using the criteria set by the International Headache Society. Then, the Finnish Migraine-Specific Questionnaire was used to independently diagnose migraine based on the patients' responses. In the second stage, 100 questionnaires from an ongoing family study were analyzed, and the respondents were contacted by phone for an interview and migraine diagnosis. Unfortunately, contact could not be made with six cases. The questionnaire showed a sensitivity of 0.99 (167 out of 168; combining validation stages 1 and 2) and a specificity of 0.96 (25 out of 26 cases; validation stage 2) for diagnosing migraine. Additionally, the questionnaire was able to differentiate between migraine with and without aura. The chance-corrected agreement (Cohen's kappa) was 0.804 for diagnoses based on the questionnaire responses alone and 0.858 when combined with the results of the telephone interviews. A Cohen's kappa value greater than 0.75 indicates good agreement. Therefore, the use of the Finnish Migraine-Specific Questionnaire in migraine genetics research is justified.

title: Defining early lineage specification of human embryonic stem cells by the orchestrated balance of canonical Wnt/beta-catenin, Activin/Nodal and BMP signaling.
text: The Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway plays various important roles in embryonic development, stem cell renewal, and cancer progression. In this study, we discovered that increased expression of beta-catenin disrupted the self-renewal of human embryonic stem cells. As a result, a significant portion of these cells developed into primitive streak/mesoderm progenitors, resembling early stages of mammalian embryogenesis. The formation of these progenitors relied on the combined action of beta-catenin, Activin/Nodal, and BMP signaling pathways. Interestingly, blocking BMP signaling completely prevented the generation of mesoderm and caused a shift in cell fate towards anterior primitive streak progenitors. The PI3-kinase/Akt pathway, but not the MAPK pathway, played a crucial role in specifying the anterior primitive streak, partly by enhancing the stability of beta-catenin. Furthermore, the cooperation between Activin/Nodal and Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathways promoted the generation and specification of anterior primitive streak/endoderm. Overall, our findings demonstrate that the balance between Activin/Nodal and BMP signaling pathways determines the cell fate of nascent primitive streak cells induced by canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling in human embryonic stem cells.

title: Sphingosine can pre- and post-condition heart and utilizes a different mechanism from sphingosine 1-phosphate.
text: In line with previous findings, a high concentration (5 microM) of sphingosine was found to be harmful to the heart, as indicated by an increase in the size of the damaged area during ischemia/reperfusion in a rat heart model. On the other hand, sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) at the same concentration was shown to have a protective effect on the heart. However, at a physiological concentration (0.4 microM), both sphingosine and S1P were effective in protecting the heart from injury caused by ischemia/reperfusion, whether they were administered before the ischemic period (preconditioning) or during the reperfusion phase (postconditioning). The protection provided by sphingosine and S1P was evident in both preconditioning and postconditioning, with a recovery of over 75% in left ventricular developed pressure during reperfusion and a decrease in the size of the damaged area from 45% to less than 8% of the at-risk area. When VPC23019, an antagonist of the S1P(1and3) G-protein coupled receptor, was added to the medium during preconditioning or postconditioning along with S1P, it completely blocked the protective effect of S1P. However, VPC 23019 did not affect the ability of 0.4 microM sphingosine to provide preconditioning or postconditioning protection to the heart. Further studies on preconditioning revealed that inhibition of protein kinase C with GF109203X blocked the preconditioning effect of S1P, but had no effect on the preconditioning effect of 0.4 microM sphingosine. Similarly, co-treatment with the PI3 kinase inhibitor wortmanin blocked the preconditioning effect of S1P, but not that of sphingosine. In contrast, inhibition of protein kinase G with KT5823 had no effect on S1P preconditioning, but completely eliminated the preconditioning effect of sphingosine. Additionally, the protein kinase A inhibitory peptide 14-22 amide blocked the preconditioning effect of sphingosine, but not that of S1P. These findings indicate for the first time that sphingosine is not toxic at physiological concentrations, but rather acts as a potent cardioprotectant through a mechanism that is completely different from that of S1P. This mechanism is independent of G-protein coupled receptors and instead utilizes cyclic nucleotide-dependent pathways.

title: Coordination of p300-mediated chromatin remodeling and TRAP/mediator function through coactivator PGC-1alpha.
text: The protein acetyl transferase p300, the TRAP/Mediator complex, and the regulated PGC-1alpha are transcriptional coactivators that interact physically and functionally with PPARgamma. Our study reveals that PGC-1alpha directly interacts with TRAP/Mediator, specifically through the PPARgamma-interacting subunit TRAP220, and enhances TRAP/Mediator-dependent function on DNA templates. Additionally, PGC-1alpha stimulates p300-dependent histone acetylation and transcription on chromatin templates in response to PPARgamma, although it is ineffective on its own. These functions are mediated by distinct interaction domains in PGC-1alpha for PPARgamma, p300, and TRAP220. However, p300 and TRAP220 exhibit ligand-dependent interactions with a common region of PPARgamma. These findings demonstrate that PGC-1alpha plays a crucial role in coordinating chromatin remodeling and preinitiation complex formation or function (transcription) through its dynamic interactions with other proteins.

title: Phospholipid synthesis and lipid composition of subcellular membranes in the unicellular eukaryote Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
text: Improved procedures were used to isolate and analyze the lipid composition and enzymatic activities of various subcellular membranes in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. These membranes included mitochondria, microsomes, plasma membranes, secretory vesicles, vacuoles, nuclear membranes, peroxisomes, and lipid particles. The microsomal fraction was found to be heterogeneous in terms of density and marker proteins, as well as the distribution of phospholipid-synthesizing enzymes. The highest activity of phosphatidylserine synthase was observed in a distinct microsomal subfraction, separate from the heavier microsomes containing phosphatidylinositol synthase and phospholipid N-methyltransferases. The presence of phosphatidylserine decarboxylase exclusively in mitochondria was confirmed. CDO-diacylglycerol synthase activity was detected in both mitochondria and microsomal membranes. The lipid particle fraction exhibited the highest specific activities of glycerol-3-phosphate acyltransferase and sterol delta 24-methyltransferase. Nuclear and plasma membranes, vacuoles, and peroxisomes showed minimal activity of the analyzed lipid-synthesizing enzymes. The plasma membrane and secretory vesicles were enriched in ergosterol and phosphatidylserine. Lipid particles were characterized by their high content of ergosteryl esters. The high content of ergosterol in the plasma membrane and secretory vesicles contributed to their rigidity, as determined by fluorescence anisotropy measurements using trimethylammonium diphenylhexatriene as a probe.

title: Use of health services by prison inmates: comparisons with the community.
text: The future organization of prison healthcare recommends that the NHS and the Prison Service collaborate to plan and deliver healthcare services for prisoners, instead of the Prison Service solely being responsible for this. Therefore, the NHS needs to assess the current demand and provision of prison healthcare. To facilitate joint planning, it is important to gather data on the current utilization of healthcare services. This paper compares the utilization of primary care and inpatient health services by UK prisoners with that of equivalent community populations. In the community, general practitioners and other healthcare professionals, such as nurses, primarily provide primary care. Community residents have access to the full range of outpatient and inpatient facilities offered by the NHS. In prisons, primary care is provided by medical officers, some of whom are general practitioners, as well as nursing grades and health care officers who have received some healthcare training. Some prisons have their own inpatient facilities, known as health care center beds, which offer a limited level of inpatient care that does not have a direct equivalent in the community. Prisoners also have access to NHS outpatient and inpatient facilities, as well as visiting specialists. The prison population experiences a high turnover and fluctuates on a daily basis. Therefore, the average daily population over a one-year period is used to represent the prison population.

title: Regulation of p53 in response to DNA damage
text: The activation of p53 can occur when cells experience various types of stress, such as DNA damage, lack of oxygen, and depletion of nucleotides. Different forms of DNA damage, including those caused by ionising radiation, radio-mimetic drugs, ultraviolet light, and chemicals like methyl methane sulfonate, have been shown to activate p53. Normally, p53 levels are kept low due to its short half-life. Additionally, p53 typically exists in an inactive state with limited ability to bind to DNA and activate transcription. However, when DNA damage occurs, p53 levels rapidly increase and its ability to bind DNA and activate transcription improves. This leads to the activation of genes that regulate cell-cycle arrest, apoptosis, and DNA repair. Recent research suggests that this regulation is primarily achieved through a series of phosphorylation, de-phosphorylation, and acetylation events on the p53 protein. In this discussion, we will explore the nature of these modifications, the enzymes responsible for them, and how changes in p53 modification result in p53 activation.

title: Hydrogen sulphide regulates intracellular pH in vascular smooth muscle cells.
text: We conducted a study to examine the role of hydrogen sulphide (H(2)S) in regulating intracellular pH (pH(i)) in vascular smooth muscle cells and its impact on vasodilation. We found that NaHS, a donor of H(2)S, caused a concentration-dependent decrease in pH(i), ranging from 10 microM to 1mM. The inhibition of the Na(+)/H(+) exchanger with 5-(N-ethyl-N-isopropyl) amiloride (EIPA, 10 microM), or the plasmalemmal Ca(2+)-ATPase with CdCl(2) (20nM), did not affect the effect of NaHS on pH(i). However, when we blocked the Cl(-)/HCO3- exchanger with 4,4'-diisothiocyanatostilbene-2,2'-disulfonic acid (DIDS), we observed a significant reduction in the pH(i) lowering effect of NaHS. Additionally, NaHS increased the activity of the Cl(-)/HCO3- exchanger, as measured using the NH(4)Cl prepulse method. DIDS attenuated the vasorelaxation caused by NaHS, while EIPA and CdCl(2) had no effect. In conclusion, H(2)S leads to intracellular acidification by activating the Cl(-)/HCO3- exchanger, which is partially responsible for the vasorelaxation induced by H(2)S.

title: Cell and biomolecule delivery for tissue repair and regeneration in the central nervous system.
text: Tissue engineering is often used to replace damaged or diseased tissue by utilizing cells and scaffolds. Originally, it was developed as a way to deliver biomolecules like insulin or neurotrophic factors, as cells naturally produce these therapeutic agents. Therefore, cell delivery is an essential aspect of tissue engineering. Controlled release of biomolecules is also crucial for facilitating cell delivery, as these biomolecules can enhance cell engraftment, regulate inflammatory response, and improve the behavior of the delivered cells. This article focuses on advancements in cell and biomolecule delivery for tissue regeneration, particularly in the central nervous system (CNS). The first section discusses encapsulated cell therapy, while the second section explores biomolecule delivery using polymeric nano/microspheres and hydrogels for nerve regeneration and stimulation of endogenous cells. The third section examines combination strategies involving neural stem/progenitor cells or mesenchymal stem cells and biomolecule delivery for tissue regeneration and repair. Throughout each section, the challenges and potential solutions associated with delivering these therapies to the CNS are highlighted.

title: The angiotensin II type 1 receptor blocker olmesartan preferentially improves nocturnal hypertension and proteinuria in chronic kidney disease
text: The available evidence suggests that an altered ambulatory blood pressure (BP) profile, specifically elevated nighttime BP, is indicative of organ damage and is a better predictor of cardiorenal risk in hypertensive patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) compared to clinic BP or daytime BP. This study aimed to investigate the positive effects of olmesartan, an angiotensin II type 1 receptor blocker (ARB), on ambulatory BP profiles and renal function in hypertensive CKD patients. A total of 46 patients were randomly assigned to either the olmesartan add-on group (n=23) or the non-ARB group (n=23). Ambulatory BP monitoring and renal function parameter measurements were conducted at baseline and after a 16-week treatment period. Although the baseline clinic BP levels and the after-treatment/baseline (A/B) ratios of clinic BP levels were similar in both groups, the A/B ratios of ambulatory 24-hour and nighttime BP levels were significantly lower in the olmesartan add-on group. Additionally, the A/B ratios of urinary protein, albumin, and type IV collagen excretion were significantly lower in the olmesartan add-on group compared to the non-ARB group (urinary protein excretion: 0.72±0.41 vs. 1.45±1.48, P=0.030; urinary albumin excretion: 0.73±0.37 vs. 1.50±1.37, P=0.005; urinary type IV collagen excretion: 0.87±0.42 vs. 1.48±0.87, P=0.014), despite similar A/B ratios for the estimated glomerular filtration rate in both groups. These findings suggest that in hypertensive patients with CKD, olmesartan add-on therapy improves the ambulatory BP profile by specifically reducing nighttime BP and concurrently inhibiting renal injury.

title: Surgical vs nonsurgical treatment of adults with displaced fractures of the proximal humerus: the PROFHER randomized clinical trial.
text: The importance of surgery for patients with displaced proximal humeral fractures is uncertain, but its usage is on the rise. The objective of this study was to assess the clinical effectiveness of surgical versus nonsurgical treatment for adults with displaced fractures of the proximal humerus involving the surgical neck. The study, called the Proximal Fracture of the Humerus Evaluation by Randomization (PROFHER) trial, was a pragmatic, multicenter, parallel-group, randomized clinical trial. It recruited 250 patients aged 16 years or older who presented at orthopedic departments of 32 UK National Health Service hospitals between September 2008 and April 2011. The patients were followed up for 2 years, and 215 had complete follow-up data. Fracture fixation or humeral head replacement was performed by experienced surgeons, while nonsurgical treatment involved sling immobilization. Both groups received standardized outpatient and community-based rehabilitation. The primary outcome was the Oxford Shoulder Score, assessed over a 2-year period. Secondary outcomes included the Short-Form 12 (SF-12), complications, subsequent therapy, and mortality. The results showed no significant difference in the Oxford Shoulder Score between the surgical and nonsurgical groups over the 2-year period. There were also no significant differences in the SF-12 scores, complications, subsequent therapy, or mortality. The study concluded that surgical treatment did not provide better patient-reported clinical outcomes compared to nonsurgical treatment for patients with displaced proximal humeral fractures involving the surgical neck. These findings do not support the increasing trend of surgery for these fractures.

title: Kinetics and Fidelity of the Repair of Cas9-Induced Double-Strand DNA Breaks
text: The Cas9 enzyme, which is guided by RNA, is a powerful tool for editing genomes. However, there is limited knowledge about the speed and accuracy of the repair process that occurs after Cas9 cuts DNA in living cells. To address this, we have developed a method to measure the speed of repair for specific locations in human cells. By analyzing the repaired DNA over time, we have found that the repair rates can vary and are often slow, with some repairs taking up to 10 hours. Additionally, the repair of the DNA breaks is prone to errors. Both traditional and microhomology-mediated pathways contribute to these erroneous repairs. By estimating the rate constants for each pathway, we have discovered that the balance between them changes over time and can be influenced by ionizing radiation. Our approach provides valuable quantitative information about the speed and accuracy of DNA repair at specific locations, revealing that Cas9-induced DNA breaks are repaired in an unconventional manner.
