title: Network meta-analysis for indirect treatment comparisons.
text: I will discuss techniques to evaluate the comparative effectiveness of two treatments that have not been directly compared in a randomized trial, but have been compared to other treatments individually. These network meta-analysis methods enable us to estimate both the variability in the effectiveness of a specific treatment and the inconsistency in the evidence from different treatment pairs. I will provide a straightforward estimation approach using linear mixed models, which will be applied in a meta-analysis of treatments for acute myocardial infarction.

title: Liver transplantation and opioid dependence.
text:
Chronic hepatitis C is the primary reason for liver transplantation in the United States, with intravenous drug use being the main cause of hepatitis C virus transmission, accounting for about 60% of cases. However, the United Network of Organ Sharing (UNOS) does not address substance use among liver transplantation patients. The objective of this study was to identify the criteria for admission to the UNOS liver transplantation waiting list for individuals with addiction-related issues and to examine the problems faced by patients prescribed maintenance methadone after transplantation. 

A mail survey was conducted in March 2000, followed by telephone interviews in May and June 2000, involving all 97 adult US liver transplantation programs affiliated with UNOS. The main focus was on the acceptance and management of patients with a history of substance use disorder. 

Out of the 97 programs surveyed, 87 (90%) responded. It was found that all programs accept applicants with a history of alcoholism or other addictions, including heroin dependence. The majority of programs (88%) require a minimum of 6 months of abstinence from alcohol and 83% require abstinence from illicit drugs. Additionally, 94% of programs have addiction treatment requirements and 86% seek consultations from substance abuse specialists. However, only 56% of programs accept patients receiving methadone maintenance. It was reported that approximately 180 patients receiving methadone maintenance have undergone liver transplantation. 

In conclusion, most liver transplantation programs have established policies for patients with substance use disorders. However, there seems to be a lack of representation for opiate-dependent patients receiving opiate replacement therapy in transplantation programs. There is little evidence to suggest that opiate replacement therapy negatively impacts liver transplantation outcomes. Policies that require the discontinuation of methadone in 32% of programs contradict the evidence supporting the effectiveness of long-term replacement therapies and may lead to relapse in previously stable patients.

title: RIG-I-mediated antiviral responses to single-stranded RNA bearing 5'-phosphates.
text: The activation of antiviral immunity, which is mediated by the RNA helicase enzymes RIG-I and MDA5, is believed to be triggered by double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) produced during viral replication. Our research has shown that influenza A virus infection does not produce dsRNA. Instead, RIG-I is activated by viral genomic single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) that has 5'-phosphates. However, this activation is blocked by the influenza protein NS1, which forms a complex with RIG-I in infected cells. These findings indicate that RIG-I acts as a sensor for ssRNA and may be targeted by viruses to evade the immune response. Furthermore, it suggests that the ability of RIG-I to detect 5'-phosphorylated RNA has evolved in the innate immune system as a way to distinguish between self and nonself.

title: In-hospital switching between adenosine diphosphate receptor inhibitors in patients with acute myocardial infarction treated with percutaneous coronary intervention: Insights into contemporary practice from the TRANSLATE-ACS study.
text: The aim of this study was to investigate the frequency, effectiveness, and safety of switching between adenosine diphosphate (ADP) receptor inhibitors in routine clinical practice for patients with acute myocardial infarction. The study included 11,999 patients who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention at 230 hospitals between April 2010 and October 2012. The patients were divided into two groups: those initially treated with clopidogrel and those initially treated with prasugrel or ticagrelor. The study found that switching between ADP receptor inhibitors occurred in 11.4% of patients initially treated with clopidogrel and 13.6% of patients initially treated with prasugrel or ticagrelor. The majority of switches occurred after percutaneous coronary intervention or at the time of hospital discharge. The study also found that switching between ADP receptor inhibitors was not associated with an increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events or bleeding. In conclusion, switching between ADP receptor inhibitors is common in clinical practice and does not appear to have a significant impact on patient outcomes.

title: Platelet activation in type 2 diabetes mellitus.
text: Diabetes causes an abnormal metabolic state that makes arteries more susceptible to atherosclerosis. This can affect the functioning of various cell types, including endothelium and platelets. Specifically, changes in platelet metabolism and signaling pathways within platelets may contribute to the development of atherothrombotic complications in diabetes. There are several mechanisms that can lead to increased platelet aggregation, with hyperglycemia being a potential cause of platelet activation in vivo. Hyperglycemia can also cause nonenzymatic glycation of platelet glycoproteins, altering their structure and function, as well as affecting the dynamics of membrane lipids. Additionally, hyperglycemia-induced oxidative stress can lead to increased peroxidation of arachidonic acid, resulting in the formation of biologically active isoprostanes. This oxidative stress also activates transcription factors and triggers the expression of redox-sensitive genes, leading to a pro-thrombotic state in the endothelium. This initial platelet activation, adhesion, and subsequent formation of platelet aggregates are all influenced by increased oxidative stress. Clinical trials have shown that controlling metabolic factors can improve platelet function in diabetic patients, and aspirin treatment may be particularly beneficial for this population. Proper medical management of diabetes is crucial for improving long-term outcomes in this high-risk group.

title: Nicotinic receptor-mediated neuroprotection in neurodegenerative disease models.
text: There is a wealth of evidence, spanning various levels of research, that suggests a connection between nicotinic transmission and the development of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD). This article aims to present evidence supporting the protective effects of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) and the signaling pathways involved in this mechanism. The data primarily comes from our studies using cultured primary neurons from rats. We found that nicotine-induced protection was hindered by an antagonist of the alpha7 nAChR, an inhibitor of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K), and an inhibitor of Src. Additionally, nicotine administration led to increased levels of phosphorylated Akt, which is an effector of PI3K, as well as increased levels of Bcl-2 and Bcl-x. Based on these experimental findings, our hypothesis is that the alpha7 nAChR stimulates the Src family, which activates PI3K to phosphorylate Akt. This phosphorylation then transmits a signal that up-regulates Bcl-2 and Bcl-x. The up-regulation of these proteins may protect cells from neuronal death caused by beta-amyloid (Abeta), glutamate, and rotenone. These findings suggest that therapeutic interventions aimed at stimulating nAChRs could potentially delay the progression of neurodegenerative diseases like AD and PD.

title: High-throughput parallel proteogenomics: a bacterial case study.
text: In recent years, a new method called "proteogenomics" has emerged as a paradigm for genome annotation. This method utilizes peptide MS to annotate a genome by mapping peptides to a six-frame translation of the genome, including splice databases. This can help refine gene models by identifying exon boundaries, novel genes, gene boundaries, frame shifts, reverse strands, translated UTRs, and novel splice junctions. However, there are challenges in assigning confidence to the resulting annotation and applying gene model refinements. Many gene prediction tools are designed for specific types of genomes and have been trained on model organisms like Arabidopsis thaliana and Escherichia coli. Additionally, these tools have varying degrees of features that can use external evidence. In this study, we describe an approach for preprocessing mass spectra and optimizing the MS/MS search for a given dataset. We also discuss future challenges in proteogenomics and propose better strategies for addressing them using existing tools. To illustrate our approach, we use Bradyrhizobium diazoefficiens, a nitrogen-fixing bacteria with a 9.1 Mb genome, as a case study. We employ the latest proteogenomics tools and multiple gene models to cross-validate the proteogenomics annotations.

title: Keratinocyte-specific transglutaminase of cultured human epidermal cells: relation to cross-linked envelope formation and terminal differentiation.
text: In cultured normal human epidermal keratinocytes, the main type of cross-linking enzyme known as transglutaminase is primarily found in the cell particulate material. However, it can be made soluble by using a nonionic detergent. When subjected to anion-exchange or gel-filtration chromatography, it elutes as a single peak. Monoclonal antibodies that were developed against the particulate enzyme show a cross-reaction with one of the two transglutaminases present in the cell cytosol. The second cytosolic transglutaminase, which has different kinetic and physical properties compared to the first one, does not show any cross-reaction and is not necessary for the formation of the keratinocyte cross-linked envelope in laboratory conditions. The antibodies against transglutaminase stain the more differentiated layers of the epidermis in a similar pattern as the anti-involucrin antiserum. These findings support the hypothesis that the identified transglutaminase plays a role in the formation of the cross-linked envelope in the living organism.

title: The effects of genetic and pharmacological blockade of the CB1 cannabinoid receptor on anxiety.
text: The purpose of this study was to compare the impact of disrupting CB1 cannabinoid receptors through genetics and pharmacology on anxiety levels using the elevated plus-maze test. The first experiment involved comparing the behavior of CB1-knockout mice with wild-type mice. In the second experiment, both CB1-knockout and wild-type mice were administered the cannabinoid antagonist SR141716A at varying doses (0, 1, and 3 mg/kg). The untreated CB1-knockout mice exhibited reduced exploration of the open arms of the plus-maze apparatus, indicating higher levels of anxiety compared to the wild-type mice. However, there were no noticeable changes in locomotion. The CB1-knockout mice injected with the vehicle in the second experiment also displayed increased anxiety compared to the wild-type mice. Surprisingly, the cannabinoid antagonist SR141716A reduced anxiety levels in both the wild-type and CB1-knockout mice, with minimal impact on locomotor behavior. Recent evidence suggests the presence of a new cannabinoid receptor in the brain, and it has been demonstrated that SR141716A binds to both the CB1 receptor and this potential new receptor. The data presented in this study supports these findings, as the cannabinoid receptor antagonist affected anxiety levels in both the wild-type and CB1-knockout mice. It is tentatively suggested that the difference in effects between the genetic and pharmacological blockade of the CB1 receptor indicates a potential role of the new receptor in anxiety.

title: Immune activation and HIV persistence: implications for curative approaches to HIV infection.
text: Despite successfully suppressing HIV replication with combination antiretroviral therapy, both the virus and chronic inflammation/immune dysfunction continue to persist indefinitely. Understanding the relationship between the virus and the host immune system during treatment could potentially lead to new interventions that aim to either cure the infection or prevent the development of inflammation-related diseases. Chronic inflammation and immune dysfunction can contribute to the persistence of HIV by promoting virus production, creating new cells that the virus can infect, facilitating infection of both activated and resting cells, altering the movement of susceptible cells, increasing the growth of infected cells, and hindering the normal mechanisms that clear HIV from the body. Likewise, ongoing HIV production or replication can also contribute to persistent inflammation and immune dysfunction. The emerging data on these matters strongly suggest the existence of a harmful cycle in which HIV persistence triggers inflammation, which in turn further supports HIV persistence.

title: Tissue-specific alterations in the glucocorticoid sensitivity of immune cells following repeated social defeat in mice
text: The role of endogenous glucocorticoids (GC) in ending the inflammatory response after infection and tissue injury is important. However, recent findings suggest that stress can hinder the anti-inflammatory effects of these hormones. Mice that were repeatedly exposed to social disruption (SDR) stress showed reduced sensitivity to the immunosuppressive effects of corticosterone (CORT) when their splenocytes were stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS). This was evident through increased production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and improved cell survival. The presence of myeloid cells expressing the CD11b marker was found to be crucial in this process. We aimed to investigate whether the bone marrow could be a potential source of these GC-insensitive cells. Our study revealed that LPS-stimulated bone marrow cells, without any experimental stress, were essentially resistant to GC and maintained high levels of cell viability even after CORT treatment. However, repeated exposure to acute stress for 2, 4, or 6 days resulted in an increase in GC sensitivity of the bone marrow cells. This increase was associated with elevated mRNA expression of granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF), an increase in the number of myeloid progenitors, and a decrease in the proportion of mature CD11b+ cells. These changes in the cellular composition of the bone marrow were accompanied by an increase in the number of CD11b+ cells in the spleen. When assessing GC sensitivity in both the bone marrow and spleen simultaneously, a significant negative correlation was observed, suggesting that social stress causes the redistribution of GC-insensitive myeloid cells from the bone marrow to the spleen.

title: Delays in the diagnosis of lung cancer.
text:
The aim of this study was to investigate the delays experienced by patients with lung cancer who were referred to a regional cancer center. A prospective cohort of patients with newly diagnosed lung cancer were surveyed over a period of three months to assess the time it took for them to be diagnosed. The patients were asked about when they first experienced symptoms, when they saw their doctor, what tests were done, when they saw a specialist, and when they started treatment. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the different time intervals.

Out of the 73 patients who were approached, 56 agreed to participate in the study. However, only 52 patients were interviewed as two had passed away before they could be interviewed and two could not be reached. The average age of the patients was 68 years. The distribution of the stages of lung cancer was as follows: 10% had stage IB/IIA, 20% had stage IIIA, and 70% had stage IIIB/IV. The patients waited a median of 21 days before seeing a doctor and an additional 22 days to complete any necessary investigations. The median time from presentation to specialist referral was 27 days, and it took a further 23.5 days to complete the investigations. The median wait to start treatment once the patients were seen at the cancer center was 10 days. The overall time from the development of first symptoms to starting treatment was 138 days.

In conclusion, patients with lung cancer experience significant delays from the onset of symptoms to the initiation of treatment. There is a need to raise awareness about the symptoms of lung cancer and to develop and evaluate rapid assessment clinics for patients suspected of having lung cancer.

title: Calcium and peak bone mass.
text:
Previous epidemiological, clinical, and experimental studies have shown that consuming enough calcium during growth can have a significant impact on peak bone mass and density. This can help prevent osteoporosis in postmenopausal and elderly individuals. During adolescence, calcium intake directly affects calcium retention in the skeleton, and it may be necessary to consume up to 1600 mg of calcium per day. Therefore, adolescent females going through puberty are likely the best population to focus on for early prevention of osteoporosis through calcium intake.

Young individuals need to have a positive calcium balance in order to provide the necessary calcium for skeletal development and consolidation. However, it is unclear how much of a positive balance is needed to achieve peak bone mass and density. To determine the calcium requirements for young individuals and understand the factors that affect calcium metabolism during the acquisition of peak bone mass, researchers analyzed 487 calcium balances from previously published reports. They categorized the data based on developmental phase and calcium intake.

The analysis revealed that calcium intake and skeletal modeling/turnover are the most important factors influencing calcium balance during growth. The highest calcium requirements are during infancy and adolescence, followed by childhood and young adulthood. Infants with adequate vitamin D supply and adolescents have higher calcium absorption compared to children and young adults, as they have higher calcium requirements. Calcium absorption during periods of rapid bone modeling/turnover is likely influenced by Nicolaysen's endogenous factor. Urinary calcium levels increase with age and reach a peak at the end of puberty. The analysis also showed that calcium intake has minimal impact on urinary calcium excretion during the period of rapid skeletal formation, with only a weak correlation observed in children and young adults.

Based on these studies, it has been suggested that the recommended daily allowance (RDA) for calcium should be higher than the current guidelines for children, adolescents, and young adults. This is necessary to ensure sufficient skeletal retention of calcium for maximal peak bone mass. In addition to nutrition, heredity (both parents) and endocrine factors (sexual development) also play significant roles in the formation of peak bone mass. The majority of skeletal mass is accumulated by late adolescence, indicating the importance of early timing for achieving peak bone mass.

title: Most clinical tests cannot accurately diagnose rotator cuff pathology: a systematic review.
text:
QUESTION: Can clinical tests accurately diagnose rotator cuff pathology?
DESIGN: This study aimed to systematically review the diagnostic accuracy of clinical tests for rotator cuff pathology.
PARTICIPANTS: Individuals with shoulder pain who underwent clinical testing to diagnose rotator cuff pathology.
OUTCOME MEASURES: Likelihood ratios were used to determine the diagnostic accuracy of clinical tests.
RESULTS: Thirteen studies met the inclusion criteria, evaluating a total of 14 clinical tests in 89 separate diagnostic accuracy evaluations. Only one evaluation, which focused on palpation for supraspinatus ruptures, yielded significant positive and negative likelihood ratios. Out of the 89 evaluations, eight resulted in significant positive or negative likelihood ratios, but these findings were not replicated in other studies. The majority (80%) of the 89 evaluations did not yield significant positive or negative likelihood ratios across different studies.
CONCLUSION: Overall, most clinical tests for rotator cuff pathology were found to be inaccurate and cannot be recommended for clinical use. However, certain tests such as palpation, combined Hawkins/painful arc/infraspinatus test, Napoleon test, lift-off test, belly-press test, or drop-arm test may increase suspicion of a rotator cuff tear, while a negative palpation, empty can test, or Hawkins-Kennedy test may reduce suspicion.

title: Skeletal muscle interleukin‐6 regulates metabolic factors in iWAT during HFD and exercise training
text: The aim of this study was to examine the role of interleukin-6 (IL-6) in skeletal muscle (SkM) in the regulation of adipose tissue metabolism. To do this, muscle-specific IL-6 knockout (IL-6 MKO) mice and IL-6(loxP/loxP) (Floxed) mice were fed a standard rodent diet (Chow), high-fat diet (HFD), or HFD combined with exercise training (HFD ExTr) for 16 weeks. The results showed that total fat mass increased in both genotypes with HFD, but IL-6 MKO mice had lower inguinal adipose tissue (iWAT) mass compared to Floxed mice. Additionally, IL-6 MKO mice had lower levels of glucose transporter 4 (GLUT4) protein, 5'AMP activated protein kinase (AMPK)(Thr172) phosphorylation, and fatty acid synthase (FAS) mRNA in iWAT compared to Floxed mice on Chow. On the other hand, IL-6 MKO mice on HFD had higher levels of AMPK(Thr172) and hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL)(Ser565) phosphorylation, as well as perilipin protein content, compared to HFD Floxed mice. Furthermore, IL-6 MKO mice on HFD ExTr had higher levels of pyruvate dehydrogenase E1α (PDH-E1α) protein compared to HFD ExTr Floxed mice. In conclusion, these findings suggest that SkM IL-6 plays a role in regulating iWAT mass by influencing glucose uptake capacity, as well as lipogenic and lipolytic factors.

title: Risk of hospitalization or death from ischemic heart disease among British vegetarians and nonvegetarians: results from the EPIC-Oxford cohort study.
text:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies have not thoroughly examined the differences in the risk of developing ischemic heart disease (IHD) between vegetarians and nonvegetarians.

OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to investigate the association between a vegetarian diet and the risk of developing incident (nonfatal and fatal) IHD.

DESIGN: The analysis included 44,561 individuals from England and Scotland who participated in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC)-Oxford study. Of these participants, 34% followed a vegetarian diet at the beginning of the study. Incident cases of IHD were identified through hospital records and death certificates. A subset of 1519 individuals without IHD were matched to IHD cases based on sex and age. The risk of IHD based on vegetarian status was assessed using multivariate Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: After an average follow-up of 11.6 years, there were 1235 cases of IHD (1066 hospital admissions and 169 deaths). Compared to nonvegetarians, vegetarians had a lower average BMI (-1.2 kg/m²), non-HDL cholesterol concentration (-0.45 mmol/L), and systolic blood pressure (-3.3 mm Hg). Vegetarians had a 32% lower risk of developing IHD compared to nonvegetarians (HR: 0.68; 95% CI: 0.58, 0.81). This association was only slightly weakened after adjusting for BMI and did not significantly differ based on sex, age, BMI, smoking, or the presence of IHD risk factors.

CONCLUSION: Following a vegetarian diet was associated with a reduced risk of developing IHD, likely due to differences in non-HDL cholesterol and systolic blood pressure.

title: The Supporting Independent Immunization and Vaccine Advisory Committees (SIVAC) initiative: a country-driven, multi-partner program to support evidence-based decision making.
text: The need for evidence-based decision making in immunization programs is heightened by multiple health priorities, limited human resources and logistical capacities, and the high cost of vaccines with limited funds available. The Supporting Independent Immunization and Vaccine Advisory Committees (SIVAC) Initiative aims to assist countries in establishing or strengthening their National Immunization Technical Advisory Groups (NITAGs), which provide recommendations on immunization policies and programs such as vaccination schedules, improving routine immunization coverage, and introducing new vaccines. SIVAC, funded by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, follows a country-driven approach that ensures tailored support and emphasizes the sustainability of NITAGs. SIVAC supports countries by enhancing the capabilities of the NITAG scientific and technical secretariat and offering specific support activities in consultation with the country and other international partners. Furthermore, SIVAC and its partners have developed the NITAG Resource Center, an electronic platform that offers information, tools, and briefings to NITAGs and the wider immunization community.

title: Redox-relevant aspects of the extracellular matrix and its cellular contacts via integrins.
text: IMPORTANCE The extracellular matrix (ECM) plays a crucial role in the functioning of multicellular organisms by providing structural support and signaling cues to cells. When cells attach to the ECM, it triggers a signaling process mediated by reactive oxygen species (ROS). RECENT PROGRESS has shown that ECM attachment influences the production of ROS by cells, which in turn affects the production, assembly, and turnover of the ECM during wound healing and tissue remodeling. Abnormal levels of ROS can lead to excessive ECM production and tissue contraction in fibrotic disorders and desmoplastic tumors. Integrins, which are cell adhesion molecules, have been identified as targets of redox-regulation by ROS. By modifying specific regions within integrin heterodimers, ROS can induce conformational changes that alter integrin binding activity. KEY ISSUES include the role of disulfide bridges within integrin subunits in controlling the transition between inactive and active conformations. These bridges occur in the stalk domain of both integrin subunits, while the ligand-binding headpiece remains unaffected by redox-regulation. FUTURE RESEARCH should focus on understanding the mechanism behind redox-regulation of integrin activation, as it may hold potential for developing new treatments for fibrotic disorders.

title: Prevalence of hypertension and pre-hypertension among adolescents.
text:
The objective of this study was to determine the prevalence of hypertension and pre-hypertension in an adolescent school-screening population based on the 2004 National High Blood Pressure Education Program Working Group guidelines. The study design involved a cross-sectional assessment of blood pressure in 6790 adolescents (11-17 years) in Houston schools from 2003 to 2005. Initial measurements included height, weight, and 4 oscillometric blood pressure readings. Repeat measurements were taken on 2 subsequent occasions for students with consistently high blood pressure. The final prevalence was adjusted for loss to follow-up, and logistic regression was used to assess risk factors.

The results showed that at the initial screening, 81.1% of the adolescents had normal blood pressure, 9.5% had pre-hypertension, and 9.4% had hypertension (8.4% Stage 1; 1% Stage 2). After three screenings, the prevalence changed to 81.1% normal, 15.7% pre-hypertension, and 3.2% hypertension (2.6% Stage 1; 0.6% Stage 2). The prevalence of hypertension and pre-hypertension increased with higher body mass index. Factors such as sex, race, and classification as at-risk for overweight or overweight were independently associated with pre-hypertension. Only classification as overweight was associated with hypertension.

In conclusion, the application of new classification guidelines for adolescents with elevated blood pressure revealed that approximately 20% are at risk for hypertension. Further research is needed to determine the significance of each blood pressure category and refine the definitions to account for blood pressure variability.

title: Increased short- and long-term risk of inflammatory bowel disease after salmonella or campylobacter gastroenteritis.
text:
BACKGROUND & OBJECTIVES The pathogenesis of inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) may involve various commensal enteric bacteria, including potentially pathogenic ones. In this study, we aimed to compare the risk of IBD between patients with documented Salmonella or Campylobacter gastroenteritis and a control group from the same population in Denmark, matched for age and gender.

METHODS We identified 13,324 patients with Salmonella/Campylobacter gastroenteritis from laboratory registries in North Jutland and Aarhus counties, Denmark, between 1991 and 2003. We also selected 26,648 unexposed controls from the same counties. We excluded 176 exposed patients with pre-existing IBD, along with their 352 unexposed controls, and 80 unexposed individuals with pre-existing IBD before the Salmonella/Campylobacter infection. The final study cohort consisted of 13,148 exposed and 26,216 unexposed individuals, who were followed for up to 15 years (mean, 7.5 years).

RESULTS Among the study participants, 107 exposed individuals (1.2%) and 73 unexposed individuals (0.5%) were diagnosed with IBD for the first time. After adjusting for age, gender, and comorbidity, the Cox proportional hazards regression analysis showed a hazard ratio (95% confidence interval) of 2.9 (2.2-3.9) for IBD during the entire study period. Excluding the first year after the Salmonella/Campylobacter infection, the hazard ratio was 1.9 (1.4-2.6). The increased risk of IBD in exposed subjects was consistent throughout the 15-year observation period. The risk was similar for both Salmonella (n = 6463) and Campylobacter (n = 6685) infections, as well as for a first-time diagnosis of Crohn's disease (n = 47) and ulcerative colitis (n = 133).

CONCLUSIONS This population-based cohort study with complete follow-up provides evidence of an increased risk of IBD in individuals with a history of Salmonella/Campylobacter gastroenteritis, as documented in laboratory registries.

title: Establishment of a cell line (NPC/HK1) from a differentiated squamous carcinoma of the nasopharynx.
text: A cell line of squamous epithelial cells was successfully established from a recurrent squamous carcinoma in the nasopharynx of a Chinese male, 17 and a half years after radiation therapy. This cell line, named NPC/HK1, has been cultured for a year and has undergone 72 passages. Examination under light and electron microscopes confirmed that the cells are of the squamous epithelial type. When these cells were transplanted into athymic nude BALB/c (nu/nu) mice, tumors resembling well-differentiated squamous carcinomas were observed at the injection sites. These tumors closely resembled the original human tumor from which the cell line was derived. Karyotypic analysis revealed that the cells have an abnormal number of chromosomes (aneuploid) with a modal chromosome count of 74, including both numerical and structural abnormalities. No viral particles or Epstein-Barr viral nuclear antigen (EBNA) were detected in the cells from the primary culture or in several subcultures that were tested. The presence of EBNA in touch smears prepared from the biopsy tissue was inconclusive. Attempts to infect the subcultured cells with EBV from P3HR1 and B95-8 cells were unsuccessful.

title: Effect of lipid restriction on mitochondrial free radical production and oxidative DNA damage.
text: Numerous studies have demonstrated that reducing calorie intake by 40% can reduce the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in mitochondria of rodents. Additionally, we have recently discovered that restricting protein intake by 40% for 7 weeks, without significant calorie restriction, also decreases ROS production in the liver of rats. This finding is intriguing because protein restriction has been linked to increased lifespan in rodents. In our current study, we aimed to investigate the impact of dietary lipids on the effects of caloric restriction on mitochondrial oxidative stress. We conducted experiments using semipurified diets and reduced lipid intake by 40% in male Wistar rats, while keeping other dietary components at the same level as the control group. After 7 weeks of treatment, we observed significant increases in oxygen consumption with complex I-linked substrates (pyruvate/malate and glutamate/malate) in the liver mitochondria of rats on the lipid-restricted diet. However, there were no changes in mitochondrial H(2)O(2) production or oxidative damage to mitochondrial or nuclear DNA in the lipid-restricted group. It is worth noting that oxidative damage to mitochondrial DNA was significantly higher than that of nuclear DNA in both dietary groups. These findings suggest that lipids do not play a role in the decrease of mitochondrial ROS production and DNA damage observed in caloric restriction, further supporting the potential role of dietary proteins in these effects.

title: Kruppel-like factor 2 is a transcriptional regulator of chronic and acute inflammation.
text: The activation of myeloid cells is necessary for an effective innate immune response, but it must be carefully regulated to avoid harm to the host tissue. Kruppel-like factor 2 (KLF2) is a powerful controller of the proinflammatory activation of myeloid cells. Studies have shown that human subjects with acute or chronic inflammatory disorders have a decrease of approximately 30% to 50% in KLF2 levels. To understand the impact of this reduction, we examined the biological response to inflammation in mice with partial deficiency of KLF2 (KLF2(+/-)). Our findings demonstrate that a lack of KLF2 influences the in vivo response to both acute (sepsis) and subacute (skin) inflammatory challenges. We have also discovered that the anti-inflammatory effects of KLF2 are linked to the inhibition of NF-κB transcriptional activity. These observations provide valuable insights into how KLF2 regulates these inflammatory processes and suggest that manipulating KLF2 could be a potential therapeutic strategy.

title: Simian immunodeficiency viruses replication dynamics in African non-human primate hosts: common patterns and species-specific differences.
text:
In order to identify common characteristics of simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) infections in various naturally infected host species, we conducted a comparison of viral replication dynamics in different monkey species. Specifically, we examined 31 African green monkeys (10 sabeus, 15 vervets, and seven Caribbean AGMs), 14 mandrills, and three sooty mangabeys (SMs) that were infected with their respective species-specific viruses in a controlled experiment.

The results of our study showed that after infection, the SIVs replicated rapidly, reaching high viral loads (VLs) of 10(5)-10(9) copies/ml of plasma between days 9-14 post-infection (p.i). Set point viremia, which refers to the stable viral load reached during the chronic phase of infection, was established between days 42 and 60 p.i. In SMs and mandrills, the set point viremia levels were approximately 10(5)-10(6) copies/ml, while in AGMs, the levels were lower, ranging from 10(3)-10(5) copies/ml. Interestingly, the viral genome structure did not correlate with VL during the chronic phase. For example, SIVmnd-2, which contains the vpx gene, and SIVmnd-1, which lacks the vpu or vpx genes, replicated to similar levels in mandrills. Additionally, the viral strain played a role in determining VL, as vervets infected with different viral strains exhibited distinct patterns of viral replication. However, the replication pattern of SIVagm.sab, which utilizes both CCR5 and CXCR4 co-receptors, was similar to that of the other viruses.

In conclusion, our findings demonstrate a common pattern of SIV replication in both naturally and experimentally infected hosts. This pattern is similar to what is observed in pathogenic SIV infections in macaques. Therefore, it suggests that the differences in clinical outcomes between pathogenic and non-pathogenic infections are primarily influenced by host responses rather than the characteristics of the virus itself.

title: The role of the transcription factor KLF2 in vascular development and disease.
text: The zinc-finger transcription factor KLF2 plays a crucial role in converting the mechanical forces generated by blood flow into molecular signals that regulate various biological responses. Initially identified as a transcription factor responsive to blood flow in endothelial cells, KLF2 is now recognized to be expressed in different cell types and involved in numerous developmental and disease-related processes. These include maintaining endothelial balance, regulating blood vessel function, controlling vascular growth and remodeling, and modulating inflammation. This review provides an overview of the current knowledge about KLF2, with a particular emphasis on its impact on vascular biology.

title: Implementation of contemporary oral antiplatelet treatment guidelines in patients with acute coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a report from the GReek AntiPlatelet rEgistry (GRAPE).
text:
BACKGROUND: Limited data is available regarding the implementation of current guidelines for oral antiplatelet treatment in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) who undergo percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).

METHODS: The GReek AntiPlatelet rEgistry (GRAPE) is a prospective, observational, multicenter cohort study that began in January 2012. The study focuses on the contemporary use of P2Y12 inhibitors. We assessed the appropriateness of P2Y12 inhibitor selection at the start and at discharge using an eligibility-assessing algorithm based on contraindications, specific warnings, and precautions for P2Y12 inhibitors.

RESULTS: Initially, 45.8% of patients had an appropriate P2Y12 inhibitor selection, 47.2% had a less preferable selection, and 6.6% had an inappropriate selection. At discharge, 64.1% had an appropriate selection, 29.2% had a less preferable selection, and 6.6% had an inappropriate selection. Clopidogrel was the most commonly chosen less preferable option, both initially (69.7%) and at discharge (75.6%). The initial appropriate selection of newer agents was high (79.2%-82.8%), and it further increased at discharge (89.4%-89.8%). Inappropriate selection of newer agents decreased from 17.2%-20.8% initially to 10.2%-10.6% at discharge. Factors such as increased bleeding risk, presentation with ST elevation myocardial infarction, and absence of reperfusion within the first 24 hours were the most significant predictors of appropriate P2Y12 selection initially. Age ≥75 years, increased bleeding risk, and regional trends mostly influenced appropriate P2Y12 selection at discharge.

CONCLUSIONS: The adherence to recently released guidelines for oral antiplatelet therapy was satisfactory in the GRAPE study. Clopidogrel was commonly used as a less preferable option, while the selection of prasugrel or ticagrelor was mostly appropriate. Certain factors can predict the implementation of guidelines at the start and at discharge. The study is registered on clinicaltrials.gov with the identifier NCT01774955.

title: Comorbidity of depressive and anxiety disorders in chronic daily headache and its subtypes.
text:
AIM: This study aims to examine the prevalence of depressive and anxiety disorders in individuals with chronic daily headache. 

BACKGROUND: There is a lack of available data regarding the extent of psychiatric comorbidity in patients with different subtypes of chronic daily headache. 

METHODS: We enrolled consecutive patients with chronic daily headache who visited a headache clinic between November 1998 and December 1999. The subtypes of chronic daily headache were classified based on the criteria proposed by Silberstein et al. A psychiatrist conducted evaluations using the structured Mini-International Neuropsychiatric Interview to assess the presence of depressive and anxiety disorders. 

RESULTS: A total of 261 patients with chronic daily headache were included in the study. The average age was 46 years, and 80% of the participants were women. Transformed migraine was diagnosed in 152 patients (58%), while chronic tension-type headache was diagnosed in 92 patients (35%). Among those with transformed migraine, 78% had psychiatric comorbidity, including major depression (57%), dysthymia (11%), panic disorder (30%), and generalized anxiety disorder (8%). In patients with chronic tension-type headache, 64% had psychiatric diagnoses, including major depression (51%), dysthymia (8%), panic disorder (22%), and generalized anxiety disorder (1%). After controlling for age and sex, the frequency of anxiety disorders was significantly higher in individuals with transformed migraine (P =.02). Both depressive and anxiety disorders were more prevalent in women. 

CONCLUSION: Psychiatric comorbidity, particularly major depression and panic disorders, was found to be highly prevalent in patients with chronic daily headache attending a headache clinic. These findings highlight that women and individuals with transformed migraine are at a higher risk of psychiatric comorbidity.

title: The precursor form of IL-1alpha is an intracrine proinflammatory activator of transcription.
text: Recent evidence suggests that certain cytokines, although primarily known for their effects on cell surface receptors, also have functions within the nucleus. In this study, we examined the precursor form of IL-1alpha in different cells and evaluated its activity in the presence of IL-1 receptor antagonist, which prevents receptor signaling. Initially located in the cytoplasm of resting cells, IL-1alpha moved to the nucleus after activation by endotoxin, a Toll-like receptor ligand. The precursor form of IL-1alpha, but not the mature form, significantly activated the transcriptional machinery in the GAL4 system. This activation was mainly attributed to the N terminus, where the nuclear localization sequence is located. When IL-1 receptor signaling was blocked, overexpression of the precursor and propiece forms of IL-1alpha were enough to activate NF-kappaB and AP-1. Cells that overproduced the precursor form of IL-1alpha released IL-8 and IL-6 cytokines and showed increased sensitivity to low concentrations of tumor necrosis factor alpha or IFN-gamma. These findings suggest that the intracellular functions of IL-1alpha may have an unexpected role in inflammation. During disease-related events, the cytosolic precursor moves to the nucleus and enhances the transcription of proinflammatory genes. Since this mechanism is not affected by extracellular inhibitors, targeting the intracellular functions of IL-1alpha could be beneficial in certain inflammatory conditions.

title: Three-dimensional structure of the AAH26994.1 protein from Mus musculus, a putative eukaryotic Urm1.
text: Using NMR spectroscopy, we have determined the solution structure of protein AAH26994.1 from Mus musculus. Our findings suggest that this protein represents the first three-dimensional structure of a ubiquitin-related modifier 1 (Urm1) protein. By comparing amino acid sequences, we have identified AAH26994.1 as a member of the Urm1 family of ubiquitin-like modifier proteins. The most well-studied member of this family is known to play a role in nutrient sensing, invasive growth, and budding in yeast. Although proteins in this family have only a weak sequence similarity to ubiquitin, the structure of AAH26994.1 bears a striking resemblance to the MoaD subunits of molybdopterin synthases. Notably, the known structures of three bacterial MoaD proteins share 14%-26% sequence identity with AAH26994.1. Both AAH26994.1 and the MoaD proteins exhibit the characteristic secondary structure fold of ubiquitin, but they differ from ubiquitin in regions outside of this fold. This structural similarity supports the hypothesis that ubiquitin and ubiquitin-related proteins evolved from a protein-based sulfide donor system similar to that of molybdopterin synthases.

title: Concurrent endometrial carcinoma in women with a biopsy diagnosis of atypical endometrial hyperplasia: a Gynecologic Oncology Group study.
text:
Adenocarcinoma of the endometrium is the most common type of gynecologic cancer in the United States, with around 36,000 cases of invasive carcinoma diagnosed each year. The majority of these cases (75-80%) are of the endometrioid adenocarcinoma (EC) subtype. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of concurrent carcinoma in women diagnosed with atypical endometrial hyperplasia (AEH), a precursor lesion to endometrial cancer.

The study included women who had received a community diagnosis of AEH. Biopsy samples were independently reviewed by three gynecologic pathologists using the criteria set by the International Society of Gynecologic Pathologists/World Health Organization. Participants underwent hysterectomy within 12 weeks of enrollment in the study, without receiving any interim treatment. The hysterectomy slides were also reviewed by the study pathologists for further analysis.

Between November 1998 and June 2003, a total of 306 women were enrolled in the study. However, 17 women were excluded from the analysis due to unreadable slides, non-endometrial slides, unavailability of slides, or evidence of interval intervention in the hysterectomy specimens. Therefore, the current analysis included 289 patients.

The review of the AEH biopsy specimens by the study panel yielded the following interpretations: 25.6% were diagnosed as less than AEH, 39.8% as AEH, and 29.1% as endometrial carcinoma. In 5.5% of cases, there was no consensus on the biopsy diagnosis. The rate of concurrent endometrial carcinoma among the analyzed specimens was 42.6%. Of these cases, 30.9% were myoinvasive, and 10.6% involved the outer 50% of the myometrium.

Among the women with hysterectomy specimens showing carcinoma, 18.9% had a biopsy consensus diagnosis of less than AEH, 39.1% had a diagnosis of AEH, and 64.3% had a diagnosis of carcinoma. Among the women with no consensus in their biopsy diagnosis, 62.5% had carcinoma in their hysterectomy specimens.

In conclusion, the prevalence of endometrial carcinoma in patients with a community hospital diagnosis of AEH was found to be high (42.6%). Therefore, when considering management strategies for women with a biopsy diagnosis of AEH, both clinicians and patients should be aware of the significant rate of concurrent carcinoma.

title: The prevalence and clustering of four major lifestyle risk factors in an English adult population.
text:
This study aimed to investigate the clustering of four major lifestyle risk factors (smoking, heavy drinking, lack of fruit and vegetable consumption, and lack of physical activity) and the variation across different socio-demographic groups in the adult population of England. The data used for this study was obtained from the 2003 Health Survey for England, with a sample size of 11,492 participants. The clustering of risk factors was analyzed by comparing the observed and expected prevalence of different combinations. A multinomial multilevel regression model was employed to examine the socio-demographic variation in the clustering of these risk factors. 

The findings of this study revealed that a majority of the English population simultaneously exhibit multiple lifestyle risk factors when assessed against British health recommendations. Clustering of risk factors was observed at both ends of the lifestyle spectrum, with a greater prevalence among women compared to men. Furthermore, the study identified that multiple risk factors were more prevalent among men, individuals from lower social class households, singles, and those who were economically inactive. Conversely, the prevalence of multiple risk factors was lower among home owners and older age groups. 

In conclusion, the clustering of multiple risk factors supports the implementation of interventions targeting multiple behaviors rather than focusing on individual behaviors alone.

title: Cutting edge: interleukin 17 signals through a heteromeric receptor complex.
text: IL-17, an inflammatory cytokine, is primarily produced by a specific type of CD4 T cells and plays a crucial role in the development of various autoimmune diseases. The receptor for IL-17, known as IL-17RA, is expressed throughout the body and is essential for the biological effects of IL-17. Although IL-17RA is widely expressed, the main function of IL-17 is to stimulate the production of inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and other mediators by stromal cells. In mouse stromal cells lacking IL-17RA, the response to IL-17 is not effectively replaced by human IL-17RA, indicating the presence of a species-specific component that is necessary for IL-17 activity. This component is called IL-17RC and belongs to the IL-17R family. Therefore, the biological effects of IL-17 rely on a complex formed by IL-17RA and IL-17RC, which suggests a new way of understanding the interactions between the various IL-17 ligands and their receptors.

title: Long non-coding RNAs with low expression levels in cells are enriched in secreted exosomes.
text: The involvement of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in various cellular processes such as chromatin modifications, gene transcription, mRNA translation, and protein function has been established. In our recent study, we observed significant variation in the basal expression levels of a panel of lncRNAs in HeLa and MCF-7 cells, as well as their differential response to DNA damage. Based on this, we hypothesized that lncRNA molecules with distinct cellular expression patterns may exhibit different levels of abundance in secreted exosomes, and that these exosome levels could reflect the cellular response to DNA damage. To investigate this, we characterized the presence of MALAT1, HOTAIR, lincRNA-p21, GAS5, TUG1, and CCND1-ncRNA in exosomes secreted from cultured cells. Interestingly, we observed a different expression pattern of these lncRNAs in exosomes compared to cells. RNA molecules with relatively low expression levels (lincRNA-p21, HOTAIR, and ncRNA-CCND1) were highly enriched in exosomes. TUG1 and GAS5 levels showed a moderate increase in exosomes, while MALAT1, which was the most abundant molecule in cells, was present in exosomes at levels comparable to its cellular abundance. Notably, lincRNA-p21 and ncRNA-CCND1 were the main molecules whose exosome levels best reflected the changes in their cellular levels upon exposure of the cells to bleomycin-induced DNA damage. In conclusion, our findings provide evidence for a selective loading of lncRNAs into exosomes, leading to their differential abundance in these extracellular vesicles.

title: Olanzapine depot exposure in male rats: Dose-dependent lipogenic effects without concomitant weight gain.
text: The use of second-generation antipsychotic drugs like olanzapine often leads to metabolic side effects, such as increased appetite, weight gain, and abnormal lipid levels, in both male and female patients. However, the exact molecular mechanisms behind these side effects are still not fully understood, and studying rodents has been a valuable method for investigating them. Unfortunately, the reliability of rodent models is hindered by the fact that antipsychotics cause weight gain in female rats but not in male rats. Additionally, the short half-life of orally administered olanzapine in rats makes it difficult to maintain stable levels of the drug in their bloodstream. However, we recently discovered that a single injection of a long-acting olanzapine formulation in female rats resulted in clinically relevant levels of the drug in their blood, along with several metabolic abnormalities. In our current study, we found that depot injections of 100-250 mg/kg of olanzapine also produced clinically relevant levels of the drug in male rats. Surprisingly, despite experiencing temporary increased appetite, the male rats actually lost weight instead of gaining it when given olanzapine. This decrease in weight gain was accompanied by a slight increase in markers of thermogenesis in their brown adipose tissue, but the reasons behind this reduction in weight gain are still unclear. Despite the lack of weight gain, olanzapine doses of 200mg/kg or higher did cause significantly higher levels of cholesterol in the blood and activated genes related to lipid production in the liver. These findings confirm that olanzapine stimulates lipid production effects independently of weight gain and suggest that hormonal factors may play a role in the gender-specific metabolic effects of antipsychotics in rats.

title: Glutamate mediates the function of melanocortin receptor 4 on Sim1 neurons in body weight regulation.
text: The role of the melanocortin receptor 4 (MC4R) in maintaining body weight balance is well-known. However, the specific neurotransmitter(s) responsible for MC4R function are largely unknown, resulting in limited knowledge about the second-order neurons in the MC4R neural pathway. Certain brain regions that express Single-minded 1 (Sim1), such as the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus (PVH), play a crucial role in mediating the effects of melanocortin. In this study, we restored MC4R expression in Sim1 neurons in mice lacking the Mc4r gene. This restoration significantly reduced obesity in these mice. However, when we selectively disrupted the release of glutamate from the same Sim1 neurons, the anti-obesity effect was completely reversed. This reversal was due to decreased energy expenditure and increased food intake. Additionally, disrupting glutamate release from adult PVH neurons led to rapid obesity development through reduced energy expenditure and increased food intake. Therefore, this study establishes glutamate as the primary neurotransmitter responsible for mediating the effects of MC4Rs on Sim1 neurons in the regulation of body weight.

title: Intracellular sterol dynamics.
text: In this review, we examine the cellular mechanisms involved in the movement and distribution of cholesterol. Recent research has shed light on how sterols are distributed within cells, including their distribution across the cell membrane. The interaction between cholesterol and other lipids, as well as its involvement in various trafficking processes, determines its concentration in specific membranes. As a result, the distribution of cholesterol varies among different organelles within the cell. The amount of cholesterol present is crucial, as it plays a vital role in membrane function, controlling their physical and chemical properties, as well as important cellular processes like signal transduction and protein trafficking. The movement of cholesterol between organelles is a dynamic process that can occur through both vesicular and non-vesicular mechanisms. Numerous studies have investigated the proteins involved in these processes, providing valuable insights into the relative importance of these two pathways in cholesterol transport. While some trafficking routes are still not well understood, several potential proteins responsible for sterol transport have been extensively studied, leading to a better understanding of the molecular mechanisms involved in cholesterol movement between membranes.

title: A plasma membrane component able to bind and alter virions of poliovirus type 1: studies on cell-free alteration using a simplified assay.
text: In this study, it was found that intact HeLa cells have the ability to bind poliovirus type 1 and convert them into altered particles when incubated at 37°. These altered particles have a slower sedimentation rate compared to virions, lack VP-4, and can be disrupted by sodium dodecyl sulfate. However, their RNA remains intact and resistant to ribonuclease. This allows for the assessment of altered particles and particles that have released their RNA through nuclease digestion with or without sodium dodecyl sulfate treatment. By using this straightforward assay procedure, quantitative measurements of binding and alteration can be obtained. The binding-altering activity is localized in plasma membranes, and it has been demonstrated that pure membranes are capable of carrying out alteration. This membrane-bound activity is eliminated by proteases and nonionic detergents. Only altered particles are formed by membranes, while the release of RNA is not caused by membranes but rather by intact cells. The processes of binding and alteration are closely linked, suggesting that alteration may be a result of binding by multiple receptors in a fluid membrane.

title: Resequencing studies of nonmodel organisms using closely related reference genomes: optimal experimental designs and bioinformatics approaches for population genomics.
text: The decreasing costs of next-generation sequencing (NGS) experiments have opened up a wide range of genomic questions that can now be studied in nonmodel organisms. However, conducting experimental designs and analyzing NGS data from less well-known species can be challenging due to the lack of genomic resources. In this study, we explore different experimental designs and bioinformatics approaches to estimate variability and neutrality tests based on the site-frequency-spectrum (SFS) using individual resequencing data. We specifically focus on the difficulties encountered when studying nonmodel organisms, particularly the absence of a species-specific reference genome, although phylogenetically similar genomes are assumed to be available. We compare the performance of three bioinformatics approaches - genotype calling, genotype-haplotype calling, and direct estimation without calling genotypes. Our findings reveal that relying on genotype calls leads to biased estimates of population genetic statistics at low to moderate read depth (2-8X). Genotype-haplotype calling provides more accurate estimates regardless of the divergence to the reference genome, but it requires moderate depth (8-20X). Direct estimation without calling genotypes yields the most accurate estimates of variability and most SFS tests, even at low read depth (2-4X). Therefore, studies without a species-specific reference genome should aim for low read depth and avoid genotype calling unless individual genotypes are crucial. Alternatively, aiming for moderate to high depth at the expense of the number of individuals and using genotype-haplotype calling is recommended.

title: Thalassemia and malaria: new insights into an old problem.
text: The hemoglobinopathies are likely the most common genetic diseases worldwide. According to the World Health Organization, at least 5% of the population carries one of the most severe forms, such as alpha- and beta-thalassemias, as well as the structural variant hemoglobins S, C, and E. These variants are found at varying frequencies in many countries. Interestingly, all of these hemoglobinopathies are believed to offer protection against malaria. It is believed that natural selection in malarial regions has played a role in increasing and maintaining the gene frequencies of these variants, an idea first proposed by J.B.S. Haldane 50 years ago. In the 1950s, epidemiological studies conducted in Africa on hemoglobin S supported the "malaria hypothesis." However, verifying this hypothesis for the thalassemias has been challenging until recently. The use of molecular methods has opened up new opportunities to address this long-standing question. Through population and molecular genetic analysis of thalassemia variants, as well as microepidemiological studies on the relationship between alpha-thalassemia and malaria in the southwest Pacific, clear evidence of protection has been found. Surprisingly, some of this protection seems to come from increased susceptibility in very young children with thalassemia to both Plasmodium falciparum and, particularly, P. vivax. This early exposure appears to lay the foundation for better protection later in life.

title: Endocrine control of spermatogenesis: Role of FSH and LH/ testosterone.
text: The assessment of testicular functions, including sperm production and androgen production, is a crucial part of preclinical safety evaluation. Testicular toxicity is more commonly observed than ovarian toxicity. This chapter focuses on two main aspects: (1) the histological consequences of disrupted reproductive endocrinology in rats, dogs, and nonhuman primates, and (2) a review of our current understanding of the roles of gonadotropins and androgens. The response of the testes to hormonal disturbances differs between rodents and dogs/primates. Initially, different types of germ cells and stages of spermatogenesis are affected in rodents compared to dogs and primates. Additionally, end-stage spermatogenic involution is more pronounced in dogs and primates than in rodents. Luteinizing hormone (LH) and testosterone, as well as follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), play crucial roles in regulating testicular functions. The relative importance of these hormones differs somewhat between rodents and primates. However, both LH/testosterone and FSH are necessary for normal spermatogenesis, particularly in non-seasonal species.

title: Extravasation injuries on regional neonatal units.
text: A study conducted on neonatal intensive care units in the region found that 38 out of every 1000 newborns experienced an extravasation injury resulting in skin necrosis. The majority of these injuries occurred in infants born at or before 26 weeks gestation, who received parenteral nutrition through intravenous cannulae. The most commonly used treatments included exposing the wounds to air, infiltrating them with hyaluronidase and saline, and applying occlusive dressings.

title: Nonstructural protein 3-4A: the Swiss army knife of hepatitis C virus.
text: The complex known as Hepatitis C virus (HCV) nonstructural protein 3-4A (NS3-4A) consists of NS3 and its cofactor NS4A. It possesses serine protease and NTPase/RNA helicase activities, which are crucial for viral polyprotein processing, RNA replication, and virion formation. When combined with pegylated interferon-α and ribavirin, specific inhibitors of the NS3-4A protease greatly enhance sustained virological response rates in patients with chronic hepatitis C. Additionally, the NS3-4A protease can hinder innate immune pathways and alter growth factor signaling by targeting certain cellular proteins. Therefore, NS3-4A is not only vital for the viral replication complex and a prime target for antiviral intervention but also plays a significant role in the persistence and pathogenesis of HCV. This review offers a concise update on the biochemical and structural aspects of NS3-4A, its involvement in the pathogenesis of chronic hepatitis C, and the clinical progress of NS3-4A protease inhibitors.

title: Phase 2 safety trial targeting amyloid beta production with a gamma-secretase inhibitor in Alzheimer disease.
text: The objective of this study was to assess the safety, tolerability, and response to the gamma-secretase inhibitor LY450139 in patients with Alzheimer's disease. The study design was a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, dose-escalation, placebo-controlled trial conducted at community-based clinical research centers. A total of 51 individuals with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease were randomly assigned to receive either placebo (n=15) or LY450139 (100 mg [n=22] or 140 mg [n=14]). Of these, 43 completed the treatment phase. The LY450139 groups received 60 mg/d for 2 weeks, followed by 100 mg/d for 6 weeks, and then either 100 or 140 mg/d for an additional 6 weeks. The main outcome measures included adverse events, levels of amyloid beta (Abeta) in plasma and cerebrospinal fluid, vital signs, electrocardiographic data, and laboratory safety test results. Secondary outcome measures included cognitive and functional assessments using the Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale cognitive subscale and the Alzheimer's Disease Cooperative Study Activities of Daily Living Scale. The results showed differences in skin and subcutaneous tissue concerns between the treatment groups, including possible drug rashes and reports of hair color change. Three adverse event-related discontinuations occurred, including one case of transient bowel obstruction. The plasma Abeta(40) concentration was significantly reduced by 58.2% in the 100-mg group and 64.6% in the 140-mg group. However, no significant reduction was observed in cerebrospinal fluid Abeta levels. There were no group differences in cognitive or functional measures. In conclusion, LY450139 was generally well tolerated at doses up to 140 mg/d for 14 weeks, but close clinical monitoring is necessary in future studies. The decrease in plasma Abeta concentrations suggests that gamma-secretase inhibition was achieved. The trial was registered at clinicaltrials.gov with the identifier NCT00244322.

title: Reduction in skin grafting after the introduction of hydrofiber dressings in partial thickness burns: a comparison between a hydrofiber and silver sulphadiazine.
text:
The purpose of this study was to compare the clinical outcomes of children with scald burns who were treated with a hydrofiber dressing (Aquacel, Convatec Inc.) versus the previous standard of care with silver sulfadiazine (Flammazine, Solvay Pharmaceuticals). The study focused on surgical intervention and length of stay (LOS) in the hospital.

A retrospective study was conducted, reviewing all consecutive children aged zero to four years with primary scald burns up to 10% of their body surface area (TBSA) who were admitted to the Burn Centre of the Maasstad Hospital Rotterdam between January 1987 and January 2010. Data collection was done using a prospective computerized database. The study period was divided into two periods: 1987-1999 (period 1) and 1999-2010 (period 2), representing the time before and after the introduction of the hydrofiber dressing (HFD), respectively.

The results showed that over the entire study period, 27.3% of the 502 patients treated with silver sulfadiazine (Ag-SD) underwent surgery. Before the introduction of HFD, 30.5% of the 338 Ag-SD treated patients required surgery. After the introduction of HFD, only 20.7% of the 164 patients treated with Ag-SD eventually needed skin grafting, which was a significant difference compared to the 11.6% of the 302 patients whose wounds were dressed with HFD (p<0.01).

In conclusion, the use of hydrofiber dressings in the treatment of mixed partial thickness scald burns up to 10% TBSA in children aged 0-4 years resulted in a reduced number of surgical interventions compared to silver sulfadiazine treatment. Additionally, this mode of treatment also led to a shorter hospital length of stay.

title: Induction of the heat-shock response by carbon dioxide in Chironomus thummi.
text: We have analyzed the impact of various stress treatments on the gene expression of Chironomus thummi salivary gland cells. Out of all the treatments tested, only the recovery from carbon dioxide exposure showed a response similar to the heat-shock treatment. This response included the activation of heat-shock puffs and the synthesis of heat-shock polypeptides. Additionally, we observed puffing and transcription of telomeric regions under these conditions, resulting in the formation of the temperature-inducible telomeric Balbiani ring T-BR-III. Despite subjecting C. thummi larvae or salivary gland cells to other stress conditions, these treatments did not induce the heat-shock response.

title: Candida albicans-Staphylococcus aureus polymicrobial peritonitis modulates host innate immunity.
text: Despite advancements in medical device fabrication and antimicrobial treatment therapies, the occurrence of fungal-bacterial polymicrobial peritonitis remains a grave complication for patients undergoing surgery, those on peritoneal dialysis, and individuals who are critically ill. Through the use of a mouse model of peritonitis, we have successfully demonstrated that infection with Candida albicans or Staphylococcus aureus alone does not result in death. However, when these infections occur simultaneously, the mortality rate increases to 40% within one day of infection, and there is a higher presence of microbes in the spleen and kidney. By employing a multiplex enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, we have also identified a distinct group of innate proinflammatory cytokines (interleukin-6, granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, keratinocyte chemoattractant, monocyte chemoattractant protein-1, and macrophage inflammatory protein-1α) that are significantly elevated during polymicrobial peritonitis compared to monomicrobial peritonitis. This leads to an increased infiltration of inflammatory cells into the peritoneum and target organs. Treatment of coinfected mice with the cyclooxygenase (COX) inhibitor indomethacin effectively reduces the infectious load, production of proinflammatory cytokines, and infiltration of inflammatory cells, while simultaneously preventing mortality. Further experiments have shown that the immunomodulatory eicosanoid prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) is synergistically increased during coinfection compared to monomicrobial infection, and indomethacin treatment also decreases elevated PGE2 levels. Additionally, the introduction of exogenous PGE2 into the peritoneal cavity during infection overrides the protective effects of indomethacin and restores increased mortality and microbial burden. These findings underscore the ability of fungal-bacterial coinfection to manipulate innate inflammatory responses, resulting in severe consequences for the host.

title: Techniques and probes for the study of Xenopus tropicalis development.
text: The frog Xenopus laevis has provided valuable insights into the processes of development and cellular functions. However, due to its allotetraploid genome, X. laevis cannot be used for forward genetic analysis. In contrast, Xenopus (Silurana) tropicalis, which has a diploid genome and a shorter generation time, may be suitable for genetic analysis. In this study, we demonstrate that many tools used to study X. laevis development can also be applied to X. tropicalis. Using the Nieuwkoop and Faber developmental staging system, we find that X. tropicalis embryos develop at similar rates to X. laevis, although they have a narrower temperature tolerance range. Furthermore, we show that many of the analytical reagents used for X. laevis can be effectively used for X. tropicalis. The X. laevis protocol for whole-mount in situ hybridization to mRNA transcripts can be successfully applied to X. tropicalis without any modifications. Additionally, X. laevis probes often work in X. tropicalis, eliminating the need to clone X. tropicalis orthologs before initiating developmental studies. Antibodies that react against X. laevis proteins can effectively detect X. tropicalis proteins using established immunohistochemistry procedures. Antisense morpholino oligonucleotides (MOs) provide a new alternative for studying gene activity loss during development, and we demonstrate that MOs function in X. tropicalis. Finally, X. tropicalis offers the potential for forward genetics and genomic analysis.

title: Requirement of c-myb in T cell development and in mature T cell function.
text: Previous studies have indicated that the protooncogene c-myb plays a role in the development of T cells in the thymus and the proliferation of mature T cells. To further investigate this, we created two mouse models with T cell-specific c-myb knockout, known as myb/LckCre and myb/CD4Cre. Our findings demonstrate that c-myb is essential for the development of thymocytes at the DN3 stage, as well as for the survival and proliferation of double-positive thymocytes. Additionally, c-myb is crucial for the differentiation of single-positive CD4 and CD8 T cells, and for the proliferative responses of mature T cells. Furthermore, our data suggests that c-myb directly contributes to the formation of double-positive CD4+CD8+CD25+, CD4+CD25+, and CD8+CD25+ T cells, which are involved in developmental processes that may be linked to autoimmune dysfunction.

title: Effect of losartan on ambulatory short-term blood pressure variability and cardiovascular remodeling in hypertensive patients on hemodialysis.
text:
The aim of this study was to investigate whether the angiotensin II type 1 receptor blocker losartan could improve ambulatory short-term blood pressure (BP) variability in hypertensive patients on hemodialysis. Forty hypertensive patients on hemodialysis therapy were randomly assigned to either the losartan treatment group or the control treatment group. 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring, echocardiography, and measurements of brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV) and biochemical parameters were conducted at baseline, as well as 6 and 12 months after the treatment. 

The results showed that after 6 and 12 months of treatment, nighttime short-term BP variability, as measured by the coefficient of variation of ambulatory BP, significantly decreased in the losartan group, while it remained unchanged in the control group. Additionally, compared to the control group, losartan significantly reduced left ventricular mass index (LVMI), baPWV, and the plasma levels of brain natriuretic peptide and advanced glycation end products (AGE). Furthermore, the analysis revealed significant correlations between changes in LVMI and changes in nighttime short-term BP variability, as well as between changes in LVMI and changes in the plasma levels of AGE. 

In conclusion, these findings suggest that losartan has a beneficial effect on suppressing pathological cardiovascular remodeling through its inhibitory effect on ambulatory short-term BP variability during nighttime.

title: Interleukin-17 mRNA expression in blood and CSF mononuclear cells is augmented in multiple sclerosis.
text: Myelin-directed autoimmunity is believed to play a crucial role in the development of multiple sclerosis (MS). It is commonly observed that both pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines are produced in higher quantities in individuals with MS. Interleukin-17 (IL-17), a recently discovered cytokine, is primarily produced by activated memory T cells in humans. IL-17 can stimulate the production of proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines from parenchymal cells and macrophages. To identify and count IL-17 mRNA expressing mononuclear cells (MNC) in the blood and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of MS patients and control subjects, we utilized in situ hybridization with synthetic oligonucleotide probes. The numbers of IL-17 mRNA expressing blood MNC were found to be higher in MS patients and those with acute aseptic meningoencephalitis (AM) compared to healthy individuals. Furthermore, MS patients examined during clinical exacerbation had higher numbers of IL-17 mRNA expressing blood MNC compared to those in remission. In CSF, MS patients had higher numbers of IL-17 mRNA expressing MNC compared to blood. However, this increase in CSF was not observed in patients with AM. Our findings demonstrate an increase in the numbers of IL-17 mRNA expressing MNC in MS, with the highest numbers observed in CSF compared to blood, and the highest numbers in blood during clinical exacerbations.

title: A European perspective on population studies of dementia.
text: The increasing age demographics worldwide and the projected increase in age-related diseases, such as dementia, are causing significant public health concerns. Extensive research has been conducted in the United States and Europe to comprehend the development and spread of dementia. This article provides a broad perspective on the history of dementia research in Europe and compares it with research in the United States. The review emphasizes the shared challenges that researchers from both regions have recognized and attempted to address. To enhance the knowledge gained from global studies, it is crucial to improve the harmonization of research methods, as suggested by current research practices.

title: The cost of providing comprehensive HIV treatment in PEPFAR-supported programs.
text:
The aim of this study was to analyze the costs and cost trends of HIV treatment in developing countries. The study focused on 43 outpatient clinics in Botswana, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Uganda, and Vietnam that were supported by PEPFAR and provided free comprehensive HIV treatment. Data on costs were collected over consecutive 6-month periods, starting from when dedicated HIV treatment services were scaled up at each site. The study included all patients receiving HIV treatment and care at these sites, totaling 62,512 patients on antiretroviral therapy (ART) and 44,394 pre-ART patients. The outcomes measured were costs per patient and total program costs, categorized by major cost categories. 

The results showed that the median annual economic costs were US$202 for pre-ART patients and US$880 for ART patients. Excluding the cost of antiretrovirals, the per patient ART costs were US$298. The study also found that care for newly initiated ART patients cost 15-20% more than for established patients. However, the per patient costs decreased significantly as the sites matured, with a 46.8% drop in ART costs between the first and second 6-month periods after scale-up, and an additional 29.5% drop the following year. 

In terms of funding, PEPFAR provided 79.4% of the funding for service delivery, while national governments provided 15.2%. 

In conclusion, this study highlights the wide variation in treatment costs between sites and countries, as well as the significant cost reductions that occur as sites mature. While cost reductions may allow for program growth in the short term, it is important for programs to consider the trade-off between improving services for current patients and expanding coverage to new patients.

title: A sperm cytoskeletal protein that signals oocyte meiotic maturation and ovulation.
text: Oocytes in Caenorhabditis elegans, like those in most animals, undergo a pause during meiotic prophase. The resumption of meiosis (maturation) and the contraction of smooth muscle-like gonadal sheath cells, necessary for ovulation, are facilitated by sperm. Our study reveals that the major sperm cytoskeletal protein (MSP) serves as a dual signal for oocyte maturation and sheath contraction. Additionally, MSP plays a role in sperm locomotion, similar to actin. This suggests that MSP has evolved to possess both extracellular signaling and intracellular cytoskeletal functions for reproduction. Similar proteins containing MSP-like domains have been identified in plants, fungi, and other animals, indicating the possibility of related signaling functions in other phyla.

title: Unmet need for mental health care among U.S. children: variation by ethnicity and insurance status.
