text: The aim of this study was to address the lack of national estimates regarding the use of mental health services among children and adolescents. The authors utilized three national data sets to examine ethnic disparities in unmet need for mental health services. The authors conducted secondary data analyses on three nationally representative household surveys conducted between 1996 and 1998. They analyzed rates of mental health service use among children and adolescents aged 3-17, as well as differences based on ethnicity and insurance status. The authors also examined the association between unmet need and ethnicity and insurance status among children identified as needing mental health services. The results showed that in a 12-month period, only 2%-3% of children aged 3-5 and 6%-9% of children and adolescents aged 6-17 utilized mental health services. Furthermore, nearly 80% of children and adolescents identified as needing mental health services did not receive any care. After controlling for other factors, the authors found that Latino children and uninsured children had higher rates of unmet need compared to white children and publicly insured children, respectively. These findings highlight the significant gap in mental health services for children, particularly among Latinos and the uninsured. The low rates of mental health service use among preschool children also indicate a need for further research to understand the reasons behind the high rates of unmet need in specific groups. This research can inform policy and clinical programs to address these disparities.

title: Conditional economic incentives for reducing HIV risk behaviors: integration of psychology and behavioral economics.
text: GOAL This article examines the integration and application of psychology and behavioral economics in conditional economic incentive (CEI) programs for reducing HIV risk behavior. METHODS We explore the history of HIV prevention approaches, highlighting the insights and limitations of psychological theories. We provide an overview of the relevant theoretical principles of behavioral economics for HIV prevention and use CEIs as an example of how these two fields can be combined for new approaches. RESULTS Behavioral economic interventions can enhance psychological frameworks for reducing HIV risk by offering unique insights into the conditions under which risky decisions can be influenced. Results from CEI programs demonstrate mixed but generally promising effects on HIV and sexually transmitted infection (STI) prevalence, HIV testing, medication adherence, and drug use. CONCLUSIONS CEI programs can complement psychological interventions for HIV prevention and behavioral risk reduction. To maximize effectiveness, CEI programs should be tailored to contextual and population-specific factors that may impact intervention applicability and success.

title: ALDH1 is a marker of normal and malignant human mammary stem cells and a predictor of poor clinical outcome.
text: The lack of simple methods for identifying and isolating normal and malignant stem cells has limited the application of stem cell biology to breast cancer research. However, through the use of in vitro and in vivo experimental systems, we have discovered that human mammary epithelial cells with increased aldehyde dehydrogenase activity (ALDH) possess stem/progenitor properties. These cells represent a subpopulation of normal breast epithelium with the widest range of lineage differentiation potential and the greatest growth capacity in a xenotransplant model. In breast carcinomas, high ALDH activity indicates the presence of tumorigenic cells capable of self-renewal and generating tumors that mirror the heterogeneity of the original tumor. In a study involving 577 breast carcinomas, the expression of ALDH1, as detected through immunostaining, was found to be associated with a poor prognosis. These findings provide a valuable new tool for studying both normal and malignant breast stem cells and facilitate the clinical application of stem cell concepts.

title: Interleukin-6 and interleukin-8 levels in serum and synovial fluid of patients with osteoarthritis.
text: The chemiluminescence-ELISA (CL-ELISA) method was used to determine the concentrations of interleukin (IL)-6 and IL-8 in serum and synovial fluid from patients with knee osteoarthritis (OA). This method has a sensitivity that is 100-1,000 times greater than the conventional ELISA method. The results were compared to those from patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and healthy individuals. The mean levels of IL-6 and IL-8 in synovial fluid were higher in RA compared to OA. In serum, both IL-6 and IL-8 levels were significantly higher in both RA and OA patients compared to controls. Among OA patients who showed significant improvement in hydrarthrosis, the initial examination revealed relatively higher levels of IL-6 and IL-8 in synovial fluid, which significantly decreased after treatment with sodium hyaluronate (NaHA). On the other hand, among those who did not show improvement in hydrarthrosis, the initial examination showed relatively lower levels of IL-6 and IL-8 in synovial fluid, and hydrarthrosis did not significantly improve even after NaHA treatment. Additionally, there was a tendency for the levels of IL-6 and IL-8 in synovial fluid to decrease as the levels of HA increased. Evaluation of X-ray findings showed that in cases with low-grade severity, the levels of IL-6 in synovial fluid at the initial examination were significantly higher compared to high-grade cases. In low-grade cases, there was a significant decrease in IL-6 levels in synovial fluid after treatment with NaHA.

title: Inhibition of SRC expression and activity inhibits tumor progression and metastasis of human pancreatic adenocarcinoma cells in an orthotopic nude mouse model.
text: In 70% of pancreatic adenocarcinomas, there is an overexpression of the nonreceptor protein tyrosine kinase Src. In this study, we investigated the impact of reducing Src through molecular and pharmacological means on the development, growth, and spread of pancreatic tumor cells in an orthotopic model. To decrease Src expression, we utilized a plasmid encoding small interfering RNA (siRNA) specific to c-src and introduced it into L3.6pl human pancreatic tumor cells. This resulted in a reduction of Src expression by more than 80%, without affecting the expression of related kinases c-Yes and c-Lyn. The proliferation rates of the siRNA clones were similar to those of the control clones. Additionally, the phosphorylation of Akt and p44/42 Erk mitogen-activated protein kinase, as well as the production of VEGF and IL-8 in the culture supernatants, were significantly reduced. When these cells were implanted into nude mice, there was no change in tumor incidence. However, the siRNA clones failed to develop large tumors, and the occurrence of metastasis was significantly reduced. This suggests that c-Src activity plays a critical role in tumor progression. To further investigate this, we treated mice with established wild-type tumors with the Src/Abl-selective inhibitor BMS-354825 (dasatinib). Tumor size decreased, and the occurrence of metastases was significantly reduced compared to the control group. These findings demonstrate that Src activation contributes to the progression of pancreatic tumors in this model, making Src a potential target for therapy.

title: Eicosapentaenoic acid is converted via ω-3 epoxygenation to the anti-inflammatory metabolite 12-hydroxy-17,18-epoxyeicosatetraenoic acid.
text: The beneficial effects of eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) in various inflammatory disorders have been well-documented. In this particular study, it was observed that dietary EPA underwent ω-3 epoxygenation in the mouse peritoneal cavity, resulting in the formation of 17,18-epoxyeicosatetraenoic acid (17,18-EpETE). Mediator lipidomics analysis revealed the presence of several new oxygenated metabolites of 17,18-EpETE. Among these metabolites, one major compound called 12-hydroxy-17,18-epoxyeicosatetraenoic acid (12-OH-17,18-EpETE) exhibited strong anti-inflammatory properties by reducing neutrophil infiltration in murine zymosan-induced peritonitis. In vitro experiments demonstrated that 12-OH-17,18-EpETE effectively inhibited neutrophil chemotaxis and polarization induced by leukotriene B4, with an EC50 value of 0.6 nM. The complete structures of two naturally occurring isomers were identified as 12S-OH-17R,18S-EpETE and 12S-OH-17S,18R-EpETE, using chemically synthesized stereoisomers. These natural isomers displayed potent anti-inflammatory effects, while the synthetic stereoisomers showed negligible activity. These findings highlight the conversion of dietary EPA into a highly active metabolite, 12-OH-17,18-EpETE, which may contribute to the development of an endogenous anti-inflammatory pathway.

title: Scrapie in mice. Agent-strain differences in the distribution and intensity of grey matter vacuolation.
text: We used five different strains of scrapie agent to infect two inbred mouse strains, C57BL and VM, as well as their F1 cross. Each strain of agent caused a different degree of vacuolation in specific regions of the brain, resulting in a unique "lesion profile" for each agent. Based solely on these histological parameters, we were able to reliably distinguish between any of the five scrapie agents, regardless of the mouse strain used. Interestingly, the dose of the agent did not affect the lesion profile, even when using varying doses of the ME7 agent in C57BL mice spanning a wide range. The genotype of the mouse had a significant impact on the overall degree of vacuolation and the shape of the lesion profile, with some agents showing more pronounced effects than others. Depending on the strain of agent used, certain areas of the brain in the (C57BL × VM)F1 cross exhibited either significantly more or significantly less vacuolation compared to either parental genotype. However, the genetic control of the lesion profile was found to be too complex for further detailed analysis based on these data.

title: Cyclin A2 is an RNA binding protein that controls Mre11 mRNA translation
text: Cyclin A2 is responsible for activating the cyclin-dependent kinases Cdk1 and Cdk2. It is expressed at higher levels from the S phase until early mitosis. Our research has shown that mice with a mutation preventing the elevation of cyclin A2 experience chromosomal instability and are prone to developing tumors. This instability is caused by a failure to increase the levels of the Mre11 nuclease during the S phase. This leads to difficulties in resolving stalled replication forks, inadequate repair of double-stranded DNA breaks, and improper segregation of sister chromosomes. Surprisingly, cyclin A2 controls the abundance of Mre11 through a C-terminal RNA binding domain. This domain selectively and directly binds to Mre11 transcripts, facilitating their loading onto polysomes and translation. These findings demonstrate that cyclin A2 plays a diverse role in regulating DNA replication. It combines various kinase-dependent functions with a kinase-independent, RNA binding-dependent role to ensure the proper repair of common replication errors.

title: Cluster sampling to assess immunization coverage: a review of experience with a simplified sampling method.
text:
The Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) is utilizing a simplified cluster sampling technique to estimate immunization coverage levels. This method involves randomly selecting 210 children from 30 clusters, with each cluster consisting of 7 children. The results of both actual and computer simulated surveys are analyzed in this article. A total of 446 sample estimations of immunization coverage were available for analysis, derived from 60 actual surveys conducted in 25 countries. It was found that 83% of the sample results had 95% confidence limits within a range of + or - 10%. None of the surveys had 95% confidence limits exceeding + or - 13%. 

To further validate the EPI method, 12 hypothetical population strata were established for computer simulation. These strata had immunization coverage rates ranging from 10% to 99%. Additionally, 10 hypothetical communities were created by allocating different proportions of each stratum. The results of these simulated surveys also supported the validity of the EPI method, with over 95% of the results being within + or - 10% of the actual population mean. 

Based on the findings from both actual and simulated surveys, the precision of the EPI method is considered satisfactory for the program's requirements. Among the actual surveys, the proportion of results with confidence limits exceeding + or - 10% was highest (50%) when the immunization coverage in the sample ranged from 45% to 54%.

title: Gender differences in the utilization of health care services.
text:
Research has consistently shown that women tend to utilize more health care services compared to men. In order to further explore this gender disparity, we conducted a study that took into account important factors such as patient sociodemographics and health status. 

For this study, we randomly assigned 509 new adult patients to primary care physicians at a university medical center. We closely monitored their use of health care services and the associated charges over a period of one year. To measure self-reported health status, we utilized the Medical Outcomes Study Short Form-36 (SF-36). In our statistical analyses, we controlled for variables such as health status, sociodemographic information, and primary care physician specialty. 

Our findings revealed that women had significantly lower self-reported health status compared to men. Additionally, women had a higher average number of visits to their primary care clinic and diagnostic services compared to men. When it came to charges, women had significantly higher mean charges for primary care, specialty care, emergency treatment, diagnostic services, and annual total charges, but there were no differences in mean hospitalizations or hospital charges. 

Even after accounting for health status, sociodemographics, and clinic assignment, women still had higher medical charges across all categories except for hospitalizations. 

In conclusion, our study confirms that women tend to utilize more medical care services and incur higher associated charges compared to men. While we did not determine the appropriateness of these differences, these findings have important implications for the provision of health care.

title: Recombinant human tumor necrosis factor administered as a 24-hour intravenous infusion. A phase I and pharmacologic study.
text: We conducted a phase I trial to assess the effects of recombinant human tumor necrosis factor (rH-TNF) on tumors. During the trial, we administered rH-TNF through continuous infusion for 24 hours. A total of 115 courses of therapy were given to 50 patients, with doses ranging from 4.5 to 645 micrograms of rH-TNF/m2. As the dose of rH-TNF increased, we observed an increase in systemic toxicity, including fever, chills, fatigue, and hypotension. Doses exceeding 454 micrograms/m2 often resulted in severe lethargy and fatigue, preventing patients from being discharged from the hospital after completing therapy. The main dose-limiting toxicity was hypotension, and five patients treated at the highest dose levels required dopamine treatment. However, other organ-specific toxicity was mild and resolved within 48 hours. Additionally, the 24-hour infusions of rH-TNF led to significant reductions in serum cholesterol and high-density lipoprotein levels. Pharmacokinetic studies using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay showed peak plasma rH-TNF levels ranging from 90-900 pg/mL. Despite continuous infusion, we did not achieve a steady-state level of rH-TNF. Based on our findings, we recommend a dose of 545 micrograms/m2 for rH-TNF as a 24-hour continuous infusion in phase II trials.

title: Detection and comparison of epidermal growth factor receptor mutations in cells and fluid of malignant pleural effusion in non-small cell lung cancer.
text: The cells or fluid without cells found in malignant pleural effusion could be an important sample for screening epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, their effectiveness in detecting mutations has not been thoroughly compared. In this study, we included 26 East Asian NSCLC patients with malignant pleural effusion and determined the EGFR mutation status in both the cells and the corresponding cell-free fluid using sequencing and mutant-enriched PCR. By comparing the types of mutations, we discovered that both the cells and the cell-free fluid from the pleural cavity could be suitable samples for detecting EGFR mutations in inoperable NSCLC cases, as long as sensitive genotyping assays are used. Direct sequencing may fail to identify a significant number of mutations in these diverse samples. More sensitive methods, such as mutant-enriched PCR and gene scan, could provide more reliable information about mutations.

title: Materials and Methods Figs. S1 to S15 References Supporting Online Materials
text: The recognition of viral pathogens by endosomal Toll-like receptors (TLRs) 7 and 9 triggers a series of signals that activate nuclear factor κB (NF-κB)-dependent proinflammatory cytokines and interferon regulatory factor 7 (IRF7)-dependent type I interferons (IFNs). However, the recognition of viral nucleic acids by TLR9 specifically requires its cleavage in the endolysosomal compartment. In this study, we demonstrate that the activation of type I IFN genes, but not proinflammatory cytokine genes, by TLR9 signals necessitates the trafficking of TLR9 from endosomes to a specialized lysosome-related organelle. Additionally, we have identified adapter protein-3 as the protein complex responsible for the transportation of TLR9 to this specific subcellular compartment. These findings shed light on an intracellular mechanism that allows for the separation of TLR9 signals through the selective trafficking of the receptor within the endosomal system.

title: Sedimentation velocity method in the analytical ultracentrifuge for the study of protein-protein interactions.
text: The analytical ultracentrifuge can be used to detect macromolecular interactions through sedimentation analysis. When two molecules interact, the resulting complex gains mass, which can be observed in its sedimentation behavior. This chapter explores how this phenomenon can be utilized to determine quantitative parameters of an interaction. An example is provided, focusing on the interaction between a single-stranded DNA binding protein and a subunit of DNA polymerase III holoenzyme. The chapter also includes a comprehensive discussion of the relevant theory and an explanation of the evaluation algorithms used.

title: Structural trends in the aging femoral neck and proximal shaft: analysis of the Third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry data.
text:
The Third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES III) conducted hip scans on adults aged 20-99 years in the United States. The scans were done using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and were analyzed using a structural analysis program. The program examined narrow regions at specific locations on the proximal femur to measure bone mineral density (BMD) and other factors such as cross-sectional areas, moments of inertia, section moduli, subperiosteal widths, and estimated mean cortical thickness. This analysis focuses on a subgroup of non-Hispanic white individuals, consisting of 2,719 men and 2,904 women. Measurements were taken in a cortical region across the proximal shaft, 2 cm below the lesser trochanter, and a mixed cortical/trabecular region at the narrowest point of the femoral neck.

The study investigated apparent age trends in BMD and section modulus for both regions, taking into account body weight differences between individuals. In the narrow neck region, BMD declined with age similarly to the Hologic neck region. BMD in the shaft also decreased, but at a slower rate. However, a different pattern was observed for section modulus, and this pattern varied by sex. Specifically, the section modulus remained relatively constant in both the narrow neck and shaft regions until the fifth decade in females, after which it declined at a slower rate than BMD. In males, the section modulus in the narrow neck declined slightly until the fifth decade and then remained stable, while the section modulus in the shaft remained constant until the fifth decade and then increased steadily.

The discrepancy between BMD and section modulus appears to be due to a linear expansion in subperiosteal diameter in both sexes and regions. This expansion helps offset the net loss of medullary bone mass and maintains mechanical strength. These findings suggest that the loss of bone mass with aging in the hip does not necessarily indicate reduced mechanical strength. In fact, the femoral neck section moduli in the elderly were found to be within 14% of young values in females and within 6% in males, on average.

title: Turning blood into brain: cells bearing neuronal antigens generated in vivo from bone marrow.
text: The bone marrow stem cells have the ability to generate different types of blood cells and replenish the blood supply in adults. Our study demonstrates that when adult bone marrow cells are transplanted into mice that cannot produce myeloid and lymphoid cells, these cells migrate to the brain and transform into cells that exhibit specific characteristics of neurons. These results suggest that bone marrow-derived cells could potentially serve as an alternative source of neurons for individuals suffering from neurodegenerative diseases or central nervous system damage.

title: A negative staining method for high resolution electron microscopy of viruses.
text: This abstract presents a straightforward method for examining the external shape and structure of virus particles. By combining virus samples with a 1% solution of phosphotungstic acid at pH 7.5 and applying it directly onto carbon-based electron microscope films, excellent contrast and preservation are achieved. The technique has been successfully applied to the study of tobacco mosaic virus and turnip yellow mosaic virus, revealing structural features previously identified through X-ray diffraction analysis.

title: Nef induces multiple genes involved in cholesterol synthesis and uptake in human immunodeficiency virus type 1-infected T cells.
text: Recent reports suggest that cholesterol may play a significant role in the replication of human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1). To investigate this further, we conducted a study using microarrays to examine the effects of HIV-1 infection on cholesterol biosynthesis and uptake. Our findings revealed that HIV-1 infection led to an increase in the expression of cholesterol genes in both transformed T-cell lines and primary CD4(+) T cells. This was supported by our observation of increased incorporation of (14)C-labeled mevalonate and acetate in HIV-1-infected cells. Importantly, our data also indicated that these changes in cholesterol biosynthesis and uptake were only present when functional Nef was present. This suggests that the increased synthesis of cholesterol may contribute to Nef-mediated enhancement of virion infectivity and viral replication.

title: Long noncoding RNA as modular scaffold of histone modification complexes
text: The regulation of chromatin states and epigenetic inheritance is carried out by long intergenic noncoding RNAs (lincRNAs). In this study, we demonstrate that the lincRNA HOTAIR acts as a framework for two distinct histone modification complexes. The 5' region of HOTAIR interacts with the polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2), while the 3' region of HOTAIR binds to the LSD1/CoREST/REST complex. This unique ability to connect two different complexes allows for the assembly of PRC2 and LSD1 through RNA mediation, facilitating the coordinated targeting of these complexes to chromatin. This coordinated targeting results in the simultaneous methylation of histone H3 lysine 27 and demethylation of lysine 4. Our findings suggest that lincRNAs can act as scaffolds by providing binding sites for specific histone modification enzymes, thereby determining the pattern of histone modifications on target genes.

title: Therapeutic Clearance of Amyloid by Antibodies to Serum Amyloid P Component.
text:
BACKGROUND: Systemic amyloidosis is caused by the presence of amyloid fibril deposits, which always contain the normal plasma protein serum amyloid P component (SAP). The drug CPHPC effectively removes SAP from the plasma, but some SAP remains in the amyloid deposits. This residual SAP can be targeted by therapeutic IgG anti-SAP antibodies. In murine amyloid A type amyloidosis, these antibodies bind to the remaining SAP in the deposits, activating complement and triggering the rapid clearance of amyloid by macrophage-derived multinucleated giant cells.

METHODS: We conducted a phase 1 trial involving 15 patients with systemic amyloidosis. The trial was open-label and single-dose-escalation. We first used CPHPC to deplete circulating SAP, and then infused a fully humanized monoclonal IgG1 anti-SAP antibody. Patients with cardiac involvement were excluded for safety reasons. We monitored organ function, inflammatory markers, and amyloid load.

RESULTS: No serious adverse events were reported. Some initial recipients of higher doses of the antibody experienced infusion reactions, which were reduced by slowing the infusion rate for later patients. At 6 weeks, patients who received an adequate dose of antibody relative to their amyloid load showed decreased liver stiffness, as measured by transient elastography. These patients also experienced improvements in liver function, along with a significant reduction in hepatic amyloid load, as demonstrated by SAP scintigraphy and measurement of extracellular volume using magnetic resonance imaging. A reduction in kidney amyloid load and shrinkage of an amyloid-laden lymph node were also observed.

CONCLUSIONS: Treatment with CPHPC followed by an anti-SAP antibody safely triggered the clearance of amyloid deposits from the liver and other tissues. The study was funded by GlaxoSmithKline and registered under ClinicalTrials.gov number NCT01777243.

title: LPA Gene, Ethnicity, and Cardiovascular Events
text:
Background: The relationship between single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the LPA gene, apolipoprotein(a) isoforms, and lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] levels with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in different ethnic groups is not well understood.

Methods: We measured LPA SNPs, apolipoprotein(a) isoforms, Lp(a), and oxidized phospholipids on apolipoprotein B-100 (OxPL-apoB) levels in a total of 3419 subjects from different ethnic backgrounds (1792 black, 1030 white, and 597 Hispanic) who were enrolled in the Dallas Heart Study. We examined the interdependent relationships between these factors and their prospective association with MACE after a median follow-up of 9.5 years.

Results: We found that the prevalence of LPA SNPs varied among ethnic groups, with rs3798220 being most prevalent in Hispanics (42.38%), rs10455872 in whites (14.27%), and rs9457951 in blacks (32.92%). The correlation between each SNP and the size of the major apolipoprotein(a) isoform differed among ethnic groups. In the entire cohort, Cox regression analysis with adjustment for multiple variables showed that individuals in the highest quartiles of Lp(a) and OxPL-apoB had hazard ratios for MACE of 2.35 (95% confidence interval: 1.50–3.69, P<0.001) and 1.89 (95% confidence interval: 1.26–2.84, P=0.003), respectively, compared to those in the lowest quartile. When we included the major apolipoprotein(a) isoform and the three LPA SNPs in the models, the risk was attenuated but remained significant for both Lp(a) and OxPL-apoB. When we analyzed MACE in specific ethnic groups, we found that Lp(a) was a positive predictor and the size of the major apolipoprotein(a) isoform was an inverse predictor in blacks, the size of the major apolipoprotein(a) isoform was an inverse predictor in whites, and OxPL-apoB was a positive predictor in Hispanics.

Conclusions: The prevalence and association of LPA SNPs with the size of apolipoprotein(a) isoforms, Lp(a), and OxPL-apoB levels vary greatly among different ethnic groups. However, the relationship with MACE is primarily driven by elevated plasma Lp(a) or OxPL-apoB levels, despite significant ethnic differences in LPA genetic markers.

title: Protein kinase CK2 modulates developmental functions of the abscisic acid responsive protein Rab17 from maize.
text: This study demonstrates the significance of Rab17 phosphorylation by protein kinase CK2 in plant responses to stress. We provide evidence of the specific interaction between Rab17 and CK2 regulatory subunits CK2 beta-1 and CK2 beta-3, which is independent of Rab17's phosphorylation state. Live-cell fluorescence imaging reveals that CK2 phosphorylation regulates the intracellular dynamics of Rab17. Both CK2 beta subunits and Rab17 are found in the cytoplasm and nucleus, while catalytic CK2 alpha subunits and a non-phosphorylatable Rab17 mutant protein (mRab17) accumulate in the nucleoli. A dual-color image shows that the CK2 holoenzyme primarily accumulates in the nucleus. To assess the importance of Rab17 phosphorylation in vivo, transgenic plants were used. Overexpression of Rab17, but not mRab17, halts seed germination under osmotic stress conditions. Therefore, Rab17's role in growth processes is mediated through its phosphorylation by protein kinase CK2.

title: Reduced plasma concentrations of nitrogen oxide in individuals with essential hypertension.
text: Patients diagnosed with essential hypertension display diminished responses in the dilation of blood vessels due to the endothelium, which can be primarily attributed to a decrease in the effectiveness of nitric oxide (NO). To investigate this further, we measured the levels of nitrate plus nitrite (collectively known as nitrogen oxide), the end product of NO metabolism, and examined the connection between the severity of hypertension and the concentration of nitrate plus nitrite in the plasma of patients with essential hypertension. Comparatively, the combined concentration of nitrate plus nitrite in the plasma, which represents the end products of NO metabolism, was lower in individuals with essential hypertension when compared to control subjects (15.7+/-1.1 versus 22.8+/-1.4 mmol x L(-1), P<.001). Individuals with borderline hypertension displayed values that fell between those of the other two groups (18.2+/-1.2 mmol x L(-1), P<.001). The concentration of nitrogen oxide in the plasma exhibited significant negative correlations with both systolic and diastolic blood pressures. In individuals with essential hypertension, the basal concentration of nitrogen oxide in the plasma was reduced, particularly in the peripheral circulation.

title: Isolation of superoxide dismutase mutants in Escherichia coli: is superoxide dismutase necessary for aerobic life?
text: Mutations and gene fusions were created by inserting Mu transposons carrying the chloramphenicol resistance marker into the cloned Escherichia coli genes sodA and sodB, which code for manganese superoxide dismutase (MnSOD) and iron superoxide dismutase (FeSOD) respectively. The mutated sodA or sodB genes were then introduced into the bacterial chromosome through allelic exchange. Activity measurements and immunoblot analysis confirmed that the resulting mutants lacked the corresponding SOD. In rich medium under aerobic conditions, the absence of FeSOD or MnSOD did not significantly affect growth or sensitivity to the superoxide generator, paraquat. However, in minimal medium, aerobic growth was unaffected but sensitivity to paraquat was increased, particularly in the sodA mutant. A sodA sodB double mutant, completely lacking SOD, was also obtained. This double mutant was able to grow aerobically in rich medium, with unaffected catalase levels, but showed high sensitivity to paraquat and hydrogen peroxide. However, the double mutant was unable to grow aerobically on minimal glucose medium. Growth could be restored by removing oxygen, providing an SOD-overproducing plasmid, or supplementing the medium with the 20 amino acids. These findings suggest that the complete absence of SOD in E. coli creates a conditional sensitivity to oxygen.

title: Late presentation of HIV-infected individuals.
text:
Despite the significant improvement in prognosis due to antiretroviral therapy (ART), late presentation remains a major concern in HIV care. We consider a first presentation for HIV care as 'late' if the individual has an AIDS-defining opportunistic disease or if their CD4+ T-cell count is below 200/microliter. In developed countries, around 10-30% of HIV-infected individuals still present with CD4+ T-cell counts below 50 and 200/microliter, respectively. The numbers are even higher in developing countries.

When opportunistic diseases are present, the focus is on diagnosing and treating them, as well as providing intensive supportive care in hospitals. However, starting ART promptly has its benefits, such as faster resolution of opportunistic diseases and a reduced risk of recurrence. On the other hand, there are potential downsides to starting ART immediately, including toxicity, drug interactions, and immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS).

For individuals who present late but are asymptomatic or have mild symptoms, initiating ART and primary prophylaxis is recommended. However, approximately 10-20% of these individuals may develop symptoms due to drug toxicity or undiagnosed opportunistic complications, including IRIS. These individuals require appropriate therapies.

In this review, we discuss the issue of late presentation in HIV care, the extent of the problem, the evaluation of late-presenting patients, and the challenges associated with initiating potent ART in the presence of acute opportunistic infections and other comorbidities.

title: Rapid clearance of human papillomavirus and implications for clinical focus on persistent infections.
text:
To effectively utilize the information provided by new molecular screening tests, it is crucial for health professionals and the public to have a clear understanding of the natural progression of human papillomavirus (HPV) infections of the cervix. In order to investigate this, we conducted a study on 599 women enrolled in a population-based cohort in Guanacaste, Costa Rica, where we detected 800 carcinogenic HPV infections.

For each individual infection, we analyzed the cumulative proportions of three outcomes at 6-month intervals over a period of 30 months. These outcomes included viral clearance, persistence without the development of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+), or persistence with a new diagnosis of CIN2+. To determine the presence of carcinogenic HPV genotypes, we used an L1 degenerate-primer polymerase chain reaction method to test cervical specimens.

Our findings revealed that HPV infections typically cleared rapidly, with 67% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 63% to 70%) of infections clearing within 12 months. However, among infections that persisted for at least 12 months, there was a 21% (95% CI = 15% to 28%) risk of developing CIN2+ by the 30-month mark. Notably, women under the age of 30 with HPV-16 infections that persisted for at least 12 months had the highest risk of CIN2+ diagnosis, with a rate of 53% (95% CI = 29% to 76%).

Based on these findings, it is important for the medical community to prioritize the persistence of cervical HPV infection rather than solely relying on single-time detection of HPV in the management strategies and health messages provided to patients.

title: The role of alcohol in the Russian mortality crisis.
text:
The sharp rise in mortality in Russia from 1990-94 is believed to be largely influenced by alcohol consumption. However, the increase in standard alcohol consumption alone does not fully explain the rise in mortality. This study takes a unique approach to examining the role of alcohol in increased mortality by investigating whether the discrepancy between mortality trends and recorded alcohol consumption is due to an underestimation of the consumption increase.

The study begins by estimating the impact of alcohol on the male accident rate using data from 1959-89. Then, the estimated alcohol effect and the observed accident mortality rate from 1990-98 are used to estimate alcohol consumption during that period. This backcasted alcohol series is then used to predict trajectories in alcohol poisoning mortality, homicide rate, and overall mortality from 1990-98.

The findings reveal a much stronger increase in the backcasted consumption proxy compared to the standard alcohol consumption proxy from 1990-98. There is a significant gap between the observed mortality rates and the rates predicted from the standard alcohol consumption proxy, while the predictions from the backcasted alcohol proxy align much more closely with the actual rates.

In conclusion, a large portion of the rise in Russian mortality from 1990-94 can be attributed to increased alcohol consumption among the population. However, this increase is greatly underestimated by the commonly used consumption proxy, which combines alcohol sales, estimation of illicit alcohol production, and the proportion of alcohol-related violent deaths.

title: The lateral hypothalamus: a primary site mediating excitatory amino acid-elicited eating.
text: Injecting excitatory neurotransmitter glutamate or its agonists, kainic acid, D,L-alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-isoxazole propionic acid (AMPA), or N-methyl-D-aspartic acid (NMDA), into the lateral hypothalamic (LH) region can quickly induce a strong feeding response in satiated rats. To determine if the LH is responsible for this effect, we compared the ability of these compounds to stimulate feeding when injected into the LH versus other nearby sites. We measured food intake in groups of adult male rats one hour after injecting glutamate (30-900 nmol), KA (0.1-1.0 nmol), AMPA (0.33-3.3 nmol), NMDA (0.33-33.3 nmol), or a control substance into one of seven brain sites using implanted guide cannulas. These sites included the LH, the anterior and posterior tips of the LH, the thalamus above the LH, the amygdala beside the LH, and the paraventricular and perifornical areas near the LH. The results showed that the eating-stimulatory effects were greatest with injections into the LH, regardless of the dose or agonist used. In the LH, glutamate doses between 300 and 900 nmol caused a dose-dependent feeding response of up to 5 g within one hour (P < 0.01). Each of the other agonists at doses of 3.3 nmol or less induced feeding responses of at least 10 g when injected into this site. Injections into the other brain sites either did not cause eating or occasionally resulted in smaller and less consistent feeding responses.

title: A Gateway® compatible vector for gene silencing in bloodstream form Trypanosoma brucei.
text: RNA interference is the fastest way to create conditional knockdown mutants in Trypanosoma brucei. The use of the dual T7 promoter (pZJM) and stem-loop vectors has been common in generating stable inducible RNAi cell lines, with the latter offering better regulatory control. However, the process of cloning stem-loop constructs is complex, requiring multiple cloning steps or multi-fragment ligation reactions. We have developed a vector (pTrypRNAiGate) based on pLEW100 that utilizes the Gateway® recombination system to simplify the production of hairpin RNA constructs. This approach allows the final stem-loop RNAi construct to be created through a single cloning step of the PCR-derived gene fragment, followed by an in vitro recombination reaction. The new vector enables efficient gene silencing and serves as a valuable tool for functional genomics in T. brucei, particularly in high-throughput applications.

title: Prolonged effect of calcium supplementation on risk of colorectal adenomas in a randomized trial.
text:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies have shown that taking calcium supplements can reduce the risk of colorectal adenoma recurrence. However, it is unclear how long this protective effect lasts after stopping active supplementation.

METHODS: In the Calcium Polyp Prevention Study, 930 individuals with a history of colorectal adenoma were randomly assigned to receive either a placebo or 1200 mg of elemental calcium daily for 4 years. The Calcium Follow-up Study, which was an observational phase of the trial, monitored adenoma occurrence for an average of 7 years after the end of the randomized treatment. Information on medication, vitamin, and supplement use during this period was also collected. Follow-up data was obtained for 822 participants, with 597 undergoing at least one colonoscopy after the end of the study treatment and included in the analysis. Generalized linear models were used to calculate relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) to assess the effect of calcium treatment on adenoma recurrence during the first 5 years after treatment ended and the subsequent 5 years. Statistical tests were two-sided.

RESULTS: During the first 5 years after treatment ended, individuals in the calcium group had a significantly lower risk of any adenoma compared to those in the placebo group (31.5% versus 43.2%; adjusted RR = 0.63, 95% CI = 0.46 to 0.87, P = .005). There was also a smaller, non-significant reduction in the risk of advanced adenomas (adjusted RR = 0.85, 95% CI = 0.43 to 1.69, P = .65). However, there was no association between randomized treatment and the risk of any type of polyp during the following 5 years. Similar findings were observed when analyzing participants who did not report using any calcium supplements after the treatment phase of the trial.

CONCLUSION: The protective effect of calcium supplementation on the risk of colorectal adenoma recurrence lasts up to 5 years after stopping active treatment, even without continued supplementation.

title: Influence of DNA on the activities and inhibition of neutrophil serine proteases in cystic fibrosis sputum.
text: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is characterized by uncontrolled proteolysis caused by neutrophil serine proteases (NSPs) in lung secretions. Our research has demonstrated that the active neutrophil elastase, protease 3, and cathepsin G in CF sputum are resistant to inhibition, partially due to their binding to neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) secreted by activated neutrophils in CF sputum and to genomic DNA released from senescent and dead neutrophils. Treatment of CF sputum with DNase significantly increases elastase activity, which can then be effectively inhibited by exogenous elastase inhibitors. However, DNase treatment does not have the same effect on protease 3 and cathepsin G activities, suggesting that they are distributed differently or bound differently in CF sputum. When purified blood neutrophils are stimulated by opportunistic CF bacteria Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus, the activities of the three proteases remain unchanged. However, subsequent DNase treatment leads to a significant increase in all three proteolytic activities. Neutrophils activated with a calcium ionophore do not secrete NETs but release large amounts of active proteases, which are not affected by DNase. Our findings indicate that NETs serve as reservoirs of active proteases, protecting them from inhibition and maintaining their rapid mobilization. Combining the use of protease inhibitors with DNA-degrading agents could effectively counteract the harmful proteolytic effects of NSPs in CF lung secretions.

title: Clinical effects of Abeta immunization (AN1792) in patients with AD in an interrupted trial.
text:
The authors conducted a phase IIa immunotherapy trial of AN1792(QS-21) in patients with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease (AD). The trial aimed to assess the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of the immunization. However, the trial was interrupted due to meningoencephalitis in 6% of the immunized patients. 

The trial included 372 patients aged 50 to 85 years with probable AD. They were randomly assigned to receive either IM AN1792 225 microg plus the adjuvant QS-21 50 microg (300 patients) or saline (72 patients). Injections were planned at regular intervals over a period of 12 months. The safety and tolerability of the immunization were evaluated, and pilot efficacy measures such as cognitive function, brain imaging, and biomarkers were assessed in patients who developed an antibody response to AN1792.

Following reports of meningoencephalitis in 18 out of 300 patients (6%), the immunization was stopped after one, two, or three injections, depending on the individual. Out of the 300 AN1792(QS-21)-treated patients, 59 (19.7%) developed the desired antibody response. The double-blind assessments were conducted for the full 12-month duration of the trial. 

The results showed no significant differences between the antibody responder group and the placebo group in terms of cognitive function, disability assessment, clinical rating, or global impression of change. However, analysis of the neuropsychological test battery revealed slight differences favoring the antibody responders. Additionally, in the subset of patients who underwent cerebrospinal fluid examinations, those who developed an antibody response showed a decrease in CSF tau levels compared to the placebo group.

In conclusion, despite being interrupted, this trial suggests that immunotherapy targeting beta-amyloid may have potential benefits in the treatment of Alzheimer's disease.

title: Quantitative characterization of metastatic disease in the spine. Part I. Semiautomated segmentation using atlas-based deformable registration and the level set method.
text: Metastatic disease in the bone is often considered difficult to measure, leading to the exclusion of patients with skeletal metastases from clinical trials. To effectively quantify the impact of metastatic tumor involvement in the spine, it is necessary to accurately segment the vertebra. Manual segmentation can be accurate but requires extensive user interaction and is time-consuming. To automate the segmentation of metastatically involved vertebrae, potential solutions include demons deformable image registration and level set methods. The aim of this study was to develop a semi-automated method that accurately segments tumor-bearing vertebrae using these techniques. By maintaining the morphology of an atlas, the demons-level set composite algorithm was able to accurately distinguish between trans-cortical tumors and surrounding soft tissue with identical intensity. The algorithm successfully segmented both the vertebral body and trabecular centrum of tumor-involved and healthy vertebrae. This research validates our approach as being equally accurate to that of an experienced user.

title: Activation of lysosomal function during dendritic cell maturation.
text: Dendritic cells (DCs) undergo a transformation from immature cells, which are specialized for capturing antigens, to mature cells, which are specialized for stimulating T cells, in response to various stimuli. This maturation process involves an increased ability of DCs to form and accumulate peptide-MHC (major histocompatibility complex) class II complexes. Our study reveals that the activation of lysosomal function plays a crucial role in this alteration. In immature DCs, antigens that are internalized are degraded slowly and inefficiently used for peptide loading. However, maturation triggers the activation of the vacuolar proton pump, which enhances lysosomal acidification and antigen proteolysis. This facilitates the efficient formation of peptide-MHC class II complexes. Therefore, it appears that lysosomal function in DCs is specialized for the regulated processing of internalized antigens during development.

title: Comparison of agar dilution, microdilution, and disk elution methods for measuring the synergy of cefotaxime and its metabolite against anaerobes.
text: We conducted tests on 173 anaerobic clinical isolates to evaluate the effectiveness of cefotaxime (CTX) and desacetyl cefotaxime (des-CTX), both individually and in combination. Among 60 Bacteroides fragilis isolates, the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of CTX in broth was 22.4 micrograms/ml, whereas it was 47.4 micrograms/ml in agar. This decrease in efficacy in agar was observed across all species tested, which contradicts the reported clinical efficacy of the drug. However, we observed synergy between CTX and des-CTX in 70 to 100% of the isolates, including 60% of all Bacteroides spp. tested. The susceptibility results in the synergy system aligned well with those obtained using a broth-disk elution method incorporating 32 micrograms of CTX and 8 micrograms of des-CTX per ml. However, the correlation was weaker when the broth-disk method contained 16 micrograms of CTX and 8 micrograms of des-CTX per ml.

title: Retinoblastoma regulatory pathway in lung cancer.
text: Lung cancer is responsible for more cancer-related deaths than breast, colon, and prostate cancers combined. The Rb-p16 regulatory pathway is crucial in suppressing tumors in the lung epithelium. This is supported by the fact that almost all cases of lung cancer show changes in Rb-p16 pathway components, and individuals with inherited Rb mutations have a higher risk of developing pulmonary carcinomas. Interestingly, p16 loss and Rb mutations are more common in specific subtypes of lung cancer. Through the analysis of human tumors, researchers have identified a sequence of molecular alterations in preneoplastic lesions that lead to lung cancer. Early modifications in the p16 gene, known as epigenetic changes, are a significant step in the progression of lung cancer. This review summarizes studies in humans that highlight the critical role of the Rb-p16 tumor suppressor pathway in the development of lung cancer. It also discusses how these findings, along with studies using genetically engineered mouse models, have greatly enhanced our understanding of the causes of lung cancer.

title: Human papillomavirus and Papanicolaou tests to screen for cervical cancer.
text:
The effectiveness of screening for cervical cancer using human papillomavirus (HPV) testing is uncertain. It is unclear whether the increased sensitivity in detecting high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) represents overdiagnosis or protection against future high-grade cervical epithelial neoplasia or cervical cancer. 

To investigate this, a population-based screening program was conducted in Sweden. A total of 12,527 women aged 32 to 38 years were randomly assigned to either undergo an HPV test plus a Papanicolaou (Pap) test (intervention group) or a Pap test alone (control group) in a 1:1 ratio. Women with a positive HPV test and a normal Pap test result were offered a second HPV test after at least 1 year. Those who were persistently infected with the same high-risk type of HPV were then offered colposcopy with cervical biopsy. A similar number of double-blinded Pap smears and colposcopies with biopsy were performed in randomly selected women in the control group. The women were followed for an average of 4.1 years using comprehensive registry data. The rates of grade 2 or 3 CIN or cancer detected at enrollment and subsequent screening examinations were compared between the two groups.

The results showed that at enrollment, the proportion of women in the intervention group with grade 2 or 3 CIN or cancer was 51% higher than in the control group. However, at subsequent screening examinations, the proportion of women in the intervention group with grade 2 or 3 lesions or cancer was 42% lower, and the proportion with grade 3 lesions or cancer was 47% lower compared to the control group. Women with persistent HPV infection remained at high risk for grade 2 or 3 lesions or cancer even after referral for colposcopy.

In conclusion, adding an HPV test to the Pap test for screening women in their mid-30s reduces the incidence of grade 2 or 3 CIN or cancer detected by subsequent screening examinations.

title: Chronic Exercise Increases Both Inducible and Endothelial Nitric Oxide Synthase Gene Expression in Endothelial Cells of Rat Aorta
text: The expression of the endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) gene is upregulated with chronic exercise. However, it is currently unknown whether exercise affects the expression of the inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS). To investigate this, we conducted a study using isolated rat aortic endothelial and smooth muscle cells. Male Wistar rats were divided into control and exercise groups and underwent 10 weeks of running training. After the training period, the rats were sacrificed under ether anesthesia. We used the quantitative competitive reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction method to measure the expression of NOS mRNA in the isolated cells. Additionally, we examined the functional role of iNOS by assessing vascular responses induced by phenylephrine, with and without pretreatment with aminoguanidine. Our findings revealed that chronic exercise increased the expression of iNOS and eNOS mRNA in endothelial cells. Furthermore, chronic exercise dampened phenylephrine-induced vascular responses, likely due to increased release of nitric oxide through iNOS. These results demonstrate that chronic exercise enhances the expression of both iNOS and eNOS genes in the endothelium, which may contribute to the altered vascular response observed after exercise.

title: Frontal stroke syndromes.
text: The frontal lobe, the largest lobe of the brain, is frequently affected by strokes. Surprisingly, while almost one in five strokes are limited to the prerolandic areas, clinical frontal dysfunction in stroke is relatively rare. This is in contrast to patients with other diseases like brain tumors, where frontal behavioral syndromes are more commonly reported. This paradox may be due to the volume effect, where acute strokes cause more clinical dysfunction than chronic diseases like tumors. Frontal strokes also involve "silent" strokes, which may lead to intellectual decline and hinder recovery from subsequent strokes with specific neurological dysfunction. Understanding frontal lobe dysfunction in stroke is crucial for clinical-topographic classification correlations, given the focal nature of the disease. Luria's school attempted to classify frontal lobe syndromes, and recent MRI studies have improved this classification. We propose six main clinical-anatomic frontal stroke syndromes: prefrontal, premotor, superior medial, orbital-medial, basal forebrain, and white matter. Additionally, there are instances where frontal lobe symptoms occur despite sparing the frontal cortex or white matter, such as lenticulo-capsular, caudate, and thalamic strokes. Studies suggest that diaschisis, frontal lobe dysfunction from a remote lesion, may play a role, likely due to dynamic interruption of complex circuitry rather than static frontal lobe deactivation.

title: Interaction of cytosine arabinoside and lovastatin in human leukemia cells.
text: The use of cytosine arabinoside (ara-C) for treating leukemias is common, but it comes with significant toxicities. On the other hand, lovastatin, an inhibitor of HMG-CoA reductase, is widely used to treat hypercholesterolemia. We conducted a study to investigate whether lovastatin could enhance the effectiveness of ara-C. We examined their effects on the human erythroleukemia K562 cell line and the ara-C resistant ARAC8D cell line. Surprisingly, we found that the two drugs had a synergistic interaction. Our research suggests that this interaction is not mediated by RAS, but rather by lovastatin's ability to reduce MAPK activity and prevent ara-C-induced MAPK activation. This is the first study to describe a potentially beneficial interaction between lovastatin and ara-C, which could have implications for the treatment of human leukemia.

title: The crystal structure of TAL effector PthXo1 bound to its DNA target.
text: TAL effectors use tandem repeats, each consisting of 33 to 35 amino acids, to recognize DNA. These repeats contain unique repeat-variable diresidues (RVDs) that specify nucleotides. Through high-throughput computational structure prediction and heavy-atom derivatization, the crystal structure of PthXo1 bound to its DNA target was determined. Each repeat forms a two-helix bundle that presents a loop containing an RVD to the DNA. These repeats come together to form a superhelix that wraps around the DNA major groove in a right-handed manner. The first RVD residue interacts with the protein backbone to provide stability, while the second RVD residue makes a specific contact with the DNA sense strand. Additionally, two amino-terminal repeats interact with the DNA. The structure, which includes multiple RVDs and noncanonical associations, provides insight into how TAL effectors recognize DNA.

title: Prediction of creatinine clearance from serum creatinine.
text: A new formula has been created to estimate creatinine clearance (Ccr) based on serum creatinine (Scr) levels in adult males. This formula also accounts for a 15% decrease in females. The development of this formula involved studying the relationship between age and 24-hour creatinine excretion per kilogram in 249 patients ranging from 18 to 92 years old. Using this formula, Ccr values were predicted and compared to four other methods, as well as the average of two 24-hour Ccr measurements in 236 patients. The correlation coefficient between the predicted and measured Ccr values was found to be 0.83. On average, the difference between the predicted and measured values was similar to the difference between paired clearances. To ensure accurate predictions, factors for age and body weight must be taken into consideration.

title: Dendritic cells, T cells and lymphatics: dialogues in migration and beyond.
text: Immune cells continuously travel through lymph vessels from peripheral tissues to the blood. The movement of these cells is facilitated by their interaction with lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). However, lymphatic vessels serve a greater purpose than just transporting fluid and immune cells. Recent data suggests that LECs play a role in supporting the survival of T cells, promoting tolerance to self-antigens, preventing excessive T cell proliferation during immune responses, and maintaining T cell memory. Conversely, leukocytes also impact LEC biology, with dendritic cells influencing lymphatic vessel permeability and lymphocytes regulating LEC proliferation during inflammation. Overall, these findings shed light on the close relationship between LECs and leukocytes, contributing to our understanding of immune responses.

title: CRISPR–Cas9 genome editing induces a p53-mediated DNA damage response
text: In this study, we have discovered that using CRISPR-Cas9 for genome editing in immortalized human retinal pigment epithelial cells activates a DNA damage response and causes cell cycle arrest. This response is mediated by the p53 pathway, leading to a decrease in the number of cells with a functional p53 pathway. However, when p53 is inhibited, the damage response is prevented, and the rate of homologous recombination from a donor template is increased. These findings suggest that inhibiting p53 could enhance the efficiency of genome editing in non-transformed cells. Therefore, it is important to monitor p53 function when developing cell-based therapies that utilize CRISPR-Cas9. Overall, the DNA damage triggered by CRISPR-Cas9 activates p53, which limits the effectiveness of gene editing in immortalized human retinal pigment epithelial cells.

title: Comparative Structural Analysis of Lipid Binding START Domains
text:
The Steroidogenic acute regulatory (StAR) protein related lipid transfer (START) domains are small globular modules that have a cavity where lipids and lipid hormones can bind. These domains are able to transport ligands to help with the exchange of lipids between biological membranes. It has been suggested that they can also affect the activity of other parts of the protein when a ligand binds. There are over a dozen human genes that encode START domains, and some of them have been linked to diseases.

In this study, we present the crystal structures of four human lipid transfer domains: STARD1, STARD5, STARD13, and STARD14. These domains belong to four out of the six functional classes of START domains. By comparing these structures with previously reported ones, we have identified the structural elements that determine the function and specificity of human START domains.

For a more interactive experience, this article is also available in an enhanced version that includes 3D representations and animated transitions. Please note that you will need to install a web plugin to access this enhanced functionality. Instructions for installing and using the web plugin can be found in Text S1.

title: Staphylococcus aureus infection dynamics
text: Staphylococcus aureus is a type of bacteria that normally lives in humans without causing harm, but it can also cause serious infections throughout the body. To do this, it must evade the immune system and find different places within the body to grow. However, we still don't fully understand how the disease develops and which parts of the immune system are most important in fighting the infection. Previous research has shown that when S. aureus infects the body, only a small number of bacteria are able to survive and cause abscesses, which are characteristic of many infections. In this study, we investigate the factors in the body that limit the number of bacteria and then allow them to multiply and spread. We find that this bottleneck is a common feature in different infection models and is not specific to a particular strain of S. aureus. Interestingly, when we use high doses of S. aureus in a commonly used infection model, the bottleneck is less pronounced, suggesting that the host's defenses are overwhelmed. This raises questions about the validity of this model. By depleting certain immune mediators, we identify key points in the infection process and how it spreads throughout the body. When we remove certain types of immune cells, such as macrophages, we see increased susceptibility to infection, but the bottleneck is no longer present and the infection spreads to other organs. On the other hand, when we remove neutrophils, another type of immune cell, we see greater susceptibility to disease, but the bottleneck remains and the infection does not spread. We also use a new microscopy technique to study the structure and distribution of abscesses within organs. Based on our observations, we develop a model that explains how S. aureus infection progresses from the initial infection to the formation of mature abscesses. This research emphasizes the importance of understanding the complex process of infection in order to identify the roles of both the host and the bacteria. It also helps explain why a high number of bacteria is needed to cause S. aureus disease and how interventions like vaccines could be developed more effectively.

title: Strategies for optimizing maternal nutrition to promote infant development
text:
The importance of optimal maternal nutrition for the health and development of infants and young children is increasingly recognized. However, there are still unresolved strategies for addressing the challenges associated with this. This review aims to highlight the significance of maternal nutrition and the strategies currently being used to improve outcomes. 

Recent literature was examined, with a particular focus on the rationale for and the results of maternal nutrition supplements, including lipid-based supplements. The findings are as follows: 

1) There is a strong argument for improving the maternal and in utero environment in low-resource populations to enhance fetal and post-natal growth and development. 
2) Poverty reduction has shown promise in improving adult height over generations, suggesting that it can have a positive impact on maternal and child health. 
3) Low-resource environments are associated with maternal, newborn, and infant characteristics that indicate undernutrition, such as low weight and impaired linear growth. 
4) Most efforts to improve fetal growth and development have focused on maternal nutrition interventions during pregnancy, in addition to broader public health and educational initiatives. 
5) The benefits of iron/folic acid and multiple micronutrient maternal supplements during pregnancy have been reasonably established. 
6) Recent studies on a maternal lipid-based supplement have not consistently shown additional benefits compared to multiple micronutrient supplements alone. 
7) However, both multiple micronutrient and lipid-based supplements appear to be more effective when started early in pregnancy. 

In conclusion, poor maternal nutrition is a significant factor contributing to impaired fetal and early post-natal growth. Maternal interventions targeting nutrition have shown improvements in in utero development, including increased birth weights and partial corrections of impaired birth length. It is important to consider not only the quality of maternal nutrition supplements but also the timing and quantity of interventions, taking into account the differences between populations. Ultimately, these steps should be seen as a starting point towards creating an environment that supports optimal nutrition and overall health.

title: Key questions about the checkpoint blockade-are microRNAs an answer?
text: The introduction of immune-checkpoint blockade in cancer therapy has revolutionized the management of advanced stage cancers. Currently, there are several FDA approved checkpoint inhibitors, with many other agents currently being tested in clinical trials. While the therapeutic potential of immune checkpoint inhibitors has expanded in recent years, it remains unclear who can truly benefit from this treatment. MicroRNAs, which are small non-coding RNAs, play a crucial role in posttranscriptional control of protein expression by binding to the 3' untranslated region of messenger RNA. A network of microRNAs directly and indirectly regulates the expression of checkpoint receptors, and some microRNAs can target multiple checkpoint molecules, mimicking the therapeutic effect of a combined immune checkpoint blockade. In this review, we will discuss the microRNAs that control the expression of immune checkpoints and address four specific challenges in immune checkpoint therapy for cancer: (1) lack of precise therapeutic indication, (2) difficulty in evaluating treatment response, (3) occurrence of numerous immunologic adverse events, and (4) absence of response to immune therapy. Finally, we propose microRNAs as potential solutions to overcome these challenges. We believe that microRNAs could become important therapeutic partners in immune checkpoint therapy in the near future.

title: Metformin reverses established lung fibrosis in a bleomycin model
text: Fibrosis is a condition that occurs when tissue repair goes awry after an injury, and it can affect various organs, including the lungs. The process of tissue repair and remodeling is regulated by cellular metabolism. AMPK, a crucial sensor of cellular energy levels, plays a role in switching from building up to breaking down molecules for energy. However, the exact role of AMPK in fibrosis is not well understood. In this study, we found that in individuals with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and in a mouse model of lung fibrosis, AMPK activity is lower in the fibrotic regions where there are metabolically active and apoptosis-resistant myofibroblasts. By activating AMPK in myofibroblasts from IPF patients' lungs, we observed reduced fibrotic activity, increased production of new mitochondria, and restored sensitivity to apoptosis. In a mouse model of lung fibrosis caused by bleomycin, the drug metformin accelerated the resolution of well-established fibrosis in an AMPK-dependent manner. These findings suggest that insufficient AMPK activation contributes to the development of non-resolving, pathological fibrosis, and indicate that metformin or other AMPK activators could potentially reverse established fibrosis by promoting deactivation and apoptosis of myofibroblasts.

title: Are expert athletes 'expert' in the cognitive laboratory? A meta-analytic review of cognition and sport expertise
text: In recent studies, the benefits of fitness and computer-based cognitive training in improving cognition and brain function have been highlighted. However, it remains unclear whether the combination of fitness and cognitive training that comes from years of extensive sport training leads to better performance on cognitive tests. This study aims to address this question through a quantitative meta-analysis involving 20 studies. The findings reveal that athletes outperformed non-athletes in processing speed and various attentional paradigms, with the largest effects observed in athletes from interceptive sports and males. Based on these results, further research should focus on higher-level cognitive tasks, such as executive function, and explore different aspects of visual attention. Additionally, future studies should include more female athletes and encompass a wider range of sport types and expertise levels.

title: Effects of Age, Sex, and Ethnicity on the Association Between Apolipoprotein E Genotype and Alzheimer Disease: A Meta-analysis
text:
Objective: The objective of this study was to investigate the relationship between apolipoprotein E (APOE) genotype and Alzheimer's disease (AD) in different ethnic and racial populations, considering age and sex as factors.

Data Sources: Data from 40 research teams were collected, including information on APOE genotype, sex, age at disease onset, and ethnic background. The study included 5930 patients with probable or definite AD and 8607 dementia-free controls recruited from clinical, community, and brain bank sources.

Main Outcome Measures: Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated to assess the association between AD and APOE genotypes (∈2/∈2,∈2/∈3,∈2/∈4,∈3/∈4, and ∈4/∈4), adjusted for age and study. The analysis was stratified by major ethnic groups (Caucasian, African American, Hispanic, and Japanese) and source. Logistic regression procedures were used to evaluate the influence of age and sex on the OR for each genotype.

Results: Among Caucasian subjects from clinic- or autopsy-based studies, individuals with genotypes ∈2/∈4, ∈3/∈4, and ∈4/∈4 had a significantly higher risk of AD, with ORs of 2.6, 3.2, and 14.9, respectively. Conversely, individuals with genotypes ∈2/∈2 and ∈2/∈3 had decreased ORs of 0.6. The association between APOE∈4 and AD was weaker among African Americans and Hispanics, with significant heterogeneity in ORs among African American studies.

Conclusions: The APOE∈4 allele is a major risk factor for AD in all ethnic groups studied, across all ages from 40 to 90 years, and in both men and women. Further research is needed to clarify the association between APOE∈4 and AD in African Americans, and to investigate the attenuated effect of APOE∈4 in Hispanics.

title: Comparison of glioblastoma (GBM) molecular classification methods.
text: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a prevalent and aggressive form of brain cancer in adults. It is known for its poor survival rates and high variability in tumor characteristics, both within and between tumors. Unfortunately, there are currently no effective therapies available for GBM. Recent advancements in genetic, genomic, and epigenetic research have provided valuable insights into the heterogeneity of GBM tumors. This has led to the development of various methods aimed at classifying tumors based on the key molecular events that drive the most aggressive cellular components. The goal is to develop targeted therapies for specific subtypes of GBM. However, despite these efforts, the molecular subtyping of GBM has not resulted in improved patient outcomes. The complexities arising from the intratumoral molecular heterogeneity have hindered the success of targeted or tailored therapies for specific mutations or subtypes. Most tumors eventually develop resistance to treatment and recur. GBM stem cells (GSCs) have been identified as a potential source of intratumoral cellular heterogeneity. Recent studies using single cell sequencing have suggested that the hierarchical organization of tumor cells, originating from GSCs, may partially explain the intratumoral cellular heterogeneity. Therefore, molecular subtyping based on GSCs derived from patients may hold promise for more effective subtype-specific treatments. In this review, we examine the molecular alterations of GBM, the methods used for molecular subtyping, and the plasticity of subtypes in primary and recurrent tumors. We also emphasize the clinical relevance of potential targets for further drug development.

title: Mesenchymal Stromal Cells: From Discovery to Manufacturing and Commercialization
text: In recent decades, there has been significant research conducted on mesenchymal stromal cells (MSC) due to their unique qualities. These cells can be easily obtained and grown in a lab setting, thanks to their ability to renew themselves. Additionally, MSC have the ability to modulate the immune system and can be transformed into different cell types, making them highly desirable for cell-based therapies. This review aims to provide a concise historical overview of the discovery and characterization of MSC, as well as the initial clinical studies conducted. We also examine the current methods used to manufacture MSC, with a focus on the use of bioreactors to produce clinically relevant cell quantities that comply with Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) standards. Furthermore, we discuss the first commercially available MSC-based products and the challenges that still need to be addressed in order to widely utilize MSC-derived products.

title: Delta–Notch—and then? Protein interactions and proposed modes of repression by Hes and Hey bHLH factors
text: The Hes and Hey genes are the mammalian versions of the Hairy and Enhancer-of-split genes found in Drosophila. They are the main targets of the Delta-Notch signaling pathway. Hairy-related factors play a crucial role in various stages of embryonic development, and when their regulation goes awry, it can lead to defects. The Hes and Hey genes, also known as Hesr, Chf, Hrt, Herp, or gridlock, encode transcriptional regulators of the basic helix-loop-helix class, primarily functioning as repressors. However, the exact mechanisms by which Hes and Hey proteins control transcription are not yet fully understood. Proposed mechanisms include direct binding to specific DNA sequences on target promoters (N- or E-boxes), indirect binding through other sequence-specific transcription factors, or sequestration of transcriptional activators. Repression may involve the recruitment of corepressors, induction of histone modifications, or interference with the general transcriptional machinery. All of these models rely heavily on protein-protein interactions. In this review, we examine published data on the interactions between Hairy-related factors and other proteins or DNA, and discuss their implications for transcriptional regulation. Additionally, we provide an overview of recent advancements in identifying potential target genes and analyzing mouse models.

title: The Long Noncoding RNA CAREL Controls Cardiac Regeneration.
text: The ability of the adult mammalian heart to regenerate after ischemic injury is hindered by the loss of cardiomyocyte mitosis. However, the specific molecular mechanisms responsible for the post-mitotic nature of cardiomyocytes are not well understood. This study aimed to investigate the role of long noncoding ribonucleic acids (lncRNAs) in heart regeneration during postnatal and adult injury. The researchers used transgenic mice with cardiomyocyte-specific overexpression of lncRNA-CAREL driven by Myh6, as well as adenovirus-mediated silencing of endogenous CAREL in vivo. They assessed the impact of CAREL on cardiomyocyte replication and heart regeneration after apical resection or myocardial infarction by examining mitosis and cytokinesis. The results showed that CAREL was significantly up-regulated in cardiomyocytes from neonatal mice (P7) in parallel with the loss of regenerative capacity. Overexpression of CAREL in mice reduced cardiomyocyte division and proliferation, and hindered neonatal heart regeneration after injury. Conversely, silencing CAREL in vivo significantly promoted cardiac regeneration and improved heart function after myocardial infarction in neonatal and adult mice. CAREL acted as a competing endogenous RNA for miR-296, which led to the derepression of Trp53inp1 and Itm2a, the target genes of miR-296. Overexpression of miR-296 increased cardiomyocyte replication and cardiac regeneration after injury. The decline in cardiac regenerative ability observed in CAREL transgenic mice was also rescued by miR-296. A short fragment containing the conserved sequence of CAREL had the same effect on reducing the proliferation of human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes as the full-length CAREL. In conclusion, lncRNA CAREL regulates cardiomyocyte proliferation and heart regeneration in the postnatal and adult heart after injury by acting as a competing endogenous RNA on miR-296, which targets Trp53inp1 and Itm2a.

title: BCAP links IL-1R to the PI3K–mTOR pathway and regulates pathogenic Th17 cell differentiation
text: The toll-like receptor (TLR) and interleukin (IL)-1 family of receptors have several signaling components in common, including the main adapter, MyD88. In a previous study, we discovered a new adapter called B cell adapter for phosphoinositide 3-kinase (BCAP), which is involved in regulating inflammatory responses downstream of TLR signaling. In this study, we found that BCAP also plays a crucial role in regulating T helper (Th) 17 and Th1 cell differentiation downstream of IL-1 and IL-18 receptors, respectively. Although the absence of BCAP in T cells did not affect the development of naturally occurring Th1 and Th17 lineages, it did lead to defects in the differentiation of pathogenic Th17 lineage cells. As a result, mice lacking BCAP in T cells were less susceptible to experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis. Importantly, we discovered that BCAP is essential for the activation of phosphoinositide 3-kinase-Akt-mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway induced by IL-1R. Inhibition of mTOR completely prevented the differentiation of pathogenic Th17 cells induced by IL-1β, similar to the effects observed in BCAP-deficient cells. This study highlights the critical role of BCAP in linking IL-1R signaling to the metabolic status of activated T cells, ultimately regulating the differentiation of inflammatory Th17 cells.
