title: Vegetarian vs. conventional diabetic diet – A 1-year follow-up
text: The objective of our previous study was to compare the effects of a vegetarian diet (V) and a conventional diet (C) on cardiovascular risk factors for patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D). The study, which lasted for 6 months, showed that the vegetarian diet had beneficial effects such as increased insulin sensitivity, reduced body weight, decreased volume of visceral and subcutaneous fat, lower LDL-cholesterol levels, and improved oxidative stress markers and chosen adipokines. In order to determine if these improvements persisted after the study, we conducted a 1-year follow-up with 62 subjects who had completed the study. The participants were measured for weight, waist circumference, HbA1c, and blood lipids. No efforts were made to maintain their previously assigned diets. Out of the 62 subjects, 44 (71%) attended the follow-up. It was found that hypoglycemic agents were increased by 14% in the vegetarian group and by 26% in the conventional group. Insulin therapy was introduced in 5% of the vegetarian group and in 13% of the conventional group one year after the intervention. There were no significant changes in weight or waist circumference in either group. HbA1c levels increased similarly in both groups (+0.49 ± 1.04% in V vs. +0.42 ± 0.8% in C). Blood lipids did not change in either group. In conclusion, one year after the intervention, the positive effects of a vegetarian diet on cardiovascular risk factors compared to a conventional diet were partially maintained.

title: Alcohol, wine, and health
text: Abstract Background: Over the past two decades, numerous studies have established a link between alcohol consumption and various disease states, including overall mortality, arteriosclerotic vascular diseases, hypertension, cancers, peptic ulcer, respiratory infections, gall stones, kidney stones, age-related macular degeneration, bone density, and cognitive function. Methods: A thorough examination of these studies reveals that each one compared the outcomes of individuals who consumed different amounts of alcohol with those who abstained completely. Results: In each analysis, a U-shaped or J-shaped curve emerged, indicating a reduced relative risk of developing a particular disease compared to abstainers. This suggests that moderate alcohol consumption is beneficial. For men, moderation means limiting intake to 2 to 4 drinks per day, while for women it should not exceed 1 to 2 drinks per day. Conclusions: Alcohol alone has positive effects on high-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels and platelet aggregation inhibition. Wine, especially red wine, contains high levels of phenolic compounds that have favorable effects on multiple biochemical systems. These include increased high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, antioxidant activity, reduced platelet aggregation and endothelial adhesion, suppression of cancer cell growth, and promotion of nitric oxide production.

title: Contraceptive practices of women requesting termination of pregnancy : A study from China
text: This abstract presents the findings of a survey conducted in Zheng Zhou City, Henan Province, P.R. China, to develop a program for preventing unwanted pregnancies. The survey involved 1520 women seeking abortion at eight large hospitals between March 1996 and May 1996. The main cause of unplanned pregnancies was contraceptive failure, accounting for 71.9% of cases. Of these pregnancies, 61.7% could have been predicted due to nonuse of contraception or recognition of contraceptive failures. The highest proportion of contraceptive failures was attributed to condom mishaps (29.7%), followed by IUD failures (23.5%) and rhythm miscalculation (15.9%). Most of the women seeking abortion (77.1%) had previously used some form of contraception, but only 19.7% had used contraception during their first sexual intercourse. Among the abortion seekers, 57.6% had previously used condoms, and 50.9% of condom users had experienced at least one condom mishap. The rhythm method had been used by 31.7% of the women seeking abortion, and 59.1% of rhythm users had experienced at least one rhythm failure. Of those who had used pills (16.8%), 58.0% had experienced pill failures. The majority of condom and pill failures (46.4% and 56.0% respectively) were due to user failure (poor compliance). Among the women seeking abortion, 56.4% had previously undergone at least one abortion, and 5.3% had undergone multiple abortions. Only 10 subjects had used emergency contraception prior to their current pregnancy.

title: Oncologists' perceptions of the effects of cancer patients' companions on physician-patient interactions
text: In order to assess how the presence of companions of cancer patients affects physician-patient communication, we conducted semistructured interviews with 12 oncologists (6 medical, 4 surgical, and 2 radiation) out of a total of 21 oncologists. According to the physicians, approximately three-fourths of their patients brought companions to consultations, which made the consultations more complex for the physicians. The behavior of the companions varied, ranging from dominating the conversation to simply taking passive notes. The most assertive companions were typically young professional men or older women accompanying their husbands, who also asked the most questions. During medical visits, all possible combinations of companions were observed. The physicians perceived that companions and patients often had different priorities, and they also noticed differences in the behavior of companions based on their gender and whether they lived in rural or urban areas.

title: Wolff's Headache and Other Head Pain.
text: There has never been a book on headaches that compares to the late Harold Wolff's work. The second edition, published a decade ago, remains a masterpiece of writing. It provides a comprehensive and captivating exploration of Wolff's extensive research and understanding of headaches. The new edition, revised by Dalessio, brings certain aspects of headache treatment up to date, particularly in relation to drug therapy. However, the focus on holistic treatment rather than solely relying on medication remains intact. Dalessio has made some slight changes to the book's structure, although the "new chapters" on cluster headaches and trigeminal neuralgia are simply relocated from other sections of the original edition. The section on migraines, which forms the core of the book, has been reworked, with some anecdotal content removed, but minimal additions. It is worth noting that the observations on methysergide (UML-491) in Wolff's original work are still included in the revised edition.

title: Ansichten von Hausärzten zur Versorgung von unheilbar kranken Patienten am Lebensende - Ergebnisse einer Befragung in Niedersachsen
text:
Background: Family physicians play a crucial role in providing healthcare for terminally ill patients. However, the current state of palliative care in Germany has faced significant criticism. Despite this, there is a lack of empirical data, especially regarding the perspectives of family doctors. 

Methods: To address this gap, a study was conducted to examine the attitudes of family doctors (sample: n=257) in four representative regions in Lower Saxony. Semi-structured telephone interviews were utilized as part of a comprehensive expert report on the healthcare system. 

Results: Out of the 257 doctors approached, 71 were successfully interviewed (28% response rate). On average, these doctors were currently caring for four palliative patients with cancer and eight palliative patients with other diseases. Many doctors made themselves available to their patients at all times, particularly during the final stages of illness. The main area identified for improvement was the provision of psychosocial support, which was deemed more important than pain therapy, the usual focus of attention. Additionally, there was a notable willingness among family doctors to embrace new palliative care structures. 

Conclusion: Family doctors demonstrate a high level of motivation and openness towards palliative care improvements. It is crucial to acknowledge and consider the diverse opinions among different healthcare professionals and disciplines regarding the current state and future development of palliative care.

title: Novel Risk Factors for Systemic Atherosclerosis: A Comparison of C-Reactive Protein, Fibrinogen, Homocysteine, Lipoprotein(a), and Standard Cholesterol Screening as Predictors of Peripheral Arterial Disease
text:
In recent times, several new risk factors for atherosclerosis have been suggested, but there is limited comparative data available to guide the clinical use of these emerging biomarkers. The objective of this study was to compare the predictive value of 11 lipid and nonlipid biomarkers as risk factors for the development of symptomatic peripheral arterial disease (PAD).

The study design was a nested case-control study using plasma samples collected at baseline from a prospective cohort of 14,916 initially healthy male physicians aged 40 to 84 years in the US. Out of this cohort, 140 individuals subsequently developed symptomatic PAD (cases), and 140 age- and smoking status-matched men who remained free of vascular disease during an average 9-year follow-up period were randomly selected as controls. The main outcome measure was incident PAD, determined by baseline levels of total cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), total cholesterol-HDL-C ratio, triglycerides, homocysteine, C-reactive protein (CRP), lipoprotein(a), fibrinogen, and apolipoproteins (apo) A-I and B-100.

In univariate analyses, it was found that plasma levels of total cholesterol, LDL-C, triglycerides, apo B-100, fibrinogen, CRP, and the total cholesterol-HDL-C ratio were significantly higher at baseline among men who subsequently developed PAD compared to those who did not. On the other hand, levels of HDL-C and apo A-I were lower. There were no significant baseline elevations of lipoprotein(a) and homocysteine. In multivariable analyses, the total cholesterol-HDL-C ratio was the strongest lipid predictor of risk, while CRP was the strongest nonlipid predictor. When assessing joint effects, the addition of CRP to standard lipid screening significantly improved risk prediction models based on lipid screening alone.

In conclusion, out of the 11 atherothrombotic biomarkers assessed at baseline, the total cholesterol-HDL-C ratio and CRP were found to be the strongest independent predictors of the development of peripheral arterial disease. Additionally, CRP provided additional prognostic information beyond standard lipid measures.

title: Assessment of older people: Self-maintaining and instrumental activities of daily living.
text: Formal devices for evaluating function are now commonly used in agencies that cater to the elderly. In a recent study conducted by the Gerontological Society on functional assessment (Howell, 1968), a wide range of rating scales, checklists, and other techniques used in practical settings were easily gathered. Currently, it seems that each researcher or practitioner feels compelled to create their own scale and argue that existing scales cannot adequately fit their specific situation. The authors of this study also contribute to this trend by introducing two scales that were standardized on their own population (Lawton, 1969). However, they find solace in the fact that one of the scales, the Physical Self-Maintenance Scale (PSMS), was primarily developed and utilized by other researchers (Lowenthal, 1964), and was adapted for their own institution. The second scale, the Instrumental Activities of Daily Living Scale (IADL), addresses a level of functioning that has previously been insufficiently represented in attempts to assess everyday functional competence. Both scales have been further tested for their effectiveness in various types of institutions and facilities that serve older individuals in the community. Before delving into the specific behaviors measured by these scales, we will provide a brief overview of the framework of competence in which these behaviors are categorized (Lawton, 1969). Human behavior is seen as varying in complexity, depending on the tasks at hand. The lowest level is referred to as life maintenance, followed by progressively more complex levels of functioning.

title: Diabetes in pregnancy: management of diabetes and its complications from preconception to the postnatal period (NG3)
text: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) released new guidelines (NG3) in February 2015 regarding the management of diabetes during pregnancy. It is important for healthcare teams to be aware of these guidelines and implement the recommended practices. The guidelines include providing preconception care with a target HbA1c level of 48 mmol/mol. Women who are at risk of developing gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) should undergo a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT). The diagnostic criteria for GDM have changed to a fasting glucose level of 5.6 mmol/L or higher, or a 2-hour glucose level of 7.8 mmol/L or higher. The glycaemic targets for all pregnant women with diabetes have changed to a fasting glucose level below 5.3 mmol/L (4-5.2 mmol/L if on insulin), and a 1-hour postprandial glucose level below 7.8 mmol/L if it can be achieved safely. Continuous glucose monitoring and insulin pump therapy should not be used as a routine, but can be considered if there are difficulties in achieving glycaemic control. Capillary ketone testing should be done regularly for women with type 1 diabetes when they have high blood sugar levels, and for all women with diabetes, including those with GDM, when they are acutely unwell. There is now more flexibility in the recommended timing for delivery, with women with types 1 and 2 diabetes being advised to deliver between 37+0 weeks and 38+6 weeks, and women with GDM being advised to deliver before 40+6 weeks (and earlier if complications arise). Postnatal testing for women with GDM should be done using fasting glucose levels (not OGTT) at 6-13 weeks after giving birth. HbA1c can be used for testing after this time period. Implementing these changes will have resource implications, including an expected increase in the number of women diagnosed with GDM.

title: Mental health difficulties across childhood and mental health service use: findings from a longitudinal population-based study.
text:
In the last two decades, the prevalence of mental disorders among children and adolescents in high-income countries has remained unchanged, despite increased investment in mental health services. One possible reason for this is the lack of sufficient contact with mental health professionals. However, it is unclear how many children actually receive the necessary treatment according to clinical practice guidelines, or how long they have to wait before receiving treatment. 

The aim of this study was to examine the level of mental healthcare received by Australian children between the ages of 4 and 14. The researchers used the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire to track the trajectories of mental health symptoms. They also analyzed data from national Medicare Benefits Schedule and Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme records to identify health professional visits and medications prescribed. 

The results revealed four different trajectories of mental health symptoms: low, high-decreasing, moderate-increasing, and high-increasing. Most children with mental health symptoms had very few visits to mental health professionals, and only a small percentage received treatment that met the minimum standards outlined in the study. Interestingly, children in the high-increasing and moderate-increasing trajectories were more likely to seek care, but their symptoms did not improve. 

In conclusion, it is crucial for children and adolescents with mental health issues to receive treatment that adheres to minimal practice guidelines. Further research is necessary to assess the quality of care currently provided to children with mental health difficulties, and to determine how clinicians can be adequately funded and supported to deliver care that meets these guidelines. The authors of this study have no conflicts of interest to declare.

title: Rembrandt Scholz
text: This study examines how changes in medical care have affected population health in Lithuania, Hungary, and Romania, with a comparison to west Germany. We focused on deaths from certain causes that should not occur with timely and effective healthcare (amenable mortality) and calculated how changes in mortality from these conditions have influenced changes in life expectancy from birth to age 75 [e (0-75)] between the periods of 1980/81 to 1988 and 1992 to 1997. Temporary life expectancy consistently improved in west Germany, with men gaining 2.7 years and women gaining 1.6 years. In contrast, the gains were relatively small in the other countries, except for Hungarian women who gained 1.3 years. Romanian men experienced a loss of 1.3 years. In the 1980s, the reduction in infant mortality significantly contributed to improvements in temporary life expectancy in all countries, ranging from a quarter to half a year. More than half of this improvement can be attributed to amenable conditions. Among older age groups, the decline in amenable mortality contributed about 40% to those over 40 in Germany and to a lesser extent in Hungary, while causing a decrease in life expectancy in Romania. In the 1990s, improvements in infant mortality continued to have a significant impact on life expectancy in Lithuania and Hungary, but had little effect in Germany or Romania. Among adults, improvements in amenable mortality continued to benefit Hungarians and west Germans. In Lithuania, up to two-thirds of the increase in temporary life expectancy can be attributed to the decline in mortality from ischaemic heart disease, while medical care seemed to have a negative impact otherwise. Romanian men and women experienced an increase in amenable mortality, which contributed to up to half of the overall decrease in life expectancy. Our findings suggest that over the past 20 years, changes in medical care have had a significant impact, both positive and negative, on mortality in selected central and eastern European countries.

title: The Women's Interagency HIV Study
text: The Women's Interagency HIV Study is the largest group of HIV-positive women in the United States to date, consisting of 2,058 participants. Additionally, there is a comparison group of 568 women who are HIV-negative. This article provides a detailed description of the methodology used, as well as the training and quality assurance measures implemented. The study population is also discussed.

title: Prevalence of the Metabolic Syndrome Among Us Adults: Findings From the Third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
text: Metabolic syndrome is diagnosed when three or more of the following conditions are met: abdominal obesity (waist circumference exceeding 102 cm in men and 88 cm in women), hypertriglyceridemia of 150 mg/dl or higher, low levels of high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol (less than 40 mg/dl in men or 50 mg/dl in women), high blood pressure (130/85 mm Hg or above), or fasting glucose levels of at least 110 mg/dl. Individuals with metabolic syndrome are at a higher risk of developing diabetes and cardiovascular disease, and have increased mortality rates from all causes, particularly cardiovascular disease. The aim of the study was to determine the prevalence of metabolic syndrome in the United States by analyzing data from the Third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, which included 8814 men and women aged 20 years and older between 1988 and 1994. This survey is a cross-sectional health survey of a sample of the noninstitutionalized civilian American population. The overall age-adjusted prevalence of metabolic syndrome was found to be 23.7%. The prevalence increased from 6.7% in individuals aged 20 to 29 years to 42% in those aged 70 years and older. There was no significant difference in prevalence rates between genders across different racial groups. Metabolic syndrome was most prevalent in Mexican Americans and least prevalent in whites, African Americans, and other racial groups. Among both African Americans and Mexican Americans, women had higher prevalence rates than men. Based on age-specific prevalence rates and US census data from 2000, it is estimated that 47 million US residents have metabolic syndrome. Given its high prevalence, it is important to estimate the direct medical costs associated with metabolic syndrome. In the majority of cases, improper nutrition and lack of physical activity are the main contributing factors, highlighting the importance of addressing obesity and promoting physical activity in the United States.

title: Baseline cytology, human papillomavirus testing, and risk for cervical neoplasia: A 10-year cohort analysis
text: As more information is gathered about the development of cervical cancer, there is growing doubt about the necessity of annual Pap smear screenings for all women. This study aimed to determine if testing for the presence of human papillomavirus (HPV) in cervical smears could identify women at higher risk for cervical cancer. By identifying these women, it would be possible to increase the interval between Pap smear screenings for women at lower risk. The study included women enrolled in the Kaiser Permanente healthcare plan in Portland, Oregon, who underwent annual Pap smear screenings between April 1989 and November 1990. Out of 23,702 women, 20,810 had satisfactory cervical smears with enough samples for HPV testing. The testing was done using a polymerase chain reaction-based method with MYO9/11 primers. During the study period, most women (83.6%) had at least one follow-up smear. However, women with abnormal results had more smears than those with normal results. Follow-up was conducted annually for a total of 122 months. The HPV results did not influence patient management decisions. Of the 20,810 baseline Pap smears, 96% were negative (N = 20,156). Among these patients, 13% tested positive for HPV. Out of the 20,810 women, 654 (3.1%) had baseline smears classified as ASC or worse. Among these, 63.8% tested positive for HPV. One hundred seventy-eight women had a cytologic diagnosis of a low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion or worse, and 80.3% of them tested positive for HPV. Over the 10-year follow-up period, 171 patients developed cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) 3 or cervical cancer. Among these, 112 had a normal baseline smear and 59 had an abnormal baseline smear. Only 49.2% of the patients diagnosed within the first 45 months of follow-up had an abnormal baseline smear. During this initial 45-month period, 7.85% of women with at least ASC on their initial Pap test were diagnosed with CIN 3 or cancer. The cumulative incidence at 10 years of follow-up was 10.2%. Sixty out of the 171 women with CIN 3 or cervical cancer had a negative baseline HPV test. Among the 118 women diagnosed within the first 45 months, 79.4% were initially HPV positive. The cumulative incidence of CIN 3 or cancer among women with a positive baseline HPV test was 6.92% over 10 years, but only 1.73% at 45 months. The risk of developing CIN 3 or cancer remained elevated throughout the study for women with a positive baseline HPV test. The predictive ability of the baseline Pap smear decreased as the follow-up interval increased. Out of the 3,216 patients, 15% had a positive Pap smear, positive HPV test, or both at the initial examination. Among the 171 women who developed CIN 3 or cancer, 71.9% fell into this category. Within the first 45 months, 86% of the patients diagnosed were positive in at least one of the screening tests. The cumulative incidence over 45 months for women with positive HPV testing and/or abnormal Pap smear results was 4.54%. Women with negative results in both screening tests had a cumulative risk of 0.16% for the same period. At 10 years, the cumulative risk incidence for these two groups was 6.83% and 0.79%, respectively, resulting in a negative predictive value of 99.1% for combined testing.

title: Preconception Care and the Risk of Congenital Anomalies in the Offspring of Women With Diabetes Mellitus: A Meta-Analysis
text: Preconception care (PCC) and strict control of blood sugar levels before and during pregnancy are both used to reduce the chances of birth defects in babies born to women with type 1 or type 2 diabetes. These defects are largely attributed to poor control of blood sugar levels during the time of conception. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of PCC by analyzing published studies on PCC in women with diabetes from 1970 to 2000. The data was collected by two reviewers independently, and the rate and relative risk of major and minor birth defects were combined from eligible studies using a random effects model. The levels of glycosylated hemoglobin in the early stages of the first trimester were also recorded. The study included eight retrospective and eight prospective cohort studies conducted in Europe, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Israel. Most participants had type 1 diabetes, but three studies included women with type 2 diabetes. The women who received PCC were on average about 2 years older than those who did not. The methods of PCC varied, but most centers provided some education to the mothers about the risks associated with poor control of blood sugar levels during pregnancy. In seven studies that reported early gestational glycosylated hemoglobin values, the levels were consistently lower in women who received PCC. Among 2104 babies, the rate of major and minor birth defects was 2.4% in the PCC group and 7.7% in the non-PCC group, resulting in a combined relative risk of 0.32. Among 2651 babies, major birth defects were less common in the PCC group (2.1% vs. 6.5%), with a combined relative risk of 0.36. Similar results were found when only prospective studies were analyzed and when the examiners of the babies were unaware of the mothers' PCC status. The study with the lowest risk of major birth defects was the one that administered folic acid to its PCC recipients, resulting in a relative risk of 0.11. This meta-analysis, which included both retrospective and prospective studies, shows that PCC is associated with a significantly lower risk of birth defects in babies born to women with diabetes. This reduced risk is accompanied by lower levels of glycosylated hemoglobin in the first trimester in women who receive PCC.

title: Behçet's disease associated with a lymphoproliferative disorder, mixed cryoglobulinemia, and an immune complex mediated vasculitis.
text: This abstract discusses the case of a 59-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Behcet's disease for the past 13 years. Throughout this period, she has experienced various symptoms including aphthous stomatitis, genital ulcers, uveitis leading to blindness, recurrent erythema nodosum, and synovitis. In 1970, she was also diagnosed with a poorly differentiated diffuse lymphocytic lymphoma and received radiotherapy as treatment. Six years later, she developed mixed cryoglobulinemia and immune complex mediated vasculitis, which presented as purpura and neuropathy. However, these symptoms improved with prednisone and chlorambucil therapy. The subsequent progression of her lymphoproliferative disorder suggests that it was ultimately benign.

title: Older People at the End of Life: Delivery of Care and Needs for Improvement from the Perspective of Bereaved Relatives
text:
As the number of older individuals with chronic illnesses and multiple health conditions continues to rise, the importance of palliative care for geriatric patients has become increasingly evident. This study aimed to investigate the perspectives of bereaved relatives regarding their experiences and expectations of care for older individuals in the final phase of life. 

Qualitative interviews were conducted with 12 relatives of deceased older patients, all aged 60 years or older. These interviews were recorded, transcribed, coded, and analyzed using the qualitative content analysis approach developed by Mayring. 

The findings revealed that bereaved relatives perceived various inadequacies in the care provided to geriatric patients in their final phase of life. They criticized instances of overtreatment, such as unnecessary skin cancer diagnostics, as well as unmet needs, including inadequate pain management, lack of patient-centered care, and poor communication. Family doctors were identified as the primary point of contact within the healthcare system. 

In conclusion, from the perspective of bereaved relatives, the care provided to older individuals in their final phase of life is severely lacking. They highlight inappropriate prioritization and a disregard for palliative care. There is a clear need for improved communication and information exchange regarding the needs and expectations of patients and their relatives, as well as the treatment goals. To address these issues, it may be beneficial to utilize advance directives more extensively. Additionally, there is a need to strengthen generalist palliative care, particularly through the involvement of family doctors and community nurses.

title: Role of Computerized Physician Order Entry Systems in Facilitating Medication Errors
text: Compared to the control group, the intervention group had a lower percentage of patients with deep-vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism at 90 days (8.2 percent vs. 103). The Kaplan-Meier estimates showed that the likelihood of freedom from these conditions at 90 days was higher in the intervention group (94.1 percent) compared to the control group (90.6 percent). The computer alert program reduced the risk of deep-vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism at 90 days by 41 percent. This study suggests that notifying physicians about their patients' increased risk for venous thromboembolism can lead to a decrease in the incidence of these conditions. It also highlights the importance of using appropriate prophylactic measures for urology patients who are at higher risk. The use of computer alert systems may become more common in healthcare settings if they are proven to improve the quality of care.

title: Beta-band oscillations--signalling the status quo?
text: This review examines the potential functional role of beta-band oscillations, which is currently not well understood. We explore recent studies that provide evidence on top-down mechanisms involved in cognitive processing, the motor system, and the pathophysiology of movement disorders. These studies suggest a unifying hypothesis: beta-band activity appears to be linked to the preservation of the current sensorimotor or cognitive state. We propose that beta oscillations and/or coupling in the beta-band are more pronounced when maintaining the status quo is intended or predicted, compared to when a change is expected. Additionally, we propose that an excessive increase in beta-band activity due to pathology may lead to an abnormal persistence of the status quo and a decline in flexible behavioral and cognitive control.

title: Safety, pharmacokinetics and efficacy of IMCgp100, a first-in-class soluble TCR-antiCD3 bispecific t cell redirector with solid tumour activity: Results from the FIH study in melanoma.
text:
Background: T-cell based bispecific agents have demonstrated effectiveness in treating hematologic cancers, but their efficacy in solid tumors remains uncertain. IMCgp100 is a bispecific biologic that combines an enhanced T-cell receptor specific for gp100 with an anti-CD3 scFV. In laboratory tests, IMCgp100 has shown the ability to bind to gp100+ melanoma cells, redirect cytotoxicity, and induce strong immune responses. 

Methods: Phase I of the study was conducted on patients with advanced melanoma who were HLA-A2+. The study used a 3+3 design to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD). Patients were treated with IMCgp100 intravenously either weekly (QW, Arm 1) or daily for 4 weeks followed by a 3-week break (4QD3W, Arm 2) to assess safety, pharmacokinetics (PK), and efficacy. The recommended phase 2 regimen (RP2D-QW) was established based on the results.

Results: In the dose escalation phase of Phase I, 31 patients received doses ranging from 5ng/kg to 900ng/kg. In Arm 1, dose-limiting toxicity of grade 3 or 4 hypotension was observed, which was associated with the rapid movement of lymphocytes from the peripheral blood to the skin and tumor. The MTD was determined to be 600ng/kg QW. IMCgp100 exhibited a dose-proportional profile, with a plasma half-life of 5-6 hours at the RP2D...

title: The Bitterest Pills: The Troubling Story of Antipsychotic Drugs
text: This text is protected by copyright © Joanna Moncrieff 2013. All rights are reserved. It presents a thought-provoking reassessment of the antipsychotics' history, shedding light on their evolution from harmful neurological substances to seemingly miraculous remedies. It highlights the tendency to magnify their advantages while downplaying or disregarding their harmful effects.

title: Variables Affecting Kinetics of Minimal Residual Disease Clearance in Children with Lymphoblastic Leukaemia; Results of the United Kingdom Medical Research Council (UK MRC) Protocols ALL97, ALL97/99 and ALL2003.
text: We conducted a study to examine how patient, leukaemia, and treatment characteristics affect the rate at which Minimal Residual Disease (MRD) clears in children with lymphoblastic leukaemia who are treated using an intensive risk stratified approach. The UK MRC protocol ALL97 (1997-1999) and its amended version ALL 97/99 (1999-2002) compared the effectiveness and side effects of dexamethasone (DEX) with prednisolone (PRED), and 6-thioguanine (TG) with 6-Mercaptopurine (MP) in a randomized manner. The trial showed a 5-year event-free survival (EFS) rate of 80%, with better outcomes in terms of systemic and Central Nervous System effects in DEX recipients compared to PRED recipients, but no difference between TG and MP recipients. Throughout the trial, there were changes made to the risk stratification and treatment regimens, which allowed us to assess their impact on MRD clearance. We compared this with the clearance in patients treated on the subsequent trial ALL 2003, which had a more intensive induction phase including DEX and Pegylated Asparaginase. The variables we investigated for their potential influence on MRD status at the end of induction (EOI) were: NCI Risk; Asparaginase intensity (Erwinia Asparaginase [ERW] in ALL 97 and early part of ALL97/99 vs native or Pegylated E. Coli Asparaginase [E. Coli] in later part of ALL 97/99 and ALL2003); DEX vs PRED; and marrow response at day 8/15 of induction (Slow Early Response [SER] >25% blasts vs Rapid Early Response [RER] ⩽ 25% blasts). We assessed MRD using either a semi-quantitative sequence-specific PCR (ALL97) or Real-Time Quantitative PCR (ALL99 and ALL 2003) of antigen receptor gene re-arrangements at EOI. MRD status was classified as NEG if no MRD was detected by two markers sensitive to 10^-4; POS if > 10^-4, and Positive Outside Quantitative Range (POQR) if positive > 10^-4. We had results from retrospective testing in 66 ALL97 and 76 ALL97/99 patients, and 204 ALL2003 patients who were monitored prospectively. We found no significant difference in the proportions of patients who were MRD NEG, POS, or POQR in the steroid or NCI sub-groups. However, significantly more ERW Asparaginase recipients were MRD POS compared to E.Coli recipients (p < 0.001). Importantly, we found that patients who were MRD POS at EOI had the same low risk of relapse as those who had undetectable MRD.

title: Chromosome numbers in certain Indian species ofUtricularia L. (Lentibulariaceae)
text: The chromosome numbers obtained from meiotic studies have been documented for the following species of Utricularia: U. aurea Lour. (n=21), U. baouleënsis A. Chev. (n=10), U. caerulea L. (n=20), U. inflexa var. stellaris (Linn.f.) P. Taylor (n=21), U. minutissima Vahl (n=8), U. scandens Benj. (n=6, 7), and U. stricticaulis Stapf (n=7). It is worth noting that U. scandens consists of two distinct cyto-races.

title: Detection of [Ca2+]I Changes In Sub-Plasma Membrane Micro Domains in A Single Living Cell By an Optical Fiber-Based Nanobiosensor
text: A nanobiosensor based on optical fiber was successfully created to detect changes in intracellular calcium ion concentration in specific areas of a single living smooth muscle cell and a single living cardiomyocyte. This was achieved by coating silver and then immobilizing Calcium Green-1 Dextran, a calcium ion sensitive dye, on the distal end of the nanoprobe. The nanobiosensor was able to detect extremely low levels of calcium ions within the nanomolar range, which is similar to the natural level of calcium ions in a single living cell. The response time was very fast, allowing for the detection of brief calcium ion signaling events associated with calcium ion microdomains. The effects of stimulants such as high potassium buffer solution and norepinephrine solution were also studied. This system has the potential to greatly enhance the development of a sophisticated nano-diagnostic platform for real-time sensing and diagnosing of intracellular calcium ion concentration at the individual cell level.

title: Construction of plant bacterial artificial chromosome (BAC) libraries: an illustrated guide.
text:
Title: A Comprehensive Protocol for Constructing Plant Bacterial Artificial Chromosome (BAC) Libraries

Abstract: Bacterial artificial chromosome (BAC) libraries have become indispensable tools in plant genetic research. However, the lack of detailed protocols and the challenges associated with isolating clean, high molecular weight DNA from plant cells hinder the creation of plant BAC libraries by new practitioners. This article presents an illustrated, step-by-step protocol that addresses these issues and aims to facilitate the construction of plant BAC libraries. The protocol is designed to be accessible to both novice and experienced investigators, with the goal of overcoming barriers to BAC cloning in plants and promoting advancements in plant genomics.

title: Activation by IKKα of a second, evolutionary conserved, NF-κB signaling pathway
text: The degradation of IκB inhibitors is the basis for the canonical nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) signaling pathway activated in response to infections in mammals. This pathway relies on the IκB kinase (IKK), which consists of two catalytic subunits, IKKα and IKKβ. While IKKβ is crucial for the phosphorylation and degradation of inducible IκB, IKKα does not play a role in this process. Our study demonstrates that IKKα is necessary for B cell maturation, the development of secondary lymphoid organs, the upregulation of specific NF-κB target genes, and the processing of the NF-κB2 (p100) precursor. IKKα exhibits a preference for phosphorylating NF-κB2, and this activity requires its phosphorylation by upstream kinases, potentially including NF-κB–inducing kinase (NIK). Consequently, IKKα serves as a critical component of an alternative NF-κB activation pathway that relies on regulated NF-κB2 processing rather than IκB degradation.

title: Identification and transmission of Piper yellow mottle virus and Cucumber mosaic virus infecting black pepper (Piper nigrum) in Sri Lanka
text: A mixture of viruses was found in Sri Lankan black pepper affected by yellow mottle disease. These viruses included Piper yellow mottle virus (PYMV) particles, Cucumber mosaic virus (CMV), and unidentified virus-like particles. To purify PYMV, an effective procedure was developed. Only partially purified extracts were able to detect badnavirus particles using immunosorbent and conventional electron microscopy. PYMV was identified as the cause of the disease, while the other two viruses did not contribute to the symptoms. PYMV was transmitted through grafting and by insect vectors such as citrus mealy bug and black pepper lace bug. However, it was not transmitted through mechanical inoculation or seeds. CMV was transmitted to indicator plants through mechanical inoculation and the vector Aphis gossypii, but not through Myzus persicae. However, neither mechanical nor insect transmission of CMV to black pepper was successful. A sensitive polymerase chain reaction assay was developed to detect PYMV in black pepper.

title: A forkhead-domain gene is mutated in a severe speech and language disorder
text: Individuals with developmental disorders of speech and language struggle to acquire expressive and/or receptive language, even without any significant sensory or neurological impairments, and despite having adequate intelligence and opportunities. While studies on twins consistently indicate a strong genetic component, most families with speech and language deficits show complex inheritance patterns, and a specific gene that predisposes individuals to these disorders has not been identified. However, we have conducted research on a unique three-generation family, known as KE, where a severe speech and language disorder is passed down as an autosomal-dominant monogenic trait. Our previous work successfully mapped the responsible locus, SPCH1, to a specific region on chromosome 7. Additionally, we discovered an unrelated individual, CS, who has a chromosomal translocation involving the SPCH1 interval and experiences speech and language impairment. In our latest findings, we demonstrate that the gene FOXP2, which encodes a potential transcription factor with a polyglutamine tract and a forkhead DNA-binding domain, is directly disrupted by the translocation breakpoint in CS. Furthermore, we have identified a point mutation in affected members of the KE family that alters a crucial amino acid residue in the forkhead domain. These discoveries strongly suggest that FOXP2 plays a role in the developmental process leading to speech and language abilities.

title: The Growth and Sporulation of the Benign and Malignant Tertian Malarial Parasites in the Culture Tube and in the Human Host
text: Dr. Sinton began researching the cultivation of malaria parasites in Liverpool some time ago, at my suggestion. Later, Drs. J. G. Thomson and McLellan, as well as Dr. D. Thomson, took over the research with even better results. We are extremely grateful to Sir Edwin Durning-Lawrence, Bart., for providing us with the expertise of Dr. J. G. title: Innate immunity to a facultative intracellular bacterial pathogen.
text: For a long time, the murine reaction to Listeria monocytogenes has been regarded as a prime example of T-cell-based immunity. Nevertheless, there is now significant evidence suggesting that mice lacking T-cells can still survive when faced with a L. monocytogenes infection. In recent times, progress has been achieved in comprehending the cellular processes and disease development associated with this infection.

title: Diversity and Evenness: A Unifying Notation and Its Consequences
text: The concept of diversity can be measured using three commonly used methods: Simpson's index, Shannon's entropy, and the total number of species. These measures are connected to Renyi's definition of a generalized entropy, which allows for a unified understanding of diversity. This unified concept suggests that there is a range of possible diversity measures. These measures can estimate the effective number of species present and differ only in their inclusion or exclusion of less common species. The idea of diversity in a community, as opposed to a sample, is explored and linked to the shape of the species-abundance curve in the long run. Additionally, a new and reasonable definition of evenness is established.

title: Guide to yeast genetics and molecular biology
text: This book, along with its companion Volume 350, has been meticulously crafted to cater to the requirements of graduate students, postdoctoral students, and researchers. It offers a comprehensive collection of the latest techniques essential for studying genes in yeast. The included procedures are designed to assist newcomers in establishing a yeast laboratory and acquiring proficiency in fundamental manipulations. Additionally, the book provides pertinent background information and references for each procedure, serving as a valuable resource for developing protocols across various disciplines. The book covers a wide range of specific topics such as cytology, biochemistry, cell fractionation, and cell biology.

title: Cutadapt removes adapter sequences from high-throughput sequencing reads
text: The reads obtained from sequencing small RNA on current sequencing machines are typically longer than the RNA itself. As a result, these reads often contain portions of the 3' adapter. Before mapping the reads, it is necessary to locate and remove this adapter accurately, even in the presence of errors. Existing solutions for this task are either difficult to use or lack the necessary features, particularly support for color space data. To address this, we have developed a user-friendly command-line tool called cutadapt. Cutadapt is capable of handling data from 454, Illumina, and SOLiD (color space) platforms. It offers two adapter trimming algorithms and various other useful features. The source code for Cutadapt, which is licensed under MIT, can be downloaded from http://code.google.com/p/cutadapt/.
