title: Levels of selection in evolution
text: Since the groundbreaking work of George Williams, W. D. Hamilton, and Richard Dawkins, evolutionary biologists have acknowledged that natural selection primarily benefits lower-level units such as individuals, cells, and genes, rather than the group as a whole. This raises a fundamental question in biology: how can competition between these different levels of natural selection be prevented from undermining the benefits of cooperation? In this book, twelve prominent scientists explore this question by providing a comprehensive overview of the current research in evolutionary biology. Recent studies have revealed that various mechanisms have evolved at different levels of biological organization to mitigate potential conflicts in natural selection. The editor, Laurent Keller, aims to bring together leading researchers from all biological disciplines to discuss these conflicts and their resolutions. This multi-level approach not only provides valuable insights into the evolution of life but also bridges the gap between molecular and organismal biologists. The chapters in this book adhere to a rigorous theoretical framework, resulting in a unique synergy that is characteristic of multi-authored books. The contributors, along with the editor, include H. Charles J. Godfray, Edward Allen Herre, Dawn M. Kitchen, Egbert Giles Leigh, Jr., Catherine M. Lessells, Richard E. Michod, Leonard Nunney, Craig Packer, Andrew Pomiankowski, H. Kern Reeve, John Maynard Smith, and Eors Szathmary.

title: A psychometric evaluation of the Beck Depression Inventory–II.
text: This article presents psychometric information about the second edition of the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI-II; A. T. Beck, R. A. Steer, & G. K. Brown, 1996), focusing on internal consistency, factorial validity, and gender differences. Both versions of the inventory showed high internal reliability in the entire student sample. Due to significant differences between the average scores of BDI and BDI-II, new cutoffs were developed for analog research on the BDI-II. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses revealed that a 2-factor solution best summarized the data for both versions of the inventory, explaining 41% and 46% of the shared variance in BDI and BDI-II responses, respectively. These factor solutions were consistently validated, although the significance of each factor varied by gender. The authors conclude that the BDI-II has a stronger factor structure compared to the BDI.

title: Why people feel crowded: An examination of objective and subjective crowding
text: Previous research has discovered a limited connection between objective and subjective crowding, which goes against logical and common-sense explanations for why people feel crowded. To investigate this phenomenon, we collected data from a representative sample in Bangkok, Thailand, where household crowding is four times higher than in Western societies. We explored various possibilities to understand why this disparity exists. By examining seven different indicators of objective crowding, our analysis indicates that the modest relationship is not due to measurement errors. Contrary to previous assumptions, our findings suggest that the relationship between objective and subjective crowding is not linear and that there is a limit to how much increased objective crowding affects the feeling of being crowded. Additionally, our analysis suggests that the strength of this relationship is somewhat influenced by household circumstances, such as the level of control an individual has over the use of household space.

title: Self-Report and Tests of Memory Aging
text: There has been a lack of correlation between memory complaints and memory tests. However, when participants were asked self-report questions about their everyday remembering abilities, sixty volunteers ranging from 21 to 84 years old accurately rated their memory competence. These participants were divided into four memory processes and were given six tests to assess their verbal, faces, story, nonverbal auditory, visual, and tactual memory. The results showed a canonical correlation (r = 0.67) between the self-report and test measures, and both sets of measures declined with age in a similar manner. Interestingly, the older participants were more accurate in their self-ratings compared to the younger participants, although this was not the case for all tests. It appeared that some participants were influenced by their expectations of performing poorly, which affected their actual performance.

title: Code of the Street: Decency, Violence, and the Moral Life of the Inner City
text: The inner-city black community is often associated with unpredictable and irrational street violence. However, this violence is not as haphazard as it may seem; it is actually governed by an informal yet widely recognized set of rules known as the code of the street. Your appearance, manner of speech, ability to make eye contact, and understanding of social hierarchy - these seemingly insignificant details can have life-or-death consequences, especially for young people who are particularly vulnerable. This analysis of the inner-city mindset reveals that the code is a response to various factors such as the scarcity of well-paying jobs, racial discrimination, widespread drug abuse, feelings of isolation, and a lack of hope. The police have little control over this situation, leaving individuals to rely on their ability to command respect in public for their safety and self-worth. This respect is established through physical and psychological dominance, often accompanied by an implicit threat of violence. The most effective counterforce against the code is a strong and loving family, but unfortunately, the street culture prevails and often undermines decency by exerting control over public spaces, ensnaring individuals with higher aspirations in its grip.

title: A generic measure of relationship satisfaction.
text: This article discusses the creation of a concise and dependable measure of satisfaction that can be applied to various types of close relationships in today's society. In the first study, the Relationship Assessment Scale (RAS), consisting of 7 items, was given to 125 individuals who identified themselves as being "in love." The analysis revealed that the scale had a single factor structure, with strong factor loadings and moderate correlations among the items. Additionally, the scale showed significant correlations with measures of love, sexual attitudes, self-disclosure, commitment, and investment in a relationship. In the second study, the scale was administered to 57 couples in ongoing relationships. The analysis supported a single factor structure, with a high alpha reliability of .86, and correlations with relevant relationship measures. The scale also showed a strong correlation of .80 with a longer criterion measure, the Dyadic Adjustment Scale (Spanier, 1976), and both scales were effective in distinguishing between couples who stayed together and those who broke up. Overall, the RAS is a concise and reliable measure of relationship satisfaction that has been validated psychometrically.

title: ECONOMIC RESTRUCTURING AND SUBURBANIZATION IN CHINA
text: Suburbanization in China followed a pattern similar to other countries, occurring after cities experienced significant industrial and population growth. This study focuses on suburbanization in Beijing, Shanghai, Shenyang, and Dalian. Economic restructuring led to a decline in population in the urban core from 1982 to 1990 due to decentralization, while the inner suburbs experienced population growth. Several factors contributed to suburbanization, including the marketization of urban land, the conversion of industrial land for tertiary use, transportation improvements, access to foreign and domestic capital, urban housing rehabilitation, and the construction of new housing in the suburbs. While there are some similarities, there are also major differences between American and Chinese suburbanization. Unlike the polycentric spatial structure seen in current metropolitan areas in the United States, suburbanization in China is still in its early stages, with suburbs primarily centered around the city.

title: The Assumption of Caregiving: Grandmothers Raising the Children of the Crack Cocaine Epidemic:
text: This article presents selected findings from a study that focuses on the experiences of 71 African American women who have taken on the sole responsibility of caring for at least one grandchild or great-grandchild due to the parent's involvement in crack cocaine use. Despite the individual circumstances of each case, three distinct patterns of assuming the caregiving role emerged from the analysis of in-depth interviews and participant observation: sudden assumption, negotiated assumption, and inevitable assumption of the permanent caregiver role. Each pattern is described across six dimensions: forewarning, initiation, the triggering event, the caregiver's goal, her anticipated duration of the caregiving period, and her perceived impact on her own future. These accounts offer valuable insights for professionals working with women, children, and families, shedding light on the far-reaching consequences of the crack cocaine epidemic.

title: The effect of information related to fat content and taste on consumer responses to a reduced-fat frankfurter and a reduced-fat chocolate bar
text:
The study aimed to examine how product information influences people's responses to frankfurter sausages and chocolate bars. This was done by comparing sensory and hedonic ratings in two different conditions: blind tasting and tasting with information provided. Additionally, the study investigated the impact of information alone by having participants rate the expected sensory and hedonic intensities of the products based on different package claims.

Three groups of participants were included in the study, each receiving different information. The first group, referred to as the basic group, received no additional claims about the products (n = 31). The second group, known as the reduced-fat group, was informed that the products had reduced-fat (n = 29). The third group, called the flavorful group, was told that the products had full meat or chocolate flavor (n = 31).

The results showed that product information increased the perceived pleasantness of the frankfurter sausages in all three information groups compared to the blind ratings. However, the information did not have any effect on the pleasantness ratings of the chocolate bars. Furthermore, the reduced-fat group rated the expected attribute intensities of both the frankfurters and chocolates lower than the other groups.

Overall, the impact of product information was more evident in the ratings of sensory attributes rather than in the pleasantness ratings.

title: Transnationalism and identity
text: The concepts of transnationalism and identity inherently require a comparison. This is because many people's networks of exchange and involvement across borders are based on a shared sense of identity. On the other hand, the identities of numerous individuals and groups are shaped within social contexts that span multiple locations. In this introductory article, we will first explore the transnational perspective on migration studies, followed by some criticisms and unresolved questions. The final section will summarize the key points raised by the contributing authors of the main articles in this themed issue of JEMS, particularly regarding how transnational settings and dynamics impact the formation, negotiation, and perpetuation of identities.

title: Social Isolation and Social Support: An Applied Perspective
text: Considerable evidence from empirical studies supports the idea that social networks and support play a crucial role in the health and well-being of older adults. However, more research is needed before effective interventions can be widely implemented to improve an elderly person's social network. This article discusses social support and isolation from a practical standpoint. The authors have combined presentations from a symposium on applied gerontology sponsored by the National Institute on Aging in August 1992. They provide general observations about the field of applied social relations in later life, discuss the mental health aspects of these relationships, outline fundamental principles and existing technology in this field, describe a screening tool for social isolation developed by one of the authors (Lubben), and explore different areas of knowledge related to social relations among older adults. They conclude by highlighting areas that require further attention and research.

title: Wine and health: faraway concepts?
text: The aim of this paper is to investigate how consumers perceive the health benefits of wine and how this relates to their wine consumption habits. The study involved conducting face-to-face surveys with 402 wine consumers, and the data was analyzed using two-step cluster analysis. Differences among groups were confirmed using ANOVA, and χ2 significance analysis was used to profile the groups. A multivariate binary logistic regression was used to determine the influence of wine consumption on perceptions of healthiness. The findings revealed that consumers can be categorized into four groups: two groups that prioritize health – optimistic and medical, and two groups that do not prioritize health – unintentional drinkers and unconvinced. There were no significant differences in socio-economic terms among the groups. The study also found that wine consumption behavior has an impact on health orientation, particularly for monthly and wine drinkers compared to weekly and other alcohol drinkers. Health-oriented consumers are more likely to value and be willing to pay more for wine that enhances health. Consumers believe that wine...

title: The Changing Problem of Overcrowded Housing
text: The problem of overcrowding in the United States has seen a significant increase after a long period of decline. This increase has been particularly pronounced in certain areas and among specific ethnic groups. The definition of overcrowding and how it is addressed in policy has also evolved. In this study, we explore the unique characteristics of those affected by overcrowding, where they are located, the reasons behind the resurgence of overcrowding, and why it is concentrated in specific areas. While factors such as ethnicity, age, immigration, and poverty play significant roles, the conditions of the housing market appear to have less influence. Additionally, we demonstrate that the standards used to assess overcrowding have changed over time and that social norms differ among ethnic groups. The issue of overcrowding highlights the challenges of establishing uniform standards in a diverse and evolving multiethnic society. To address the most severe housing needs, it would be beneficial to adopt a more flexible approach to setting standards that takes into account the unique circumstances of highly impacted areas.

title: Best response dynamics and socially stable strategies
text: This paper explores the concept of an evolutionarily stable strategy, which refers to a strategy that remains robust even when faced with a small number of mutant invaders. Additionally, it examines the best response dynamics, a dynamic process where a strategy's frequency increases only if it is the best response to the current strategy distribution. The stability concept proposed by Gilboa and Matsui is directly derived from this dynamic process. By modifying these two stability concepts, the paper demonstrates the equivalence between the static and dynamic concepts. It also highlights the existence of set-valued versions of these concepts. Furthermore, the paper provides examples to illustrate the usefulness of these concepts in analyzing forward induction and preplay communication.

title: From youth to adult homelessness
text: Governments have expressed interest in early intervention strategies to combat youth homelessness, but critics argue that these programs lack clear outcomes. This study aims to explore the consequences of not implementing early intervention programs and how young individuals transition into adult homelessness. Specifically, the study examines the "social adaptation" hypothesis, which suggests that the longer young people experience homelessness, the more they become accustomed to it as a way of life. The research analyzes data from 1,677 individuals who first became homeless at 18 years old or younger. Among the sample, three-quarters had progressed to adult homelessness (defined as 25 years or older), while one-quarter were young adults aged 19 to 24. The findings confirm that the longer individuals experience homelessness, the more challenging it becomes to escape it. However, the study argues that the social adaptation theory exaggerates the extent to which people accept homelessness as a permanent lifestyle. With long-term support, individuals can reintegrate into conventional housing. The paper concludes by offering three policy recommendations.

title: Urban spatial development in the land policy reform era: evidence from Beijing
text: This paper examines the characteristics of urban spatial development in Beijing and investigates the influence of the emerging land market and land policy reform on these characteristics. By analyzing the land use rights granted between 1993 and the first half of 2000 in the built-up area of Beijing, empirical analyses demonstrate that both land prices and land development density decrease as the distance from the city core increases. Additionally, the study finds that the slope of the land rent curve varies depending on the type of land use. This suggests that the land market plays a role in shaping land development decisions and the overall urban form. Furthermore, the research reveals that the slope of the land rent curve and the elasticity of land-capital substitution change over time. The former declines due to significant investments in transportation infrastructure, which have reduced transport costs and shifted the land rent curve. The latter increases, indicating the impact of prices on land development density. These changes in the land rent function and the elasticity of land-capital substitution indicate the maturing of the Beijing land market. However, it is important to note that there are significant land developments occurring outside of the land market, such as those on administratively allocated land. These developments can distort the urban land use patterns observed in this study.

title: The Mismatch Argument: The Construction of a Housing Orthodoxy in Australia
text: Australia's housing policy discourse is characterized by several widely accepted beliefs. While these beliefs are not universally embraced, they hold significant symbolic authority within the discourse. One particularly influential belief in Australia is the idea that there is a "mismatch" between the available housing stock and the size of households, resulting in significant underutilization and underoccupancy of housing. This belief is so deeply ingrained in housing policy discussions that it is often taken for granted. However, there are various criticisms of the mismatch belief, including empirical, conceptual, and discursive critiques. The discursive critique focuses on the statements made about the relationship between households and dwellings, rather than the actual empirical relationship itself. Through this analysis, we can understand how the mismatch belief originated in Australia and how it has shaped housing discourse. This paper explores the development of the mismatch belief, tracing its origins in the early 1970s to its establishment in national and state housing policy research by the early 1990s. It demonstrates how the discourse structures reinforce the belief, despite empirical and conceptual challenges to its validity. Of particular concern is the impact of this belief on individuals who are deemed to be underutilizing their dwellings, as well as its influence on policy interpretations, such as occupancy standards.

title: Citizen Participation and Citizen Evaluation in Disaster Recovery
text:
The disastrous flood that occurred in April 1997 had a significant impact on Grand Forks, North Dakota, and East Grand Forks, Minnesota. Since then, both cities have become prime examples of successful recovery efforts, as recognized by the Federal Emergency Management Agency. The federal government played a major role in funding the necessary infrastructure updates for these cities. As a result, their downtown areas are now undergoing reconstruction and attracting new businesses.

However, the aftermath of the flood has led to diverging paths for the two cities in terms of social and political outcomes. East Grand Forks took the advice of consultants and implemented extensive citizen participation initiatives. This approach has resulted in political stability and high levels of citizen satisfaction in East Grand Forks. On the other hand, Grand Forks primarily relied on bureaucratic guidance to respond to the disaster. Consequently, Grand Forks has experienced changes in its government structure, turnover of elected and appointed officials, and a less positive evaluation from its citizens.

This study aims to explore how citizens' perceptions of their participation in the recovery process influence their evaluation of the overall success of the recovery efforts.

title: Population growth, urban sprawl and landscape integrity of Beijing City
text: Airborne remote sensing data collected between 1997 and 2002 was used to analyze the detailed landscape pattern of the urban area within Beijing City's 6th ring road. Fragstats 3.3 was utilized to compute landscape indices at the landscape level, and changes in land use/cover types were examined during the specified time period. The findings indicate significant transformations in the urban built area (UBA) and farmland within the 6th ring road, with farmland being replaced by UBA. The number of patches increased by 106.6%, while the mean patch area decreased by 51.6%. Additionally, the splitting index increased by 94.3%, and the landscape diversity index increased by 17.8%. These changes resulted in a more fragmented and diversified landscape pattern over the course of five years. The primary drivers of this landscape change were the escalating demand for land due to population growth, unsustainable urban expansion, and improvements in housing standards. The negative impacts of rapid urbanization on the urban landscape in Beijing are evident.

title: Drink Choice: Factors Influencing the Intention to Drink Wine
text: This paper examines why consumers prefer wine over other alcoholic beverages, focusing on the beliefs consumers hold about wine drinking behavior. The research findings indicate that attitudes are somewhat more influential in determining the intention to drink wine compared to perceived social pressure. However, both attitudinal and normative factors are necessary to fully understand wine consumption. Although health emerged as a prominent belief in the qualitative phase of the research, the subsequent quantitative study revealed that drinking wine for its supposed health benefits did not significantly impact attitudes or behavior. On the other hand, the enjoyment of various tastes and flavors, as well as its compatibility with food, were found to be significantly more important. These results suggest that promoting awareness of the health benefits of wine drinking may have limited effectiveness.

title: Application of growth technologies in enhancing food security and sustainability
text:
For over 50 years, anabolic steroids have been widely utilized in the beef cattle industry as effective and safe growth-promoting agents. In fact, more than 90% of feedlot cattle in the US receive some form of steroidal implant during their lifetime (NAHMS, USDA 2000). The FDA has approved a range of growth promotants, which can be found in Table 1. Implants have consistently demonstrated the ability to enhance growth rate by 8 to 28%, improve feed efficiency by 5 to 20%, and increase lean tissue mass in the carcass by 3 to 10% (Duckett and Owens, 1997).

The advantages of these improvements in production efficiency are manifold. Firstly, they significantly reduce production costs by minimizing the amount of feed required per unit of gain (Avery and Avery, 2007). Secondly, they decrease the amount of land needed to produce equivalent quantities of food for consumers. Thirdly, they mitigate the production of greenhouse gases by reducing the number of animals necessary to produce the same amount of beef (Avery and Avery, 2007). Lastly, they extend cost savings to consumers by providing a year-round, affordable supply of beef at reduced prices (Lawrence and Ibarburu, 2006).

Given that animal products play a significant role in the caloric and nutrient intake of the human population, altering the growth composition to favor lean tissue over adipose tissue results in a healthier product with fewer calories, while still being rich in beneficial nutrients.

In addition to steroidal implants, a newer class of orally active growth promotants called b-adrenergic agonists (BAA; Ractopamine-HCl; 2003 and Zilpaterol-HCl; 2006) have gained approval for use in finishing beef cattle in the past decade. These products offer similar production benefits to steroidal implants but differ in their application and mode of action. Beta-adrenergic agonists are administered during the final 20 to 42 days of the cattle finishing period, depending on the specific product.

The aim of this paper is to elucidate the mechanisms and advantages of anabolic implants and BAA in beef cattle production.

title: Metabolic modifiers as performance-enhancing technologies for livestock production
text: The growing global population and increasing demand for food will lead to competition for land, water, and energy. This will have a negative impact on our ability to produce food and the environment. Globalization has boosted the trade in livestock products and resulted in industry growth. Livestock production has undergone changes in technology and location, posing challenges for producers who face growing demand with limited resources. The solution lies in increasing efficiency. As incomes rise in developing economies, there is a higher demand for high-quality animal proteins. The Food and Agriculture Organization predicts a 70% increase in food requirements by 2050. Technological advancements in the animal industry offer opportunities to overcome these challenges. However, there are concerns that the focus on efficiency and lean meat yield may compromise meat quality. Market differentiation, trade barriers, and consumer resistance also pose obstacles to the adoption of these technologies. To meet the global demand for animal protein, it is crucial to continue developing and adopting technologies while considering potential barriers to acceptance.

title: Assessment of hemodynamic efficacy and safety of 6% hydroxyethylstarch 130/0.4 vs. 0.9% NaCl fluid replacement in patients with severe sepsis: The CRYSTMAS study
text: Insufficient initial treatment and delayed stabilization of the body's fluid levels may increase the risk of death in patients with severe sepsis. To compare the effectiveness and safety of two different fluids, 6% HES 130/0.4 and NaCl 0.9%, in stabilizing fluid levels in patients with severe sepsis, we conducted a study in multiple intensive care units. Out of 196 patients, 174 reached stable fluid levels, with 88 receiving HES and 86 receiving NaCl. The HES group required significantly less fluid to reach stability compared to the NaCl group (1,379 ±886 ml for HES and 1,709 ±1,164 ml for NaCl, with a mean difference of -331± 1,033, 95% CI -640 to -21, P = 0.0185). The time taken to reach stable fluid levels was 11.8 ± 10.1 hours for HES and 14.3 ± 11.1 hours for NaCl. The total amount of study drug administered over four days, length of stay in the ICU and hospital, and the severity of illness measured by the SOFA score were similar between the two groups. Acute renal failure occurred in 24 (24.5%) patients in the HES group and 19 (20%) patients in the NaCl group (P = 0.454). There were no differences in the criteria used to assess kidney function or in mortality, blood clotting, or itching up to 90 days after treatment initiation. In the initial phase of fluid resuscitation for severe sepsis patients, HES required significantly less volume to achieve stable fluid levels compared to NaCl, without any difference in adverse events between the two groups. The study was registered under the identifier NCT00464204.

title: Comparisons between different polychemotherapy regimens for early breast cancer: meta-analyses of long-term outcome among 100,000 women in 123 randomised trials.
text:
BACKGROUND: We aimed to investigate potential differences in efficacy between different adjuvant chemotherapy regimens for breast cancer, as these differences could impact treatment decisions.

METHODS: We conducted meta-analyses using individual patient data from randomized trials. We compared taxane-plus-anthracycline-based regimens to non-taxane chemotherapy, anthracycline-based regimens to each other or to cyclophosphamide, methotrexate, and fluorouracil (CMF), and polychemotherapy to no chemotherapy. We used standard dosages of the drugs doxorubicin (A) and epirubicin (E) to define standard CMF, standard 4AC, and CAF and CEF. We reported the log-rank breast cancer mortality rate ratios (RRs).

FINDINGS: Trials that added four cycles of a taxane to an anthracycline-based control regimen showed a reduction in breast cancer mortality (RR 0.86, SE 0.04, p=0.0005). However, trials that added four extra cycles of a taxane while also increasing the dosage of non-taxane drugs did not show a significant difference (RR 0.94, SE 0.06, p=0.33). Trials with CMF-treated controls demonstrated that standard 4AC and standard CMF were equivalent (RR 0.98, SE 0.05, p=0.67), but anthracycline-based regimens with higher cumulative dosages (such as CAF or CEF) were superior to standard CMF (RR 0.78, SE 0.06, p=0.0004). Trials comparing chemotherapy to no chemotherapy suggested greater reductions in mortality with CAF (RR 0.64, SE 0.09, p<0.0001) compared to standard 4AC (RR 0.78, SE 0.09, p=0.01) or standard CMF (RR 0.76, SE 0.05, p<0.0001). Age, nodal status, tumor characteristics, estrogen receptor status, and tamoxifen use did not significantly affect the risk reductions observed with taxane-based or anthracycline-based regimens. Therefore, regardless of age or tumor characteristics, certain taxane-plus-anthracycline-based or higher-cumulative-dosage anthracycline-based regimens (that do not require stem cells) reduced breast cancer mortality by approximately one-third.

INTERPRETATION: The 10-year overall mortality differences aligned with the breast cancer mortality differences, despite the toxicities associated with taxane, anthracycline, and other drugs. The 10-year gains from a one-third reduction in breast cancer mortality depend on the absolute risks without chemotherapy, particularly for estrogen receptor-positive disease when appropriate endocrine therapy is used. Low absolute risk implies low absolute benefit, but further information is needed to predict risk and chemosensitivity using tumor gene expression markers or quantitative immunohistochemistry.

FUNDING: This study was supported by Cancer Research UK, the British Heart Foundation, and the UK Medical Research Council.

title: Invariant NKT cells modulate the suppressive activity of IL-10-secreting neutrophils differentiated with serum amyloid A.
text: The main cells responsible for inflammation are neutrophils, but they can also regulate excessive inflammation by releasing anti-inflammatory cytokines. However, we still don't fully understand the mechanisms that control their ability to change. Our research now demonstrates that a protein called systemic serum amyloid A 1 (SAA-1) plays a role in regulating the flexibility of neutrophil development. SAA-1 not only triggers the production of anti-inflammatory interleukin 10 (IL-10)-secreting neutrophils, but it also facilitates the interaction between these neutrophils and invariant natural killer T cells (iNKT cells). This interaction limits the suppressive effects of neutrophils by reducing IL-10 production and increasing IL-12 production. Melanomas that produce SAA-1 promote the development of IL-10-secreting neutrophils, so utilizing iNKT cells could be a valuable therapeutic approach to decrease the number of immunosuppressive neutrophils and restore immune responses specific to tumors.

title: Body-mass index and cause-specific mortality in 900 000 adults: collaborative analyses of 57 prospective studies.
text:
The main objective of the Prospective Studies Collaboration was to examine the associations between body-mass index (BMI) and overall and cause-specific mortality through long-term follow-up of a large number of individuals. In this study, data from 57 prospective studies with a total of 894,576 participants, primarily from western Europe and North America, were analyzed. The participants were mostly male (61%) with a mean recruitment age of 46 years. The baseline BMI of the participants was adjusted for age, sex, smoking status, and study. The first 5 years of follow-up were excluded to avoid reverse causality, resulting in a mean follow-up period of 8 years. During this time, there were 66,552 deaths of known cause, with a mean age at death of 67 years. The causes of death included vascular diseases, diabetes, renal or hepatic diseases, neoplastic diseases, respiratory diseases, and other causes.

The findings of the study showed that the lowest mortality rates were observed at a BMI range of about 22.5-25 kg/m(2) for both sexes. Above this range, positive associations were found for several specific causes of death, while no inverse associations were observed. The risks associated with higher BMI and smoking were roughly additive, and each 5 kg/m(2) increase in BMI was associated with approximately 30% higher overall mortality. Specifically, the hazard ratio per 5 kg/m(2) increase in BMI was 1.29 for overall mortality, 1.41 for vascular mortality, 2.16 for diabetic mortality, 1.59 for renal mortality, 1.82 for hepatic mortality, 1.10 for neoplastic mortality, 1.20 for respiratory mortality, and 1.20 for other causes of mortality. Below the BMI range of 22.5-25 kg/m(2), BMI was inversely associated with overall mortality, primarily due to strong inverse associations with respiratory diseases and lung cancer. These inverse associations were more pronounced in smokers compared to non-smokers, despite similar cigarette consumption across different BMI levels.

In conclusion, BMI is a strong predictor of overall mortality, both above and below the optimal range of 22.5-25 kg/m(2). The increased mortality observed above this range is mainly attributed to vascular diseases and is likely to be causally related. At higher BMI levels (30-35 kg/m(2) and 40-45 kg/m(2)), median survival is reduced by 2-4 years and 8-10 years, respectively, which is comparable to the effects of smoking. The excess mortality observed below 22.5 kg/m(2) is primarily due to smoking-related diseases and is not fully understood. While other anthropometric measures may provide additional information, BMI alone is a reliable predictor of mortality.

title: Targeting metabolic remodeling in glioblastoma multiforme.
text: One crucial difference between tumor cells and normal differentiated cells is their altered metabolism. Tumor cells undergo stable genetic and epigenetic changes that allow them to proliferate, survive in unfavorable conditions, and invade surrounding tissues. One well-known adaptation is the shift to aerobic glycolysis, also known as the "Warburg Effect," where cancer cells rely on glycolysis instead of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, regardless of oxygen availability. This metabolic shift is characterized by increased glucose uptake, reduced oxygen consumption, and elevated lactate production. It provides cancer cells with a survival advantage and generates essential substrates like fatty acids, amino acids, and nucleotides needed for rapid proliferation. In this review, we explore the role of key metabolic enzymes associated with aerobic glycolysis in Glioblastoma Multiforme (GBM), a highly aggressive and glycolytic brain tumor. Targeting these enzymes involved in modulating the "Warburg Effect" could offer a promising therapeutic approach, either alone or in combination with existing treatments for GBMs.

title: Signaling architectures that transmit unidirectional information despite retroactivity
text: A signaling pathway is responsible for transmitting information from one system to another in a specific direction. However, retroactivity, which is the additional reaction flux that occurs when a system interacts with downstream systems, poses a challenge to achieving unidirectional transmission. This leads to the question of whether signaling pathways have developed specialized architectures to overcome retroactivity and transmit signals in a one-way manner. In this study, we propose a mathematical analysis-based procedure to answer this question. By using this procedure, we examine the ability of various signaling architectures to transmit signals from upstream to downstream as different biological parameters are adjusted. Our findings reveal that single stage phosphorylation and phosphotransfer systems, which transmit signals from a kinase, face a design trade-off that limits their ability to overcome retroactivity. Interestingly, cascades of these architectures, which are commonly found in nature, can overcome this trade-off and enable unidirectional transmission. On the other hand, phosphotransfer systems, as well as single and double phosphorylation cycles that transmit signals from a substrate, are unable to mitigate retroactivity effects, even when cascaded, and are therefore not suitable for unidirectional information transmission. Our results identify signaling architectures that can achieve unidirectional signal transmission and possess modular processes that maintain their input/output behavior across different contexts. These findings can be applied to break down natural signal transduction networks into modules and provide a library of devices for synthetic biology to facilitate modular circuit design.

title: Association between pre-diabetes, type 2 diabetes and trabecular bone score: The Vietnam Osteoporosis Study.
text: The aim of this study was to investigate the relationship between type 2 diabetes (T2D) and trabecular bone score (TBS) in adult Vietnamese men and women. The study included 2702 women and 1398 men aged 30 years and above from the general community in Ho Chi Minh City. HbA1c levels were measured and classified into three groups: normal, pre-diabetes, and diabetes. TBS was evaluated using iNsight Software on lumbar spine BMD scans. The results showed that the prevalence of pre-diabetes and diabetes in men and women was 30.2% and 8.3% respectively. In women, TBS was lower in pre-diabetes and diabetes compared to normal individuals. However, there was no significant difference in TBS between diabetic status in men. Additionally, TBS was inversely correlated with HbA1c levels in women but not in men. In conclusion, women with type 2 diabetes and pre-diabetes have lower TBS compared to individuals without diabetes, suggesting a deterioration of bone microarchitecture associated with diabetes and pre-diabetes.

title: Adhesion molecules and chemokines: relation to anthropometric, body composition, biochemical and dietary variables
text:
Introduction: Among the various inflammatory mediators involved in the development of obesity, certain cell adhesion molecules (Pselectin, E-selectin, VCAM-1, ICAM-1) and the chemokine MCP-1 play a significant role. These molecules are crucial for cell adherence to endothelial surfaces and maintaining the integrity of the vascular wall. Additionally, they can be influenced by body composition and dietary patterns.

Objectives: The aim of this study is to describe and discuss the relationship between these cell adhesion molecules, chemokines, and various anthropometric, body composition, dietary, and biochemical markers.

Methods: Relevant papers were identified through topic searches in scientific databases, without any restrictions on the publication year.

Results: All of the mentioned molecules showed a positive association with anthropometric markers, although conflicting results were found for ICAM-1 and VCAM-1. Furthermore, E-selectin and MCP-1 levels were found to be more strongly correlated with visceral fat rather than overall obesity. Weight loss was found to reduce the levels of these molecules, except for VCAM-1. The distribution of macronutrients, particularly excessive consumption of saturated and trans fats, as well as adherence to a Western dietary pattern, were associated with increased levels of these molecules. Conversely, supplementation with omega-3 fatty acids, adherence to a healthy dietary pattern, high calcium intake, and increased dairy consumption were associated with lower levels. In terms of biochemical parameters, these molecules were inversely related to HDL cholesterol and positively related to total cholesterol, triglycerides, blood glucose, fasting insulin, and insulin resistance.

Conclusion: Normal anthropometric indicators, body composition, biochemical parameters, and dietary patterns have a positive impact on reducing subclinical inflammation associated with obesity by modulating the levels of cell adhesion molecules and chemokines.
